name: ocfs2_group_add
prose: Precondition: inode is any inode of the mounted ocfs2 filesystem, input describes a new, already formatted block group (group block number, chain, clusters, frees) to attach to the global bitmap (ocfs2/resize.c:458-598, int ocfs2_group_add(struct inode *inode, struct ocfs2_new_group_input *input)). name: SYSCALL_DEFINE1(close, unsigned int, fd)
prose: Generated system call close(fd) (open.c:1574-1602). It removes fd from the current process's descriptor table with file_close_fd(fd) (file.c:850-860, under files->file_lock); if there is no file it returns -EBADF (1581) and nothing else changes. Otherwise the table entry is already cleared; it calls filp_flush(file, current->files) (the file's ->flush op and, for non-O_PATH files, dnotify and POSIX-lock removal; the flush result is kept in retval) and then fput_close_sync(file) to drop the table's reference. If retval is 0 it returns 0 (1592); otherwise the flush error is returned, except that -ERESTARTSYS, -ERESTARTNOINTR, -ERESTARTNOHAND and -ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK are converted to -EINTR (a restart is impossible because the descriptor is already released). So the descriptor is released on every path except the -EBADF one, where there was no file to release, and even when a flush error is returned.

name: orangefs_bufmap_copy_to_iovec
prose: Precondition: the global buffer map __orangefs_bufmap is initialised, buffer_index is a valid index into its desc_array, whose page_array holds enough pages for size bytes, and iter is a destination iov_iter (orangefs/orangefs-bufmap.c:498-522, int orangefs_bufmap_copy_to_iovec(struct iov_iter *iter, int buffer_index, size_t size); the packet name orangefs_bufmap_copy_to_iter is not in the file). If a copy_page_to_iter call copies nothing (n == 0) it returns -EFAULT at 518 immediately; a short non-zero copy is not an error here: size is reduced by the amount copied and the loop continues with the next page (so after a short copy, the next page's data continues to be copied from offset 0 of the next page, and the pages are indexed by loop count i, not by bytes consumed). The iterator is advanced by what was copied; the buffer map itself is not modified.

prose: Precondition: none; pos, pos2, len and totlen are any loff_t (signed 64-bit) values (overlayfs/copy_up.c:232-243, static int ovl_verify_area(loff_t pos, loff_t pos2, loff_t len, loff_t totlen)). The function reads and writes no state.

name: ovl_remove_and_whiteout
prose: Precondition: dentry is an overlayfs dentry whose parent has an upper directory, list is the (possibly empty) list of merged directory entries of dentry (non-empty for a merged directory being removed), and the caller holds the parent's directory lock as required by ovl_cleanup_and_whiteout (overlayfs/dir.c:789-833, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno; the single return is 'return err' at 832. Errors: -EROFS (after a WARN_ON) at 800 if there is no work directory; if list is non-empty it calls ovl_clear_empty(dentry, list) to replace the directory by an empty opaque one, and an error pointer from it is returned as err without any dput (nothing was obtained); the error of ovl_lookup_upper_unlocked for the child name (going to out_dput, which dputs opaquedir if one was created); -ESTALE if the upper dentry found does not match (it must equal the opaque directory when one exists, or match the dentry's own upper dentry via ovl_matches_upper when there is no opaque directory but the dentry has an upper), in which case it does not call d_drop; otherwise err = ovl_cleanup_and_whiteout(ofs, upperdir, upper) (creates a whiteout in place of the upper entry via the work directory); on success ovl_dir_modified(dentry->d_parent, true) is called. After the whiteout step, d_drop(dentry) is executed whether or not ovl_cleanup_and_whiteout succeeded (line 826). Then the upper dentry reference and the opaque directory reference (if any) are dropped with dput, and err is returned.

name: ovl_get_inode
prose: Precondition: sb is an overlayfs superblock and oip describes the inode to get: oip->upperdentry (may be NULL), oip->oe (the lower layers; at least one of upper or lower must exist), oip->newinode (a preallocated inode or NULL), redirect strings, index and lowerdata flags (overlayfs/inode.c:1210-1315, struct inode *ovl_get_inode(struct super_block *sb, struct ovl_inode_params *oip); the packet item was the unnamed tail of it). Postcondition: returns the inode (a pointer, possibly one already in the inode cache) or ERR_PTR(err); the single return is 'return inode' at line 1309, reached directly or via out_err which logs 'failed to get inode (%i)' (ratelimited) and sets ERR_PTR(err). err starts as -EEXIST when oip->newinode is given, otherwise -ENOMEM. It chooses the real inode (upper, else lower) and whether to hash by the lower inode (ovl_hash_bylower). If hashing by upper or lower inode it gets the inode with ovl_iget5 (a NULL result goes to out_err with err as set above); if the inode already exists (not I_NEW), ovl_verify_inode must accept it or it is iput and -ESTALE returned, otherwise the upper dentry reference is dropped, oip->oe, redirect and lowerdata_redirect are freed (this call consumed them, since the existing inode already owns its state) and the existing inode is returned; for a new inode of a non-directory the link count is recomputed (ovl_get_nlink) and set. Otherwise (a lower hardlink that will break on copy up) it allocates new_inode (-ENOMEM on failure) with the real inode number and the lower layer's fsid. For a new or non-hashed inode it then calls ovl_fill_inode, ovl_inode_init (taking over oip's state), warns if the casefold state differs from ofs->casefold, sets flags OVL_IMPURE (impure upper directory), OVL_INDEX (oip->index), OVL_CONST_INO (hashed by lower), OVL_WHITEOUTS (directory that is merged, has more than one lower layer, or whose origin xattr check says it may have whiteouts), reads protection attributes from the upper dentry (ovl_check_protattr), and unlocks the inode with unlock_new_inode if it is I_NEW.

prose: Generated system call preadv2(fd, vec, vlen, pos_l, pos_h, flags) (read_write.c:1182-1192). It combines pos_h and pos_l into a loff_t pos (pos_from_hilo). name: do_signalfd4
prose: Precondition: mask points to a writable sigset_t that this function modifies in place (it clears the SIGKILL and SIGSTOP bits and complements the set; that normalisation is done by the function, not required of the caller), ufd is -1 to create a new signalfd or the descriptor of an existing signalfd, flags may contain any bits (signalfd.c:~250-304, static int do_signalfd4(int ufd, sigset_t *mask, int flags); slice cut head). If ufd == -1: kmalloc of the context (-ENOMEM at 270), ctx->sigmask = *mask, get_unused_fd_flags(flags & O_CLOEXEC) (its negative result returned after freeing the context, 277), anon_inode_getfile_fmode (an error pointer returns PTR_ERR after releasing the fd and context, 286); otherwise fd_install and the new descriptor is returned at 303. If ufd is an existing descriptor: -EBADF at 292 if it is not open, -EINVAL at 295 if its file is not a signalfd, else the stored signal mask is replaced under current->sighand->siglock and the signalfd wait queue woken; ufd is returned at 303.

name: is_retryable_error
prose: Precondition: none; error is any int (callers pass negative errno values) (smb/client/cifsglob.h:1847-1852, static inline bool is_retryable_error(int error)). Postcondition: returns true when is_interrupt_error(error) is true or error == -EAGAIN, and false otherwise. is_interrupt_error (cifsglob.h:1835-1845) is true for -EINTR, -ERESTARTSYS, -ERESTARTNOHAND and -ERESTARTNOINTR only (not -ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK). So the function returns true exactly for -EINTR, -ERESTARTSYS, -ERESTARTNOHAND, -ERESTARTNOINTR and -EAGAIN. It reads and writes no state.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (\result != 0) <==> (error == -4 || error == -11 || error == -512 || error == -513 || error == -514); */
note: slice cut head (function at 1847-1852, slice 1847-2099). reviewer round 15 right that -516 (ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK) is not in is_interrupt_error's list; verified at cifsglob.h:1837-1844. The contract uses the Linux values EINTR 4, EAGAIN 11, ERESTARTSYS 512, ERESTARTNOINTR 513, ERESTARTNOHAND 514 (negated), as constants; drop it if the verifier rejects raw errno numbers.

name: CIFSGetExtAttr
prose: Precondition: xid is the transaction id, tcon is NULL or a valid cifs_tcon with a usable session, netfid is the file handle to query, pExtAttrBits and pMask are writable pointers (smb/client/cifssmb.c:3595-3673, compiled under CONFIG_POSIX, int CIFSGetExtAttr(const unsigned int xid, struct cifs_tcon *tcon, const int netfid, __u64 *pExtAttrBits, __u64 *pMask); the packet name CIFSSMBGetExtAttr does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 with *pExtAttrBits and *pMask set from the 16-byte file_chattr_info in the response; -ENODEV at line 3606 if tcon is NULL; the error of smb_init at 3612 if the request buffer cannot be set up (returned directly without a retry, so this error can be -EAGAIN); otherwise it builds a TRANS2_QUERY_FILE_INFORMATION request with information level SMB_QUERY_ATTR_FLAGS and sends it with SendReceive. If SendReceive fails its error is returned, except -EAGAIN which makes the function release the request buffer and resend the whole request (label GetExtAttrRetry, repeating without a bound). If SendReceive succeeds, validate_t2 failing or a byte count below 2 gives -EIO, and a data count other than 16 gives -EIO; the data is located by the data offset in the response and read without a further bounds check against the buffer. On every error path the two output pointers are left unmodified. The request buffer is released (cifs_buf_release) before returning on all paths after smb_init succeeded.
note: packet name CIFSSMBGetExtAttr does not exist (the real name is CIFSGetExtAttr, cifssmb.c:3595); the slice 3604-3856 starts inside it (slice cut head). The earlier prose said the SendReceive failure is 'never -EAGAIN'; that holds for SendReceive but smb_init's error is returned directly (3611-3612) and may be -EAGAIN, so the claim was too strong.

name: CIFSFindFirst
prose: Precondition: xid is the transaction id, tcon and tcon->ses are valid, searchName is the directory path (or empty), cifs_sb provides the codepage and mount flags, pnetfid is NULL or points to a __u16, search_flags is the SMB search flags, psrch_inf points to a cifs_search_info whose info_level is set, msearch selects a wildcard search over the directory (smb/client/cifssmb.c:4306-4457, int CIFSFindFirst(const unsigned int xid, struct cifs_tcon *tcon, const char *searchName, struct cifs_sb_info *cifs_sb, __u16 *pnetfid, __u16 search_flags, struct cifs_search_info *psrch_inf, bool msearch); the packet name CIFSSMBFindFirst does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 on success, otherwise the error of smb_init (line 4328, returned directly with no retry, so it may be -EAGAIN), the SendReceive error (at 4425, after releasing the request buffer; -EAGAIN causes the whole request to be rebuilt and resent without a bound), or the validate_t2 error (4431, after releasing the buffer). On success the buffer is NOT released: psrch_inf is filled with unicode, ntwrk_buf_start = the response buffer (the caller becomes responsible for freeing it), smallBuf = false, srch_entries_start (at the response's data offset), endOfSearch, entries_in_buffer = SearchCount, index_of_last_entry = 2 + entries_in_buffer, and last_entry = srch_entries_start + LastNameOffset together with *pnetfid = the search handle when pnetfid is non-NULL; if LastNameOffset is larger than CIFSMaxBufSize it logs 'ignoring corrupt resume name', sets last_entry = NULL and leaves *pnetfid unset, still returning 0. The request builds the file name as UTF-16 (when the session uses Unicode, with an appended separator and '*' for msearch, or a lone separator for an empty name) or as a copied ASCII path (with the same additions), sets search attributes read-only|hidden|system|directory, a search count of one or CIFSMaxBufSize / sizeof(FILE_UNIX_INFO) entries for msearch, and the information level from psrch_inf->info_level.
note: packet name CIFSSMBFindFirst does not exist (real name CIFSFindFirst, cifssmb.c:4306); the slice 4375-4628 starts in its middle (slice cut head). Mechanical reviewers only; the previous prose is replaced since it was not checked against buffer ownership on success.

name: cifs_setup_ipc
prose: Precondition: ses is a valid session with a usable ses->server, seal says whether encryption is requested (smb/client/connect.c:2037-2081, struct cifs_tcon *cifs_setup_ipc(struct cifs_ses *ses, bool seal); the packet item was unnamed, and the slice 2044-2300 starts inside it, slice cut head). Postcondition: returns a new IPC tree connection or an ERR_PTR; single success return 'return tcon' at line 2080. If seal is true and the server lacks SMB2_GLOBAL_CAP_ENCRYPTION it logs and returns ERR_PTR(-EOPNOTSUPP) (2050) with nothing allocated. tcon_info_alloc failure returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) (2056). Otherwise it builds the UNC path \\<hostname>\IPC$ (reading server->hostname under srv_lock), sets tcon->ses = ses, tcon->ipc = true and tcon->seal = seal, and calls server->ops->tree_connect(xid, ses, unc, tcon, ses->local_nls) between get_xid and free_xid. If that fails it logs, frees the tcon with tconInfoFree and returns ERR_PTR(rc) (2072). On success it sets tcon->status = TID_GOOD under tc_lock and returns the tcon. Despite the header comment, this function does not store the tcon in ses->tcon_ipc; the caller owns the returned tcon and is expected to store it. No locks are held on return.
note: item unnamed; the function is cifs_setup_ipc (connect.c:2037-2081; slice 2044-2300 begins inside it and then continues into cifs_find_smb_ses, __cifs_put_smb_ses and cifs_set_cifscreds, which are not this item). Added the caveat that the header comment says the tcon is stored in the session but the code does not store it (no assignment to ses->tcon_ipc in 2037-2081).

name: cifs_negotiate_protocol
prose: Precondition: ses and server are valid, server->ops is set, the caller holds neither server->srv_lock nor other connection locks (smb/client/connect.c:4051-4104, int cifs_negotiate_protocol(const unsigned int xid, struct cifs_ses *ses, struct TCP_Server_Info *server)). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno through these return statements: -ENOSYS at 4058 if the ops lack need_neg or negotiate (state unchanged); -EHOSTDOWN at 4067 if server->tcpStatus is not CifsGood, CifsNew or CifsNeedNegotiate (state unchanged); 0 at 4073 if server->ops->need_neg(server) is false and tcpStatus is already CifsGood (no negotiation, state unchanged); and 'return rc' at 4103. Otherwise it sets tcpStatus = CifsInNegotiate and neg_start = jiffies under srv_lock and calls server->ops->negotiate(xid, ses, server). A result of -EAGAIN is retried once from the top (the status checks are repeated, so a changed tcpStatus can make the retry return -EHOSTDOWN or 0 early); a second -EAGAIN becomes -EHOSTDOWN. Afterwards, under srv_lock: on success (rc == 0) tcpStatus becomes CifsGood only if it is still CifsInNegotiate, else rc = -EHOSTDOWN; on any failure (including the converted -EHOSTDOWN) tcpStatus is set back to CifsNeedNegotiate only if it is still CifsInNegotiate. So the status is restored to CifsNeedNegotiate on failures after negotiation started, but not on the early -ENOSYS and -EHOSTDOWN returns.
note: slice cut head (function at 4051-4104, slice 3870-4120). reviewers: original right (the early -ENOSYS 4058 and -EHOSTDOWN 4067 returns leave tcpStatus unchanged); round 2 right (when need_neg is false and the status is CifsGood it returns 0 at 4073); round 15 right (after the second -EAGAIN, rc = -EHOSTDOWN at 4087 and the failure branch resets CifsInNegotiate to CifsNeedNegotiate at 4098-4099).

name: smb3_parse_opt
prose: Precondition: options and key are non-NULL NUL-terminated strings and val points to a char pointer (smb/client/fs_context.c:540-569, int smb3_parse_opt(const char *options, const char *key, char **val)). Postcondition: it duplicates options with kstrdup (-ENOMEM at line 547 if that fails, *val untouched), splits the copy on ',' and, skipping empty tokens, takes the first token whose first strlen(key) characters equal key (case-insensitive, strncasecmp) AND that contains an '=' not in the first position (so key need not be followed directly by '=': a token 'username=x' matches the key 'user', and the text after the first '=' is returned). For that token it sets *val = kstrdup(text after '=') and returns 0, or -ENOMEM with *val set to NULL if that copy fails. A token that begins with key but has no '=' is skipped and the scan continues, as is one whose '=' is the first character. If no token matches it returns -ENOENT and *val is not written. The duplicated options string is freed on every path. *val is written only in the match case (and set to NULL only on the allocation failure), not on all paths.
note: the slice (fs_context.c:1349-1649) is a middle part of smb3_fs_context_parse_param, but the item's name and prose describe smb3_parse_opt (fs_context.c:540-569), so it is fixed under that real name (slice does not contain it). reviewer round 15 wrong on all three points: the comparison is strncasecmp (case-insensitive, line 554), the key need not be followed by '=' (554-559), and *val is written only at 561 (set to NULL only if kstrdup fails).

name: smb3_fs_context_parse_param
prose: Precondition: fc is a cifs/smb3 fs_context whose private data is an smb3_fs_context, param is one parsed mount parameter (smb/client/fs_context.c:1125-1848, static int smb3_fs_context_parse_param(struct fs_context *fc, struct fs_parameter *param); the packet name cifs_parse_mount does not exist and slice 1650-1903 is the tail of this function). Postcondition: returns 0 if the option was accepted and applied to the context, or -EINVAL at 1847 via cifs_parse_mount_err, which frees and NULLs ctx->password, ctx->password2, ctx->source and fc->source before returning; there is also an early return at 1157: the negative fs_parse result, or 1 (not an error) when the sloppy option is set and the option is unknown. String options with an empty value (pass, password, user, username, pass2, password2) bypass fs_parse and are handled directly. The tail of the switch (1650 onward) handles: unix/posix extensions (conflicting settings only warn), nocase, brl (turning it off also changes file_mode when it has the default mandatory-lock form), handlecache, forcemandatorylock, setuids, intr, setuidfromacl, strictsync, serverino, rwpidforward, modesid, cifsacl, acl, locallease, sign, ignore_signature, seal, noac (only a warning), fsc (-EINVAL via the error label when the kernel lacks CONFIG_CIFS_FSCACHE), mfsymlinks, multiuser, sloppy, nosharesock, persistent and resilient handles (conflicting combinations such as persistent with nopersistent or resilient give -EINVAL), tcp_nodelay, domainauto, rdma, reparse and symlink flavors (a failing flavor parser gives -EINVAL) and symlinkroot (must be an absolute path shorter than PATH_MAX, else -EINVAL; the string pointer is taken over from param). After the switch, multiuser together with upcalltarget 'mount' gives -EINVAL, and multichannel is cleared when max_channels is 1; then it returns 0.
note: item named cifs_parse_mount (dropped as not-in-slice); that name does not exist: the slice 1650-1903 is the tail of smb3_fs_context_parse_param (fs_context.c:1125-1848; slice cut head), so FIXED under the real name per rule 6. The earlier prose was a general summary and did not list the exits (1157, 1836, 1847).

name: cifs_ses_add_channel
prose: Precondition: ses is a valid session with ses->chan_count >= 1 and room for one more channel in ses->chans; iface is the server interface (address, speed, rdma capability) to use for the new channel (smb/client/sess.c:486-645, int cifs_ses_add_channel(struct cifs_ses *ses, struct cifs_server_iface *iface); the packet name cifs_setup_channel does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno; the single return is 'return rc' at 644 after free_xid. It builds a temporary smb3_fs_context (kzalloc; -ENOMEM at 521 if that fails, going to out_free_xid), copying authentication, signing, unicode and version fields from the session and its main server, a UNC of the form \\<ses->ip_addr>\foo (kzalloc failure gives -ENOMEM via out_free_ctx), the interface's destination address and rdma capability, and the main connection's client GUID, with nosharesock set so a new connection is always made. It calls cifs_get_tcp_session(ctx, ses->server); under ses->chan_lock the result is stored in ses->chans[ses->chan_count].server: an error pointer is converted (rc = PTR_ERR, the slot's server set to NULL, lock released) and goes to out without incrementing chan_count; otherwise the slot gets the interface, chan_count is incremented, chan_seq reset, the channel marked as needing reconnect. Under ses->session_mutex it allocates the channel's crypto (smb3_crypto_shash_allocate; error: unlock and out), runs cifs_negotiate_protocol and, if that succeeded, cifs_setup_session (their error becomes rc). On failure after the channel was added (rc != 0 and the slot's server non-NULL) it drops the new connection with cifs_put_tcp_session, clears the need-reconnect bit and decrements ses->chan_count under chan_lock (WARN_ON if it would drop below 1). It then frees ctx->UNC and ctx (the strings other than UNC borrowed from the session are not freed).
note: packet name cifs_setup_channel does not exist; real function cifs_ses_add_channel at sess.c:486-645; the slice 508-763 starts inside it (slice cut head). Mechanical reviewers only; the earlier prose is replaced because it described a function with another name.

name: cifs_check_trans2
prose: Precondition: mid is the mid_q_entry for the response just received on server, buf is the received SMB buffer, malformed is non-zero when the buffer was already found malformed (smb/client/smb1transport.c:727-763, returns bool; static, the caller is the SMB1 receive path). Postcondition: returns true when the response should continue to be handled as a (possibly multi-part) trans2 response, false when it should be handled as an ordinary response. Return points: (1) if malformed is non-zero or check2ndT2(buf) <= 0 (not a secondary trans2 fragment): if mid->multiRsp is already set it sets multiEnd = true, dequeues the mid (dequeue_mid(mid, true)) and returns true (738); otherwise returns false (740). (2) Otherwise this is a fragment: mid->multiRsp is set. If mid->resp_buf already holds the first part, coalesce_t2(buf, mid->resp_buf) is called: it copies this fragment's data into the end of the stored first buffer and returns 1 when more parts are expected (the fragment has then already been copied into the target, and check_trans2 returns true at 747 leaving the mid queued), or 0 when all parts have arrived, or a negative errno (-EPROTO, -ENOBUFS) when the data is inconsistent; for 0 or a negative value multiEnd is set, the mid is dequeued (dequeue_mid(mid, malformed), where malformed is that result) and it returns true (751). (3) If this is the first part (no resp_buf): when server->large_buf is false it only logs '1st trans2 resp needs bigbuf' and returns true without keeping buf (line 762); when it is true the buffer is attached to the mid (mid->resp_buf = buf, mid->large_buf = true) and server->bigbuf is set to NULL, so the mid owns the buffer, and it returns true.
note: slice cut head (function at 727-763, slice 505-763). reviewers all right: original (the first fragment with !server->large_buf neither claims buf nor clears server->bigbuf yet returns true, 753-755, 762); round 2 (the multiRsp branch at 735-738 and the completed/error coalesce at 749-751 dequeue the mid, it is not kept in the queue); round 15 (coalesce_t2 copies the fragment before returning 1: smb1transport.c:713-718).

name: SMB2_change_notify
prose: Precondition: tcon is a valid tree connection with tcon->ses non-NULL to be dereferenced, persistent_fid and volatile_fid identify an open directory handle, watch_tree and completion_filter select what to watch, max_out_data_len is passed to the caller's design (unused here), out_data points to a char pointer, plen is NULL or points to a u32 (smb/client/smb2pdu.c:4052-4149, int SMB2_change_notify(const unsigned int xid, struct cifs_tcon *tcon, u64 persistent_fid, u64 volatile_fid, bool watch_tree, u32 completion_filter, u32 max_out_data_len, char **out_data, u32 *plen); the packet name SMB2_notify does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno. It picks a channel with cifs_pick_channel(ses); if ses or the server is NULL it returns -EIO at 4077 without touching *plen or *out_data. Otherwise (label replay_again) it sets *plen = 0 when plen is non-NULL, builds the request with SMB2_notify_init (its error goes to cnotify_exit), and, on a replay, sleeps cur_sleep ms and marks the request as a replay; it sends and waits with cifs_send_recv. If that fails it counts the failure and keeps its error. On success, if the response buffer is NULL or shorter than sizeof(struct smb2_change_notify_rsp) + 1 it exits with rc = 0, *out_data untouched and *plen 0; else it validates the output buffer offset and length with smb2_validate_iov (error: exit with it), and kmemdups the OutputBufferLength bytes at OutputBufferOffset into *out_data: failure gives -ENOMEM and *out_data = NULL; success sets *plen to OutputBufferLength (when plen is non-NULL) and the caller owns the buffer and must kfree it. cnotify_exit releases the request small buffer and the response buffer; if the result is a replayable error (is_replayable_error) and smb2_should_replay allows another attempt, the whole sequence restarts at replay_again; otherwise it returns rc at 4148. The function returns 0 both for a real notification and for an empty or short response, so the caller must look at *out_data / *plen.
note: packet name SMB2_notify does not exist; real function is SMB2_change_notify (smb2pdu.c:4052-4149); slice 4068-4322 starts inside it (slice cut head). Mechanical reviewers only. max_out_data_len is not used in the function body (4052-4149), noted; the earlier prose described the signature differently.

name: smbd_negotiate
prose: Precondition: sc is an SMB Direct socket whose status should be SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_NEGOTIATE_NEEDED (a WARN_ON_ONCE fires otherwise but the function continues) (smb/client/smbdirect.c:1640-1680, static int smbd_negotiate(struct smbdirect_socket *sc)). Postcondition: returns 0 when the socket reached SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_CONNECTED, else a negative errno. It takes a receive buffer with get_receive_buffer, sets sc->status = SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_NEGOTIATE_RUNNING and sc->recv_io.expected = SMBDIRECT_EXPECT_NEGOTIATE_REP, and posts the receive (smbd_post_recv): on failure it returns that error after put_receive_buffer, with the status left at NEGOTIATE_RUNNING. It then posts the negotiate request (smbd_post_send_negotiate_req); its error is returned at 1661 directly (the receive buffer is not returned here and the status stays NEGOTIATE_RUNNING). Then it waits interruptibly (wait_event_interruptible_timeout on sc->status_wait for the status to leave NEGOTIATE_RUNNING, up to negotiate_timeout_msec). If the status is CONNECTED afterwards it returns 0. Otherwise: a wait result of 0 (timeout) gives -ETIMEDOUT, -ERESTARTSYS gives -EINTR, and anything else (the status changed to something other than CONNECTED) gives -ENOTCONN; on a timeout or signal this function does not change the status, which can still be NEGOTIATE_RUNNING when it returns.
note: slice cut head (function at 1640-1680, slice 1526-1778). reviewers right: original (the early post-send error returns the post's errno with the status still RUNNING, 1659-1661); round 2 (on timeout or signal the status is not changed by this function, 1672-1679).

name: ndr_decode_v4_ntacl
prose: Precondition: n is an initialised NDR reader over a buffer (n->length bytes) holding an encoded v4 NT ACL xattr, acl is a writable struct xattr_ntacl (smb/server/ndr.c:450-513, int ndr_decode_v4_ntacl(struct ndr *n, struct xattr_ntacl *acl); the packet item was unnamed and the slice 507-514 is the tail of this function, slice cut head). Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno; the single return statements are early returns of ndr_read_* errors or -EINVAL, and 'return ret' at 513. It resets n->offset = 0, then reads in order: a 16-bit version into acl->version (must be 4, else -EINVAL); a 32-bit second version that must equal acl->version (else -EINVAL); a 16-bit level and a 32-bit reference id (both discarded); a 16-bit hash type into acl->hash_type; XATTR_SD_HASH_SIZE bytes into acl->hash; then 10 bytes into acl->desc, whose result is not checked, so if fewer than 10 bytes remain acl->desc is not written; acl->desc must begin with the 9 characters 'posix_acl' (strncmp, else -EINVAL with a log); a 64-bit time (discarded); XATTR_SD_HASH_SIZE bytes into acl->posix_acl_hash; then it sets acl->sd_size = n->length - n->offset (all remaining bytes), allocates acl->sd_buf with kzalloc (-ENOMEM if that fails) and copies the remaining bytes into it, returning the read result. Each ndr_read_* helper (for example ndr_read_bytes, ndr_read_int*) returns -EINVAL if the field would extend past n->length, so a truncated buffer yields -EINVAL; on any error after the allocation acl->sd_buf stays allocated and the caller owns and must free it, and on earlier errors previously decoded fields of acl remain set.
note: item unnamed; the slice 507-514 is the last lines of ndr_decode_v4_ntacl (ndr.c:450-513); FIXED under the real name (slice cut head). Mechanical reviewers only.

name: smb2_get_reparse_tag_special_file
prose: Precondition: mode is a Unix file mode (smb/server/smb2pdu.c:742-759, static __le32 smb2_get_reparse_tag_special_file(umode_t mode)). Postcondition: returns the little-endian SMB reparse tag for the file type in mode, or 0. It returns 0 (line 745) for a directory or a regular file; IO_REPARSE_TAG_LX_SYMLINK_LE (748) for a symbolic link; IO_REPARSE_TAG_LX_FIFO_LE (750) for a FIFO; IO_REPARSE_TAG_AF_UNIX_LE (752) for a socket; IO_REPARSE_TAG_LX_CHR_LE (754) for a character device; IO_REPARSE_TAG_LX_BLK_LE (756) for a block device; and 0 (758) for any other mode. The tags are the byte-swapped (cpu_to_le32) constants of the same names, whose numeric values are defined in the headers and are not restated here. The function reads and writes no state.
note: slice cut head (function at 742-759, slice 512-771). Round 2 reviewer pointed out that the earlier contract's numeric tag values were wrong; the prose now names the constants instead, and the contract is left empty for that reason (the _LE macros are byte-swapped constants the verifier cannot see).

name: smb2_ioctl
prose: Precondition: work is a ksmbd_work holding a received SMB2 IOCTL request (in work->request_buf, or the next command of a compound request) and a response buffer; the connection and tree connection are set (smb/server/smb2pdu.c:8413-8780, int smb2_ioctl(struct ksmbd_work *work); the item was marked dropped as 'enclosing dispatcher' but smb2_ioctl is a real function and the slice 8474-8737 is its middle, slice cut head and tail). Postcondition: returns 0 when the response was built and pinned (line 8763) or a negative errno after setting rsp->hdr.Status and calling smb2_set_err_rsp (8778-8779); the early return of a non-zero pin result also goes to out. Setup: it selects req and rsp (the compound case uses the next-command buffers and the compound file id when the request's VolatileFileId is not a real id), takes id = req->VolatileFileId when no compound id applies, and requires req->Flags == SMB2_0_IOCTL_IS_FSCTL (-EOPNOTSUPP otherwise); smb2_calc_max_out_buf_len negative sets STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER and fails. Dispatch on CtlCode: FSCTL_DFS_GET_REFERRALS(_EX): -EOPNOTSUPP with STATUS_FS_DRIVER_REQUIRED (goes to out2, skipping the generic status mapping); FSCTL_CREATE_OR_GET_OBJECT_ID: a zero-filled object-id reply (dummy); FSCTL_PIPE_TRANSCEIVE: nbytes from fsctl_pipe_transceive; FSCTL_VALIDATE_NEGOTIATE_INFO: -EOPNOTSUPP for dialects before SMB3.0, -EINVAL for a short input or output buffer, else fsctl_validate_negotiate_info (a negative result fails) and the file ids set to SMB2_NO_FID; FSCTL_QUERY_NETWORK_INTERFACE_INFO: nbytes from fsctl_query_iface_info_ioctl; FSCTL_REQUEST_RESUME_KEY: -EINVAL for a short output buffer, else fsctl_request_resume_key; FSCTL_COPYCHUNK and FSCTL_COPYCHUNK_WRITE: -EACCES if the tree is not writable, -EINVAL for short in/out buffers, then fsctl_copychunk fills the response; FSCTL_SET_SPARSE: -EINVAL for a short input, else fsctl_set_sparse; FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA: -EACCES if not writable, -EINVAL for short input or an invalid [offset, beyond-final-zero) range, and for a non-empty range -ENOENT if the file id is unknown, -EACCES without FILE_WRITE_DATA, else ksmbd_vfs_zero_data; FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES: -EINVAL for a short input, -E2BIG sets STATUS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW but still returns the ranges found, other negatives fail; FSCTL_GET_REPARSE_POINT: -ENOENT if the file id is unknown, else the reparse tag from smb2_get_reparse_tag_special_file of the file mode with zero data length; FSCTL_DUPLICATE_EXTENTS_TO_FILE: -EINVAL for short input, -ENOENT for an unknown source or target handle, -EACCES if the tree is read-only or the target lacks write or the source lacks read access, then vfs_clone_file_range (-EXDEV and -EOPNOTSUPP give -EOPNOTSUPP) and, for any other short clone, vfs_copy_file_range, with an error or short copy giving the negative error or -EINVAL; every other control code gives -EOPNOTSUPP. On success it fills the response header (CtlCode, InputCount 0, offsets 112, OutputCount = nbytes, StructureSize 49) and pins it with ksmbd_iov_pin_rsp. The error exit maps -EACCES to STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED, -ENOENT to STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND, -EOPNOTSUPP to STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED, -ENOSPC to STATUS_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, and any other negative value or a status still 0 to STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER.

name: smb21_lease_break_ack
prose: Precondition: work holds an SMB2 lease break acknowledgment request on an established connection (work->conn) (smb/server/smb2pdu.c:8920-8992, static void smb21_lease_break_ack(struct ksmbd_work *work); returns nothing and reports errors in the response header). Postcondition: it looks up the lease by req->LeaseKey in the connection's lease table (lookup_lease_in_table). If none is found it calls smb2_set_err_rsp(work), then sets rsp->hdr.Status = STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL and returns (no oplock_info to release). If found (a reference is held on opinfo), it takes the error exit err_out (smb2_set_err_rsp(work) and opinfo_put) with these statuses set before the call: STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL if opinfo->op_state is OPLOCK_STATE_NONE or breaking_cnt is zero; STATUS_REQUEST_NOT_ACCEPTED if check_lease_state(lease, req->LeaseState) rejects the requested state. Otherwise it sets lease->state = req->LeaseState, lease->new_state = SMB2_LEASE_NONE_LE and opinfo->level from the lease state, fills the acknowledgment response (StructureSize 36, same lease key, new lease state, duration 0) and pins it with ksmbd_iov_pin_rsp. If the pin fails it goes to err_out without setting a status of its own (only smb2_set_err_rsp is called), and the lease state changes already made are not undone. On success it sets op_state to OPLOCK_STATE_NONE under state_lock unless it is OPLOCK_CLOSING, wakes the oplock and break waiters, decrements breaking_cnt if positive (atomic_dec_if_positive) and drops the opinfo reference.
note: slice cut head (function at 8920-8992, slice 8738-8993). reviewers: original right (a missing lease key is handled, 8934-8940, with no opinfo to put); round 2 and round 15 right (on pin failure the code only calls smb2_set_err_rsp at 8989 and sets no status, 8974-8976, so the earlier claim that STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL is set there was wrong). I did not read smb2_set_err_rsp to say how it treats the header status.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(tee, int, fdin, int, fdout, size_t, len, unsigned int, flags)
prose: Generated system call tee(fdin, fdout, len, flags) (splice.c:1979-1996). Return values: -EINVAL at 1982 if flags has any bit outside SPLICE_F_ALL; 0 at 1985 if len == 0, without looking at either descriptor; -EBADF at 1989 if fdin is not open and at 1993 if fdout is not open; otherwise the result of do_tee(in, out, len, flags). do_tee (splice.c:1940-1977) returns -EBADF if the input file is not readable or the output file is not writable; -EINVAL if either file is not a pipe or both refer to the same pipe; otherwise it adds SPLICE_F_NONBLOCK when either file has O_NONBLOCK, calls ipipe_prep (input pipe) and opipe_prep (output pipe), and if both succeed link_pipe(ipipe, opipe, len, flags), returning the number of bytes duplicated (> 0), 0, or the negative error of whichever helper failed (a non-blocking call can return -EAGAIN, from either helper, depending on whether it has to wait; I did not read these helpers); on a positive result it issues fsnotify access and modify events. The data is duplicated by reference, not copied, and the input pipe's contents are not consumed. The descriptor references taken by the CLASS(fd) guards are released automatically.
note: macro-generated; name set to the SYSCALL_DEFINE4 head at splice.c:1979 (packet name __do_sys_tee). Reviewers: round 1 right that len == 0 returns 0 before touching the descriptors (1984-1985); round 2 plausible (-EAGAIN is not only for a full pipe) but depends on ipipe_prep/opipe_prep, which I did not read, so stated without detail. The SIGPIPE side effect mentioned by round 1 is in the pipe helpers, not verified here.

name: do_splice_read
prose: Precondition: in is an open file, ppos is its read position pointer (may be NULL for non-seekable files), pipe is the destination pipe with its lock held by the caller, len is the requested byte count, flags the SPLICE_F_* flags (splice.c:956-983, static ssize_t do_splice_read(struct file *in, loff_t *ppos, struct pipe_inode_info *pipe, size_t len, unsigned int flags)). Postcondition: returns -EBADF at 963 if in is not opened for reading (checked before len, so this applies even for len == 0); 0 at 965 if len is 0; otherwise len is clamped to the free pipe space (max_usage minus pipe_buf_usage, in pages) and to MAX_RW_COUNT, and the function returns -EINVAL (via warn_unsupported, which also logs a rate-limited debug message) at 975 if in->f_op->splice_read is NULL; copy_splice_read(in, ppos, pipe, len, flags) at 981 if the file is O_DIRECT or on a DAX inode; else in->f_op->splice_read(in, ppos, pipe, len, flags) at 982. In the last two cases the value returned is the underlying routine's result: the number of bytes spliced, 0 (for example at end of file or when the clamped length is 0 because the pipe is full), or a negative errno. So 0 is not returned only when len is 0.
note: slice cut head (function at 956-983, slice 778-1034). reviewers all right: round 1 (-EBADF is returned even for len == 0 because the f_mode check precedes the len check, 962-965; a missing splice_read gives -EINVAL not 0); round 15 (the result of splice_read/copy_splice_read can be 0, e.g. at EOF).

name: squashfs_xattr_handler
prose: Precondition: type is the on-disk xattr type value (prefix id in SQUASHFS_XATTR_PREFIX_MASK, optionally with the SQUASHFS_XATTR_VALUE_OOL bit) (squashfs/xattr.c:246-263, static const struct xattr_handler *squashfs_xattr_handler(int type); the packet name squashfs_xattr_handler_lookup does not exist). Postcondition: returns a pointer to one of three static handlers or NULL. It returns NULL at line 250 if type has any bit set outside SQUASHFS_XATTR_PREFIX_MASK | SQUASHFS_XATTR_VALUE_OOL. Otherwise it switches on type & SQUASHFS_XATTR_PREFIX_MASK (the out-of-line value bit is ignored): SQUASHFS_XATTR_USER returns &squashfs_xattr_user_handler, SQUASHFS_XATTR_TRUSTED returns &squashfs_xattr_trusted_handler and SQUASHFS_XATTR_SECURITY returns &squashfs_xattr_security_handler; any other prefix value returns NULL (261). It reads and writes no state.
note: packet name squashfs_xattr_handler_lookup does not exist; real function squashfs_xattr_handler at xattr.c:246-263 (slice 252-271 contains its switch and the handler array; slice cut head). reviewer round 15 wrong: the code does return NULL when bits outside the mask are set (xattr.c:248-250); only the VALUE_OOL bit is allowed and ignored.

prose: Generated system call stat(filename, statbuf) (stat.c:424-435, under __ARCH_WANT_OLD_STAT) writes a struct __old_kernel_stat. name: eventfs_iterate
prose: Precondition: file is an open eventfs directory (tracefs inode flagged TRACEFS_EVENT_INODE) and ctx is the caller's dir_context (tracefs/event_inode.c:599-713, static int eventfs_iterate(struct file *file, struct dir_context *ctx)). Postcondition: returns an int; the return statements are: 0 at line 615 if dir_emit_dots stops (the dots do not fit); -EINVAL at 619 if the inode is not an eventfs inode; and 'return ret' at 707 with ret = -EINVAL if the eventfs_inode is NULL or already freed when looked up (the lookup is under eventfs_mutex; the srcu read lock is held from line 623 and released at out), or if ei->is_freed is seen while walking the children (684); ret = 0 if the walk stops early, either because a directory entry does not fit (dir_emit false) or because ei->is_freed was set while processing the file entries (651); and ret = 1 after the whole entry list and child list have been walked (703). The function resumes from ctx->pos: c = ctx->pos - 2 entries are skipped. For each file entry from index c it calls the entry's callback under eventfs_mutex (entries whose callback returns <= 0 are skipped but ctx->pos still advances through the for-statement increment) and emits the name as DT_REG with dir_emit; when dir_emit returns false the loop exits via goto out without executing the increment, so ctx->pos is left pointing at that entry. After the file entries it subtracts the number of skipped entries from c and walks the child directories (srcu list walk): children are skipped while c > 0, then each visited child increments ctx->pos before it is checked; a freed child is skipped (ctx->pos stays incremented), and if dir_emit of a live child fails, ctx->pos is decremented again (out_dec) and the function returns 0. So ctx->pos is advanced for skipped entries as well as emitted ones, and it is not advanced for an entry whose dir_emit failed.
note: slice cut head (function at 599-713, slice 529-779). reviewers all right: original (1 is returned only after completing the iteration, 703, and 0 on a full buffer, 661/701); round 2 (ctx->pos also advances for skipped entries: callback <= 0 at 655-656 and freed children at 691-694); round 15 (the for-increment at 641 is skipped when dir_emit fails or is_freed bails out of the loop).

name: power_cut_emulated
prose: Precondition: c is a UBIFS filesystem description with c->dbg allocated and in power-cut-testing mode (dbg_is_tst_rcvry(c), checked by ubifs_assert), lnum is the logical eraseblock being accessed and write is non-zero for a write (ubifs/debug.c:2482-2574, static int power_cut_emulated(struct ubifs_info *c, int lnum, int write)). Postcondition: returns 0 (no power cut now) or 1 (a power cut is emulated: d->pc_happened is set, a warning and a stack dump are emitted). State advanced: on the first call (d->pc_cnt == 0) it randomly (1/2) chooses a delay mode: pc_delay = 1 with a random timeout of up to 60 s (pc_timeout set from jiffies) or pc_delay = 2 with pc_cnt_max random below 10000 calls, otherwise pc_delay stays unchanged (no delay), and pc_cnt is incremented. On every call it then returns 0 if pc_delay is 1 and the timeout has not passed, or if pc_delay is 2 and pc_cnt++ is still below pc_cnt_max (so in mode 2 pc_cnt advances on every call). Once past the delay it decides by LEB class with random chances, returning 0 on a 'chance' hit and otherwise logging the class and emulating the power cut: the superblock LEB (write: 1/2 skip then 19/20 skip), the master LEBs (19/20 skip), log LEBs (writes 99/100 skip, then 399/400 skip), LPT LEBs (writes 7/8 skip, then 19/20 skip), orphan LEBs (writes 1/2 skip, then 9/10 skip), the index head LEB (99/100 skip), the GC head LEB (9/10 skip), a non-bud LEB on writes when buds exist (19/20 skip), a bud LEB while a commit is running (999/1000 skip), and any other bud LEB (9999/10000 skip). The result therefore depends on random numbers and on internal state, not only on the arguments; both 0 and 1 are possible results for the same arguments, but while a delay is pending it is always 0.
note: slice cut head (function at 2482-2574, slice 2313-2569). reviewers right: original (the delay counters are advanced only in specific branches: pc_cnt at 2509 and 2515); round 2 (the delay branches 2513-2516 force 0 before the LEB class logic runs). Contract left empty (global/random state). The 'chance(a, b)' helper's exact meaning was not read; it is described only as 'a chance hit returns 0' as the code uses it.

name: lpt_gc
prose: Precondition: c is a UBIFS filesystem description with a valid LPT eraseblock table c->ltab for lpt_lebs LEBs; the caller does not hold c->lp_mutex (it is taken here) (ubifs/lpt_commit.c:1150-1169, static int lpt_gc(struct ubifs_info *c)). Postcondition: returns -ENOSPC at line 1167 if no LPT LEB was selected, else the result of lpt_gc_lnum(c, lnum) at 1168 for the selected LEB (0 on success or a negative errno from that function, not only -ENOSPC). Under c->lp_mutex it scans every LPT LEB (each entry is asserted not to be in 'tgc' state): it skips the LEB that is the node head (c->nhead_lnum) and any LEB whose free plus dirty space equals leb_size (nothing clean to preserve, so it is not worth collecting), and among the others picks the one with the largest dirty space, requiring dirty to be strictly greater than the running maximum that starts at 0; so a LEB with zero dirty space is never selected, and if every candidate has dirty == 0 (or all are skipped) the function returns -ENOSPC. The mutex is released before lpt_gc_lnum is called.
note: slice cut head (function at 1150-1169, slice 1027-1286). reviewers all right: original (lpt_gc_lnum's own errors are returned, 1168); round 2 (the skip test is free + dirty == leb_size, 1158); round 15 (the strict '>' against an initial 0 at 1160 means a zero-dirty LEB is never selected and -ENOSPC is returned).

name: mount_ubifs
prose: Precondition: c is a struct ubifs_info whose mount options have been parsed and whose volume information and vfs_sb are set (ubifs/super.c:1200-1602, static int mount_ubifs(struct ubifs_info *c); the packet name ubifs_mount does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 on success (line 1568, with the filesystem added to ubifs_infos and c->mounting cleared) or a negative errno at 1601 after the unwinding below. It sets ro_mount from the superblock flags and probing from SB_SILENT, then runs, with failure paths shown: init_constants_early and ubifs_debugging_init (their errors are returned directly, without cleanup labels, at 1212 and 1216); ubifs_sysfs_register (error: out_debugging); check_volume_empty; -EROFS if the volume is empty and the mount or media is read-only, or if a read-write mount is asked on read-only media (error: out_free); allocation of bottom_up_buf, sbuf, ileb_buf (read-write), write_reserve_buf (read-write) with -ENOMEM; bulk-read init; authentication init (-EINVAL if auth_key_name is set but authentication is not built in); ubifs_read_superblock (out_auth); -ENOTSUPP if the superblock's default compressor is not compiled in; init_constants_sb; allocation of cbuf and write buffers; creation of the background thread for read-write mounts; ubifs_read_master (out_master), init_constants_master, setting need_recovery if the master node is marked dirty; for a writable mount needing recovery ubifs_recover_inl_heads; ubifs_lpt_init; the space-fix-up; writing the master node with the dirty flag when no recovery is needed; the offline-signed-image HMAC update and superblock write; dbg_check_idx_size; ubifs_replay_journal (out_journal); ubifs_mount_orphans; then for read-write mounts check_free_space, a log-space check with ubifs_consolidate_log, and either recovery (ubifs_recover_size, ubifs_rcvry_gc_commit) or take_gc_lnum plus ubifs_leb_unmap of the GC LEB, and dbg_check_lprops; for read-only mounts needing recovery ubifs_recover_size, otherwise take_gc_lnum. It then adds c to the global ubifs_infos list, completes recovery for read-write mounts (need_recovery cleared) or reports it deferred for read-only ones, runs dbg_check_filesystem (error: out_infos), sets up debugfs, clears c->mounting and logs the mounted volume and geometry. Unwinding: out_infos removes c from the list; out_orphans frees orphans; out_journal destroys the journal; out_lpt frees the LPT; out_master frees the master nodes and stops the background thread; out_wbufs frees write buffers; out_cbuf frees cbuf; out_auth exits authentication; out_free frees write_reserve_buf, bulk-read buffer, ileb_buf, sbuf, bottom_up_buf, sup_node and unregisters sysfs; out_debugging exits debugging; the failure value err is returned.
note: packet name ubifs_mount does not exist; the slice 1290-1567 is the middle of mount_ubifs (super.c:1200-1602; slice cut head and tail), so FIXED under the real name. Only mechanical reviewers.

name: vboxsf_dirinfo
prose: Precondition: root is the shared-folder root id, handle an open directory handle, parsed_path is a shfl_string pattern or NULL, flags are the list flags, index the resume point (entry index to continue from), buf_len points to a u32 holding the size in bytes of the output buffer buf (a struct shfl_dirinfo area), and file_count points to a u32 (vboxsf/vboxsf_wrappers.c:250-292, int vboxsf_dirinfo(u32 root, u64 handle, struct shfl_string *parsed_path, u32 flags, u32 index, u32 *buf_len, struct shfl_dirinfo *buf, u32 *file_count); the packet name vboxsf_list does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 on success, 1 at the end of the directory, or a negative errno (per the comment at line 249); at its single return (291) both output counters are always written: *buf_len = the host-updated byte count (parms.cb) and *file_count = the number of entries returned. It fills a shfl_list parameter block (root, handle, flags, cb = *buf_len, the pattern path as a kernel input buffer or an empty input buffer when parsed_path is NULL, buf as a kernel output buffer of size *buf_len, resume_point = index, file_count = 0 as an output-only field) and calls vboxsf_call(SHFL_FN_LIST, ..., &status). If the call returned -ENODATA and the host status is VERR_NO_MORE_FILES, err becomes 1 (end of directory); any other result of vboxsf_call is returned as is. The host status value is read only when err == -ENODATA; it is not otherwise examined.
note: packet name vboxsf_list does not exist; the real function is vboxsf_dirinfo (vboxsf_wrappers.c:250-292); the slice 257-371 starts inside it (slice cut head) and continues into other wrappers. Mechanical reviewers only; the earlier prose was for a function of another name.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE6(setxattrat, int, dfd, const char __user *, pathname, unsigned int, at_flags,
prose: Generated system call setxattrat(dfd, pathname, at_flags, name, uargs, usize) (xattr.c:719-741): returns -EINVAL if usize < XATTR_ARGS_SIZE_VER0 (730), -E2BIG if usize > PAGE_SIZE (732), the copy_struct_from_user error for the xattr_args block (-EFAULT or -E2BIG for non-zero trailing bytes), and otherwise path_setxattrat(dfd, pathname, at_flags, name, args.value, args.size, args.flags). path_setxattrat (xattr.c:679-717) returns -EINVAL if at_flags has bits other than AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW and AT_EMPTY_PATH; then setxattr_copy (xattr.c:604-627) returns -EINVAL if flags has bits other than XATTR_CREATE and XATTR_REPLACE, the import_xattr_name error (-ERANGE if the name is empty or too long, or the strncpy_from_user error), -E2BIG if size exceeds XATTR_SIZE_MAX, or the vmemdup_user error for the value (with kvalue left NULL). It then gets the file name with getname_maybe_null(pathname, at_flags) (a plain getname when AT_EMPTY_PATH is not set): with a NULL name and dfd >= 0 it uses the descriptor (-EBADF if dfd is not open; else file_setxattr, which needs write access to the mount via mnt_want_write_file and calls do_setxattr), otherwise filename_setxattr (lookup error, mnt_want_write error or the do_setxattr result, retried once on -ESTALE; the name is consumed). do_setxattr (629-638) sets POSIX ACLs through do_set_acl for names of POSIX ACL attributes and otherwise calls vfs_setxattr with the flags; its errors (permission, security hooks, -EOPNOTSUPP, -ENODATA for XATTR_REPLACE on a missing attribute, -EEXIST for XATTR_CREATE on an existing one, and similar) are returned as is. The kernel copy of the value is freed (kvfree) before returning.

name: xfs_ag_shrink_space
prose: Precondition: pag is the last allocation group of the filesystem (ASSERT), *tpp is the caller's active transaction, delta is the number of blocks to remove from the end of the AG (xfs/libxfs/xfs_ag.c:739-873, int xfs_ag_shrink_space(struct xfs_perag *pag, struct xfs_trans **tpp, xfs_extlen_t delta)). Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno; *tpp may have been rolled. Early returns without any change: the error of xfs_ialloc_read_agi (764) or xfs_alloc_read_agf (770); -EFSCORRUPTED (777, with the AGF marked sick) if the AGF and AGI lengths differ; -EINVAL (780) if delta >= the AG length; the error of xfs_ialloc_check_shrink (788) if the last inode cluster could overlap the new end. Then it frees the per-AG reservation (xfs_ag_resv_free) and tries to allocate exactly the last delta blocks with xfs_alloc_vextent_exact_bno; no allocation (agbno == NULLAGBLOCK) becomes -ENOSPC. On an allocation error it holds the AGF and AGI buffers, rolls the transaction (a roll error is returned at 818 and the per-AG reservation is then NOT re-initialised), rejoins the buffers and goes to resv_init_out, which calls xfs_ag_resv_init and returns the original error if that succeeds (866-868). On success of the allocation it reduces the AGI and AGF lengths by delta and calls xfs_ag_resv_init: if that fails the lengths are restored and, when the error is not -ENOSPC, it goes to resv_err (warning 'Error %d reserving per-AG metadata reserve pool.' and xfs_force_shutdown(SHUTDOWN_CORRUPT_INCORE), returning that error, 872); when it is -ENOSPC the blocks are returned with xfs_free_extent_later (an error there also goes to resv_err), the deferred operations are finished (xfs_defer_finish; its error is returned at 850), error is set to -ENOSPC and resv_init_out runs, so a reservation that cannot be re-established gives -ENOSPC. When the reservation succeeds it updates the perag block count and inode range, logs the AGI and AGF length fields and returns 0 (863). The failure to re-initialise the per-AG reservation at resv_init_out also triggers the warning and forced shutdown (869-872), with err2 returned.
note: slice cut head (function at 739-873, slice 766-978). reviewer round 15 right: the warning and forced shutdown at resv_err (869-872) are also reached when xfs_ag_resv_init fails with a non-ENOSPC error (835-836) or when xfs_free_extent_later fails (840-841), not only from the final re-init at resv_init_out.

name: xfs_allocbt_maxlevels_ondisk
prose: Precondition: none; no parameters (xfs/libxfs/xfs_alloc_btree.c:579-591, unsigned int xfs_allocbt_maxlevels_ondisk(void)). Postcondition: returns xfs_btree_compute_maxlevels(minrecs, XFS_MAX_FREESP_RECORDS) at line 590, the largest height a free-space btree can ever have on disk, computed for the smallest legal block geometry. blocklen is the smaller of (XFS_MIN_BLOCKSIZE - XFS_BTREE_SBLOCK_LEN) and (XFS_MIN_CRC_BLOCKSIZE - XFS_BTREE_SBLOCK_CRC_LEN), i.e. the usable bytes in the smallest non-CRC and CRC block; minrecs[0] is half of xfs_allocbt_block_maxrecs(blocklen, true) (leaf records of sizeof(xfs_alloc_rec_t)) and minrecs[1] is half of xfs_allocbt_block_maxrecs(blocklen, false) (node entries of key plus pointer size); XFS_MAX_FREESP_RECORDS is (XFS_MAX_AG_BLOCKS + 1) / 2, the number of records when every other block of the largest AG is free. The numeric result depends on those header constants and on xfs_btree_compute_maxlevels, which I did not evaluate, so no specific number is claimed here (the earlier prose and reviewers disagreed on 6, 7 and 8). The function reads no mutable state and has no side effects.

The earlier prose said 'returns 7' and reviewers disputed the value (6, 7 or 8) because the record bound XFS_MAX_FREESP_RECORDS (xfs_alloc_btree.c:575) depends on XFS_MAX_AG_BLOCKS; I did not compute it and removed the numeric claim. name: xfs_attr_set_iter
prose: Precondition: attr points to a valid xfs_attr_intent whose xattri_da_args is valid and whose xattri_dela_state names the current step of the attribute set/replace/remove state machine; called repeatedly by the deferred-operation code, once per transaction, until the state is XFS_DAS_DONE (xfs/libxfs/xfs_attr.c:810-951, int xfs_attr_set_iter(struct xfs_attr_intent *attr)). Postcondition: performs one or more steps for the current state and returns 0 (continue or done, with the state advanced) or a negative errno; the state is updated in place and is not reverted on errors, and some error returns happen after the state has changed. Return/exits by state: XFS_DAS_UNINIT: ASSERT and -EFSCORRUPTED; XFS_DAS_SF_ADD, LEAF_ADD, NODE_ADD: return xfs_attr_sf_addname, xfs_attr_leaf_addname or xfs_attr_node_addname (those set their own next state). SF_REMOVE, LEAF_REMOVE: call xfs_attr_sf_removename/xfs_attr_leaf_removename and set the state to xfs_attr_complete_op(attr, xfs_attr_init_add_state(args)) regardless of the error; the error is then returned at 950. NODE_REMOVE: xfs_attr_node_removename_setup; -ENOATTR during recovery is treated as success and completes the removal step, any other error is returned at 849 without changing the state, else the state becomes NODE_REMOVE_RMT (or the following state when there is no remote value). LEAF_SET_RMT/NODE_SET_RMT: xfs_attr_rmtval_find_space (error returned, state unchanged), state incremented, then falls through; ALLOC_RMT: xfs_attr_rmtval_alloc (error returned), and either break when the state is DONE or loop back through next_state. LEAF_REPLACE/NODE_REPLACE: xfs_attr3_leaf_flipflags (error returned) then the state is incremented. LEAF_REMOVE_OLD/NODE_REMOVE_OLD: xfs_attr_restore_rmt_blk, then, if there is a remote value, xfs_attr_rmtval_invalidate (error returned without advancing) else a first state increment, then a second increment and loop. LEAF_REMOVE_RMT/NODE_REMOVE_RMT: xfs_attr_rmtval_remove; -EAGAIN is turned into 0 and the function returns (breaks) with the state unchanged so that it is called again, other errors are returned, success increments the state. LEAF_REMOVE_ATTR: xfs_attr_leaf_remove_attr, then the state becomes the completion state whatever the result. NODE_REMOVE_ATTR: xfs_attr_node_remove_attr then, if that succeeded, xfs_attr_leaf_shrink, then the completion state. Any other state ASSERTs and falls out. At 949-950 it traces the new state and returns error.
note: slice cut head (function at 810-951, slice 783-1033). reviewers right: original (xfs_attr_rmtval_remove -EAGAIN is converted to 0 at 913-915 without advancing the state, so 'success advances the state' is not always true); round 2 (several returns, e.g. the SF/LEAF_REMOVE cases, set xattri_dela_state to the completion state even when error is non-zero, 831-837 and 933-934, 941-942, and the REMOVE_OLD/SET_RMT cases increment the state before later steps fail). Only the visible function was read; the callee functions were not.

name: xfs_bmap_add_extent_unwritten_real
prose: Precondition: tp is the running transaction, ip an inode whose fork whichfork contains an extent PREV (at the cursor icur) that fully covers the range of new and whose state (written or unwritten) differs from new->br_state; *curp is the fork's bmap btree cursor or NULL when the fork is in extent format; new has a real (non-delayed) start block (ASSERTs); logflagsp is writable (xfs/libxfs/xfs_bmap.c:2008-2562, int xfs_bmap_add_extent_unwritten_real(struct xfs_trans *tp, xfs_inode_t *ip, int whichfork, struct xfs_iext_cursor *icur, struct xfs_btree_cur **curp, xfs_bmbt_irec_t *new, int *logflagsp); the item was marked dropped as not-in-slice but the function is real, and the slice 2061-2323 is its middle, slice cut head and tail). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno at the single 'return error' (2558) after the done label; *logflagsp is set to 0 at entry and ORed with the logging flags (rval, plus those from an extent-to-btree conversion) at done on every path, including failures. Method: it reads PREV and its left and right neighbours (LEFT, RIGHT) and sets state bits: LEFT_FILLING / RIGHT_FILLING when new starts / ends exactly at PREV's start / end, and LEFT_CONTIG / RIGHT_CONTIG when the neighbour is a real extent that is adjacent in file offset and disk block, has the same state as new, is on the same realtime group, and the merged length does not exceed XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN (also for the all-three-merged case). It then handles these combinations: (1) fills all of PREV and merges with both neighbours (removes two incore extents, updates LEFT; with a btree cursor it deletes RIGHT and PREV records and updates LEFT); (2) fills all of PREV and merges left; (3) fills all of PREV and merges right; (4) fills all of PREV with no merge (changes PREV's state); (5) fills the first part of PREV and merges left; (6) fills the first part with no merge (PREV shrinks and new is inserted before it); (7) fills the last part and merges right; (8) fills the last part with no merge; (9) fills a middle part (PREV is split into three, increasing the extent count by 2). The cases with a contiguity bit but not matching a filling pattern (LEFT_FILLING|LEFT_CONTIG|RIGHT_CONTIG, RIGHT_FILLING|LEFT_CONTIG|RIGHT_CONTIG, LEFT_FILLING|RIGHT_CONTIG, RIGHT_FILLING|LEFT_CONTIG, LEFT_CONTIG|RIGHT_CONTIG, LEFT_CONTIG, RIGHT_CONTIG) are impossible (ASSERT(0)). With a btree cursor each case does record lookups, deletes, updates and inserts: a lookup that does not find the expected record (i != 1, or i != 0 for an insert position) marks the btree sick and gives -EFSCORRUPTED, and any btree call error goes to done; the in-memory extent list and if_nextents were already changed before these btree operations, so an error leaves them updated. After the switch it records the rmap change (xfs_rmap_convert_extent), converts the fork to a btree if now needed (xfs_bmap_extents_to_btree, whose error goes to done), clears cur->bc_bmap.allocated and stores *curp.
note: item named xfs_bmap_add_extent_unwritten_real marked dropped as 'not in slice'; the function is real (xfs_bmap.c:2008-2562) and the slice 2061-2323 is its middle, so FIXED per rule 6. The earlier prose (not shown to me beyond its first sentence) was dropped; the description above covers the whole function but the numbering (1)-(9) is mine. Helper functions (xfs_btree_* and xfs_iext_*) were not read.

name: xfs_bmap_extsize_align
prose: Precondition: mp is the mount; gotp is the extent after the request (it may be the end-of-file record) and prevp the extent before it (offset NULLFILEOFF when there is none); extsz is the extent size hint and must be non-zero (it is a divisor); rt, eof, delay and convert are flags; offp and lenp point to the requested file offset and length (xfs/libxfs/xfs_bmap.c:2817-2988, static int xfs_bmap_extsize_align(xfs_mount_t *mp, xfs_bmbt_irec_t *gotp, xfs_bmbt_irec_t *prevp, xfs_extlen_t extsz, int rt, int eof, int delay, int convert, xfs_fileoff_t *offp, xfs_extlen_t *lenp); the packet name xfs_file_alloc_size_align does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 with *offp and *lenp adjusted, or -EINVAL with them unchanged; the return statements are 0 at 2839 (convert is set: nothing is changed), 0 at 2852 (the request lies entirely inside gotp and neither delay nor eof is set: unchanged), -EINVAL at 2945 and 2970 (realtime only) and 0 at 2987 with the new values stored. Computation: it rounds the start down to a multiple of extsz (extending the length by the amount moved), rounds the length up to a multiple of extsz, and reduces the length by extsz steps while it exceeds XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN. It then moves the start forward to the end of the previous extent if the aligned start (when it was moved) lies before it, moves the start back so the end does not run into the next extent (not before offset 0), repeats the previous-extent check, and, if the end still overlaps the next extent, shortens the length to end exactly at the next extent. For a realtime inode whose resulting length is not a multiple of the realtime extent size it removes blocks by moving the start up, or pulling the end in, or trimming the length, and returns -EINVAL if the result would not cover the original request [orig_off, orig_end) (checked at 2942-2945 and 2969-2970); for non-realtime inodes the cover property is only ASSERTed (debug builds), including an allowance when the length was cut to XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN, so the result may not cover the whole original request in that case. The function takes no locks or references and only writes *offp and *lenp.
note: packet name xfs_file_alloc_size_align does not exist; the described function is xfs_bmap_extsize_align (xfs_bmap.c:2817-2988); the slice 2841-3141 starts inside it (slice cut head). Mechanical reviewers only. The earlier prose said the result always covers the original request; for non-realtime inodes that is only asserted (2972-2975), and the length can be capped at XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN (2881-2882), so it is qualified here.

name: xfs_bmap_del_extent_real
prose: Precondition: ip is an inode, tp the running transaction, icur an extent cursor positioned at the extent got that fully contains del, cur is the bmap btree cursor or NULL when the fork is in extent format, del is the non-empty range being removed (must satisfy got.br_startoff <= del->br_startoff and got's end >= del's end, ASSERTed), logflagsp is writable, whichfork is the fork, bflags the XFS_BMAPI_* flags (xfs/libxfs/xfs_bmap.c:4909-5162, int xfs_bmap_del_extent_real(xfs_inode_t *ip, xfs_trans_t *tp, struct xfs_iext_cursor *icur, struct xfs_btree_cur *cur, xfs_bmbt_irec_t *del, int *logflagsp, int whichfork, uint32_t bflags)). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno; *logflagsp is zeroed at entry, set to XFS_ILOG_CORE once past the early check and OR-ed with the fork's extent logging flag when no btree is used. Early returns: -ENOSPC at 4961 when the transaction has no block reservation (t_blk_res == 0), the fork is in extent format at its maximum extent count and del is strictly inside got (so the removal would split the extent and force a btree conversion), with *logflagsp still 0; with a cursor, the result of xfs_bmbt_lookup_eq(cur, &got) is returned if it fails and -EFSCORRUPTED (btree marked sick) if the record is not found (4972-4978). By how del sits in got: whole extent (the incore entry is removed and if_nextents decremented; with a cursor xfs_btree_delete, a miss gives -EFSCORRUPTED); first part (got is moved up and shortened; btree record updated); last part (got shortened; btree record updated); middle (got shortened to the part before del, a new extent for the part after is inserted; with a cursor the record is updated, the cursor incremented and the new record inserted: an -ENOSPC from the insert is undone by re-looking up got, restoring the original btree record and incore extent, setting *logflagsp = 0 and returning -ENOSPC; other errors are returned as is and an insert miss gives -EFSCORRUPTED). Btree operations are only done when cur is non-NULL. After the switch it removes the reverse mapping (xfs_rmap_unmap_extent) and, unless XFS_BMAPI_REMAP is set, schedules the blocks to be freed: refcount decrease for a reflink inode's data fork, xfs_bmap_free_rtblocks for a realtime fork without rtgroups, otherwise xfs_free_extent_later (with SKIP_DISCARD for NODISCARD or unwritten extents, and the REALTIME flag for realtime); an error from the free step is returned (5147). Finally it subtracts the block count from ip->i_nblocks and, unless REMAP, adjusts the quota (realtime or normal block count) and returns 0.
note: item xfs_bmap_del_extent_real marked dropped; the real function is xfs_bmap.c:4909-5162 and the slice 4680-4933 is the end of an earlier function plus the head of this one (slice cut). FIXED per rule 6. reviewers: original right (the btree is updated only when cur is non-NULL); round 2 describes the copy-on-write/delayed variant (xfs_bmap_del_extent_delay), a different function; this one has no COW-fork-only path. Helper functions were not read.
