On that path the access/delegation checks and nfsrv_openctrl run only while nd_repstat is 0, vp is unlocked, stp is freed if still non-NULL, the parent's post-op attributes are fetched when nd_repstat is 0, and if nd_repstat is still 0 the reply (stateid, change info, rflags, attribute bitmap, delegation information) is marshalled and *vpp = vp (the caller then owns that reference), otherwise a non-NULL vp gets vrele; dirp is vrele'd if non-NULL and both ACL buffers are freed. nd_repstat values set in this code include NFSERR_INVAL (bad access or deny value, create with a claim other than null, exclusive create in a named-attribute directory, time_access_set with exclusive-41, create with the FH-style claims), NFSERR_BADXDR, EEXIST (guarded create of an existing file, or exclusive-create verifier mismatch), NFSERR_PERM (doomed vnode in the FH claims), NFSERR_ISDIR or NFSERR_SYMLINK for a non-regular file, and statuses from nfsrv_opencheck, nfsvno_namei, nfsvno_open, nfsvno_accchk, nfsvno_getattr and nfsrv_openctrl.
note: Slice is inside nfsrvd_open (:3054); fixed under real name. Reviewer r15 (lock-state storage is allocated and freed here, not caller-provided) right (:3099, :3471). Old prose also wrongly said the function returns a nonzero status stored in nd_repstat for protocol errors: it returns 0 for those (nd_repstat only, :3096-3097, :3246-3250) and said 'in every path' it releases everything, which only holds with the per-path qualifications above.

name: nfsrvd_deallocate
prose: The slice covers the tail of nfsrvd_deallocate(nd, isdgram, vp, exp) at nfs_nfsdserv.c:5872-5972 and the start of the next function, so it is fixed under the real name of the NFSv4.2 DEALLOCATE service. Precondition: nd holds the request positioned at the DEALLOCATE arguments (stateid, offset, length), vp is a locked, referenced vnode that this function takes over, exp is the export. Return paths: (1) if NFSM_DISSECT cannot obtain the arguments it goes to nfsmout, does vput(vp) and returns that error (EBADRPC); (2) otherwise it always reaches the end, does vput(vp) once and returns 0, with the outcome in nd->nd_repstat. The statuses, evaluated in this order while nd_repstat is still 0: NFSERR_NOTSUPP for a DS server (set before any check), NFSERR_FBIG when off < 0 or the end offset exceeds NFSRV_MAXFILESIZE, NFSERR_INVAL when len == 0 or the end offset is below the start (a negative len is replaced by OFF_MAX), NFSERR_WRONGTYPE when vp is not a regular file, the status of nfsvno_getattr (which is called regardless, fetching the owner), the nfsvno_accchk(VWRITE) result when the file owner differs from the caller or the export has strict access checking, the nfsrv_lockctrl result when the stateid is not the all-ones/0x55555555 proxy stateid, and finally the status of nfsvno_deallocate. If nd_repstat is 0 at the end the deallocation was applied by nfsvno_deallocate; the function itself builds no reply data.
note: Slice 5945-6207 is the tail of nfsrvd_deallocate (:5872) plus the start of nfsrvd_copy_file_range; fixed under real name instead of dropping (HAND_METHOD rule 6). Old prose omitted NFSERR_NOTSUPP/FBIG/INVAL and said the function returns the mbuf parse error 'when it completes' wrongly worded; checked against :5886-5971.

name: nfsrvd_compound
prose: Static function nfsrvd_compound(nd, isdgram, tag, taglen, minorvers) at nfs_nfsdsocket.c:708-1444 (the slice cut the head). It returns void; its results are the reply built in nd and nd->nd_repstat. Entry: nd holds a dissected NFSv4 COMPOUND request; taglen < 0 means that parsing the tag/minor version failed earlier. The function first takes either the V4 root lock (nfsv4_lock, then it may update the stable-storage file and expire clients and releases the lock with a reference count) or only a reference count (nfsv4_getref), and in every case releases that reference (nfsv4_relref) at the exit label nfsmout. Flow: if taglen < 0 it sets error to EBADRPC and jumps to nfsmout before the tag is copied, so no tag is written in that case; otherwise it copies the tag into the reply and reserves the result-count word, reads the operation count, sets nd_repstat to NFSERR_MINORVERMISMATCH (and runs zero operations) for an unsupported or out-of-range minor version, then loops over the operations. For each it writes the opcode and either a status word or, on success, 0; the status is nfsd_errmap(nd) for a nonzero nd_repstat, and the loop stops after the first operation that leaves nd_repstat nonzero. nd_repstat is set by this function to NFSERR_OPILLEGAL (opcode out of range or not valid for the negotiated minor version), NFSERR_MOVED (a referral on the current file handle for an operation other than GETATTR that allows it), NFSERR_SEQUENCEPOS, NFSERR_OPNOTINSESS or NFSERR_NOTONLYOP (NFSv4.1 sequencing rules), NFSERR_RESOURCE (only at the first operation, when the reply cache is flooded or malloc/mbuf memory is near its limit), NFSERR_NOFILEHANDLE, NFSERR_RESTOREFH, NFSERR_XDEV, NFSERR_PERM (vnode lock failure) or a status returned by file-handle conversion or the operation routine. An error value returned by an operation routine is mapped: EBADRPC or NFSERR_BADXDR becomes nd_repstat = NFSERR_BADXDR, any other value is copied into nd_repstat. A failure of NFSM_DISSECT or of file-handle parsing, or taglen < 0, reaches nfsmout with error EBADRPC, and nfsmout then sets nd_repstat = NFSERR_BADXDR (an error of any other kind there is only logged); nd_repstat is never left as EBADRPC. Only when an operation returns ERELOOKUP is there a rollback: nd_md and nd_dpos are reset to the values saved for that operation, the partial reply is trimmed with nfsm_trimtrailing, and the operation is retried (ND_ERELOOKUP set); ordinary failed operations are not rolled back, their opcode and error status remain in the reply. At nfsmout it writes the final reply word (the count of operations answered, retops, or two zero words when taglen < 0), vrele()s the current file-handle vnode and the saved-file-handle vnode if non-NULL, restores nd_cred if root credentials were substituted for a machine-credential operation (and frees the root credential), and releases the V4 root reference.
note: Slice cut head (function starts :708); fixed under real name. Reviewer r15 (tag not copied when taglen < 0; EBADRPC returned before nfsm_strtom) right (:842-847): tag sentence fixed. Old prose also wrong on: final nd_repstat 'EBADRPC' (code maps to NFSERR_BADXDR, :1370-1371, :1419-1420) and 'reply rolled back to saved cursors' for failing operations (only for ERELOOKUP retry, :1379-1394).

name: nfsrv_lockctrl
prose: Function nfsrv_lockctrl(vp, new_stpp, new_lopp, cfp, clientid, stateidp, exp, nd, p) at nfs_nfsdstate.c:1816-2552 (the slice cut the head and ends inside the next function, nfsrv_opencheck). Precondition: vp is a locked vnode (it is unlocked and re-locked internally only when local locking is enabled), *new_stpp describes the operation (flags NFSLCK_LOCK, UNLOCK, TEST, CHECK or SETATTR), *new_lopp is non-NULL because the lock range is read for LOCK, UNLOCK, TEST and CHECK, and for the LOCK/UNLOCK cases both structures should be malloc'd (a TEST/CHECK caller may use stack structures, since they are not consumed); the caller does not hold the NFS state lock. The function returns 0 on success or an error value; the error is the first of: the result of nfsrv_checkrestart, NFSERR_RESOURCE (LOCK and the state limit exceeded), errors found while looking up the client and stateid (nfsrv_getclient, nfsrv_getstate, NFSERR_BADSTATEID for a wrong-type or wrong-file stateid, nfsrv_checkseqid, NFSERR_BADSEQID for an existing lock owner on NFSv4.0, NFSERR_OLDSTATEID), nfsrv_checkgrace, NFSERR_NOGRACE, then nd->nd_repstat or the error from nfsrv_getlockfh/nfsrv_getlockfile/nfsrv_locallock, NFSERR_EXPIRED (no lockfile and not LockT; for CHECK/SETATTR without a special stateid NFSERR_BADSTATEID, and 0 for LockT or a special stateid), NFSERR_OPENMODE (access bits do not match the open, or a conflicting deny), NFSERR_PERM, NFSERR_DENIED, NFSERR_RECLAIMCONFLICT or NFSERR_LOCKED for a conflicting lock, errors from nfsrv_cleandeleg/nfsrv_delegconflict, and NFSERR_SERVERFAULT if the vnode is doomed after re-locking. Success effects: for UNLOCK nfsrv_updatelock removes the range and the stateid seqid is advanced (skipping 0 on NFSv4.1+); for LOCK with an existing lock owner nfsrv_updatelock adds the range and the seqid is advanced; for an open-to-lock-owner LOCK the new lock owner nfsstate is initialised, linked into the client's state hash and the open's list, the reply-cache entry is referenced (nfsrvd_refcache) and *new_lopp and *new_stpp are set to NULL; with local locking, the local locks are committed or the local unlock is done; TEST and CHECK create and change no lock or open state (they renew the client lease and may delay a delegation timeout), SETATTR calls nfsrv_cleandeleg and then returns 0 unless it was combined with CHECK and open, lock or delegation state still exists, in which case checking continues. When a conflicting lock is found and cfp is non-NULL (and nfsrv_clientconflict returned 0), cfp is filled with it. On every return the NFS state lock has been released, the V4 root lock is released if it was taken (haslock), vp is re-locked if the function unlocked it, and other_lop is freed unless it was consumed. On an error return with local locking active, local locks are rolled back and nfsrv_unlocklf is called, with one exception: when a conflicting lock is found and nfsrv_clientconflict returns 2 (NFSERR_PERM), the code at the conflict exit rolls back and unlocks only when that return was 0, so that path returns without the rollback and nfsrv_unlocklf.
note: Slice cut head (function starts :1816); fixed under real name. Reviewer r15 (ret == 2 / NFSERR_PERM path skips local-lock rollback and nfsrv_unlocklf) right (:2449-2470, rollback conditional on ret == 0): prose qualified. Old prose also wrong: 'takes a reference on its open owner' (code calls nfsrvd_refcache on the reply-cache entry, :2507), 'a test/check changes no state' (lease renewal, delegation timeout), 'on error any local locks are rolled back' without the exception.

name: nfsrv_openctrl
prose: The slice is the middle of nfsrv_openctrl(nd, vp, new_stpp, clientid, stateidp, delegstateidp, rflagsp, exp, p, filerev) at nfs_nfsdstate.c:2813-3452 (there is no function nfsrv_open in this file), so it is fixed under its real name. Precondition: *new_stpp is a malloc'd nfsstate describing the open request (access/deny bits, claim flags, owner), vp is the file's vnode, and the caller holds no NFS state lock. The function allocates a nfslockfile, an open nfsstate and a delegation nfsstate (and a scratch buffer) up front. Return value: 0 or an error. Error returns: NFSERR_EXPIRED if nfsrv_checkrestart fails, if nfsrv_getclient fails, if a claim-delegate-current has no matching current delegation or asks for write access on a read delegation, or if a claim-delegate-previous finds no old delegation; the error of nfsrv_getlockfh or nfsrv_getlockfile; NFSERR_PERM, NFSERR_RECLAIMCONFLICT or NFSERR_SHAREDENIED when nfsrv_clientconflict reports a share conflict (return 2, reclaim, or otherwise); the error of nfsrv_delegconflict when it fails other than with a retry (-1 restarts at tryagain); and NFSERR_RECLAIMCONFLICT when a delegation reclaim finds an existing delegation or open for the client and owner. When it returns 0 it has either created a new open for the file (new owner, or existing owner with no open for this file, or by upgrading the open of the same owner and file with the new share bits), or converted an unconfirmed owner's open to the new request (setting NFSV4OPEN_RESULTCONFIRM in *rflagsp), or, for claim-previous with a delegation, created the delegation plus an associated open (or moved an old delegation to the current list), and it copies the open's stateid into *stateidp; delegation issuance goes through nfsrv_issuedelegation and sets delegation bits in *rflagsp and the stateid in *delegstateidp. A new open owner consumes *new_stpp, which is then set to NULL; the NFSv4.1+ first-open case also writes a stable-storage timestamp after the locks are released. On every return the NFS state lock and (if it was taken, haslock) the V4 root lock are released, and the unused preallocated nfslockfile, open and delegation structures and the scratch buffer are freed; on the early restart-check failure only the scratch buffer pointer (NULL at that point) is freed.
note: Slice 3150-3438 is the middle of nfsrv_openctrl (:2813); fixed under the real name instead of dropped (HAND_METHOD rule 6). Old prose said 'preallocated new_open/new_deleg/new_stp held by caller' (only *new_stpp comes from the caller) and 'on failure preallocated entries freed' (only the new_open/new_deleg/new_lfp allocated here, not new_stp). Claims in the new prose checked against :2829-3451; the per-case state building (:3117-3421) is summarised, not enumerated.

name: nfsrv_checkreclaimcomplete
prose: Function nfsrv_checkreclaimcomplete(nd, onefs) at nfs_nfsdstate.c:6146-6175 (the slice also contains neighbouring functions). Precondition: nd->nd_sessionid identifies the session to look up (it need not exist) and onefs is any int; the caller holds neither the NFS state lock nor a session-hash lock. The function takes the NFS state lock and the session-hash lock for nd_sessionid and then looks up the session with nfsrv_findsession. Return paths: (1) no session matches: both locks are released and NFSERR_BADSESSION is returned, with no client state changed; (2) onefs is nonzero: LCL_RECLAIMONEFS is set in the session's client flags and 0 is returned (LCL_RECLAIMCOMPLETE is not examined); (3) onefs is zero and LCL_RECLAIMCOMPLETE is already set: NFSERR_COMPLETEALREADY is returned with no change; (4) onefs is zero and LCL_RECLAIMCOMPLETE is not set: it sets LCL_RECLAIMCOMPLETE, calls nfsrv_markreclaim on the client and returns 0. In paths (2)-(4) both locks are released before returning (path (1) releases them before its own return), so the caller holds no lock afterwards.
note: nfs_nfsdstate.c:6146-6175. Reviewers o1 (precondition requires an existing session, code returns NFSERR_BADSESSION) and r2 (contract omits state effects) both right and already reflected in prose (:6157-6171); prose re-checked and tightened. Contract stays empty (global lock/state).

name: smbfs_writevnode
prose: Function smbfs_writevnode(vp, uiop, cred, ioflag) at smbfs_io.c:249-309 (the slice starts after its head and also contains smbfs_doio and following code; the real name is smbfs_writevnode, not smbfs_write). Precondition: vp is a vnode on an SMBFS mount, uiop describes the write (uio_offset, uio_resid, iovec and uio_td set by the caller), cred is the caller's credential. Return paths in code order: (1) EIO if vp->v_type is not VREG; (2) EINVAL if uio_offset is negative; (3) if ioflag has IO_APPEND or IO_SYNC and np->n_flag has NMODIFIED, it removes the attribute-cache entry and calls smbfs_vinvalbuf, returning that call's error if it is nonzero; then, if IO_APPEND is set, uio_offset is set to np->n_size; (4) 0 if uio_resid is 0 (checked after step 3, so the append offset has already been set and the cache invalidated); (5) the error of vn_rlimit_fsize if nonzero; (6) otherwise it allocates a smb_cred, calls smb_write and frees the smb_cred, and, if smb_write returned 0 and the final uio_offset exceeds np->n_size, sets np->n_size to it and calls vnode_pager_setsize; it returns smb_write's error (0 on success). The smb_cred is allocated and freed only on path (6), so the caller gains and loses no reference or lock in any path. On an smb_write error the uio may already have been partly advanced and np->n_size is not updated.
note: Slice cut head; real name smbfs_writevnode (:250). Old prose said the temporary smb_cred is allocated and freed 'inside the call' for all paths (only on the smb_write path) and used the wrong function name; it did not mention the resid == 0 check coming after the append/offset and invalidation steps (:270-290). No reviewer reasons beyond name mismatch.

name: tarfs_strtofflags
prose: Function tarfs_strtofflags(str, end) at tarfs_subr.c:502-537 (the slice cut the head; there is no function named tarfs_parse_flags). Precondition: str points to a NUL-terminated string and end is a non-NULL pointer to a char * (the function reads *end at its exit, so end itself must not be NULL; the pointed-to value may be NULL). It walks str as comma-separated tokens; a token is scanned character by character and parsing stops (jump to the exit) at the first character that is not between 'a' and 'z' and is not a comma or NUL; otherwise the token is compared for exact equality against each name in the static tarfs_flags table (nodump, uchg, uappnd, opaque, uunlnk, arch, schg, sappnd, sunlnk) and, on the first exact match, its flag is OR'd into the result; if no table entry matches (this includes an empty token, e.g. a leading comma, doubled comma or trailing comma, because no table name is empty), parsing stops. Return value: the OR of the flags of the tokens fully matched before parsing stopped (0 if none or if str is empty); a token that caused the stop contributes nothing. At the exit, if *end is non-NULL on entry, it is set to the position in str where parsing stopped: the offending character of an invalid token, or the end of an unmatched token (the comma that follows it, or the terminating NUL if it was last), or the terminating NUL when the whole string was consumed; if *end is NULL on entry it is left unchanged. The result is a pointer into str, no memory is allocated or freed, and only debug logging has other effects.
note: Slice cut head; real name tarfs_strtofflags (:503). Old prose named it tarfs_parse_flags (no such function) and was otherwise accurate; checked against :510-536 (the trailing-comma case ends at the NUL). No reviewer reason beyond name mismatch.

name: tarfs_alloc_one
prose: The slice is the middle of the static function tarfs_alloc_one(tmp, blknump) at tarfs_vfsops.c:432-845 (there is no function tarfs_parse_header), so it is fixed under its real name. Precondition: tmp is an initialized tarfs mount whose backing tar file can be read, and *blknump is the block number of the next tar header to read. It reads one 512-byte header (looping back to 'again' after an extended header or a first zero block), and returns 0 on success or when the archive ends, otherwise a positive errno. Return paths: (1) a read error from tarfs_io_read_buf is returned as that errno, and a short read (fewer than 512 bytes for a header, or fewer than the extended-header size) gives EIO; (2) two consecutive all-zero blocks: tmp->nblocks is set, *blknump is set to TAR_EOF and 0 is returned (an extended header still held is freed); (3) header magic: a GNU tar header gives EFTYPE, any other non-ustar header gives EINVAL; a bad checksum gives EINVAL; an unparsable size or modification time gives EINVAL (an invalid mode becomes S_IRUSR, and an invalid uid or gid is replaced by the root's and clears the setuid or setgid bit, neither being an error); (4) a global extended header (typeflag 'g') is skipped by advancing past its data; a second extended header before a file header gives EFTYPE, and a malformed extended-header record (bad length, no '=' or a bad numeric value for size, GNU.sparse.* or SCHILY.fflags) or one that overruns the data gives EINVAL; (5) after the extended-header data is merged (path, linkpath, size, sparse fields, flags), an inconsistent sparse description gives EINVAL; the name comes from the extended header, or prefix/name from the header; tarfs_lookup_path failure gives EINVAL; a path that already exists is skipped (success) if the new entry is a directory, and gives EINVAL otherwise; (6) by typeflag it calls tarfs_alloc_node for a directory, regular file (plus tarfs_load_blockmap if sparse), hard link (EINVAL if the target is missing, not a regular file, or itself a link, and increments the target's link count), symbolic link (EINVAL if the target is empty), block or character device (EINVAL for an invalid major or minor), and EINVAL for any other typeflag, returning an error from tarfs_alloc_node or tarfs_load_blockmap unchanged; (7) on success it advances blknum by the data size in blocks, stores it in tmp->nblocks and *blknump, and returns 0. On every return other than the TAR_EOF return in (2), exthdr and the name buffer are freed; *blknump is not updated on errors, and a node created earlier in the call is not freed here.
note: Slice is inside tarfs_alloc_one (:433); fixed under real name instead of dropped (HAND_METHOD rule 6). The old prose said 'error EINVAL/EFTYPE and control jumps to cleanup, success allocates a node or skips' only; this version lists the paths (:456-845). Hand-checked that the GNU-tar branch tests magic twice (:489-490) but that does not change which errors are returned.

name: tarfs_readdir
prose: Static VOP_READDIR method tarfs_readdir(ap) at tarfs_vnops.c:307-508 (the slice starts before it and ends before its final return). Precondition: ap->a_vp is a tarfs vnode and ap->a_uio is a valid uio; when the '..' entry will be produced, the directory's tarfs_node has a non-NULL parent (MPASS); every child's name must fit in the dirent d_name field, but the only length assertion made is MPASS(tnp->namelen < sizeof(cde.d_name)) on the directory's own name, so the child names are not checked before the memcpy. Return paths: (1) ENOTDIR if a_vp is not a directory; (2) uio_offset == TARFS_COOKIE_EOF: sets *a_eofflag to 1 if non-NULL and returns 0 with uio_offset unchanged and no cookies; (3) a uiomove failure while writing '.' or '..' is returned at once, before the common exit (uio_offset, the saved resume state and *a_eofflag are not updated by that exit); (4) otherwise it writes '.' (when uio_offset is TARFS_COOKIE_DOT), then '..' (when uio_offset is TARFS_COOKIE_DOTDOT, including right after '.'), then the children in list order, taking the start child from the first child or, when resuming, from tarfs_lookup_dir for uio_offset (EINVAL if that lookup fails), and leaves through the common exit ('done'): a uiomove failure on a child gives that error; a child of unexpected vnode type panics; an entry that does not fit in uio_resid ends the loop with EINVAL if no entry has yet been written by this call (the count includes '.' and '..') and 0 otherwise. At the common exit, if no child is pending (the list is exhausted, the directory has no children, the failure was on the lookup, or the stop happened before any child was selected, which includes when '.' or '..' did not fit, so children may remain) it sets uio_offset to TARFS_COOKIE_EOF and the directory's lastcookie to 0 and lastnode to NULL; otherwise it saves the pending child's inode number and node as lastcookie/lastnode (uio_offset already holds that inode number). It sets *a_eofflag, if non-NULL, to 1 exactly when the error is 0 and no child is pending, and to 0 otherwise. When the error is 0 and both a_cookies and a_ncookies are non-NULL it allocates (M_WAITOK, M_TEMP) an array of ndirents off_t cookies, stores it in *a_cookies and the count in *a_ncookies, filling it with the successive resume offsets; the caller must free it, and the code asserts (MPASS) that the last cookie equals the final uio_offset. In the case of an empty directory where '..' was written, that entry is not counted in ndirents (the count is skipped when the first child is NULL).
note: tarfs_vnops.c:307-508. Reviewer o1 (EOF set and uio_offset EOF when '..' does not fit although list not exhausted; EINVAL omitted) right (:380-381, :453-469). Reviewer r2 (0/eofflag=1 also when '..' written and no children) right (:387-389, :462-465). Reviewer r15 (assertion is on tnp->namelen, the directory's name, not the child's) right (:434): precondition corrected. New observation: empty-directory case does not count '..' in ndirents (:388-393).

name: tmpfs_chtimes
prose: Function tmpfs_chtimes(vp, vap, cred, td) at tmpfs_subr.c:2286-2321 (the slice cut the head and also contains tmpfs_itimes and tmpfs_truncate). Precondition: vp is an exclusively locked vnode of a tmpfs mount (ASSERT_VOP_ELOCKED at entry and exit), vap points to an initialized vattr whose va_atime, va_mtime and va_birthtime tv_sec may be VNOVAL, and cred and td identify the caller. Return paths: (1) EROFS if the mount has MNT_RDONLY, with nothing modified; (2) EPERM if tn_flags has IMMUTABLE or APPEND, with nothing modified; (3) the nonzero error of vn_utimes_perm, with nothing modified; (4) otherwise 0, after: setting tn_accessed to true if va_atime.tv_sec is not VNOVAL; setting TMPFS_NODE_MODIFIED in tn_status if va_mtime.tv_sec or va_birthtime.tv_sec is not VNOVAL; calling tmpfs_itimes(vp, &va_atime, &va_mtime), which returns at once if tn_accessed is false and neither MODIFIED nor CHANGED is set, and otherwise, under the node lock, copies the given atime into tn_atime if tn_accessed is set, copies the given mtime into tn_mtime if MODIFIED is set (copying va_mtime as given, even when its tv_sec is VNOVAL, for instance when only the birth time was requested), sets tn_ctime to the current time if CHANGED is set, and clears MODIFIED, CHANGED and tn_accessed; and finally storing va_birthtime into tn_birthtime if its tv_sec is not VNOVAL. vp stays locked and the function acquires and releases no references or memory. The header comment says the caller should run tmpfs_update afterwards.
note: tmpfs_subr.c:2286-2321. Slice cut head (name outside slice). Old prose said tmpfs_itimes writes tn_atime/tn_mtime/tn_ctime for 'the flags set' (right) but did not mention the early return or that tn_mtime takes va_mtime verbatim; checked against :2344-2377. No reviewer disagreement.

name: tmpfs_rename
prose: Static VOP_RENAME method tmpfs_rename(v) at tmpfs_vnops.c:1048-1367 (the slice cut the head). Entry state assumed by the code: fdvp and fvp are referenced and not locked, tdvp and, if non-NULL, tvp are locked and referenced (they are released with vput at the end). The function takes the source directory lock itself when fdvp differs from both tdvp and tvp. Flags accepted are AT_RENAME_NOREPLACE and AT_RENAME_EXCHANGE; other flag bits give EOPNOTSUPP. Exit paths: (1) label out, reached for EXDEV (source or target on another mount), EOPNOTSUPP, and fvp == tvp (error 0, nothing renamed); (2) when fdvp must be locked and vn_lock(LK_NOWAIT) fails, tmpfs_rename_relock is called, and if it fails its error is returned directly from this function without the releases below; after a successful relock it returns EEXIST (if AT_RENAME_NOREPLACE was given and tvp exists, checked only in this relock path of this function) or 0 (if fvp == tvp) through out_locked; (3) label out_locked, which unlocks fdvp if this function locked it (fdvp differs from tdvp and tvp) and falls into out; used by EINVAL (source name is '.' or ISDOTDOT), ENOENT (source entry not found, or the target entry not found for exchange), EPERM (tvp node with NOUNLINK/IMMUTABLE/APPEND, tdvp with APPEND/IMMUTABLE when tvp exists, the source node with NOUNLINK/IMMUTABLE/APPEND, or the source directory with APPEND/IMMUTABLE), ENOTEMPTY, ENOTDIR and EISDIR (non-exchange only: replacing a non-empty directory, with whiteout-only contents allowed under IGNOREWHITEOUT, or a directory/non-directory mismatch), the error of tmpfs_rename_check_parent when a directory moves to another parent, and the success paths. Success paths: with AT_RENAME_EXCHANGE it makes the two directory entries refer to each other's nodes (adjusting parent pointers for moved directories), purges and re-enters the name cache and updates both directories' status and times (no names change); otherwise it detaches the source entry, adds or removes whiteouts as the componentnames request, renames the entry in place if the name changed, detaches and frees any existing target entry (clearing whiteouts of a replaced directory and marking its node changed), attaches the entry to the target directory and updates the name cache. In all cases at out it ends the seqc write sections it began, releases tdvp (vrele if tdvp == tvp, else vput), vputs tvp if non-NULL, vreles fdvp and fvp, and returns error; ownership of all four references is consumed on every path except the tmpfs_rename_relock failure return in (2).
note: Slice cut head (function starts :1049); fixed under real name. Reviewer r15 (claims AT_RENAME_EXCHANGE swaps entries; code has no exchange path) wrong: exchange handled at :1090, :1143-1164, :1249-1268. Qualified old prose: EEXIST for AT_RENAME_NOREPLACE is only produced in the relock path (:1109-1112); the prose previously said it always applied.

name: g_journal_worker
prose: Static function g_journal_worker(arg) at g_journal.c:2012-2176 (the slice cut the head and includes the following functions up to part of g_journal_create). It is the kproc entry point for a gjournal device. Precondition: arg points to a fully set up g_journal_softc (queues, mutex sc_mtx, consumers, geom), and the thread holds neither the topology lock nor sc_mtx. Startup, executed once: it sets its priority, calls g_journal_initialize (if GJF_DEVICE_CLEAN is set) or g_journal_sync, probes BIO_FLUSH support with g_io_flush on the journal consumer and, if different, the data consumer (setting GJ_FLUSH_JOURNAL / GJ_FLUSH_DATA), then under the topology lock creates the '<name>.journal' provider with the softc's media and sector sizes and marks it available, releases the topology lock, and releases sc->sc_rootmount (root_mount_rel, then sets it to NULL) if it is non-NULL. Main loop: with sc_mtx taken it takes the first bio from the back queue, otherwise from the regular queue. If both are empty (or on a jump from the delayed-write case below) it examines the flags: with GJF_DEVICE_SWITCH or GJF_DEVICE_DESTROY set and sc_current_count > 0 it runs g_journal_flush and g_journal_flush_send and loops; with a flush or copy in progress it waits (g_journal_wait); with GJF_DEVICE_SWITCH set it runs g_journal_switch, wakes sc_journal_copying and loops; with GJF_DEVICE_DESTROY set (and SWITCH not set) it sets sc->sc_worker to NULL, wakes up &sc->sc_worker, unlocks sc_mtx and ends the kproc with kproc_exit(0), which is the only normal way out; otherwise it waits. A regular WRITE found at the head while GJF_DEVICE_SWITCH is set is not dequeued and goes to the same flag examination, so that exit can also be reached while such a write is still queued. A dequeued bio is dispatched with sc_mtx released: regular READ to g_journal_read, regular WRITE to g_journal_add_request plus g_journal_flush_send, copy READ/WRITE to the copy completion routines plus g_journal_copy_send, journal bios to g_journal_flush_done plus g_journal_flush_send; any other bio_cmd for regular or copy bios, or an unknown or GJ_BIO_READ type, panics. The function never returns to its caller.
note: Slice cut head (function starts :2013); fixed under real name. Reviewer r15 (exit only when both bio queues are empty; check sits under bp == NULL) partly right: exit check is under the try_switch label (:2090-2117), reached when both queues are empty and also by goto from a delayed WRITE during SWITCH (:2126-2130), so the exit is not strictly limited to empty queues; prose states this. Also added: exit needs DESTROY and not SWITCH (SWITCH is handled first, :2104-2109).

name: g_mirror_try_destroy
prose: Function g_mirror_try_destroy(sc) at g_mirror.c:1901-1931 (the slice also contains neighbouring functions). Precondition: sc is a valid mirror softc and the caller holds sc->sc_lock exclusively. If sc->sc_rootmount is non-NULL it is released with root_mount_rel and set to NULL. The topology lock is then taken, and every path releases it again before returning. Return paths: (1) if g_mirror_can_destroy(sc) reports the device cannot be destroyed, it releases the topology lock and returns 0, with sc->sc_lock still held and the root mount already released; (2) otherwise it sets sc->sc_geom->softc and sc->sc_sync.ds_geom->softc to NULL, releases the topology lock and returns 1, after one of: if G_MIRROR_DEVICE_FLAG_DRAIN is set, it releases sc->sc_lock with sx_xunlock, calls wakeup(&sc->sc_worker) (the wait channel address; no specific thread handle) and then sets sc->sc_worker to NULL (this store happens after sc_lock was dropped), so sc_lock is no longer held on return; if the DRAIN flag is not set, it calls g_mirror_destroy_device(sc) with sc_lock still held at the call, and the softc is not accessed by this function afterwards.
note: g_mirror.c:1901-1931. Reviewer o1 (DRAIN path unconditionally unlocks sc_lock) right (:1923) and r2 (wakeup is on &sc->sc_worker and sets sc_worker to NULL, not a worker thread) right (:1924-1925); both already in the old prose, which was re-checked and kept with two added details (sc_worker store after unlock, root mount released before can_destroy test).

name: g_mirror_config
prose: The slice is the tail of g_mirror_config(req, mp, verb) at g_mirror_ctl.c:1088-1129, the gctl verb dispatcher of the mirror class, so it is fixed under that name instead of being dropped. It returns void. Precondition: the topology lock is held on entry (g_topology_assert), req is a gctl request and verb is a NUL-terminated string. Behaviour: if the 'version' parameter is absent it calls gctl_error ('No version argument') and returns with the topology lock still held; if the version differs from G_MIRROR_VERSION it calls gctl_error ('out of sync') and returns, again with the topology lock held; otherwise it releases the topology lock, then calls exactly one handler chosen by string comparison of verb: configure, create, rebuild, insert, remove, resize, deactivate, forget, stop (g_mirror_ctl_stop with 0), destroy (g_mirror_ctl_stop with 1), or, for any other verb, gctl_error ('Unknown verb.'). It then takes the topology lock again before returning. Errors from the handlers are reported through the gctl request, not through a return value.
note: Slice 1105-1129 is the end of g_mirror_config (:1089); fixed under real name instead of dropped (HAND_METHOD rule 6). Old prose omitted the two early returns (version missing or mismatched) in which the topology lock is not released (:1095-1103).

name: g_part_bsd_write
prose: Function g_part_bsd_write(basetable, cp) at g_part_bsd.c:497-539 (the slice cut the head). Precondition: basetable is a BSD partition table whose bbarea buffer has room for the label (at least BBSIZE bytes) and for gpt_entries 16-byte slots at offset sectorsize + 148, whose entry list holds entries in ascending gpe_index order, and cp is a consumer opened for writing whose provider has a valid sectorsize. For each slot number index from 1 to gpt_entries the function looks at the entry pointer it holds (initially the first list entry): if that entry's gpe_index equals index, the slot at bbarea + sectorsize + 148 + (index - 1) * 16 is filled from the entry's partition data (size, offset, fsize, fstype, frag, cpg) when the entry is not marked deleted, and zeroed when it is marked deleted; if no list entry matches index, the slot is zeroed; the entry pointer advances to the next list entry whenever one matched (deleted or not). Entries with a gpe_index above gpt_entries, or out of ascending order, are not written. It then zeroes the 16-bit checksum field at label + 136, stores in it the XOR of the little-endian 16-bit words from the start of the label up to (not including) label + 148 + gpt_entries * 16, and writes BBSIZE bytes of bbarea at offset 0 of the provider with g_write_data. It returns the error from g_write_data (0 on success); the label updates remain in bbarea whether or not the write succeeds. No locks or references are taken or released.
note: g_part_bsd_write is at :497 (slice cut head). Reviewer r15 (matching but deleted entry's slot is zeroed, not only the no-entry case) right (:515-523): added. Also added that only in-order entries are matched (:513, :525-526).

name: g_part_gpt_setunset
prose: Function g_part_gpt_setunset(basetable, baseentry, attrib, set) at g_part_gpt.c:1110-1193 (the slice also contains neighbouring functions). The attribute name attrib is compared case-insensitively; baseentry may be NULL. Return paths in code order: (1) attrib 'active' under Boot Camp (table->bootcamp): ENXIO if the entry is NULL, EINVAL if baseentry->gpe_index is greater than NDOSPART, otherwise it sets byte 0 of each of the NDOSPART MBR partition slots, slot gpe_index - 1 getting 0x80 when set is nonzero and 0 when it is zero, and all other slots getting 0, and returns 0; (2) 'active' without Boot Camp: ENXIO if the entry is non-NULL, otherwise it sets byte 0 of each MBR slot whose type byte is 0xee to 0x80 (set nonzero) or 0 (set zero) and byte 0 of every other slot to 0, and returns 0; (3) 'lenovofix': ENXIO if the entry is non-NULL, otherwise it zeroes the MBR partition table, writes a 0xee protective entry (start 1, size limited to UINT32_MAX) into MBR slot index 1 when set is nonzero and slot index 0 when set is zero, and returns 0 (it reads the first consumer's provider of the geom for the media size, so a consumer must exist); (4) for any other attrib, ENODEV if the entry is NULL, whatever the name; (5) with a non-NULL entry, EINVAL if attrib is not 'bootme', 'bootonce' or 'bootfailed'; (6) otherwise the corresponding attribute bit (BOOTME, BOOTONCE or BOOTFAILED, plus the BOOTME bit when 'bootonce' is set, but not cleared when 'bootonce' is cleared) is ORed into ent_attr when set is nonzero or cleared when it is zero; if the resulting value differs from the old one it is stored and, when the entry was not newly created (gpe_created is clear), baseentry->gpe_modified is set to 1; it returns 0 also when nothing changed. The function allocates nothing and takes no lock or reference.
note: g_part_gpt.c:1111-1193. Reviewer o1 (active/lenovofix success updates the MBR, not ent_attr or gpe_modified) right (:1124-1161), r2 (lenovofix writes the 0xee entry into slot index 0 when unset, bootonce set also sets BOOTME) right and already stated. New: an unknown attribute with a NULL entry returns ENODEV, not EINVAL (:1163-1164, :1180-1181); old prose said EINVAL for any unrecognised name.

name: ddf_meta_read
prose: Function ddf_meta_read(cp, meta) at md_ddf.c:1048-1284 (the slice cut the head and runs into ddf_meta_write). Precondition: cp is a geom consumer whose provider has a sectorsize and mediasize, and meta is a ddf_meta whose previous contents may be discarded (it is freed with ddf_meta_free at entry). Return paths: (1) ENXIO if the provider sectorsize is smaller than a struct ddf_header; (2) the g_read_data error if the anchor block (the last sector) cannot be read; (3) EINVAL if the anchor has neither big- nor little-endian DDF signature, is not of header type anchor, has a CRC mismatch, or has a primary header LBA or (when it is not -1) secondary header LBA that lies too close to or beyond the end of the media; (4) otherwise it reads the primary header (lba = plba) and then, one after another, the controller data, physical-disk, virtual-disk, configuration, physical-disk-data and, when the header records one, bad-block-management sections; for the primary copy, any failure after the anchor checks, whether a read error or a header check failure (signature or CRC or GUID differing from the anchor, LBA fields differing from the anchor, wrong header type, section extents beyond the media, a section length of maxphys or more, a bad signature on the controller, physical-disk, virtual-disk, physical-disk-data or BBM section, or no matching physical-disk record for the pdd reference), causes the whole read to restart, with meta freed, from the secondary header if one is recorded (slba != -1); (5) if that retry, or the only copy, fails on a read the g_read_data error is returned, and if it fails a check EINVAL is returned; (6) on success it returns 0 with meta->sectorsize and meta->bigendian set and meta->hdr (a copy of the primary or secondary header, whose CRC field was overwritten with 0xffffffff), cdr, pdr, vdr, cr, pdd and, if a BBM log was present, bbm holding malloc'd copies of the on-disk records, which the caller releases with ddf_meta_free. On every nonzero return meta has been freed and holds no buffers; the anchor buffer is freed on all paths after it was read. The configuration records have no signature check.
note: Slice cut head (function starts :1049); fixed under real name. Reviewer r15 (omits EINVAL for bad cdr/pdr/vdr/pdd/bbm signatures, pdd lookup, and section length/range checks) right (:1166-1185, :1195-1276): added. Also corrected: read errors on the primary copy cause a retry on the secondary (:1118-1125), they are not returned immediately as the old prose implied.

name: g_raid_md_ctl_ddf
prose: The slice is the middle of g_raid_md_ctl_ddf(md, req) at md_ddf.c:2257-2732, the gctl command handler of the DDF metadata module, so it is fixed under that name instead of being dropped. Precondition: md is the DDF metadata object, req carries the 'verb' string and an 'nargs' integer (both are dereferenced without a NULL check) and the thread does not hold the topology lock (it takes and releases it itself around consumer opening). It returns 0 on success or a negative code, and all negative codes except -100 are accompanied by gctl_error. Verbs: (1) 'label': -1 if nargs < 4, -2 no volume name, -3 no RAID level, -4 unknown level, -5 unsupported level or disk count; then for each disk argument ('NONE' skipped) -6 missing disk name, -7 if an existing disk is not active or has no free partition, -8 if the disk cannot be opened (a loop error destroys the disk objects created in this call that are still in state NONE, then returns); afterwards -8 if no sector size was obtained, -9 size larger than the available space, -10 strip smaller than the sector size, -11 strip not a multiple of the sector size, -13 size too small after rounding (these later returns do not destroy the disk objects created for the call); on success it creates the volume, its metadata and subdisks, activates the disks and subdisks, writes the metadata, refills from spare disks, sends the start event and returns 0. (2) 'add': always -99 (not applicable). (3) 'delete': with a single argument equal to the node name it returns -4 if force is supplied as 0 and some volume is open, otherwise erases metadata on every disk, destroys the node and returns 0; with more than two arguments -1; -2 if no volume name, -3 if the volume (found by name, provider name, 'raid/' name or numeric global id) is not found, -4 if force is supplied as 0 and the volume is open; otherwise, if there are at least two volumes it destroys the volume, purges disks and writes metadata, and if it was the last volume it erases metadata on all disks and destroys the node, and returns 0. (4) 'remove' and 'fail': -1 if nargs < 2; for each disk argument -2 for a missing name and -3 for a disk not found, either of which stops the loop; 'fail' marks the disk failed, 'remove' erases its metadata and destroys it; after the loop (also after an early stop, so earlier arguments stay applied) it purges volumes and writes metadata, destroys the node if no disks remain, else refills, and returns 0 or the loop's -2/-3. (5) 'insert': -1 if nargs < 2; per disk -3 missing name or -4 cannot open (stop); otherwise it makes the disk a spare, creates its metadata, writes the metadata and refills, returning 0 or the loop's error. (6) any other verb: -100 without gctl_error.
note: Slice 2388-2648 is the middle of g_raid_md_ctl_ddf (:2258); fixed under real name instead of dropped (HAND_METHOD rule 6). Old prose said '0 or a small negative code' only; new prose lists the codes per verb from :2286-2731.

name: g_raid_md_ctl_jmicron
prose: Function g_raid_md_ctl_jmicron(md, req) at md_jmicron.c:1018-1382, the gctl command handler of the JMicron metadata module (the packet name g_raid_md_jmicron_ctl_start does not exist; the slice is the middle of this function), so it is fixed instead of dropped. Precondition: req carries 'verb' and 'nargs' (both dereferenced without a NULL check) and the thread does not hold the topology lock (it takes it around consumer opening). It returns 0 or a negative code, and every negative code is accompanied by gctl_error. Verbs: (1) 'label': -1 if nargs < 4, -2 no volume name, -3 no level, -4 unknown level ('RAID5' is read as 'RAID5-LA'), -5 unsupported level or disk count; for each disk argument ('NONE' creates a placeholder disk with no consumer) -6 missing name, -7 disk cannot be opened (any disk objects created earlier in the call are not destroyed on this return); afterwards -8 if no sector size, -9 size larger than the smallest disk minus one sector, -10 strip smaller than the sector size, -11 strip not a multiple of the sector size, -12 if the strip value at that point (still the default 131072 when this check runs, since the user value is stored afterwards) is above 65535 sectors, -13 size too small after rounding, -14 size above 0xffffffffffff sectors; otherwise it creates the volume (level, strip and size computed), attaches subdisks to the created disks (active, or offline for placeholders), writes the metadata, refills from spare disks, sends the volume start event and returns 0. (2) 'delete': -4 if the force argument is present as 0 and a volume is open; otherwise it erases the metadata of every disk with a consumer, destroys the node and returns 0. (3) 'remove' and 'fail': -1 if nargs < 2; per disk argument -2 for a missing name and -3 for a disk not found, either stopping the loop; 'fail' marks the disk failed; 'remove' erases its metadata and then, if the disk was assigned a position, makes it offline, kills its consumer and disconnects its subdisks, otherwise destroys the disk; after the loop (also after an early stop) it writes the metadata and destroys the node if only offline placeholders remain, else refills; returns 0 or the loop's -2/-3. (4) 'insert': -1 if nargs < 2; per disk -3 missing name, -4 cannot open, -8 if after starting the disk it is neither active nor spare (the disk is destroyed and the loop stops); it writes the metadata if anything changed and returns 0 or the loop's error. (5) any other verb: gctl_error 'Command is not supported' and -100.
note: Slice 1038-1289 is the middle of g_raid_md_ctl_jmicron (:1019); fixed under real name instead of dropped (HAND_METHOD rule 6). Old prose gave only 'negative error code'; codes listed from :1043-1381. Quirk noted: the strip-too-big check at :1157 uses the default strip, not the user value.

name: g_raid_md_ctl_nvidia
prose: Function g_raid_md_ctl_nvidia(md, req) at md_nvidia.c:1022-1386, the gctl command handler of the NVIDIA metadata module (the slice is its middle and the item was unnamed). Precondition: req carries 'verb' and 'nargs' (both dereferenced without a NULL check) and the thread does not hold the topology lock (it takes it around consumer opening). It returns 0 or a negative code, and every negative code is accompanied by gctl_error. Verbs: (1) 'label': -1 if nargs < 4, -2 no volume name, -3 no level, -4 unknown level ('RAID5' is read as 'RAID5-LS'), -5 unsupported level or disk count; for each disk argument ('NONE' creates a placeholder disk with no consumer) -6 missing name, -7 disk cannot be opened (disk objects created earlier in the call are not destroyed on this return); afterwards -8 if no sector size, -9 requested size larger than the smallest disk minus two sectors, -10 strip smaller than the sector size, -11 strip not a multiple of the sector size, -12 if the strip value at that point (still the default 131072, since the user value is stored after the check) is above 65535 sectors, -13 size too small after rounding, -14 if the computed volume size exceeds 0xffffffff sectors; otherwise it creates the volume, attaches subdisks to the created disks (active, or offline for placeholders), writes the metadata, refills from spare disks, sends the volume start event and returns 0. (2) 'delete': -4 if the force argument is present as 0 and a volume is open; otherwise it erases the metadata of each disk that has a consumer, destroys the node and returns 0. (3) 'remove' and 'fail': -1 if nargs < 2; per disk argument -2 for a missing name and -3 for a disk not found, either stopping the loop; 'fail' marks the disk failed; 'remove' erases its metadata and then, if the disk was assigned a position, makes it offline, kills its consumer and disconnects its subdisks, otherwise destroys the disk; after the loop (also after an early stop, leaving earlier arguments applied) it writes the metadata and destroys the node if only offline placeholders remain, else refills; it returns 0 or the loop's -2/-3. (4) 'insert' (there is no 'add' verb): -1 if nargs < 2; per disk -3 missing name, -4 cannot open, -8 if after starting the disk it is neither spare nor active (the disk is destroyed and the loop stops); the metadata is written if anything changed; it returns 0 or the loop's error. (5) any other verb: gctl_error 'Command is not supported' and -100. g_topology is taken and released inside the opening code and is not held on any return.
note: Slice 1042-1292 is inside g_raid_md_ctl_nvidia (:1023); fixed under real name. Old prose wrongly listed an 'add' verb, listed -2/-3 for 'add' and placed 'unknown RAID level' under -4 only for delete; codes rechecked against :1047-1385. The -12 check uses the default strip (:1160).

name: g_raid_md_ctl_promise
prose: Function g_raid_md_ctl_promise(md, req) at md_promise.c:1276-1710, the gctl command handler of the Promise metadata module (the packet name g_raid_mdctl_promise does not exist; the slice is its middle). Precondition: req carries 'verb' and 'nargs' (both dereferenced without a NULL check) and the thread does not hold the topology lock (it takes it around consumer opening). It returns 0 or a negative code; every negative code except -100 is accompanied by gctl_error. Verbs: (1) 'label': -1 if nargs < 4, -2 no volume name, -3 no level, -4 unknown level ('RAID5' is read as 'RAID5-LA'), -5 unsupported level or disk count; for each disk argument ('NONE' skipped) -6 missing name, -7 if an existing disk is not active or already carries the maximum number of subdisks, -8 if the disk cannot be opened (when a loop error occurs, the disk objects created in this call that are still in state NONE are destroyed before returning); afterwards -8 if no sector size, -9 requested size larger than the available space, -10 strip smaller than the sector size, -11 strip not a multiple of the sector size, -13 size too small after rounding (these later returns do not destroy the disk objects created for the call); otherwise it creates the volume with a random id, subdisks at the computed offsets (activating the disks and subdisks), writes the metadata, refills from spare disks, sends the volume start event and returns 0. (2) 'add': -99 (not applicable). (3) 'delete': with a single argument equal to the node name it returns -4 if force is supplied as 0 and a volume is open, otherwise erases metadata on every disk, destroys the node and returns 0; otherwise -1 if nargs > 2, -2 no volume name, -3 volume not found (by name, provider name, 'raid/' name or numeric id), -4 if force is supplied as 0 and the volume is open; if there are at least two volumes it destroys the volume, purges disks and writes metadata, else it erases the disks' metadata and destroys the node, returning 0. (4) 'remove' and 'fail': -1 if nargs < 2; per disk argument -2 missing name and -3 disk not found, either stopping the loop; 'fail' marks the disk failed, 'remove' erases its metadata and destroys it; after the loop (also after an early stop) it purges volumes, writes metadata, destroys the node if no disks remain, else refills, and returns 0 or the loop's -2/-3. (5) 'insert': -1 if nargs < 2; per disk -3 missing name, -4 cannot open; each opened disk is made a spare, gets spare metadata written and a refill is attempted; it returns 0 or the loop's error. (6) any other verb: -100 without gctl_error.
note: Slice 1297-1548 is inside g_raid_md_ctl_promise (:1277); fixed under real name instead of dropped (HAND_METHOD rule 6). Old prose gave only 'negative error code'; codes listed from :1301-1709.

name: allocate_chunk
prose: Static function allocate_chunk(sc, comp, comp_no_p, chunk) at g_virstor.c:1801-1844 (the slice cut the head and also contains dump_component, bioq_dismantle and other code, which are not part of this function). Precondition: sc->curr_component is less than sc->n_components (KASSERTed) and comp, comp_no_p and chunk are writable. *comp is always set to the component currently selected by sc->curr_component. Return paths: (1) that component still has free chunks (chunk_next < chunk_count): *comp_no_p is set to its index, *chunk to its chunk_next (relative to the component), chunk_next is incremented, and 0 is returned; (2) the current component is full and it is the last component: an error is logged, -1 is returned, *comp still points to that full component and *comp_no_p and *chunk are not written; (3) the current component is full and a later one exists: the CURRENT flag is cleared on the old one, sc->curr_component is advanced by one, *comp points to the new component (a warning is logged when the number of remaining components is within the watermark), the new component's chunk_next is raised to its chunk_reserved if it is lower, its flags get VIRSTOR_PROVIDER_ALLOCATED and VIRSTOR_PROVIDER_CURRENT, *comp_no_p is set to the new index, *chunk to the new chunk_next, chunk_next is incremented, and 0 is returned; the code does not check that the new component itself has a free chunk. No locks are taken or released by the function.
note: Slice 1807-1904 is the body of allocate_chunk (:1802-1844) plus other functions; fixed under real name instead of dropped (HAND_METHOD rule 6). Old prose said '*comp points at the current component' and 'returns -1 when all components exhausted': *comp is advanced when switching, and -1 is returned only when the current, last, component is full (:1813-1819).

name: __elfN(imgact)
prose: __elfN(imgact)(imgp) treats imgp->image_header as an ELF header; the caller holds imgp->vp locked shared. It returns -1 (line 1044, before anything is changed) if __elfN(check_header) fails or e_type is neither ET_EXEC nor ET_DYN. Past that point it returns an errno or 0. Two ENOEXEC returns leave without going through the cleanup label: e_phoff + e_phnum*e_phentsize wraps, and e_phnum exceeds __elfN(phnums); nothing has been allocated or changed at that point. Every other exit goes to label ret, which asserts that imgp->vp is locked, frees interp if it was allocated by __elfN(get_interp) (free_interp), frees the temporary program-header buffer m_phdrs (NULL when the headers were read from the header page) and returns error. Errors reaching ret: an error from vn_rdwr reading the program headers (the vnode is unlocked during the malloc and relocked shared before the read); ENOEXEC for a PT_LOAD alignment that is not a power of two or exceeds the maximum, for a mapsize overflow, for a second PT_INTERP, and for a PT_GNU_STACK whose translated protection lacks read and write (checked only when __elfN(nxstack) is set); the error from __elfN(get_interp); ENOEXEC when __elfN(get_brandinfo) returns NULL; ENOEXEC for an ET_DYN file whose brand lacks BI_CAN_EXEC_DYN; ENOEXEC for 'Excessive mapping size' (mapsz >= maxv - vm_map_min); under PAX_ASLR ENOEXEC for a non-ET_DYN file when can_exec_nonpie fails; and any error from __elfN(load_sections), __elfN(enforce_limits), __elfN(load_interp) or exec_map_stack. Side effects before the later checks: when imgp->credential_setid is set it clears the ASLR and WXORX bits in p_flag2 under the proc lock; once the brand is chosen it calls exec_new_vmspace and then stores sv in imgp->proc->p_sysent and brand_info in p_elf_brandinfo before testing the result of exec_new_vmspace (an error from it is kept in error and is replaced by ENOEXEC if the mapping-size check also fails), so these fields and the new vmspace can be left in place when an error is returned. PT_GNU_STACK sets imgp->stack_sz, and imgp->stack_prot only when __elfN(nxstack) is set. On success it returns 0 after setting imgp->entry_addr, anon_loc of the new map, imgp->auxargs (a freshly allocated Elf_Auxargs), imgp->interpreted = 0, imgp->reloc_base, p_osrel, p_fctl0 and p_elf_flags; imgp->et_dyn_addr is set to ET_DYN_LOAD_ADDR (or the PAX ASLR base) for an ET_DYN file with a zero first load address.
note: slice cut the head (starts at line 1034 inside the body); real function is the static ELF activator defined with the __elfN macro name. Old prose said 'returns 0 ... or errno' without the early-return split and wrongly implied no state change on failure after exec_new_vmspace; rewritten from returns list at imgact_elf.c lines 1044,1063,1068,1083 and ret at 1323-1328.

name: __elfN(trans_prot)
prose: __elfN(trans_prot)(flags) returns a vm_prot_t built from flags with a single return at the end: VM_PROT_EXECUTE is set when PF_X is set in flags, VM_PROT_WRITE when PF_W is set, VM_PROT_READ when PF_R is set, and no other bit is set in the result; bits of flags other than PF_X, PF_W and PF_R are ignored. It reads and writes no global state and takes no locks.
note: slice began inside the body/included untrans_prot; real function is the static trans_prot defined with the __elfN macro name (imgact_elf.c 2835-2848). Old prose correct apart from 'Generated function' wording; no lock or memory effect.

name: vty_enabled
prose: vty_enabled(vty) uses the static variable vty_selected (initially 0) and the static buffer vty_name. If vty_selected is still 0 it fetches the tunable kern.vty into vty_name with TUNABLE_STR_FETCH, then picks the console driver: with DEV_SC compiled in and vty_name equal to 'sc' it selects VTY_SC; with DEV_VT compiled in and vty_name equal to 'vt' it selects VTY_VT; otherwise it defaults to VTY_VT if DEV_VT is compiled in, else to VTY_SC if DEV_SC is compiled in (if neither is compiled in, vty_selected stays 0). When vty_selected is then VTY_VT or VTY_SC it overwrites vty_name with 'vt' or 'sc'. There is a single return, which returns whether (vty_selected & vty) is non-zero. When vty_selected is already non-zero, the selection is not redone. No lock is taken, so concurrent first calls can both run the selection.
note: slice cut the head (starts at line 772 inside vty_enabled, kern_cons.c 745-778); old prose wrongly described vty_name as a caller buffer and a parameter. vty_name is a static 16-byte file-scope buffer; function takes only 'unsigned vty'.

name: cf_set_method
prose: cf_set_method(dev, level, priority) changes the CPU frequency level of dev's cpufreq softc. It first calls the cpufreq_pre_change event handlers with level and &error; if they set error non-zero it calls the cpufreq_post_change handlers with level and that error and returns that error without taking sc->lock. Otherwise it takes sc->lock (CF_MTX_LOCK) and every later path goes through label out, which drops sc->lock, calls the cpufreq_post_change handlers with level and error, prints 'set freq failed' when error is non-zero and the local pointer set is non-NULL, and returns error. Paths to out: ENXIO when SMP is configured without EARLY_AP_STARTUP, mp_ncpus > 1 and smp_started is not yet set; EPERM when priority is lower than sc->curr_priority; when level is NULL, ENXIO if sc->saved_freq is empty, otherwise the first saved entry's level and priority are used instead; EINVAL if level->total_set.freq is below cf_lowest_freq; ENXIO if the absolute-setting device (set->dev non-NULL) or any relative-setting device is not attached; error 0 with no level recorded when the absolute-setting device's CPU has no pcpu (cpu_get_pcpu returns NULL); an error from CPUFREQ_DRV_SET for the absolute or any relative setting (earlier settings are not backed out); and ENOMEM if the malloc (M_NOWAIT) that saves the previous level fails. If the requested frequency equals sc->curr_level.total_set.freq the driver calls are skipped, but the code still continues to the 'skip' step below, so this case can also return ENOMEM. At the skip step, if the current frequency is not CPUFREQ_VAL_UNKNOWN and priority is higher than sc->curr_priority, the current level and priority are pushed onto sc->saved_freq. Then sc->curr_level = *level and sc->curr_priority = priority are recorded; if a saved level was being restored, sc->curr_level.total_set.freq is set to CPUFREQ_VAL_UNKNOWN, the saved entry is removed from sc->saved_freq and freed, and the post-change handlers are then called with a level pointer that referred to that freed entry. It returns 0 on those completed paths unless an error was set above. During each driver call the thread is temporarily bound to the target CPU at priority PRI_MIN and restored afterwards.
note: slice cut the head: the function is cf_set_method(device_t dev, const struct cf_level *level, int priority) (kern_cpu.c 238-426), not cpufreq_set. Reviewer claim (already-current path can return ENOMEM) is right: the goto skip at line 321 falls into the save-previous-level malloc (394-398) which can set ENOMEM.

name: kern_cpuset_getdomain
prose: kern_cpuset_getdomain(td, level, which, id, domainsetsize, maskp, policyp, cb) returns ERANGE if domainsetsize is below sizeof(domainset_t) or above DOMAINSET_MAXSIZE / NBBY, and otherwise the error from cpuset_check_capabilities if that is non-zero; both of these return before anything is allocated. It then allocates a zeroed temporary mask of domainsetsize bytes and calls cpuset_which2, whose error (for example ESRCH or EPERM) is returned after freeing the buffer. Under CPU_LEVEL_ROOT or CPU_LEVEL_CPUSET it takes the thread's cpuset (CPU_WHICH_TID, CPU_WHICH_PID) or the set found by cpuset_which2 (CPU_WHICH_CPUSET, CPU_WHICH_JAIL), takes the root or base set of it and copies its domainset to a local outset; the CPU_WHICH_IRQ, INTRHANDLER, ITHREAD and DOMAIN selections give EINVAL. Under CPU_LEVEL_WHICH it copies the thread's domainset (TID), ORs the masks of all threads in the process and takes the policy and preferred domain of the last thread (PID), or copies the cpuset's domainset (CPUSET, JAIL); the other selections give EINVAL; any other level gives EINVAL. It then releases the cpuset reference if one was held and drops the proc lock if one was held, and if outset.ds_policy is DOMAINSET_POLICY_PREFER it replaces the mask with a mask holding only ds_prefer. If error is still 0 it copies the mask out with cb->cpuset_copyout(mask, maskp, domainsetsize) and returns that callback's error if non-zero; then it stores the policy with suword32 and sets EFAULT if that fails. The temporary mask is freed on every path that allocated it and the function returns error; 0 only when both copy-outs succeeded.
note: Both reviewer claims are right: the size and capability checks are returns of the function (kern_cpuset.c 2297-2302), not preconditions. The 'every path releases references' claim is true on my reading (goto out at 2307 and 2326 occur only when p and set are NULL), but the old prose said EFAULT for the copyout, which is whatever cb->cpuset_copyout returns.

name: cpuset_modify_domain
prose: cpuset_modify_domain(set, domain) is static. It returns the error of priv_check(curthread, PRIV_SCHED_CPUSET) if non-zero, and EPERM if the current credential is jailed and set has CPU_SET_ROOT; both returns happen before any allocation or lock. Otherwise it initialises a freelist of domainsets, replaces domain by the result of domainset_create(domain), and takes the spin lock cpuset_lock. In a loop it gets the root of set and returns EINVAL (via out) if domainset_valid(root's domainset, domain) fails; if the policy is DOMAINSET_POLICY_PREFER it copies set->cs_domain's current mask into domain->ds_mask; it then calls cpuset_testupdate_domain, going to out with its error if non-zero. If the number of free domainsets already prepared is at least the number needed it leaves the loop; otherwise it drops the spin lock, adds the missing entries to the freelist, retakes the lock and re-evaluates. After the loop it calls cpuset_update_domain on set, which applies the domainset to set and its descendants. At out it releases cpuset_lock, frees the leftover freelist entries, and calls domainset_notify() only when error is 0. It returns 0 on success; on the error paths from out nothing has been applied to the hierarchy because the update is only reached after the validity and testupdate checks succeeded.
note: Reviewer claim (privilege/jail are checks, not preconditions) is right; the old prose already listed them as returns, so it was kept in substance and the preconditions wording and an unqualified 'on every error path' removed (kern_cpuset.c 812-883).

name: kern_dup
prose: kern_dup(td, mode, flags, old, new) duplicates descriptor old to a new descriptor in the calling process's table. Returns before taking the table lock: EBADF if old < 0; if new < 0, or new >= getmaxfd(td), EINVAL when mode is FDDUP_FCNTL and EBADF otherwise. It then takes the filedesc exclusive lock. Returns EBADF (lock released) if descriptor old is not open (fget_noref returns NULL) or if fhold on its file fails. If mode is FDDUP_FIXED and old == new it sets td->td_retval[0] = new, ORs fddup_to_fde_flags(flags) into that entry's flags, releases the lock and returns 0 without taking a new reference. Otherwise it takes a reference on the old file with fhold and obtains the target: for FDDUP_NORMAL and FDDUP_FCNTL it calls fdalloc(td, new, &new), and on error drops the reference, releases the lock and returns that error; new may then be a different (higher) descriptor number than requested; for FDDUP_FIXED, if new >= fd_nfiles it (under RACCT, when enabled) calls racct_set_unlocked(p, RACCT_NOFILE, new + 1) and on failure drops the reference, releases the lock and returns EMFILE, then grows the table to new + 1, and it marks new used if it was not. It then copies the file pointer and capabilities from the old entry to the new entry (sequence-count write bracket under CAPABILITIES), sets the new entry's flags to the old flags without UF_EXCLOSE and UF_FOCLOSE ORed with fddup_to_fde_flags(flags), sets td->td_retval[0] = new and error = 0. If the new entry previously held a file (delfp, only possible in FDDUP_FIXED mode) it calls closefp on that file, which is entered with the lock held and releases it, and the return value of closefp is ignored; otherwise it releases the lock. It finally frees the old capability ioctl list that was detached from the new entry (filecaps_free_finish) and returns error (0 on the success paths).
note: slice cut the head; the function is kern_dup(td, mode, flags, old, new) (kern_descrip.c 1043-1176), not fddup. The old prose used the wrong name and described fhold/getmaxfd correctly in places but wrongly said 'always releases the table lock via closefp or unlock' without noting that closefp does the unlock, and omitted the old==new FIXED case and the fhold-failure EBADF.

name: do_execve
prose: do_execve(td, args, mac_p, oldvmspace) is the in-kernel implementation of execve/fexecve for thread td; all arguments are consumed (exec_free_args(args) is called on every path that reaches the common exit). It takes the proc lock, waits via execve_block_pass if exec is blocked, sets P_INEXEC and drops the lock; it zeroes a local image_params, records the old credential, p_osrel, p_fctl0 and p_elf_brandinfo, and (with MAC) calls mac_execve_enter, going to exec_fail on error. At label interpret it obtains the image vnode in one of three ways: by name through namei (returning to exec_fail with its error, or ECAPMODE when in capability mode), from an interpreter vnode already supplied by an activator, or from args->fd through fgetvp_exec (error to exec_fail). It then runs exec_check_permissions, PAX checks when configured, maps the first page (exec_map_first_page), clears p_osrel, p_fctl0 and p_elf_brandinfo, decides whether the credentials change (set-id files, not under MNT_NOSUID, not capability mode, not P_TRACED) and builds imgp->newcred, then calls each non-NULL ex_imgact in turn until one returns something other than -1. Failures up to this point jump to exec_fail_dealloc with error set; if no activator matched error becomes ENOEXEC. If the activator set imgp->interpreted, the first page and text reference are released, the old vnode and name are freed and the loop restarts at interpret with the interpreter name. Otherwise it unlocks the vnode and fails with ENOEXEC if disallow_high_osrel rejects the osrel, with the error from sv_copyout_strings, with EINVAL if argc is not positive, with the error from sv_fixup, or with the error from fdcheckstd (set-id case); each of those relocks the vnode and goes to exec_fail_dealloc. On the success path it unshares the file descriptor table and process-descriptor state, closes close-on-exec files, optionally builds a new cached argument copy, copies shared sigacts, then under the proc lock resets signals, names the process and thread, sets P_EXEC, wakes a vfork parent, installs the new credentials (proc_set_cred, freeing the old credential reference), swaps in the new p_textvp, p_textdvp and p_binname, clears P_INEXEC, installs the new argument cache, runs the hwpmc/hwt hooks when active, calls sv_setregs and updates the access time. At exec_fail_dealloc, if error is non-zero it restores the saved p_osrel, p_fctl0 and p_elf_brandinfo; it unmaps the first page, closes and releases the vnode (vput on error, plain unlock on success) and frees the name buffer, deallocates imgp->object and frees the resolved path; on success it sets TDB_EXEC when PTRACE_EXEC is requested, on error (and for jumps to exec_fail) it clears P_INEXEC under the proc lock. It then frees the new credential if it was not installed, the old text vnodes, binname, argument cache, sigacts and uidinfo. If error is non-zero and the vmspace was already destroyed (imgp->vmspace_destroyed) it calls exec_cleanup and kern_exit(td, 0, SIGABRT) instead of returning an error to the caller. Otherwise it returns EJUSTRETURN when error is 0 and error when it is non-zero.
note: slice cut the head and was only a middle fragment; the function is the static do_execve(td, args, mac_p, oldvmspace) (kern_exec.c 457-1179). Old prose was only a fragment and falsely implied an 'imgp is zeroed by the caller' precondition (the function does bzero(imgp) itself at 519).

name: fork1
prose: fork1(td, fr) creates a child process (or, without RFPROC, only unshares resources). It first returns immediately, with no allocations made and without the pause below: the error from pax_segvguard_check when PAX_SEGVGUARD is configured and the process is not pid 0; EINVAL for undefined flags, RFTSIGFLAGS without RFTSIGZMB, RFFDG together with RFCFDG, an out-of-range RFTSIGZMB signal, or RFPROCDESC without RFPROC, without fr_pd_fd or with pd flags outside PD_ALLOWED_AT_FORK. (MPASS checks on fr_procp/fr_pidp are assertions only.) If RFPROC is clear it stores NULL in *fr_procp or, otherwise if fr_pidp is set, 0 in *fr_pidp, and returns fork_norfproc(td, flags). Otherwise it increments nprocs and fails with EAGAIN if the count reaches maxproc - 10 and the caller lacks PRIV_MAXPROC, or reaches maxproc. If p1 has several threads it takes pg_killsx shared, or single-threads the process with thread_single(SINGLE_BOUNDARY) and returns ERESTART if that fails; it returns ERESTART if sx_slock_sig fails, or if the process changed process group or sig_intr() reports a pending signal. It then, if requested, allocates the process descriptor with procdesc_falloc (its error is returned), allocates a proc and thread (ENOMEM if thread_alloc fails; error from thread_recycle), forks the vmspace when RFMEM is clear (ENOMEM if vmspace_fork or swap_reserve fails), copies the credential, and calls racct_proc_fork (EAGAIN on failure), and checks the per-uid process count with chgproccnt (EAGAIN if over the limit without PRIV_PROC_LIMIT). On success it calls do_fork and returns 0 with nprocs left incremented. Every failure after nprocs was incremented goes through fail0/fail1/fail2: it frees the vmspace if any, drops the reference on the new proc, closes and drops the procdesc file if one was allocated, decrements nprocs, then at cleanup releases pg_killsx and ends single-threading if they were taken, and for any non-zero error sleeps hz/2 ticks with pause() before returning the error.
note: slice cut the head (fork1 is at kern_fork.c 896-1171). Reviewer claim 'pause only for EAGAIN' is WRONG: label cleanup runs pause('fork', hz/2) for any non-zero error that reaches it (kern_fork.c 1168-1169). But the old prose was wrong elsewhere: the EINVAL/segvguard/flag-check returns (920-958) return immediately with no cleanup and no pause, racct_proc_fork failure is mapped to EAGAIN (1118), and the failed-limit paths give EAGAIN or ERESTART.

name: kern_jail_set
prose: kern_jail_set(td, optuio, flags) creates and/or updates a jail from the name/value options in optuio. It returns immediately (no cleanup needed) with EPERM if JAIL_CREATE is set without JAIL_AT_DESC and the caller's prison has pr_childmax 0, and with EINVAL if flags contain bits outside JAIL_SET_MASK or both JAIL_USE_DESC and JAIL_AT_DESC. With JAIL_ATTACH it then calls prison_attach_thread_single and returns its error if non-zero. From then on it holds a reference on the caller's prison and every exit goes through the done_deref / done_errmsg / done_free labels. It builds the option list with vfs_buildopts, parses and validates the parameters (desc, jid, securelevel, children.max, enforce_statfs, name, host.*, path, ip4/ip6 addresses, allow and boolean flags and others) and fails with errors that include EINVAL, ENAMETOOLONG, EPERM (when PRIV_JAIL_SET or PRIV_JAIL_ATTACH is denied, or a parent/permission check fails), ENOTDIR and errors from namei or the descriptor helpers (jaildesc_find, jaildesc_alloc). Then it takes the allprison lock exclusively and, depending on jid/name and the CREATE/UPDATE flags, finds or creates the prison, failing with errors that include EAGAIN, EEXIST, ENOENT, EINVAL, EPERM, EADDRINUSE and ENOMEM-type allocation errors. It applies the settings under the prison mutex, calls the OSD methods PR_METHOD_CREATE (for a new jail) and PR_METHOD_SET (errors go to done_deref), marks a new prison alive, attaches the calling process with do_jail_attach if JAIL_ATTACH is set (error becomes 'attach failed'), writes the jail descriptor number back into the 'desc' option if one was requested, and on success sets td->td_retval[0] to the prison id and returns 0. At done_deref it queues NOTE_JAIL_SET for an existing, possibly changed jail, calls prison_deref (or drops the allprison lock itself) and releases the root vnode; for a non-zero error it copies any 'errmsg' text back to the user; at done_free it frees the copied IP lists, drops the descriptor file reference and closes the new descriptor if an error occurred, frees the path buffer and the option list, drops the reference on the caller's prison, ends the attach single-threading when JAIL_ATTACH was set, and returns error. Because settings are applied before later steps can fail, a non-zero return does not guarantee that the jail was left unchanged.
note: slice cut the head and is a middle fragment of kern_jail_set(td, optuio, flags) (kern_jail.c 1006-2372); jail_set is not a separate function. Old prose claimed that failures never create or update a jail, which is false: the code itself notes (2320-2324) that changes may have been made before a failure.
