name: sctp_kick_prsctp_reorder_queue
prose: Precondition: stcb is non-NULL (KASSERT), the TCB lock on stcb and the endpoint read lock are held, and strmin is a stream input queue of stcb's association. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It first scans strmin->inqueue in order and stops at the first control whose mid is later than the initial strmin->last_mid_delivered; it delivers each non-fragmented control (flags marking SCTP_DATA_NOT_FRAG) with a mid at or before that value, and for a fragmented control it ignores it unless first_frag_seen is set, in which case it sets last_mid_delivered to the control's mid minus 1 and stops scanning. Delivering a control means: if on_strm_q is nonzero it is removed from strmin->inqueue (SCTP_ON_ORDERED) or strmin->uno_inqueue (SCTP_ON_UNORDERED), with a panic under INVARIANTS for any other nonzero value, and on_strm_q cleared; asoc->size_on_all_streams is reduced by control->length (a panic under INVARIANTS if it is smaller, else set to 0); asoc->cnt_on_all_streams is decremented; and only if stcb->sctp_socket is non-NULL the TSN is marked non-revokable and the control is added to the read queue. If the scan stopped on a fragmented control it calls sctp_deliver_reasm_check, afterwards restores last_mid_delivered to the initial mid unless the latter is not greater, and returns immediately if that call returned 0. Then it repeats the delivery for non-fragmented controls of strmin->inqueue whose mid equals last_mid_delivered + 1, +2, and so on, setting last_mid_delivered to each delivered mid (also when there is no socket), skips a fragmented control at the expected mid that has no first fragment yet, ends at the first control with another mid, and, if it ended on a fragmented control with first_frag_seen (last_mid_delivered set to its mid minus 1), calls sctp_deliver_reasm_check once more.
note: Reviewer right (r15): the INVARIANTS panic needs a nonzero on_strm_q that is neither ordered nor unordered (sctp_indata.c:5244-5254); r1 point about the socket NULL check is already in the prose. Slice 5061-5361 cuts the head (function at 5221).

name: sctp_process_cookie_existing
prose: Precondition: the TCB lock on stcb is held by the caller (stcb is non-NULL), m holds a COOKIE-ECHO chunk containing the cookie, offset locates that chunk, netp points to the association's current destination, and init_src, notification and the other arguments are valid. Postcondition: it returns either stcb, with the TCB lock still held, or NULL; the NULL returns either leave the TCB unlocked or free the association, with the exceptions noted. It returns NULL, after unlocking stcb, when the state is SHUTDOWN_ACK_SENT (it first sends SHUTDOWN-ACK and an operation error), when the INIT or INIT-ACK embedded in the cookie cannot be read or has the wrong chunk type, when both tags match but the INIT-ACK initial TSN differs from asoc->init_seq_number, when the case C tag combination applies (silent discard), when the association is OPEN, the peer supports NAT and an ABORT with the NAT collision cause is sent, when the case B tag combination applies but the initial TSN differs, and in the final catch-all; it returns NULL after sctp_abort_association (which disposes of the association itself) when sctp_process_init or sctp_load_addresses_from_init fails in any of the cases. When both tags match (case D) and the state is COOKIE_WAIT or COOKIE_ECHOED it processes the INIT, stops timers, moves to OPEN, sets *notification to SCTP_NOTIFY_ASSOC_UP and starts autoclose if enabled; in other states it changes nothing beyond timers; it then loads the peer addresses, discards old cookies, sends a COOKIE-ACK and returns stcb. In case B (our tag matches, the peer tag differs or is unset) it marks sent chunks for retransmission if the peer tag changed, processes the INIT, loads addresses, sets *notification to ASSOC_UP when coming from COOKIE_WAIT or COOKIE_ECHOED, sets OPEN, sends a COOKIE-ACK and returns stcb. When both tags differ from ours and the tie tags match the nonces (case A, peer restart) and the peer supports NAT it returns the result of sctp_process_cookie_new, unlocking stcb only if that result is NULL; without NAT it sets *notification to SCTP_NOTIFY_ASSOC_RESTART, resets sequence numbers, mapping arrays and the stream, control, asconf and pending queues (the TCB lock is released and reacquired together with the INP info and INP write locks), re-hashes the association under the new vtag, processes the INIT, loads addresses, sends a COOKIE-ACK and returns stcb; in this case the state becomes OPEN unless it was SHUTDOWN_SENT without SHUTDOWN_PENDING.
note: Real function (sctp_input.c:1346-1945) was dropped only because the slice 1604-1876 lacks its head; the old prose claim that the state always becomes OPEN with ASSOC_UP or ASSOC_RESTART was too broad (case D in OPEN, case A in SHUTDOWN_SENT), enumerated per case instead.

name: sctp_process_control
prose: Precondition: ch points to the first chunk header at *offset in the packet m of the given length, stcb is NULL or a locked association, netp points to the destination pointer, and the SCTP common header sh has been validated by the caller. Postcondition: returns a struct sctp_tcb pointer, either the association, still locked, or NULL, and updates *offset. *offset is set to length (the packet is finished) on most returns that stop processing, and otherwise advanced past each processed control chunk with the SCTP_SIZE32 padded length. It returns stcb (locked) when a chunk header length is below the minimum or a chunk extends past the end of the packet, when a chunk cannot be read from the mbuf, when an INIT or INIT-ACK is not the only chunk, after an authentication failure, for an unknown chunk with the discard bits, and when the loop ends normally (after sending an ASCONF-ACK if an ASCONF was processed). It returns NULL, with the association unlocked or freed (or abort-processed, or sctp_handle_abort having freed it), for a bad verification tag, an INIT with a nonzero tag or longer than SCTP_LARGEST_INIT_ACCEPTED, an out-of-the-blue packet without an association (sctp_handle_ootb), a failed COOKIE-ECHO, a SHUTDOWN, SHUTDOWN-ACK, SHUTDOWN-COMPLETE, OPERATION-ERROR, FORWARD-TSN, STREAM-RESET or SACK handler that asked for the association to be closed, and an INIT-ACK abort with abort_no_unlock; the exception is an ABORT chunk with a non-NULL stcb and a NULL *netp, which returns NULL at once without unlocking stcb (line 4806), and an ABORT with a destination returns NULL if sctp_handle_abort reports that the association is gone and stcb otherwise. The caller must not use stcb after NULL.
note: Reviewer right (r15): ABORT with stcb non-NULL and *netp == NULL returns NULL without SCTP_TCB_UNLOCK (sctp_input.c:4799-4806). Function is sctp_input.c:4309-5242; read all return statements; per-handler lock handling stated only for cases checked (4360-4366, 4482-4485, 4495-4499, 4597-4600, 4608-4611, 4851-4855, 4940-4947). name: sctp_send_str_reset_req
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the TCB lock on stcb (SCTP_TCB_LOCK_ASSERT); number_entries and list describe the streams of an incoming-reset request. Postcondition: returns EBUSY if asoc->stream_reset_outstanding is nonzero; EINVAL if none of send_in_req, send_tsn_req and add_stream is nonzero or if both send_in_req and send_tsn_req are nonzero; ENOMEM if number_entries is above (MCLBYTES - SCTP_MIN_OVERHEAD - sizeof(struct sctp_chunkhdr) - sizeof(struct sctp_stream_reset_out_request)) / sizeof(uint16_t), if no chunk can be allocated, or if the mbuf cannot be allocated (the chunk is freed in that case); and 0 otherwise. No association state is changed on an error return. On a 0 return it builds a STREAM RESET chunk addressed to the alternate or primary destination (taking a reference on it, held by the chunk): if send_in_req is nonzero it first adds an outgoing-reset request, counting it in asoc->stream_reset_outstanding only if sctp_add_stream_reset_out returns nonzero; if add_stream bit 1 is set and fewer than adding_o free slots remain in strmout it tries to enlarge the strmout array, and when SCTP_MALLOC fails it clears that bit and goes on without the out-stream request, so the chunk may end up carrying no request; it adds out-stream, in-stream, incoming-reset and TSN-reset requests as requested, incrementing stream_reset_outstanding once per request it adds in that part, sets asoc->str_reset to the chunk, appends it to asoc->control_send_queue (incrementing ctrl_queue_cnt), sends a SACK if asoc->send_sack is set and starts the SCTP_TIMER_TYPE_STRRESET timer on the chunk's destination. The caller keeps the TCB lock.
note: Reviewer right: precondition 'stream_reset_outstanding is zero' is a runtime check returning EBUSY (sctp_output.c:12171-12177), not an assumption; prose rewritten. Out-stream failure path 12257-12268 leaves chunk without that request but still queued. Slice 12168-12429 cuts the head (function at 12153).

name: sctp_lower_sosend
prose: Precondition: so is an SCTP socket; message data is supplied either through uio or, when uio is NULL, through the mbuf chain top (neither supplied gives EINVAL); addr, control and srcv are optional; the caller holds no TCB lock. Postcondition: the function has a single exit, label out/out_unlocked (lines 13762-13783), which returns the local variable error (0 on success). At the exit it releases the association-create lock if it applied it, and if stcb is non-NULL it returns the send-budget reservation (sb_send_resv) it took, drops the association reference (refcnt) it took if still applied, and releases the TCB lock; it then frees top and control if they are still non-NULL. Errors set by the code include EINVAL (neither uio nor top, bad sockaddr length, negative uio_resid, NULL inp, EOR requested without uio, a listening TCP-style endpoint, invalid sinfo flags, SCTP_ADDR_OVER without addr or with an unknown destination or wrong port, a destination socket that is gone, an IPv6 address on a socket not bound to IPv6, SCTP_ABORT before the association is up, zero-length data without SCTP_EOF, an invalid stream number or stream state, a stream locked to another stream), EAFNOSUPPORT (unsupported address family), ENOTCONN (the found association belongs to another endpoint, or the association is about to be freed, including after a wait), ENOENT (no association and no address, or SCTP_ABORT or a zero-length EOF for a nonexistent association), ECONNRESET (association aborted, also when found aborted while waiting), EMSGSIZE (message larger than the send limit or, with fragmentation disabled, the smallest MTU; an oversized abort reason), ENOMEM (abort reason mbuf), EAGAIN for some stream states, EWOULDBLOCK (non-blocking socket with no room), EPIPE (new message while a shutdown is in progress), ECONNABORTED (SCTP_EOF with an incomplete user message, after the association is aborted), and errors propagated from sctp_sendall, sctp_findassociation_cmsgs, sctp_aloc_assoc_connected, uiomove or sctp_copy_resume, sbwait, so_error, be.error and sctp_msg_append. Along the way it loops copying data from uio into the stream queue (waiting for send-buffer space, releasing and re-taking the TCB lock around sbwait and uiomove), may start a shutdown or an abort for SCTP_EOF or SCTP_ABORT (the abort paths set stcb to NULL so the exit does not unlock it), and ends by calling sctp_chunk_output or sctp_med_chunk_output when sending is permitted (queue_only, Nagle and peers_rwnd decide).
note: Slice 12986-13276 is the middle of sctp_lower_sosend (sctp_output.c:12560-13784; head cut), listed as dropped. Single return(error) at 13783, error assignments listed from grep of the whole function.

name: sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output
prose: Precondition: inp is the endpoint; stcb and net may be NULL; to is the destination sockaddr; m is a mbuf chain holding an SCTP common header and chunks but no IP header, and the function takes ownership of m. Postcondition: it returns 0 when the lower layer reports success, otherwise an errno, and m has been consumed in every case (freed here on the early error returns, passed to ip_output or ip6_output otherwise). It returns EFAULT, after freeing m, when net is non-NULL with SCTP_ADDR_OUT_OF_SCOPE set and when the destination address family is neither AF_INET nor AF_INET6 (or the family is not compiled in). When auth and stcb are both non-NULL it first fills in the AUTH chunk's HMAC digest. For AF_INET it prepends an IP header (plus a UDP header when port is nonzero), returning ENOMEM if the header mbuf cannot be allocated, EHOSTUNREACH if the cached source address is unusable and no other can be chosen, if source address selection fails, if the UDP tunneling port is 0 while port is set, or if a route cannot be obtained, and ENOMEM if SCTP_GET_HEADER_FOR_OUTPUT cannot prepend the output header; it computes the SCTP checksum in software for UDP-encapsulated packets and otherwise sets CSUM_SCTP for offload, calls ip_output and returns its result. For AF_INET6 it does the same with an IPv6 header, additionally returning EINVAL for some address-scope failures, the error of sa6_recoverscope, and the result of ip6_output. After the send it updates statistics, frees a temporary route when net is NULL, and may lower net->mtu and call sctp_pathmtu_adjustment when the route reports a smaller path MTU.
note: Slice 4076-4327 is the AF_INET branch of the static function sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output (sctp_output.c:3949-4615, head cut), listed as dropped. Returns checked: 4001,4039,4116,4131,4145,4182,4198,4266,4613.

name: sctp_arethere_unrecognized_parameters
prose: Precondition: in_initpkt is a mbuf chain holding an INIT or INIT-ACK chunk (cp points at its chunk header), param_offset is the offset of its first parameter, abort_processing and nat_friendly point to writable ints (nat_friendly is written without a NULL check), and cookie_found and edmid may be NULL. Postcondition: *abort_processing is set to 0 at entry, *cookie_found (if non-NULL) is cleared and set to 1 if an SCTP_STATE_COOKIE parameter is seen, and *edmid (if non-NULL) is set to SCTP_EDMID_NONE and then to the value of a well-sized zero-checksum-acceptable parameter. The function walks the parameters while at least a parameter header of bytes remains, and returns a mbuf chain of operational error causes or NULL (also NULL when allocation of the error mbuf fails). A parameter whose length is above the remaining length or below the header size, or whose padded size is invalid for its known type, sets *abort_processing to 1, frees any error chain built so far and returns a protocol-violation cause mbuf naming the type and length (or NULL if no parameter header could be read or the allocation fails). An SCTP_HOSTNAME_ADDRESS parameter sets *abort_processing to 1, discards the earlier chain and returns an unresolvable-address cause containing the parameter (or NULL if allocation or the copy fails). A parameter of an unknown type with the 0x4000 report bit adds an unrecognised-parameter cause to the chain (the chain is freed and discarded on allocation failure); with the 0x8000 bit clear the walk stops and the chain built so far is returned with *abort_processing still 0; with it set the parameter is skipped and the walk continues. Reaching the end of the parameters returns the chain, possibly NULL.
note: Slice 5101-5392 holds the tail of sctp_arethere_unrecognized_parameters (sctp_output.c:4914-5270, head cut) followed by the beginning of the next function; the dropped 'unnamed parameter-walk error builder' is this function. Returns: 5137 (hostname), 5223 (stop processing), 5233 (end), 5269 (invalid_size).

name: sctp_send_initiate_ack
prose: Precondition: inp is the endpoint, stcb is NULL or an association (when non-NULL its TCB lock is held and is temporarily released and reacquired while picking a new tag), init_pkt and init_chk locate the received INIT chunk, src, dst, sh and the flow arguments describe the received packet. Postcondition: the function returns nothing and sends at most one INIT-ACK. It builds the INIT-ACK itself in a newly allocated mbuf, together with the state cookie, and consumes that mbuf in every case: it frees it and sends nothing when the INIT-ACK mbuf, a pad mbuf or the cookie cannot be allocated or the socket is gone (inp->sctp_socket is NULL), when source address selection fails for the association's destination, and when sctp_add_cookie fails. When stcb exists in a state other than COOKIE_WAIT it instead sends an ABORT, without building an INIT-ACK, if the INIT carries addresses new to the association or the remote encapsulation port changed; it also sends an ABORT, with a generated cause if none exists, if sctp_arethere_unrecognized_parameters sets abort_flag or if the address family is not AF_INET or AF_INET6. The INIT-ACK reuses the association's tag and initial TSN in COOKIE_WAIT, INUSE or COOKIE_ECHOED, and otherwise gets a fresh tag and TSN; it carries the supported-extension, ECN, PR-SCTP, authentication, adaptation and NAT parameters as configured, any operational error returned by sctp_arethere_unrecognized_parameters, and the signed cookie. It is sent with sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output; on ENOBUFS it sets asoc->ifp_had_enobuf and bumps sctps_lowlevelerr, on success it clears ifp_had_enobuf (only when stcb is non-NULL), and sctps_outcontrolchunks is incremented after any send attempt.

name: sctp_med_chunk_output
prose: Precondition: the TCB lock on stcb is held (SCTP_TCB_LOCK_ASSERT), inp, stcb and asoc are valid, num_out and reason_code point to writable ints, now and now_filled describe a timestamp cache the function may fill in, and control_only, from_where, frag_point and so_locked are as supplied by the caller. Postcondition: *num_out is set to 0 and *reason_code to 0 on entry; the function returns 0 on every path except three ENOMEM returns (at lines 8160, 8387 and 8737, with *reason_code set to 8, 8 and 3 respectively). It returns 0 with *reason_code 9 when there is nothing to send (control queue empty or only ECN-echo chunks, no ASCONF chunks, send queue or unsent stream data), and 0 with *reason_code 8 when the control, ASCONF and send queues are all empty at the later check at line 7988. Otherwise it walks the destinations, bundles control chunks, ASCONF chunks and eligible data chunks into packets limited by the MTU, cwnd and peer window, and sends each packet with sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output. A failed lower-level send is not returned: it counts statistics, sets asoc->ifp_had_enobuf for ENOBUFS, moves chunks away from the destination for EHOSTUNREACH, records *reason_code 6 or 7 and moves on; at the end *reason_code is overwritten with 4 (nothing was sent and the code was still 0) or 5, so the final value is 4 or 5 unless the function returned earlier. *num_out counts chunks sent, *now and *now_filled are filled in when a timestamp is needed, sctp_clean_up_ctl is called before the normal return, and the TCB lock stays held. The local variable quit_now is not an output of this function.
note: Old prose wrong: it said the function returns the error of sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output with *reason_code 7 and that *quit_now is an output. Code: errors at 8225-8247 and 8866-8890 only set reason_code 6/7 and continue; the final lines 8942-8948 overwrite with 4/5 and return 0; quit_now (line 7857) is a local. name: sctp_load_addresses_from_init
prose: Precondition: stcb is a locked association; m is the packet and offset points at the first parameter of an INIT or INIT-ACK whose parameters end at limit; src, dst and altsa (an alternate source address that replaces src when non-NULL) and port describe the received packet. Postcondition: returns 0 on success and a negative value otherwise; the distinct negative values (-1 to -35, -100, -101) identify the failing step. It marks every existing net SCTP_ADDR_NOT_IN_ASSOC, adds the source address as a remote address if no association exists for it (returns -1 or -2 if sctp_add_remote_addr fails, -3 if the address belongs to another association, in which case that association's lock is released, and -4 if stcb->asoc.state is 0), then walks the parameters: it adds IPv4 and IPv6 addresses as remote addresses (clearing the not-in-association mark of ones already known and returning other negative values for failures such as an address owned by another association or a failed sctp_add_remote_addr), records supported features (ECN, PR-SCTP, auth, ASCONF, reconfig, NR-SACK, packet-drop, IDATA), takes the RANDOM, HMAC and CHUNK list parameters (returning negative values for malformed ones), and stops the walk at an unknown parameter whose upper bit is clear. Afterwards it removes remote addresses still marked not-in-association (reselecting the primary destination), turns off locally enabled features that the peer did not advertise, returns -31, -32 or -33 for inconsistent authentication or ASCONF parameters, builds the peer random key and installs it in asoc.authinfo.peer_random, returning -34 if the key cannot be allocated, clears the cached keys and returns 0.

Return list from 5989-6582: -1..-35, -100, -101, final 0. Parameter-level conditions only summarised where read; the early prose 'distinct negative error code' retained.

name: sys_sctp_generic_recvmsg
prose: Precondition: td is the calling thread and uap holds the user's descriptor, iovec array, optional sinfo, from, fromlenaddr and msg_flags pointers. Postcondition: the function returns an errno or 0, with the received byte count stored in td->td_retval[0] on the success paths. It returns getsock's error without dropping a file reference; returns the copyiniov error (EMSGSIZE limit) after dropping the file reference; after the iovec has been allocated every exit frees iov, and every exit after a successful getsock drops the file reference with fdrop. It returns EOPNOTSUPP if the socket is not an SCTP socket, the mac_socket_check_receive error with MAC, the copyin error for fromlenaddr or msg_flags, and EINVAL if the sum of the iov lengths overflows. It then calls sctp_sorecvmsg; if that returns an error and some data was already received and the error is ERESTART, EINTR or EWOULDBLOCK, the error is cleared; any other error is returned. When sctp_sorecvmsg returned 0 it copies sinfo out when uap->sinfo is set, returning the copyout error; this copy is skipped when the error was converted to 0 above. On success it sets td_retval[0] to the number of bytes received, copies the source address (truncated to the user's length) and its length out when fromlen and uap->from are set, and copies msg_flags out when uap->msg_flags is set, returning the first copyout error.
note: No function sctp_recvmsg exists in this file; slice 519-577 is the tail of sys_sctp_generic_recvmsg (sctp_syscalls.c:446-577, head cut). Old prose claimed iov freed and fp dropped on every path (not true for getsock/copyiniov failure) and did not note that sinfo copyout is skipped when an interrupted read with partial data is turned into success (lines 529-536).

name: sctp_threshold_management
prose: Precondition: stcb is non-NULL with its TCB lock held (KASSERT and SCTP_TCB_LOCK_ASSERT), inp is its endpoint, net may be NULL, and threshold is the association error limit. Postcondition: if net is non-NULL its error_count is incremented. When it then exceeds net->failure_threshold and SCTP_ADDR_REACHABLE is set in net->dest_state, SCTP_ADDR_REACHABLE, SCTP_ADDR_REQ_PRIMARY and SCTP_ADDR_PF are cleared and an interface-down notification is delivered; if it exceeds the threshold but the address is not marked reachable, nothing more happens to the destination state. Otherwise, when net->pf_threshold is below net->failure_threshold, error_count exceeds pf_threshold and SCTP_ADDR_PF is not set, SCTP_ADDR_PF is set, last_active is updated, a heartbeat is sent and the heartbeat timer is stopped and restarted. For a non-NULL net stcb->asoc.overall_error_count is incremented only if SCTP_ADDR_UNCONFIRMED is not set in net->dest_state; for a NULL net it is always incremented. If overall_error_count then exceeds threshold the association is aborted with sctp_abort_an_association and the function returns 1 (the caller must not use stcb afterwards); otherwise it returns 0.
note: Matches sctp_timer.c:84-157; the r2 reviewer point (notify only when REACHABLE was set) is in the code at line 98 and is stated explicitly. Slice 1-257 starts at file head, function at 84.

name: sctp_getopt
prose: Precondition: so is an SCTP socket; optval is a buffer of at least the size required by optname and *optsize holds its size. Postcondition: the function returns an errno value, 0 on success. It returns EINVAL at once, without touching *optsize, if optval is NULL or so->so_pcb is NULL. Otherwise it dispatches on optname: for each recognised option it checks the buffer size with SCTP_CHECK_AND_CAST (EINVAL if too small), finds the association where required (SCTP_FIND_STCB) and fills the buffer with the option value taking the appropriate lock, setting *optsize to the size of the option structure on success; options that need a bound-all endpoint, an association or a particular socket type give EINVAL otherwise, and an unrecognised optname gives ENOPROTOOPT. Any nonzero error causes *optsize to be set to 0 before the single return at the end; the buffer contents are then unspecified.
note: No function sctp_getsockopt exists; slice 1588-1847 is a fragment of the option switch inside sctp_getopt (sctp_usrreq.c:1504-3716, head cut). Returns verified: 1514, 1520, 3715 (only three returns); error => *optsize = 0 (3712-3714). Old claim '*optsize unchanged on error' was wrong. Per-option details not enumerated.

name: sctp_setopt
prose: Precondition: so is an SCTP socket; optval points to optsize bytes of option data and p is the calling thread. Postcondition: the function returns an errno value, 0 on success. It returns EINVAL at once if optval is NULL or so->so_pcb is NULL. Otherwise it dispatches on optname; for each recognised option it checks the buffer size with SCTP_CHECK_AND_CAST (EINVAL when too small), locates the association by id where the option is per-association, and updates either the endpoint defaults or the association (or all associations) under the corresponding lock. Several cases return directly: EPERM for SCTP_AUTO_ASCONF set to a nonzero value while the auto_asconf sysctl is off, EINVAL for SCTP_AUTO_ASCONF on a socket that is not bound-all, SCTP_I_WANT_MAPPED_V4_ADDR on a socket that is not bound to IPv6, SCTP_AUTOCLOSE on a TCP-style socket, and EINVAL for SCTP_PEER_ADDR_PARAMS with both heartbeat enable and disable flags, both PMTU-discovery flags, or a path MTU outside SCTP_SMALLEST_PMTU..SCTP_LARGEST_PMTU with PMTU discovery disabled; in those cases the TCB lock taken so far is released. An unrecognised optname returns ENOPROTOOPT; other failures return the error assigned in the case (for example EINVAL, EAFNOSUPPORT, ENOENT). The function returns the final value of error.

name: sctp_shutdown
prose: Precondition: so is a socket whose so_pcb is an SCTP endpoint (MPASS) and how is SHUT_RD, SHUT_WR or SHUT_RDWR. Postcondition: it returns EOPNOTSUPP, without waking waiters, if the endpoint is neither SCTP_PCB_FLAGS_TCPTYPE nor SCTP_PCB_FLAGS_IN_TCPPOOL; it returns ENOTCONN, also without waking waiters, if the socket is listening (setting so_error to ECONNABORTED and waking listeners unless how is SHUT_WR) or is none of connected, connecting or disconnecting. Otherwise, for SHUT_RD and SHUT_RDWR it sets SCTP_PCB_FLAGS_SOCKET_CANT_READ and empties the endpoint's read queue: each control is unlinked, its mbufs are accounted off the socket buffer, and, when the control is not on a stream queue, the control and its data are freed, while a control that is still on a stream queue is not freed and, if an association exists, its length is added back to size_on_all_streams; if any control that is not a notification was discarded and an association exists it aborts that association and returns ECONNABORTED; otherwise it calls sorflush and, for SHUT_RD, returns 0. For SHUT_WR, or SHUT_RDWR continuing, it calls socantsendmore and does nothing more if there is no association, if it is about to be freed, or if its state is not COOKIE_WAIT, COOKIE_ECHOED or OPEN; in the remaining cases it either sends SHUTDOWN and moves to SHUTDOWN_SENT (OPEN with empty queues), sets SHUTDOWN_PENDING, or aborts the association when a user message is incomplete and the send and sent queues are empty, then (unless it aborted) calls sctp_chunk_output; the result is 0. Every path after the entry checks, including the ECONNABORTED return, ends at label out, which wakes sleepers on so_timeo and returns error.

name: sctp_release_pr_sctp_chunk
prose: Precondition: the TCB lock on stcb is held, tp1 is the chunk of the message to abandon (first chunk found in stcb's sent queue for the message), sent says whether the message had been transmitted, and so_locked says whether the caller holds the socket lock. Postcondition: it first increments the abandoned counters (abandoned_sent if sent is nonzero or tp1 is not a first fragment, abandoned_unsent otherwise) for the association, the PR-SCTP policy and the stream. Starting at tp1 it walks forward through the sent queue until it has marked a chunk that is unfragmented or has the LAST_FRAG flag (or the queue ends); for each walked chunk it adds book_size to the returned size, and, if the chunk still has data, reduces the flight size and total flight when its sent state is below SCTP_DATAGRAM_RESEND, frees the buffer space accounting, adds send_size plus sctp_peer_chunk_oh to peers_rwnd, delivers SCTP_NOTIFY_SENT_DG_FAIL (sent set) or SCTP_NOTIFY_UNSENT_DG_FAIL, frees the data and updates the removable-chunk count; every walked chunk is set to SCTP_FORWARD_TSN_SKIP and stays on the sent queue. If the end of the message was not found, it takes the chunks of the same stream and message from the head of the send queue, adding their book_size to the result, freeing buffer space (without any flight or peers_rwnd change), notifying, freeing data, setting book_size to 0 and SCTP_FORWARD_TSN_SKIP and moving them to the tail of the sent queue. If the end is still not found and the stream out queue has a pending entry sp, it sets discard_rest on it, allocates a LAST_FRAG chunk carrying the next TSN on the sent queue if no send-queue chunk was found (if that allocation fails it skips the chunk and the message-id advance), otherwise sets the LAST_FRAG flag on the chunk and advances the stream's message id, and frees sp's data (adding sp->length to the result) and updates accounting. It wakes the sending socket if anything was freed and returns the total (int); the caller keeps its locks.
note: Reviewer right (r15): flight size and peers_rwnd are only adjusted for sent-queue chunks (sctputil.c lines 5100-5107); send-queue chunks only get buffer-space, notification and data free (5158-5167). First loop adds book_size even when tp1->data is NULL (5099). Slice 4881-5181 cuts the head (function at 5065).

name: sctp_sorecvmsg
prose: Precondition: so is an SCTP socket and uio non-NULL; mp, from, sinfo and msg_flags are optional; the caller holds no socket-buffer or read-queue lock. Postcondition: it returns an errno or 0, with a single exit at the end of the function. It returns EINVAL, without any lock held, if uio is NULL or MSG_PEEK is combined with a non-NULL mp, EOPNOTSUPP if MSG_OOB is set, EFAULT if so_pcb is NULL, and, after taking the socket receive I/O lock, the error of SOCK_IO_RECV_LOCK. While looking for data it returns 0 when the endpoint socket is gone or when the receive side is shut down with nothing available (end of file; nothing copied), so_error (cleared unless MSG_PEEK) when it is set and no data is available, ECONNRESET or ENOTCONN on a TCP-style endpoint that is not connected, EWOULDBLOCK for a non-blocking call without data, or the sbwait error. When data is available it takes the first suitable control from the read queue, copies data into uio (or hands mbufs to *mp), frees consumed mbufs and controls, may wait for more data when only part of a message has arrived, and returns the error of uiomove or of a wait, or 0. At the exit it stores out_flags in *msg_flags when msg_flags is non-NULL, sets serinfo_next_flags to SCTP_NO_NEXT_MSG when MSG_EOR is not set in out_flags, the call was not a peek, sinfo is given and extended receive info is enabled, releases the read lock, socket buffer lock and receive I/O lock it holds, drops the association reference and saves freed_so_far if it applied one, may send a window update through sctp_user_rcvd, and wakes the reader if wakeup_read_socket was set.
note: Reviewer (r15) right: the so_error return exists at sctputil.c lines 5617-5621 and 5631-5636; r1/r2 point that 0 can be returned at EOF with no data copied is stated. Function is 5511-6473; slice 5435-5707 holds the end of sctp_user_rcvd and the start of this function.

name: tcp_do_segment
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the inpcb write lock and is inside a network epoch (NET_EPOCH_ASSERT, INP_WLOCK_ASSERT), tp is a tcpcb in a state after TCPS_LISTEN and not TCPS_TIME_WAIT (KASSERTs), m holds the received segment, th points to its TCP header, drop_hdrlen is the header length to trim, tlen the payload length and iptos the TOS byte. Postcondition: the function returns nothing and consumes m on every path (it frees it, appends it to the socket receive buffer, or passes it to tcp_reass). It runs the segment through TCP input processing (SYN and RST handling, PAWS and options, window and sequence trimming, ACK processing with congestion control, RTT, SACK and fast recovery, window update, data queueing, FIN handling, and state changes), and may call tcp_output, tcp_close, tcp_drop, tcp_twstart or tcp_dropwithreset. It releases the inpcb write lock itself on the normal exit (INP_WUNLOCK at check_delack and dropafterack) and at the drop and dropwithreset labels when tp is non-NULL; it does not unlock where tp has been set to NULL by tcp_close or tcp_drop; and in the CLOSING and FIN_WAIT_2 cases that call tcp_twstart it returns without calling INP_WUNLOCK, tcp_twstart having released the lock. When tcp_close or tcp_drop frees tp the caller must not use it afterwards.
note: Reviewer (r15) wrong: tcp_do_segment does release the inp lock: INP_WUNLOCK at tcp_input.c lines 3390, 3418, 3425, 3435; it returns after tcp_twstart at 3071 and 3372 (tcp_twstart unlocks, tcp_timewait.c:185/190). Not read: every intermediate statement of this 1900-line function; ownership of m checked at the m_freem/sbappend/tcp_reass sites. Slice 1587-1839 cuts the head (function at 1519).

name: tcp_do_segment
prose: tcp_do_segment(tp, m, th, drop_hdrlen, tlen, iptos) is the main TCP input state machine for a segment on an existing connection; it returns void and always consumes m. The caller must hold the inpcb write lock inside a network epoch (NET_EPOCH_ASSERT, INP_WLOCK_ASSERT); tp->t_state must be after LISTEN and not TIME_WAIT (the two KASSERTs at tcp_input.c:1547-1550). It first drops (goto drop) a segment with both SYN and FIN when V_drop_synfin is set, and sends a reset (goto dropwithreset) for a segment with ACK in SYN_SENT whose acknowledgement is outside (iss, snd_max]. It then updates idle and receive time, scales the window, processes ECN and parses the TCP options, and goes through the state-dependent checks and processing (header prediction for the common established-connection cases, SYN_SENT and SYN_RECEIVED handling, PAWS/timestamp and sequence-window checks and trimming, RST handling, ACK processing, window update, data queueing via tcp_reass or direct append, FIN handling); this slice (lines 2113-2375 of the file) shows only the middle part of that logic. Along the way it may call tcp_drop or tcp_close, which can free tp, or tcp_twstart, after which it returns. The function leaves through one of these exits, all verified at tcp_input.c:3371-3438: (1) after tcp_twstart it returns; (2) check_delack: if TF_DELACK is set it is cleared and the delayed-ACK timer is armed, the inpcb write lock is released and it returns (m is consumed earlier on that path); (3) dropafterack: for SYN_RECEIVED with an out-of-range ACK it takes dropwithreset, otherwise it sets TF_ACKNOW, calls tcp_output, releases the inpcb lock and frees m; (4) dropwithreset: tcp_dropwithreset(m, th, tp, tlen) (which consumes m) and the inpcb lock is released if tp is non-NULL; (5) drop: the inpcb lock is released if tp is non-NULL and m is freed. After tcp_output at the end of normal processing (when needoutput or TF_ACKNOW) it falls into check_delack.
note: reviewer round15 wrong: the KASSERTs require state > LISTEN and != TIME_WAIT (tcp_input.c:1547-1550). Summary-level description of a ~1900-line function (1520-3438); only the opening and the exits were read in full

name: tcp_default_output
prose: tcp_default_output(tp) is the default stack's TCP output routine (the packet calls it tcp_output; tcp_output.c:186-1741). It decides whether and what to send for connection tp and sends at most the data allowed by the windows; it must be called with the inpcb write lock held inside a network epoch, and the mbuf for a segment is built inside the function. Return values: for a TCP-offload connection (TF_TOE) it returns tcp_offload_output(tp); for a TFO connection in SYN_SENT or SYN_RECEIVED that has already sent its SYN or SYN|ACK and is not retransmitting it returns 0; when it finds nothing to send (label just_return) it returns 0; if a UDP tunnelling port is set for the connection but the tunnelling port has been removed it returns EHOSTUNREACH (after unlocking the send buffer); otherwise it builds a segment and sends it with ip_output or ip6_output. If an error is produced when building or sending (EMSGSIZE when the IP header chain and the TCP header would not fit in one segment (RFC 7112 case), ENOBUFS for mbuf allocation failures, a failed TCP-MD5 digest calculation (the mbuf is freed), or the error from ip_output/ip6_output), control reaches the common 'out' code. There: if the segment had TH_RST it returns 0 whatever the error was (the sequence variables are not advanced). Otherwise, unless in persist-forced state, snd_nxt is advanced over the sent SYN, FIN and len bytes (a SACK retransmission instead pulls snd_nxt up to the scoreboard) and snd_max, the round-trip timing and the retransmit timer (or, for a zero-length send with queued data and no timers, the persist timer) are updated; in the persist-forced case only snd_max is advanced. After an ip_output error the advance is rolled back (including the SACK rxmit pointer and FIN) unless the send was a persist-forced one, the segment carried a SYN, or the error is EPERM. The error is then handled: EACCES and EPERM set t_softerror and return the error; ENOBUFS sets snd_cwnd to one segment and returns 0; EMSGSIZE clears TF_TSO if TSO was used and, when an MTU was learned from ip_output, updates the MSS and retries ('goto again'), else returns the error; EHOSTDOWN, EHOSTUNREACH, ENETDOWN and ENETUNREACH set t_softerror and return 0 if a SYN has been received (TCPS_HAVERCVDSYN) and return the error otherwise; every other error is returned. On success it counts the segment, updates rcv_adv and last_ack_sent, clears TF_ACKNOW and TF_DELACK, cancels the delayed-ACK timer and then loops ('goto again') if more data can be sent in the same call (sendalot), otherwise returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function is tcp_default_output (tcp_output.c:186), the file has no function named tcp_output; the slice is a fragment of it. Return paths verified at 227, 240, 758, 892, 1530, 1685-1721, 1740. Reviewers right: R1 (RST returns 0 even on output error; EPERM/SYN not rolled back), R2 (rollback for EACCES happens before the return), R15 (ENOBUFS returns 0)

Otherwise, unless in persist-forced state, snd_nxt is advanced over the sent SYN, FIN and len bytes (a SACK retransmission instead pulls snd_nxt up to the scoreboard) and snd_max, the round-trip timing and the retransmit timer (or, for a zero-length send with queued data and no timers, the persist timer) are updated; in the persist-forced case only snd_max is advanced. After an ip_output error the advance is rolled back (including the SACK rxmit pointer and FIN) unless the send was a persist-forced one, the segment carried a SYN, or the error is EPERM. The error is then handled: EACCES and EPERM set t_softerror and return the error; ENOBUFS sets snd_cwnd to one segment and returns 0; EMSGSIZE clears TF_TSO if TSO was used and, when an MTU was learned from ip_output, updates the MSS and retries ('goto again'), else returns the error; EHOSTDOWN, EHOSTUNREACH, ENETDOWN and ENETUNREACH set t_softerror and return 0 if a SYN has been received (TCPS_HAVERCVDSYN) and return the error otherwise; every other error is returned. On success it counts the segment, updates rcv_adv and last_ack_sent, clears TF_ACKNOW and TF_DELACK, cancels the delayed-ACK timer and then loops ('goto again') if more data can be sent in the same call (sendalot), otherwise returns 0.

name: tcp_reass
prose: tcp_reass(tp, th, seq_start, tlenp, m) queues an out-of-order segment on tp's reassembly queue and, when possible, delivers in-sequence queued data to the socket receive buffer. The caller holds the inpcb write lock. If th is NULL it only tries to deliver already queued data (used after the connection becomes established). Otherwise seq_start and tlenp must be non-NULL, th->th_seq must be >= rcv_nxt (KASSERTs), *tlenp is the payload length and m the segment's mbuf chain, which the function always consumes (queued, appended to so_rcv, trimmed or freed). Drops that free m and return 0, setting *tlenp = 0 where noted: a zero-length segment without FIN, or a FIN-only segment before the connection is established (m freed, *tlenp unchanged); the mbuf-count limit reached when the segment is not the next expected one on an established connection (tcps_rcvreassfull, *tlenp = 0); a FIN that would end before the last queued segment (*tlenp = 0); data after a queued FIN (*tlenp = 0); the queue length limit reached (*tlenp = 0); a failed uma_zalloc for a new queue entry (*tlenp = 0). A segment completely overlapped by an existing queued one is dropped with return 0 and *seq_start and *tlenp set to that queued segment's start and length. Segments that join, replace or prepend to an existing queued entry update *seq_start and *tlenp to the resulting entry's start and length. A segment equal to rcv_nxt on an established connection that reaches new_entry is appended directly to so_rcv (or freed if SBS_CANTRCVMORE), rcv_nxt is advanced, TF_WAKESOR is set and the function returns the segment's FIN flag (0 or TH_FIN) without setting *seq_start or *tlenp. A segment that becomes a new separate queue entry is inserted with *seq_start and *tlenp left unchanged. After queueing, the 'present' step runs: if the connection is not established or the head entry does not start at rcv_nxt it returns 0; otherwise under the receive buffer lock it removes and delivers consecutive queue entries starting at rcv_nxt (freeing the data if SBS_CANTRCVMORE), advances rcv_nxt, updates t_segqlen and t_segqmbuflen, sets TF_WAKESOR and returns the TH_FIN bit of the last entry delivered.
note: reviewer round15 right: *seq_start is not set on the new-entry queueing path (tcp_reass.c:954-1045) nor on the direct in-order append path (955-967). Old prose also wrongly said the queue-limit drop paths set no *tlenp; tcp_reass.c:516-1115. slice cut the head

name: bbr_output_wtime
prose: bbr_output_wtime(tp, tv) is the BBR stack's output routine (bbr.c:11859-14067); the slice shows an interior fragment of it. Its documented return value is 0 on success and an errno on failure to send; a 0 return may mean nothing was sent (for example when the connection is waiting on the hpts pacer); a non-zero value is the error from ip_output/ip6_output; negative values (-EFAULT and -ENETDOWN at bbr.c:13175 and 13796) are returned to make the caller drop the connection. Other exits: tcp_offload_output for offloaded connections, early 'return 0' paths when the connection is on the pacer or timers handled it (the timer result is returned as retval if negative, else 0), EHOSTUNREACH when the UDP tunnelling port was removed, and the final return of the accumulated error (after ENOBUFS is converted to 0). The part shown works out how much to send (len) from the scoreboard (rsm, sack_rxmit), the flags and the windows; if len is not positive no segment is sent and, depending on state, persist mode may be entered.

name: bbr_set_sockopt
prose: bbr_set_sockopt(tp, sopt) handles setsockopt for the BBR stack. For IPPROTO_IP and IPPROTO_IPV6 levels and for any option name that is not one of the listed TCP_RACK_* / TCP_BBR_* / TCP_DELACK / TCP_DATA_AFTER_CLOSE options it returns tcp_default_ctloutput(tp, sopt). For the listed options it drops the inpcb write lock, copies an int in with sooptcopyin (returning that error with the lock NOT re-taken), re-takes the lock and returns ECONNRESET (lock released) if the inpcb was dropped or ENOPROTOOPT (lock released) if tp no longer uses the BBR stack. It then applies the value inside a switch on the option name: simple options store optval into the matching bbr field; others validate it (for example TCP_DELACK accepts 0, 1 or 2..99 and gives EINVAL for 100 or more, and may send an immediate ACK; TCP_BBR_POLICER_DETECT, TCP_BBR_TMR_PACE_OH and TCP_BBR_PACE_OH return EINVAL in the Google mode restrictions shown) and set error to EINVAL when the value or the current mode does not allow the change, leaving the field unchanged. Each option increments its option counter. The remaining part of the function (not in the slice) releases the lock and returns the error. The packet name bbr_setopt_switch does not exist: the slice is the inner switch of bbr_set_sockopt.

name: bbr_log_ack
prose: bbr_log_ack(tp, to, th, prev_acked) processes the scoreboard (rc_map of bbr_sendmap entries) for an incoming ACK and returns the number of bytes newly acknowledged by SACK blocks (sack_changed, possibly 0). If the segment has RST it returns 0 at once without writing *prev_acked. Otherwise, if th_ack advances beyond snd_una it updates the progress time; cumulatively acknowledged entries are removed from rc_map and rc_tmap (a fully acked entry is freed with bbr_free; a partly acked entry has r_start moved up to th_ack), with RTT samples taken (bbr_update_rtt) for entries not already SACKed and with rc_sacked, rc_lost_bytes, rc_lost, rc_lt_lost, rc_holes_rxt and the rc_next and rc_sacklast markers adjusted; for a SYN-ACK with no map and a timestamp echo it derives an initial RTT sample. After that it detects a peer that reneged (bbr_peer_reneges), and if the options carry SACK blocks it filters and sorts the valid blocks (recording D-SACK blocks with tcp_record_dsack), and processes each with bbr_proc_sack_blk, setting r_wanted_output when SACK data changed. At the end *prev_acked is set to p_acked, which is the sum of the sizes of scoreboard entries that had been SACKed earlier and are now cumulatively acked (not the total number of bytes cumulatively acked); if SACK changed the state and the connection is not in recovery it checks whether to enter recovery (bbr_check_recovery_mode), sets r_wanted_output and rc_resend; in recovery it may set rc_resend. The caller keeps ownership of its arguments.

name: rack_do_syn_recv
prose: rack_do_syn_recv(m, th, so, tp, to, drop_hdrlen, tlen, tiwin, thflags, nxt_pkt, iptos) processes a segment for a RACK-stack connection in SYN_RECEIVED. By its contract a return of 1 means the TCB has been dropped/unlocked (probably gone) and m consumed, and 0 means the TCB is still locked. Paths: a RST, or a FIN when t_fin_is_rst is set, returns ctf_process_rst(...) unchanged; an ACK with ack <= snd_una or > snd_max logs TCP_EI_STATUS_RST_IN_FRONT, calls ctf_do_dropwithreset and returns 1; for a TFO connection, a segment with both SYN and ACK is dropped with reset and returns 1, a SYN (not the initial one) while a RXT, TLP or RACK timer is running is dropped with ctf_do_drop and returns 0 (without such a timer, processing continues), and a segment with none of ACK, FIN, RST is dropped with ctf_do_drop and returns 0; a PAWS failure calls ctf_ts_check, and if it reports the segment handled the function returns its ret_val; a sequence number below irs logs RST_IN_FRONT, drops with reset and returns 1; ctf_drop_checks reporting a drop returns its ret_val; otherwise (when those helpers return 0) processing continues. Without the ACK bit it returns rack_process_data(...) (calling rack_cc_conn_init first for TFO). With ACK it counts a connect, completes the socket connection, applies window scaling, moves the state to ESTABLISHED (or FIN_WAIT_1 if TF_NEEDFIN), advances snd_una for the ACK of the SYN, flushes queued data with tcp_reass when the segment carries no data or FIN, takes an RTT sample from the timestamp echo, then returns ret_val if rack_process_ack reports a drop; if the state is FIN_WAIT_1 and our FIN was acknowledged it moves to FIN_WAIT_2 (with the 2MSL timer and soisdisconnected when no more data can be received); finally it returns rack_process_data(...).
note: reviewers right: round2 (RST path is ctf_process_rst without logging), round15 (ctf_ts_check/ctf_drop_checks returning 0 means continue), original (return 0 after ctf_do_drop); rack.c:12899-13105

name: rack_do_compressed_ack_processing
prose: rack_do_compressed_ack_processing(tp, so, m, nxt_pkt, tv) handles a compressed-ACK mbuf holding between 1 and TCP_COMP_ACK_ENTRIES ACK entries for a RACK-stack connection (rack.c:15494-16164; the slice shows its middle part). Each entry is treated as one of a cumulative-ack advance, an ACK behind the cumulative point, a window update or a duplicate ACK; cumulative and window state are advanced, RTT and SACK scoreboard updates are done, and recovery and congestion-control state are updated as entries are processed. The function always consumes m. Return values: 1 when the connection has been closed or dropped (tcp_close returned NULL, tcp_drop on a progress timeout, tcp_twstart in CLOSING, tcp_close in LAST_ACK, or tcp_output returned a negative value); and 0 otherwise, in which case the TCB is still locked, and when nxt_pkt is non-zero the function returns 0 right after freeing m without sending output. When no further packet is pending, it may call tcp_output (when output is wanted, fast output is on or TF_ACKNOW is set), frees excess send-map entries and audits the timers before returning 0. A socket in a late state with no data left and TF2_DROP_AF_DATA set is reset by closing the connection and sending output from the closed state (the 'send_out_a_rst' path).

name: rack_get_pacing_delay
prose: rack_get_pacing_delay(rack, tp, len, rsm, segsiz, line) returns the pacing delay in microseconds (int32_t) to apply after sending len bytes; the slice shows its end. Besides computing the delay it may change pacing state: with hardware pacing enabled it may start, change or release a hardware rate (tcp_set_pacing_rate / tcp_chg_pacing_rate / tcp_rel_pacing_rate), set rc_pace_max_segs and r_ctl.crte, and update counters and logs. If rack->rc_always_pace is 0 (or the bandwidth estimate cannot be used, or the wanted rate is 0) the 'old method' is used: len divided by a per-ms rate derived from the cwnd and the minimum RTT or srtt, reduced by rack_slot_reduction, converted to microseconds and optionally adjusted by pace_to_fill_cwnd. With rc_always_pace set and a rate (fixed rate, delivery rate or an estimate from cwnd), the delay is derived from len and the wanted rate. In the part shown: when rack_limit_time_with_srtt is set and neither a fixed rate nor hardware pacing is in use, the delay is capped at the smoothed RTT (or RACK_INITIAL_RTO milliseconds converted to microseconds when there is no srtt); and when the hardware rate entry has seen ENOBUFS (rs_num_enobufs > 0), a boost delay (time_between times rack_enobuf_hw_boost_mult, limited to the range [rack_enobuf_hw_min, rack_enobuf_hw_max]) is added to the delay before it is returned. With rr_config 1 and a retransmission (rsm non-NULL) it returns rc_min_to without computing anything else. This tree adds a guard: a zero wanted rate falls back to the old method (bw division by zero avoided).

name: rack_fast_rsm_output
prose: rack_fast_rsm_output(tp, rack, rsm, ts_val, cts, ms_cts, tv, len, doing_tlp) sends a retransmission of the send-map entry rsm through the 'fast' path, using the mbuf offsets saved in rsm, with len bytes (normally one MSS) (the packet called it rack_output; the slice is the middle of this function, rack.c:18336-18878). On success it returns 0 after sending: it logs the output, counts the send (and TLP bookkeeping when doing_tlp), reduces the PRR send count, clears TF_ACKNOW and TF_DELACK, starts RTT timing if idle, and arms the hpts timer: with an ENOBUFS result the slot is (1 + rc_enobuf) ms, at least 10 ms (so the function still returns 0), otherwise the slot comes from rack_get_pacing_delay. A failure while building the segment (label failed) frees the partial mbuf and returns -1. Other errors from the output call do not change the return value 0.

name: rack_output
prose: rack_output(tp) is the RACK stack's output routine (rack.c:19582-22517; the packet slices show interior fragments). It runs with the inpcb write lock held inside a network epoch. Return values: for an offloaded connection tcp_offload_output(tp); 0 for a TFO connection in SYN_RECEIVED that has only sent its SYN|ACK, when the connection is in persist, when an ACK is required after a timeout, when the connection is on the hpts and the pacer should not be overridden, and after rack_start_hpts_timer for the TFO SYN case; when the timer processing (rack_process_timers) wants the connection dropped it returns the negative value it returned and otherwise 0; the fast-output path may return its result directly. If a segment is built and the output call fails: EPERM and EACCES set t_softerror and return the error; ENOBUFS arms a pacing slot of (1 + rc_enobuf) ms (at least 10 ms) and goes on with the normal tail, finally returning 0 (error is cleared at the end); EMSGSIZE clears TF_TSO if used, may update the MSS from a learned MTU and retry ('goto again') if the MSS shrank, otherwise starts the pacer with 10 ms and returns the error; ENETUNREACH, EHOSTDOWN, EHOSTUNREACH and ENETDOWN record a soft error and clear the error if a SYN has been received, then like other errors start the pacer with 10 ms and return the error. After a successful send it updates rcv_adv and last_ack_sent, clears TF_ACKNOW and TF_DELACK, computes the next pacing slot with rack_get_pacing_delay when appropriate (no further send after a RST), may set up fast output for the next segment, loops ('goto again') when more can be sent in this call, and finally makes snd_nxt at least snd_max, starts the hpts timer and returns the error (0 for success). The function also returns EHOSTUNREACH if a UDP tunnelling port was removed (rack.c:21268).

name: rack_inherit
prose: rack_inherit(tp, parent) is called when a new connection tp is created from a listening parent inpcb; it returns void. If the parent's stack (t_fb) is not the same as tp's, or either connection's RACK control block pointer is NULL, it only logs (tcp_log_socket_option) and returns. Otherwise it copies from the parent's RACK state to tp's each option field that differs (including turning on dgp via rack_set_dgp, the rxt options, pacing and measurement options, the data-after-close flag and the lesser-lt-bw flags), counting the changed fields in cnt, and logs the count with tcp_log_socket_option(tp, 0, cnt, 0). The comment says the parent should be read-locked while this runs; the function itself takes no lock.
