name: rack_timer_start
prose: rack_timer_start(tp, rack, cts, sup_rack) decides which RACK-stack timer to run and returns its timeout in microseconds, setting the matching PACE_TMR_* flag in rack->r_ctl.rc_hpts_flags. It returns 0 and changes nothing if rack->t_timers_stopped is set. If rack->rc_in_persist is set it returns rack_get_persists_timer_val(tp, rack) (which sets PACE_TMR_PERSIT; rc_on_min_to is not touched; it indexes tcp_backoff by t_rxtshift). Otherwise it clears rc_on_min_to. It then takes the retransmit (RXT) branch when the state is before ESTABLISHED, SACK is not permitted, the transmit-order list rc_tmap is empty or sup_rack is set; the RXT branch sets PACE_TMR_RXT only when snd_una < snd_max or the send buffer holds data, and returns tp->t_rxtcur reduced by the time since the last send or timer (or rc_min_to if it would not remain positive; at least 1), with a cap derived from the KEEPINIT timeout before establishment; if neither condition holds it returns 0 and sets no flag. Otherwise it picks the first entry of rc_tmap (the lowest un-SACKed one if that was SACKed). If that entry has SACK_PASSED, RWND_COLLAPSED or dupack >= DUP_ACK_THRESHOLD it uses the RACK timer: unless only a FIN is outstanding (then RXT) or, with PRR active in fast recovery and fewer than one segment of PRR credit, in which case it goes to the TLP branch, it computes a RACK threshold and returns the time until last send + threshold, or rc_min_to if that is not in the future or below the minimum (setting rc_on_min_to when r_rr_config == 3), and sets PACE_TMR_RACK. In the TLP branch (also reached for the PRR case) it falls back to the RXT branch when a TLP is in progress and the TLP count limit is reached, when there is no last entry in rc_tmap, when that entry holds the FIN, or when the TLP timeout would exceed TICKS_2_USEC(tcp_rexmit_max); otherwise it returns the TLP threshold minus the time since the last send (rc_min_to if that is not positive), at least rack_tlp_min and at least 1, and sets PACE_TMR_TLP. It takes no locks.
note: reviewer round15 right: PRR starvation goes to the TLP branch (activate_tlp, rack.c:6101-6114), not to RXT; round2 right: the persist path returns before rc_on_min_to is cleared (6011-6015); rack.c:5993-6218

name: rack_update_rtt
prose: rack_update_rtt(tp, rack, rsm, to, cts, ack_type, th_ack) tries to take an RTT sample from the send-map entry rsm; it returns 1 if a sample was accepted and 0 if not. It returns 0 immediately, changing nothing, if rsm is already RACK_ACKED or RACK_WAS_ACKED or r_no_rtt_allowed is set. If the entry was sent once (r_rtr_cnt == 1) it computes t from cts and the send time, updates tp->t_rttlow and rc_rack_min_rtt, passes a microsecond sample to the congestion control's rttsample callback if there is one, calls rack_apply_updated_usrtt and tcp_rack_xmit_timer (with confidence 2 for a SACKed entry, or computed from app-limited state for a cumulatively acked one), signals CC_NDUPACK for an acked TLP when not in fast recovery and rc_tlp_cwnd_reduce is set, updates rc_rack_tmit_time and rc_rack_rtt if this send is more recent, and returns 1. If the entry was retransmitted, it first sets t_rxtshift and t_softerror to 0 and recomputes t_rxtcur; then with a timestamp echo on a cumulative ack (and not RACK_OVERMAX) it finds which transmission the echo matches: for a match that is not the last transmission it returns 0 (spurious retransmission) after calling the CC callback, for a match on the last transmission it updates t_rttlow, rc_rack_min_rtt, rc_rack_tmit_time and rc_rack_rtt, calls tcp_rack_xmit_timer and returns 1; with no match, or when there is no timestamp, SACKed, or otherwise, it uses the last send time to compute t: if rc_rack_min_rtt is non-zero and t is smaller than it, it returns 0 (improper retransmit); if rc_rack_min_rtt is non-zero otherwise it only updates rc_rack_tmit_time and rc_rack_rtt when this send is newer (rc_rack_min_rtt is not changed there, because t is not below it) and returns 1; if rc_rack_min_rtt is 0 it returns 0.
note: reviewers right: round1 (ts_not_found commit does not touch t_rttlow or the xmit timer, also returns 0 with no min_rtt), round2 (early returns precede the rxtshift reset), round15 (rc_rack_rtt is also set in the no-timestamp path); rack.c:8716-8958

name: rack_need_set_test
prose: rack_need_set_test(tp, rack, rsm, th_ack, line, use_which) restarts the goodput (gput) measurement point after an ACK; it returns void and changes state only if TF_GPUTINPROG is set in tp->t_flags and rsm->r_end >= tp->gput_seq. If rsm was transmitted more than once (r_rtr_cnt > 1) it returns without any change. Otherwise it clears rack->app_limited_needs_set, sets tp->gput_ts to the receive time, and moves tp->gput_seq: to rsm->r_start when use_which is RACK_USE_BEG and r_start >= gput_seq; to rsm->r_end when RACK_USE_END and r_end >= gput_seq; and for RACK_USE_END_OR_THACK to th_ack if th_ack is beyond rsm->r_end, else to rsm->r_end. It sets rc_gp_output_ts to the first send time of the send-map entry found at gput_seq (when gput_seq < snd_max and an entry exists); otherwise to rsm's first send time and sets app_limited_needs_set to 1. If gput_seq is beyond gput_ack it recomputes gput_ack as gput_seq plus max(initial window, MIN_GP_WIN * maxseg) when rc_gp_filled is 0, else plus the measurement window. It clears measure_saw_probe_rtt when not in probe RTT, the flag is set and gput_seq >= rc_probertt_sndmax_atexit. If rc_gp_filled is set and the window gput_ack - gput_seq is smaller than max(initial window, MIN_GP_WIN * maxseg), it either clears TF_GPUTINPROG (when the ideal measurement window exceeds the data in the send buffer) or sets gput_ack to gput_seq plus the ideal window. It then calls rack_tend_gp_marks and rack_log_gpset.
note: reviewers right: original (rc_gp_output_ts from the entry at gput_seq), round2 (RACK_USE_BEG only if r_start >= gput_seq), round15 (max(rc_init_window, MIN_GP_WIN*maxseg), not just the initial window); rack.c:9020-9172

name: tcp_respond
prose: tcp_respond(tp, ipgen, th, m, ack, seq, flags) builds and sends one TCP segment (usually an ACK or RST) in reply to a segment or from a connection template; it returns void. tp and m must not both be NULL; ipgen points to the IPv4 or IPv6 header (its version selects the family) and th to the TCP header (inside m if m is non-NULL); the network epoch is entered and, if tp is non-NULL, the inpcb lock is held. If m is NULL it allocates a new header mbuf (returning silently if allocation fails) and copies the template headers from ipgen and th without swapping addresses or ports (the template is already addressed from this side), and forces flags to TH_ACK. If m is not writable or a UDP tunnelling port is in use, it allocates a new mbuf (freeing m and returning on failure of allocation or of m_dup_pkthdr), copies the headers into it with addresses and ports swapped, and frees m. Otherwise it reuses m: the chain after the first mbuf is freed and addresses and ports are swapped in place. The window is 0 for a RST, and otherwise the receive buffer space capped at TCP_MAXWIN << rcv_scale, shifted down by rcv_scale. It adds timestamp (and, with TF_SIGNATURE, TCP-MD5) options when tp is non-NULL and TF_NOOPT is clear (a failed TCP-MD5 signature frees the mbuf and returns), sets lengths, ECN bits, hop limit or TTL, checksums, logs a server RST via tcp_log_end_status when tp is non-NULL and TH_RST is set, updates TCP statistics, and sends the packet with ip_output or ip6_output, which consume the mbuf. The mbuf passed in is always consumed.
note: reviewer round15 right: the m == NULL branch does not swap addresses or ports (tcp_subr.c:1789-1822); tcp_subr.c:1726-2150, the output call at the end was not read

name: tcp_default_ctloutput
prose: tcp_default_ctloutput(tp, sopt) is the default TCP-level getsockopt/setsockopt handler (tcp_usrreq.c:2020-~2640; the packet calls it tcp_ctloutput; the slice is the tail of it). It is called with the inpcb write lock held for the connection tp; sopt describes a TCP-level option and sopt_dir is SOPT_SET or SOPT_GET. It returns 0 on success or an errno: EINVAL, EPERM, ENOPROTOOPT, EFAULT, ENOENT, EOPNOTSUPP, ECONNABORTED when INP_WLOCK_RECHECK finds the inpcb dropped after the lock was released for a copyin, or an error propagated from sooptcopyin, sooptcopyout, TCPMD5_PCBCTL, the tcp_log_* helpers, stats_blob_snapshot or the KTLS helpers. The inpcb write lock is released before it returns (by the function or, on some paths, by the helper it calls). The TCP_STATS option additionally unholds the pages it held and on success sets sopt_valsize to the snapshot size.
note: reviewer round15 right (ECONNABORTED from INP_WLOCK_RECHECK); only a prior summary of a large switch, errno list not fully re-verified

name: in6p_join_group
prose: in6p_join_group(inp, sopt) joins an IPv6 multicast group (optionally source-specific) for the socket's inpcb; it handles IPV6_JOIN_GROUP, MCAST_JOIN_GROUP and MCAST_JOIN_SOURCE_GROUP and returns EOPNOTSUPP for any other sopt_name. The caller holds inp's write lock. Before it takes IN6_MULTI_LOCK it can return, without releasing inp: the sooptcopyin error, EADDRNOTAVAIL (unknown interface index, or the interface is missing or not IFF_MULTICAST), EINVAL (non-AF_INET6 or wrong-length group or source sockaddr, source address that is multicast, or group address that is not multicast) and EOPNOTSUPP. After taking IN6_MULTI_LOCK it finds the inpcb's membership for the group; if none exists and IPV6_MAX_MEMBERSHIPS are already joined it fails with ENOMEM; if one exists, a join with a source on an exclusive-mode membership fails with EINVAL, a join with a source already in the filter list fails with EADDRNOTAVAIL, and a join without a source fails with EADDRINUSE. Otherwise a new filter is allocated for a new membership (ENOMEM on failure), the source (if any) is grafted into the include list (ENOMEM on failure), and for a new membership it takes a reference on inp, drops the inp lock, calls in6_joingroup_locked, re-takes the lock and returns ENXIO if the inp was freed meanwhile, or the join error; for an existing membership it merges the filter state (in6m_merge) and calls mld_change_state. On success the filter state is committed (so a join with a source on an existing inclusive membership just adds a source) and it returns 0. On all paths after IN6_MULTI_LOCK it releases the inp write lock (unless the inp was freed) and IN6_MULTI_LOCK, and frees an unused new filter.
note: reviewer round2 wrong: the function does release inp's write lock (out_in6p_locked: INP_WUNLOCK, in6_mcast.c:2185-2187); round15 right (the precondition on sopt_name contradicts the EOPNOTSUPP return); original right (existing inclusive membership with a source only adds a source); in6_mcast.c:1899-2200

name: ip6_tryforward
prose: ip6_tryforward(m) is the IPv6 fast-forwarding path (ip6_fastfwd.c:96-331). It returns the mbuf m unchanged when the packet must go through the slow path in ip6_input (broadcast/multicast mbuf, hop-by-hop options, multicast, link-local or unspecified source or destination, or a destination that is a local address) or when a firewall hook sets M_FASTFWD_OURS (both before and after the outgoing hook); otherwise it returns NULL, after either forwarding the packet with the output interface's if_output or dropping it. The packet is dropped (and freed unless an ICMPv6 error consumed it) for: zero payload length (jumbogram), packet shorter than the IPv6 header's payload length, hop limit of 1 or less (ICMPv6 time exceeded, unless ip6stealth), pfil rejection, no route (ip6_findroute), and packets larger than the next hop's MTU (ICMPv6 packet too big); over-long packets are trimmed. A packet filter may change the destination or attach a next hop, in which case the route lookup is redone. On the forward path it decrements the hop limit (unless ip6stealth), completes delayed TCP/UDP and SCTP checksums if the interface does not do them, and calls if_output, updating the forward or discard statistics according to its result. The slice shows the tail of the function.
note: slice cut the head; real function ip6_tryforward (the packet name ip6_forward is a different function in ip6_forward.c); old prose said NULL was always returned on success and failure but m is returned for the slow path cases

name: ip6_process_hopopts
prose: ip6_process_hopopts(m, opthead, hbhlen, rtalertp, plenp) walks the options of an IPv6 hop-by-hop options header (the packet name ip6_hbh_options does not exist; ip6_input.c:1019-1143). opthead points into m's data and the bytes opthead..opthead+hbhlen must be contiguous. Pad1 and PadN options are skipped (a PadN's declared length is not checked against the remaining length; a final option that overruns simply ends the loop with 0). A Router Alert option stores its 16-bit value in host order in *rtalertp. A Jumbo Payload option stores its length in *plenp. Unknown options are passed to ip6_unknown_opt according to the option's action bits (skip, silently discard, ICMP even if multicast, or ICMP if not multicast). It returns 0 on success (m not freed). It returns -1, with m freed either by m_freem or by icmp6_error, when: an option with fewer bytes remaining than its minimum header length (PadN, Router Alert, Jumbo or unknown option) is found (counted as toosmall, m_freem); a Router Alert or Jumbo option has the wrong length (ICMP parameter problem); a Jumbo option appears while the IPv6 header's payload length is non-zero; a second Jumbo option is found (*plenp already non-zero); a Jumbo length is 65535 or less; or ip6_unknown_opt requests discarding.
note: reviewer round15 right: PadN/unknown option lengths that exceed hbhlen are not rejected; the loop just ends and 0 is returned (ip6_input.c:1029-1040, 1136-1138)

name: ip6_output
prose: ip6_output(m0, opt, ro, flags, im6o, ifpp, inp) sends an IPv6 packet (ip6_output.c:403-1294; the packet shows two interior fragments). It always consumes m0 and the extension-header mbufs it builds, except that some failure returns before the packet is queued are described below. Errors and exits: EOPNOTSUPP for an unspecified source address without IPV6_UNSPECSRC or a multicast source address; EINVAL when the packet options contain a routing header (routing headers are rejected unless RTHDR_SUPPORT_IMPLEMENTED is defined, which it is not here) or when the hop-by-hop options processed for a locally sourced packet are invalid; ENOBUFS when an extension header cannot be copied or built; EHOSTUNREACH for route or scope lookup failures; ENETUNREACH for multicast on an interface that is not IFF_MULTICAST; EACCES when the output packet filter drops the packet; 0 when a packet filter consumes the packet, when multicast forwarding or loopback consumes it, when the packet is queued with netisr_queue for local delivery (returning that call's result), or when it is sent; EMSGSIZE when DONTFRAG applies and the packet is larger than the link MTU, when the path MTU is below IPV6_MMTU, for a jumbo payload that would need fragmenting, or when a fragment would be smaller than 8 bytes; and the error returned by in6_selectroute, mb_unmapped_to_ext (ENOMEM mapped to ENOBUFS), ip6_output_send or ip6_fragment. If ifpp is non-NULL it is set to the output interface after routing succeeds. A destination changed by a packet filter, or a changed FIB, causes the route lookup to be redone. An unfragmented packet is sent with ip6_output_send. If fragmentation fails, the fragments already made are freed (not sent) and the non-zero ip6_fragment error is returned; otherwise each fragment is sent with ip6_output_send, and after the first send error the remaining fragments are freed and that error is returned; ip6s_fragmented is counted only when every fragment was sent.
note: slice cut the head; reviewer round15 right: a fragmentation or fragment-send error frees the fragments and returns non-zero (ip6_output.c:1248-1279); the mb_unmapped_to_ext failure return at line 1114 relies on that helper freeing the chain, not verified here

name: ip6_ctloutput
prose: ip6_ctloutput(so, sopt) handles getsockopt and setsockopt at the IPPROTO_IPV6 level and a few SOL_SOCKET options for IPv6 sockets (ip6_output.c:1576-~2400). The inpcb is obtained with sotoinpcb(so) and the caller holds no inpcb lock; locks are taken inside as needed. It returns 0 on success, or an errno such as EINVAL, ENOPROTOOPT, EOPNOTSUPP, EPERM, ENOBUFS, EISCONN, EFAULT or one propagated from sooptcopyin, soopt_mcopyin, sooptcopyout, sosetfib, ip6_pcbopts, ip6_pcbopt, ip6_setmoptions or IPSEC_PCBCTL. An unhandled option name at the IPPROTO_IPV6 level returns ENOPROTOOPT, and an invalid sopt_dir returns EINVAL. Setting the options IPV6_HOPLIMIT, IPV6_TCLASS, IPV6_DONTFRAG, IPV6_USE_MIN_MTU, IPV6_PREFER_TEMPADDR and the advanced-API packet options returns ECONNRESET, with the inpcb write lock released, when the inpcb has been dropped. For IPV6_2292PKTOPTIONS/IPV6_PKTOPTIONS set, the option mbuf m obtained with soopt_getm is freed after ip6_pcbopts, but if soopt_getm or soopt_mcopyin fails the function breaks out with the error and m is not freed by this code. For SOPT_GET most values are copied out with sooptcopyout, and IPV6_2292PKTOPTIONS/IPV6_PKTOPTIONS get a size of 0.
note: reviewers right: round2 (ENOPROTOOPT / EINVAL rather than EOPNOTSUPP for unhandled names and bad directions), round15 (the mbuf is not freed when soopt_mcopyin fails, ip6_output.c:1663-1673); original (EFAULT from the copy routines); the full errno list of the old prose was not re-verified line by line and is replaced by this shorter summary

name: ip6_output
prose: ip6_output(m0, opt, ro, flags, im6o, ifpp, inp) sends an IPv6 packet (ip6_output.c:403-1294; the packet shows two interior fragments). It always consumes m0 and the extension-header mbufs it builds, except that some failure returns before the packet is queued are described below. Errors and exits: EOPNOTSUPP for an unspecified source address without IPV6_UNSPECSRC or a multicast source address; EINVAL when the packet options contain a routing header (routing headers are rejected unless RTHDR_SUPPORT_IMPLEMENTED is defined, which it is not here) or when the hop-by-hop options processed for a locally sourced packet are invalid; ENOBUFS when an extension header cannot be copied or built; EHOSTUNREACH for route or scope lookup failures; ENETUNREACH for multicast on an interface that is not IFF_MULTICAST; EACCES when the output packet filter drops the packet; 0 when a packet filter consumes the packet, when multicast forwarding or loopback consumes it, when the packet is queued with netisr_queue for local delivery (returning that call's result), or when it is sent; EMSGSIZE when DONTFRAG applies and the packet is larger than the link MTU, when the path MTU is below IPV6_MMTU, for a jumbo payload that would need fragmenting, or when a fragment would be smaller than 8 bytes; and the error returned by in6_selectroute, mb_unmapped_to_ext (ENOMEM mapped to ENOBUFS), ip6_output_send or ip6_fragment. If ifpp is non-NULL it is set to the output interface after routing succeeds. A destination changed by a packet filter, or a changed FIB, causes the route lookup to be redone. An unfragmented packet is sent with ip6_output_send. If fragmentation fails, the fragments already made are freed (not sent) and the non-zero ip6_fragment error is returned; otherwise each fragment is sent with ip6_output_send, and after the first send error the remaining fragments are freed and that error is returned; ip6s_fragmented is counted only when every fragment was sent.
note: slice cut the head; same function as the other ip6_output fragment

name: mld_v2_enqueue_group_record
prose: mld_v2_enqueue_group_record(mq, inm, is_state_change, is_group_query, is_source_query, use_block_allow) appends an MLDv2 group record for membership inm to the report queue mq; the caller holds the IN6 multicast list lock. It returns the number of bytes appended (nbytes), 0 when nothing needed to be appended (no change to report, or a source query that finds no recorded sources), or a negative errno (-ENOMEM) when the queue is full or an mbuf allocation or m_append fails; when only the filter list changed it returns the result of mld_v2_enqueue_filter_change instead. The record type is chosen from the old and new filter modes (a current-state record when is_state_change is 0). It appends to the tail packet of mq if is_group_query is 0, the packet has room and fewer than MLD_V2_REPORT_MAXRECS records, otherwise it allocates a new packet; then it appends the group record and as many in-mode sources (recorded ones only when is_source_query) as fit; further packets are allocated for remaining sources. On -ENOMEM, a packet that was allocated by the failing step is freed if it is not the reused tail packet, but packets already enqueued in earlier steps stay in the queue. The returned byte count adds the sources of the first packet twice (once per source and again after the loop), so it overstates the data by msrcs * sizeof(struct in6_addr) for that first packet.
note: reviewer round15 right on both points: packets enqueued before the failure remain in the queue, and nbytes counts first-packet sources twice (mld6.c:2541 and 2549); mld6.c:2295-2640

name: nd6_na_input
prose: nd6_na_input(m, off, icmp6len) processes an ICMPv6 neighbor advertisement; it returns void and consumes m on every path. The caller is in the network epoch (assert); m_pkthdr.rcvif is the receiving interface. The mbuf is freed without further action for fragmented packets, invalid ND options, NAs for a CARP address when we are not the CARP master, NAs for our own addresses (a tentative address calls nd6_dad_na_input, any other own address is logged), a missing neighbor entry, and static entries. A hop limit other than 255, a multicast target, a solicited advertisement sent to a multicast destination, a failed in6_setscope or a target link-layer address option of the wrong length is counted as a bad NA (icp6s_badna) and freed; a failed m_pullup frees the chain and returns. For an entry that is INCOMPLETE it records the link-layer address (an NA without a link-layer option is ignored on links that have addresses), sets the state to REACHABLE if solicited, STALE otherwise, remembers the router flag and, if the router flag is set, calls pfxlist_onlink_check() at the end. For other entries it applies the override/solicited/lladdr rules of RFC 4861 (changing the address, state and, when the router flag was dropped, removing the default router or flushing routes); pfxlist_onlink_check is not called in that case. It resets la_asked, grabs the hold chain, and at the end unlocks the entry, flushes the hold chain (and the children's chain after resolving an INCOMPLETE entry) and frees m.
note: reviewer round15 right: pfxlist_onlink_check() is only called when checklink was set in the INCOMPLETE branch (nd6_nbr.c:826, 942-943); original precondition about ln was wrong because ln is a local; nd6_nbr.c:649-954

name: defrouter_select_fib
prose: defrouter_select_fib(fibnum) chooses and installs the default router for one FIB; it returns void. If fibnum is RT_ALL_FIBS it calls itself for every FIB from 0 to rt_numfibs - 1 and returns. Otherwise, holding the ND6 read lock and the network epoch, it does nothing if the default router list is empty. It scans the list considering only routers whose ifp->if_fib equals fibnum: the first reachable one (is_dr_reachable) becomes selected_dr and the router marked installed becomes installed_dr (a second installed router is logged as an error); each is referenced. If no router was found reachable, it scans forward through the list (TAILQ_FOREACH_FROM, no wraparound) starting at the head when no router is installed or the installed one is the last list entry, otherwise at the entry after the installed router, and selects the first router found for this FIB (none if there is no such router). If a reachable router was selected and an installed router exists, the installed router is kept when it is still reachable and rtpref(selected) <= rtpref(installed). After dropping the ND6 lock, if the selected and installed routers differ it deletes the installed router's route (defrouter_delreq) if there is one and adds the selected router's route (defrouter_addreq) if there is one. It then releases the temporary references it took. No routing change is made when no router for fibnum is found.
note: reviewers round2 and round15 wrong: the fallback loop checks dr->ifp->if_fib == fibnum for every entry from the start point on (nd6_rtr.c:1021-1027), so it cannot select a router of another FIB; original right (no-op when no router matches); nd6_rtr.c:952-1053

name: rip6_input
prose: rip6_input(mp, offp, proto) delivers a received IPv6 packet to the raw sockets that match it; it always returns IPPROTO_DONE and always consumes the mbuf *mp (the pointer is not changed). The caller is in the network epoch. It iterates over the raw IPv6 PCBs matching protocol and addresses (each locked for reading). For each PCB it skips the socket if the IPsec policy check fails, if a jailed socket without its own vnet is not permitted the destination address, if it is bound to another FIB (unless V_rip_bind_all_fibs), or if it has multicast options that filter out a multicast destination (MLD traffic with M_RTALERT_MLD is exempt), and skips it if m_copym fails. If the PCB has a checksum offset set and the checksum is bad, the PCB lock is released, proto is set to IPPROTO_NONE and the whole loop stops (so remaining PCBs get no copy, while copies already delivered stay). Otherwise it copies the packet, saves control information if the socket wants it, strips the headers and appends the data with the source address to the socket's receive buffer; if sbappendaddr fails it calls soroverflow, frees the copy and counts rip6s_fullsock, else it wakes the reader and counts the delivery. If no socket received a copy, it counts rip6s_nosock and frees m: with proto == IPPROTO_NONE it is freed silently, otherwise icmp6_error sends a parameter problem (unrecognised next header) and consumes it; ip6s_delivered is decremented. If at least one socket received a copy, m is freed.
note: reviewer round15 right (sbappendaddr failure drops that copy and calls soroverflow, raw_ip6.c:302-308); also a bad checksum ends the iteration (244-246); slice cut the head; real function rip6_input (raw_ip6.c:183-329)

name: sctp6_getaddr
prose: sctp6_getaddr(so, sa) fills the sockaddr_in6 at sa with the socket's local address and returns 0 or an errno. It first zeroes the whole structure and sets sin6_len and sin6_family = AF_INET6 (so on every error return the port and address fields are zero, except where noted). It returns ECONNRESET if the socket has no SCTP inpcb. With the inpcb read-locked it sets sin6_port to the local port. For a bound-all socket that is connected, it takes the first association, finds the first of its nets with an IPv6 address and sets sin6_addr from sctp_source_address_selection (left zero if that returns no address); with no association or no IPv6 net it returns ENOENT (sin6_port already set). For a bound-all socket that is not connected, sin6_addr is the unspecified address. For a socket not bound to all, sin6_addr is the first IPv6 address in the local address list, or ENOENT if there is none (port already set). After releasing the lock it calls sa6_recoverscope and returns its error if non-zero (the port and address have then been written); otherwise it returns 0.
note: reviewers right: original (sa6_recoverscope error return; port already set on ENOENT) and round15 (the initial compound literal zeroes all fields, sctp6_usrreq.c:897-900); sctp6_usrreq.c:889-979

name: sctp6_peeraddr
prose: sctp6_peeraddr(so, sa) fills the sockaddr_in6 at sa with the peer's address and returns 0 or an errno. It first zeroes the whole structure and sets sin6_len and sin6_family = AF_INET6. It returns ENOTCONN if the socket has no SCTP inpcb or the inpcb is not connected, and ECONNRESET if the connected inpcb has no association. Otherwise it takes the first association (holding its TCB lock), finds the first net with an IPv6 address and copies that address and the association's remote port into sa, then releases the TCB lock. If no net has an IPv6 address it returns ENOENT (port and address stay zero). It then calls sa6_recoverscope and returns its error if non-zero (the port and address have already been written), else 0.
note: reviewers right: original (sa6_recoverscope error) and round15 (all fields are zeroed first, sctp6_usrreq.c:992-995); sctp6_usrreq.c:982-1036

name: udp6_send
prose: udp6_send(so, flags_arg, m, addr6, control, td) sends a UDP or UDP-Lite datagram on an IPv6 socket (the packet's name udp6_sendto does not exist; udp6_usrreq.c:676-981). The function takes the inpcb lock itself (write lock when addr6 is NULL, or when the socket has no local address and no local port, otherwise a read lock) and enters the network epoch for the output part; the caller must not hold the inpcb lock. It always consumes m and control. Errors: EAFNOSUPPORT if addr6 is not AF_INET6, EINVAL for a wrong sa_len or an IPv6-only socket given a v4-mapped destination, the error from sa6_embedscope, the error from ip6_setpktopts, EADDRNOTAVAIL for destination port 0, EISCONN if a destination is given on a connected socket, the error from in6_selectsrc_socket, the error from in6_pcbsetport (with the inpcb local address reset to in6addr_any), ENOTCONN if addr6 is NULL on an unconnected socket, ENOBUFS if the header cannot be prepended, and the error from ip6_output. On a non-IPv6-only socket, if the destination (or the connected address) is v4-mapped, the lock is released and the datagram is handed to udp_send with PRUS_IPV6 added to the flags, returning its result. On success it builds the UDP header (UDP-Lite coverage handling), the IPv6 header and checksum and calls ip6_output, returning its result. On every path the inpcb lock is released and the epoch exited before returning, any control mbuf has its packet options cleared and is freed, and m is freed on failure paths (consumed by ip6_output on the send path).
note: slice cut the head; the real function is udp6_send; old prose wrongly required the caller to hold the inpcb write lock and omitted the validation, v4-mapped and lock-selection steps (udp6_usrreq.c:692-796)

name: frrequest
prose: frrequest(softc, unit, req, data, set, makecopy) handles ioctl requests that add, insert, remove or zero IPFilter rules (fil.c:4439-~5100; the packet's name for the slice is an unnamed fragment of this function). If makecopy is non-zero, data is a user rule: it is copied in with ipf_inobj, and the function returns the copyin error, EINVAL if the rule is a built-in type, shorter than frentry_t, has a size not equal to sizeof(frentry_t) plus the name length, or a name length outside 0..ipf_max_namelen, and ENOMEM if the rule buffer cannot be allocated; the copied rule has its list pointers cleared and FR_COPIED set, and each name string in it is validated (EINVAL on failure, via donenolock which frees the copy). If makecopy is zero, data is a kernel (built-in) rule and EINVAL is returned if it is not marked built-in. Further checks (data size and pointer consistency, and so on) give EINVAL. For a zero-statistics request (OP_ZERO) the matching rule's counters are copied out to the caller and zeroed only if the copy out succeeded, ESRCH if no rule matches, EFAULT on a failed copyout, the temporary copy freed and the ipf_mutex released before returning. Add and insert requests place the rule in the list or group chosen by its fr_collect field. The slice shown is a middle fragment; the ipf_mutex write lock taken in the function is released on its return paths.
note: summary-level; only the start (4439-4555), the zero path (4960-5011) and the return list were read in full, not every validation step

name: ipf_token_find
prose: ipf_token_find(softc, type, uid, ptr) looks up or creates a token for the tuple (ptr, type, uid) in softc's ipf_token list and returns it with a reference held for the caller, or NULL. It first allocates and zeroes a new token (KMALLOC) in case it is needed, then takes the ipf_tokens write lock and searches the list for a token with the same context pointer, type and uid and with ipt_complete < 2. If none is found it uses the new token (setting ipt_ctx, ipt_uid, ipt_type and ipt_ref = 1), or returns NULL (releasing the lock) if the allocation had failed. If one is found the spare allocation is freed; if the found token has ipt_complete > 0 (that is 1) the result is NULL; otherwise the token is unlinked from its position. A token to be returned is appended at the tail of the list, its ipt_ref is incremented (so a new token ends with 2) and ipt_die is set to ipf_ticks + 20. The lock is released before returning.
note: slice cut the head; real function ipf_token_find (fil.c:7537-7587); prose from the earlier round verified

name: ipf_frag_deref
prose: ipf_frag_deref(arg, frp[, lock]) is a static function (the lock parameter exists only with USE_MUTEXES) that drops one reference on a fragment-cache entry. It reads the entry from *frp and sets *frp to NULL unconditionally (so the caller can no longer use the pointer, even when the entry is not freed), takes the lock for writing, decrements the entry's ipfr_ref, and calls ipf_frag_free(softf, entry) if the count is now zero or less; then it releases the lock. It returns void.
note: slice cut the head; ip_frag.c:1275-1292

name: ipf_log_items
prose: ipf_log_items(softc, unit, fin, items, itemsz, types, cnt) appends one log record built from cnt items (copied with bcopy for type 0 and with COPYDATA from an mbuf for type 1, after an iplog_t header with magic, sequence number, size and kernel time) to the log queue of the device unit. It returns 0 on success and -1 when the record is not logged. It raises the spl level, takes ipl_mutex[unit] and increments ipl_counter[unit] (on every path). If the used log space plus the record length would exceed the log size, or the buffer cannot be allocated, it increments ipl_logfail[unit], releases the mutex and returns -1 (this path does not restore the saved spl level). Otherwise it copies the items; if suppression is enabled (ipl_suppress) and fin is non-NULL with fin_off == 0 and the previous record (ipll[unit]) exists with the same CRC and the first FI_LCSIZE bytes of fin equal, it increments that previous record's count, releases the mutex, restores the spl level, frees the new buffer and returns 0. In all other cases it saves fin's data for the next comparison (or clears it when suppression is on and fin does not qualify), counts ipl_logok, links the new record at the tail, adds its length to ipl_used[unit], releases the mutex, wakes readers (WAKEUP and POLLWAKEUP, or cv_signal and pollwakeup on Solaris), restores the spl level and returns 0; the queue then owns the buffer.
note: slice cut the head; real function ipf_log_items (ip_log.c:506-616); prose checked

name: ipf_nat_ioctl
prose: ipf_nat_ioctl(softc, data, cmd, mode, uid, ctx) is IPFilter's NAT ioctl handler (ip_nat.c:973-~1500; the slice shows its first part). On FreeBSD it returns EPERM if FWRITE is set in mode and securelevel is 3 or higher, and EOPNOTSUPP for a jailed caller without a vnet. getlock is false when NAT_LOCKHELD is set in mode. For SIOCADNAT, SIOCRMNAT and SIOCPURGENAT the rule (an ipnat_t) is read from data (copied with ipf_inobj/ipf_inobjsz unless NAT_SYSSPACE is set): EFAULT-type errors from the copy routines are returned, EINVAL for in_size smaller than ipnat_t, in_size different from sizeof(ipnat_t) plus in_namelen, in_namelen out of range or invalid name strings, ENOMEM if the rule buffer cannot be allocated, and the error from ipf_nat_rule_init; the rule is then looked up in the NAT rule list under ipf_nat_io. SIOCADNAT needs FWRITE (EPERM otherwise), returns EEXIST (copying the found rule out first) if an identical rule exists, ENOMEM if there is no copied rule, and otherwise calls ipf_nat_siocaddnat to link it in (ownership of the allocated rule passes to the list on success). SIOCRMNAT and SIOCPURGENAT need FWRITE (EPERM) and an existing rule (ESRCH); SIOCPURGENAT first copies the rule out to data with ipf_outobjsz and only afterwards sets IPN_PURGE on the list entry, so the copied-out rule does not carry IPN_PURGE; then ipf_nat_siocdelnat removes the rule. The other commands handled in the switch include the NAT log commands (SIOCIPFFB, SIOCSETLG, SIOCGETLG, FIONREAD), SIOCGNATS (statistics) and further lookup, iterator and table commands not shown in the slice, each returning 0, EPERM, EFAULT or the delegated helper's error as appropriate; an unknown command returns EINVAL. The ipf_nat_io mutex is released on all paths on which it was taken and temporary rule copies are freed on failure.
note: reviewer round15 right: SIOCPURGENAT copies the rule out before IPN_PURGE is set (ip_nat.c:1204-1211); the long list of errors in the earlier prose for the later commands was not re-verified here and has been replaced by a general statement; only lines 973-1235 were read

name: ipf_nat6_icmperror
prose: ipf_nat6_icmperror(fin, nflags, dir) fixes up an incoming ICMPv6 error packet whose embedded (offending) IPv6 packet belongs to an existing NAT entry. It returns NULL, with *nflags untouched and nothing modified, in two cases: fin->fin_flx has FI_SHORT or FI_FRAGBODY set (statistics counter ns_icmp_short is bumped), or fin->fin_v != 6 or ipf_nat6_icmperrorlookup(fin, dir) returns NULL (ns_icmp_notfound is bumped). Otherwise it sets *nflags = IPN_ICMPERR and always rewrites the embedded packet's ip6_src and ip6_dst from the entry: when (fin_out == 0 and the entry is NAT_MAP) or (fin_out == 1 and the entry is NAT_REDIRECT) they are set to the entry's original source and destination (nat_osrc6, nat_odst6), otherwise to nat_ndst6 (as source) and nat_nsrc6 (as destination). If the embedded next header is TCP or UDP and at least 4 bytes of it are present (dlen >= 4), the embedded source and destination ports are also rewritten from the entry (original or new ports to match the address choice), and the embedded TCP/UDP checksum is adjusted with ipf_fix_datacksum only when the embedded UDP has dlen >= 8 and a non-zero checksum, or the embedded TCP has dlen >= 18; when the embedded checksum is not adjusted, the port delta is accumulated into sumd2 instead. The outer ICMPv6 checksum is adjusted with ipf_fix_incksum only in this TCP/UDP branch, and only if sumd or sumd2 is non-zero and the final sumd2 is non-zero. If the embedded next header is ICMPv6 and at least 8 bytes are present, then only when the direction test selected the 'original' side (odst == 1) and the embedded ICMPv6 id differs from nat_osport, the embedded ICMPv6 id is replaced with nat_oicmpid and the embedded ICMPv6 checksum is compensated via ipf_fix_datacksum; the outer ICMPv6 checksum is not modified in this branch. Other embedded protocols get only the address rewrite. On every non-NULL path it returns the nat_t found by ipf_nat6_icmperrorlookup; this function takes no lock and does not itself release or acquire a reference on it.
note: reviewer 2 right: outer ICMPv6 checksum is only touched in the TCP/UDP branch (ip_nat6.c:1783), the ICMP-query branch (1787-1819) only fixes the embedded id and checksum; also prose omitted dlen/odst conditions

name: ipf_p_raudio_in
prose: ipf_p_raudio_in(arg, fin, aps, nat) is the RealAudio proxy handler for packets coming back from the server; it returns 0 on every return statement in the function (lines 197, 206, 222, 238, 246 and the final return), so its return value does not distinguish cases. It does nothing if rap->rap_sdone is already set, if there is no TCP payload (dlen <= 0), if the first-seen sequence is not yet established and the string 'PNA' is not found in the payload (memstr), if the packet's sequence number is beyond the 19-byte capture window (seq > rap_sseq + sizeof(rap_svr)), or if the 19-byte server reply (rap_sbf == 0x7ffff) together with the end-of-start-messages flag rap_eos has not yet been seen. Along the way it copies up to 19 payload bytes into rap->rap_svr and sets bits in rap_sbf. Once the 19 bytes are complete and rap_eos is set, it sets rap_sdone = 1 and, if the reply carries RA_ID_ROBUST at offset 11, stores the robust UDP port in rap_srport. It then temporarily rewrites the IP header (protocol set to UDP, source = nat_ndstip, destination = nat_odstip, length = header plus a TCP header), builds a pseudo packet descriptor fi on a copy of fin, and for RAP_M_UDP_ROBUST mode with a non-zero rap_srport and for RAP_M_UDP mode it creates a slave UDP NAT entry with ipf_nat_add (called while holding softn->ipf_nat_new, released right after), and when the entry is created calls ipf_nat_proto, ipf_nat_update under nat2->nat_lock, and ipf_state_add. NAT and state creation failures are ignored. At the end it restores ip_p, ip_len, ip_src and ip_dst of the original packet; early returns happen before the header is modified.
note: slice cut the head: function is ipf_p_raudio_in (ip_raudio_pxy.c:170). Old prose 'always returns 0 / header restored' is true for the whole function but described only the tail

name: ipf_state_tcpinwindow
prose: ipf_state_tcpinwindow(fin, fdata, tdata, tcp, flags) decides whether a TCP segment is inside the tracked window of a state entry; fdata is the sender's data block and tdata the peer's. It returns 1 if the segment is accepted and 0 if it is rejected. Before any decision it computes the (scaled) window, treating a zero window as 1, and may update fdata state: on a non-SYN packet with TCP_WSCALE_FIRST set it clears that flag and sets fdata->td_maxwin to the window; and if fdata->td_end == 0 and either IS_TCPFSM is not set in flags or the packet has both SYN and ACK, it initialises fdata->td_end, td_maxwin = 1 and td_maxend. Return 0 paths: (a) IS_STRICT set in flags and seq != fdata->td_end: iss_tcp_strict is bumped, FI_OOW is set in fin->fin_flx; (b) the packet matches none of the acceptance tests: iss_oow is bumped and FI_OOW is set. Return 1 happens when 'inseq' is set by any of: the normal window test (td_maxend >= end, seq >= td_end - maxwin, and the ack skew within MAXACKWINDOW bounds); the SACK case (seq == td_maxend, ackskew == 0, both sides TCP_SACK_PERMIT), which bumps iss_winsack; the RST|ACK case with seq == 0 and ackskew in [-1, 1]; or, only when IS_TCPFSM is not set and neither TCP_WSCALE_SEEN nor TCP_WSCALE_FIRST is set on fdata, the extra guesses (seq == td_maxend with ackskew == 0, or seq + maxwin >= td_end - maxwin). On return 1 it updates tdata->td_end = ack if ackskew < 0, fdata->td_maxwin if the window grew, fdata->td_end if end is beyond it, and tdata->td_maxend if ack + win >= td_maxend, and leaves fin_flx unchanged. It takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: reviewer round2 right (winsack bumped on return 1 path); round15 right (missed !IS_TCPFSM extra-guess return-1 paths); ip_state.c:2188-2224

name: ipf_tcp_age
prose: ipf_tcp_age(tqe, fin, tqtab, flags, ok) runs the TCP state machine for the direction fin->fin_rev of timeout-queue entry tqe. It reads the old state of the other direction (ostate) and the current state of this direction (nstate), and uses the TCP flags of the packet. The caller is expected to hold the lock on the parent of tqe. It computes an internal result rval: 0 means the flag/state combination is not allowed, 1 means allowed with a transition (or confirmation) of the queue, 2 means allowed without touching the queue. If the packet has RST, nstate becomes CLOSED when the packet has no PUSH flag and no payload, otherwise CLOSE_WAIT; and if ostate <= ESTABLISHED, tqe_state[1 - dir] is set to CLOSE_WAIT immediately (even if ok is 0); rval = 1. Otherwise a switch on the current state gives: LISTEN accepts SYN|ACK (to SYN_RECEIVED) or SYN (to SYN_SENT), and, when IS_TCPFSM is not set in flags, a bare ACK guess depending on ostate; SYN_SENT, SYN_RECEIVED, HALF_ESTAB, ESTABLISHED, CLOSE_WAIT, FIN_WAIT_1 and CLOSING move as the flags dictate (rval 2 for a retransmitted SYN in SYN_SENT or SYN|ACK in SYN_RECEIVED); LAST_ACK accepts only packets with ACK (no state change); TIME_WAIT gives CLOSED and rval 1 if ostate is LAST_ACK and rval 2 otherwise; CLOSED gives rval 2; FIN_WAIT_2 and any unknown state leave rval 0. Finally, rval 2 is converted to 1 with no queue update; for rval 1, tqe_state[dir] is set to nstate only if ok is non-zero, and unless TQE_RULEBASED is set in tqe_flags the entry is moved with ipf_movequeue to tqtab + nstate (this move happens even when ok is 0). It returns 1 for rval 1 or 2, and 0 for rval 0, in which case tqe_state[dir] is not stored and the entry is not moved.
note: slice cut the head: function is ipf_tcp_age (ip_state.c:3933); old prose listed LAST_ACK/FIN_WAIT_2/unknown as the only 0 cases, but LISTEN/SYN_SENT/etc. with non-matching flags also return 0, and ok only gates the state store, not the queue move

name: _n##_rb_insert
prose: Generated function _n##_rb_insert(head, node), defined by RBI_CODE; it returns void. It sets node's left and right links to the sentinel _n##_rb_zero, walks down from the root (head->top._f.right) comparing with _cmp(node, n), going left when the result is negative and right otherwise (so equal keys go to the right), and links node at the leaf position found with colour red and the last visited node as parent. It then restores the red-black properties with the usual recolouring and rotate_left/rotate_right steps while the parent is red, forces the root colour to black, and increments head->count. It has no failure path, does not check for duplicates, allocates or frees nothing and takes no lock. node must not already be linked, head must have been initialised with _n##_rb_init, and the caller serialises access.
note: ipf_rb.h RBI_CODE(_n, _t, _f, _cmp) macro body; the real function is _n##_rb_X generated per tree type; head->top is a dummy node whose _f.right field holds the tree root, and _n##_rb_zero is the per-type shared sentinel. prior prose OK; name fixed to macro-generated head

name: _n##_rb_delete
prose: Generated function _n##_rb_delete(head, node), defined by RBI_CODE; it returns the original node pointer. If node has at most one child, that child (or the sentinel) is spliced into node's place under node's parent (or head->top._f.right when the parent is the sentinel). If node has two children, the leftmost node of its right subtree (the in-order successor) is unlinked from its place and then takes over node's position: the successor's link fields are overwritten with a copy of node's (*node = *old in the code, so its parent, children and colour become node's), node's neighbours are re-pointed to the successor, and node's own link fields are left as they were. In both cases, if the colour of the node that was physically removed was black, deleteblack(head, parent, node) is called to repair the tree, and head->count is decremented; the function then returns the original node argument. It does not free memory, take locks or check that node is in the tree. head must be initialised and the caller must serialise access.
note: ipf_rb.h RBI_CODE(_n, _t, _f, _cmp) macro body; the real function is _n##_rb_X generated per tree type; head->top is a dummy node whose _f.right field holds the tree root, and _n##_rb_zero is the per-type shared sentinel. prior prose said the successor's contents move into node; code copies the node's link fields onto the successor (ipf_rb.h:253), contents are not moved

name: _n##_rb_init
prose: Generated function _n##_rb_init(head), defined by RBI_CODE; it returns void. It zeroes the whole head structure with memset, then zeroes the per-type shared sentinel _n##_rb_zero (a global object, so initialising any head of this type resets that shared sentinel), points head->top's left and right links at the sentinel and its parent at head->top itself, and points the sentinel's left, right and parent links at itself. As a result head->count is 0 and head->compare is NULL, and the tree is empty. It allocates and frees nothing and takes no lock; calling it on a tree that is in use or while another head of the same type is in use is not safe.
note: ipf_rb.h RBI_CODE(_n, _t, _f, _cmp) macro body; the real function is _n##_rb_X generated per tree type; head->top is a dummy node whose _f.right field holds the tree root, and _n##_rb_zero is the per-type shared sentinel. added that the global sentinel is also reset

name: codel_dequeue
prose: Inline function codel_dequeue(q) is the CoDel dequeue step for dummynet queue q. It returns the mbuf it dequeued from the queue (the caller now owns it, whether or not it was ECN-marked) or NULL if the queue yielded no packet; it does not just look at the head. It reads the clock once (now = AQM_UNOW) and calls codel_dodequeue(q, now, &ok_to_drop), which removes one packet, sets ok_to_drop to 1 only when the packet's sojourn time has stayed at or above target for interval and the queue holds more than maxpkt_size bytes, and sets first_above_time as a side effect (reset to 0 when the queue is empty or the sojourn time is below target). Case dropping was true: if ok_to_drop is 0, dropping is cleared; then while now >= drop_next_time and dropping is still true, the current packet is ECN-marked if CODEL_ECN_ENABLED is set and ecn_mark(m) succeeds, in which case count is incremented, drop_next_time is advanced with control_law and that marked packet is returned immediately; otherwise the packet is dropped (update_stats(q, 0, 1) then FREE_PKT) and the next one is taken with codel_dodequeue, after which dropping is cleared if ok_to_drop is 0 and otherwise count is incremented and drop_next_time advanced with control_law. Case dropping was false and ok_to_drop is 1: unless ECN is enabled and ecn_mark succeeds on the packet, the packet is dropped (update_stats and FREE_PKT) and replaced with the result of another codel_dodequeue; in either sub-case dropping is then set true, count becomes count - 2 if count > 2 and (aqm_stime_t)now - (aqm_stime_t)drop_next_time < 8 * interval, otherwise 1, and drop_next_time is set to control_law(cst, cprms, now). Case dropping was false and ok_to_drop is 0: no further state changes beyond those made by codel_dodequeue. The packet returned at the end is the last one dequeued.
note: reviewers right: count/drop_next_time are not updated when not dropping and ok_to_drop is 0; dropping is cleared on empty queue (ok_to_drop is 0). Old prose called the result 'mbuf now at the head' which is wrong: it is the dequeued packet. dn_aqm_codel.h:131-215

name: dn_ht_scan_bucket
prose: dn_ht_scan_bucket(ht, bucket, fn, arg) scans only one hash bucket of ht. If ht or fn is NULL it returns 0 without touching anything. Otherwise, if *bucket is greater than ht->buckets it is set to 0 (this is the only change made to *bucket; the header comment about decrementing it is not implemented in the code); then the chain at ht->ht[*bucket] is walked, with the next-pointer read before fn(cur, arg) is called. If the callback result has DNHT_SCAN_DEL set, the entry is unlinked from the chain, ht->entries is decremented and a counter is incremented (the entry itself is not freed here); otherwise the walk steps past it. If the callback result has DNHT_SCAN_END set, the function returns the counter immediately after handling that entry; otherwise it returns the counter when the chain ends. The return value is the number of entries unlinked, not the number visited.
note: slice cut the head: dn_heap.c:528 dn_ht_scan_bucket (dn_heap.c:493 dn_ht_scan is the unbucketed variant)

name: do_config
prose: do_config(p, l) is the dummynet configuration entry point; p is a buffer of l bytes holding a sequence of TLV blocks, each starting with a struct dn_id. It first copies sizeof(struct dn_id) bytes from p without checking l, and returns EINVAL if o.id is not DN_API_VERSION. It then loops while l >= sizeof(struct dn_id): a block with o.len < sizeof(struct dn_id) or o.len > l sets err = EINVAL and stops; otherwise l is reduced by o.len and the block is dispatched on o.type. Unknown types are logged and skipped with err 0; DN_CMD_CONFIG is a plain header; DN_CMD_DELETE needs o.len >= sizeof(dn_id) + sizeof(uintptr_t) (else EINVAL) and reads a target from the bytes after the header: for subtype DN_LINK it takes the BH write lock, calls delete_schk(a) and delete_schk(a + DN_MAX_ID), releases the lock and returns the first non-zero result; for DN_FS it returns EINVAL if a < 1 or a >= DN_MAX_ID, otherwise delete_fs(a, 0); other subtypes give EINVAL; DN_CMD_FLUSH calls dummynet_flush() under the BH write lock; DN_TEXT frees any previous argument buffer and stores a malloc'd copy of the block (ENOMEM on failure) for later blocks; DN_LINK, DN_PROFILE, DN_SCH and DN_FS allocate one shared scratch union (ENOMEM on failure), copy a full sizeof(struct) of the matching type from the block regardless of o.len, and call config_link, config_profile, config_sched or config_fs with the saved DN_TEXT argument; for DN_FS the result is 1 (not an errno) when config_fs returns NULL. When EMULATE_SYSCTL is defined, DN_SYSCTL_SET returns kesysctl_emu_set(p, l) directly, without freeing the DN_TEXT and scratch buffers. Processing stops at the first non-zero err; on a zero err the offset advances by o.len. On normal exit both temporary buffers are freed and err is returned; if the buffer holds less than one dn_id after the first check (l < sizeof(struct dn_id)) the loop never runs and err is returned uninitialised. The input buffer p is not modified. The config_* handlers manage their own locking; do_config takes the BH write lock only around the delete-link and flush operations.
note: round1 reviewer right on contradictory precondition, wrong that function takes no lock (it takes DN_BH_WLOCK around delete link and flush, ip_dummynet.c:2080,2101); round15 reviewer right: struct sizes are copied without checking o.len (2121,2131,2142,2153); new finding: err uninitialised if l < sizeof(dn_id), and DN_SYSCTL_SET leaks buffers

name: ipfw_chk
prose: ipfw_chk(args) is the ipfw packet classifier: it decides the fate of one packet (an mbuf or a contiguous memory block, optionally with an Ethernet header) against the layer-3 rule chain and returns an IP_FW_* verdict (IP_FW_PASS, IP_FW_DENY, IP_FW_DIVERT, IP_FW_TEE, IP_FW_DUMMYNET, IP_FW_NETGRAPH, IP_FW_NGTEE, IP_FW_REASS, or a value returned by the NAT or external-action handler). The slice shown is only the tail of the function (from the O_NETGRAPH case to the end); the name do_action does not exist in ip_fw2.c. Exit paths: it returns IP_FW_PASS immediately if the mbuf has M_SKIP_FIREWALL set or V_ipfw_vnet_ready is false, and again after taking the chain read lock if V_ipfw_vnet_ready has become false; it returns IP_FW_DENY on header pullup failure (pullup_failed, printing a message when V_fw_verbose), for an IPv6 packet with an unknown routing header type, invalid single fragment header, unknown extension header or non-advertisement CARP packet when the respective denial flags apply (V_fw_deny_unknown_exthdrs, or unconditionally for CARP), and for a first-fragment-offset-1 TCP packet (RFC 3128). Otherwise it parses the headers into local variables and args->f_id, takes the chain read lock, finds the starting rule (from args->rule when IPFW_ARGS_REF is set, otherwise rule 0) and evaluates each rule's opcodes. In the tail shown: O_NETGRAPH/O_NGTEE set the match and return IP_FW_NETGRAPH or IP_FW_NGTEE; O_SETFIB, O_SETDSCP and O_SETMARK modify the mbuf fib, the IP TOS or IPv6 flow label, or the packet mark and continue with the next rule; O_NAT returns IP_FW_DENY when the packet is not IPv4, the NAT module is not loaded or no NAT instance is found, otherwise the value returned by ipfw_nat_ptr; O_REASS calls ip_reass on fragmented IPv4 packets and yields IP_FW_DENY if the fragment was swallowed or IP_FW_REASS with a fixed-up header checksum; O_EXTERNAL_ACTION returns what ipfw_run_eaction gives; an unknown opcode causes panic. When a rule action ends processing, the matched rule's counters are updated and the dtrace probe fires; if no rule ended the scan the packet is denied with a printed 'skip past end of rules' message. Before returning the verdict the chain read lock is released, a reject packet is sent with send_reject or send_reject6 if one was requested, and a cached ucred is released. Several other actions (PIPE, QUEUE, DIVERT, TEE, FORWARD_IP, DENY, REJECT, ACCEPT, SKIPTO, CALLRETURN and so on) are handled earlier in the same switch, outside this slice.
note: slice cut the head: this is a fragment of ipfw_chk (ip_fw2.c:1405-3581). Return paths verified at 1533, 1679, 1703, 1763, 1790, 1888, 3557-3580. do_action does not exist; fixed under the real name rather than dropped (rule 6)

name: list_ifaces
prose: list_ifaces(ch, op3, sd) is the ipfw sockopt handler that lists the interfaces tracked by the chain (the packet name ipfw_list_ifaces does not exist; the real function is list_ifaces in ip_fw_iface.c, the slice cut its head). It first calls ipfw_get_sopt_header(sd, sizeof(struct _ipfw_obj_lheader)); if that returns NULL, or if sd->valsize is smaller than olh->size, it returns EINVAL before taking any lock. Otherwise it takes the chain UH read lock, sets count to the number of entries in the interface object hash (0 if the chain has no such hash), computes size = count * sizeof(ipfw_iface_info) + sizeof(ipfw_obj_lheader), and fills olh->count and olh->objsize whatever the buffer size. If size > olh->size it sets olh->size = size, drops the lock and returns ENOMEM. Otherwise it sets olh->size = size, calls ipfw_objhash_foreach with export_iface_internal (one ipfw_iface_info per interface written into the sopt buffer: name, the IPFW_IFFLAG_RESOLVED flag when resolved, ifindex, refcount, generation count), drops the lock and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real name list_ifaces (ip_fw_iface.c:496); reviewer-free packet, prose checked against 505-538

name: ipfw_check_opcode
prose: ipfw_check_opcode(pcmd, plen, ci) validates one instruction of a rule body and returns an enum ipfw_opcheck_result: SUCCESS, CHECK_ACTION, BAD_SIZE or FAILED. It reads the instruction at *pcmd and its length F_LEN, and for most opcodes returns BAD_SIZE when the length does not equal the size that opcode requires (or, for O_IP_SRC_MASK/O_IP_DST_MASK and the IPv6 mask opcodes, when the length is even; for O_NOP, O_IPID and similar when it is outside 1..31; for O_MAC_TYPE and the port opcodes outside 2..31). Opcodes that only match (for example O_PROTO, O_IN, O_IP_SRC) return SUCCESS after the size check. Side effects on ci on non-error paths: ci->object_opcodes is incremented for O_PROBE_STATE, O_KEEP_STATE, O_EXTERNAL_ACTION, O_LIMIT, the table lookup opcodes, O_RECV/O_XMIT/O_VIA and O_CHECK_STATE and for the O_EXTERNAL_INSTANCE that may follow an external action; IPFW_RCIFLAG_HAS_STATE is set in ci->flags only by O_PROBE_STATE and O_KEEP_STATE; O_LOG sets log_left to max_log; a lookup instruction of the ipfw_insn_table size gets the lookup-masking flag when its lookup type is not LOOKUP_NONE and the match-table-value flag otherwise. FAILED is returned for: a zero kidx on O_EXTERNAL_ACTION or its following O_EXTERNAL_INSTANCE; an instruction after O_EXTERNAL_ACTION that is neither O_EXTERNAL_DATA nor O_EXTERNAL_INSTANCE; O_FIB with arg1 >= rt_numfibs; O_SETFIB with arg1 not IP_FW_TARG and (arg1 & 0x7FFF) >= rt_numfibs; O_IP_SRC_SET/O_IP_DST_SET with arg1 equal to 0 or above 256; a lookup or O_TABLE_LOOKUP kidx >= V_fw_tables_max; O_DIVERT/O_TEE when ip_divert_ptr is NULL; O_NETGRAPH/O_NGTEE when ng_ipfw_input_p is NULL; O_NAT when the NAT module is not loaded; the bad_targ cases, where tablearg (IP_FW_TARG) is used while HAS_STATE is already set, which apply to O_SETFIB, O_PIPE, O_QUEUE, O_DIVERT, O_TEE, O_NETGRAPH, O_NGTEE, O_NAT, O_SETDSCP, O_SKIPTO and O_SETMARK (checked on d[0] for the last two), and O_CALLRETURN unless F_NOT marks it as a return, and for O_FORWARD_IP with address INADDR_ANY; any unknown opcode; and IPv6 opcodes when the kernel has no INET6. CHECK_ACTION is returned for the action opcodes: O_EXTERNAL_ACTION (also after an O_EXTERNAL_DATA or valid O_EXTERNAL_INSTANCE follows it), O_SETFIB, O_PIPE, O_QUEUE, O_FORWARD_IP, O_FORWARD_IP6, O_DIVERT, O_TEE, O_NETGRAPH, O_NGTEE, O_NAT, O_SKIPTO, O_CALLRETURN, O_SETMARK, O_CHECK_STATE, O_FORWARD_MAC, O_COUNT, O_ACCEPT, O_DENY, O_REJECT, O_SETDSCP, O_UNREACH6 and O_REASS, after the size check. For O_EXTERNAL_ACTION, if *plen differs from the instruction length it first subtracts that length from *plen and advances *pcmd to the next instruction; this happens before the next instruction is examined, so it also takes effect on the FAILED and BAD_SIZE returns that follow (a wrong-size O_EXTERNAL_INSTANCE gives BAD_SIZE; the size of a following O_EXTERNAL_DATA is not checked). All other paths leave *pcmd and *plen unchanged.
note: round1 right (bad_targ FAILED for O_SETFIB with IP_FW_TARG when HAS_STATE set); round2 wrong about the return code (O_SETFIB returns CHECK_ACTION in old prose too, ip_fw_sockopt.c:1419); round15 right (O_EXTERNAL_ACTION advances *pcmd/*plen before BAD_SIZE/FAILED returns, 1377-1393). Checked all cases 1326-1685

name: nat64_do_handle_ip6
prose: nat64_do_handle_ip6(m, aaddr, aport, cfg, logdata) translates one IPv6 packet to IPv4 for NAT64 and sends it out. The slice named nat64_translate; the real function is nat64_do_handle_ip6 in nat64_translate.c:1558 and the slice cut its head. It returns NAT64SKIP, without freeing or counting anything, if the IPv6 source or destination fails nat64_check_ip6. It returns NAT64MFREE (the caller must free the mbuf) after incrementing cfg->stats dropped when: the IPv4 source aaddr fails nat64_check_ip4; the IPv4 destination extracted from the IPv6 destination with cfg->plat_plen is 0; nat64_getlasthdr returns a negative protocol; the fragment header is not contiguous in the first mbuf; the protocol after a fragment header is ICMPv6; or the payload length is negative or larger than the mbuf. It returns NAT64RETURN, with the mbuf consumed, after nat64_icmp6_reflect for: hop limit <= IPV6_HLIMDEC (only when *V_nat64ip6stealth is 0, ICMP6_TIME_EXCEEDED); a fragment with the more-fragments flag whose length is not a multiple of 8 octets (ICMP6_PARAM_PROB); no IPv4 route to the destination (noroute4 counted, ICMP6_DST_UNREACH); or nh_mtu < plen + sizeof(struct ip) (ICMP6_PACKET_TOO_BIG). For an ICMPv6 payload whose type is neither echo request nor echo reply it returns whatever nat64_handle_icmp6 returns. Otherwise it builds the IPv4 header, completes a delayed IPv6 checksum if needed, converts the TCP, UDP or ICMPv6 echo checksum (replacing the source port or ICMP id with aport when aport is non-zero and changing the ICMPv6 echo type to the ICMP echo type), trims the mbuf to the new header, calls V_nat64out->output, increments opcnt64 if that returned 0, and returns NAT64RETURN regardless of the output result.
note: reviewer round15 right: hop-limit reflection depends on *V_nat64ip6stealth == 0 (nat64_translate.c:1596). Also found NAT64SKIP path (1576-1579) missing from earlier prose; real name nat64_do_handle_ip6

name: pfsync_in_clr
prose: pfsync_in_clr(m, offset, count, flags, action) handles a pfsync 'clear states' message. Each record is a struct pfsync_clr of IFNAMSIZ + 4 bytes (a 16-byte interface name and a 32-bit creatorid, packed, 20 bytes). It calls m_pulldown(m, offset, 20 * count, &offp); if that returns NULL it increments pfsyncs_badlen and returns -1 (it does not free m and takes no lock; the caller releases the rules lock and does not free m on this path). Otherwise, for each of the count records, the record is skipped if its ifname is non-empty and pfi_kkif_find(ifname) returns NULL; for the remaining records it scans every row of the state ID hash (0..V_pf_hashmask), taking the row lock, and for each state whose creatorid equals the record's it sets PFSTATE_NOSYNC and calls pf_remove_state, then restarts the scan of that row (goto relock) until no state with that creatorid remains in the row, and releases the row lock. The interface name is only checked for existence; it is not used to restrict which states are removed. The function returns 20 * count, the number of payload bytes consumed, and holds no row lock on return. The caller (pfsync_input) is expected to hold PF_RULES_RLOCK.
note: reviewers round2 and round15 right: sizeof(struct pfsync_clr) is IFNAMSIZ(16)+4 = 20 bytes, packed (net/if_pfsync.h:140), not 24; round1 claim concerns the caller, which indeed returns IPPROTO_DONE on -1 without m_freem (if_pfsync.c:1127-1129), consistent with this prose (m not freed)

name: pf_purge_expired_states
prose: pf_purge_expired_states(i, maxcheck) is called only from the pf purge thread and scans up to maxcheck rows of the state ID hash starting at row i. It first sets V_pf_status.states from the state zone's current count. While maxcheck > 0 it takes row i: if the row's state list is non-empty it takes the row lock and walks it; a state whose expiry (pf_state_expires) is not after time_uptime is removed with pf_remove_state (V_pf_status.states is decremented by its result) and the walk of that row restarts after re-taking the lock; every other state has its rule, nat rule, anchor, match rules, interface and route interface marked with PFRULE_REFS or PFI_IFLAG_REFS reference flags. The row lock is released, then i is incremented; if i has passed V_pf_hashmask the function sets V_pf_status.states again from the zone count and returns 0 (a wrap to the start); otherwise maxcheck is decremented and the loop continues. When maxcheck reaches 0 it refreshes V_pf_status.states and returns i, which is the first row not scanned: the starting i plus the number of rows scanned. If maxcheck <= 0 on entry no row is scanned and i is returned unchanged. No row lock is held on return.
note: reviewers round2 right (maxcheck <= 0 returns i unchanged, may be 0) and original review right that the formal ensures was imprecise; contract dropped because the function reads/writes global state (V_pf_idhash, V_pf_status). pf.c:2907-2962

name: pf_test_state_icmp
prose: pf_test_state_icmp(state, pd, reason) matches an ICMP or ICMPv6 packet against pf state; *state must be NULL on entry (MPASS) and pd->proto must be IPPROTO_ICMP or IPPROTO_ICMPV6 (any other value panics; the real pf.c name and head are at pf.c:7908). It returns a pf action: PF_PASS, PF_DROP, PF_AFRT, or a non-match action passed through from pf_icmp_state_lookup or pf_find_state. Query/reply branch (pf_icmp_mapping returns 0): it looks up an ICMP state with pf_icmp_state_lookup (retrying with a multicast match for an outbound IPv6 packet after PF_DROP); if the lookup returns a non-negative action that action is returned with *state NULL. Otherwise it refreshes (*state)->expire and sets timeout to PFTM_ICMP_ERROR_REPLY, and if the state's wire and stack keys differ it rewrites the addresses (pf_change_a or pf_change_a6) and the ICMP id in the packet and copies the header back, returning PF_DROP if an address-family translation (pf_translate_icmp_af) fails (no *reason set), PF_AFRT after a successful family translation, and otherwise PF_PASS. Error branch: it extracts the inner IP header and the inner protocol headers (pf_pull_hdr, pf_walk_header or pf_walk_header6), returning PF_DROP with a reason set by those helpers (or PFRES_FRAG when the inner IPv4 header is a non-first fragment); it returns PF_DROP with PFRES_BADSTATE if the outer destination does not equal the inner source. The inner packet is then looked up by protocol: TCP (state found with pf_find_state, sequence checked against the peer window unless PFSTATE_SLOPPY, giving PF_DROP with PFRES_BADSTATE if outside), UDP, SCTP (PF_DROP without reason if the verification tag differs), inner ICMP and ICMPv6 (PF_DROP with PFRES_NORM if the inner family is wrong), and a default case for other protocols, each returning the non-PF_MATCH action from the lookup or, on a match, translating addresses and ports in the inner and outer headers (with checksum fixups and m_copyback) when the state keys differ; a failed family translation returns PF_DROP without setting *reason, and a successful one returns PF_AFRT, otherwise PF_PASS. On a PF_DROP that happens after a state was found, *state is left pointing at the state.
note: reviewer round15 right: PF_DROP from pf_translate_icmp_af / pf_change_icmp_af failure sets no *reason (pf.c:7995, 8290-8300). Old claim '*state left NULL otherwise' is wrong for DROP after a state was found; summary-level description of a ~1000-line function

name: pf_altq_ifnet_event
prose: pf_altq_ifnet_event(ifp, remove) rebuilds the ALTQ configuration after an interface event; it returns void. The caller is expected to hold the PF rules write lock. It returns doing nothing if ALTQ_IS_READY(&ifp->if_snd) is false. Otherwise it rolls back an open inactive altq set (pf_rollback_altq with the inactive ticket) if V_altqs_inactive_open is set, and starts a new transaction with pf_begin_altq; if pf_begin_altq fails it returns with no further change. It then copies each entry of the active altq_if list into a malloc'd (M_NOWAIT) pf_altq (ENOMEM and stop on allocation failure), passes it to pf_altq_ifnet_event_add and, if that returns 0, appends it to the inactive interface list. pf_altq_ifnet_event_add marks the copy PFALTQ_FLAG_IF_REMOVED when the interface name no longer resolves or when remove is non-zero and it is the event interface; otherwise it calls altq_add, then returns EBUSY if the ticket no longer equals V_ticket_altqs_inactive, and frees the copy if either altq_add or the ticket check produced an error. If the first loop fails, it goes to the rollback. Otherwise it does the same for each entry of the active altq (queue) list, but first assigns the copy a queue id with pf_qname2qid (a zero result frees the copy and sets EBUSY) and sets altq_disc from the matching-interface entry of the new inactive interface list or NULL; successful copies are appended to the inactive queue list. On any error it calls pf_rollback_altq(ticket) to discard the partially built inactive sets; with no error it calls pf_commit_altq(ticket) and ignores its return value, so a commit failure is not reported.
note: reviewers right: round15 (altq_add failure frees the copy and aborts) and round2 (IF_REMOVED only if interface missing or remove && same ifp), original review right (early return when pf_begin_altq fails, commit result ignored). pf_ioctl.c:1149-1247
