name: pf_load
prose: pf_load() is the pf module load handler (static, no parameters). It initialises the pf_end_lock sx lock and calls pf_mtag_initialize(), then creates the /dev/pf character device with make_dev(&pf_cdevsw, 0, UID_ROOT, GID_WHEEL, 0600, PF_NAME). If make_dev returns NULL it returns ENOMEM; the lock initialisation and mtag initialisation are not undone. Otherwise it sets pf_end_threads to 0 and creates the 'pf purge' kernel process with kproc_create(pf_purge_thread, ..., &pf_purge_proc, ...); if that returns a non-zero error it returns that error (pf_dev stays created and pfi_initialize is not called). Otherwise it calls pfi_initialize() and returns 0.
note: pf_ioctl.c:7088-7109; contract dropped (writes global state and the old contract was malformed)

name: pf_normalize_tcp
prose: pf_normalize_tcp(pd) applies TCP scrubbing to the segment described by pd and returns PF_PASS or PF_DROP. It asserts the rules read lock (PF_RULES_RASSERT). It walks the active scrub ruleset (counting r->evaluations for each rule visited) to find the first matching rule rm, using skip steps on interface, direction, address family, protocol, source and destination address and port, and OS fingerprint. If at least one scrub rule exists and either no rule matched or the matched rule's action is PF_NOSCRUB, it returns PF_PASS without changing the packet. If a rule matched and is not PF_NOSCRUB it adds the packet and byte counters of that rule and copies the rule's actions into pd->act. If there are no scrub rules at all, normalization still proceeds with rm == NULL. If rm has PFRULE_REASSEMBLE_TCP, PFDESC_TCP_NORM is set in pd->flags. It then returns PF_DROP when the TCP flags are illegal: SYN with RST or with FIN; a segment without SYN that has neither ACK nor RST; FIN, PUSH or URG without ACK; or when th_off is below sizeof(struct tcphdr)/4 words (5). On a drop it computes reason = PFRES_NORM in a local variable only (no reason is returned to the caller) and logs the packet through PFLOG_PACKET when rm is non-NULL and the rule has logging. Otherwise it returns PF_PASS after possibly sanitising the header: the condition for clearing reserved bits tests TH_RES1 and TH_RES2 (TH_RES2 is tested twice and TH_RES3 is not tested), so a segment with only TH_RES3 set is not changed by this step; when it does trigger, TH_RES1, TH_RES2 and TH_RES3 are all cleared and the checksum is adjusted; a non-zero urgent pointer without TH_URG is zeroed with a checksum adjustment; and if either change was made the TCP header is copied back to the mbuf with m_copyback.
note: reviewers right: round15 (TH_RES3 omitted from the test, pf_norm.c:1469, while the clear at 1473 includes it), round2 (PF_PASS when no scrub rule matches or NOSCRUB), original (th_off < 5 drop). Also old prose said '*reason set' but reason is a local variable (1384, 1496)

name: pf_normalize_sctp
prose: pf_normalize_sctp(pd) applies SCTP scrubbing and returns PF_PASS or PF_DROP; it never modifies the packet. It asserts the rules read lock, then walks the active scrub rules, incrementing r->evaluations for each rule it visits (so counters are touched even when it later returns PF_PASS without normalizing), looking for the first rule that matches interface, direction, address family, protocol, addresses and ports. If at least one scrub rule exists and either no rule matched or the matched rule's action is PF_NOSCRUB, it returns PF_PASS. If a rule matched and is not PF_NOSCRUB, that rule's packet and byte counters for the packet's direction are incremented. When there are no scrub rules at all the checks below still run. It returns PF_DROP if (pd->tot_len - pd->off - sizeof(struct sctphdr)) is not a multiple of 4, or if PFDESC_SCTP_INIT is set together with any other bit in pd->sctp_flags. On a drop, reason = PFRES_NORM is set in a local variable, the packet is logged with PFLOG_PACKET if a rule matched and has logging enabled, and PF_DROP is returned. Otherwise it returns PF_PASS.
note: reviewers: original right that scrub rules do not themselves reject; round2 right (checks still run with no scrub rules); round15 right (evaluations incremented for every rule walked, pf_norm.c:2151). pf_norm.c:2136-2208

name: pf_validate_op
prose: pf_validate_op(op) checks that op is one of the pf comparison operators PF_OP_NONE, PF_OP_IRG, PF_OP_EQ, PF_OP_NE, PF_OP_LT, PF_OP_LE, PF_OP_GT, PF_OP_GE, PF_OP_XRG, PF_OP_RRG (the values 0 through 9). It returns 0 for those values and EINVAL (22) for every other uint8_t value. It reads and writes no memory.
note: pf_nv.c:373-393; enum in netpfil/pf/pf.h:55

name: pf_syncookies_setmode
prose: pf_syncookies_setmode(mode) sets the pf syncookie mode. It returns EINVAL if mode is greater than PF_SYNCOOKIES_MODE_MAX (PF_SYNCOOKIES_ADAPTIVE, 2) and changes nothing. If mode equals V_pf_status.syncookies_mode it returns 0 with no change. Otherwise it stores mode in V_pf_status.syncookies_mode and, if the new mode is PF_SYNCOOKIES_ALWAYS, calls pf_syncookie_newkey() and sets V_pf_status.syncookies_active to true; it then returns 0. It does not take any lock itself; it reads and writes the vnet pf status.
note: pf_syncookies.c:243-258; contract dropped because the function reads and writes global pf state

name: pfr_ina_define
prose: pfr_ina_define(tbl, addr, size, nadd, naddr, ticket, flags) defines a table, with an optional address list, inside an open table transaction. It asserts the rules write lock. It returns EINVAL if flags has any bit outside PFR_FLAG_DUMMY | PFR_FLAG_ADDRSTOO (ACCEPT_FLAGS), if size is non-zero but PFR_FLAG_ADDRSTOO is not set, or if pfr_validate_table rejects tbl; it returns EBUSY if the ruleset for tbl->pfrt_anchor does not exist, is not open for tables, or ticket differs from the ruleset's table ticket. None of these early returns changes anything. After them it sets PFR_TFLAG_INACTIVE in the caller's tbl->pfrt_flags. It looks up the table in the global tree; if absent, it creates it (ENOMEM on failure), counts it in xadd, and for a table in an anchor looks up or creates a root table (ENOMEM on failure, destroying the already created table); if the table exists but is not currently PFR_TFLAG_INACTIVE it is counted in xadd. It then creates a shadow table (ENOMEM on failure, destroying the work list) and, for each of the size addresses, returns EINVAL if pfr_validate_addr rejects it, skips duplicates, creates and routes an entry (ENOMEM if creation fails, silently skipping entries that fail to route), counting each added entry in xaddr. Any of those errors after the shadow was created destroys the shadow table, the new tables and the new entries and returns the error. If flags lacks PFR_FLAG_DUMMY the previous shadow of kt (if any) is destroyed, PFR_TFLAG_INACTIVE is set on kt, the newly created tables are inserted into the global tree, shadow->pfrkt_cnt is set to xaddr if PFR_FLAG_ADDRSTOO was given and to NO_ADDRESSES otherwise, and the shadow is installed as kt->pfrkt_shadow. If PFR_FLAG_DUMMY is set, the shadow table, new tables and entries are destroyed and nothing is installed. On success it stores xadd in *nadd and xaddr in *naddr when those pointers are non-NULL (also for the dummy case) and returns 0.
note: reviewers right: round15 (tbl->pfrt_flags INACTIVE is set only after the EINVAL/EBUSY checks, pf_table.c:1540); round2 prose already agrees with code (xadd counts new tables and existing non-inactive tables); original right (shadow installed only when not DUMMY, 1592-1605)

name: audit_send_trigger
prose: audit_send_trigger(trigger) queues an audit trigger value for the userspace audit daemon. It first allocates a struct trigger_info with malloc(M_WAITOK), which may sleep, before taking audit_trigger_mtx. It then takes audit_trigger_mtx; if audit_isopen is false (no reader has opened the audit device) it releases the mutex, frees the allocation and returns ENODEV, leaving trigger_list unchanged. Otherwise it stores trigger in the entry, appends the entry to the tail of trigger_list, calls selwakeup on audit_trigger_rsel and wakeup on trigger_list, releases the mutex and returns 0. The queued entry is later removed and freed by audit_read or audit_close; the caller gets no reference to it. The caller must not hold audit_trigger_mtx.
note: audit_trigger.c:147-166; contract dropped (function modifies global queue state)

name: mac_proc_vm_revoke_recurse
prose: mac_proc_vm_revoke_recurse(td, cred, map) revokes memory-map permissions that MAC policy no longer allows for a process, in map and recursively in its sub-maps; it returns void. If mac_mmap_revocation is false it returns immediately without touching the map. Otherwise it takes the map lock (vm_map_lock) and visits each map entry: for a sub-map entry it calls itself on the sub-map and continues; an entry with MAP_ENTRY_COW or MAP_ENTRY_NOSYNC set or with zero max_protection, with a NULL object, or whose deepest backing object is not OBJT_VNODE is skipped. For a vnode-backed entry it locks the vnode, calls mac_vnode_check_mmap_downgrade to get the permissions still allowed, and computes revokeperms = max_protection & ~result; if that is empty the entry is skipped; otherwise it prints a message with the pid and the revoked permissions. If the entry's current protection does not include any revoked permission, only max_protection is reduced by revokeperms. Otherwise: when write is revoked it takes a temporary reference on the object, starts a vnode write and cleans the object's pages for the entry's range (vm_object_page_clean with OBJPC_SYNC under the vnode and object locks), then releases the locks and the reference; it clears VM_PROT_WRITE from max_protection and protection unless mac_mmap_revocation_via_cow is set, and independently of mac_mmap_revocation_via_cow sets MAP_ENTRY_COW | MAP_ENTRY_NEEDS_COPY when read is not being revoked; when execute is revoked it clears VM_PROT_EXECUTE from both max_protection and protection; when read is revoked both are set to 0; it then calls pmap_protect on the entry's range with protection & ~revokeperms and vm_map_try_merge_entries with the previous entry. It finishes by releasing the map lock with vm_map_unlock.
note: reviewers right: round15 (COW/NEEDS_COPY is set whenever read is not revoked regardless of mac_mmap_revocation_via_cow: the '} if' at mac_process.c:352 is a separate if), round2 (early return when mac_mmap_revocation is false), original (via_cow leaves write max_protection)

name: mac_sysvmsq_check_msqrcv
prose: mac_sysvmsq_check_msqrcv(cred, msqkptr) asks the MAC framework whether credential cred may receive from the SysV message queue msqkptr. It runs MAC_POLICY_CHECK_NOSLEEP(sysvmsq_check_msqrcv, cred, msqkptr, msqkptr->label) and then the probe macro MAC_CHECK_PROBE2, and returns the resulting error. The macro calls the sysvmsq_check_msqrcv entry point of every policy that defines one: the static policy list without a lock, and, if the dynamic policy list is not empty, the dynamic list while holding a non-sleeping read lock on the policy list (mac_policy_slock_nosleep), released before return. It does not stop at the first failing policy; the individual results are combined with mac_error_select, which gives precedence to EDEADLK, EINVAL, ESRCH, ENOENT, EACCES and EPERM in that order, then to any other non-zero error, so the result is 0 only if every policy that defines the entry point returned 0. The probe does not change the returned value. It acquires and releases no references.
note: reviewer right: the dynamic-policy path takes the policy list read lock (mac_internal.h:311-322), so 'no locks are taken' was false; also the old prose 'first nonzero error' is wrong: errors are merged with mac_error_select (mac_framework.c:700)

name: maybe_demote
prose: maybe_demote(subjlabel, objlabel, actionname, objname, vp) demotes the current process's LOMAC label after it has accessed a lower-level object, and logs the demotion; it returns 0 on both of its returns. It takes subj = the process label slot of curthread's process and locks subj->mtx. If subj->mac_lomac has MAC_LOMAC_FLAG_UPDATE set (a demotion already pending) and lomac_dominate_single(objlabel, &subj->mac_lomac) is true, that is, objlabel's single label dominates the pending single label, it unlocks the mutex and returns 0 leaving the pending label unchanged and logging nothing. Otherwise it zeroes subj->mac_lomac, copies objlabel's single into it (objlabel must have a single label), copies subjlabel's range into it (subjlabel must have a range), sets the range low to objlabel's single only if objlabel's single does not dominate that low element (otherwise the low stays that of subjlabel), sets the range high to objlabel's single, sets MAC_LOMAC_FLAG_UPDATE and schedules a TDA_MAC AST with ast_sched. It then caches the single label in a local, unlocks subj->mtx, builds three sbuf strings (subject label, new label read from subj->mac_lomac after the unlock, object label), and logs a LOG_INFO message that includes the inode number and mount point when vp is non-NULL and VOP_GETATTR succeeds, or without them otherwise. It deletes the three sbufs and returns 0.

name: sysctl_ffs_fsck
prose: sysctl_ffs_fsck(SYSCTL_HANDLER_ARGS) is the write-only sysctl handler through which fsck_ffs submits filesystem repair commands; the slice shows only the later cases of its switch. It returns EBADRPC if the request has no new value or newlen exceeds sizeof(struct fsck_cmd), the error from SYSCTL_IN, ERPCMISMATCH if cmd.version is not FFS_CMD_VERSION, the error from getvnode on cmd.handle with CAP_FSCK, EINVAL if the file is not a regular file or directory (dropping the file reference) or is not on a 'ufs' mount (also ending the write started with vn_start_write), and EROFS if the mount is read-only. Otherwise it holds a write reference on the mount (vn_start_write) and dispatches on the sysctl OID number: FFS_SET_FLAGS sets or clears fs_flags bits; FFS_ADJ_REFCNT, FFS_ADJ_BLKCNT, FFS_ADJ_DEPTH (ENOTDIR for non-directories) and FFS_SET_SIZE look up an inode by number (ffs_vget) and adjust its link count, block count, directory depth or size, then call ffs_update; FFS_DIR_FREE and FFS_FILE_FREE free a range of inodes with ffs_freefile, stopping at the first error; FFS_BLK_FREE frees a range of blocks with ffs_blkfree; FFS_ADJ_NDIR, NBFREE, NIFREE, NFFREE and NUMCLUSTERS add cmd.value to the matching superblock summary counter; FFS_SET_CWD changes the caller's current directory to the inode (change_dir); FFS_SET_DOTDOT rewrites '..' in the current directory with ufs_dirrewrite; FFS_UNLINK drops the mount write reference first (setting mp to NULL) and calls kern_funlinkat; any other OID gives EINVAL. After the switch the file reference is dropped with fdrop and the write reference is finished (a no-op for mp == NULL), and the case's error is returned.

name: softdep_flushfiles
prose: softdep_flushfiles(oldmnt, flags, td) flushes all vnodes and soft-dependency worklist items of the mount; oldmnt must be a soft-updates mount. It starts with loopcnt = 10 and retry_flush_count = 3. In each loop iteration it calls ffs_flushfiles(oldmnt, flags | early, td), where early is EARLYFLUSH when MNTK_UNMOUNT is set in the mount and retry_flush_count != 1 (this applies to the initial attempt as well as the first retry), otherwise 0, and then softdep_flushworklist(oldmnt, &depcount, td); the loop ends on an error from either call or when depcount is 0. If the loop ran out (loopcnt reached 0) it panics when MNTK_UNMOUNT is set and otherwise sets EBUSY. If there is no error so far it calls softdep_waitidle and keeps its result. If still no error and the mount is being unmounted, it checks for remaining work (vnodes on the mount's list, or quota vnodes under QUOTA): if there is, it decrements retry_flush_count and, while that is still positive, resets loopcnt to 3 and repeats from the start; when retry_flush_count reaches 0 it sets EBUSY instead. It returns 0 or the first error (EBUSY, or an error from ffs_flushfiles, softdep_flushworklist or softdep_waitidle).
note: reviewer round15 right: early = EARLYFLUSH on the initial unmount attempt too (ffs_softdep.c:2123-2124: ((retry_flush_count == 1 || !unmount) ? 0 : EARLYFLUSH)); slice contains the second (real) definition at ffs_softdep.c:2093

name: ffs_mount
prose: ffs_mount(mp) mounts or updates a UFS/FFS filesystem. It returns EINVAL if vfs_filteropt rejects the option list; it creates the FFS inode and dinode UMA zones on first use; deletes the groupquota and userquota options; gets the 'from' option with vfs_getopts and returns that error if it fails (ENOENT when absent); sets MNT_UNTRUSTED, MNT_ACLS, MNT_SNAPSHOT (removing 'snapshot' from the option lists) and MNT_NFS4ACLS from the options, returning EINVAL if both acls and nfsv4acls are given; then clears MNTK_FPLOOKUP and ORs the new flags into mnt_flag. For a snapshot request it returns EINVAL if MNT_UPDATE is not set, and otherwise returns ffs_snapshot(mp, fspec) directly (so a successful snapshot returns 0 before vfs_mountedfrom and before MNTK_FPLOOKUP is set). Otherwise it drops the busy reference for an update, looks up fspec with namei, re-takes the busy reference, and returns the error from namei, from vn_isdisk_error (not a disk) or from the permission check VOP_ACCESS followed by priv_check(PRIV_VFS_MOUNT_PERM), releasing the device vnode on those paths. For a new mount it calls ffs_mountfs and returns its error (releasing the vnode). For an update it returns EINVAL if the named device differs from the mounted one; if the filesystem is writable and 'ro' was requested it suspends writes, flushes files (softdep_flushfiles or ffs_flushfiles), updates the superblock and marks the mount read-only, returning the error and restoring read-write state (and MNT_SOFTDEP) if the flush or ffs_sbupdate fails, or the error of vn_start_write / vfs_write_suspend_umnt; it runs ffs_reload when MNT_RELOAD is set, returning its error; and for a read-only filesystem asked to become writable it checks VOP_ACCESS/priv_check on the original device, returns EPERM if the filesystem is unclean and neither forced nor an allowed soft-updates case, requests write access with g_access, suspends writes, clears read-only, starts soft updates (softdep_mount) and writes the superblock with ffs_sbupdate, restoring the read-only state and returning the error if softdep_mount or ffs_sbupdate fails, and resumes writes. Finally, on success of the new-mount or update path it clears MNT_ASYNC when soft updates is mounted, keeps MNT_ACLS / MNT_NFS4ACLS from the superblock flags, sets MNTK_FPLOOKUP unless MNT_ACLS, MNT_NFS4ACLS or MNT_UNION is set (panicking if it was already set), calls vfs_mountedfrom and returns 0.
note: reviewer round15 right: snapshot success returns before vfs_mountedfrom/MNTK_FPLOOKUP (ffs_vfsops.c:420-424); round2 prose already says ENOENT/vfs_getopts error; original review right that flushing only happens on the rw to ro transition; function at ffs_vfsops.c:348-719

name: QCMD

name: ufs_setattr
prose: ufs_setattr(ap) is the VOP_SETATTR implementation for UFS: ap->a_vp is the vnode, ap->a_vap the requested attributes (fields not to change are VNOVAL) and ap->a_cred the credential. Checks and changes happen in this order, each returning the stated value: EINVAL if va_type is not VNON, or any of va_nlink, va_fsid, va_fileid, va_blocksize, va_rdev, (int)va_bytes or va_gen is not VNOVAL. If va_flags is set: EOPNOTSUPP for unsupported flag bits; EROFS on a read-only mount; the error from VOP_ACCESS(VADMIN); for a caller with PRIV_VFS_SYSFLAGS, the securelevel_gt error if system flags are currently set and EPERM if the snapshot flag would be toggled; for a caller without it, EPERM if any of SF_NOUNLINK, SF_IMMUTABLE or SF_APPEND is currently set or any settable system flag would change; otherwise the flags are stored, IN_CHANGE is set and UFS_UPDATE is called; if the new flags include IMMUTABLE or APPEND the function returns right away with the UFS_UPDATE result (0 or its error), skipping every other requested attribute, otherwise the UFS_UPDATE result is not used. Then, if the inode has IMMUTABLE or APPEND set, it returns EPERM whether or not other attributes were requested. Owner or group change: EROFS on read-only mounts, else the error from ufs_chown. If va_size is set: EISDIR for a directory; for VLNK and VREG, EROFS on a read-only mount, EPERM for a snapshot, then the errors of vn_rlimit_trunc or UFS_TRUNCATE; for any other file type the function returns 0 at once and ignores the size and every later change (times, mode). If any of atime, mtime or birthtime is set: EROFS on read-only mounts, EPERM for a snapshot, the error from vn_utimes_perm, then the times are stored (birthtime only on UFS2) and UFS_UPDATE is called, returning its error. If va_mode is set: EROFS on read-only mounts, EPERM if a snapshot would get write or execute bits, otherwise the result of ufs_chmod. If no attribute is requested (and the inode is not immutable/append-only) it returns 0.
note: reviewers right: original (size ignored for unsupported types, birthtime UFS2 only), round2 (EISDIR), round15 (early return after flags when IMMUTABLE/APPEND). Prior prose also wrong that va_type must be VNOVAL (it must be VNON) and that EPERM for immutable needs further attributes requested (ufs_vnops.c:717-718 returns EPERM unconditionally)

name: ufs_chmod
prose: ufs_chmod(vp, mode, cred, td) changes the permission bits of the inode of vp; the inode must be locked by the caller and stays locked. It returns the error from VOP_ACCESSX(vp, VWRITE_ACL, ...) if that fails; EFTYPE if vp is not a directory, mode has the sticky bit and priv_check_cred(PRIV_VFS_STICKYFILE) fails; the priv_check_cred(PRIV_VFS_SETGID) error if mode has setgid and the caller is not a member of the inode's group; and the priv_check_cred(PRIV_VFS_ADMIN) error if mode has setuid and the inode's owner is not cred->cr_uid. Otherwise it replaces the ALLPERMS bits of i_mode with those of mode, updates the on-disk copy and sets IN_CHANGE. When UFS_ACL is compiled in and the mount has MNT_NFS4ACLS, it then resynchronises the NFS4 ACL from the new mode (ufs_update_nfs4_acl_after_mode_change) and an error from that is returned without calling UFS_UPDATE; if no error and IN_CHANGE is set it returns the result of UFS_UPDATE(vp, 0), otherwise 0.
note: prose checked against ufs_vnops.c:872-921; the mode change is applied before the ACL resync / UFS_UPDATE and is not undone on their errors

name: redzone_size_ntor
prose: redzone_size_ntor(nsize) returns the size of the allocation that must be made to hold nsize bytes plus the red zones: nsize + redzone_roundup(nsize) + REDZONE_FSIZE (16). redzone_roundup(n) first raises n to at least REDZONE_HSIZE (the size of a stack record, an unsigned long and 16 bytes), then returns 128, 256, 512, 1024 or 2048 for the first of those that is at least n, and PAGE_SIZE for anything larger (so for n above PAGE_SIZE it still returns PAGE_SIZE). Thus the result is between nsize + 144 and nsize + PAGE_SIZE + 16. The arithmetic is on u_long and wraps when nsize is within PAGE_SIZE + 16 of ULONG_MAX. The function has no side effects.
note: reviewer round15 right: redzone_roundup returns PAGE_SIZE even when n > PAGE_SIZE (redzone.c:55-72), so the 'at least max(nsize, HSIZE)' claim was wrong; round2 right about the overflow bound

name: swap_reserve
prose: swap_reserve(incr) returns swap_reserve_by_cred(incr, curthread->td_ucred), with incr a byte count that must be a multiple of PAGE_SIZE (KASSERT in the callee). swap_reserve_by_cred first, when RACCT is enabled, charges RACCT_SWAP to curproc under the process lock and returns false at once if racct_add fails. It then atomically adds atop(incr) pages to swap_reserved; computes the limit from swap_total, adding free non-wired memory when SWAP_RESERVE_ALLOW_NONWIRED is set in vm_overcommit and the new total exceeds swap_total; if SWAP_RESERVE_FORCE_ON is set, the new total exceeds the limit and priv_check(PRIV_VM_SWAP_NOQUOTA) fails, it takes the failure path. Otherwise it calls swap_reserve_by_cred_rlimit, which adds the pages to the user's ui_vmsize and, only when SWAP_RESERVE_RLIMIT_ON is set, the result exceeds RLIMIT_SWAP and priv_check(PRIV_VM_SWAP_NORLIMIT) fails, undoes that addition and reports failure; on such a failure the swap_reserved increment is also undone. It returns true on success. On either failure it prints a rate-limited message naming the uid and pid, undoes the RACCT charge when RACCT is enabled, and returns false. The racct failure path returns false without a message and with no counters changed.
note: prose from earlier round checked against swap_pager.c:258-330; round 2 reviewer right that FORCE_ON is required for the overcommit failure; the function itself only forwards to swap_reserve_by_cred

name: vm_domainset_iter_page
prose: vm_domainset_iter_page(di, obj, domain, pages) advances a page-allocation domain iterator after a failed allocation. In NUMA kernels, if vm_domainset_iter_next finds another domain it stores it in *domain and returns 0. Otherwise, if neither VM_ALLOC_WAITOK nor VM_ALLOC_WAITFAIL is set in di->di_flags it returns ENOMEM. Otherwise, if obj is non-NULL it unlocks the object write lock and, only if pages is also non-NULL, resets the pctrie iterator; it waits with vm_wait_doms(&di->di_valid_mask, 0); it then re-locks obj if non-NULL; then it returns ENOMEM if VM_ALLOC_WAITFAIL is set, and otherwise restarts the search with vm_domainset_iter_first, returning 0 if a domain was found (stored in *domain) and ENOMEM if not. In a kernel without NUMA the function does nothing and returns EJUSTRETURN. obj, if non-NULL, must be write-locked on entry and is locked again on every return path.
note: reviewers right: round2 (obj re-locked after vm_wait_doms) and round15 (pages reset only when obj != NULL, vm_domainset.c:292-296); original right about the non-NUMA EJUSTRETURN (365-371)

name: vm_ksubmap_init
prose: vm_ksubmap_init(kmi) sizes and creates boot-time kernel memory structures and returns void. It makes two passes over kern_vfs_bio_buffer_alloc(v, physmem_est), where physmem_est is physmem limited to the size of kernel_map in pages: the first pass computes the required size, then memory is allocated (with kmem_alloc_attr below 4 GB when VM_FREELIST_DMA32 is defined, falling back to kmem_malloc(M_ZERO | M_WAITOK)), and the second pass assigns addresses; it panics if no memory could be obtained or if the two passes disagree on the size. It allocates the clean map with kva_alloc for nbuf * BKVASIZE + bio_transient_maxcnt * maxphys bytes and records clean_sva/clean_eva, sets kmi->buffer_sva and buffer_eva and initialises the buffer arena with vmem_init (with a quantum cache when mp_ncpus > 4); if bio_transient_maxcnt is non-zero it initialises transient_arena right after the buffer arena with size bio_transient_maxcnt * maxphys. Finally it computes the exec map size from exec_map_entries (8 * mp_ncpus on LP64, 2 * mp_ncpus + 4 otherwise), exec_map_entry_size = round_page(PATH_MAX + ARG_MAX), the tunable vm.exec_map_guard_pages (default 1) and 64 extra pages, and creates exec_map and pipe_map (size maxpipekva) as submaps of kernel_map with kmem_subinit.
note: slice cut the head (vm_init.c:175-286); old prose claimed 'always returns normally' but the function can panic at 227 and 235, and kmi->buffer_eva is set by this function rather than being a precondition

name: vm_map_entry_pred
prose: Static inline function vm_map_entry_pred(entry) returns the in-order predecessor of entry in the vm_map entry tree (a threaded splay tree in which an empty left link points to the predecessor). It sets prior = entry->left; if prior->right->start is less than entry->start it follows prior = prior->right until prior->right == entry, and then returns prior; otherwise (prior->right->start >= entry->start) it returns entry->left itself. entry, entry->left and entry->left->right must be valid non-NULL pointers. It reads the tree only and takes no locks.
note: slice cut the head; vm_map.c:1033-1044. Reviewer round15 right: the returned node is entry->left when prior->right->start >= entry->start, not always the node whose right pointer is entry

name: vm_phys_early_alloc
prose: vm_phys_early_alloc(domain, alloc_size) takes physical memory out of phys_avail[] before the page allocator is running and returns its physical address (it never returns an error). domain must be -1 or a valid domain (checked by KASSERT only). On NUMA kernels with a non-NULL mem_affinity it scans the array up to the first entry of zero size (end == start), picks the largest range, among entries matching domain when domain != -1, and uses it as the [mem_start, mem_end] window (entry 0 if none matched); otherwise the window is all of memory. It then picks the phys_avail chunk with the largest size among those whose end is not above mem_end and for which end - alloc_size is not below mem_start (chunk 0 if none qualifies; alloc_size is not yet rounded here). alloc_size is then rounded up to a whole page. If it equals PAGE_SIZE the page at the start of the chosen chunk is returned and the chunk's start advances by PAGE_SIZE, without checking that the chunk is non-empty. Otherwise align = (chunk end) & (alloc_size - 1); if alloc_size + align exceeds the chunk size it panics; if align is non-zero the tail of align bytes is split into its own chunk with vm_phys_avail_split, or simply discarded (chunk end reduced by align) when the split fails; then the chunk end is reduced by alloc_size and returned as the address, so the block lies at the end of the chunk. The region returned is removed from phys_avail[]; the caller owns it.
note: reviewer round15 right: the mem_affinity loop ends at the first entry with end - start == 0, not end == 0 (vm_phys.c:1960-1963). Also the single-page path has no size check; the KASSERT on domain is debug-only

name: vm_reserv_reclaim_contig
prose: vm_reserv_reclaim_contig(domain, npages, low, high, alignment, boundary) searches the domain's partially populated reservation queue for the least recently changed reservation that has npages contiguous free pages satisfying the physical address range [low, high) and the alignment and boundary constraints; if one is found the reservation is broken and the first page of that run is returned, otherwise NULL is returned. The slice named vm_reserv_alloc_contig is actually this function (vm_reserv.c:1273-1370); vm_reserv_alloc_contig is a different function. It returns NULL at once if npages > VM_LEVEL_0_NPAGES - 1 or if vm_addr_bound_ok(0, size, boundary) fails. Otherwise it takes the per-domain scan lock and the domain reservation lock and walks the queue: reservations entirely below low, entirely above high or with unaligned start are skipped; for the others it locks the reservation (using a marker entry in the queue while the domain lock is dropped if the trylock fails, and skipping the reservation if the queue changed meanwhile), computes the page window inside the reservation allowed by low and high and calls vm_reserv_find_contig. When a position is found it releases the scan lock, adds npages to popcnt, sets the matching popmap bits, calls vm_reserv_reclaim to break the reservation, releases the reservation lock and returns the page at that position (after a KASSERT that its address satisfies alignment and boundary). If the walk ends without a match it releases the domain lock and the scan lock and returns NULL.
note: reviewer round15 right: the slice shown is vm_reserv_reclaim_contig, not vm_reserv_alloc_contig; the old prose described alloc_contig (vm_reserv.c:688-824), which is a different function. Fixed under the real name of the sliced code

name: vm_reserv_populate
prose: vm_reserv_populate(rv, index) marks page index of reservation rv as populated; rv must be locked, rv->object non-NULL, the popmap bit at index clear, popcnt below VM_LEVEL_0_NPAGES, rv->pages->psind in [0, VM_LEVEL_0_PSIND), and rv->domain valid (KASSERTs, debug builds). It sets the popmap bit, increments popcnt, and, when VM_SUBLEVEL_0_NPAGES is defined and the sublevel containing index is now full, sets psind = 1 on that sublevel's first page. If fewer than PARTPOPSLOP ticks have passed since rv->lasttick, rv is on the partially populated queue and popcnt is not yet VM_LEVEL_0_NPAGES, it returns without touching the queue. Otherwise it sets lasttick to ticks and, under the domain reservation lock, removes rv from the queue if it is on it, then if popcnt < VM_LEVEL_0_NPAGES appends it to the tail and sets inpartpopq, or, when the reservation became full, asserts (KASSERT) that rv->pages->psind == VM_LEVEL_0_PSIND - 1 and sets it to VM_LEVEL_0_PSIND, leaving rv off the queue. It returns void.
note: reviewers right: round15 (psind must be VM_LEVEL_0_PSIND - 1 when full, a KASSERT at vm_reserv.c:664) and round2 (sublevel psind), original (PARTPOPSLOP skip); vm_reserv.c:625-670

name: vnode_pager_setsize
prose: vnode_pager_setsize(vp, nsize) tells the VM system that the file's size changed; it returns void. It returns at once if vp->v_object is NULL. In INVARIANTS builds, if vp->v_mount is non-NULL and the mount does not have MNTK_VMSETSIZE_BUG, it asserts that vp is exclusively locked. It takes the object write lock; if the object is OBJT_DEAD, or nsize already equals the stored vnp_size, it unlocks and returns without changes. Otherwise it computes nobjsize = OFF_TO_IDX(nsize + PAGE_MASK). If the file shrank (nsize < vnp_size) it removes cached pages from nobjsize up to the old object size when nobjsize < object->size, and if nsize is not page-aligned it grabs the page containing nsize without creating it; if that page exists and is not entirely invalid it calls vnode_pager_subpage_purge on the bytes from nsize to the end of the page, and the page is then unbusied. In every case that reaches the end, it stores nsize as vnp_size, sets object->size = nobjsize and unlocks the object. Growth only updates the two sizes.
note: reviewers right: round15 (assertion only when v_mount != NULL), round2 (purge only if page exists and is not none-valid), original (function takes the object lock itself; dead object returns before updating vnp_size); vnode_pager.c:496-563

Otherwise, depending on option, it returns bDirty (EntryDirty), the key's bLocal (EntryLocalized), bGlobal (EntryGlobal), bImmutable (EntryImmutable), bDeleted (EntryDeleted), bExpand (EntryExpansion) or bNotify (EntryNotify), and false for any other option value.

prose: KCoreConfigSkeleton::useDefaults(b) switches the skeleton between its normal values and default values. If b equals the current mode d->mUseDefaults it returns that mode (that is, b) and changes nothing. Otherwise it stores b in d->mUseDefaults, calls swapDefault() on every item in d->mItems, calls the virtual usrUseDefaults(b), and returns !d->mUseDefaults, which is the previous mode unless usrUseDefaults changed d->mUseDefaults.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of kconfig_compiler generates a configuration class from a .kcfg XML file and a .kcfgc code-generation file. It creates a QCoreApplication and parses the command line (QCommandLineParser::process may itself exit on --help, --version or a parse error). With --license it prints the license text and returns 0. It returns 1 with a message if fewer than two or more than two positional arguments are given. Otherwise it takes the .kcfg and .kcfgc names, ensures the output directory (-d, default '.') ends with a slash, creates the parameter and XML parser objects, parses the XML, and returns 1 if hasErrors(...) reports a problem; otherwise it adds up the non-modify signals, derives baseName by dropping the last five characters of the input file name, runs the header and source generators (start() then save() each), frees the parsed entries and falls off the end of main, which returns 0.

name: KDirWatchPrivate::removeEntry(KDirWatch *instance, const QString &_path, Entry *sub_entry)
prose: KDirWatchPrivate::removeEntry(instance, _path, sub_entry) looks up the entry registered for _path with entry(_path); if there is none it does nothing; otherwise it calls removeEntry(instance, e, sub_entry) on it. That removes sub_entry from the entry's sub-entry list (or, when sub_entry is NULL, removes the client instance from the entry's clients), so the entry is always changed when it exists; it is dropped from the watch (queued in removeList when delayRemove is set, otherwise unwatched, its StatMode counters updated, its inotify mapping removed and erased from m_mapEntries) only if no clients and no sub-entries are left, in which case the entry pointer becomes invalid. instance may be NULL only when sub_entry is non-NULL.
note: reviewer round15 right on the Entry overload prose ('e unchanged' is wrong when the client or sub-entry was already removed); kdirwatch.cpp:959-967

name: KDirWatchPrivate::removeEntry(KDirWatch *instance, Entry *e, Entry *sub_entry)
prose: KDirWatchPrivate::removeEntry(instance, e, sub_entry) first removes e from removeList. It then removes sub_entry from e->m_entries, or, when sub_entry is NULL, removes the client instance from e (the entry is modified before any early return). If e still has clients or sub-entries it returns. Otherwise, if delayRemove is set it inserts e into removeList (e stays in m_mapEntries, now invalid) and returns. Otherwise, if e's status is Normal it calls removeWatch(e); if not (a NonExistent entry) it removes e from its parent entry by calling removeEntry(nullptr, parent path, e), recursively. If e's mode is StatMode it decrements statEntries and stops the stat rescan timer when it reaches 0; it then removes e's inotify watch descriptor mapping and erases e from m_mapEntries, so the pointer e is no longer valid. It returns void.

name: KJob::emitResult
prose: KJob::emitResult() does nothing if the job is already finished. Otherwise it calls finishJob(true), which sets the finished flag, quits the job's event loop if exec() is running one, emits finished(this), then emits result(this), and finally calls deleteLater() if the job is set to auto-delete. Calling it again after that has no further effect.

name: KMacroExpanderBase::expandMacrosShellQuote
prose: KMacroExpanderBase::expandMacrosShellQuote(str, pos) scans str from index pos, tracking shell quoting state (single quote, $'...', double quote, $(...), $((...)), ${...}, (...) and {...} groups) on a stack, and replaces each macro recognised by expandEscapedMacro (when an escape character is configured and the current character equals it) or expandPlainMacro with its expansion quoted for the current context; str and pos are modified in place. When a macro hook returns a negative length the text is left as is and pos is advanced by the absolute length. An empty expansion outside quotes removes the macro text. Backslashes skip the next character. A backquote construct is rewritten into $( ... ) form: the opening backquote becomes '$( ', backslash escapes of $, backquote, backslash and (inside double quotes) the double quote are unescaped, and the closing backquote becomes ')'. A '$((' that turns out to be '$( (' is detected at the first ')' not followed by ')' and the scan restarts from the saved copy of the string and position. Return values: false at once, with pos at or beyond str.length(), if a backquote construct is not closed before the end of str; otherwise, when the scan ends, it returns true if the context stack is empty and false if it is not. The scan ends when pos reaches str.length() or on a ')' or '}' that does not match an open group of the proper kind (pos is then left at that character), so true can be returned before the end of the string is reached, and false is returned for unclosed quotes or groups. It takes no locks and the caller keeps ownership of str.

name: KStringHandler::capwords(const QString&)
prose: KStringHandler::capwords(text) returns text unchanged if it is empty. Otherwise it takes strippedText = text.trimmed(), splits it on single U+0020 characters, passes the pieces to capwords(const QStringList&) (which uppercases the first UTF-16 unit of each piece), joins the result with single spaces, and returns a copy of text in which strippedText has been replaced by the joined string, so leading and trailing whitespace of text is preserved. Because the split is on every single space, consecutive spaces inside the text produce empty pieces, and so does a text consisting only of whitespace (its trimmed form is empty and splits into one empty piece); capwords(const QStringList&) reads and writes element 0 of every piece, so such input reaches an out-of-range access on an empty string. The input is not modified; the result is a new QString.
note: reviewer round 1 right: empty pieces from consecutive spaces / all-whitespace text reach str[0] on an empty QString in capwords(QStringList) (kstringhandler.cpp:29,40)

name: KStringHandler::capwords(const QStringList&)
prose: KStringHandler::capwords(list) copies list and, for each string in the copy, replaces its first UTF-16 code unit with str.at(0).toUpper(); the other characters are unchanged. The returned list has the same number of elements as list, and list itself is not modified. Every element must be non-empty: for an empty string the code reads and assigns index 0, which is out of range.

name: KStringHandler::perlSplit(QStringView,QStringView,int)
prose: KStringHandler::perlSplit(sep, str, max) returns a new QStringList of the pieces of str separated by occurrences of sep, skipping empty pieces. It repeatedly finds the next occurrence of sep from the current search position and, while an occurrence exists and (max == 0 or fewer than max - 1 pieces have been collected), appends the non-empty piece before it and continues after the occurrence. Afterwards the rest of str after the last consumed occurrence is appended if it is non-empty. So max == 0 means no limit; for max > 0 at most max pieces are returned and the last one holds the unsplit remainder; for max == 1 or max < 0 no separator is consumed and the result is str itself if str is non-empty, or an empty list otherwise. Empty pieces are not counted towards max. sep must be non-empty: for an empty sep the search position never advances and no piece is ever appended, so the loop (entered when max == 0 or max > 1) does not terminate. max must not be INT_MIN (max - 1 would overflow when max != 0). str and sep are not modified.
note: reviewer round 1 wrong: max == 0 is handled as 'no limit' (ignoreMax, kstringhandler.cpp:78,86) and the prose already said so; claim concerns max<=0 and max<0 only. Checked on all four perlSplit overloads

name: KStringHandler::perlSplit(const QString&,const QString&,int)
prose: KStringHandler::perlSplit(sep, s, max) forwards to perlSplit(QStringView(sep), QStringView(s), max) and returns its result: a new QStringList of the non-empty pieces of s between occurrences of sep, where max == 0 means no limit, max > 0 returns at most max pieces with the last holding the unsplit remainder, and max == 1 or max < 0 consumes no separator, giving s itself if non-empty or an empty list otherwise. sep must be non-empty (otherwise the search does not advance) and max must not be INT_MIN. Neither argument is modified.

name: KStringHandler::perlSplit(const QRegularExpression&,const QString&,int)
prose: KStringHandler::perlSplit(sep, str, max) returns an empty list at once if str is empty. Otherwise it copies sep into a local QRegularExpression and calls setPatternOptions(UseUnicodePropertiesOption) on the copy, which replaces whatever pattern options sep had (sep itself is not changed). It iterates over the global matches of the copy in str; while there is a match and (max == 0 or fewer than max - 1 pieces were collected) it appends the non-empty text between the end of the previous match and the start of this match and continues after the match. Afterwards the text after the last consumed match is appended if it is non-empty. max == 0 means no limit, max > 0 returns at most max pieces with the last holding the unsplit remainder, and max == 1 or max < 0 consumes no match, giving a one-element list holding str. Empty pieces are not counted towards max. max must not be INT_MIN. str is not modified.

name: ConnectionBackend::waitForIncomingTask
prose: ConnectionBackend::waitForIncomingTask(ms) waits until one complete command has been received from the worker socket or until ms milliseconds have passed (ms == -1 waits without a time limit); it returns true when a complete command was emitted from socketReadyRead (signalEmitted was set) and false otherwise. The state must be Connected and socket non-null (Q_ASSERTs). If the socket is not in the connected state on entry, it sets state to Idle and returns false without touching signalEmitted. Otherwise it sets signalEmitted = false and, if bytes are already available, calls socketReadyRead(); if that emitted a command it returns true. If not, it loops, calling socket->waitForReadyRead with the remaining time, while the socket is connected, no command has been emitted and the time limit has not expired, leaving the loop when waitForReadyRead returns false. After the loop it returns true if signalEmitted is set; otherwise it sets state to Idle if the socket is no longer connected and returns false (state stays Connected on a timeout with the socket still connected).

name: KIO::DesktopExecParser::resultingArguments
prose: KIO::DesktopExecParser::resultingArguments() const builds the argument list for launching the service's Exec line and returns it as a QStringList; on failure it returns an empty list (with d->m_errorString set) or, for a missing kdesu, a list containing just 'kdesu'. Failures returning an empty list: the Exec field is empty; the executable derived from the Exec line is not found or has no execute permission (error text says which); the Exec line has a shell syntax error (expandMacrosShellQuote fails); or the configured terminal emulator cannot be found, or the terminal command line has a syntax error. If temp files are requested and the application has no X-KDE-HasTempFileOption and there are URLs, it returns the kioexec path with --tempfiles, the Exec string, optionally --suggestedfilename and the URLs. With D-Bus support, URLs that the application cannot handle are mounted through KIOFuse; if a KIOFuse mount fails and some URL is unsupported, it returns the kioexec command line with the Exec string and URLs, otherwise it replaces the mounted URLs by their local paths. It then appends --tempfile when applicable, appends ' %f' if the Exec line has no URL/file specifier, expands the macros, and if the service wants a terminal it starts the result with the terminal command and '-e'. In the end the program is run as: with substituteUid, 'su' (terminal) or the kdesu helper with '-u' (otherwise), then the user name, '-c' and a command string that is either '/bin/sh -c <quoted exec>' when shell metacharacters were found or the joined argument list; without substituteUid, '/bin/sh -c exec' when shell metacharacters were found, otherwise the split argument list, whose first element is replaced by the resolved executable path when one was found. This slice shows only the last part of the function (from the KShell::splitArgs call to the final return).

name: KCoreDirListerCache::slotUpdateResult
prose: KCoreDirListerCache::slotUpdateResult(j) handles the end of a ListJob started to update an already listed directory; it returns void. jobUrl is the job's (possibly redirected) URL with trailing slashes stripped. Listers are collected from directoryData[jobUrl] (those holding the URL plus those listing it, after moveListersWithoutCachedItemsJob), and the list must not be empty (Q_ASSERT, compiled out in release builds). On a job error it calls jobDone(job) on every lister; when the job property _kdlc_silent is false it also emits listingDirCanceled(jobUrl) for each lister; for a lister left with no jobs it sets complete = true regardless of _kdlc_silent and emits canceled() only when not silent; then it removes the job from runningListJobs, calls processPendingUpdates() and returns. On success it looks up the DirItem in itemsInUse (if there is none it logs a warning, asserts in debug builds and would then dereference a null pointer later) and marks it complete; it compares the job's buffered entries with the cached items, skipping entries with an empty name or '..', setting the root item from '.' when none exists yet, hiding local files listed in .hidden, re-inserting items found to have changed (also those queued in pendingUpdates or pendingRemoteUpdates) and notifying listers with addRefreshItem, and collecting new items; it sorts the new items by URL, inserts them into the DirItem and calls addNewItems on every lister; removes the job from runningListJobs; calls deleteUnmarkedItems for the old items not seen again; then for each lister it calls emitItems and jobDone(job), emits listingDirCompleted(jobUrl), and when the lister has no jobs left sets complete = true and emits completed(). Finally it calls processPendingUpdates() and, if the job property need_another_update is true, updateDirectory(jobUrl).

name: FtpInternal::ftpOpenDataConnection
prose: FtpInternal::ftpOpenDataConnection() sets up the FTP data connection by trying connection modes in order; it asserts that the session is logged on and first closes any existing data connection. If passive mode is not disabled (config DisablePassiveMode), it tries PASV (ftpOpenPASVDataConnection), returning 0 on success and otherwise remembering the PASV error code and closing the data connection; unless EPSV is disabled it then tries EPSV and returns 0 on success; if an 'EPSV ALL' command was already sent (epsvAllSent), it returns the PASV error code at that point without trying active mode. Otherwise it tries ftpOpenPortDataConnection and returns 0 on success; if that also fails it closes the data connection and returns the PASV error code if there was one, else the error code of the port attempt. The result is 0 or a positive KIO error code (it can be ERR_INTERNAL, since ftpOpenPortDataConnection returns ERR_INTERNAL for a failed port command, contrary to the comment in the source); on active-mode success m_data is not set, only m_server is listening. The caller is responsible for reporting a non-zero result.
note: reviewers right: round1 (positive KIO codes, not < 0), round2 (active-mode success leaves only m_server listening); ftp.cpp:900-942

name: FtpInternal::ftpOpenPortDataConnection
prose: FtpInternal::ftpOpenPortDataConnection() tries to set up an active-mode data connection; m_control must exist and m_data must be null (asserts). It sets m_bPasv to false and returns ERR_INTERNAL immediately, leaving m_server as it is, if EPRT is known to be unsupported (eprtUnknown). Otherwise it creates m_server (a QTcpServer listening on any address, port 0) if there is none; if m_server is not listening it deletes it, sets it to null and returns ERR_CANNOT_LISTEN. It then sets the maximum pending connections to 1 and builds a PORT command from the control connection's IPv4 local address and the server port, or an EPRT command for an IPv6 local address (the command stays empty for any other address family). If sending the command succeeds with a 2xx reply it returns 0, leaving m_server listening and m_data unset; otherwise it deletes m_server, sets it to null and returns ERR_INTERNAL.
note: reviewers right: round1 (eprtUnknown path leaves m_server), round2 (non-IP address family ends with ERR_INTERNAL, not ERR_CANNOT_LISTEN); ftp.cpp:950-996

name: TrashImpl::adaptTrashSize
prose: TrashImpl::adaptTrashSize(origPath, trashId) makes room in the trash for the path origPath according to the trash's settings in ktrashrc (group named by the trash directory): UseTimeLimit (default false), Days (7), UseSizeLimit (true), Percent (10.0) and LimitReachedAction (0). If UseTimeLimit is set it first deletes every trashed file of this trashId whose deletion date is more than Days days before now. If UseSizeLimit is false it returns true. Otherwise it computes the size of origPath and returns true if the usage percentage of (current trash size + that size) relative to the partition is below Percent. It then evaluates util.usage(partitionSize + additionalSize) and, if that is >= Percent, sets m_lastErrorCode to KIO::ERR_TRASH_FILE_TOO_LARGE with its error message and returns false; because usage() is size * 100 / partition size, this value is at least 100 whenever the partition size is non-zero, so with Percent <= 100 control only gets past this check when the partition size is 0. Past that check: LimitReachedAction 0 sets m_lastErrorCode = KIO::ERR_WORKER_DEFINED with a 'trash is full' message and returns false; action 1 or 2 deletes trashed items oldest-first (action 1) or biggest-first (action 2) until the usage including origPath drops below Percent and returns true (also returns true if all items were deleted without reaching it); any other action value prints a warning and returns false without setting m_lastErrorCode or m_lastErrorMessage.
note: reviewer round15 right: the too-large check is util.usage(partitionSize + additionalSize) >= percent (trashimpl.cpp:1326), not 'empty trash plus origPath', and the action paths are practically unreachable for Percent <= 100; original right about the other-action path; trashimpl.cpp:1275-1368

name: KShortUriFilter::filterUri
prose: KShortUriFilter::filterUri(data) const tries to turn the typed string data.typedString() into a URL; it returns true when it set a result (data's filtered URI and URI type, or the error type with an error message) and false when it could not filter the string and leaves data unmodified. The name filterShortUri used in the packet does not exist: the function is KShortUriFilter::filterUri (kshorturifilter.cpp:99-479). Steps in order: extra leading slashes are reduced to one; absolute local paths become file URLs, others are parsed as URLs; with several '@' in the string all but the last are percent-encoded; an unknown protocol followed by a port-like ':' is treated as no protocol. 'start-here:' returns the 'system:/' URL as LocalDir; strings starting with '#', 'man:' or 'info:' return a man:/ or info:/ URL of type Help; a string starting with two backslashes becomes an smb: URL of type NetProtocol. A leading '~' is expanded to the home directory of the current or named user (a user that does not exist or has no home directory yields type Error with a message and returns true), and a leading '$VAR' is expanded from the environment. A '#ref' is split off an existing path. If an absolute directory was supplied in data it is combined with a relative path and checked for existence; a full local path that exists, or whose last component is a wildcard pattern over an existing directory (a name filter), is returned as a local URL: if the 'open' action is not authorized, as LocalFile; a non-directory with execute permission as Executable; a directory or regular file as LocalDir or LocalFile (name filter appended to the path); other file types fall through. If data.checkForExecutables() is set and the first word of the command is found on $PATH, it returns that executable (type Executable, trailing arguments stored with setArguments). A well-formed URL with a known protocol that is not a local full path is returned as Help for man and help and NetProtocol otherwise. If the string has no space, each configured URL hint whose regular expression matches at position 0 yields the hint's URL and type; a protocol-less potential short URL gets the default scheme prepended (and '://' if needed): a valid result is NetProtocol, an invalid one with a known scheme yields type Error with the original URI, and in both cases it returns true (for an invalid URL with an unknown scheme data is left unmodified but true is returned). Finally a full local path that does not exist is returned as LocalFile (for completion); everything else returns false.
note: slice cut the head: real name KShortUriFilter::filterUri; old prose omitted the early branches (start-here:, man/info, UNC, ~ and $ expansion, errors) and the invalid-short-URL-with-unknown-scheme case, which returns true with data unmodified

name: DelegateAnimationHandler::animationState
prose: DelegateAnimationHandler::animationState(option, index, view) returns the hover animation state for an item of the view, creating or updating it as needed. It returns nullptr at once if view is null or the view is in a dragging state. Otherwise it looks up the existing state for (view, index) and whether option has State_MouseOver. If there is no state and the item is hovered it creates and registers a new AnimationState; it starts the animation unless a fade-in was started less than 300 ms ago, in which case it marks it finished in the forward direction (progress 1.0, not animating); it then restarts the fade-in timer and calls eventuallyStartIteration(index). If a state exists and the item is not hovered and the state is not animating or is moving forward, it sets the direction to backward (progress reset to 0 if the state was created less than 200 ms ago), starts the animation and, if index is the sequence index, stops the sequence iteration and clears the sequence index. If a state exists, the item is hovered and the direction is backward, it sets the direction forward, starts the animation if it is not already running and calls eventuallyStartIteration. If there is no state, the item is not hovered and the model reports HasJobRole for the index, it creates and registers a state, starts its animation and marks it as a job animation. In every case it returns the resulting state, which is nullptr if none was found or created.

name: KIO::JobUiDelegate::askDeleteConfirmation
prose: KIO::JobUiDelegate::askDeleteConfirmation(urls, deletionType, confirmationType) asks the user to confirm a delete, trash or empty-trash operation and returns true if the operation may proceed. With confirmationType ForceConfirmation it always asks; otherwise it reads the key ConfirmDelete (default true), ConfirmTrash (default false) or ConfirmEmptyTrash (default true) from the Confirmations group of the kiorc config and asks only if it is true. If it does not ask it returns true. When it asks, it builds a list of display names (for trash: URLs the leading numeric prefix is removed from the path) and shows a KMessageBox continue/cancel warning appropriate for the deletion type and item count, window modal. Afterwards, if the key name is non-empty and the 'Notification Messages' entry for that key in the default config has become false (the user ticked 'do not ask again'), it sets that entry back to true, syncs it and writes false to the key in kiorc's Confirmations group. It returns true if the user chose Continue and false otherwise. The slice named askContinue; that name does not exist (askDeleteConfirmation, jobuidelegate.cpp:178-302).

name: KXErrorHandler::error
prose: KXErrorHandler::error(sync) const returns the handler's was_error flag, which is set by handle() when an X error for this handler's display and for a request at or after the one current when the handler was created was delivered and was counted as an error: with no user handler set every such error counts, with a user handler it counts when that handler returns true (handler1) or non-zero (handler2). The first counted error is stored and later ones do not change it. If sync is true it first calls XSync(d->display, False), which requires the display to be a valid open connection, so that pending errors are delivered before the flag is read.

It selects the screen: the screen with index screen when screen != -1 and screen < the setup's roots_len, otherwise the first screen; it stores that screen's root window and its width and height in pixels as rootSize. name: AppletQuickItemPrivate::compactRepresentationCheck
prose: AppletQuickItemPrivate::compactRepresentationCheck() switches the applet item between its full and compact representation; it returns void. It returns at once, changing nothing, if initComplete is false, if q's width or height is <= 0, if compactRepresentationCheckGuard is already set, or if the current representation already corresponds to appletShouldBeExpanded() (the full item equals currentRepresentationItem when it is true, the compact item equals it when false). Otherwise it sets compactRepresentationCheckGuard for the duration of the function and clears it before returning. If appletShouldBeExpanded() is true: it calls createFullRepresentationItem(); only if that returns a non-null item, the expander item (if any) has its fullRepresentation and compactRepresentation properties cleared and is hidden; fullRepresentationWasVisible is computed as fullRepresentationItem->parentItem() == q; unless the item is q itself it is parented to q and anchored to fill it; the compact item (if any) is hidden; the item becomes currentRepresentationItem and its layout is connected; and if expanded was false and fullRepresentationWasVisible was false, expanded is set to true and expandedChanged(true) is emitted. If it is false: it calls createCompactRepresentationItem() and createCompactRepresentationExpanderItem(), and only if both return non-null items, it makes the compact item visible, parents the expander to q, makes it visible and anchors it to fill q, sets the full representation's parent property to null only if it exists and was parented to q, sets the expander's compactRepresentation to the compact item and clears its fullRepresentation, makes the compact item currentRepresentationItem with its layout connected, and if expanded was true and the full representation had been parented to q, sets expanded to false and emits expandedChanged(false). When a needed creation call returns null, nothing else changes.
note: reviewers right: original (null creation results leave the state unchanged), round2 (condition is parentItem() == q); appletquickitem.cpp:351-446

name: AppletQuickItem::itemForApplet
prose: Static function AppletQuickItem::itemForApplet(applet) returns the AppletQuickItem of a Plasma::Applet, creating it on first use; the caller must not delete it. It returns nullptr if applet is null. If an item is already cached in s_itemsForApplet it returns that item (this check comes before the shutdown check). Otherwise it returns nullptr if the application is closing down or the applet is destroyed. It then creates a SharedQmlEngine owned by the applet, loads the applet's main script and takes its root object as a ContainmentItem (for containments) or PlasmoidItem (other applets); if the root object has the wrong type and the component has no error it sets a launch error message on the applet. If there is no item, the component has errors or the applet failed to launch, it builds error information (version mismatch messages, QML errors or a missing-package message), logs a warning, loads the shell package's 'appleterror' QML instead and disables the applet's configuration interface; it returns nullptr if that fallback QML itself has errors (without setting a launch error message), and otherwise sets the applet's launch error message to the reason, and returns nullptr if the fallback root object is not a PlasmoidItem (after logging) or else stores the error information in the item's errorInformation property. For an item that was obtained, it stores it in s_itemsForApplet, completes the delayed initialization, marks the applet UI ready (UiReadyConstraint) for non-containments and CustomEmbedded containments, sets the _plasma_applet property, item->d->applet and item->d->qmlObject, sets the 'plasmoid' context property unless PLASMA_NO_CONTEXTPROPERTIES is set, and connects the applet's appletDeleted signal so that the SharedQmlEngine (and with it the item) is deleted and the cache entry removed when the applet is deleted; it also sets the applet's _plasmoid property and returns the item.
note: reviewer round15: 'null applet is dereferenced' is wrong (appletquickitem.cpp:512-514 returns nullptr first); 'fallback-error path returns without setting launch error' is right for the fallback QML-error return (622-624); slice cut the head (510-670)

name: Dialog::event
prose: Precondition: event is a non-null pointer to a valid QEvent and the Dialog's d-pointer is valid. Postcondition: the function has these exits. (1) Expose: if the platform is not Wayland, or the process is KWin, or isExposed() is false, it returns QQuickWindow::event(event) at once. If Wayland outside KWin, exposed, d->needsSetupNextExpose is true and isVisible() is true, it calls d->updateVisibility(true), calls QQuickWindow::event(event) and keeps the result, calls d->updateTheme(), sets d->needsSetupNextExpose to false and returns the kept result. Any other Expose (Wayland outside KWin, exposed, but needsSetupNextExpose false or not visible) falls through to the forwarding block below. (2) Show calls d->updateVisibility(true); Hide calls d->updateVisibility(false) and sets d->needsSetupNextExpose to true; Move with d->type != Dialog::OnScreenDisplay calls PlasmaShellWaylandIntegration::get(this)->setPosition(me->pos()); each of these then falls through. (3) Forwarding block, entered only when d->mainItem is non-null and its size is not empty: for MouseMove/MouseButtonPress/MouseButtonRelease, when d->resizableEdges is non-zero, a MouseMove for which d->updateMouseCursor(globalPosition) returns true returns QQuickWindow::event(event), and a MouseButtonPress whose d->hitTest(globalPosition) & d->resizableEdges is non-zero calls startSystemResize(sides) and returns true; otherwise, if geometry() contains the global position and the main item does not contain the scene position, it builds an adjusted QMouseEvent, sends it to this window only if isVisible(), and returns true whether or not it was sent. Wheel, DragEnter, DragMove and Drop events whose position is outside the main item likewise build an adjusted copy, send it only if isVisible(), and return true (no geometry() check for these). Events inside the main item, DragLeave and all other event types leave the block via break/default. (4) Every path not returned above ends with return QQuickWindow::event(event). The event is not owned or deleted by this function; the adjusted copies are stack objects.
note: slice shows only the body; checked against dialog.cpp:1370-1527. Reviewers' points (Move sets Wayland position; mouse forwarding needs geometry containment and visibility) were right about the old prose and are now stated (1394-1404, 1431-1444). Old prose omitted that the forwarding block needs a non-empty mainItem (1409) and that an Expose with needsSetupNextExpose false or invisible falls through (1387-1393).

name: DrmOutput::computeCapabilities
prose: Precondition: m_connector and m_gpu are valid; the function is const and reads m_connector properties, m_gpu queries, m_autoRotateAvailable, m_autoBrightnessAvailable and m_state (highDynamicRange, brightnessDevice, allowSdrSoftwareBrightness, detectedDdcCi) as currently stored. It is called from the DrmOutput constructor (drm_output.cpp:64) as well as later (e.g. lines 278, 612, 794, 812), so it must not assume the construction is finished; during the constructor call those members hold their initial values. Postcondition: returns a Capabilities set that contains Dpms, IccProfile and CustomModes and additionally: Overscan if overscan or underscan is valid; Vrr if vrrCapable is valid and true; Tearing if the gpu supports async pageflips; RgbRange if broadcastRGB is valid; WideColorGamut if colorspace is valid and has a BT2020_RGB or BT2020_YCC enum, the EDID supports BT2020, and the gpu check passes (on i915: s_allowColorspaceIntel override set or kernel version at least 6.11; on NVIDIA: s_allowColorspaceNVidia override set or driver version at least 565.57.1; on any other gpu: no extra condition); HighDynamicRange if hdrMetadata is valid, the EDID supports PQ and WideColorGamut was just added; AutoRotation if the connector is internal and m_autoRotateAvailable; BrightnessControl if m_state.highDynamicRange, m_state.brightnessDevice or m_state.allowSdrSoftwareBrightness; AutomaticBrightness only when BrightnessControl was added, m_autoBrightnessAvailable is true and it is not the case that HDR is off with a brightness device that uses DDC/CI; BuiltInColorProfile if the EDID is valid and has a default colorimetry; DdcCi if m_state.detectedDdcCi; MaxBitsPerColor if maxBpc is valid; Edr if m_state.brightnessDevice is set and the output is internal; SharpnessControl if the gpu supports sharpness. No locks are taken and nothing is allocated or handed to the caller besides the returned value.

name: WaylandQPainterCursorLayer::doBeginFrame
prose: Precondition: m_backend is valid and its graphicsBufferAllocator() is usable; targetRect() gives the cursor buffer size. Postcondition: if m_swapchain is null or its size differs from targetRect().size(), m_swapchain is replaced by a new QPainterSwapchain of that size with format DRM_FORMAT_ARGB8888. It then assigns m_back = m_swapchain->acquire() (this overwrites the previous m_back even when acquire fails). If m_back is empty it returns std::nullopt and m_renderTime is left unchanged. Otherwise it stores a new CpuRenderTimeQuery in m_renderTime and returns an OutputLayerBeginFrameInfo whose renderTarget wraps m_back->view()->image() and whose repaint region is Region::infinite().

name: GlobalShortcutFilter::touchDown
prose: Precondition: event is a valid TouchDownEvent; this is the GlobalShortcutFilter member (input.cpp:1187) and its members m_gestureTaken, m_gestureCancelled, m_touchPoints, m_lastTouchDownTime and m_syntheticCancel are consistent; workspace()->outputAt(event->pos) must return a valid output when a point is already tracked. Postcondition, by exit: (1) if m_gestureTaken is true: input()->shortcuts()->processSwipeCancel(DeviceType::Touchscreen), m_gestureCancelled = true, return true; the point is not recorded. (2) Otherwise, if m_touchPoints is empty, m_lastTouchDownTime = event->time and flow continues to step 5. (3) If points are tracked and event->time - m_lastTouchDownTime > 250ms: m_gestureCancelled = true and return false, without updating m_lastTouchDownTime and without recording the point. (4) If points are tracked and the time check passes: m_lastTouchDownTime = event->time is updated first, then the distance test runs over the tracked points using the output's orientated physical size (190x100 if that size is invalid) and accepts if some tracked point has |xfactor*dx| + |yfactor*dy| < 50; if no point matches, m_gestureCancelled = true and return false (the time was already updated, the point is not recorded). (5) Otherwise m_touchPoints.insert(event->id, event->pos); if m_touchPoints.count() >= 3 and m_gestureCancelled is false, it sets m_gestureTaken = true, sets m_syntheticCancel true while input()->processFilters(&InputEventFilter::touchCancel) runs, resets it to false, calls processSwipeStart(DeviceType::Touchscreen, count) and returns true. (6) In all other cases it returns false. The event is not owned by this function.

name: GLVertexBuffer::map<T>(size_t count)

The pointer may refer to a GL-mapped range, a persistent idle range or client-side memory depending on the buffer mode (glvertexbuffer.cpp:385-410). The caller must call unmap() and must not make GL calls that access the buffer while it is mapped.

name: OutputConfigurationStore::save
prose: Precondition: this OutputConfigurationStore holds the current m_outputs and m_setups. Postcondition: builds a JSON array with an 'outputs' object (one entry per m_outputs element, each field written only when the optional is set or the string is non-empty) and a 'setups' object (per setup the lidClosed flag and its outputs' enabled, outputIndex, priority, position and replicationSource). Then it forms the path QStandardPaths::writableLocation(ConfigLocation) + '/kwinoutputconfig.json'. If opening it for writing fails it logs a warning with qCWarning and returns without writing. Otherwise it writes document.toJson() and flushes; the QFile is closed by its destructor. It returns void and the caller acquires no lock or memory.

name: OutputConfigurationStore::generateConfig
prose: Precondition: outputs holds valid BackendOutput pointers; m_outputs and m_setups hold the stored state; input() is available if chooseScale needs it for an internal output. Postcondition: (1) if isLidClosed is true and generateLidClosedConfig(outputs) returns a value, that configuration is returned immediately. (2) Otherwise findPartialSetup(outputs, isLidClosed) and the kscreen config (readOutputConfig) are fetched, and the outputs are reordered with std::ranges::partition so that outputs for which findOutputIndex found a stored OutputState (members of globalOutputIndices) come first; outputs with no stored state stay after them, and the order within each group is not guaranteed. (3) For each output a change set is filled: if a partial setup exists and has a state for the output's stored index, enabled, pos and priority come from that setup state, else enabled comes from the kscreen change set or defaults to true unless the lid is closed on an internal output when more than one output exists, pos is the running rightMostPosition (initially (0,0)) and priority is the running counter. mode is the output's own mode equal to the stored mode (size, refresh rate, flags if stored), else the kscreen mode, else chooseMode(output). Stored values (the m_outputs entry, empty if none) are used for scale (else chooseScale; the kscreen scale is deliberately ignored); for transform, manualTransform, overscan, rgbRange and vrrPolicy the stored value is used first, then the kscreen value, then a default; and for the other fields (HDR, reference luminance, wide gamut, auto-rotation, colour profile source, brightness, SDR software brightness, colour power tradeoff, DDC/CI flags, EDR policy, sharpness, automatic brightness) stored value else a hard-coded default; uuid, maxBitsPerColor, customModes and autoBrightnessCurve are copied from the stored state. (4) The priority counter advances and, for enabled outputs, rightMostPosition is updated to the output's top-right corner when that is further right (or same x and higher). The function returns the filled OutputConfiguration. It has two returns (lid-closed config and the final return).
note: checked outputconfigurationstore.cpp:623-725 and findOutputIndex 198-296 / findPartialSetup 582-621. Reviewer round 1 (kscreen scale ignored) right; round 2 (hardcoded defaults) right; round 15 claim that partition is a no-op is WRONG: findOutputIndex can return nullopt (lines 267, 294), so globalOutputIndices does not contain all outputs; but it does contain every output with a stored state, not only those covered by the setup, which the old prose got wrong.

name: OutputConfigurationStore::chooseScale
prose: Precondition: output and mode are valid; for an internal output input()->devices() is consulted. Postcondition: returns 1.0 if the output's physical height or width is below 3. Otherwise it picks targetDpi and minSize (internal output with a lid switch: 125 and 800; internal without: 150 and 360; external with physical height above 500: 30.5 and 800; other external: 96 and 800), computes for each axis the pixel density dpi = pixels / (physical mm / 25.4), a maximum scale clamp(pixels / minSize, 1.0, 3.0) and scale clamp(dpi / targetDpi, 1.0, thatMax), takes the smaller of the two, rounds it to the nearest multiple of 0.05 with std::round and, if the rounded result is below 1.20, returns 1.0 instead. The returned value is therefore 1.0 or a multiple of 0.05 between 1.20 and about 3.0 (rounding can exceed the per-axis maximum by up to 0.025). It has two returns (early 1.0 at line 806 and the final return at 866).
note: slice cut the head: real function is OutputConfigurationStore::chooseScale at outputconfigurationstore.cpp:801-867; slice covers only lines 849-867 of it. Old prose said the result never exceeds min(maxScaleX,maxScaleY) and that raw<1.2 gives 1.0; both imprecise (rounding precedes the 1.20 test, and rounding can overshoot).

name: EisInputCapture::handleEvents
prose: Precondition: m_eis is a valid eis context; m_client, m_seat, m_pointer, m_keyboard and m_absoluteDevice are null or valid references held by this object. Postcondition: calls eis_dispatch, then loops over eis_get_event until it returns null. Per event: CLIENT_CONNECT disconnects a sender client or a second client (leaving m_client unchanged), otherwise connects the client, sets m_client and creates m_seat configured with the allowed capabilities; CLIENT_DISCONNECT for a client other than m_client does nothing; SEAT_BIND creates or removes m_absoluteDevice, m_pointer and m_keyboard according to the capabilities bound; DEVICE_CLOSED nulls whichever of the three members equals the device, then calls eis_device_remove and eis_device_unref on it; other types are logged. After each of these the event is eis_event_unref'd. The exception is CLIENT_DISCONNECT for client == m_client: it unrefs and nulls m_seat and m_client, calls m_manager->removeInputCapture(QDBusObjectPath(m_dbusPath)) and returns from the function at line 274 without unref'ing that event and without touching m_pointer, m_keyboard or m_absoluteDevice. The loop otherwise returns when no events remain.

Old prose claimed device pointers are always null or valid on other paths; on the m_client disconnect return they are left as they were. Event leak on that return checked at 274 vs the unref at 323.

name: grabTexture
prose: Precondition: texture and target are valid pointers, a GL context is current (EglContext::currentContext() is used) and target has allocated storage. Postcondition: a static function. If texture->contentTransform() is Normal or FlipY it calls doGrabTexture(texture, target), which returns without writing target when texture->size() != target->size(), otherwise reads the texture pixels into target (readnpixels through a temporary framebuffer on GLES or NVIDIA, else glGetnTexImage) and flips the rows when needed. For any other transform it computes size = contentTransform.map(texture->size()); if allocating the GL_RGBA8 backing texture fails it returns with target unchanged; otherwise it renders texture into the backing texture through a framebuffer (this happens even if sizes will not match target), then calls doGrabTexture(backingTexture, target), which again leaves target untouched if the sizes differ. So target is filled only when the (transformed) texture size equals target->size(); the transformed path may still perform GL work before returning without modifying target.
