name: TabBox::keyPress
prose: Precondition: this TabBox is valid; keyEvent is a KeyboardKeyEvent. Postcondition: returns nothing. If m_tabGrab is false it returns at once with no state change. Otherwise it tests the shortcut pairs of the TABBOX_MODE_COUNT modes in cyclic order starting from the current mode (a collision keeps the current mode) with matchShortcuts. On the first mode that gives a non-Steady direction: if that mode differs from mode(), it calls accept(false) (activates the current client if one exists and, if that client is a desktop, toggles showing-desktop), calls setMode(testedMode), schedules a 50 ms single-shot that calls reset() and nextPrev(direction == Forward), and returns; if it equals mode(), the loop stops with that direction. If no mode matched (direction Steady): for Qt::Key_Escape it calls close(true) (removes the grab if grabbed, hide(true), clears m_tabGrab and m_noModifierGrab, updates the keyboard, re-enables pointer constraints); for any other key it builds a QKeyEvent(KeyPress, key, NoModifier) and passes it to grabbedKeyEvent; both then return. If a direction matched and keyEvent.state is Repeated, it returns without advancing when direction is Forward and the current row equals clientList().count() - 1 or direction is Backward and the current row is 0. Otherwise it calls KDEWalkThroughWindows(direction == Forward), which calls nextPrev(forward) and so setCurrentIndex plus tabBoxUpdated.
note: slice starts inside the file but the function head is present (tabbox.cpp:902-964). Checked all returns (906, 937, 950, 956, 958, end). Reviewer claim (auto-repeat at list boundary returns without advancing) is right and is stated.

name: MemoryMap::operator=(MemoryMap &&other)
prose: Precondition: *this and other may be in any state (valid mapping, MAP_FAILED, moved-from). Postcondition: if m_data != MAP_FAILED, munmap(m_data, m_size) is called on the old mapping; then m_data and m_size are taken from other with other.m_data set to MAP_FAILED and other.m_size set to 0, and *this is returned. For two distinct objects this leaves other empty and *this owning other's old mapping. Self-assignment (&other == this) is not handled: the mapping is unmapped by the munmap call and then m_data and m_size are re-assigned from their own old values, so the object keeps the stale (already unmapped) pointer and size and the destructor will later call munmap on that stale pointer again.
note: checked memorymap.h:43-51. Reviewer round 15 is right: std::exchange(other.m_data, MAP_FAILED) returns the old value which is then assigned back into the same member, so a self-move leaves a dangling pointer, not MAP_FAILED/0. Old prose wrong.

name: SurfaceInterfacePrivate::applyState
prose: Precondition: next is a non-null pointer to a valid SurfaceState (normally the pending state) and current is valid; q is the owning SurfaceInterface. Postcondition: before merging it records which changes happened (from next->committed and a comparison with current): bufferChanged and bufferReleasePointChanged when the Buffer field is committed and buffer/releasePoint differ, transformChanged when BufferTransform is committed and differs, visibilityChanged when Buffer is committed and bool(buffer) differs, colorDescription/yuvCoefficients change when committed and different, and the plain committed flags for opaque, shadow, blur, contrast, slide, subsurface order, presentation mode hint and alpha multiplier (those are flagged whenever committed, even if the value is the same). It saves the old surfaceSize, bufferSourceBox and inputRegion, calls next->mergeInto(current.get()) (which moves next's committed fields, frame callbacks, damage and buffer damage into current and clears next's committed mask, damage and buffer damage), sets bufferRef = current->buffer and, only if both a buffer and a release point exist, registers the release point on the buffer, resets presentationFeedback if there is no buffer, and sets scaleOverride = pendingScaleOverride. With a buffer it recomputes bufferSourceBox, surfaceSize (viewport destination size, else viewport source size, else the transformed buffer size over bufferScale), inputRegion (input & surface rect), opaqueRegion (the whole surface rect if the buffer has no alpha channel, else opaque & surface rect), and bufferDamage (buffer damage united with mapped damage, limited to the buffer rect), clears current's damage and bufferDamage, and, if scaleOverride != 1.0, scales and rounds out the opaque and input regions and divides surfaceSize by scaleOverride; without a buffer it sets size 0, empty source box, empty damage, input and opaque regions. It then emits signals: opaqueChanged when the opaque flag was committed; inputChanged when the input region differs; bufferTransformChanged; updateEffectiveMapped() (not a signal) when visibilityChanged; bufferSourceBoxChanged when the box differs; bufferChanged; sizeChanged when the size differs; shadowChanged, blurChanged, contrastChanged, slideOnShowHideChanged, childSubSurfacesChanged when committed; when the color description or rendering intent changed, or the YUV coefficients changed, it replaces current->colorDescription with withYuvCoefficients(coefficients, range) and emits colorDescriptionChanged; presentationModeHintChanged, bufferReleasePointChanged, alphaMultiplierChanged; damaged(bufferDamage) if non-empty. Finally parentApplyState() is called on every below and above subsurface of current, extension->applyState on every extension state, and committed() is emitted. The caller keeps ownership of both states.
note: checked surface.cpp:679-821 and mergeInto (surface.cpp:622-677). Slice cut the head; function is SurfaceInterfacePrivate::applyState. Reviewers: release-point (round 0), flags-emitted-even-if-unchanged (round 1) and yuvCoefficients (round 2) were all right about older wordings and are now stated.

name: Window::setupWindowManagementInterface
prose: Precondition: this Window is valid; waylandServer() is available. Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns immediately, changing nothing, if m_windowManagementInterface is already set or if waylandServer()->windowManagement() is null. Otherwise it creates a PlasmaWindowInterface with windowManagement()->createWindow(this, internalId()), fills it from the window's current state (title, active, fullscreen, keep above/below, maximized, minimized, demands attention, closeable/maximizable/minimizable/fullscreenable, application menu paths, icon, resource name and app id, skip taskbar/switcher, pid, resizable/movable, virtual-desktop-changeable true, no-border and can-set-no-border, exclude-from-capture, parent window, frame and client geometry), connects Window signals so later changes are pushed to it, connects its request signals (close, move, resize, fullscreen, minimized, maximized, keep above/below, demands attention, active (activates the window only when set is true), no-border, exclude-from-capture, enter/enter-new/leave virtual desktop, enter/leave activity, send-to-output) to Window actions, adds the window's virtual desktops then sets on-all-desktops, adds its activities, and finally stores the interface in m_windowManagementInterface. The Window deletes it only in destroyWindowManagementInterface (window.cpp:1922-1926).
note: slice cut the head: the real function is Window::setupWindowManagementInterface (window.cpp:1727-1920); createWindowManagementInterface does not exist. Two early returns at 1731 and 1735. Old prose invented a name and said 'm_windowManagementInterface is null' as a precondition, but the code handles the non-null case by returning.

name: Window::setKeepAbove
prose: Precondition: none; any bool b. Postcondition: b is replaced by rules()->checkKeepAbove(b). If the replaced value is true and rules()->checkKeepBelow(false) is false, setKeepBelow(false) is called, before the equality test, so it can change keep-below state even if keep-above does not change. If the value equals keepAbove(), the function then returns with no further change. Otherwise m_keepAbove is set, doSetKeepAbove() and updateLayer() are called, updateWindowRules(Rules::Above) is called and keepAboveChanged(m_keepAbove) is emitted.

name: X11Window::readUserTimeMapTimestamp
prose: Precondition: info is valid; if asn_data is non-null and info->userTime() is non-zero, asn_id must be non-null (it is dereferenced); asn_data may be null; session is true or false. Postcondition: let time = info->userTime(). If asn_data is non-null and time != 0 and asn_id->timestamp() != 0 and (time == 4294967295 or NET::timestampCompare(asn_id->timestamp(), time) > 0), time is replaced by asn_id->timestamp(). If the resulting time is not 4294967295 (including 0), it is returned. If it is 4294967295: when the active window (as an X11Window) exists and does not belong to the same application (RelaxedForActive), the function decides whether this is the first window of the application (for a transient window: first if the active window has this as transient, or this is group-transient and no main window matches the same-application predicate; for a non-transient window: first unless the workspace has another client matching the same-application predicate), and returns 0 if it is not the first window and the effective focus-stealing-prevention level is above None; otherwise, if session is true it returns 4294967295, else it returns readUserCreationTime() (which is 4294967295 when the property is missing). The function is const and acquires nothing.
note: checked x11window.cpp:4191-4272. Reviewer round 1 (asn_id may be null) is right as to the precondition; round 2 (ASN used only when ASN timestamp non-zero) is right and the guard is now stated.

name: X11Window::allowWindowActivation
prose: Precondition: time is an X timestamp or 4294967295 meaning unknown; focus_in says whether activation follows a FocusIn event; this is a valid window. Postcondition: returns a bool, by this order of checks: t = time, or userTime() when time is 4294967295; level = rules()->checkFSP(options->focusStealingPreventionLevel()); true if the session manager is Saving and level <= Medium; ac = the active window, or the last active window if focus_in and there is no active window; false if t == 0 and rules()->checkAcceptFocus(false) is false; protection = ac's checkFPP(Medium) or None when ac is null; true if level == None or protection == None; false if level == Extreme or protection == Extreme; true if ac is null or ac->isDesktop(); true if the window belongs to the same application as ac (RelaxedForActive) and protection < High; false if level > Medium and protection > Low; if t == 4294967295, true when level < Medium and protection < High, else false; otherwise NET::timestampCompare(t, ac->userTime()) >= 0. No state is changed.
note: checked x11window.cpp:4348-4429. Reviewer round 2 (session saving can return true even with t==0) is right and the order is now explicit; round 1 concerned the formal contract, now empty.

name: _gtk_accelerator_parse
prose: Precondition: accelerator should be a NUL-terminated string; accelerator_key and accelerator_mods are NULL or point to writable storage. Postcondition: returns nothing. First, each non-NULL output pointer is set to 0. If accelerator is NULL, g_return_if_fail returns at that point with both outputs 0. Otherwise it scans the string: modifier tokens <release>, <control>, <ctrl>, <ctl>, <shift>, <shft>, <alt>, <mod1> to <mod5>, <hyper>, <super> add the corresponding GDK mask (hyper and super both add GDK_MOD4_MASK), <meta> is consumed without adding a mask, and any other <...> token is skipped up to and including the next '>'. A string that does not start with '<' at the current position is treated as the key: if it begins with '0x' followed by two hex digits (a hex keycode, at least 4 chars) the function sets an error because it cannot store keycodes; otherwise keyval is _gdk_keyval_from_name of the whole rest of the string and an unknown name (GDK_KEY_VoidSymbol) sets an error. The rest of the string is consumed by the key. On error both results are set to 0; otherwise *accelerator_key is the keyval (0 if there was no key part) and *accelerator_mods the accumulated mask, each only when its pointer is non-NULL. An unterminated '<' makes the skip loop at lines 258-264 consume past the terminating NUL and leave len at -1, after which the outer while (len) loop continues reading beyond the string.
note: slice cut the head: real function is _gtk_accelerator_parse (gtkaccelparse_p.c:157-315). The out-of-bounds note is from tracing lines 258-264 with an input like "<"; checked by hand, not by running.

name: ibus_panel_impanel_navigate
prose: Precondition: impanel is a valid IBusPanelImpanel with a usable engineManager; when impanel->selected < 0 the bus is a valid IBusBus. Postcondition: returns nothing. If start is true, impanel->selected is set to -1 first (even if the function then returns early). If engineManager->length() < 2 it returns. Otherwise it picks engine_desc: ibus_bus_get_global_engine(bus) when selected < 0; engines()[selected] with an added reference when 0 <= selected < length(); null when selected >= length(). If engine_desc is null it uses engines()[0] with an added reference. (If engines()[0] is itself null the final else branch returns without changing selected.) It then calls engineManager->navigate(engine_desc, forward), sets impanel->selected to (int)getIndexByName(name) (that function returns length() when the name is not found, not -1), unrefs engine_desc, and calls ibus_panel_impanel_real_register_properties(impanel) only if 0 <= selected < length().
note: checked panel.cpp:126-160 and enginemanager.cpp:84-133. Reviewer round 15 right (engines()[0] fallback also covers selected >= length()); round 1 right (start resets selected before early return). Old prose said getIndexByName may give -1: wrong, it gives length().

name: Backend::parentPid
prose: Precondition: this is a Backend and pid is a process id. Postcondition: const function that builds a local KSysGuard::Processes table and calls updateOrAddProcess(pid). It returns -1 if no process object is found for pid. If the process's parentPid() is -1 it returns -1. Otherwise it updates the table with the parent pid and returns -1 if the parent process object is not found; returns parentProc->pid() if proc's cgroup is non-empty and equal to the parent's cgroup; and returns -1 otherwise. The table is destroyed on return and nothing is handed to the caller.
note: slice cut the head: real function is Backend::parentPid (backend.cpp:494-519). Four returns: 501, 510, 514, 518.

name: Attica::KdePlatformDependent::loadAccessToken
prose: Precondition: none beyond a constructed object. Postcondition: returns nothing. If KAccounts::accountsManager() is null it logs a debug message and returns. Otherwise, for each account id of type "opendesktop-rating": it logs, skips ids for which accountsManager->account(id) is null (with a warning), and for the others creates a KAccounts::GetCredentialsJob (child of the accounts manager) and connects its finished signal to a lambda. When a job finishes, the lambda reads the IdToken from the credentials; if empty it logs a warning and leaves m_accessToken unchanged; otherwise it sets m_accessToken to the token and emits readyChanged(). The function itself does not wait for the jobs, so m_accessToken is changed later, by whichever job finishes with a non-empty token, with the last such job winning.
note: slice cut the head: real function is Attica::KdePlatformDependent::loadAccessToken (kdeplatformdependent.cpp:239-277); the dropped item was the loop/lambda inside it. Whether the job is started is not visible in this function.

name: mouseKeysShortcut
prose: Precondition: display is a valid X Display pointer. Postcondition: returns a QString. It returns an empty string if neither XK_MouseKeys_Enable nor XK_Pointer_EnableKeys maps to a non-zero keycode, if XkbGetMap fails, or if the chosen keysym is not found in the key's groups/levels (the Xkb map is freed before the last of these returns). Otherwise it takes the modifier mask of the first active type-map entry matching the keysym's level, builds the key name from KKeyServer::xEventToQt and QKeySequence(key).toString(), and prepends modifier names in this order of prepending: AltGraph, Hyper, Super, the translated word "Meta" (when the Meta/Win modifier is set), the Qt::META key-sequence text (same condition), Alt, Ctrl, Shift, each followed by '+', when the corresponding bit is in the found modifier mask (AltGr/Meta/Super/Hyper masks computed from Xkb with the bits of the other modifiers removed). The returned string is that name.
note: slice cut the head: real function is mouseKeysShortcut (kaccess.cpp:468-555). Note the WinMask test appears twice (lines 543-546) so a Meta modifier adds both 'Meta+' and the Qt::META text.

name: KAccessConfig::launchOrcaConfiguration
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns nothing. It runs QProcess::execute("gsettings", {"set", "org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications", "screen-reader-enabled", "true"}) and waits for it. If the return value is non-zero (including the not-started and crashed codes) it sets the orca launch feedback to an error text naming that command and returns without starting orca. Otherwise it calls QProcess::startDetached("orca", {"--setup"}, QString(), &pid) and, if that returns false, sets the feedback to the text 'Error: Could not launch "orca --setup"'. On success the pid is only stored in a local variable and no feedback is set or cleared.
note: slice cut the head: real function is KAccessConfig::launchOrcaConfiguration (kcmaccess.cpp:246-265). Three exits: 257, 264 (feedback), and normal end.

Postcondition: sets the current value of m_enabled to true, m_leftHanded to false, the current pointer acceleration, flat and adaptive profile values, disable-events-on-external-mouse, disable-while-typing, tap-to-click, tap-and-drag, tap-drag-lock, middle emulation, natural scroll, two-finger, edge and on-button-down scrolling, click-method areas and click-finger to their stored default values, and m_scrollFactor to 1.0. name: DeviceModel::data
prose: Precondition: this is the const model; index belongs to it. For a child index, the settings must hold device info for the UDI (the Q_ASSERT at line 289 only checks this in debug builds). Postcondition: returns an empty QVariant for an invalid index. For a top-level index (no parent): DisplayRole in column 0 gives the row text for rows RowAll ("All Devices" or "All Known Devices" depending on automountUnknownDevices), RowAttached and RowDetached; CheckStateRole for row RowAll gives Qt::Checked/Unchecked from automountOnLogin in column 1 and automountOnPlugin in column 2; every other top-level combination gives an empty QVariant. For a child index: an empty QVariant if the parent row is above RowDetached, the column is >= columnCount() (3) or the row is >= rowCount(parent) (this includes all children of RowAll, whose rowCount is 0). Otherwise TypeRole gives Attached or Detached by the parent row, Qt::UserRole gives the UDI string, and then by column: column 0 gives for attached devices the Solid description (DisplayRole), the text "UDI: ..." (ToolTipRole) or the Solid icon (DecorationRole), and for detached devices the stored name, tooltip and stored icon; column 1 gives CheckStateRole as Checked/Unchecked from shouldAutomountDevice(udi, Login) and a login tooltip; column 2 gives the same for Attach; any other role/column combination gives an empty QVariant. No state is modified.
note: slice cut the head: real function is DeviceModel::data (DeviceModel.cpp:248-331). Reviewer round 15 is right: child CheckStateRole in columns 1 and 2 was missing from the old prose.

name: ref_main
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are as passed to main; the function parses its own options (getopt with "HLPRfhvx") into local flags. Postcondition: it never returns normally: every exit is exit(rval) or a call that exits. ref_usage() (prints usage and exit(1)) is called for an unknown option or when fewer than two arguments remain after the options. With -R and -h together it calls errx(1). The flags argument is parsed as octal if it starts with a digit '0'..'7' (err(1) if errno is set or the value is negative, errx(1) if trailing characters remain) and otherwise as symbolic flags with strtofflags (errx(1) if it fails). It then calls fts_open on the remaining files (err(1) if NULL) and loops with fts_read: FTS_D entries are skipped when -R is not given and otherwise processed at the post-order visit; FTS_DNR sets rval = 1 after a warning and still falls through to the flag change; FTS_ERR and FTS_NS warn, set rval = 1 and continue; each other entry gets newflags = the octal value, or (st_flags | set) & clear, is skipped if equal to the current flags, and otherwise chflagsat is called; a failure sets rval = 1 and warns unless -f, and a success prints the path (and old/new flags at -vv or on SIGINFO) when -v or SIGINFO. If errno is non-zero after the loop it calls err(1, "fts_read"). Otherwise it calls exit(rval), which is 0 unless some FTS error occurred or a chflagsat failed without -f.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_main (oracle.c:203-355). Old prose said the option globals were already set by option parsing; they are locals set by getopt in this function.

name: ref_pop_undo_stack
prose: Precondition: u_p is the number of valid entries in ustack; each entry has type UADD, UDEL, UMOV or VMOV and each UMOV/VMOV entry has its partner at the next lower index. Postcondition: if u_current_addr == -1 or u_addr_last == -1 it sets errmsg to "nothing to undo" and returns ERR with no other change. Otherwise: modified is set to 1 only when u_p != 0; get_addressed_line_node(0) is called and SPL1() is raised unconditionally (also when u_p == 0). It walks the stack from the top down re-linking nodes (UADD: unlink the range; UDEL: relink it; UMOV/VMOV: the pair is handled in one step), toggling each processed entry's type with ^= 1 (for a UMOV/VMOV pair only the lower entry's type is toggled), then reverses the order of the u_p entries, calls clear_active_list() if isglobal is set, exchanges current_addr with u_current_addr and addr_last with u_addr_last, calls SPL0() and returns 0.
note: checked oracle.c:538-583. Reviewer round 15 is right: the 'else if (u_p) modified = 1;' only guards modified; get_addressed_line_node(0) and SPL1 are unconditional. Round 2 (only lower UMOV/VMOV entry toggled) right and already in the old prose.

name: ref_exec_command
prose: Precondition: ibufp points at the command letter in the command buffer; addr_cnt, first_addr, second_addr, current_addr, addr_last and the editor state (isglobal, modified, scripted, errmsg, old_filename and the static substitution pattern state) are those of the command just parsed. Postcondition: reads one command letter after skipping blanks and runs that command. It returns ERR (with errmsg set by the command or its helpers) for the error cases of each command (bad address range, unexpected address or suffix, invalid destination, invalid pattern delimiter, no previous substitution, nested global command, unknown command, failed helper, crypt command 'x'), EMOD for 'e' on a modified buffer when not scripted, FATAL only for 'e'/'E' when close_sbuf succeeded but open_sbuf failed, and otherwise returns gflag: 0 for most commands, or the accumulated print-suffix bits (GPR/GLS/GNP from the p, l, n suffix) for commands such as a, c, d, i, j, m, t, which makes the caller print the current line; EOF for 'q'/'Q' (and for 'wq'/'wQ' unless the write left a modified non-scripted buffer, in which case EMOD, and for 'q' alone EMOD when the buffer is modified and not scripted). Errors do not guarantee the buffer is unchanged: for 'e'/'E' the buffer lines are deleted (delete_lines(1, addr_last)) and the undo stack cleared before close_sbuf/open_sbuf/read_file are tried, so those errors leave an emptied buffer; other commands that fail inside a helper may have already changed lines.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_exec_command (oracle.c:1873-2296); every return was checked against cases a to '='/'!'/newline and the final 'return gflag'. Old prose claimed ERR leaves the buffer unchanged or recoverable by undo; not true for e/E (lines 1928-1946).

name: ref_move_lines
prose: Precondition: first_addr..second_addr is a valid non-empty range of existing lines and addr is a destination in 0..addr_last that is not inside the range, i.e. addr < first_addr or addr >= second_addr (the caller 'm' checks this). Postcondition: SPL1() is called on entry and SPL0() before each return. If addr == first_addr - 1 or addr == second_addr nothing is relinked and no undo record is pushed; current_addr = second_addr. Otherwise two UMOV undo records are pushed with push_undo_stack and the lines are relinked after addr, and current_addr becomes addr + (second_addr - first_addr + 1) when addr < first_addr and addr otherwise. In both cases, if isglobal the moved lines are removed from the active node set, modified = 1 and the function returns 0. If either push_undo_stack call returns NULL, the function returns ERR after SPL0() without relinking; because push_undo_stack's failure path (realloc failure) clears and frees the whole undo stack, no UMOV record of this call remains, and current_addr, modified and the active set are unchanged.
note: checked oracle.c:2515-2554 and ref_push_undo_stack (oracle.c:531-560). Old prose said the first UMOV record stays after a second-push failure; push_undo_stack clears the entire stack on its failure path (lines 552-559), so that is wrong.

name: ref_copy_lines
prose: Precondition: first_addr..second_addr is a valid non-empty range of existing lines and addr is in 0..addr_last. Postcondition: current_addr is set to addr at the start. If first_addr <= addr < second_addr the lines first_addr..addr are copied first and then the lines originally at addr+1..second_addr; otherwise lines first_addr..second_addr are copied in order. Each copy is made under SPL1()/SPL0() around that single line: dup_line_node, add_line_node (inserts after current_addr and advances current_addr), then for the first copy push_undo_stack(UADD, current_addr, current_addr) and for later copies up->t is moved to the new line, then modified = 1. On success it returns 0 with current_addr = addr + (second_addr - first_addr + 1) and modified = 1, and one UADD record covers all inserted lines. If dup_line_node fails it calls SPL0() and returns ERR with the lines copied so far still inserted (current_addr at the last inserted line, or addr if none) and modified = 1 only if at least one line was completely processed. If push_undo_stack fails (only possible for the first copy) the line has already been inserted by add_line_node, current_addr has advanced, modified is not set by this call, the undo stack has been cleared by push_undo_stack's failure path, and the function returns ERR.
note: checked oracle.c:2556-2587. Reviewer round 1 (SPL1 per line, not on entry) already reflected; checked np re-fetch for the overlapping case at line 2568.

name: ref_get_marked_node_addr
prose: Precondition: n is a character code; the code uses islower((unsigned char)n), so values outside 0..255 are not valid inputs (a value whose low byte is a lowercase letter would pass the test and then index mark[] out of range). Postcondition: if n is not a lowercase letter it sets errmsg to "invalid mark character" and returns ERR. Otherwise it returns get_line_node_addr(mark[n - 'a']): the line number of the marked node when the node is in the buffer list; if the mark is unset (NULL) or the node is not in the list, get_line_node_addr walks the list, and when the buffer is non-empty it sets errmsg to "invalid address" and returns ERR; for an unset mark on an empty buffer it returns 0. No locks are taken and nothing is allocated or freed.
note: checked oracle.c:2645-2652 and ref_get_line_node_addr (oracle.c:978-990). Reviewer round 1 ('get_line_node_addr returns ERR without setting errmsg') is WRONG: line 986 sets errmsg = "invalid address". The old prose repeated that mistake and is corrected; the empty-buffer case returning 0 is new.

name: ref_exec_global
prose: Precondition: interact is 0 or 1 and gflag holds print-suffix flags; when interact is 0, ibufp addresses the rest of the global command (under BACKWARDS a lone newline gives the command 'p'). Postcondition: returns long. When interact is 0 it reads the command list with get_extended_line; if that fails it returns ERR before clear_undo_stack is called. Then clear_undo_stack() is called and the function loops over the active lines: it sets current_addr = get_line_node_addr(lp) and returns ERR (leaving the negative value in current_addr) if that is negative. In interactive mode it displays the line (return ERR if display_lines fails), reads a reply with get_tty_line (negative: returns ERR; zero: errmsg 'unexpected end-of-file', ERR); a lone newline skips the line; '&' reuses the saved command or, if there is none, sets errmsg 'no previous command' and returns ERR; otherwise it reads the command with get_extended_line (ERR on failure) and copies it into the static buffer ocmd, growing ocmdsz with REALLOC (on failure errmsg 'out of memory' and ERR). It then runs the command list on that line: for each command it calls extract_addr_range and exec_command, and a negative status from either (ERR, EMOD, FATAL, or EOF from 'q') is returned immediately; a positive status from exec_command is passed to display_lines, whose negative result is also returned. Remaining active lines are then not processed. If all active lines are done it returns 0.
note: checked oracle.c:704-765 and REALLOC (oracle.c:97-111). Reviewer round 15 is right: get_line_node_addr failure leaves current_addr negative (line 726). Round 2 (clear_undo_stack after get_extended_line) is right and stated; round 1 (get_line_node_addr failure return) right.

name: ref_st_hash
prose: Precondition: name points to at least len readable bytes (len >= 0) and tabsz > 0 (the final key % tabsz divides by tabsz after conversion to unsigned int). Postcondition: if len exceeds MAXKEYLEN (128) only the last 128 bytes are used. The used bytes are consumed as steps = len/sizeof(u_int) chunks of sizeof(u_int) bytes copied into a u_int in memory order and added to key with unsigned wraparound, plus, if res = len % sizeof(u_int) is non-zero, a final chunk of the last res bytes zero-padded on the right (val = 0 first). It returns key % tabsz computed in unsigned arithmetic. The sum wraps modulo 2^32 before the reduction by tabsz. Nothing is allocated or modified outside local variables.

name: ref_yylex
prose: Precondition: arith_buf points to a NUL-terminated string; if the next token is an identifier, the malloc behind stalloc succeeds (its result is not checked). Postcondition: calls oracle_init_is_type(), then skips ' ', '\t' and '\n' in a local pointer. For a letter or '_' it stores a malloc'd NUL-terminated copy of the identifier in yylval.name (ownership passes to the caller), sets arith_buf past it and returns ARITH_VAR (6). Otherwise it returns the operator code, with arith_buf advanced past the token: '=' gives ARITH_ASS (1) or ARITH_EQ (12) for '=='; '||' ARITH_OR (2); '&&' ARITH_AND (3); '!' ARITH_NOT (7) or ARITH_NE (23) for '!='; '<' ARITH_LT (10), '<=' ARITH_LE (8), '<<' ARITH_LSHIFT (15), '<<=' ARITH_LSHIFTASS (26); '>' ARITH_GT (11), '>=' ARITH_GE (9), '>>' ARITH_RSHIFT (16), '>>=' ARITH_RSHIFTASS (27); '%' ARITH_REM (13) or ARITH_REMASS (24); '&' ARITH_BAND (14) or ARITH_BANDASS (25); '*' ARITH_MUL (17) or ARITH_MULASS (28); '+' ARITH_ADD (18) or ARITH_ADDASS (29); '|' ARITH_BOR (19) or ARITH_BORASS (30); '-' ARITH_SUB (20) or ARITH_SUBASS (31); '^' ARITH_BXOR (21) or ARITH_BXORASS (32); '/' ARITH_DIV (22) or ARITH_DIVASS (33); '(' ARITH_LPAREN (34); ')' ARITH_RPAREN (35); '~' ARITH_BNOT (36); '?' ARITH_QMARK (37); ':' ARITH_COLON (38). yylval is modified only for ARITH_NUM and ARITH_VAR.

name: tmp
prose: Precondition: none; reads TMPDIR with secure_getenv. Postcondition: formats "<TMPDIR or /tmp>/bt.XXXXXXXXXX" into a MAXPATHLEN buffer. If the formatted length is negative or does not fit it sets errno to ENAMETOOLONG and returns -1 before touching the signal mask. Otherwise it blocks all signals (saving the old mask), calls mkostemp(path, O_CLOEXEC), unlinks the path if mkostemp succeeded, restores the saved signal mask, and returns the descriptor from mkostemp, which is -1 (with errno as set by mkostemp) on failure.

name: ref___bt_stkacq
prose: Precondition: t is a valid btree with a buffer pool, *hp is a pinned page, c is the cursor with a key and cursor page number c->pg.pgno. Postcondition: returns 0 on success and 1 on failure. It first releases the page *hp (mpool_put) and runs __bt_search for c->key; if that returns NULL it returns 1 with *hp unchanged. If the page found has pgno == c->pg.pgno it skips to the exit. Otherwise it walks right along nextpg links, repairing the descent stack with BT_POP/BT_PUSH, and if the cursor page is still not found it re-runs __bt_search and walks left along prevpg links. Any mpool_get failure during the walks, or a failing __bt_search, returns 1 with *hp unchanged. When a walk ends (cursor page found, or no more neighbours) control reaches the exit, which releases the page it holds and sets *hp = mpool_get(c->pg.pgno): the function returns 0 if that fetch succeeds (even if the walks did not locate the cursor page) and returns 1 with *hp set to NULL if it fails. On success *hp is the cursor page, pinned, and the descent stack is the path of the last page visited (the cursor page itself is not pushed).
note: checked oracle.c:402-532 (record starts mid-file but head present). Reviewer round 1 right (exit reached even when the cursor page is not located); round 2 right (not pushed); round 15 right (*hp becomes NULL on final fetch failure).

name: ref___hdtoa
prose: Precondition: d is any double; xdigs points to the hex digit string; decpt, sign are valid int pointers; rve may be NULL; ndigits is the requested digit count (0 is treated as 1, negative means as many as needed). Postcondition: sets *sign from the sign bit of d. For zero it sets *decpt = 1 and returns nrv_alloc("0", rve, 1); for infinity it sets *decpt = INT_MAX and returns nrv_alloc("Infinity", rve, 8); for NaN or any unrecognised class it sets *decpt = INT_MAX and returns nrv_alloc("NaN", rve, 3). For normal and subnormal values (subnormals are scaled by 2^514 first) it sets *decpt from the exponent, allocates bufsize = ndigits (or SIGFIGS if ndigits < 0) with rv_alloc, rounds to ndigits hex digits when 0 < ndigits < SIGFIGS (this can change *decpt), writes a leading '1' followed by hex digits taken from the mantissa, trims trailing zero digits when ndigits was negative, NUL-terminates the string at position ndigits, sets *rve to that terminator if rve is not NULL, and returns the allocated string (to be released with freedtoa by the caller).

name: ref_rangematch
prose: Precondition: pattern points just past the opening '[' of a NUL-terminated pattern (this function itself consumes a leading '!' or '^' as negation); test is the wide character to match; string is the position in the subject string after test; patmbs and strmbs point to mbstate_t objects; newp and news are writable pointers. Postcondition: returns RANGE_MATCH (1) when the bracket expression matches test (taking negation into account), RANGE_NOMATCH (0) when it does not match, or when the pattern contains a '/' while FNM_PATHNAME is set, or when mbrtowc finds an invalid or incomplete sequence in the pattern; and RANGE_ERROR (-1) for a malformed expression (pattern ends before the closing ']', a [. [= [: construct without its terminator, a collating symbol that is empty, unknown or multi-character where it is not allowed, a range start or end that is an equivalence class or character class, an unknown character class name, or a range end that is NUL). Only on the normal exit (after scanning to the closing ']') it stores a pointer just past that ']' in *newp and the current subject position in *news; this subject position can be ahead of the argument if a multi-character collating symbol or equivalence class consumed subject characters. Every early return leaves *newp and *news unmodified. *patmbs and *strmbs may be modified by the multibyte conversions.

name: ref_fts_build
prose: Precondition: sp is a valid FTS handle, sp->fts_cur (cur) is a directory node, and type is BREAD, BNAMES or BCHILD. Postcondition: the function has these exits. (1) If __opendir2(cur->fts_accpath) fails it returns NULL; only when type == BREAD it also sets cur->fts_info = FTS_DNR and cur->fts_errno = errno; no directory stream was opened. Otherwise it reads all entries: when a chdir into the directory is needed (nlinks non-zero or type == BREAD) and fails, it sets FTS_DONTCHDIR on cur (and cur->fts_errno = errno when nlinks and type == BREAD) and every entry becomes FTS_NS with fts_errno = that errno if nlinks is non-zero or FTS_NSOK otherwise; entries that need no stat are FTS_NSOK, the others get their fts_info from fts_stat; afterwards, if FTS_NOSTAT_TYPE is set, any FTS_NSOK entry (including those from the failed-chdir case) is converted from d_type to FTS_DEFAULT, FTS_F, FTS_SL or FTS_W when d_type is one of the listed types. (2) If fts_alloc or growing the path buffer fails, it frees the entries so far, closes the stream, sets cur->fts_info = FTS_ERR, sets FTS_STOP, restores errno and returns NULL without changing the working directory back. (3) A readdir error sets cur->fts_errno and cur->fts_info = FTS_ERR if some items were read or FTS_DNR if not; the stream is closed. (4) If we descended and (type == BCHILD or no items were read) and changing back (to sp->fts_rfd at the root level, otherwise to ".." via the parent) fails, it frees the list, sets cur->fts_info = FTS_ERR, sets FTS_STOP and returns NULL. (5) If no items were found it returns NULL, and for type == BREAD sets cur->fts_info = FTS_DP unless it is already FTS_DNR or FTS_ERR. (6) Otherwise it sorts the list with fts_compar when there is one and more than one item and returns the head of the new singly linked list (owned by the caller). When FTS_NOCHDIR is set the path buffer is reset to its original length before exits (3) to (6).
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_fts_build (oracle.c:742-1030). Reviewer round 15 is right (FTS_NOSTAT_TYPE conversion also applies to FTS_NSOK entries from the failed chdir). Old prose claimed the stream is 'always closed' and missed the FTS_DP case; both fixed.

name: ref_ftw
prose: Precondition: path is a NUL-terminated string and fn is a callable function pointer; no precondition on nfds (values below 1 are handled). Postcondition: if nfds < 1 it sets errno = EINVAL and returns -1 without doing anything else. Otherwise it opens an fts handle (FTS_LOGICAL | FTS_COMFOLLOW | FTS_NOCHDIR) on path and returns -1 with errno from fts_open if that fails. It then loops over fts_read: post-order directory visits (FTS_DP) are skipped; other entries are mapped to FTW_D, FTW_DNR, FTW_F, FTW_NS or FTW_SL and fn(path, stat, flag) is called; if fn returns a non-zero value the loop stops and that exact value is the result; a directory cycle (FTS_DC) sets errno = ELOOP and any other unexpected fts_info stops the loop, both giving result -1. When fts_read returns NULL (end of walk, or an error that this function does not check) the loop ends with result 0. After the loop it saves errno, calls fts_close, and if fts_close fails while the result is still 0 the result becomes -1 and errno is left as fts_close set it; otherwise errno is restored to its saved value. It returns the result.
note: checked oracle.c:29-88. Reviewer round 15 is right (precondition nfds >= 1 contradicted the EINVAL return); round 2 right (fts_read error not distinguished from end); round 1 right (callback value returned verbatim).

name: ref__citrus_db_hash_std
prose: Precondition: r points to a valid struct _region whose head is readable for _region_size(r) bytes. Postcondition: returns a uint32_t hash computed over the region bytes: starting from 0, for each byte it shifts hash left by 4, adds the ASCII-lowercased byte (only 'A'..'Z' are changed), and if any of the top four bits (mask 0xF0000000) are set, clears them in hash and XORs hash with them shifted right by 24. The region is not modified.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref__citrus_db_hash_std (oracle.c:549-570). Old prose said 'folding the high nibble into the low bits' which is vague; now exact.

name: ref_mbrtoc32_l
prose: Precondition: pc may be NULL; s may be NULL; if s is not NULL it points to at least n readable bytes; ps is NULL (the locale's own state is used) or points to an mbstate_t used as a conversion state; locale is valid or NULL (FIX_LOCALE substitutes the default). Postcondition: if s is NULL, or the state is not initialised, the function opens the iconv converter from the locale's codeset to UTF-32-INTERNAL; if that fails it marks the state uninitialised, sets errno = EINVAL and returns (size_t)-1; otherwise it clears the buffered source and destination lengths and marks the state initialised, and if s is NULL it returns 0 without writing *pc. With s non-NULL: if a converted character is already pending in the state it is delivered, written to *pc when pc is non-NULL, and the function returns (size_t)-3 (or 0 if that character is NUL), consuming no input. Otherwise at most MB_LEN_MAX minus the already buffered bytes of s are appended to the state's source buffer and conversion is attempted. If a character is produced it is stored in *pc when pc is non-NULL, the buffered source length is reset to 0, and the function returns the number of bytes of this call's input used (at least 1), or 0 if the character is NUL. If the converter reports an invalid sequence it discards the buffered input, sets errno = EILSEQ and returns (size_t)-1. If the input is an incomplete sequence it keeps the unconverted remaining bytes (srcleft of them) in the state's buffer and returns (size_t)-2. *pc is not written on the s == NULL, -1 and -2 paths.
note: checked oracle.c:785-866. Reviewer rounds 1 and 2 (s == NULL path, EINVAL) were right about older wording; round 15 is right (the -2 path keeps the unconsumed bytes, not 'all consumed').

name: mock_mbrtowc
prose: Precondition: ps points to a _UTF8State holding the partial-character state (want, lbound, ch); pwc may be NULL; s may be NULL; otherwise s has at least n readable bytes. Postcondition: if us->want is outside 0..6 it sets errno = EINVAL and returns (size_t)-1 first of all. If s is NULL it behaves as if s were an empty string with n == 1 and pwc == NULL. If n == 0 it returns (size_t)-2 with no state change. With no pending partial character (want == 0): an ASCII byte is stored in *pwc when pwc is non-NULL and the function returns 1 (0 for NUL); a UTF-8 lead byte for 2 to 4 bytes starts decoding; any other lead byte sets errno = EILSEQ and returns (size_t)-1. When resuming (want != 0) it continues from the saved want, lbound and ch. A continuation byte that is not 10xxxxxx gives EILSEQ and (size_t)-1 with the state unchanged. If the input ends before the character is complete it saves the remaining count in us->want, lbound and ch and returns (size_t)-2 without writing *pwc. If complete but below lbound (overlong), a surrogate, or above U+10FFFF it sets EILSEQ and returns (size_t)-1. Otherwise it stores the value in *pwc when pwc is non-NULL, sets us->want = 0 and returns the number of bytes consumed by this call (when resuming, the bytes that were still needed), or 0 if the decoded value is 0.
note: checked oracle.c:244-326. Reviewer round 15 first point is right (EINVAL return contradicts a precondition that want is 0..6). Its second point ('bytes consumed' wrong when resuming) is WRONG: on resume want = us->want is the remaining count (line 291) and the loop consumes exactly that many bytes, so the return value is the bytes consumed by this call.

name: ref_chainsearch
prose: Precondition: table is a valid struct xlocale_collate with valid info; key points to a readable NUL-terminated wide string; len points to a writable int; when info->chain_count > 0, chain_pri_table points to chain_count entries ordered the way the binary search expects (by first wide character, then by string). Postcondition: if chain_count <= 0 it returns NULL. Otherwise it binary-searches indices 0..chain_count-1: at each probe it compares *key with the entry's first wide character and, if equal, compares wcsncmp(key, entry->str, wcsnlen(entry->str, COLLATE_STR_LEN)); if that comparison is zero it stores the entry string length in *len and returns the entry; otherwise it moves low or high by the sign of the comparison. If no probe matches it returns NULL and *len is not modified. Because it stops at the first probe that matches, which of several matching chains is returned (for example a shorter prefix chain versus a longer one) depends on table order and the probe path. No other memory is modified.
note: checked oracle.c:218-247 (head present, defined through #define chainsearch ref_chainsearch at line 183). Reviewer rounds 1 and 2 are right that the result depends on the table's sort order and that a prefix chain can be missed; stated.

name: ref_findmust
prose: Precondition: p and g are valid; g->strip is an SOP program ending in OEND; g->must is NULL and g->mlen is 0 from setup. Postcondition: returns nothing. If p->error != 0 it returns at once without touching g. If MB_CUR_MAX > 1 and the current locale encoding is not UTF-8 it also returns without touching g. Otherwise it sets g->moffset = 0 and scans the program for the longest run of OCHAR operators (counting bytes of their multibyte encoding, first-found wins on ties), tracking an offset; if skipping an OQUEST_/OCH_ group finds an operator that is not O_QUEST, O_CH or OOR2 it sets BAD in g->iflags and returns (g->mlen and g->moffset may already have been updated). After the scan, if g->mlen == 0 it sets g->moffset = -1 and returns. Otherwise it mallocs g->mlen + 1 bytes; if malloc fails it sets g->must = NULL (the malloc result), g->mlen = 0, g->moffset = -1 and returns. Otherwise g->must holds the NUL-terminated byte string of the longest run and g->mlen its length, and g->moffset is the computed offset (which can be -1 when it could not be determined).
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_findmust (oracle.c:1847-2015). Reviewer round 15 is right: line 1997-2001 assigns g->must from malloc, so it becomes NULL on failure, not 'unchanged'. Note g->moffset is set to 0 at line 1876 right after the two early returns.

name: float32_lt
prose: Precondition: a and b are 32-bit patterns read as IEEE single-precision values. Postcondition: static function. If either operand is a NaN (exponent field 0xFF and non-zero fraction, quiet or signalling), it calls float_raise(float_flag_invalid), which ORs 16 into the global ref_float_exception_flags, and returns 0. Otherwise it returns 1 exactly when a < b as IEEE values: if the signs differ it returns 1 when a is negative and not both operands are zero (so -0 and +0 give 0), else 0; if the signs match it returns 1 when a != b and (for positive operands) a < b as bit patterns or (for negative operands) a > b as bit patterns. The only memory it modifies is ref_float_exception_flags (and only in the NaN case).
note: checked oracle.c:55-71. Contract emptied: it touched a global (exception flags), and reviewer round 15 is right that the old contract omitted that side effect.

name: ref_float32_lt
prose: Precondition: a and b are 32-bit patterns read as IEEE single-precision values. Postcondition: returns float32_lt(a, b) unchanged: 1 exactly when neither operand is a NaN and a < b (so -0 and +0 give 0), and 0 otherwise. When either operand is a NaN, float32_lt ORs float_flag_invalid (16) into the global ref_float_exception_flags before returning 0; that is the only memory touched.
note: checked oracle.c:73-78. Contract emptied (global side effect); reviewer round 15 right.

name: ref___ltsf2
prose: Precondition: a and b are 32-bit patterns read as IEEE single-precision values. Postcondition: returns -float32_lt(a, b): -1 exactly when neither operand is a NaN and a < b, and 0 otherwise (including when either operand is a NaN and when a == b or a > b). When either operand is a NaN, float32_lt ORs float_flag_invalid into the global ref_float_exception_flags; that is the only memory touched.
note: checked oracle.c:92-98. Reviewer round 1 (prose reverses return values) was about older wording; current text matches the code. Contract emptied (global side effect).

name: rand_f64
prose: Precondition: prng_state holds any uint64_t value (normally set by prng_seed). Postcondition: draws r = prng_next() and switches on r & 7. Cases 0, 1 and 2 return one further prng_next() value. Case 3 returns sign (bit 8 of r) | 0x7FF0000000000000 | frac, where frac is the low 52 bits of a further draw, reduced with frac &= 0xF (all bits above the low nibble cleared) when (r >> 9) & 3 == 0; this is an infinity or a NaN. Case 4 returns sign | frac with exponent zero, frac being the low 52 bits of a further draw, set to 0 when (r >> 9) & 3 == 0 and masked to its low 8 bits when it equals 1; this is a signed zero or subnormal. Case 5 draws q to pick one of the 11 exponents {0, 1, 2, 0x3FD, 0x3FE, 0x3FF, 0x400, 0x401, 0x7FD, 0x7FE, 0x7FF} (q mod 11) and a further draw for a 52-bit fraction, and returns sign | exponent | fraction. Case 6 draws q and returns the value whose eight bytes are 0x80 | (corresponding byte of q & 0x7F). Case 7 draws q and returns sign | (0x3FF + q % 5 - 2) << 52 with zero fraction. prng_state is advanced by two prng_next calls in every case except case 5, where it advances by three.
note: checked harness.cpp:90-140. Reviewer round 15 is right: frac &= 0xF keeps only the low nibble, the old prose said the opposite. Reviewer round 2 (one further draw in most branches) is consistent with the old 'two calls total'.

name: ref_float32_to_float64
prose: Precondition: none; a is any 32-bit single-precision bit pattern. Postcondition: for an infinity it returns the double infinity with the same sign; for a NaN it returns ref_commonNaNToFloat64(ref_float32ToCommonNaN(a)), a quiet double NaN (0x7FF8... bit set) with a's sign and payload, and raises float_flag_invalid if a is a signalling NaN; for zero it returns a zero of the same sign; for a subnormal it normalises and returns the exactly equal double; for a normal number it returns the exactly equal double (exponent rebiased by 0x380, fraction shifted). No rounding occurs and no flag is raised except invalid for a signalling NaN.
note: checked oracle.c:1732-1753, ref_float32ToCommonNaN (987-997) and ref_commonNaNToFloat64 (1107-1115). Reviewer round 15 right: the common-NaN path raises invalid for a signalling NaN, so 'no flags' was wrong. 'Quiet' is correct because 0x7FF8000000000000 is OR-ed in.

name: ref_addFloat32Sigs
prose: Precondition: a and b are 32-bit single-precision patterns and zSign is 0 or 1; it adds the absolute values, so it is meant to be called with zSign equal to the sign of the intended result. Postcondition: let aExp, bExp be the exponent fields. If aExp > bExp: if aExp is 0xFF it returns ref_propagateFloat32NaN(a, b) when a is a NaN, otherwise a unchanged (its own sign, not zSign). If aExp < bExp: if bExp is 0xFF it returns ref_propagateFloat32NaN(a, b) when b is a NaN, otherwise an infinity with sign zSign. If the exponents are equal: if aExp is 0xFF it returns the NaN from ref_propagateFloat32NaN when either fraction is non-zero, otherwise a unchanged (this includes both operands being infinite); if aExp is 0 it returns the exact sum of the two subnormal fractions packed with sign zSign and exponent field 0 (so a zero result carries sign zSign); otherwise it rounds the sum. In the remaining cases it aligns the smaller operand (shifting with jamming), adds the significands and returns ref_roundAndPackFloat32(zSign, zExp, zSig), i.e. |a| + |b| rounded under the global float_rounding_mode with sign zSign. The called helpers may set bits in the global exception flags.
note: checked oracle.c:1828-1889. Reviewer round 15 is right: when both operands are infinite the result is a, not an infinity with sign zSign; the old prose listed the b-infinite case without excluding a being infinite.

name: ref_float64_to_int32_round_to_zero
prose: Precondition: none; a is any 64-bit double bit pattern. Postcondition: with shiftCount = aExp - 0x413: if |a| < 1 it returns 0, setting float_flag_inexact when a is non-zero (zero gives 0 with no flag). If aExp > 0x41E (|a| >= 2^32, an infinity or a NaN) it raises invalid and returns 0x7FFFFFFF for a NaN or positive a and INT32_MIN for negative a. Otherwise it computes the truncated magnitude absZ (as an unsigned 32-bit value) and z = -absZ for negative a, absZ for positive a; if the sign of z disagrees with the sign of a and z is non-zero it raises invalid and returns 0x7FFFFFFF for positive a, INT32_MIN for negative a. This also covers 2^31 <= a < 2^32. A negative a whose truncated magnitude is exactly 2^31 (that is, -2^31 - 1 < a <= -2^31) returns INT32_MIN without raising invalid (inexact is raised if a has a fractional part). In the non-invalid cases it returns z and sets float_flag_inexact if any discarded bits were non-zero. Invalid is raised through ref_float_raise; the inexact bit is ORed into float_exception_flags.
note: checked oracle.c:2521-2561. Reviewer round 2 and 15 both right: values in (-2^31-1, -2^31] truncate to -2^31 with no invalid.

name: ref___printf_render_float
prose: Precondition: io is a valid output stream, pi describes a floating conversion (spec one of a, A, e, E, f, F, g, G; any other spec reaches an assert(pi->spec == 'f')), and arg[0] points to a double, or to a long double when pi->is_long_double is set. Postcondition: it converts the value with __hdtoa/__hldtoa (a, A) or dtoa/__ldtoa (other specs), builds sign, optional 0x prefix, digits, decimal point, locale grouping separators (the grouping table is consulted only when pi->alt is set) and exponent, and writes them to io with padding (blank, zero or left-adjusted according to pi->pad, pi->left and pi->width) through __printf_pad and __printf_puts. Infinity and NaN are printed as 'inf'/'INF' or 'nan'/'NAN' (lower case when spec >= 'a'), with no sign for NaN. After output it calls __printf_flush(io), frees the dtoa buffer with freedtoa if one was allocated, and returns ret, the sum of the values returned by the __printf_pad and __printf_puts calls. It has a single return (line 421).

name: test_recvmsg
prose: Precondition: none; a static void function without parameters that uses its own stack buffers and the helpers case_recvmsg and rng_*. Postcondition: sets up a zeroed msghdr pointing at its name, control and iov buffers; calls case_recvmsg with a NULL msghdr for every combination of 10 socket values, 9 flag values and 9 return values; calls case_recvmsg for each of the 10 socket values with a zero-length msghdr (namelen, iovlen, controllen all 0), flags 0 and ret 0; runs a loop that steps an unsigned char b by 0x3f (8-bit wraparound) from 0 until it reaches 0xff (65 iterations), each time with msg_namelen = 1, msg_iovlen = 1 and one 1-byte iov, passing b as the flags and (int8_t)b as the return value; runs a loop with cnt from 0 to IOV_MAX_TEST + 2, filling the first min(cnt, IOV_MAX_TEST) iovs, with namelen 4, iovlen cnt, controllen MSG_CTRL_CAP, socket 7, flags cnt and ret cnt; and finally seeds the generator with 0x7263766d and runs 200000 random cases with random sizes for name, control and iov data. It returns void and leaves nothing allocated.
note: checked harness.cpp:755-844. Reviewer round 15 is right: the byte sweep is over flags/return value with namelen and iovlen fixed at 1; the namelen and iovlen sweeps are in the cnt loop and the random loop. The 65-iteration count is from a quick simulation of the unsigned-char loop.

name: ref__Tthr_kill
prose: Precondition: pthread is a thread handle, sig a signal number; _get_curthread, _thr_find_thread, _thr_send_sig and THR_THREAD_UNLOCK are test doubles in this oracle (a real implementation would lock the target in _thr_find_thread). Postcondition: if sig < 0 or sig > _SIG_MAXSIG it returns EINVAL and does nothing else. Otherwise it takes curthread = _get_curthread(). If curthread == pthread it calls _thr_send_sig(pthread, sig) only when sig > 0 and returns 0. Otherwise it calls _thr_find_thread(curthread, pthread, 0); if that returns 0 it calls _thr_send_sig only when sig > 0 and then THR_THREAD_UNLOCK(curthread, pthread), and returns 0; if it returns a non-zero value it returns that value with no signal sent and no unlock call.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref__Tthr_kill (oracle.c:497-527), not pthread_kill. The old prose omitted the EINVAL return for an out-of-range signal (lines 503-505).

name: cexpl
prose: Precondition: z is any long double complex value passed by value. Postcondition: with x = creall(z) and y = cimagl(z), the first matching case applies, in this order: (1) y == 0: returns (expl(x), y). (2) x == 0 (and y != 0): returns (cos y, sin y) from sincosl, for any y including infinities and NaN. (3) y not finite (and x != 0): if x is finite or NaN returns (y - y, y - y), a NaN pair; if x is negative infinity returns (0.0, 0.0); otherwise (x positive infinity) returns (x, y - y). (4) y finite and x != 0: if exp_ovfl < x < cexp_ovfl returns __ldexp_cexpl(z, 0); otherwise (x <= exp_ovfl, x >= cexp_ovfl, or x NaN) returns (expl(x) * cos y, expl(x) * sin y), the cases covering ordinary x, large x and x = +-Inf; a NaN x gives NaN parts. No locks or memory are involved; floating-point exceptions may be raised by the calls.
note: slice cut the head: real function is cexpl (oracle.c:1018-1066). Reviewer round 15 is right: for x == 0 with non-finite y the code returns sincosl(y) (line 1030-1032), not NaN,NaN, because the x == 0 test precedes the isfinite(y) test.

name: tanpil
prose: Precondition: none; x is any long double. Postcondition: with ax = |x|: if ax < 1: for ax < 2^-60 it returns x when x == 0 (signed zero preserved) and otherwise an approximation of pi*x computed with the pi_hi/pi_lo split and rescaled by 2^-113; for 2^-60 <= ax < 0.5 it uses t = __kernel_tanpil(ax); for ax == 0.5 it uses t = 1/vzero (positive infinity); for 0.5 < ax < 1 it uses t = -__kernel_tanpil(1 - ax); in these three cases it returns -t if x < 0 and t otherwise. If 1 <= ax < 2^112 it splits ax into integer part ai and fraction ar with FFLOORL128, sets odd = +1 when ai is even and -1 when odd, and uses t = copysign(0, odd) when ar == 0 (zero whose sign depends on the parity of ai), __kernel_tanpil(ar) for 0 < ar < 0.5, odd/vzero (an infinity whose sign depends on the parity) for ar == 0.5, and -__kernel_tanpil(1 - ar) for ar > 0.5; it returns -t if x < 0 and t otherwise. If x is an infinity or NaN it returns vzero/vzero (NaN). For finite ax >= 2^112 it returns zero with the sign of x (copysignl of t, x). It has no side effects other than floating-point exceptions.
note: slice cut the head: real function is tanpil (oracle.c:231-283). Reviewer round 15 is right: the sign of the zero for integer ax in [1, 2^112) depends on the parity of the integer part, not only on the sign of x. For ax >= 2^112 the result takes the sign of x (line 282), so parity does not matter there.

name: ref_powl
prose: Precondition: x and y are long double values. Postcondition: this slice holds only the tail of ref_powl (x raised to y). The function returns, in order of checks: 1 if y is zero; 1 if x == 1 or if x == -1 and y is infinite; the NaN from nan_mix(x, y) if either operand is a NaN; for y = +-infinity, y - y (NaN) for |x| == 1, y or 0 for |x| > 1 and -y or 0 for |x| < 1; 1/x if y is -1 and x if y is +1, x*x for y == 2, sqrtl(x) for y == 0.5 and x >= +0; for x equal to +-0, +-infinity or +-1 it returns |x| (or 1/|x| when y < 0) with its sign negated when x < 0 and y is an odd integer, or NaN when x is -1 and y is not an integer; NaN for x < 0 and y not an integer; overflow (huge*huge) or underflow (tiny*tiny) for very large |y| unless x is close to 1. Otherwise (the part in the slice) it computes log2|x| in extended precision, forms z = y*log2|x|, and returns s*huge*huge (overflow) when z > 16384 (or z == 16384 and p_l + ovt > z - p_h), s*tiny*tiny (underflow) when z < -16495 (or z == -16495 and p_l <= z - p_h), and otherwise s*2^z computed by reducing z (n = nearest integer, polynomial for 2^(z-n), exponent adjusted by n, via scalbnl when the result is subnormal), where s is -1 when x < 0 and y is an odd integer and +1 otherwise.
note: slice cut the head and the name was wrong: the listed 'expl' is the tail of ref_powl (oracle.c:288-583); the slice also contains the start of the exp2l section (line 606+) but no expl. Reviewer round 15 is right (s is not the sign of x, thresholds are about z = y*log2|x| rather than exact).

name: ref___kernel_cosl
prose: Precondition: x and y are long double values (the kernel argument and its tail). Postcondition: returns a long double computed as z = x*x, r = z*(C1 + z*(C2 + z*(C3 + z*(C4 + z*(C5 + z*(C6 + z*C7)))))), hz = 0.5*z, w = 1 - hz, and w + (((1 - w) - hz) + (z*r - x*y)). On amd64 and i386 C1 is built as (long double)C1hi + C1lo from two doubles. It reads constants and modifies no memory.
note: slice cut the head: the function is ref___kernel_cosl on long double arguments (oracle.c:247-257), not a double __kernel_cos; the old prose described double arguments and a polynomial without the outer z factor. I kept the statement to the arithmetic in the body and made no accuracy claim.

Postcondition: runs the edge, walk, bit-pattern and random (210000 iterations) check_* cases, which update the stats of scalbnf, fabsf, copysign and gammaf; prints a header, one row per stat (name, cases, failures) and a TOTAL row; sets a failure flag if any of the four stats has zero cases (printing '<name>: no cases were run') or a non-zero failure count; prints 'FAIL' or 'PASS' and returns 1 if the flag is set and 0 otherwise.

name: __kernel_rem_pio2
prose: Precondition: x points to nx doubles holding successive 24-bit integer pieces of a positive value whose scaled exponent is e0 (e0 <= 16360); prec is 0 (single), 1 (double), 2 (extended) or 3 (quad); y has room for 1 element when prec == 0, 2 when prec is 1 or 2, and 3 when prec == 3; nx and the derived jk keep the 20-element local arrays in range. Postcondition: reduces the value modulo pi/2 using the table ipio2 and writes the reduced argument to y: y[0] for prec 0; y[0] and y[1] for prec 1 or 2; y[0], y[1] and y[2] for prec 3, each negated when the internal flag ih is non-zero. It returns n & 7, the low three bits of the quotient (octant). It may recompute with more terms of ipio2 until the result is non-zero, and it modifies no memory other than y and its locals.
note: slice cut the head: real function is __kernel_rem_pio2 (oracle.c:431-580). Reviewer round 15 is right: y is not filled for 0..prec, only 1, 2 or 3 elements are written (lines 549, 556-559, 574-577). Old prose said prec+1 elements; that is wrong for prec 2 and 3.

name: ref_acosh
prose: Precondition: none; any double x. Postcondition: using the high word hx of x: if hx < 0x3ff00000 (x below 1, which includes every negative value, -0, -infinity and negative NaNs because hx is signed) it returns (x - x)/(x - x), a NaN. If hx >= 0x41b00000 (|x| >= 2^28): for hx >= 0x7ff00000 (+infinity or positive NaN) it returns x + x, otherwise log(x) + ln2. Else if x == 1.0 exactly it returns 0.0. Else if hx > 0x40000000 (x of about 2 or above, up to 2^28) it returns log(2x - 1/(x + sqrt(x*x - 1))). Otherwise (1 < x with high word at most 0x40000000, which includes x just above 2 up to the next high-word step) it sets t = x - 1 and returns log1p(t + sqrt(2t + t*t)). No state is modified.
note: checked oracle.c:38-60. Reviewer round 2 right (negative NaN takes the x<1 branch); round 15 right (the log1p formula is used until the high word exceeds 0x40000000, i.e. slightly beyond x = 2); round 1 right about the huge branch.

name: ref_erfc
prose: Precondition: none; x is any double. Postcondition: with hx the high word of x and ix = |hx|: if ix >= 0x7ff00000 it returns (double)((hx >> 31) << 1) + 1/x, i.e. NaN for a NaN, 0 for +infinity and 2 for -infinity. If |x| < 0.84375: for |x| < 2^-56 it returns 1 - x; otherwise it computes y = r/s and returns 1 - (x + x*y) when hx < 0x3fd00000 (every negative x and x < 1/4) and half - (x*y + (x - half)) otherwise. If 0.84375 <= |x| < 1.25 it returns (1 - erx) - P/Q for x >= 0 and 1 + (erx + P/Q) for x < 0. If 1.25 <= |x| < 28: for x <= -6 (ix >= 0x40180000 with the sign set, including x = -6 exactly) it returns two - tiny (reached only when |x| >= 1/0.35); otherwise it forms r from the exp products and returns r/x for x > 0 and two - r/x for x < 0 (so x between -6 exclusive and -1.25). If |x| >= 28 it returns tiny*tiny for x > 0 and two - tiny otherwise. No memory is modified.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_erfc (oracle.c:246-301). Reviewer round 15 is right: for x = -6 the code returns two - tiny (lines 289-290), so the old 'x >= -6' range was wrong. Also added the NaN/inf case at lines 252-255.

name: ref_writelabel
prose: Precondition: the globals lab, bootarea, specname, bbsize, labeloffset, labelsoffset, lba_offset, disable_write, installboot and is_file are set up; if installboot is set, ref_readboot must be able to open and read the boot file (it exits the process through err or errx on open, read or size failure). Postcondition: if disable_write is non-zero it warns, displays the label with ref_display(stdout, NULL) (which uses lab) and returns 0 without changing lab or writing the disk. Otherwise it sets lab.d_magic and d_magic2 to DISKMAGIC, sets d_checksum to 0 and then to dkcksum(lab), calls ref_readboot if installboot is set, adds lba_offset to p_offset of every partition among the first d_npartitions whose p_size is non-zero (modifying lab in place; partitions with zero size are untouched), encodes lab into bootarea at labeloffset + labelsoffset * lab.d_secsize, and opens specname O_RDWR. If the open fails: for is_file it warns and returns 1; otherwise it saves errno, calls ref_geom_class_available("PART") (which can exit via errc(1) if the GEOM tree cannot be read) and returns 1 after warning (with a hint to use gpart(8) if the PART class exists). If the open succeeds it writes bbsize bytes of bootarea; a short or failed write warns, closes the descriptor and returns 1; otherwise it closes the descriptor and returns 0. The descriptor is closed on every path where it was opened.
note: checked oracle.c:370-424. Reviewer round 15 is right: line 388-389 adds lba_offset only to partitions with non-zero p_size, not to every non-zero p_offset. Note d_checksum is computed before the offsets are adjusted.

name: ref_readlabel
prose: Precondition: specname, is_file, bootarea, labeloffset, labelsoffset and the label globals are set up; flag says whether a missing label is fatal. Postcondition: opens specname O_RDONLY (err(1) on failure). If is_file it calls ref_get_file_parms (fstat failure err(4); not a regular file or link errx(4); sets secsize = DEV_BSIZE and mediasize = file size); otherwise it sets mediasize and secsize from g_mediasize and g_sectorsize and calls err(4) if either is negative. It calls errx(1) if mediasize exceeds 0xffffffff * secsize. It seeks to 0 and reads BBSIZE bytes into bootarea (err(4) if the read returns -1, errx(4) if fewer than BBSIZE bytes) and closes the descriptor. It decodes the label from bootarea + labeloffset + labelsoffset * secsize into lab with bsd_disklabel_le_dec, storing the status in error; if flag is non-zero and error is non-zero it calls errx(1). If is_file it returns 0 (even when decoding failed and flag was zero). Otherwise it sets lba to the minimum p_offset over the first d_npartitions partitions whose p_size is non-zero (starting from ~0); if lba != 0 and the RAW_PART offset equals lba, it subtracts lba from p_offset of every partition with non-zero p_size and stores lba in lba_offset; it then returns error (0 for a valid label, non-zero otherwise). The descriptor is closed on all paths that return.
note: checked oracle.c:445-504. Reviewer round 15 is right: the subtraction at 493-496 is guarded by p_size, not applied to every non-zero offset.

name: ref_zone
prose: Precondition: this is the full ref_zone(device, argc, argv, combinedopt, task_attr, retry_count, timeout, verbosemode); device is a valid CAM device and argv/combinedopt are usable by getopt. Postcondition: allocates a CCB (error 1 with a warning if that fails) and parses the options: -a, -c (command name looked up in zone_cmd_map, case-insensitive; ambiguous or unknown gives error 1), -l (strtoull of the whole argument, else error 1), -N, -o (report option lookup) and -P (print flags lookup); other options are ignored. Without -c it returns 1. It calls get_device_type and calls errx(1) if that fails. For the report-zones action it allocates a 64 KiB buffer (err(1) if that fails) and builds a SCSI ZBC IN command or an ATA ZAC/NCQ receive command by device type (build_ata_cmd failure returns its non-zero value after a warning; an unknown device type gives 1); for other actions it builds a ZBC OUT or ATA command similarly. It then sets CAM_DEV_QFRZDIS (and CAM_PASS_ERR_RECOVER when retry_count > 0), sends the CCB (failure: warning and result -1) and checks the CCB status (not CAM_REQ_CMP: error print and result 1). For non-report actions it then returns 0. For report zones it computes the valid length, calls ref_zone_rz_print, and if that returns ZONE_PRINT_MORE_DATA it clears the CCB and cdb_storage and repeats the request from the buffer reset, otherwise a ZONE_PRINT_ERROR result gives 1. On every path that reaches the common exit it frees the CCB (if allocated), the data buffer and cdb_storage and returns the result: 0, 1, -1 or the non-zero value from build_ata_cmd.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_zone (oracle.c:319-671); the slice is only the second half. Checked every goto bailout and the restart_report loop.

name: ref_Transform
prose: Precondition: buf points to four UINT4 words and in points to sixteen UINT4 words, not overlapping; both are readable and buf is writable. Postcondition: static void. It copies buf[0..3] into a, b, c, d, runs the 64 MD5 steps (four rounds of 16 FF, GG, HH or II steps, each reading one word of in and adding a constant), then adds a, b, c, d to buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], buf[3] respectively using UINT4 arithmetic. in is only read, not written. There is no return value and no other side effect.

name: ref_nametokva
prose: Precondition: name is a string; iocfunc is a callable ioctl function pointer; opts is the global option word. Postcondition: strncpy copies at most sizeof(res.ipfu_name) bytes of name into the request (the destination is not NUL-terminated if name is at least that long) and the result address starts as NULL. If OPT_DONTOPEN is not set in opts it opens IPL_NAME O_RDONLY and returns NULL if that fails. It then calls (*iocfunc)(fd, SIOCFUNCL, &res), ignoring the return value, with fd = -1 when OPT_DONTOPEN is set, closes fd if it is non-negative, and returns res.ipfu_addr, replacing a NULL address with (ipfunc_t)-1. Any descriptor it opened has been closed before it returns.

name: ref_main
prose: Precondition: argc and argv come from the C runtime; getprogname() decides the personality (a name containing 'halt' sets dohalt, 'nextboot' sets donextboot). Postcondition: it calls ref_usage (which exits 1) for an unknown option or leftover arguments; errx(1) when the no-shutdown file exists (unless -f or nextboot), for conflicting options, and for -r with other options; for -D it exits 0 if the nextboot file does not exist, otherwise unlinks it (warning on failure) and exits 0. A non-nextboot caller with a non-root euid gets err(1) with EPERM. With -q it calls reboot(howto) and, if that returns, err(1). With -k and no -f it checks that /boot/<kernel>/kernel exists and is a regular file (err or errx(1) otherwise). If any environment was collected it calls ref_write_nextboot; the nextboot personality then exits 0. Otherwise it logs the action (unless -l), records a shutdown utmpx entry, syncs (unless -n), ignores several signals and: for -r it sends SIGEMT to init, calling err(1) if kill fails and otherwise returning 0 from the function (the only return statement, line 448); in the normal case it sends SIGTSTP to init (err(1) on failure), SIGTERM to all processes (err(1) unless ESRCH), waits and syncs, sends SIGKILL repeatedly (jumping to restart on a kill error other than ESRCH, warning if processes remain after 5 rounds), and calls reboot(howto). If reboot(2) returns, or a kill error sent control to restart, it sends SIGHUP to init and calls errx(1) with the saved errno text (prefixed '(can't restart init): ' if the SIGHUP also failed). So the function never returns except the reroot case returning 0, and otherwise ends in an exit call.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_main (oracle.c:240-502). Old prose said it never returns and lists exit 0 after a successful reboot(2); the reroot branch returns 0 at line 448 and reboot(2) does not return on success.

name: ref_main
prose: Precondition: argc and argv as passed to main. Postcondition: if argc < 2 it returns ref_veriexec_usage() (prints usage, returns 0). It opens _PATH_DEV_VERIEXEC write-only into dev_fd and parses options with getopt: -h returns ref_veriexec_usage() (0); -C stores the directory; -i queries the state (err(EX_UNAVAILABLE) if the device is not open or the ioctl fails; errx(EX_USAGE) for an unknown state name) and exits with (x & state) == 0; -l (when HAVE_VERIEXEC_GET_PATH_LABEL is defined) prints labels and exits EX_OK; -S enables strict validity checking; -v increments Verbose; -x checks paths and exits 0 or 2; -z modifies the state: 'debug' (a prefix match) needs a following level 'off' or an integer 0..INT_MAX (errx(EX_USAGE) otherwise), other names are mapped by ref_veriexec_state_modify; it then needs an open device (err(EX_UNAVAILABLE)), issues the ioctl (err(EX_UNAVAILABLE) on failure), prints the debug level or the state in octal, and exits EX_OK; any other option calls ref_veriexec_usage and exit(EX_USAGE). After the options it prints the verbosity if set, exits with err(EX_UNAVAILABLE) if the device is not open, opens the log, errx(EX_OSFILE) if ve_trust_init() < 1, optionally reads the veriexec version, loads each remaining manifest argument with ref_veriexec_load (err(EX_DATAERR) if one fails) and finally calls exit(EX_OK). It returns only in the two usage cases (value 0); all other paths end in exit, err or errx.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add)
prose: Generated function arch_atomic_add(int i, atomic_t *v), produced by ATOMIC_OP(add, addl) inside ATOMIC_OPS(add) (atomic.h:38-52, 156-166). Precondition: v points to a valid atomic_t. Postcondition: it runs a load-locked/store-conditional loop: ldl_l temp from v->counter, addl temp, i, temp, stl_c temp back, and branches back to retry if the store-conditional failed; on exit v->counter is its previous value plus i (32-bit add) with no concurrent update to the counter lost. It returns nothing and the asm has no memory clobber or barrier (it is a relaxed operation). The same ATOMIC_OPS(add) invocation also generates arch_atomic_add_return_relaxed, arch_atomic_fetch_add_relaxed and the arch_atomic64_ add variants, which are separate functions.
note: checked atomic.h:37-52 and 156-165. Reviewer round 15 only notes that the invocation also generates other functions; they are separate items, so the prose for arch_atomic_add itself stays.

name: ffs
prose: Precondition: none; word is any int. Postcondition: static inline function with attribute const. Returns 0 when word is 0; otherwise it returns __ffs(word) + 1, i.e. 1 plus the index of the least significant set bit of word, a value from 1 to 32 (the int is sign-extended to unsigned long, which does not change the lowest set bit). The function has no side effects.
note: checked bitops.h:376-380. The old formal contract was rejected by random testing (false for word = 65536); contract left empty because the result depends on __ffs (cmpbge/ctz) architecture intrinsics.

name: io7_init_hose
prose: Precondition: io7 points to a valid struct io7 and port is a valid port index of it; runs at init time (__init). Postcondition: returns nothing. It allocates a pci_controller with alloc_pci_controller (memblock_alloc_or_panic, no NULL check), sets hose->index to the next value of a static counter and, for index 0, sets pci_isa_hose; stores the io7_port csrs and hose pointers and hose->sysdata; allocates io_space and mem_space resources with alloc_resource and fills in the bases, config space base and the IO and MEM resource ranges, names and flags; requests ioport_resource for the IO range and iomem_resource for the MEM range, printing a KERN_ERR message and continuing if either request fails; saves the four POx_WBASE, POx_WMASK and POx_TBASE values into io7_port->saved_wbase, saved_wmask and saved_tbase; calls marvel_pci_tbi(hose, 0, -1); creates the ISA scatter-gather arena (8 MB at 8 MB) into hose->sg_isa and the PCI arena (up to 1 GB at 3 GB) into hose->sg_pci with iommu_arena_new_node, dereferencing both without a NULL check and setting align_entry = 8; programs window 0 as scatter-gather, window 1 as direct-mapped (__direct_map_base, __direct_map_size, TBASE 0) and window 2 as scatter-gather, disables window 3 (WBASE[3] = 0), clears bit 61 of POx_CTRL, prints 'FIXME: disabling master aborts' and clears bits 14-15 of POx_MSK_HEI, and calls marvel_pci_tbi(hose, 0, -1) again. The hose and resources are owned by the kernel and never freed here.

name: titan_agp_info
prose: Precondition: none beyond kernel init state; no parameters. Postcondition: searches for an AGP port: pachip0's a_port gives hosenum 2 if titan_query_agp reports AGP present; otherwise, if pchip1 is present and its a_port reports AGP, hosenum is 3. It then looks for the hose with that index in the hose list and returns NULL (allocating nothing) if there is none (this includes hosenum -1, no AGP port) or the hose has no sg_pci arena. It then kmallocs an alpha_agp_info (GFP_KERNEL) and returns NULL if that fails. Otherwise it fills hose, private = the AGP port, ops = &titan_agp_ops, aperture bus_base 0, size 0 and sysdata NULL, capability lw 0 with rate 3, sba 1 and rq 7, and mode lw 0 with rate = 1 << apctl_v_agp_rate, sba = apctl_v_agp_sba_en, rq 7 and enable = apctl_v_agp_en read from the port's pctl.csr, and returns it; the caller owns the allocation.
