prose: Generated function __do_sys_pciconfig_iobase(which, bus, dfn). Precondition: when IOBASE_FROM_HOSE is clear and bus and dfn are both 0, pci_isa_hose must be non-NULL; for a found device dev->sysdata must be non-NULL; for IOBASE_ROOT_BUS the chosen hose's bus pointer must be non-NULL. Postcondition: if (which & IOBASE_FROM_HOSE) the hose is the first in hose_head whose index equals bus, else -ENODEV if none; otherwise, if bus == 0 and dfn == 0 the hose is pci_isa_hose, else dev = pci_get_domain_bus_and_slot(0, bus, dfn) (-ENODEV if NULL), the hose is dev->sysdata and the device reference is released with pci_dev_put before the switch. Then by (which & ~IOBASE_FROM_HOSE) it returns hose->index (IOBASE_HOSE), sparse_mem_base, dense_mem_base, sparse_io_base, dense_io_base, or hose->bus->number (IOBASE_ROOT_BUS), and -EOPNOTSUPP for any other selector. No reference is held on return.

name: common_shutdown_1
prose: Precondition: generic_ptr points to a struct halt_info (mode and restart_cmd, which may be NULL); the function is the on_each_cpu callback and runs on every CPU. It makes no assumption about whether interrupts are enabled on entry. Postcondition: it calls local_irq_disable() and never re-enables interrupts. It locates this CPU's per-cpu HWRPB flags and clears 0x00ff0001. With CONFIG_SMP on a CPU other than boot_cpuid it sets the 'remain halted' flag (0x40000), stores the flags, clears this CPU from the present and possible masks and calls halt() (no return). On the boot CPU, if mode == LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_RESTART it sets the cold bootstrap flag (0x20000) when restart_cmd is NULL and the warm bootstrap flag (0x30000) otherwise; for any other mode it sets 'remain halted'; it stores the flags. With CONFIG_SMP it clears the boot CPU from the present and possible masks and spins until the present mask is empty. If alpha_using_srm: with CONFIG_DUMMY_CONSOLE it calls irq_exit() if in a hard IRQ, takes the console lock, takes over the console with dummy_con and unlocks; then it calls pci_restore_srm_config() and set_hae(srm_hae). It then calls alpha_mv.kill_arch(mode) if set. If !alpha_using_srm and mode != LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_RESTART it returns (with local interrupts still disabled). Otherwise it calls srm_paging_stop() when alpha_using_srm and then halt().
note: checked process.c:75-163. Reviewer round 15 is right: on_each_cpu runs callbacks with interrupts disabled, so the old 'interrupts enabled' precondition was wrong. Older reviewers (non-SRM non-restart path returns; no loop) are right and the prose says it returns.

Postcondition: it takes the atomic ops lock with atomic_ops_lock(flags) (irq disabling on UP, a spinlock on SMP), executes v->counter -= i, releases the lock with atomic_ops_unlock(flags), and returns nothing; the update is not seen half-done by other users of the same lock. The int subtraction has no overflow check in the function body. The same invocation also generates arch_atomic_sub_return and arch_atomic_fetch_sub, which are separate functions.

name: raw_copy_from_user
prose: Precondition: to is a kernel buffer of at least n writable bytes; from is a user address that may fault; n may be 0. Postcondition: returns 0 immediately if n == 0. Faulting loads are recovered through the exception table (.fixup jumps past the failing chunk). Three paths. (1) If CONFIG_ARC_USE_UNALIGNED_MEM_ACCESS is off and either pointer is not 4-byte aligned, it copies byte by byte with a hardware loop, decrementing n after each completed byte; on a faulting load the loop is left and the function returns n, the exact number of bytes not copied. (2) If n is a compile-time constant it copies in ladder blocks of 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1 bytes; each block loads its words first and then stores them, and its counter res (initially n) is decremented only when the whole block has been stored. A fault inside a block abandons that block only (the loaded words are not stored, while `from` may already have advanced past them), and the later smaller blocks are still attempted, so after a fault the copy is not necessarily a clean prefix and the data of later blocks can come from shifted source addresses. (3) If n is not a constant a single asm sequence copies the 16-byte chunks, then the remaining 8, 4, 2 and 1 bytes; a fault jumps to the end and abandons everything after the failing chunk, so only whole completed chunks are copied. In paths (2) and (3) the function returns res: n minus the sizes of the completed blocks, which is 0 when every block completed.
note: checked uaccess.h:138-336. Reviewer round 2 is right (in the constant-n path later blocks still run after a fault, with from advanced past the loaded-but-unstored words); round 15 (return overcounts) is not right: loads precede stores inside each block, so res counts every unstored byte of the failing block; the real hazard is that later blocks can still run.

name: raw_copy_to_user
prose: Precondition: to is a user address that may fault, from a kernel buffer of at least n readable bytes, n may be 0. Postcondition: returns 0 immediately if n == 0. The exception-table entries are on the stores to user memory (labels 1, 11, 12, 13, 14-18), so faulting stores are recovered by a .fixup that jumps past the failing chunk. (1) If CONFIG_ARC_USE_UNALIGNED_MEM_ACCESS is off and either pointer is not 4-byte aligned it copies byte by byte, decrementing n after each completed store; on a faulting store the loop is left and the function returns n, the exact number of bytes not written. (2) For a compile-time constant n it copies in blocks of 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1 bytes (loads of the block, then its stores), subtracting the block size from res (initially n) only after the whole block was stored; after a fault the failing block is abandoned but the following smaller blocks are still attempted, and `from` may have advanced past the loaded words while `to` advanced only past the stores that completed. (3) For a non-constant n one asm sequence copies the 16-byte chunks and then 8, 4, 2 and 1 bytes; a fault jumps to the end and abandons every later chunk. In (2) and (3) it returns res, which counts the bytes of the failing block as not copied even if some of that block's stores (up to three 4-byte words of a 16-byte chunk) had already succeeded, so it is an upper bound on the bytes not written; it is 0 when everything was stored.
note: checked uaccess.h:370-529. Reviewer rounds 2 and 15 ('exception table covers loads, not user stores') are WRONG for raw_copy_to_user: labels 1:, 11:-13:, 14:-18: sit on the st.ab stores (e.g. lines 407-415, 475-499), unlike raw_copy_from_user where they sit on loads. Reviewer round 1 (remaining count of the failed chunk, not exact) is right.

name: __clear_user
prose: Precondition: to is a user address, n a byte count; the caller keeps ownership of the memory and the user stores are protected by the exception table. Postcondition: res starts as n. If the address is odd it stores one zero byte (res -= 1); then if the (new) address has bit 1 set it stores a zero halfword (res -= 2); so at most two alignment stores, up to 3 bytes, are issued before the count is looked at. It then loads lp_count with res >> 2 (arithmetic) and stores that many zero words, subtracting 4 each; then it stores a zero halfword if bit 1 of res is set (res -= 2) and a zero byte if bit 0 of res is set (res -= 1). A faulting store jumps to the end, skipping every later store without decrementing res for it. It returns res as unsigned long: n minus the bytes stored when no padding-underflow occurs, so 0 if every store completed (exactly the n bytes at to are zeroed), or the number of bytes not stored when a store faults. There is no guard for n smaller than the alignment padding (n < 3 with a misaligned to): in that case the padding stores can write beyond n bytes, res becomes negative, and the negative value is passed through the arithmetic shift into lp_count for the word loop (the loop runs for the huge count the hardware takes from it, if lp_count is treated as unsigned, until a store faults); a fault in the padding stores instead returns n or n - 1 (n - 2 etc. depending on which stores completed).
note: checked uaccess.h:530-576. Reviewers: round 1 (writes up to 3 bytes when n smaller than padding) right; round 2 (fault during padding returns n, not negative) right and stated; round 15 (at most two alignment stores) right: stb then stw. The behaviour of lp_count with a negative value is an inference from asr.f/lpnz, not verified on hardware.

name: __arch_swab32
prose: Statement-expression macro (three alternative definitions chosen by CONFIG_ARC_HAS_SWAPE and ARC_BSWAP_TYPE in swab.h); it is not a function definition.
note: macro, not a function.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE0(arc_gettls)
prose: Generated syscall function __do_sys_arc_gettls (process.c:41-44). Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns task_thread_info(current)->thr_ptr, an unsigned long, converted to the syscall's long return type; it reads one field of the current thread's info and changes nothing. The value is whatever arc_settls last stored there ((unsigned int) of the user pointer), or the initial value if never set. Where long is 32 bits (32-bit ARC) a stored value with the top bit set becomes a negative long. No locks or references are taken.
note: checked process.c:25-44 and thread_info.h:43 (thr_ptr is unsigned long). The old claim that the result is always 0..4294967295 and never negative was wrong on a 32-bit long; contract removed.

name: processCFI
prose: Precondition: start and end delimit a readable CFI byte range, state points to a valid unwind_state, ptrType is the pointer encoding, targetLoc is 0 or a location to stop at. Because the advance_loc2 and advance_loc4 handlers read their operand bytes after only a check against end + 2 or end + 4 that cannot fail here (ptr is at most end after the opcode byte), up to 2 or 4 bytes beyond end can be read for those opcodes. Postcondition: returns 0 or 1. (a) If start != state->cieStart it first sets state->loc = state->org and runs processCFI over the CIE (state->cieStart..cieEnd, targetLoc 0); if targetLoc == 0 and state->label == NULL it returns that result at once (0 or 1). (b) Otherwise it executes instructions while result is non-zero and ptr < end: set_loc sets result 0 when read_pointer gives 0; advance_loc1 gives result 0 if ptr >= end; advance_loc2/4 set state->loc through advance_loc (always 1); DW_CFA_remember_state returns 1 (clearing state->label) when ptr == state->label, returns 0 when stackDepth >= MAX_STACK_DEPTH, otherwise pushes ptr; DW_CFA_restore_state returns 0 if stackDepth is 0, else it saves loc and label, sets label from the saved stack, resets cfa to badCFA, zeroes regs and stackDepth, recursively processes [start, end) with targetLoc 0 (its result becomes result) and restores loc and label; GNU_window_save and unknown opcodes set result 0; other opcodes update the rules or the cfa. After each instruction ptr > end sets result 0, and if result is non-zero and targetLoc != 0 and targetLoc < state->loc it returns 1. (c) After the loop it returns result && ptr == end && (targetLoc == 0 || state->label == NULL). state->loc, regs, cfa, stack, stackDepth and label can be partly modified even when 0 is returned.
note: checked unwind.c:693-815. Reviewer round 15 (advance_loc4 reads up to 8 bytes past end) is WRONG: ptr <= end after the opcode, so the 4-byte read stays within end+4. Round 1 (the end+2/end+4 checks do not reject over-reads) is right. Round 2 (augmentation) concerned an older wording.

name: PINMUX_PIN
prose: Object-like/function-like macro used to build pin-mux constants in a device-tree header; it is not a function definition.
note: macro, not a function.

name: bL_switcher_thread
prose: Precondition: arg points to a struct bL_thread (the thread's own slot) whose lock, wait queue and started completion are initialised. Postcondition: it sets the current task to low FIFO priority with sched_set_fifo_low(current) and calls complete(&t->started). It then runs a do-while loop (the body runs at least once): if a signal is pending it flushes it; it waits interruptibly on t->wq until t->wanted_cluster != -1 or kthread_should_stop() (the wait can also end because of a signal, its return value is ignored); under t->lock it copies wanted_cluster, completer and completer_cookie and sets wanted_cluster to -1 and completer to NULL; and if the copied cluster is not -1 it calls bL_switch_to(cluster) and then, if the copied completer is non-NULL, completer(completer_cookie). The loop ends when kthread_should_stop() is true after an iteration, and the function returns 0 (its only return). Because the request is cleared under the lock before the switch and the callback run, a new request may be accepted while the previous switch is in progress, and a request with a NULL completer can be overwritten by a later one before the thread services it.
note: checked bL_switcher.c:270-304. Reviewer rounds 1 and 2 are right and covered; the added points are the do-while shape and the signal flush.

name: ATOMIC64_OPS(add, adds, adc)
prose: Generated function arch_atomic64_add(s64 i, atomic64_t *v), produced by ATOMIC64_OP(add, adds, adc) inside ATOMIC64_OPS (atomic.h:311-326, 376-381). Precondition: v points to a valid atomic64_t whose counter is 8-byte aligned (ldrexd/strexd). Postcondition: after prefetchw it repeats ldrexd, adds on the low word, adc on the high word, strexd until the exclusive store succeeds, so v->counter becomes its previous value plus i (64-bit two's complement) without losing a concurrent update; there is no barrier in the function. It returns nothing. The same ATOMIC64_OPS(add, ...) invocation also generates arch_atomic64_add_return and arch_atomic64_fetch_add, which return s64 and are separate functions.
note: checked atomic.h:311-326. Reviewer round 15's omission of the return variants concerns other generated functions, not this one.

name: arch_read_trylock
prose: Precondition: rw points to an initialised arch_rwlock_t whose lock word is 4-byte aligned. Postcondition: after prefetchw it repeats ldrex of the lock word, computes old + 1, and executes strex of that sum only if the sum is non-negative as a signed value (strexpl), until the exclusive store does not fail. Then, with contended holding old + 1 (mod 2^32): if contended < 0x80000000 it issues smp_mb() and returns 1 (the lock word was incremented, which happens for old values 0 up to 0x7ffffffe, and also for old = 0xffffffff, which wraps to 0); otherwise it returns 0 with no store and the lock word unchanged (this covers a write-held lock, 0x80000000, and also old = 0x7fffffff, whose increment would reach 0x80000000).
note: slice cut the head: real function is arch_read_trylock (spinlock.h:248-271). Reviewer round 15 is right: 0x7fffffff is left unchanged and returns 0. The old-value 0xffffffff case is from tracing adds/strexpl, not from a documented use.

name: uaccess_save_and_enable
prose: Precondition: none; takes no arguments. Postcondition: one of three alternative definitions, chosen at build time. With CONFIG_CPU_SW_DOMAIN_PAN (always inline) it reads the domain register, sets the user domain to DOMAIN_CLIENT with set_domain and returns the old domain value. With CONFIG_CPU_TTBR0_PAN (always inline) it reads TTBCR, writes it back with the A1, EPD0 and T0SZ bits cleared, executes isb() and returns the old TTBCR. Otherwise it returns 0 and changes nothing. The caller is expected to pass the returned value to uaccess_restore. No locks, references or memory are transferred.
note: checked uaccess.h:29-69. The prose already matched the three variants; only the 'any context' remark was dropped.

name: arch_timer_arch_init
prose: Precondition: none; runs once at init (__init). Postcondition: it reads arch_timer_get_rate(); if that is 0 it returns -ENXIO (-6) and registers nothing. Otherwise it calls arch_timer_delay_timer_register(), which sets arch_delay_timer.read_current_timer to arch_timer_read_counter_long, sets arch_delay_timer.freq to a second reading of arch_timer_get_rate(), and calls register_current_timer_delay(&arch_delay_timer); it then returns 0.
note: checked arch_timer.c:20-42. Contract removed: the function writes a static delay_timer and registers it. Note the rate is read twice (lines 21 and 24).

name: watchpoint_handler
prose: Precondition: called from hw_breakpoint_pending for a synchronous (or asynchronous) watchpoint exception with preemption disabled; local interrupts may be enabled (hw_breakpoint_pending enables them if they were enabled in the interrupted context); addr and fsr describe the access and regs the interrupted context. Postcondition: returns nothing. It takes rcu_read_lock once, scans the per-cpu wp_on_reg slots (0..core_num_wrps-1) and releases the lock at the end. For each non-NULL slot: on debug architectures before v7.1 (only slot 0 allowed, BUG_ON otherwise) trigger is set to the watchpoint's configured address; on later ones, if debug_exception_updates_fsr() the access type derived from fsr must match the watchpoint type or the slot is skipped; the watchpoint value and control registers give the distance to addr, which updates the closest match, and only an exact match (distance 0) records trigger = addr. For an exact match: if the fault came from a uaccess routine (kernel mode and user-privilege watchpoint) no perf event is emitted and single-step is enabled; otherwise perf_bp_event is called and single-step is enabled only if the overflow handler is the default one. After the scan, if no exact match was found but some slot had a non-zero distance (min_dist > 0 and != -1), the closest slot gets trigger = addr, perf_bp_event is called for it, and single-step is enabled if its overflow handler is the default one (this closest-match path does not apply the uaccess check).
note: checked hw_breakpoint.c:727-820 and hw_breakpoint_pending (938-975). Reviewer round 15 is right: hw_breakpoint_pending may call local_irq_enable before this handler, so 'interrupts disabled' was wrong. Round 2 (one RCU read-side section around the whole loop) is right.

name: apply_relocate
prose: Precondition: sechdrs, strtab, symindex, relindex and module describe a loaded module image whose REL relocation section, target section, symbol table and string table are consistent and whose target sections already sit at their load addresses. Postcondition: it processes the Elf32_Rel entries of the relocation section in order and patches the target words in place. It returns -ENOEXEC, after printing an error and leaving the earlier relocations applied and the later ones unapplied, for a bad symbol index, an r_offset outside the target section, an ARM branch to a symbol with an odd (Thumb) address, a branch or PREL31 or LDR_PC_G2 relocation that is out of range (after trying a PLT entry via get_module_plt when CONFIG_ARM_MODULE_PLTS is set, for the branch types), a Thumb branch to an ARM function symbol, a Thumb branch out of range, or an unknown relocation type. It returns 0 after all entries were applied; R_ARM_NONE is ignored. No memory is allocated for the caller (a PLT entry may be allocated in the module).
note: the listed name apply_relocate_add does not exist in arm/kernel/module.c; the slice is the tail of apply_relocate (module.c:76-470) and the arch uses REL relocations. Checked all return statements (86-91 start of the function, 98, 103, 118, 151-156, 168, 223, 253, 354, 399, 462).

name: perf_reg_validate
prose: Precondition: mask is any 64-bit value. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL (-22) if mask is 0 or mask has any bit set at or above bit PERF_REG_ARM_MAX (16), i.e. (mask >> 16) != 0; otherwise returns 0. No state is changed.
note: checked perf_regs.c:19-25 (REG_RESERVED = ~((1ULL << PERF_REG_ARM_MAX) - 1), PERF_REG_ARM_MAX = 16 from uapi/asm/perf_regs.h). Contract corrected to cover both outcomes.

name: spectre_v2_update_state
prose: Precondition: none; state and method are unsigned values (state is one of the SPECTRE_* levels, method a SPECTRE_V2_METHOD_* bit). Postcondition: the static variable spectre_v2_state becomes state if state is greater than its current value (otherwise unchanged), and the static variable spectre_v2_methods is ORed with method. It returns nothing.
note: the listed name spectre_v2_state is a static variable, not a function; the prose described spectre_v2_update_state (spectre.c:25-30), which is in the slice, so it is fixed under that name.

name: unwind_exec_insn
prose: Precondition: ctrl points to an initialised unwind_ctrl_block whose instruction stream (ctrl->insn, byte, entries) is set up and whose stack is readable at the addresses the instruction pops. Postcondition: reads one instruction byte with unwind_get_byte (which returns 0 with a warning if no entries are left, and decrements ctrl->entries each time a 32-bit word is used up) and returns URC_OK (0) or -URC_FAILURE. 0x00-0x3f adds ((insn & 0x3f) << 2) + 4 to ctrl->vrs[SP]; 0x40-0x7f subtracts it; 0x80-0x8f reads a second byte, fails if the 12-bit mask is 0, otherwise pops registers r4-r15 selected by the mask (a pop of r13 loads vrs[SP] from the stack; if r13 is not in the mask vrs[SP] is set to the advanced stack pointer after all pops); 0x90-0x9f except 0x9d and 0x9f copies vrs[insn & 0xf] into vrs[SP]; 0xa0-0xaf pops r4 to r4+(insn & 7) and optionally r14, then sets vrs[SP] to the advanced stack pointer; 0xb0 sets vrs[PC] from vrs[LR] if vrs[PC] is 0 and sets ctrl->entries to 0; 0xb1 reads a mask byte, fails if it is 0 or has bits 4-7 set, otherwise pops r0-r3 per the mask and sets vrs[SP] to the advanced pointer; 0xb2 adds 0x204 + (uleb128 << 2) to vrs[SP]; any other opcode, including 0x9d and 0x9f, warns and fails. On a failure from a pop, vrs[SP] is unchanged but earlier popped registers in vrs[] may already be overwritten; on every path the instruction stream position and ctrl->entries reflect the bytes consumed. No locks are taken and no memory is allocated.
note: checked unwind.c:211-333 (get_byte, pop helpers) and 337-408. Reviewer round 15 is right (a popped r13 loads vrs[SP] rather than advancing it); round 2 right (r13 is the last register so a later pop cannot fail); round 1 partly right (vrs[SP] unchanged on failure, as I found). Old prose said ctrl->entries unchanged on failure; unwind_get_byte decrements it as bytes are consumed.

name: xscale_cp0_init
prose: Precondition: none; runs once as a late initcall. Postcondition: returns 0 on every path. If the CPU is not in the XScale family it returns 0 without touching anything. Otherwise it reads the coprocessor access register, clears bits 0-1 and writes the value with bit 0 set, then probes for iWMMXt. If iWMMXt is detected and CONFIG_IWMMXT is not set it only prints a warning (no notifier, no hwcap change). If detected and CONFIG_IWMMXT is set it prints an info message, sets HWCAP_IWMMXT in elf_hwcap, registers the iWMMXt thread notifier and the iWMMXt undefined-instruction handler. If iWMMXt is not detected it prints an info message, registers the DSP thread notifier and sets bit 0 in the access value. It finally writes the access value (bits 0-1 clear in the iWMMXt cases, bit 0 set in the DSP case) back to the coprocessor access register.
note: checked xscale-cp0.c:150-180. The old contract was dropped because the function changes coprocessor and global state; the prose already matched the code.

name: exynos_cpu_power_state
prose: Precondition: cpu is a core index for which EXYNOS_ARM_CORE_STATUS(cpu) designates a readable PMU register. Postcondition: returns the 32-bit value read with pmu_raw_readl from that register ANDed with S5P_CORE_LOCAL_PWR_EN (0x3, include/linux/soc/samsung/exynos-regs-pmu.h:183), converted to int, so the result is 0, 1, 2 or 3 and is non-zero when either of the two low bits is set. It takes no lock and allocates nothing.
note: checked platsmp.c:129-133. Reviewer round 15 is WRONG: S5P_CORE_LOCAL_PWR_EN is 0x3 in this tree, so the range 0..3 is right; the claim 'nonzero exactly when the power-enable bit is set' is refined to 'either low bit'.

name: exynos_cluster_power_state
prose: Precondition: cluster is a cluster index for which EXYNOS_COMMON_STATUS(cluster) designates a readable PMU register. Postcondition: returns the 32-bit value read with pmu_raw_readl from that register ANDed with S5P_CORE_LOCAL_PWR_EN (0x3), converted to int, so the result is 0, 1, 2 or 3 and is non-zero when either of the two low bits is set. It takes no lock and allocates nothing.
note: checked platsmp.c:159-163. Reviewer round 15 is WRONG: the constant is 0x3 (exynos-regs-pmu.h:183).

name: tzic_set_irq_fiq
prose: Precondition: only built with CONFIG_FIQ (otherwise tzic_set_irq_fiq is #defined to NULL); tzic_base is mapped. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL (-22) without touching a register when (hwirq >> 5) >= 4, i.e. hwirq >= 128. Otherwise it reads INTSEC0 of bank hwirq >> 5, sets bit (hwirq & 31), clears that bit again if type is non-zero, writes the value back to the same register and returns 0.
note: checked tzic.c:52-67. Contract removed because the function accesses device registers; the prose already matched.

name: tzic_enable_wake
prose: Precondition: tzic_base is mapped and the TZIC was initialised by tzic_init_dt. Postcondition: writes 1 to the DSMINT register and reads it back; if the read-back is 0 it returns -EAGAIN (-11) without touching the wakeup registers; otherwise it copies each of the four ENSET0 bank registers into the corresponding WAKEUP0 register and returns 0.
note: checked tzic.c:207-221. Contract removed because the function accesses device registers; the prose already matched.

name: calc_dsor_exp
prose: Precondition: rate and realrate are unsigned long clock rates in Hz. Postcondition: returns -EIO (-5) if realrate is 0. Otherwise it halves a copy of realrate (integer division) up to three times and returns the smallest d in 0..3 for which realrate / 2^d (successive halving) is at most rate; if even realrate / 8 is greater than rate it returns 4, which callers must treat as invalid. It reads no other state.
note: checked clock.c:138-162. The old contract was dropped (round 15 right: realrate is modified in the loop so a postcondition on it needs the original value).

name: omap_readb
prose: Precondition: pa is a physical address inside the OMAP1_IO window that omap1_map_io statically maps (OMAP1_IO_PHYS, size OMAP1_IO_SIZE), so that OMAP1_IO_ADDRESS(pa), which is pa - OMAP1_IO_OFFSET (0x00f00000), is its mapped device virtual address. Postcondition: returns the 8-bit value from __raw_readb of that address (0 to 255); a raw device read with no barrier, no locks and no allocation.
note: checked io.c:70-88 and hardware.h:64-65. Reviewer round 15 is right that OMAP1_IO_ADDRESS is a fixed subtraction valid for the OMAP1_IO window, so the DSP and DSPREG regions are not claimed any more.

name: omap_readw
prose: Precondition: pa is a physical address inside the OMAP1_IO window that omap1_map_io statically maps (OMAP1_IO_PHYS, size OMAP1_IO_SIZE), so that OMAP1_IO_ADDRESS(pa), which is pa - OMAP1_IO_OFFSET (0x00f00000), is its mapped device virtual address. Postcondition: returns the 16-bit value from __raw_readw of that address (0 to 65535); a raw device read with no barrier, no locks and no allocation.
note: checked io.c:70-88 and hardware.h:64-65. Reviewer round 15 is right that OMAP1_IO_ADDRESS is a fixed subtraction valid for the OMAP1_IO window, so the DSP and DSPREG regions are not claimed any more.

name: omap_readl
prose: Precondition: pa is a physical address inside the OMAP1_IO window that omap1_map_io statically maps (OMAP1_IO_PHYS, size OMAP1_IO_SIZE), so that OMAP1_IO_ADDRESS(pa), which is pa - OMAP1_IO_OFFSET (0x00f00000), is its mapped device virtual address. Postcondition: returns the 32-bit value from __raw_readl of that address (0 to 4294967295); a raw device read with no barrier, no locks and no allocation.
note: checked io.c:70-88 and hardware.h:64-65. Reviewer round 15 is right that OMAP1_IO_ADDRESS is a fixed subtraction valid for the OMAP1_IO window, so the DSP and DSPREG regions are not claimed any more.

name: omap1_cfg_reg
prose: Precondition: cfg points to a valid struct pin_config; no field is validated. Postcondition: if cfg->mux_reg is non-zero it reads that register under mux_spin_lock (irq-saving), replaces the three bits at cfg->mask_offset with cfg->mask, writes it back and releases the lock; warn is set if the old three-bit field differed from the new value. If the CPU is not an OMAP15xx and cfg->pu_pd_reg and cfg->pull_val are both non-zero it does a locked read-modify-write of cfg->pu_pd_reg at bit cfg->pull_bit (set when cfg->pu_pd_val is non-zero, cleared otherwise), setting warn if the bit was not already in that state. If cfg->pull_reg is non-zero it does a locked read-modify-write of that register at cfg->pull_bit (cleared when cfg->pull_val is non-zero, set otherwise) and sets warn if the bit changes. warn is decided from the values read before each write, not from a read-back after it. With CONFIG_OMAP_MUX_WARNINGS it prints a warning when warn is set and returns -ETXTBSY if warn was set, otherwise 0; without that option it always returns 0. With CONFIG_OMAP_MUX_DEBUG it also prints the register values. No lock is held on return.
note: checked mux.c:286-409. Reviewer round 15 is right (warn compares the pre-write value to the desired one); round 2 right (pu_pd_reg touched only when pull_val is non-zero); round 1 right (return value depends on CONFIG_OMAP_MUX_WARNINGS).

name: omap3xxx_clockdomains_init
prose: Precondition: none; runs at init (__init). Postcondition: returns nothing. If !cpu_is_omap34xx() it returns at once. Otherwise it registers the platform functions omap3_clkdm_operations and the common clockdomains, then reads omap_rev(): for AM35XX_REV_ES1_0 or ES1_1 it registers clockdomains_am35x and clkdm_am35x_autodeps; for any other revision it registers clockdomains_omap3430, then clockdomains_omap3430es1 when the revision is OMAP3430_REV_ES1_0 or clockdomains_omap3430es2plus otherwise, and clkdm_autodeps. It finishes with clkdm_complete_init().
note: slice cut the head: the function is omap3xxx_clockdomains_init (clockdomains3xxx_data.c:499-526), not clkdm_init. The old prose said exactly one clockdomain table; several tables are registered (common plus the revision-specific ones).

name: omap3xxx_cm_wait_module_ready
prose: Precondition: prcm_mod identifies a CM module; part is ignored; when idlest_id is in 1..3 the shift idlest_shift is below 32. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if idlest_id is 0 or greater than ARRAY_SIZE(omap3xxx_cm_idlest_offs) (3). Otherwise it polls the CM_IDLESTx register selected by idlest_id for the bit 1 << idlest_shift to read 0, at most MAX_MODULE_READY_TIME (2000) times with udelay(1) between polls, and returns 0 if the bit read 0 within that many polls and -EBUSY otherwise. It reads device registers and modifies no memory.
note: checked cm3xxx.c:88-107 and omap_test_timeout. The old contract was dropped because the function reads hardware registers.

name: omap2_control_base_init
prose: Precondition: none; runs at init (__init). Postcondition: walks the device-tree nodes matching omap_scrm_dt_match_table. For each match it maps the first register range with of_iomap; if the mapping fails it calls of_node_put on the node and returns -ENOMEM (-12), leaving later nodes unmapped. Otherwise, when the match data's index is TI_CLKM_CTRL it also sets omap2_ctrl_base to the mapping and omap2_ctrl_offset to data->offset, and in every successful case it stores the mapping in data->mem (the match data pointer is cast from const). It returns 0 after all matching nodes were handled, including when none matched.
note: checked control.c:700-721. Contract removed: the function writes globals.

name: omap4_dsi_mux_pads
prose: Precondition: dsi_id and lanes as passed by the caller; omap4_dsi_mux_syscon is a valid regmap for the register read to succeed. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV without touching any register if dsi_id is neither 0 nor 1. Otherwise it reads the DSIPHY syscon register through the regmap and returns the read's negative error if that fails; it then clears the lane-enable and PIPD fields for that DSI, ORs in lanes shifted into each field and masked to it, writes the register back with regmap_write (ignoring its return value) and returns 0.
note: checked display.c:73-102. Contract removed because the function uses the global regmap and writes a register.

name: omap_dsi_enable_pads
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: if cpu_is_omap44xx() is false it returns 0 without doing anything; if it is true it returns omap4_dsi_mux_pads(dsi_id, lane_mask): -ENODEV when dsi_id is neither 0 nor 1, the regmap read's negative error if the read fails, and 0 after the pad fields were updated (a failure of the final regmap_write is ignored).
note: checked display.c:111-116. Contract removed: the return depends on the CPU type and a global regmap.

name: omap4_mpuss_init
prose: Precondition: runs at init time (__init) after the PRCM and power-domain frameworks are usable; sar_base is NULL or maps SAR RAM. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV with WARN(1) at once when omap_rev() is OMAP4430_REV_ES1_0. Otherwise it fills the per-CPU PM info for CPU 0: when sar_base is non-NULL it sets scu_sar_addr, wkup_sar_addr (an OMAP44xx or OMAP5 offset) and l2x0_sar_addr; looks up "cpu0_pwrdm" (pr_err and -ENODEV if not found); clears its previous power state and previous logic state; and sets its next state to PWRDM_POWER_ON. It does the same for CPU 1 with "cpu1_pwrdm". It then looks up "mpu_pwrdm" into mpuss_pd (pr_err and -ENODEV if not found) and only clears its previous power state and previous logic state (its next state is not set). With sar_base it writes the device-type flag (1 unless a GP device) to the scratchpad and calls save_l2x0_context(). On OMAP44xx it installs finish_suspend, resume, scu_prepare and hotplug_restart in omap_pm_ops and sets cpu_context_offset for OMAP4; on OMAP5 or DRA7 it sets cpu_context_offset for OMAP54xx and calls enable_mercury_retention_mode(); on OMAP446x it additionally sets hotplug_restart to omap4460_secondary_startup. It returns 0. On any -ENODEV return the changes already made stay in place.
note: checked omap-mpuss-lowpower.c:365-446. Reviewer round 2 is right (the mpu power domain is only cleared, never set ON); round 15 concerned the formal contract, now removed.

name: _shutdown
prose: Precondition: oh points to a valid struct omap_hwmod. Postcondition: if _are_all_hardreset_lines_asserted(oh) it returns 0 without changing anything. If oh->_state is neither idle nor enabled it warns and returns -EINVAL with no other change. If the class has a pre_shutdown hook it remembers the state, calls _enable(oh) when the state is idle, calls the hook, and if the hook returns non-zero it calls _idle(oh) when the previous state was idle and returns that error. If the class has a sysc it calls _enable(oh) first when the state is idle and then _shutdown_sysc(oh). Then, if the state is now enabled, it removes the MPU initiator dependency, releases the CPU idle poll hold with cpu_idle_poll_ctrl(false) when HWMOD_BLOCK_WFI is set, calls soc_ops.disable_module if present, disables the clocks, and, if oh->clkdm is set, calls clkdm_hwmod_disable. It then asserts every hardreset line in oh->rst_lines, sets oh->_state to _HWMOD_STATE_DISABLED (after the assertions, not before) and returns 0.
note: checked omap_hwmod.c:2023-2074. Reviewer round 15 is WRONG: the assert loop (2071-2072) comes before oh->_state = _HWMOD_STATE_DISABLED (2074). Reviewer round 1 (early return 0 when all hardreset lines are asserted) is right and already in the prose.

name: dns323_identify_rev
prose: Precondition: runs at init (__init); the Orion5x PCIe ID registers and the ETH SMI register at ORION5X_ETH_VIRT_BASE + 0x2004 are accessible. Postcondition: returns DNS323_REV_A1 at once when orion5x_pcie_id reports dev == MV88F5181_DEV_ID. Otherwise it reads the SMI register up to 1000 times waiting for SMI_BUSY to clear and, if it is still busy, warns and returns DNS323_REV_B1 without writing anything. If not busy, it writes an SMI read command for PHY address 8, register 3 to the SMI register, then reads the register up to 1000 times waiting for SMI_READ_VALID and returns DNS323_REV_B1 with a warning if it never appears. Otherwise it examines the PHY ID (reg & 0xfff0): 0x0cc0 gives DNS323_REV_B1, 0x0e10 gives DNS323_REV_C1, and any other value warns and gives DNS323_REV_B1. No memory is allocated and no lock is taken.
note: checked dns323-setup.c:547-612. Reviewer round 15 is right (the busy-timeout path returns before the write); round 2 right (the SMI register is also written).

name: rcar_gen2_regulator_quirk
prose: Precondition: runs once as an arch initcall (__init) with the device tree available. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV, having allocated and mapped nothing, if the machine is not renesas,koelsch, lager, porter, stout or gose. Otherwise it walks the nodes matching rcar_gen2_quirk_match: an unavailable node ends the walk (after of_node_put); a node whose 'reg' cannot be read, or whose interrupt specifier cannot be parsed (of_irq_parse_one fails, after dropping the node reference and freeing the entry), is skipped; for each good node it kzallocs a regulator_quirk (on failure it drops the node reference, sets -ENOMEM and goes to the common cleanup), copies the i2c message template, records the node (of_node_get), marks entries with identical interrupt arguments as shared, and appends it to quirk_list. It then ioremaps IRQC_BASE (failure: -ENOMEM and cleanup) and reads the monitor register. If the REGULATOR_IRQ_MASK bit is set (IRQ2 not asserted) it unmaps irqc, empties quirk_list (node references dropped, entries freed) and returns 0 without registering anything. If the bit is clear it registers the i2c bus notifier, leaves irqc mapped and quirk_list holding the parsed entries, and returns 0. The cleanup path used for -ENOMEM empties quirk_list the same way (and irqc was either not mapped or is not unmapped on the ioremap-failure path).
note: checked regulator-quirk-rcar-gen2.c:141-235. Added the break on an unavailable node and the shared marking; the old prose's return paths were right. Contract removed because the function modifies globals and registers a notifier.

name: socfpga_pm_enter
prose: Precondition: state is any suspend_state_t value. Postcondition: for state == PM_SUSPEND_MEM it calls outer_disable(), then cpu_suspend(0, socfpga_pm_suspend) with the return value ignored, then outer_resume(), and returns 0; for any other state it returns -EINVAL and does not touch the outer cache. The suspend callback socfpga_pm_suspend returns -EFAULT without suspending if sdr_ctl_base_addr is zero (that value is discarded here), and otherwise calls the self-refresh function that socfpga_pm_init copied to OCRAM (that pointer is not checked for NULL in this path); it returns 0 in that case. No locks or references are taken.
note: checked pm.c:96-135. Old prose attributed the -EFAULT to a missing OCRAM function; the code returns -EFAULT only for a zero sdr_ctl_base_addr (line 98-99). Contract removed: the function manipulates the outer cache and CPU state.

name: tegra_sleep_cpu
prose: Precondition: tegra_cpu_car_ops is non-NULL; v2p is the virtual-to-physical offset passed by cpu_suspend. Postcondition: if tegra_cpu_car_ops->rail_off_ready is non-NULL and tegra_cpu_rail_off_ready() returns false (WARN_ON fires) it returns -EBUSY without suspending. Otherwise, only when CONFIG_OUTER_CACHE is set, Trusted Foundations firmware is registered and outer_cache.disable is non-NULL, it calls outer_cache.disable(); it then calls the firmware prepare_idle operation with TF_PM_MODE_LP2, setup_mm_for_reboot() and tegra_sleep_cpu_finish(v2p), which is not expected to return; if it does return, BUG() is executed (the final return 0 is unreachable in practice).
note: checked pm.c:139-173. Reviewer round 15 is right: the outer cache disable is conditional on CONFIG_OUTER_CACHE, TF registration and outer_cache.disable. Round 1 (the -EBUSY return) right and in the prose.

name: ve_spc_set_performance
prose: Precondition: cluster is a valid cluster index whose OPP table has been populated (info->opps and info->num_opps); freq is in kHz, the same unit as the OPP entries (no conversion is done here; the caller at spc.c:514 passes rate / 1000). Postcondition: selects req_type and performance register for an A15 or A7 cluster, then finds the OPP index whose freq equals freq exactly; if none matches it returns -EINVAL without taking info->sem. Otherwise it waits for info->sem with down_timeout (TIMEOUT_US) and returns -ETIME (-62) if that times out, with info->cur_rsp_mask untouched. With the semaphore held it reinitialises info->done, sets info->cur_rsp_mask for the request, writes the OPP index to the performance register, waits with ve_spc_waitforcompletion, which gives 0 when the completion arrives with the expected status bit, -EIO if the status lacks it, -ETIMEDOUT (-110) on timeout, or the negative value from an interrupted wait; it then clears info->cur_rsp_mask, releases info->sem and returns that result.
note: checked spc.c:262-346. Reviewer round 15 is right: ETIME is -62 (the old prose said -116). Round 1 (kHz, not Hz) right.

name: tc2_pm_wait_for_powerdown
prose: Precondition: the SCC register block is mapped and the SPC is initialised; cluster < TC2_CLUSTERS (2) and cpu < TC2_MAX_CPUS_PER_CLUSTER (3), otherwise BUG_ON fires. Postcondition: it polls up to TIMEOUT_MSEC / POLL_MSEC = 100 times; in each poll it returns 0 as soon as tc2_core_in_reset(cpu, cluster) or ve_spc_cpu_in_wfi(cpu, cluster) is true, otherwise it sleeps POLL_MSEC (10 ms) with msleep and tries again; after the last poll it returns -ETIMEDOUT (-110). It takes no locks.
note: checked tc2_pm.c:124-152. Contract removed because the function reads hardware registers; the BUG_ON is not a normal return.

name: zynq_early_slcr_init
prose: Precondition: runs early at init (__init) with the device tree available. Postcondition: if no node compatible with "xlnx,zynq-slcr" exists, or of_iomap(np, 0) fails, it prints an error and calls BUG() (does not return normally). Otherwise it stores the mapping in zynq_slcr_base and in np->data, then looks up the syscon regmap into zynq_slcr_regmap. If that lookup fails it prints an error, releases the node reference with of_node_put and returns -ENODEV (zynq_slcr_regmap then holds the error pointer). Otherwise it unlocks the SLCR, updates SLCR_L2C_RAM bits with regmap_update_bits(0x70707 mask, 0x20202) (result ignored), registers the restart handler, prints a message, releases the node reference and returns 0.
note: checked slcr.c:194-232.

name: BUILD_RAC_CACHE_OP(kern_cache_all, nobarrier)
prose: Generated function b15_flush_kern_cache_all(void) (cache-b15-rac.c:104-123). Precondition: the caller does not hold rac_lock; if the RAC_ENABLED bit of b15_rac_flags is set, b15_rac_base and rac_flush_offset are valid. Postcondition: returns nothing and calls v7_flush_kern_cache_all exactly once. If the RAC_SUSPENDED bit is set it calls v7_flush_kern_cache_all directly and returns without taking rac_lock or touching the RAC registers. Otherwise it takes rac_lock (spin_lock), reads the RAC_ENABLED bit into do_flush, and if it is set it disables the RAC and flushes it (saving the CONFIG0 value) before the v7 flush and re-enables it with the saved value afterwards; if it is clear it does no RAC register access (the 'bar' argument nobarrier expands to nothing); it releases rac_lock and leaves b15_rac_flags unchanged.
note: checked cache-b15-rac.c:63-123 and the invocation at line 143.

name: aurora_range_end
prose: Precondition: start + 1 and start + 4096 (via PAGE_ALIGN) do not overflow unsigned long; end is any unsigned long. Postcondition: returns end reduced twice: first to start + AURORA_MAX_RANGE_SIZE (1024) if end is larger, then to PAGE_ALIGN(start + 1) (the first page boundary above start) if that is smaller, i.e. the minimum of end, start + 1024 and PAGE_ALIGN(start + 1). It reads no state other than the constants and takes no locks.
note: slice cut the head: the function is aurora_range_end (cache-l2x0.c:1357-1371). Old prose and contract used 1048576; AURORA_MAX_RANGE_SIZE is 1024 (cache-aurora-l2.h:89), so they were wrong. Contract removed (depends on PAGE_SIZE).

name: check_and_switch_context
prose: Precondition: mm is a live mm with a valid pgd and context.id; the function runs on the current CPU (smp_processor_id); tsk is not used. Postcondition: returns nothing. It calls check_vmalloc_seq(mm) and cpu_set_reserved_ttbr0(). If mm->context.id belongs to the current ASID generation and atomic64_xchg of this CPU's active_asids with that ASID returns non-zero, it goes straight to cpu_switch_mm (no lock taken, mm_cpumask not updated). Otherwise it takes cpu_asid_lock with interrupts saved, re-reads the id and, if it is stale, replaces it with new_context(mm, cpu); if this CPU is set in tlb_flush_pending it clears the bit and flushes the branch predictor and TLB locally; it sets this CPU's active_asids to the ASID, sets this CPU in mm_cpumask(mm) and releases the lock restoring the saved interrupt flags. On both paths it finishes with cpu_switch_mm(mm->pgd, mm).
note: checked context.c:237-276. The old prose said the function requires interrupts enabled and always sets mm_cpumask and active_asids under the lock; the fast path (lines 250-253) does neither under the lock, and the lock uses irqsave so no interrupt-state precondition is needed.

name: PerformComparison
prose: Precondition: none; opcode is any 32-bit value and the FPA11 registers may hold any type tags. Postcondition: static function returning 0 or 1. In a CONFIG_FPE_NWFPE_XP build it returns 0, leaving the FPSR condition flags unchanged, when fType[Fn] is not typeSingle, typeDouble or typeExtended, or when Fn is not a NaN and Fm is a non-constant register whose type tag is not one of those three. In a non-XP build there is no return 0: it always returns 1. Operands that are NaN (Fn, or Fm when it is a register; checked before the Fm type test in the XP build) take the unordered path: it sets the V flag, clears N and Z, sets C only if the FPSR AC bit is set, raises the invalid exception only if opcode bit 0x400000 is set, writes the flags and returns 1. Otherwise, if opcode bit 0x200000 is set the sign of Fm is inverted, and the flags are N when Fn < Fm, Z when Fn == Fm and C when Fm < Fn, V clear, written with writeConditionCodes before returning 1. The comparison is done in 80-bit extended precision in an XP build; in a non-XP build it is done in single precision when Fn is single and Fm is a constant or also single, and otherwise in double precision (extended-tagged registers are read as doubles there).
note: checked fpa11_cprt.c:142-358. Reviewer round 15 is WRONG: the non-XP path (lines 223-327) has no return 0 at all. Round 2 is right (non-XP compares in Fn's precision and does not handle extended).

name: vfp_double_ftouiz
prose: Precondition: sd is the index of the destination single-precision VFP register, dm the index of the source double-precision register; unused and fpscr are ignored. Postcondition: returns vfp_double_ftoui(sd, unused, dm, FPSCR_ROUND_TOZERO), which stores into register sd the 32-bit unsigned integer obtained by truncating the double in dm toward zero, and returns its exception flags: FPSCR_IDC for a denormal input (a denormal also gives FPSCR_IXC because it is non-zero and below 1, with result 0); FPSCR_IOC alone (replacing IDC) with result 0xffffffff for a NaN, an infinity or a magnitude of at least 2^32 (0 for negative values of that size); for 1 <= |x| < 2^32 the truncated value with FPSCR_IXC if bits were discarded, except that a negative value whose truncation is non-zero gives result 0 with FPSCR_IOC; for 0 < |x| < 1 result 0 with FPSCR_IXC; and zero gives 0 with no flags.
note: checked vfpdouble.c:506-582. Reviewer round 15 is right (a denormal input sets IXC as well as IDC); rounds 1 and 2 (dd versus sd) are wrong: the parameter is sd.

name: sm4_ce_gcm_init
prose: Precondition: none; runs at module init (__init). Postcondition: returns -ENODEV without registering anything when cpu_have_named_feature(PMULL) is false; otherwise it returns the result of crypto_register_aead(&sm4_gcm_alg): 0 with the algorithm registered, or the negative errno from that call.
note: checked sm4-ce-gcm-glue.c:255-261. Contract removed because the function has a registration side effect.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add, add, I)
prose: Generated function __ll_sc_atomic_add(int i, atomic_t *v), produced by ATOMIC_OP(add, add, I) inside ATOMIC_OPS (atomic_ll_sc.h:25-40, 84-95). Precondition: v points to a valid atomic_t. Postcondition: after a prefetch-for-store it runs an ldxr / add / stxr loop on v->counter, repeating while the exclusive store fails, so v->counter becomes its previous value plus i (32-bit wraparound) without losing a concurrent update. It returns nothing and has neither a barrier nor a 'memory' clobber (relaxed). The same ATOMIC_OPS invocation also generates the _return and fetch_ variants, which are separate functions.
note: checked atomic_ll_sc.h:25-40.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add, add, I)
prose: Generated function __ll_sc_atomic_add_return(int i, atomic_t *v), produced by ATOMIC_OP_RETURN(, dmb ish, , l, "memory", add, add, I) (atomic_ll_sc.h:42-61, 84-95). Precondition: v points to a valid atomic_t. Postcondition: it loops ldxr / add / stlxr (release store) until the exclusive store succeeds, then executes dmb ish; the 'memory' clobber is present. v->counter becomes its previous value plus i (32-bit wraparound) and the function returns the new value.
note: checked atomic_ll_sc.h:42-61 and the ATOMIC_OPS expansion at 84-95: the full-ordering variant uses stlxr plus dmb ish.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add, add, I)
prose: Generated function __ll_sc_atomic_fetch_add(int i, atomic_t *v), produced by ATOMIC_FETCH_OP(, dmb ish, , l, "memory", add, add, I) (atomic_ll_sc.h:63-82, 84-95). Postcondition: it loops ldxr (old value), add into a second register, stlxr (release store) until the exclusive store succeeds, then executes dmb ish; v->counter becomes old + i (32-bit wraparound) and the function returns the old value.

name: ATOMIC64_OPS(add, add, I)

It returns nothing and has neither a barrier nor a 'memory' clobber.

name: __CMPXCHG_CASE( , , , 64, , , , , L)
prose: Generated function __ll_sc__cmpxchg_case_64(volatile void *ptr, unsigned long old, u64 new) (atomic_ll_sc.h:239-262, invocation at 281). Precondition: ptr points to a naturally aligned u64 that the caller may read and write. Postcondition: it loops ldxr of *ptr; if the loaded value differs from old it leaves the loop without storing; otherwise it executes stxr of new and retries if the store fails. It returns the loaded value: so when *ptr equaled old it is replaced by new and old is returned, otherwise *ptr is unchanged and its current value is returned. This variant has no acquire, release or barrier and no 'memory' clobber.

The asm is selected at run time by ARM64_LSE_ATOMIC_INSN: with LL/SC it prefetches and loops ldxr (ldaxr for acq) and stxr (stlxr for rel and mb_) until the exclusive store succeeds, with a trailing dmb ish for mb_; with LSE it uses one SWP instruction (swpa, swpl or swpal as the ordering requires) padded with nops. With 4 KiB pages (PTRS_PER_PTE 512) the 1 GiB term is 512 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 516, so the result is at least 516. It does not modify any state.

name: fpsimd_init
prose: Boot-time initcall (core_initcall(fpsimd_init)) that takes no arguments. Behaviour in order: if cpu_have_named_feature(FP) is true it calls fpsimd_pm_init() then fpsimd_hotplug_init(); these register the CPU PM notifier and the CPU hotplug dead callback only when CONFIG_CPU_PM and CONFIG_HOTPLUG_CPU are respectively enabled, otherwise the corresponding helper is an empty inline. If FP is not present it prints "Floating-point is not implemented" with pr_notice. Then, independently of FP, if ASIMD is not present it prints "Advanced SIMD is not implemented". It then calls sve_sysctl_init() and sme_sysctl_init() and returns 0. The only return statement is the final return 0; there is no error return, and return values of the registration helpers are not examined.
note: Contract cleared: function reads CPU-feature global state and performs registrations and prints, which the old ensures result == 0 contract does not cover (reviewer round 15 right on that). Reviewer round 2 claim (helpers are no-ops without CONFIG_CPU_PM/HOTPLUG_CPU) was already reflected in the prose (fpsimd.c:92-94, 109-111). Slice contains the whole function at 123-141.

name: fpsimd_save_user_state
prose: Static function with no arguments, called with preemption disabled (WARN_ON fires if preemptible() or if FPSIMD is unsupported; execution continues after the warning). It works on this CPU per-CPU fpsimd_last_state (last). Return paths: (1) if TIF_FOREIGN_FPSTATE is set it returns at once and saves nothing; (2) if the SVE save is selected but sve_get_vl() differs from the expected vl, WARN_ON fires, force_signal_inject(SIGKILL, SI_KERNEL, 0, 0) is called on the current task, and it returns without saving SVE or FPSIMD registers and without writing *last->fp_type (FPMR and SVCR/ZA saves already done before this point stay done); (3) otherwise it falls off the end after saving. Before the save step: if FPMR is supported it stores the FPMR register into *last->fpmr; SVE register saving is selected, with vl = last->sve_vl and save_ffr true, when (last->to_save is FP_STATE_CURRENT and TIF_SVE is set) or last->to_save is FP_STATE_SVE; if SME is supported it reads SYS_SVCR and stores the value into *last->svcr (whenever SME is supported, regardless of the ZA bit), calls sme_save_state(last->sme_state, system_supports_sme2()) only when SVCR.ZA is set, and when SVCR.SM is set it forces SVE saving with vl = last->sme_vl and save_ffr = system_supports_fa64(). Final step: if CONFIG_ARM64_SVE is enabled and SVE saving is selected (and the vl check passed) it calls sve_save_state at last->sve_state + sve_ffr_offset(vl) with &last->st->fpsr and save_ffr and sets *last->fp_type = FP_STATE_SVE; otherwise (including SVE saving selected but CONFIG_ARM64_SVE disabled) it calls fpsimd_save_state(last->st) and sets *last->fp_type = FP_STATE_FPSIMD.
note: Reviewer round 15 (SVCR written whenever SME is supported, not only when ZA set) is right: fpsimd.c:216-219. Round 2 (WARN_ON on unbound last) is wrong: there is only a comment at 186, no such WARN_ON; the WARN_ONs at 191-192 test FPSIMD support and preemptible(). Original-rejection claim (SIGKILL return, fp_type not set) is right: 235-243. Slice contains the whole function at 182-253.

name: find_field
prose: Static __init helper. Parameters: cmdline (token text), opt (scratch buffer already holding a prefix of len bytes, normally "<name>."), len, reg and field index f, and v (output). Precondition: reg->fields[f].name is NUL-terminated; opt is writable for indices 0 through len + strlen(name) inclusive; cmdline is readable for len + strlen(name) + 1 bytes (memcmp compares that many bytes). Behaviour: it writes the field name and then "=" into opt after the prefix, then does memcmp of cmdline against opt over len + strlen(name) + 1 bytes. If they differ it returns -1 and *v is not written. If they match it returns parse_hexdigit(cmdline + len + strlen(name) + 1, v): an initial "0x" or "0X" is skipped when present, and the result is 0 with *v set to 0..15 when the next character is a hexadecimal digit and the character after it is NUL or whitespace (later characters are not examined); otherwise -EINVAL and *v is unchanged. Returned values are therefore only -1, -EINVAL or 0. It modifies the opt buffer in all cases.
note: Reviewer round 1 (omits optional 0x) is wrong: the prose already states the 0x skip (idreg-override.c:4-5, parse_hexdigit). Reviewer round 2 (memcmp reads len bytes) is already covered by the readability precondition on cmdline; memcmp at line 25. Prose tightened and return values enumerated.

name: parse_cmdline
prose: Static __init function taking the FDT pointer and the chosen node offset; it returns nothing. It selects at most one top-level string to parse with __parse_cmdline(str, true): get_bootargs_cmdline() yields the bootargs property of the chosen node, or NULL if chosen < 0, the property is missing, or the property is empty. If CONFIG_CMDLINE_FORCE is enabled, or the property is NULL, the built-in CONFIG_CMDLINE string is parsed; if CONFIG_CMDLINE_FORCE is not enabled and the property is non-NULL, the bootargs string is parsed instead (the built-in string is then not parsed). Parsing a string (__parse_cmdline) loops: skip leading whitespace; return if the text starts with "--" followed by a whitespace character; collect a token of non-whitespace characters, with "-" replaced by "_", at most 255 characters per chunk (a longer word is processed as successive 255-character chunks); return when the token is empty (end of string); otherwise call match_options on the token, and then, only when alias parsing is enabled, for each alias whose alias string equals the token (compared with its NUL) parse the alias feature string recursively with alias parsing disabled. match_options tries, for each register in order and each field in order, the prefix "<name>.<field>=" against the token; a field is skipped if the token does not start with that prefix or the rest is not an optional 0x followed by one hex digit that ends the token; for the first field that does match: if the field has a filter that rejects the value its mask bits are set in the override val and cleared in the override mask and the scan continues with later fields; otherwise the mask bits of val are replaced by (value << shift) & mask, the mask bits are set in the override mask, and the scan stops for that token. Here mask covers bits shift to shift + width - 1, with width 4 if the field width is 0.
note: Reviewer round 1 (built-in parsed unless forced) is wrong against the prose, which already says the built-in string is parsed only when forced or when no non-empty bootargs exist (idreg-override.c:135-139). Reviewer round 2 (invalid hex digit still treated as applied) is wrong: find_field returns nonzero for invalid digits and match_options continues (55-56). Whole function and callees are in the slice (31-140).

name: init_sdei_stacks
prose: Static function with no arguments, run at boot to allocate the per-CPU SDEI normal and critical stacks. It loops over every possible CPU; for each CPU it calls _init_sdei_stack for the normal stack pointer and then for the critical one, each of which calls arch_alloc_vmap_stack(SDEI_STACK_SIZE, cpu_to_node(cpu)) and stores the result in the per-CPU pointer, or returns -ENOMEM if the allocation returned NULL. The loop stops at the first failure. Return paths: there is one return, at the end. If no allocation failed it returns 0 with a normal and a critical stack stored for each possible CPU. If an allocation failed it first calls free_sdei_stacks(), which walks all possible CPUs and for each non-NULL normal or critical stack pointer sets it to NULL and vfree()s the stack (so stacks stored before the failure are released, as is any stack that was already present), and then returns -ENOMEM.
note: Contract cleared: function reads and writes per-CPU globals and allocates, which a result-only contract cannot state (reviewer round 15 right on that). Prose now says -ENOMEM and that free_sdei_stacks frees any non-NULL pointer on every possible CPU (sdei.c:49-65, 86-106). The iff-success claim is correct: err is only 0 if no _init_sdei_stack failed.

name: init_sdei_scs
prose: Static function with no arguments, run at boot to allocate the per-CPU SDEI shadow call stacks. Return paths: (1) if scs_is_enabled() is false it returns 0 immediately without allocating; (2) otherwise it loops over every possible CPU, calling _init_sdei_scs for the normal and then the critical shadow-call-stack pointer, each of which calls scs_alloc(cpu_to_node(cpu)) and stores the result in the per-CPU pointer or returns -ENOMEM if scs_alloc returned NULL; the loop stops at the first failure. If no allocation failed it returns 0. If an allocation failed it calls free_sdei_scs(), which walks all possible CPUs and for each non-NULL pointer sets it to NULL and calls scs_free(), and then returns -ENOMEM.
note: Contract cleared: global per-CPU state and allocation are involved (sdei.c:141-162, _init_sdei_scs and free_sdei_scs read above it). Reviewer round 15 right that the contract omitted them; the iff-success wording in the old prose is accurate.

name: restore_sve_fpsimd_context
prose: Static function (this is the CONFIG_ARM64_SVE definition; without that option a stub of the same name calls WARN_ON_ONCE(1) and returns -EINVAL) that restores SVE or streaming-SVE state from the signal frame context user->sve. Return paths in order: (1) -EINVAL if user->sve_size < sizeof(*user->sve), nothing modified; (2) the error from __get_user_error (-EFAULT) if reading the vl or flags fields fails, nothing modified; (3) with sm = flags & SVE_SIG_FLAG_SM and fpsimd_only = (user->sve_size == sizeof(*user->sve)): if sm is set, -EINVAL when SME is unsupported or fpsimd_only is true, else vl = task_get_sme_vl(current); if sm is clear, -EINVAL when SVE is unsupported and fpsimd_only is false, else vl = task_get_sve_vl(current); (4) -EINVAL if the context vl differs from vl; (5) if fpsimd_only, the result of restore_fpsimd_context(user): -EINVAL if user->fpsimd_size != sizeof(struct fpsimd_context), -EFAULT if the user copy fails, otherwise 0 after clearing TIF_SVE, clearing SVCR.SM, setting fp_type to FP_STATE_FPSIMD and calling fpsimd_update_current_state (TIF_SME is not touched); (6) -EINVAL if user->sve_size < SVE_SIG_CONTEXT_SIZE(vq); (7) if sm, -ENOMEM when sme_alloc(current, false) leaves thread.sme_state NULL (no flag change); (8) -ENOMEM when sve_alloc(current, true) leaves thread.sve_state NULL, after clearing TIF_SVE (a sme_state obtained at step 7 is left in place); (9) after this point thread state is changed: if sm, SVCR.SM is set and TIF_SME set (TIF_SVE not cleared); otherwise SVCR.SM is cleared and TIF_SVE set (TIF_SME not cleared); fp_type is set to FP_STATE_SVE in both cases; then -EFAULT if the copy of SVE_SIG_REGS_SIZE(vq) bytes into thread.sve_state fails (the payload may be partially copied); then the error of read_fpsimd_context (-EINVAL if user->fpsimd_size != sizeof(struct fpsimd_context), -EFAULT on copy failure), with the earlier changes kept; (10) otherwise fpsimd_update_current_state is called to merge the FPSIMD registers into the SVE state and it returns 0. sme_alloc and sve_alloc may reuse an existing buffer; no locks are taken and no references acquired.
note: Reviewer round 15 (fp_type should be FP_STATE_SME when SM set) is wrong: signal.c:517 sets FP_STATE_SVE unconditionally after the sm branch. Round 2 (newly allocated/zeroed) is wrong about the prose, which already says buffers may be reused. Original (other TIF flag not cleared) is right and already stated: 247-253. Slice cut the tail; read real file arch/arm64/kernel/signal.c:430-527, restore_fpsimd_context 316-333, read_fpsimd_context 298-314.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE6(aarch32_pread64, unsigned int, fd, char __user *, buf, size_t, count, u32, __pad, arg_u32p(pos))
