name: __kvm_find_s1_desc_level
prose: Function __kvm_find_s1_desc_level(vcpu, va, ipa, level) with level an int pointer; it walks the guest stage-1 page tables for va looking for the table whose IPA matches ipa. It sets the translation regime to TR_EL20 or TR_EL2 (depending on vcpu_el2_e2h_is_set) if is_hyp_ctxt(vcpu), else TR_EL10, and calls setup_s1_walk. Return paths: (1) it returns the nonzero result of setup_s1_walk without touching *level; (2) if the walk result level is S1_MMU_DISABLED it warns once, sets *level = 0 and returns 0; (3) otherwise it runs walk_s1 inside scoped_guard(srcu, &vcpu->kvm->srcu), which takes the SRCU read lock on vcpu->kvm->srcu and releases it when the guarded statement ends; then if walk_s1 returned -EINTR (the match_s1_desc filter found a table with the wanted IPA) it sets *level = the matched level and returns 0; if walk_s1 returned 0 (walk completed with no match) it returns -ENOENT with *level unchanged; any other walk_s1 result is returned unchanged with *level unchanged.
note: Slice cut the head: the real name is __kvm_find_s1_desc_level (at.c:1562, level is int *, not u8 * as the old prose said). Old claim that the caller must not hold the SRCU lock removed: nothing in the code checks it. Match callback match_s1_desc at at.c:1546-1560 returns 0 on mismatch and -EINTR with the level on match.

name: check_all_fgt_masks
prose: Static __init function taking an int ret (an error code accumulated by earlier initialisation). It calls check_fgt_masks on each of the eleven FGT mask sets in its table (hfgrtr, hfgwtr, hfgitr, hdfgrtr, hdfgwtr, hafgrtr, hfgrtr2, hfgwtr2, hfgitr2, hdfgrtr2, hdfgwtr2), with no early exit regardless of ret or of earlier results. Each check_fgt_masks call logs an error per bit set in both the mask and nmask of that set (and then yields -EINVAL), recomputes that set res0 as ~(mask | nmask), and logs an info line if the new res0 differs from the old. The single return is ret ?: err: it returns ret if ret is non-zero, otherwise err, the bitwise OR of the eleven results, which is 0 or -EINVAL.
note: Contract cleared: the function mutates global mask structures and logs, so a result-only contract is incomplete (reviewers rounds 1-15 flagged that EINVAL was missing from the contract). Return expression at emulate-nested.c:2224 (slice 245); check_fgt_masks at 2180-2203 returns only 0 or -EINVAL.

name: kvm_vm_ioctl_mte_copy_tags
prose: Function taking kvm and copy_tags (guest_ipa, length, addr, flags, reserved). write is true when KVM_ARM_TAGS_FROM_GUEST is not set in flags, i.e. tags are written into the guest. Return paths before the lock: -EINVAL if kvm_has_mte(kvm) is false, if reserved[0] or reserved[1] is non-zero, if flags has bits other than KVM_ARM_TAGS_FROM_GUEST, if length or guest_ipa is not page-aligned, or if length > INT_MAX. It then takes kvm->slots_lock; every later exit goes through the out label, which releases that lock. With the lock held: if write and kvm->nr_memslots_dirty_logging is non-zero it sets ret = -EBUSY. Otherwise it loops one page at a time while length > 0: if __gfn_to_page returns NULL, or the page is not an online page (ZONE_DEVICE; the page is released unused), ret = -EFAULT and it leaves the loop; for a read it copies the page tags to the user buffer (or zeroes the user buffer if the page has no tags) and releases the page clean; for a write it copies tags from the user buffer into the page, clears the page tags if that copy was short, marks the page tagged and releases it dirty; if the number of tags copied is not MTE_GRANULES_PER_PAGE it sets ret = -EFAULT and leaves the loop; otherwise it advances gfn and the tag pointer and reduces length by PAGE_SIZE. At out, after unlocking: if length differs from the original copy_tags->length it returns copy_tags->length - length (the bytes of completed pages, positive; this is also what is returned, rather than 0, when every page was processed and copy_tags->length is non-zero); otherwise it returns ret, which is 0 only when copy_tags->length was 0, and is -EBUSY or -EFAULT if the failure happened before any page completed.
note: Reviewer round 15 is right: on full completion length reaches 0, so the check at guest.c:1080 returns copy_tags->length, not 0; old prose was wrong. Slice cut the head; read guest.c:975-1081. No lock is held on the -EINVAL early returns (lines 985-998).

name: __sysreg_restore_el1_state
prose: Static inline function taking ctxt, midr and mpidr; it returns nothing and takes no locks. It writes midr to VPIDR_EL2 and mpidr to VMPIDR_EL2. Then, depending on the first condition that holds: (a) if has_vhe() or the ARM64_WORKAROUND_SPECULATIVE_AT capability is not set, it writes SCTLR_EL1 and TCR_EL1 from ctxt; (b) otherwise, if ctxt->__hyp_running_vcpu is NULL, it writes TCR_EL1 from ctxt with TCR_EPD1_MASK and TCR_EPD0_MASK also set and then executes isb(); SCTLR_EL1 is not written, and this function does not later write TCR_EL1 in this case; (c) otherwise (non-VHE, workaround present, __hyp_running_vcpu non-NULL) neither is written yet. It then writes CPACR_EL1, TTBR0_EL1 and TTBR1_EL1 from ctxt; if ctxt_has_tcrx(ctxt) it writes TCR2_EL1, and within that also PIR_EL1 and PIRE0_EL1 if ctxt_has_s1pie(ctxt) and POR_EL1 if ctxt_has_s1poe(ctxt); it then writes ESR_EL1, AFSR0_EL1, AFSR1_EL1, FAR_EL1, MAIR_EL1, VBAR_EL1, CONTEXTIDR_EL1, AMAIR_EL1, CNTKCTL_EL1, PAR_EL1 and TPIDR_EL1 from ctxt; it writes TFSR_EL1 and TFSRE0_EL1 if ctxt_has_mte(ctxt), and, in case (c) only, executes isb(), writes SCTLR_EL1, executes isb() and writes TCR_EL1 from ctxt. Finally it writes SP_EL1, ELR_EL1 and SPSR_EL1 from ctxt and SCTLR2_EL1 if ctxt_has_sctlr2(ctxt).
note: Reviewer round 15 right: in case (b) the TCR write comes before the isb (sysreg-sr.h:227-230); old prose said after. Original rejection (SCTLR/TCR not always restored) was already reflected in the old prose. Slice cut the tail; the rest (MTE, final isb block, SP/ELR/SPSR/SCTLR2) was read from the real sysreg-sr.h after line 258.

name: host_stage2_adjust_range
prose: Static function taking addr and a struct kvm_mem_range pointer range; the caller must hold host_mmu.lock (hyp_assert_lock_held). It looks up the leaf entry for addr in the host stage-2 table with kvm_pgtable_get_leaf, giving pte and level. Return paths: (1) the error returned by kvm_pgtable_get_leaf, if non-zero; (2) -EAGAIN if kvm_pte_valid(pte); (3) -EPERM if pte is non-zero but not valid (with a WARN_ON if addr_is_memory(addr) and its host page state is not PKVM_NOPAGE); (4) with pte zero, it walks levels from the leaf level up to KVM_PGTABLE_LAST_LEVEL (towards smaller granules), skipping levels that do not support block mapping; for each candidate it forms the granule-aligned range containing addr, and if that range is not included in the input *range and the level is not the last level it tries the next level, otherwise it stores that range in *range and returns 0 (so the first, largest, candidate contained in the input range is chosen, and at the last level the candidate is taken even if it extends beyond the input range); (5) if the loop ends without choosing a level (only possible when no level from the leaf level through the last level supports block mapping, including the last level) it issues WARN_ON(1) and returns -EINVAL. *range is written only in the success case at (4).
note: Slice cut the head; read mem_protect.c:491-535. Old claim that *range is unchanged on every error path holds (only write is the success assignment at slice line 18). Original reviewer point (smallest vs largest, last level may exceed range) is right for the last-level case and is now stated; wording about direction of levels corrected.

name: host_stage2_idmap_locked
prose: Function taking addr, size and prot; the caller must hold host_mmu.lock. It returns the value of host_stage2_try(__host_stage2_idmap, addr, addr + size, prot): the macro asserts the lock is held, calls __host_stage2_idmap (kvm_pgtable_stage2_map of the identity mapping for [addr, addr + size) with prot, using host_s2_pool), and if that returns -ENOMEM it calls host_stage2_unmap_dev_all and, if that returns 0, calls __host_stage2_idmap once more. The result is 0 on success or the negative error code of the last step tried. It takes and releases no lock.
note: Callee host_stage2_try macro read at mem_protect.c:468-482; the retry on -ENOMEM was missing from the old prose, otherwise the old iff-zero statement is correct.

name: host_stage2_set_owner_locked
prose: Function taking addr, size and owner_id; the caller must hold host_mmu.lock. Return paths: (1) -EPERM if range_is_memory(addr, addr + size) is false, with no change made; (2) the non-zero result of host_stage2_try(kvm_pgtable_stage2_set_owner, &host_mmu.pgt, addr, size, &host_s2_pool, owner_id), returned without changing the vmemmap host page state (host_stage2_try retries once after host_stage2_unmap_dev_all if the first attempt returned -ENOMEM); (3) otherwise it sets the host page state of every page in [addr, addr + size) to PKVM_PAGE_OWNED if owner_id == PKVM_ID_HOST and to PKVM_NOPAGE for any other owner_id, and returns 0. It takes and releases no lock.
note: Old prose accurate; added the -ENOMEM retry in host_stage2_try. mem_protect.c slice lines 39-58.

name: host_stage2_force_pte_cb
prose: Static function taking addr, end and prot, with no side effects; it reads the memory-region table through range_is_memory(addr, end). If range_is_memory(addr, end) is true it returns (prot != PKVM_HOST_MEM_PROT); otherwise it returns (prot != PKVM_HOST_MMIO_PROT). Thus it requests page-level mappings for any protection other than the default one for that kind of range.
note: Slice lines 60-80; single if/else with a return in each branch.

name: host_stage2_idmap
prose: Static function taking a fault address addr. Before taking any lock it calls find_mem_range(addr, &range): the return value being non-NULL selects prot = PKVM_HOST_MEM_PROT, otherwise PKVM_HOST_MMIO_PROT (range is filled in either way). It then calls host_lock_component(); if host_stage2_adjust_range(addr, &range) returns non-zero that value is the result (no mapping is made); otherwise the result is host_stage2_idmap_locked(range.start, range.end - range.start, prot), 0 or a negative error code. host_unlock_component() is called before the single return on both paths.
note: Old claim that the lock is taken on every path was imprecise (find_mem_range runs before the lock); both returns go through the unlock label (slice 91-100).

name: handle_host_mem_abort
prose: Function taking the host cpu context host_ctxt (not used in the body); it returns nothing. It reads ESR_EL2 and calls __get_fault_info(esr, &fault). Return paths: (1) if __get_fault_info returns false it returns immediately (treated as a raced page-table change) without mapping anything; (2) otherwise it hits BUG_ON if the HPFAR_EL2 NS bit is not set in fault.hpfar_el2, computes addr = FIELD_GET(HPFAR_EL2_FIPA, fault.hpfar_el2) << 12, calls host_stage2_idmap(addr), hits BUG_ON if that returns a non-zero value other than -EAGAIN, and returns normally when the result is 0 or -EAGAIN.
note: Slice 103-128; old prose consistent with the code, wording tightened.

name: __host_check_page_state_range
prose: Static function taking addr, size and an expected host page state. It first calls check_range_allowed_memory(addr, addr + size) and returns its non-zero result (-EINVAL if the range crosses a memory/MMIO range boundary, -EPERM if it is not memory or is MEMBLOCK_NOMAP). It then asserts host_mmu.lock is held (hyp_assert_lock_held) and checks the host state of each page in the range: it returns -EPERM at the first page whose host state differs from state, and returns 0 if all match. It modifies no state.
note: Slice 155-172; check_range_allowed_memory read at mem_protect.c:430-447.

name: __host_set_page_state_range
prose: Static function taking addr, size and a page state; the caller holds host_mmu.lock. If the host state of the first page (at addr only) is PKVM_NOPAGE it calls host_stage2_idmap_locked(addr, size, PKVM_HOST_MEM_PROT) and, if that returns non-zero, returns that error without changing any page state. Otherwise, or after the idmap succeeded, it sets the host state of every page in [addr, addr + size) to state and returns 0.
note: Slice 174-187; old prose correct.

name: __hyp_check_page_state_range
prose: Static function taking phys, size and an expected hyp page state. It examines the hyp state of each page in [phys, phys + size) in order, returns -EPERM at the first page whose state differs from state, and returns 0 if all pages match. It does not modify state and takes no lock.

name: guest_get_page_state
prose: Static function taking a stage-2 pte and addr (addr is not used). If kvm_pte_valid(pte) is false it returns PKVM_NOPAGE; otherwise it returns pkvm_getstate(kvm_pgtable_stage2_pte_prot(pte)). It has no side effects.

name: __pkvm_host_share_hyp
prose: Function taking a page frame number pfn; phys = hyp_pfn_to_phys(pfn), size = PAGE_SIZE. It takes the host component lock and then the hyp component lock, and both are released (hyp first, then host) before its single return. Return paths: (1) the non-zero result of __host_check_page_state_range(phys, size, PKVM_PAGE_OWNED), with nothing changed; (2) the non-zero result of __hyp_check_page_state_range(phys, size, PKVM_NOPAGE) (which is -EPERM), with nothing changed; (3) otherwise it sets the hyp state of the page to PKVM_PAGE_SHARED_BORROWED and calls __host_set_page_state_range(phys, size, PKVM_PAGE_SHARED_OWNED), wrapped in WARN_ON so a failure there only warns; it returns 0 in this case.
note: Slice 225-249. The old precondition that pfn maps allowed memory is not a precondition: a bad range makes the first check fail (-EINVAL or -EPERM from check_range_allowed_memory), so the return is not just 0 or -EPERM.

name: __pkvm_host_unshare_hyp
prose: Function taking a page frame number pfn; phys = hyp_pfn_to_phys(pfn), virt = __hyp_va(phys), size = PAGE_SIZE. It takes the host component lock and then the hyp component lock, and releases both (hyp first, then host) before its single return. Return paths, with no state changed on any of them: the non-zero result of __host_check_page_state_range(phys, size, PKVM_PAGE_SHARED_OWNED); the non-zero result of __hyp_check_page_state_range(phys, size, PKVM_PAGE_SHARED_BORROWED) (-EPERM); -EBUSY if hyp_page_count((void *)virt) is non-zero. Otherwise it sets the hyp state of the page to PKVM_NOPAGE and calls __host_set_page_state_range(phys, size, PKVM_PAGE_OWNED), wrapped in WARN_ON so a failure only warns, and returns 0.
note: Slice cut the tail; read real mem_protect.c:754-781. Old text presented the shared state as a precondition although the function checks it and returns an error.

name: hyp_create_idmap
prose: Function taking hyp_va_bits (the hypervisor VA width), with no failure path of its own. It sets start to the physical address of __hyp_idmap_text_start rounded down to PAGE_SIZE and end to that of __hyp_idmap_text_end rounded up to PAGE_SIZE. It then sets the global __io_map_base to BIT(hyp_va_bits - 2) if bit (hyp_va_bits - 2) of start is clear, and to 0 if that bit of start is set (start is masked with that bit and the result is inverted with XOR, so no other bit of start is kept), and sets the global __hyp_vmemmap to __io_map_base | BIT(hyp_va_bits - 3). It returns the result of __pkvm_create_mappings(start, end - start, start, PAGE_HYP_EXEC), which maps the idmap text at its physical address with executable hyp permissions under pkvm_pgd_lock and returns the error code of kvm_pgtable_hyp_map (0 on success, otherwise a negative error). The shifts are only well-defined if hyp_va_bits >= 3 and hyp_va_bits - 2 is less than the width of unsigned long.
note: Reviewer round 15 is right: the code masks start with BIT(hyp_va_bits - 2) before the XOR (mm.c slice lines 172-173), so __io_map_base is not start with a bit toggled; old prose wrong. Reviewer round 2 (IO and vmemmap placed in disjoint quarters) is moot: the prose does not say that, and the code uses the lower/upper half of one quarter per the comment at 164-171. __pkvm_create_mappings read at mm.c:35-44.

name: kvm_pgd_pages
prose: Static function taking ia_bits and start_level that returns the number of pages in the stage-2 or hyp PGD: it builds a local struct kvm_pgtable with those two fields and returns kvm_pgd_page_idx(&pgt, -1ULL) + 1, converted to u32. kvm_pgd_page_idx computes (addr & (BIT(ia_bits) - 1)) >> kvm_granule_shift(start_level - 1), so the result is (((BIT(ia_bits)) - 1) >> kvm_granule_shift(start_level - 1)) + 1 truncated to 32 bits. It has no side effects. The expression is only well-defined when ia_bits is less than 64 and kvm_granule_shift(start_level - 1) is less than 64 (the source comment says the shift may underflow; for 4K pages that excludes start_level values that give a level below -2).
note: Contract cleared: it depended on BIT and the granule-shift definition. Reviewer round 15 is right that start_level = -3 gives an out-of-range shift (granule shift of level -4 is 9*(4-(-4))+3 = 75 for 4K pages), so the old precondition [-3, 4] was wrong; the PAGE_SHIFT remark is also right since kvm_granule_shift includes it. Source pgtable.c:56-72 and kvm_granule_shift in asm/kvm_pgtable.h:154.

name: __vgic_v3_get_gic_config
prose: Function taking no arguments that returns a u64 describing the GIC CPU interface. Return paths: (1) if cpus_have_final_cap(ARM64_HAS_GICV5_CPUIF) is true it returns read_gicreg(ICH_VTR_EL2) unchanged (no masking and no bit 63 handling); (2) otherwise it reads ICC_SRE_EL1 into sre; on VHE it saves the interrupt mask state with local_daif_save, on nVHE it sets HCR_AMO, HCR_FMO and HCR_IMO with sysreg_clear_set_hcr and executes isb; it writes 0 to ICC_SRE_EL1, isb, reads ICC_SRE_EL1 back into val, writes sre back to ICC_SRE_EL1, isb; on VHE it restores the saved mask state with local_daif_restore, on nVHE it clears HCR_AMO, HCR_FMO and HCR_IMO (regardless of whether they were set before the function ran) and executes isb; it then returns (val has ICC_SRE_EL1_SRE set ? 0 : (1ULL << 63)) OR read_gicreg(ICH_VTR_EL2), so bit 63 is set exactly when SRE read back as clear, and the other bits are those read from ICH_VTR_EL2 (documented as bits 31:0, with RES0 above). ICC_SRE_EL1 is restored to its entry value on the non-GICv5 path.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the GICv5 return at vgic-v3-sr.c slice line 183 is the raw ICH_VTR_EL2 read, so old claim that bit 63 is clear was unsupported. Reviewer round 2 (nVHE uses set via sysreg_clear_set_hcr) is already what the old prose said (set then clear); not an error in the prose. New wording also removes the claim that interrupt-mask state is left as on entry for nVHE: HCR bits are cleared, not restored (slice 221).

name: TRACE_EVENT(kvm_wfx_arm64, TP_PROTO(unsigned long vcpu_pc, bool is_wfe), TP_ARGS(vcpu_pc, is_wfe)
prose: Generated tracepoint function trace_kvm_wfx_arm64(vcpu_pc, is_wfe), produced by TRACE_EVENT in trace_handle_exit.h (the body is the generic tracepoint stub, not hand-written). It returns nothing. If the tracepoint has been enabled (a probe is registered) the stub calls the registered probes with vcpu_pc and is_wfe; the trace-event probe then copies those two values into a trace record using the TP_fast_assign block (vcpu_pc and is_wfe), and the record text is formatted later as "guest executed wf%c at: 0x%016lx" with e for wfe and i for wfi. When the tracepoint is not enabled it does nothing. The arguments are passed by value and are not otherwise validated.
note: Macro-generated function: real name does not occur literally in the source, so name is the macro invocation head (trace_handle_exit.h:11-13). Old prose said it copies into the buffer whenever enabled; recording is done by the probe, stated now.

name: TRACE_EVENT(kvm_hvc_arm64, TP_PROTO(unsigned long vcpu_pc, unsigned long r0, unsigned long imm), TP_ARGS(vcpu_pc, r0, imm)
prose: Generated tracepoint function trace_kvm_hvc_arm64(vcpu_pc, r0, imm), produced by TRACE_EVENT in trace_handle_exit.h. It returns nothing. If the tracepoint is enabled the stub calls the registered probes with the three values and the trace-event probe copies vcpu_pc, r0 and imm into a trace record (TP_fast_assign), later formatted as "HVC at 0x%016lx (r0: 0x%016lx, imm: 0x%lx)". When the tracepoint is not enabled it does nothing. The arguments are passed by value.
note: Macro-generated; trace_handle_exit.h:29-47.

name: TRACE_EVENT(kvm_arm_set_dreg32, TP_PROTO(const char *name, __u64 value), TP_ARGS(name, value)
prose: Generated tracepoint function trace_kvm_arm_set_dreg32(name, value), produced by TRACE_EVENT in trace_handle_exit.h. It returns nothing. If the tracepoint is enabled the stub calls the registered probes and the trace-event probe stores the name pointer itself (the string is not copied) and the 64-bit value in a trace record; the record is formatted later as "%s: 0x%llx", so the string behind name must still be valid when the record is printed. When not enabled it does nothing.
note: Macro-generated; trace_handle_exit.h:53-68 (the comment there notes the dreg32 name is historic and the value is 64 bit).

name: TRACE_EVENT(kvm_handle_sys_reg, TP_PROTO(unsigned long hsr), TP_ARGS(hsr)
prose: Generated tracepoint function trace_kvm_handle_sys_reg(hsr), produced by TRACE_EVENT in trace_handle_exit.h. It returns nothing. If the tracepoint is enabled the stub calls the registered probes and the trace-event probe copies hsr into a trace record, formatted later as "HSR 0x%08lx". When not enabled it does nothing.

name: vgic_v2_populate_lr
prose: Function taking vcpu, an irq and an LR index lr; the caller must hold irq->irq_lock (stated in the comment above it) and lr must be a valid index of vcpu->arch.vgic_cpu.vgic_v2.vgic_lr. It builds val starting from irq->intid and then: if irq->active, sets the active bit, for an SGI also puts irq->active_source into the source-CPU field, and for a multi-source SGI sets the EOI bit and forbids the pending bit; sets the group-1 bit if irq->group; if irq->hw and the IRQ does not need resampling it sets the HW bit and puts irq->hwintid in the physical-ID field, and forbids the pending bit when the IRQ is active; otherwise (not HW, or HW needing resampling) it sets the EOI bit if irq->config is VGIC_CONFIG_LEVEL and, for an active level IRQ, forbids the pending bit. Hence a mapped HW level IRQ that needs no resampling does not get the EOI bit from this step. If the pending bit is allowed and irq_is_pending(irq): it sets the pending bit; for an edge IRQ it clears irq->pending_latch; for an SGI it takes src = ffs(irq->source) and, if src is 0, emits a rate-limited warning and returns without writing vgic_lr[lr] (pending_latch of an edge IRQ has already been cleared at that point), otherwise puts src - 1 in the source-CPU field, clears that bit of irq->source and, if other source bits remain, sets irq->pending_latch again and sets the EOI bit. If the IRQ is a mapped level IRQ and the pending bit was set it clears irq->line_level. It then ORs in (irq->priority >> 3) at the priority position and stores val into vgic_lr[lr]. The only other return is the early one above; there is no error value.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: EOI is set for a level IRQ only in the non-HW-or-resampled branch (vgic-v2.c slice 150-153), so mapped HW level IRQs without resampling get none; old prose wrong. Round 2 (pending_latch re-set when sources remain) already stated in old prose and kept. Original (early return leaves lr unwritten) already stated. Slice 122-198.

name: early_pgtable_alloc
prose: Static __init function taking a page-table type argument that it does not use; it is for early boot allocation of a page-table page. It calls memblock_phys_alloc_range(PAGE_SIZE, PAGE_SIZE, 0, MEMBLOCK_ALLOC_NOLEAKTRACE) for one page. If that returns 0 it calls panic("Failed to allocate page table page"). Otherwise it returns the physical address that memblock returned (non-zero; the allocation was requested with PAGE_SIZE alignment). The page is not zeroed or otherwise written by this function. The only return is the final return phys.
note: Contract cleared: it depends on memblock global state (reviewers rounds 2 and 15 both complained about the contract). Panic path relies on panic() not returning. Slice lines 115-125.

name: note_page
prose: Callback of the arm64 page-table dumper taking the ptdump_state pointer pt_st, the start address addr of the next entry, its level and its raw entry value val; it returns nothing and takes no lock. The state st is the containing struct ptdump_pg_state (it must be initialised, with st->level == -1 meaning no range has been started yet; st->marker must have a valid element [1] to compare against; st->seq is passed unchanged to the print helpers, which are called whether or not it is NULL). Steps: if st->mm is set and (level == 1 and mm_p4d_folded(st->mm)) or (level == 2 and mm_pud_folded(st->mm)), level is changed to 0. prot is val & pg_level[level].mask when level >= 0 and 0 when level is negative (negative level, for example the -1 used to flush the last range, is allowed and does not index pg_level for the new entry). Then: (a) if st->level == -1 it records level, prot and addr as the current range and prints the header "---[ <marker name> ]---" for the current marker; (b) otherwise, if prot != st->current_prot, level != st->level or addr >= st->marker[1].start_address, it closes the current range: if st->current_prot is non-zero it calls note_prot_uxn and note_prot_wx (each does nothing unless st->check_wx is set; they may emit a one-time warning and add (addr - st->start_address) / PAGE_SIZE to st->uxn_pages or st->wx_pages when the old protection lacks UXN, or is not read-only and not PXN respectively); it prints the range start-addr, its size in K/M/G/T/P/E units and the name of pg_level[st->level], plus the protection bit names when st->current_prot is non-zero and that level has bits, then a newline; if addr >= st->marker[1].start_address it advances st->marker by one and prints the new marker header; finally it records addr, prot and level as the new current range; (c) if neither branch applies nothing is recorded. After (a), (b) or (c), if addr >= st->marker[1].start_address (re-evaluated) it advances st->marker by one more and prints the new marker header. So st->marker is advanced at most twice per call (at most once in cases (a) and (c)), even if addr lies beyond several marker boundaries.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: level < 0 is accepted (prot = 0, ptdump.c:204-205), so old precondition level >= 0 was wrong. Rounds 1 and 2 (marker advances at most twice per call, not for every boundary) already reflected in old prose and kept. note_prot_uxn/wx read at ptdump.c:160-189. Slice cut the head (function begins at slice line 191).

name: bpf_arch_text_poke
prose: Function bpf_arch_text_poke(ip, poke_type, old_addr, new_addr) that replaces the branch (or NOP) at ip that targets old_addr by one that targets new_addr (a NULL address means a NOP). Flow and returns: (1) if bpf_address_lookup(ip) fails it returns -ENOTSUPP (only bpf text can be poked); (2) offset == 0 means ip is the bpf prog entry: then plt is set to image + size - PLT_TARGET_OFFSET and ip is moved to the NOP slot at image + POKE_OFFSET instructions; (3) if either target is a long jump (more than 128MB from ip, NULL not counted) and ip is not the prog entry it WARNs and returns -EINVAL; (4) the branch type is link for BPF_MOD_CALL and non-link for any other poke_type; (5) it generates the old and new instructions with gen_branch_or_nop (a long jump is routed through plt) and returns -EFAULT if either generation fails; (6) plt_target is new_addr if the new target is a long jump, else &dummy_tramp if the old target is a long jump, else stays 0; only if plt_target is non-zero it makes the plt page writable (returning -EFAULT if set_memory_rw fails), writes plt->target with WRITE_ONCE and sets the page read-only again; this plt update happens before the instruction comparison below, so it can occur even when the function then returns 0 without patching; (7) if old_insn == new_insn it returns 0 without patching; (8) it takes text_mutex, reads the instruction at ip with aarch64_insn_read (any failure gives ret = -EFAULT), sets ret = -EFAULT if it differs from old_insn, otherwise ret = aarch64_insn_patch_text_nosync(ip, new_insn), then releases text_mutex and returns ret. text_mutex is held only in step (8) and released on both of its exits.
note: Reviewer round 15 right on both points: the plt may be rewritten before the old_insn == new_insn early return (bpf_jit_comp.c slice 51-71), and the plt write is only done when plt_target is non-zero (a long jump is involved), not for every bpf prog. Slice cut the head; name and locals read at bpf_jit_comp.c:2934-2956. is_long_jump/gen_branch_or_nop read at 2834-2863.

name: build_prologue
prose: Static function build_prologue(ctx, ebpf_from_cbpf) that emits the JIT prologue into ctx (ctx->prog is the program, ctx->idx the next instruction index; with ctx->image NULL the emit calls only advance the count). It sets is_main_prog = !bpf_is_subprog(prog), emits the KCFI hash for the main or subprog variant, notes idx0 = ctx->idx, then emits a BTI_JC landing pad, MOV x9, LR and a NOP. If prog->aux->exception_cb is false: it emits PACIASP when CONFIG_ARM64_PTR_AUTH_KERNEL is enabled, pushes FP and LR, sets FP = SP, calls prepare_bpf_tail_call_cnt, and if the program is not from cBPF and is a main program it computes cur_offset = ctx->idx - idx0 and, when that differs from PROLOGUE_OFFSET, prints pr_err_once and returns -1 immediately (ctx->idx stays at that point, ctx->stack_size is not yet set); otherwise in that case it emits a BTI_J pad; then it calls push_callee_regs. If exception_cb is true: it emits FP = x2 (the main program FP), SP = FP - 96, and sets ctx->fp_used = true. Then it sets ctx->stack_size = round_up(prog->aux->stack_depth, 16). If ctx->fp_used: with ctx->priv_sp_used it loads the private stack pointer (prog->aux->priv_stack_ptr + PRIV_STACK_GUARD_SZ plus the per-cpu offset) into the private-SP register and sets the BPF FP register to that plus ctx->stack_size, otherwise it sets the BPF FP register to SP. If ctx->stack_size is non-zero and ctx->priv_sp_used is false it emits SP = SP - ctx->stack_size. If ctx->arena_vm_start is non-zero it emits a load of that value into the arena base register. It then returns 0. The only return values are -1 (the PROLOGUE_OFFSET mismatch) and 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the FP/private-stack setup is guarded by ctx->fp_used (bpf_jit_comp.c slice 81-91) and the SP adjustment by stack_size and !priv_sp_used (94-95), while the old prose said they are done unconditionally. Slice cut the head; head read at bpf_jit_comp.c:511-535. Old statement that fp_used is set to true is only for the exception-callback case; kept.

name: csky_alignment
prose: Function csky_alignment(regs), the csky ABIv1 handler for a misaligned load/store fault; it returns nothing. It first picks the user or kernel path: for a user-mode fault it prints an error and goes to bad_area if align_usr_enable is zero, otherwise increments align_usr_count and reads the 16-bit instruction at the user instruction pointer with get_user, going to bad_area (after an error print) if that fails; for a kernel-mode fault it prints an error and goes to bad_area if align_kern_enable is zero, otherwise increments align_kern_count and reads the instruction directly. It then decodes rx (bits 3:0), imm (7:4), rz (11:8) and the opcode (bits 15:12); if rx or rz is 0 or 1 it goes to bad_area. For opcode OP_LDH, OP_LDW, OP_STH or OP_STW it computes addr = register rx + (imm << 1) for the halfword forms or + (imm << 2) for the word forms and calls ldh_c, ldw_c, sth_c or stw_c with rz and addr; for any other opcode the switch does nothing and ret is not assigned before the following test. If ret is non-zero it goes to bad_area; otherwise it advances regs->pc by 2 and returns. At bad_area: for a kernel-mode fault, if fixup_exception(regs) succeeds it returns; otherwise it prints the alert, shows the registers and calls make_task_dead(SIGKILL) (not expected to return). For a user-mode fault it calls force_sig_fault(SIGBUS, BUS_ADRALN, addr), where addr is 0 if bad_area was reached before an address was computed; regs->pc is not advanced.
note: The listed name do_alignment does not exist: slice cut the head and the real function is csky_alignment (abiv1/alignment.c:213). Fixed under the real name. Observation: ret is declared without an initialiser (line 214) and is only set by the four opcode cases (slice 9-26).

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add, +)
prose: Generated function arch_atomic_fetch_add_relaxed(int i, atomic_t *v) (static __always_inline, produced by ATOMIC_FETCH_OP(add) inside ATOMIC_OPS(add, +); this definition is in the CONFIG_SMP branch of the header). It runs an inline-assembly load-exclusive/store-exclusive loop on v->counter: ldex.w loads the current value, the old value is copied to the return register, add i to the loaded value, stex.w stores it, and the loop repeats until the store-exclusive succeeds. It returns the value v->counter had before the successful update and leaves v->counter equal to that value plus i (32-bit addition). No barrier instruction is emitted other than the asm memory clobber (relaxed ordering), and no lock or reference is taken.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add, +)
prose: Generated function arch_atomic_add_return_relaxed(int i, atomic_t *v) (static __always_inline, produced by ATOMIC_OP_RETURN(add, +) inside ATOMIC_OPS(add, +); CONFIG_SMP branch). Its single statement returns arch_atomic_fetch_add_relaxed(i, v) + i. So v->counter is updated by that fetch-and-add LL/SC loop (relaxed ordering), and the return value is the value the counter held before the update plus i, the int sum computed after the update from the fetched old value; no lock or reference is taken.
note: Macro-generated, atomic.h:62-67 and 76. Old prose described the update correctly but not that the returned value is derived from the fetched old value rather than re-read.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(and)
prose: Generated function arch_atomic_fetch_and_relaxed(int i, atomic_t *v) (static __always_inline, produced by ATOMIC_FETCH_OP(and) inside the single-argument ATOMIC_OPS(and); CONFIG_SMP branch). It runs an inline-assembly load-exclusive/store-exclusive loop: ldex.w loads v->counter, the old value is kept for return, and the loaded value is ANDed with i and written back with stex.w, repeating until the store-exclusive succeeds. It returns the previous value of v->counter and leaves v->counter equal to previous AND i. Ordering is relaxed (only an asm memory clobber) and no lock or reference is taken.

name: kprobe_ftrace_handler
prose: Ftrace callback for kprobes on csky, called with preemption disabled (stated by the comment on the function); arguments ip, parent_ip, ops and fregs, returns nothing. Returns and flow: (1) if kprobe_ftrace_disabled is set it returns immediately; (2) if ftrace_test_recursion_trylock(ip, parent_ip) returns a negative value it returns immediately; neither of these touches the recursion lock or per-cpu probe state. (3) Otherwise it holds the recursion lock until the single exit at the out label, where ftrace_test_recursion_unlock is called. It gets regs from fregs and looks up a kprobe at ip; if none, it looks up one at ip - MCOUNT_INSN_SIZE; if that lookup finds none, or the probe found there is disabled, it goes to out without changing anything else; if it found one there, it will use ip - MCOUNT_INSN_SIZE as the probe address (lr_saver). A probe found directly at ip is not checked for being disabled. (4) With probe p found, if kprobe_running() is true on this cpu it only calls kprobes_inc_nmissed_count(p), i.e. increments the missed count of the newly found probe p (not of the running one), leaves current_kprobe unchanged, and goes to out. (5) Otherwise it saves the current instruction pointer as orig_ip, sets the instruction pointer to ip (reduced when lr_saver), stores p in the per-cpu current_kprobe and sets the control block status to KPROBE_HIT_ACTIVE; if p has no pre_handler or the pre_handler returns 0, it sets the instruction pointer to p->addr + MCOUNT_INSN_SIZE, and if p has a post_handler it sets the status to KPROBE_HIT_SSDONE and calls it with the value 0, then restores the instruction pointer to orig_ip; if the pre_handler returns non-zero the post_handler is not called and the instruction pointer is left as the pre_handler set it. In every case of step (5) current_kprobe is then set to NULL before reaching out.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the missed count goes to p, the probe found for this ip, not to an already-running kprobe (ftrace.c slice line 33); old prose wrong. Round 2 (disabled check) is wrong about the prose: the prose already limited the disabled test to the ip - MCOUNT_INSN_SIZE probe, matching line 26. Original-rejection (current_kprobe not NULL on the missed and no-probe paths) is already what the old prose said (unchanged). Slice 6-63.

name: __clear_user
prose: Function __clear_user(to, n), written as one inline-assembly block, that zeroes n bytes of user memory starting at to. The caller must have checked the range with access_ok (stated in the comment above it; the function does not check). It returns the value left in the n register, which the comment describes as the number of bytes not cleared. Behaviour: if to is 0 it jumps to the end and returns n unchanged without writing anything; if n is 0 it returns 0; if to is not 4-byte aligned it clears byte by byte; if to is 4-byte aligned it first clears 32-byte blocks (eight word stores, n reduced by 32 only after the eight stores), then 4-byte words (n reduced by 4 after each store), then the remaining bytes (n reduced by 1 after each store). A fault on any of the user stores is redirected through the exception table to label 9, and n then holds the count as of the last completed block, word or byte step, so it includes any words of the faulting 32-byte block that were already zeroed; if all stores succeed it returns 0 and all n bytes at to are zero.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the count is decremented only after a whole 32-byte block, word or byte store sequence (usercopy.c slice 8:-16: and the subi after them), so after a fault inside a block the returned n counts words that were already written; the old prose said bytes before the fault are zeroed and the rest are the return value, which is not exact. Not claimed: what the code does after label 9 depends on the condition flag, so the prose only says n is returned as left in the register.

name: cache_wbinv_range
prose: Function cache_wbinv_range(start, end) for the csky v2 cache; it returns nothing. It calls dcache_wb_range(start, end) and then icache_inv_range(start, end). dcache_wb_range rounds start down to an L1_CACHE_BYTES boundary and, for each line address i from there while i < end, issues dcache.cval1 on i (write back the data line), then sync_is(). icache_inv_range depends on the configuration: with CONFIG_CPU_HAS_ICACHE_INS it loops the same way issuing icache.iva per line and then sync_is(), with no lock; without it, it builds a range parameter and, if irqs_disabled() is true, calls local_icache_inv_range directly (only the calling CPU invalidates), otherwise it calls on_each_cpu(local_icache_inv_range, &param, 1) so that every online CPU invalidates and the call waits for completion; local_icache_inv_range takes cache_lock with spin_lock_irqsave while it does the cr22/cr17 line operations for the range, releases it, and calls sync_is(). The loops operate on lines that start at the line containing start and stop when the line address reaches end, so when start is greater than end they do no line operation only if the line address of start is not below end; if start and end fall in the same cache line one line operation is still done.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: start > end can still operate on one line when both are in the same cache line (loop starts at start rounded down, cachev2.c:80-86). Round 1 (lock in fallback) already in the old prose. Round 2 (on_each_cpu when irqs disabled) is wrong against the prose: the old text and the code both call the local function directly when irqs are disabled (cachev2.c:57-63). Slice contained only cache_wbinv_range; callees read in the real file lines 20-93.

name: tcm_setup_pool
prose: Static __init function with no arguments. It computes pool_size and tcm_pool_start from the TCM page counts and the linker symbols (different expressions under CONFIG_HAVE_DTCM), then sets the global tcm_pool to gen_pool_create(2, -1) (minimum allocation order 2, any node) without checking the result for NULL, and calls gen_pool_add(tcm_pool, tcm_pool_start, pool_size, -1). Return paths: (1) if gen_pool_add returns non-zero it prints an error with pr_err and returns that value (gen_pool_add reports -ENOMEM on allocation failure), with tcm_pool already created but without the region; (2) otherwise it prints an info line with the size and start address and returns 0. If gen_pool_create returned NULL, the following gen_pool_add call would use a NULL pool; this function does not handle that case.

Reviewer round 2 (the old text claimed -EINVAL for NULL) is partly right: the code does not check NULL (tcm.c slice 147-149); the old prose already said the NULL return is not checked. Precondition about tcm_mapping_init removed: nothing in this function enforces or uses it.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE0(rt_sigreturn)
prose: Generated syscall function sys_rt_sigreturn (hexagon, no arguments), defined by SYSCALL_DEFINE0(rt_sigreturn). It takes regs = current_pt_regs(), sets current->restart_block.fn = do_no_restart_syscall, and takes frame = the user stack pointer pt_psp(regs) as a struct rt_sigframe pointer. It goes to badframe if access_ok(frame, sizeof(*frame)) fails or if copying the saved signal mask frame->uc.uc_sigmask from user space fails. Otherwise it installs that mask with set_current_blocked (this happens before the register context is restored, so the new mask stays installed on any later failure), then calls restore_sigcontext(regs, &frame->uc.uc_mcontext), which copies the saved registers from user space into regs and returns non-zero on a copy error (regs may already be partly overwritten) and the function then goes to badframe; then sets pt_psp(regs) = regs->r29, sets regs->syscall_nr = -1, and goes to badframe if restore_altstack(&frame->uc.uc_stack) fails (the changes above are not undone). On success it returns regs->r00. At badframe it calls force_sig(SIGSEGV) and returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: set_current_blocked runs before restore_sigcontext (signal.c:238-241) and nothing undoes it on failure; old prose implied the badframe path restores nothing else. The slice cut the tail; badframe read in the real file (signal.c:253-256). Name is the SYSCALL_DEFINE0 invocation since the generated name sys_rt_sigreturn does not occur literally.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add, i, add, +)
prose: Generated function arch_atomic_add(int i, atomic_t *v) (static inline, produced by ATOMIC_OP(add, i, add) inside ATOMIC_OPS(add, i, add, +)). It executes a single amadd.w instruction on v->counter with $zero as the destination, so the 32-bit add of i is atomic and the old value is discarded; it is the plain (non-_db, relaxed) form with only the compiler memory clobber, not a full-barrier instruction. It returns nothing and takes no lock or reference.

Name is the file-level macro invocation (atomic.h:82).

name: init_cpu_fullname
prose: Static __init function with no arguments, registered with arch_initcall. It calls of_property_read_string(of_root, "model", &model). If that returns 0 it makes a copy with kstrdup(model, GFP_KERNEL); if the copy fails it returns -ENOMEM at once, changing nothing. Otherwise it stores strsep(&cpuname, " ") in loongson_sysconf.cpuname: that is the start of the copy, truncated at the first space character (the string is empty if the model starts with a space); the allocation is not freed and stays reachable through loongson_sysconf.cpuname, while any earlier value of that field is overwritten. If of_property_read_string returned non-zero nothing of this is done. In every case that does not return -ENOMEM it then checks loongson_sysconf.cpuname (the new or the pre-existing value): if it is non-NULL and its first 8 characters are "Loongson", it sets __cpu_full_name[cpu] to that pointer for each cpu from 0 to NR_CPUS - 1. It then returns 0. Return values are only -ENOMEM and 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 right on both points: strsep returns the original start of the allocation, so the pointer is kept and nothing is leaked (env.c slice 49-52), and the Loongson check and __cpu_full_name loop (55-58) run even when the model property could not be read, so old text saying nothing changes and 0 is returned was wrong. Round 2 (strsep splits only on a space; allocation leaked) is right about the space and wrong about the leak. Round 1 (side effect on __cpu_full_name) is already in the old prose.

name: pv_send_ipi_mask
prose: Static function taking a cpumask pointer mask and an IPI action number; it returns nothing. It returns at once if mask is empty. If action is ACTION_BOOT_CPU it calls native_ops.send_ipi_mask(mask, action) and returns, setting no message bits and issuing no hypercall. Otherwise action becomes BIT(action) (so the action number must be a valid bit position) and for each CPU i in mask it atomically ORs that bit into the per-CPU irq_stat message word with atomic_fetch_or; if the previous message word was non-zero (any bit, not only this action) the CPU is skipped, the bit having already been ORed in and no hypercall being queued for it. For each other CPU it takes the hardware id cpu = cpu_logical_map(i) and adds it to a 128-bit bitmap (KVM_IPI_CLUSTER_SIZE = 2 * BITS_PER_LONG) based at min: the first CPU sets min = max = cpu; a lower id within the window shifts the bitmap and lowers min, a higher id within the window may raise max; an id outside the window first sends the pending bitmap with kvm_hypercall3(KVM_HCALL_FUNC_IPI, low word, high word, min), then restarts the bitmap at that id; the bit (cpu - min) is then set. After the loop, if the bitmap is non-zero it sends it with one more kvm_hypercall3. It takes no lock; the message-word updates are the only state changes besides the hypercalls.

Round 2 (skip when any bit already set) already stated in the old prose; original (ACTION_BOOT_CPU delegates to native_ops) also already stated. Slice 75-122.

name: arch_do_signal_or_restart
prose: Function taking the saved user register context regs of the current task; it returns nothing. It calls get_signal(&ksig). If a signal is pending, it calls handle_signal(&ksig, regs), which sets up the signal frame and may change regs and the blocked-signal mask (it can also restore or change the syscall restart state through the frame setup), and returns immediately. Otherwise: if regs->regs[0] is non-zero (the marker do_syscall sets to the syscall number plus one when the entry came from a system call), then if regs->regs[4] (the syscall result) is -ERESTARTNOHAND, -ERESTARTSYS or -ERESTARTNOINTR it sets regs->regs[4] = regs->orig_a0 (the original value of a0 saved by do_syscall) and decrements regs->csr_era by 4; if it is -ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK it sets regs->regs[4] = regs->orig_a0, regs->regs[11] = __NR_restart_syscall and decrements regs->csr_era by 4; for any other value of regs->regs[4] it changes none of those; in all cases where regs->regs[0] was non-zero it then sets regs->regs[0] = 0. If regs->regs[0] was zero, regs is not changed. In every no-signal path it finally calls restore_saved_sigmask().

Round 2 right on orig_a0: do_syscall saves the original a0 there (syscall.c:57), it is not the syscall number, and regs[0] holds nr + 1 (54); the clearing of regs[0] for non-restart values was already in the old prose. Original rejection (restore_saved_sigmask on no-signal path) already in the old prose. Slice 8-42.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE6(mmap, unsigned long, addr, unsigned long, len, unsigned long, prot, unsigned long, flags, unsigned long, fd, unsigned long, offset)

name: next_frame
prose: Static function taking an unwind_state pointer state, that advances an unwind to the next frame; info is &state->stack_info. Returns: (1) false at once, with state unchanged, if unwind_done(state) is already true. Otherwise it loops: (a) it calls unwind_by_prologue(state); if that returns true it sets state->pc = unwind_graph_addr(state, state->pc, state->sp) and returns true (state->pc, sp, ra, first and reset are as unwind_by_prologue left them; state->stack_info is not refreshed). (b) If it returned false (possibly after having modified state) and info->type is STACK_TYPE_IRQ and info->end equals state->sp, it reads the pt_regs at info->next_sp: if the regs are from user mode or csr_era is not a kernel text address it leaves the loop to the failure exit; otherwise it sets state->first = true, state->pc = csr_era, state->ra = regs[1], state->sp = regs[3], calls get_stack_info(state->sp, task, info) ignoring its result, and returns true. (c) Otherwise it sets state->sp = info->next_sp and calls get_stack_info on it; get_stack_info returns 0 when the new sp is in a known stack (the loop then repeats from (a)) and a non-zero error (setting info->type to STACK_TYPE_UNKNOWN) when it is not, which leaves the loop. The failure exit sets state->stack_info.type = STACK_TYPE_UNKNOWN and returns false; on that return state may have been altered by earlier unwind_by_prologue calls, and state->sp may have been set to info->next_sp.
note: Reviewer round 15 is wrong: get_stack_info returns 0 on success and -EINVAL on failure (kernel/stacktrace.c, in_task_stack/in_irq_stack paths return 0), so while (!get_stack_info(...)) keeps looping on success and leaves for the false return on failure (unwind_prologue.c slice 224-228). Rounds 1 and 2 (success path does not refresh ra/stack_info; state may be modified before a failed prologue unwind) are already stated and kept. Old prose accurate; restructured into steps.

name: atari_tt_hwclk
prose: Function atari_tt_hwclk(op, t) that reads (op == 0) or writes (op != 0) the Atari TT real-time clock using struct rtc_time *t; it returns 0 at its single return statement in all cases. It reads RTC_CONTROL into ctrl first. For a write (op != 0) it prepares values from t: sec, min, hour, day, mon = tm_mon + 1, year = tm_year - atari_rtc_year_offset, wday = tm_wday + (tm_wday >= 0); if ctrl has RTC_24H clear, hour > 11 sets pm = 0x80 and, unless hour is 12, subtracts 12, while hour 0 becomes 12; if ctrl has RTC_DM_BINARY clear it converts the values with bin2bcd (wday only if it is non-negative). Then, for both directions, it polls RTC_FREQ_SELECT until RTC_UIP is clear, using mdelay(1) between polls if in_atomic() or irqs_disabled() and schedule_timeout_interruptible(HWCLK_POLL_INTERVAL) otherwise. Then with interrupts saved and disabled (local_irq_save) it writes RTC_CONTROL = ctrl | RTC_SET; on read it reads the seconds, minutes, hours, day, month, year and day-of-week registers; on write it writes seconds, minutes, hours as hour + pm, day, month, year and, only if wday >= 0, day-of-week; it then writes RTC_CONTROL = ctrl & ~RTC_SET and restores interrupts. For a read it then post-processes: bit 0x80 of the hours value is stripped and sets pm = 1; if ctrl has RTC_DM_BINARY clear all values are converted with bcd2bin; if ctrl has RTC_24H clear then hour 12 with pm clear becomes 0 and pm set with hour other than 12 adds 12; finally it stores tm_sec, tm_min, tm_hour, tm_mday, tm_mon = mon - 1, tm_year = year + atari_rtc_year_offset and tm_wday = wday - 1 in *t. A write does not modify *t.

Old prose omitted the write-path value preparation (12/24 hour handling and BCD conversion) which happens before the UIP wait; the remaining claims were checked against the slice and kept.

name: ffs
prose: Static inline function ffs(x), the definition used on ColdFire parts with the bitrev instruction (it sits inside the branch guarded by __mcfisaaplus__ or __mcfisac__ and not CONFIG_M68000; other configurations use the generic ffs). If x is 0 it returns 0. Otherwise it returns __ffs(x) + 1, where __ffs executes bitrev followed by ff1 and so yields the zero-based index of the lowest set bit of x; the result is therefore in 1 to 32, for example 17 for x = 65536 and 32 only for x = INT_MIN. It has no side effects and reads no memory (declared __attribute_const__).
note: Contract left empty. The previous contract failed random testing (x=65536 gave result 18) but by the source the value is 17: bitrev then ff1 gives 16 for x = 65536 and the function adds 1 (bitops.h slice 250-255, __ffs just above). The test harness result cannot be reproduced from this code, so no contract is asserted.

name: flush_tlb_all
prose: Sun3 definition of flush_tlb_all (no arguments, returns nothing). It saves the MMU context with sun3_get_context. For each address from 0 up to TASK_SIZE in steps of SUN3_PMEG_SIZE and for each context 0 to 7 it selects that context with sun3_put_context and sets the segmap entry for the address to SUN3_INVALID_PMEG. It then restores the saved context with sun3_put_context. Finally, for each PMEG index from 0 up to but not including SUN3_INVALID_PMEG, if pmeg_alloc[index] is exactly 1 it sets pmeg_alloc[index], pmeg_ctx[index] and pmeg_vaddr[index] to 0. PMEGs whose pmeg_alloc value is not 1 are not touched.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: only PMEG indices below SUN3_INVALID_PMEG with pmeg_alloc == 1 are freed, not every allocated PMEG (tlbflush.h:~110-130). This is the variant in the Sun3 branch; the slice does not contain it, read from the real file. The name suffix in the packet is not part of the function name.

name: flush_tlb_kernel_range
prose: Sun3 definition of flush_tlb_kernel_range(start, end): its only statement is a call to flush_tlb_all(); start and end are not used and it returns nothing. The effect is that of the Sun3 flush_tlb_all: user segmap entries for addresses below TASK_SIZE are set to SUN3_INVALID_PMEG in all 8 contexts, the original context is restored, and the PMEGs with index below SUN3_INVALID_PMEG whose pmeg_alloc is 1 have their pmeg_alloc, pmeg_ctx and pmeg_vaddr cleared. Kernel-range segmap entries are not touched.

name: rt_restore_ucontext
prose: Static inline function taking regs, sw and a user ucontext pointer uc; it restores the register context from uc. It first sets current->restart_block.fn to do_no_restart_syscall. It reads uc->uc_mcontext.version into temp with __get_user, accumulating the error in err but not testing err yet; if temp != MCONTEXT_VERSION it returns -1 at once with regs and sw untouched (temp is whatever it held if the read failed). Otherwise it reads the registers from gregs: regs->d0..d5, sw->d6, sw->d7, regs->a0..a2, sw->a3..a6, the user stack pointer (written with wrusp(usp) even if an earlier read failed), regs->pc, and gregs[17], from which only the low byte replaces the low byte of regs->sr; it sets regs->orig_d0 to -1; it reads uc->uc_formatvec into temp; and calls rt_restore_fpu_state(uc) and restore_altstack(&uc->uc_stack), ORing their results into err. If err is non-zero it returns -1 (regs, sw and the user stack pointer may already have been changed). Otherwise it returns mangle_kernel_stack(regs, temp, &uc->uc_extra), which returns -1 if the frame format has no valid extra size or copying the extra frame from user space fails (before setting anything), and otherwise sets regs->format and regs->vector, moves the kernel stack frame down by the extra size when it is non-zero (updating current->thread.esp0) and returns the extra size (zero or positive).

If (pgoff & ~PAGE_MASK) is non-zero, i.e. the offset is not a multiple of the page size, it returns -EINVAL and calls nothing else. Otherwise it returns the value of ksys_mmap_pgoff(addr, len, prot, flags, fd, pgoff >> PAGE_SHIFT) unchanged. Those are its only two returns.

name: bcm63xx_set_cs_base
prose: Function bcm63xx_set_cs_base(cs, base, size) configuring the base address and size of a bcm63xx MPI chip select. Return paths: -EINVAL if cs is greater than 6 (is_valid_cs); -EINVAL if size != roundup_pow_of_two(size) (so size must be a power of two; the helper is only defined for size >= 1 and, on a 32-bit unsigned int, not above 2^31); -EINVAL if size is below 8192 or above 268435456; in each of these cases no hardware access is made. Otherwise it forms val = (base & MPI_CSBASE_BASE_MASK) | ((ilog2(size) - ilog2(8192)) << MPI_CSBASE_SIZE_SHIFT), takes bcm63xx_cs_lock with spin_lock_irqsave, writes val to MPI_CSBASE_REG(cs), releases the lock with spin_unlock_irqrestore and returns 0.

name: bcm63xx_detect_flash_type
prose: Static __init function with no arguments that reports the flash type of the board from the CPU id and boot strap registers. It switches on bcm63xx_get_cpu_id(): BCM6328 reads MISC_STRAPBUS_6328_REG and returns BCM63XX_FLASH_TYPE_SERIAL if STRAPBUS_6328_BOOT_SEL_SERIAL is set, else BCM63XX_FLASH_TYPE_NAND; BCM6338, BCM6345 and BCM6348 return BCM63XX_FLASH_TYPE_PARALLEL without reading hardware; BCM3368 and BCM6358 read GPIO_STRAPBUS_REG and return PARALLEL if STRAPBUS_6358_BOOT_SEL_PARALLEL is set, else SERIAL; BCM6362 reads MISC_STRAPBUS_6362_REG and returns SERIAL if STRAPBUS_6362_BOOT_SEL_SERIAL is set, else NAND; BCM6368 reads GPIO_STRAPBUS_REG and returns NAND, SERIAL or PARALLEL when (val & STRAPBUS_6368_BOOT_SEL_MASK) equals the corresponding STRAPBUS_6368_BOOT_SEL_ value, and -EINVAL for any other value; any other CPU id returns -EINVAL. The enum values are PARALLEL 0, SERIAL 1 and NAND 2, so the results are 0, 1, 2 or -EINVAL (-22). It has no side effects beyond reading registers.

name: main
prose: Program entry of the elf2ecoff host tool, main(argc, argv): converts the 32-bit ELF executable argv[1] into an ECOFF file argv[2]. It never returns normally: every path ends in exit(). It exits with status 1 and a stderr message if argc is below 3 or above 4, or if argc is 4 and argv[3] is not "-a" (a usage message; "-a" sets addflag so 6 section headers are written instead of 3); if argv[1] cannot be opened; if reading the ELF header gives a short count; if saveRead fails (lseek, malloc or short read of the program or section headers); if a program header has a type other than PT_NULL, PT_NOTE, PT_PHDR, PT_MIPS_REGINFO, PT_MIPS_ABIFLAGS or PT_LOAD; if combining PT_LOAD pieces finds non-contiguous text or data (combine); if the text, data and bss sections are out of order or overlap; if argv[2] cannot be opened or created (open with O_WRONLY | O_CREAT, mode 0777, no truncation); if writing the file header, a.out header or section headers does not write the full size; if an intersegment gap is larger than 65536 bytes; if a write of gap zeroes returns a negative count; if copy of a segment fails (lseek, short read or short write); or if the final 4096-byte zero page is not written in full. It sorts the program headers by vaddr, builds text, data and bss from the PT_LOAD headers (a writable segment is data plus bss, others are text), then writes the ECOFF file header, the a.out header, the section headers, up to 15 bytes of zero alignment padding to a 16-byte boundary (a negative write result is an error, a short positive write is not checked), each PT_LOAD segment with non-zero p_filesz in order preceded by a zero fill of any gap with a warning, and a 4096-byte page of zeros; then it calls exit(0). The input and output descriptors are never closed explicitly, and a failure after the output file was opened may leave a partial output file.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the alignment pad write only tests i < 0 (elf2ecoff.c slice 46-50), so a short write is not an error; the old prose said any short write exits. Missing exits added: saveRead failures and non-contiguous combine (lines 102-117, 133-155). The slice cut the head, so argument handling, ELF header read and the program-header loop were read from the real file lines 267-505. Note: after exit(1) at slice line 14 the following loop is unreachable.

name: __cvmx_get_mode_octeon2
prose: Static function __cvmx_get_mode_octeon2(interface) returning the interface mode for an Octeon II model; it only reads CSRs and has no side effects. In order: (1) on CN68XX it returns __cvmx_get_mode_cn68xx(interface); (2) interface 2 returns CVMX_HELPER_INTERFACE_MODE_NPI and interface 3 returns CVMX_HELPER_INTERFACE_MODE_LOOP, for any model reaching this point; (3) CN63XX interfaces 4 and 5 and CN66XX interfaces 4 to 7 return DISABLED; (4) on CN66XX: interface 0 reads CVMX_MIO_QLMX_CFG(2), interface 1 reads CVMX_MIO_QLMX_CFG(1), any other interface returns DISABLED; then DISABLED if qlm_spd is 15, SGMII if qlm_cfg is 9, XAUI if qlm_cfg is 11, DISABLED otherwise (this block always returns); (5) on CN61XX: interface 0 reads CVMX_MIO_QLMX_CFG(2) and interface 1 reads CVMX_MIO_QLMX_CFG(0), each returning SGMII for qlm_cfg 2, XAUI for qlm_cfg 3 and DISABLED otherwise; CN61XX interfaces other than 0 and 1 (and not 2 or 3, already handled in (2)) leave this block and continue to the code below; (6) on CNF71XX: interface 0 returns SGMII when CVMX_MIO_QLMX_CFG(0) has qlm_cfg 2, and every other case (including interface 0 with another value, and every interface other than 2 and 3, which were handled in (2)) returns DISABLED; (7) CN63XX interface 1 returns DISABLED; (8) otherwise it reads CVMX_GMXX_INF_MODE(interface): on CN63XX it returns SGMII for mode 0, XAUI for mode 1 and DISABLED for other modes; on other models it returns DISABLED if the en bit is clear, else GMII if the type bit is set and RGMII if clear.
note: Reviewer rounds 1, 2 and 15 point at exceptions to old wording: round 1 right (CN68XX delegates before the interface 2/3 tests, so those only apply to other models; the old text said this but in confusing order), round 2 wrong (old prose already said CNF71XX 2 and 3 are not DISABLED), round 15 right (old text implied CN61XX interfaces 2 and 3 fall through; they return NPI/LOOP at lines 157-161). Slice 150-244.

name: cvmx_l2c_get_hw_way_partition
prose: Function with no arguments that reads the hardware L2 way partition register. If OCTEON_IS_MODEL(OCTEON_CN63XX) it returns cvmx_read_csr(CVMX_L2C_WPAR_IOBX(0)) & 0xffff (a value 0 to 65535); otherwise it returns cvmx_read_csr(CVMX_L2C_SPAR4) & 0xFF (a value 0 to 255). It has no side effects other than the CSR read and takes no lock.

name: cvmx_l2c_get_cache_size_bytes
prose: Function with no arguments returning cvmx_l2c_get_num_sets() * cvmx_l2c_get_num_assoc() * CVMX_CACHE_LINE_SIZE (128), the L2 cache size in bytes. The set count is 1 shifted by cvmx_l2c_get_set_bits(), which depends on the Octeon model (128 to 2048 sets; an unsupported model prints a message and is treated as 2048 sets). The associativity depends on the model (4, 8 or 16 ways; unsupported models are treated as 8) reduced by the fuse bits: on CN63XX to 12, 8 or 4 ways, on other models divided by 2 or 4. Over all models and fuse settings the value is one of 32768, 65536, 131072, 262144, 524288, 1048576, 1572864 or 2097152. It reads fuse CSRs and may print through cvmx_dprintf, but changes no state.

Reviewers rounds 1, 2 and 15 are wrong about the old prose: it already listed 32768 as a possible value and already stated the sets * associativity * line size formula; I verified the possible values by enumerating every model branch of cvmx_l2c_get_set_bits / cvmx_l2c_get_num_assoc (cvmx-l2c.c, callee definitions before line 761).

name: cvmx_spi_reset_cb
prose: Function cvmx_spi_reset_cb(interface, mode) that resets an Octeon SPI4 interface; mode is not used. interface is used as the register index for CSRs (a valid SPI interface is 0 or 1; it is not checked). It busy-waits with __delay for about 10 ms, then 100 ms, then 100 ms (cpu clock based). Steps: it saves SPXX_INT_MSK and STXX_INT_MSK and writes 0 to both; clears SRXX_COM_CTL and STXX_COM_CTL; writes SPXX_CLK_CTL with runbist = 1, waits 10 ms, reads SPXX_BIST_STAT and prints a debug message for each of stat0, stat1 and stat2 that is set (BIST failures are only printed, not returned); writes 32 entries (index 0 to 31) of SRXX_SPI4_CALX and STXX_SPI4_CALX as zero with oddpar = 1; writes back the value read from SPXX_INT_REG and STXX_INT_REG (clearing pending bits) and restores the two saved interrupt masks; writes SPXX_CLK_CTL with clkdly = 0x10, statrcv = 1 and the other fields 0, waits 100 ms; sets srxdlck = 1 and rewrites SPXX_CLK_CTL, waits 100 ms; writes SPXX_TRN4_CTL with trntest = 0, jitter = 1, clr_boot = 1, set_boot = 0, maxdist = 3 on CN58XX and 8 otherwise, macro_en = 1 and mux_en = 1 (the other fields of that register value come from an uninitialised local variable); writes SPXX_DBG_DESKEW_CTL as 0; and returns 0. The only return is 0 at the end; there is no error return.

Original-rejection claim (no return statement; BIST failures not returned) is wrong about the return: cvmx-spi.c ends with return 0 (real file line ~290), but right that BIST failures are only printed. Slice cut the tail; read the rest from the real file lines 254-292. Old prose omitted the uninitialised fields of spxx_trn4_ctl.

name: csum_tcpudp_nofold
prose: Static inline function csum_tcpudp_nofold(saddr, daddr, len, proto, isum) returning the unfolded 32-bit pseudo-header checksum sum; it reads no memory and has no side effects. It adds daddr, saddr, (proto + len) and isum as unsigned long values; the (proto + len) term is cast to a signed 32-bit value first (the code assumes its sign bit is clear) and is shifted left by 8 on little-endian builds, not shifted on big-endian builds. On 32-bit builds each addition adds the carry back in (end-around carry); on 64-bit builds the 64-bit total is folded to 32 bits by adding its two 32-bit halves with the carry added back. The result is therefore the ones-complement style sum of the terms: equal to the integer total modulo 4294967295, except that a non-zero total that is a multiple of 4294967295 gives 4294967295; and the result is 0 only when all inputs contribute zero. The result is only correct when the shifted (proto + len) term fits the width of unsigned long, i.e. len + proto < 16777216 on 32-bit little-endian builds (larger on 64-bit builds); the build fails (BUILD_BUG) if neither CONFIG_32BIT nor CONFIG_64BIT is set.
note: Checked against the slice: the structure (32-bit: carry after each add; 64-bit: fold of halves, lines 157-167) matches the old prose. Precondition reworded: the 2^24 limit is a 32-bit LE limit, 64-bit builds hold the shifted term in 64 bits. Reviewer round 1 only concerned the contract, which is empty here.

name: set_dma_count
prose: Static inline function set_dma_count(dmanr, count) that programs the transfer count of DMA channel dmanr; it returns nothing and assumes the DMA controller flip-flop is clear (per the comment above it). It first decrements count (so count 0 becomes 0xffffffff). If dmanr <= 3 it writes count & 0xff and then (count >> 8) & 0xff with dma_outb to port ((dmanr & 3) << 1) + 1 + IO_DMA1_BASE. Otherwise (dmanr 4 to 7) it writes (count >> 1) & 0xff and then (count >> 9) & 0xff to port ((dmanr & 3) << 2) + 2 + IO_DMA2_BASE. Only the low 16 bits of the decremented count (of count >> 1 for channels above 3) are written, so counts larger than 64K for channels 0-3, or 128K above, are truncated; the comment states that count is in bytes and must be even for channels 5-7, but the code halves it for every channel above 3, including channel 4.
note: Reviewer round 1 right that the code halves count for all dmanr > 3 (the old prose said channels above 3 but the comment text says 5-7; both are kept visible now). Round 15 right that larger counts are truncated (set_dma_count slice lines 12-19); added. Slice 10-20.

name: get_dma_residue
prose: Static inline function get_dma_residue(dmanr) returning the number of bytes left for DMA channel dmanr; it assumes the DMA flip-flop is clear. It selects the port ((dmanr & 3) << 1) + 1 + IO_DMA1_BASE for dmanr <= 3, else ((dmanr & 3) << 2) + 2 + IO_DMA2_BASE. It reads the port once for the low byte and again for the high byte, forming an unsigned short count = (1 + low byte + (high byte << 8)) with 16-bit wraparound. It returns count for dmanr <= 3 and count << 1 (an int up to 131070) for dmanr > 3. The comment says the value is expected to be 0 after a completed transfer, that it may be 1 if the channel has not been used, and that reading during a transfer gives unpredictable results; none of these is enforced by the code. It writes no memory and takes no lock.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the code does not guarantee 1 for an unused channel; that is only the comment may-return statement, and the old prose asserted it. Slice 31-43.

name: BUILDIO_IOPORT(b, u8)
prose: Generated function _outb(val, port) (static inline, from __BUILD_IOPORT_SINGLE(_, b, u8, 1, 0) via BUILDIO_IOPORT(b, u8); an identical function __mem_outb is generated by the same invocation). It issues iobarrier_rw() (the barrier flag is 1), computes the address __swizzle_addr_b(mips_io_port_base + port), converts val with the platform _ioswabb macro (defined by the platform mangle-port.h or io.h; it may swap or leave the value unchanged) and stores the result through that volatile address. It returns nothing; the destination must be a mapped I/O address.

name: BUILDIO_IOPORT(b, u8)

It computes the address __swizzle_addr_b(mips_io_port_base + port), issues iobarrier_rw(), reads the byte through the volatile address, calls rmb() (the relax flag is 0), and returns the value passed through the platform _ioswabb macro (which may or may not change it).

It computes the address __swizzle_addr_l(mips_io_port_base + port), issues iobarrier_rw(), reads a 32-bit value through the volatile address, calls rmb(), and returns the value passed through the platform _ioswabl macro (which may swap bytes or leave it unchanged depending on the platform and CONFIG_SWAP_IO_SPACE).

name: BUILDSTRING(b, u8)

It loops count times (count is an unsigned int; with count 0 nothing happens), each time calling __mem_writeb(*__addr, mem) for the next source byte and then advancing the source pointer; the destination address mem is not advanced, so all bytes go to the same I/O address. It reads count bytes from addr and returns nothing.

name: BUILDSTRING(l, u32)

name: alchemy_gpio_direction_input
prose: Static inline function alchemy_gpio_direction_input(gpio) that returns the result of one of two helpers: alchemy_gpio2_direction_input(gpio) if gpio >= ALCHEMY_GPIO2_BASE, otherwise alchemy_gpio1_direction_input(gpio). The GPIO1 helper writes the mask 1 << (gpio - ALCHEMY_GPIO1_BASE) to AU1000_SYS_TRIOUTCLR with alchemy_wrsys and returns 0, without disabling local interrupts. The GPIO2 helper disables local interrupts with local_irq_save, calls __alchemy_gpio2_mod_dir(gpio, 0) and restores interrupts with local_irq_restore, then returns 0. The returned value is 0 in both cases; no range check is made on gpio.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: only the GPIO2 path disables local interrupts (gpio-au1000.h:231-236 vs 314-321); old prose claimed both paths do. Callee definitions read in the real file (slice shows only the wrapper, lines 216-221).

name: alchemy_gpio_direction_output
prose: Static inline function alchemy_gpio_direction_output(gpio, v) that returns the result of one of two helpers: alchemy_gpio2_direction_output(gpio, v) if gpio >= ALCHEMY_GPIO2_BASE, otherwise alchemy_gpio1_direction_output(gpio, v). The GPIO1 helper only calls alchemy_gpio1_set_value(gpio, v) (the hardware switches the pin to output when a set-value register is accessed) and returns 0, without disabling local interrupts. The GPIO2 helper calls alchemy_gpio2_set_value(gpio, v), then disables local interrupts with local_irq_save, calls __alchemy_gpio2_mod_dir(gpio, 1), restores interrupts, and returns 0. The returned value is 0 in both cases; no range check is made on gpio.
note: Reviewer round 15 right (GPIO1 path does not disable interrupts, gpio-au1000.h:238-245 vs 323-331); the old prose also said the output value is set first and then the direction, which is true for GPIO2 and for GPIO1 is the single set-value call.

name: mips_cm_l2sync
prose: Static inline function with no arguments that performs an L2-only sync. If mips_cm_has_l2sync() is false it returns -ENODEV without writing anything. Otherwise it writes 0 to mips_cm_l2sync_base with writel and returns 0. It takes no lock.
note: The old prose gave the value of ENODEV as -11; the correct Linux value of ENODEV is 19 (EAGAIN is 11), so the number was removed and the symbolic name kept (mips-cm.h slice 137-144).

name: cvmx_cmd_queue_write3
prose: Static inline function cvmx_cmd_queue_write3(queue_id, use_locking, cmd1, cmd2, cmd3) that appends three 64-bit command words to a hardware command queue. qptr is __cvmx_cmd_queue_get_state(queue_id). If use_locking is non-zero it takes the queue lock itself with __cvmx_cmd_queue_lock at the start, and every return below releases it with __cvmx_cmd_queue_unlock when use_locking is non-zero. Returns: (1) CVMX_CMD_QUEUE_FULL, with nothing written, if CVMX_CMD_QUEUE_ENABLE_MAX_DEPTH is enabled, qptr->max_depth is non-zero and cvmx_cmd_queue_length(queue_id) is greater than max_depth; (2) if qptr->index + 3 < qptr->pool_size_m1 the three words are stored at the current index of the current buffer, the index is advanced by 3, and it returns CVMX_CMD_QUEUE_SUCCESS; (3) otherwise it allocates a new buffer with cvmx_fpa_alloc(qptr->fpa_pool) and returns CVMX_CMD_QUEUE_NO_MEMORY, with nothing written, if that returns NULL; else it writes as many of cmd1..cmd3 as fit in the remaining space of the current buffer, stores the physical address of the new buffer as the link word after them, makes the new buffer current with index 0, writes the remaining command words at its start (advancing index accordingly), and returns CVMX_CMD_QUEUE_SUCCESS.
note: The listed name cvmx_cmd_queue_post_multi_3 does not exist: the slice cut the head and the function is cvmx_cmd_queue_write3 (cvmx-cmd-queue.h:~519-612). Old prose wrong on the precondition: the function takes the lock itself when use_locking is set (it does not require the caller to hold it). Slice 6-13 and 19-80 checked for returns.

name: __BUILD_BLAST_CACHE(d, dcache, Index_Writeback_Inv_D, Hit_Writeback_Inv_D, 32, )
prose: Generated function blast_dcache32() (static inline, from __BUILD_BLAST_CACHE with line size 32). It writes back and invalidates the whole primary data cache by index. With start = INDEX_BASE, end = start + current_cpu_data.dcache.waysize, ws_inc = 1 << dcache.waybit and ws_end = dcache.ways << dcache.waybit, it loops ws from 0 to ws_end in steps of ws_inc and, for each ws, addr from start to end in steps of 1024 bytes (32 lines of 32 bytes); each step issues 32 Index_Writeback_Inv_D cache operations at (addr | ws) + k * 32 for k = 0 to 31. Because the step is 1024 bytes, a waysize that is not a multiple of 1024 is covered up to the next 1024-byte boundary. It returns nothing; the dcache fields must be initialised.
note: Reviewer comments absent (status was unreviewed), but the old prose was wrong on the line size: this instance has lsize 32 (r4kcache.h:247), so the unrolled block is 32 lines of 32 bytes = 1024 bytes, not 16-byte lines with 512-byte rounding. Macro-generated; name is the invocation. Slice 201-215.

With start = page and end = page + PAGE_SIZE it runs a do-while loop: each pass issues 32 Hit_Writeback_Inv_D cache operations at start + k * 32 for k = 0 to 31 (one 1024-byte block) and then advances start by 1024 bytes; it repeats while start < end. name: spram_config

name: gt641xx_timer0_state
prose: Function with no arguments that starts timer 0 if it is not already counting. It reads GT_TC0_OFS with GT_READ. If the value is non-zero it returns 0 and performs no write. Otherwise it writes gt641xx_base_clock / HZ to GT_TC0_OFS with GT_WRITE, then writes GT_TC_CONTROL_ENTC0_MSK to GT_TC_CONTROL_OFS with GT_WRITE (a full-register write of that value), and returns 1. The only returns are 0 and 1.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the old text said it touches no register on the 0 path, but it reads GT_TC0_OFS (cevt-gt641xx.c slice line 26); the prose now says no write is made. Also removed the inference that other control bits are cleared (it is only stated that the write value is the enable mask). Slice 24-33.

name: cpu_get_msa_id
prose: Static inline function with no arguments that reads the MSA implementation register. It saves the CP0 Status register, calls __enable_fpu(FPU_64BIT), calls enable_msa() (which sets the Config5.MSAEn bit only if cpu_has_msa), reads read_msa_ir() into msa_id, calls disable_msa() (which clears Config5.MSAEn only if cpu_has_msa), writes the saved value back to CP0 Status, and returns msa_id. Status is therefore restored to its entry value, but the MSA enable bit in Config5 is cleared by disable_msa() whether or not it was set on entry. The function does not itself check that the CPU has MSA before reading the register, so it is meant to be called on a CPU known to have it.
note: Reviewer round 2 is wrong: MSA is not left as it was; disable_msa() explicitly clears Config5.MSAEn (asm/msa.h:105-111) and the Status restore does not affect Config5, so the old prose (state left exactly as on entry) was wrong, which round 1 hinted. Round 15 is right that there is no guard for CPUs without MSA, and the claim that the read value is unspecified there was unsupported. Slice 43-54.
