name: insert_sh6
prose: Inserts the SH6 operand of the rld* instructions into insn and returns the result. It only ORs bits into insn and never clears any. If PPC_OP(insn) == 4 it ORs (value & 0x1f) << 6 (bits 6-10) and (value & 0x20) >> 5 (bit 0). Otherwise it ORs (value & 0x1f) << 11 (bits 11-15) and (value & 0x20) >> 4 (bit 1). The dialect and errmsg parameters are unused; *errmsg is not written and no error is reported.
note: Reviewer 15 (else branch sets bit 1, not bit 4) RIGHT: ppc-opc.c:1970 uses (value & 0x20) >> 4, which places value bit 5 at bit 1. Slice cut head; real function at 1960-1971.

name: memex
prose: xmon 'm' (memory examine) command; it has no parameters and returns void. It reads an address into adrs with scanhex, then looks at the next non-blank character: if it is '?' it prints memex_help_string and returns; otherwise it stores that character in termch. It then sets last_cmd = "m\n" (these two assignments happen once, before the loops, and are not updated later). It reads the rest of the line, treating 'b','w','l','d' as setting size to 1, 2, 4, 8, 'r' as toggling brev, 'n' as setting mnoread and '.' as clearing it, and clamps size to 1..8. It then enters an endless loop that prints adrs and the memory contents (read with mread unless mnoread is set, byte-reversed when brev), then reads sub-commands from the input line: a hex number is written to adrs with mwrite; other characters adjust adrs, size, mnoread or brev (for example ',' '^' '/' '\\' 'm' '<' '>' '\'' for strings, '?' to print memex_subcmd_help_string); a newline ends the inner loop and adrs advances by inc. The function returns only when the sub-command character is 'x' or EOF, after calling scannl() to consume the line.
note: Reviewer 15 (termch and last_cmd set once before the loop, not updated) RIGHT: xmon.c:2404-2406. Slice cut head and name; real function at 2391-2539.

name: kernel_vector_end
prose: Ends a kernel-mode vector region started with kernel_vector_begin(). If neither has_vector() nor has_xtheadvector() is true it triggers WARN_ON and returns without any other action. Otherwise it calls riscv_v_disable() and then riscv_v_stop_kernel_context(). In the CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_V_PREEMPTIVE build that helper returns 1 when riscv_v_ctx_get_depth() != 0 or no preemptible vector context has started for current (nothing else done), and otherwise clears the dirty flag, calls riscv_v_stop(RISCV_PREEMPT_V) and returns 0; in the non-preemptive build it is defined as the constant -ENOENT, which is nonzero. If the helper's result is nonzero, kernel_vector_end calls put_cpu_vector_context(), which calls riscv_v_stop(RISCV_KERNEL_MODE_V) and then local_bh_enable() (or preempt_enable() when CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT). If the result is 0 it does not call put_cpu_vector_context. The function does not itself restore any vector register state.

name: handle_scalar_misaligned_load
prose: Emulates a misaligned scalar or FP load at regs->epc for the faulting address regs->badaddr. It always begins by recording a PERF_COUNT_SW_ALIGNMENT_FAULTS software event and setting this CPU's misaligned_access_speed to RISCV_HWPROBE_MISALIGNED_SCALAR_EMULATED. It then returns -1 (regs->epc unchanged) if unaligned_enabled is false, if the trap came from user mode and current->thread.align_ctl has PR_UNALIGN_SIGBUS, or if get_insn fails. After that it sets regs->epc = 0 and decodes the instruction (LW, LD and LWU on 64-bit, FLD, FLW, LH, LHU and the compressed C.LD, C.LDSP, C.LW, C.LWSP, C.FLD, C.FLDSP, C.LHU, C.LH, plus C.FLW and C.FLWSP on 32-bit); an unrecognised instruction restores regs->epc = epc and returns -1. If the instruction is a floating-point load and CONFIG_FPU is not enabled it returns -EOPNOTSUPP with regs->epc still 0. It then copies len bytes from addr with copy_from_user (user mode) or memcpy (kernel mode); if copy_from_user fails it returns -1 with regs->epc still 0. On success it writes the loaded value (sign-extended for the signed forms) into the destination integer or FP register and sets regs->epc = epc + INSN_LEN(insn), where insn may have been rewritten for the compressed forms, and returns 0.

Old prose also said epc is restored on failures; it is not restored after the copy_from_user failure (line 308-309) or the -EOPNOTSUPP return. Slice cut head; real function at 220-331.

prose: Implements the PR_RISCV_V_SET_CONTROL prctl for the current task. It returns -EINVAL if neither has_vector() nor has_xtheadvector() is true, or if arg has any bit outside PR_RISCV_V_VSTATE_CTRL_MASK (0x1f). It takes cur from the low two bits of arg: OFF (1) returns -EPERM if the current task's cur setting is not already OFF; ON (2) is accepted; DEFAULT (0) replaces cur with the task's current cur value; any other value (3) returns -EINVAL. It then takes next from bits 2-3 and the inherit flag from bit 4; if next is DEFAULT, OFF or ON it calls riscv_v_ctrl_set(current, cur, next, inherit) and returns 0; otherwise (next == 3) it returns -EINVAL without having called riscv_v_ctrl_set.

If etype is not SBI_PMU_EVENT_TYPE_HW it returns -EINVAL. If ecode is SBI_PMU_HW_CPU_CYCLES (1) it returns 0; if ecode is SBI_PMU_HW_INSTRUCTIONS (2) it returns 2; any other code returns -EINVAL. It has no side effects.

name: kvm_riscv_vcpu_pmu_ctr_stop
prose: Handles the SBI PMU counter-stop call for ctr_mask counters starting at ctr_base. It has one return, which always returns 0 after storing sbiret in retdata->err_val (0 if no error was recorded). sbiret is sticky: once set it is overwritten only by later errors, and it also gates the snapshot copy. It sets sbiret = SBI_ERR_INVALID_PARAM and jumps to out if kvm_pmu_validate_counter_mask fails, and SBI_ERR_NO_SHMEM and jumps to out if SBI_PMU_STOP_FLAG_TAKE_SNAPSHOT is set but kvpmu->snapshot_addr is INVALID_GPA. Then, for each set bit i of ctr_mask, it computes pmc_index = array_index_nospec(i + ctr_base, RISCV_KVM_MAX_COUNTERS) and skips counters not set in pmc_in_use. For a firmware counter: an event code >= SBI_PMU_FW_MAX sets SBI_ERR_INVALID_PARAM and jumps to out (ending the loop); a counter not started sets SBI_ERR_ALREADY_STOPPED and goes on; otherwise it marks the firmware event stopped and copies its value to pmc->counter_val. For a counter with a perf_event: if started it adds perf_event_pause(...) to counter_val and clears started, else sets SBI_ERR_ALREADY_STOPPED; with SBI_PMU_STOP_FLAG_RESET it then releases the perf event. A counter with neither sets SBI_ERR_INVALID_PARAM (the loop continues). If the snapshot flag is set and sbiret is still 0 it copies the overflow bit (if set in pmc_overflown) and counter_val into kvpmu->sdata and marks the snapshot dirty. With SBI_PMU_STOP_FLAG_RESET it sets event_idx to SBI_PMU_EVENT_IDX_INVALID, clears the in_use and overflown bits and, when the snapshot flag is set, clears the counter's bit in sdata->ctr_overflow_mask and marks the snapshot dirty; this reset step is done whether or not sbiret holds an error. After the loop, if the snapshot is dirty and kvm_vcpu_write_guest of the snapshot fails, sbiret becomes SBI_ERR_FAILURE.
note: Reviewer 1 (already-stopped/invalid counters not stopped; snapshot only when shmem_needs_update) right: vcpu_pmu.c:662-678,714-717. Reviewer 15 (overflow mask cleared under RESET even if an error was recorded) RIGHT: 699-711 is unconditional on sbiret, unlike the copy at 687. Slice cut head; real function at 627-723.

name: parse_boot_command_line
prose: Parses the s390 boot kernel command line. It sets __kaslr_enabled to IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_RANDOMIZE_BASE), copies early_command_line into command_line_buf with strscpy (truncating if too long), and loops over the copy with next_arg(). For each parameter name it applies the following checks independently (separate if statements): mem with a value sets memory_limit to memparse(val) rounded down to PAGE_SIZE; vmalloc with a value sets vmalloc_size (rounded up to _SEGMENT_SIZE) and vmalloc_size_set; dfltcc with a value of off, on, def_only, inf_only or always sets zlib_dfltcc_support to the matching constant (other values leave it); facilities with a value calls modify_fac_list; debug-alternative calls alt_debug_setup(val), even if val is NULL; nokaslr clears __kaslr_enabled; cmma runs kstrtobool(val, &enabled) and sets cmma_flag = 0 only when it parses and enabled is false; under CONFIG_KVM prot_virt sets prot_virt_host = 1 only when kstrtobool succeeds and gives true; relocate_lowcore sets MFEATURE_LOWCORE only if test_facility(193); earlyprintk sets boot_earlyprintk; debug sets boot_console_loglevel to CONSOLE_LOGLEVEL_DEBUG; bootdebug sets bootdebug and copies val into bootdebug_filter if present; quiet sets CONSOLE_LOGLEVEL_QUIET; ignore_loglevel sets boot_ignore_loglevel; loglevel sets boot_console_loglevel = simple_strtoull(val, NULL, 10) without checking val for NULL, then raises it to CONSOLE_LOGLEVEL_MIN if it is lower. Unrecognised parameters are skipped. The function returns void.

name: __physmem_alloc_range
prose: Finds a free physical address range of size bytes. It computes nranges as from_ranges if nonzero, else physmem_info.range_count (the code does not check that from_ranges <= range_count), raises align to at least 8, and starts with pos = max. In a loop over nranges, from the last range downward, it reads the range with __get_physmem_range(nranges - 1, ...) and lowers pos to the range end if that is smaller; if round_up(min, align) + size > pos it leaves the loop; otherwise it takes addr = round_down(pos - size, align); if addr is below the range start it moves to the next lower range (nranges--); if [addr, addr + size) intersects a reserved area (__physmem_alloc_intersects) it sets pos to the start of that intersection and retries; otherwise it stores nranges in *ranges_left when ranges_left is non-NULL and returns addr. If the loop ends without a result it calls die_oom(size, align, min, max) when die_on_oom is true and returns 0 otherwise (die_oom is a separate boot-time error reporter). The function only searches: it does not record the allocation itself; the callers physmem_alloc_range and physmem_alloc do.
note: Reviewer 1 (code requires from_ranges <= range_count) right as an implicit precondition, now stated. Prose rechecked against physmem_info.c:272-306. Slice cut head.

name: physmem_alloc_range
prose: Allocates a physical range of size bytes for the reserved-range type type. It lowers max to min(max, physmem_alloc_pos), calls __physmem_alloc_range(size, align, min, max, 0, NULL, die_on_oom), and if the result is nonzero records it with _physmem_reserve(type, addr, size). It always emits a boot_debug line with the address (also when addr is 0) and returns addr, which is 0 when no range was found and die_on_oom did not stop the boot.

name: physmem_alloc
prose: Allocates size bytes top-down below physmem_alloc_pos for reserved-range type type. It calls __physmem_alloc_range(size, align, 0, physmem_alloc_pos, physmem_alloc_ranges, &ranges_left, die_on_oom) and returns 0 if that returns 0 (state unchanged). If the type's existing range does not end directly below the new block (range->start != addr + size): when range->end is already nonzero it allocates a struct reserved_range (with die_on_oom true) below physmem_alloc_pos, then calls __physmem_alloc_range again for the data below that address with the remaining ranges (returning 0 if that fails, without updating the globals), copies the old *range into the new structure and chains it as range->chain; in both sub-cases it then sets range->end = addr + size. For types other than RR_VMEM it emits a boot_debug line. It then sets range->start = addr, physmem_alloc_pos = addr and physmem_alloc_ranges = ranges_left and returns addr.

name: setup_kernel_memory_layout
prose: Computes the s390 kernel virtual memory layout in the decompressor and returns the address space limit asce_limit; it has a single return at the end. It first overwrites vmemmap_size from ident_map_size (pages = ident_map_size / PAGE_SIZE, section-aligned, times sizeof(struct page)), so a previous value of vmemmap_size is not used. It estimates the virtual memory size with get_vmem_size and chooses asce_limit = _REGION1_SIZE (4-level) when CONFIG_KASAN is on, when __NO_KASLR_END_KERNEL > _REGION2_SIZE, or when the estimated size exceeds _REGION2_SIZE and kaslr_enabled(); otherwise asce_limit = _REGION2_SIZE (3-level). It sets rte_size to _REGION2_SIZE only in the case __NO_KASLR_END_KERNEL > _REGION2_SIZE and to _REGION3_SIZE otherwise, adjusts vmax with adjust_to_uv_max(asce_limit) (and under KASAN to at most KASAN_SHADOW_START) and clamps vsize. It chooses kernel_start: a random THREAD_SIZE-aligned slot below vmax when kaslr_enabled() (position 0 if get_random fails), a constrained position below vmax when vmax < __NO_KASLR_END_KERNEL or vsize > __NO_KASLR_END_KERNEL, else __NO_KASLR_START_KERNEL. It then writes the globals __kaslr_offset, MODULES_END, MODULES_VADDR, VMALLOC_END, VMALLOC_START, vmalloc_size (reduced to fit, and under KMSAN to a third), __memcpy_real_area, __abs_lowcore, vmemmap, vmemmap_size, ident_map_size (reduced so the identity map does not overlap vmemmap), max_mappable and, under CONFIG_RANDOMIZE_IDENTITY_BASE, __identity_base, and prints boot_debug lines. It takes no locks and returns asce_limit.

name: startup_kernel
prose: Entry point of the s390 decompressor; it takes no arguments, returns void and ends by calling jump_to_kernel(&psw) (that function is defined elsewhere and was not read). In order: setup_lpp, store_ipl_parmblock, uv_query_info, setup_boot_command_line and parse_boot_command_line; it computes nokaslr_text_lma (mem_safe_offset aligned to _SEGMENT_SIZE) and safe_addr, reserves RR_DECOMPRESSOR from 0 to safe_addr, reserves RR_INITRD when CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INITRD is set and parmarea.initrd_size is nonzero, and copies parmarea.oldmem_base and oldmem_size into oldmem_data (the old-memory area is recorded in oldmem_data, not reserved with physmem_reserve). It then runs read_ipl_report, SCLP and facility/machine detection, cmma_init, sanitize_prot_virt_host, detect_max_physmem_end, setup_ident_map_size, setup_vmalloc_size, setup_kernel_memory_layout (giving asce_limit), physmem_set_usable_limit, detect_physmem_online_ranges, save_ipl_cert_comp_list and rescue_initrd. It picks text_lma: a random location from randomize_within_range when kaslr_enabled(), falling back to nokaslr_text_lma when 0, ORed with the low offset bits of __kaslr_offset; sets __kaslr_offset_phys = text_lma - TEXT_OFFSET, calls kaslr_adjust_vmlinux_info, reserves RR_VMLINUX and calls deploy_kernel((void *)text_lma), then re-reserves RR_DECOMPRESSOR only up to _decompressor_end, picks amode31_lma (random below 2 GB when KASLR is on, else text_lma - amode31_size) and reserves RR_AMODE31. It then runs clear_bss_section, kaslr_adjust_relocs, kaslr_adjust_got, setup_vmem, dump_physmem_reserved, copy_bootdata and __apply_alternatives(ALT_CTX_EARLY), stores __kaslr_offset_phys | 1 (or 0) in lowcore->vmcore_info, builds a PSW with address __kaslr_offset + vmlinux.entry and mask PSW_KERNEL_BITS, and calls jump_to_kernel(&psw).

name: ecb_paes_do_one_request
prose: Crypto-engine callback that runs one ECB protected-key AES request whose skcipher walk was already prepared. It calls ecb_paes_do_crypt(ctx, req_ctx, true). If that returns -EKEYEXPIRED it calls cond_resched() and returns -ENOSPC so the engine reschedules the request; in that case it does not zero req_ctx->param, does not decrement ctx->via_engine_ctr and does not finalize the request. For any other nonzero rc it calls skcipher_walk_done(walk, rc). In every case other than -EKEYEXPIRED it then zeroes req_ctx->param with memzero_explicit, decrements ctx->via_engine_ctr and calls crypto_finalize_skcipher_request(engine, req, rc) with bottom halves disabled around those two calls, and returns 0 (the result travels through the finalization).

name: cbc_paes_setkey
prose: Sets the key for a CBC protected-key AES transform. It calls paes_ctx_setkey(ctx, in_key, key_len) and, if that returns nonzero, returns that code; then paes_convert_key(ctx) and returns its code on failure (on both early failures ctx->fc is not written). Then it selects fc from ctx->pk.type: CPACF_KMC_PAES_128, _192 or _256 for the AES-128, AES-192 and AES-256 protected key types, and 0 for any other type. It then writes ctx->fc = fc when fc is nonzero and cpacf_test_func(&kmc_functions, fc) is true, and 0 otherwise. It returns 0 if fc is nonzero (including when cpacf_test_func fails, in which case ctx->fc is 0 but the return is still 0), and -EINVAL if the key type gave fc == 0.
note: Reviewer 1 (returns 0 even if cpacf_test_func fails; early errors do not clear ctx->fc) RIGHT: paes_s390.c:639-641 (rc depends on fc, not on ctx->fc) and 616-622. Slice cut head; real function at 607-646.

name: cbc_paes_do_crypt
prose: Runs the CBC protected-key AES operation over the prepared walk. If req_ctx->param_init_done is false it reads ctx->pk_state under ctx->pk_lock: PK_STATE_NO_KEY gives rc = -ENOKEY, PK_STATE_CONVERT_IN_PROGRESS gives -EKEYEXPIRED, PK_STATE_VALID copies the protected key into param->key and sets param_init_done, and any other state gives the state value if negative or -EIO. A nonzero rc is returned at once without touching the walk. Otherwise it copies walk->iv into param->iv and loops while walk->nbytes != 0: it processes the full-block part n with cpacf_kmc(ctx->fc | req_ctx->modifier, ...); if k > 0 bytes were processed it copies param->iv back into walk->iv and sets rc = skcipher_walk_done(walk, nbytes - k) (so rc is whatever that call returns). If k < n and maysleep is false it returns -EKEYEXPIRED (walk left mapped); if maysleep is true it calls paes_convert_key, returns its error if nonzero, and otherwise refreshes param->key under ctx->pk_lock and continues the loop. When the loop ends the function returns the last rc (0 initially, then the last skcipher_walk_done result).
note: Reviewer (can return -EIO or paes_convert_key errors, not only -ENOKEY/-EKEYEXPIRED) RIGHT, now stated (paes_s390.c:672-674,699-703). Also the final rc is the last skcipher_walk_done result (692-695). Slice cut head; real function at 648-714.

name: cbc_paes_crypt
prose: Starts a CBC protected-key AES request with the given modifier. It calls skcipher_walk_virt(walk, req, false); on failure it jumps to out, returning that error with req_ctx->param zeroed and skcipher_walk_done not called. Otherwise it stores modifier and sets param_init_done to false. If ctx->via_engine_ctr is zero it tries cbc_paes_do_crypt(ctx, req_ctx, false) synchronously and returns 0 (param zeroed) if that returns 0. If rc is still 0 (the synchronous attempt was skipped because the engine counter was nonzero) or is -EKEYEXPIRED, it increments ctx->via_engine_ctr and calls crypto_transfer_skcipher_request_to_engine; if that returns anything other than -EINPROGRESS it decrements the counter again. If the resulting rc is not -EINPROGRESS (a transfer failure, or any other error from the synchronous attempt) it calls skcipher_walk_done(walk, rc). At out, if rc is not -EINPROGRESS it zeroes req_ctx->param with memzero_explicit; it returns rc. On -EINPROGRESS the param is left in place for the engine.
note: Reviewer (walk_virt failure returns -errno without skcipher_walk_done) RIGHT, stated (paes_s390.c:731-733,757-763). Slice cut head; real function at 716-765.

name: __diag288
prose: Static inline wrapper around the diagnose 0x288 instruction. It packs func and timeout into register pair r1 (even and odd halves) and action and len into register pair r3, sets rc to -EINVAL, and executes diag r1,r3,0x288 inside an asm volatile with "cc" and "memory" clobbers. If the diagnose completes without a program exception, the following lhi sets rc to 0 and it returns 0. If the diag instruction raises an exception covered by the EX_TABLE entry, the lhi is skipped and rc keeps the initial -EINVAL, which is returned. The function does not itself validate func, timeout, action or len.

name: modify_pagetable
prose: Adds (add true) or removes (add false) kernel page-table mappings for [start, end). It first returns -EINVAL (with WARN_ON_ONCE) if start | end is not page aligned, and again -EINVAL (with WARN_ON_ONCE) if end > __abs_lowcore; these two returns happen before any walk and before the TLB flush. Otherwise it walks the range one pgd entry at a time (pgd_addr_end). With add false it skips empty pgd entries; with add true an empty pgd entry gets a new p4d table from vmem_crst_alloc(_REGION2_ENTRY_EMPTY) (a NULL result goes to out with ret = -ENOMEM) which is installed with pgd_populate. It then calls modify_p4d_table(pgd, addr, next, add, direct, altmap); a nonzero result goes to out and becomes the return value; with add false it then calls try_free_p4d_table. After a complete walk ret is 0. At out, when add is false, it calls flush_tlb_kernel_range(start, end) (also on the error path), and it returns ret. Partial modifications are left in place on an error return. With add false this function itself performs no allocation; whether modify_p4d_table can return an error in that case is determined by that callee (not read).

name: zpci_event_attempt_error_recovery
prose: Tries to recover a PCI function after an error and returns a pci_ers_result_t; it starts with ers_res = PCI_ERS_RESULT_DISCONNECT. It takes device_lock(&pdev->dev) and releases it at out_unlock after calling zpci_report_status(zdev, pdev, "recovery", status_str), so every path ends there. If pdev->error_state is pci_channel_io_perm_failure it skips recovery and returns DISCONNECT. Otherwise it sets pdev->error_state = pci_channel_io_frozen; for a pass-through device, or when no driver is bound or the driver does not support error recovery, it returns DISCONNECT without further steps (no uevent is sent on these paths). It then calls zpci_event_notify_error_detected; if the result indicates abort it returns that value unchanged. If the result is not PCI_ERS_RESULT_NEED_RESET it calls zpci_event_do_error_state_clear and returns that result if it indicates abort. If the current result is NEED_RESET it calls zpci_event_do_reset. A result of PCI_ERS_RESULT_NONE is turned into RECOVERED. If the result is not RECOVERED at that point it sends pci_uevent_ers(DISCONNECT), logs that operator intervention is required, and returns the result as it is (it is not converted to DISCONNECT). Otherwise it logs, calls the driver's resume callback if there is one, sends pci_uevent_ers(RECOVERED) and returns PCI_ERS_RESULT_RECOVERED.

It then fills a zeroed union zpci_sic_iib (isc = PCI_ISC, nr_cpus = num_possible_cpus(), disb_addr = physical address of zpci_sbv->vector) and calls zpci_set_irq_ctrl(SIC_IRQ_MODE_DIRECT, 0, &iib), ignoring its result. It allocates zpci_ibv with kcalloc(num_possible_cpus(), ...) and returns -ENOMEM if that fails. For each possible CPU it creates zpci_ibv[cpu] with airq_iv_create (cache_line_size() * BITS_PER_BYTE bits, flags AIRQ_IV_DATA | AIRQ_IV_CACHELINE, plus AIRQ_IV_ALLOC for CPU 0) and returns -ENOMEM if one fails. On all three -ENOMEM returns it does not free or undo the earlier allocations or the SIC setting. On success it runs cpu_enable_directed_irq on all CPUs with on_each_cpu(..., 1), sets zpci_irq_chip.irq_set_affinity = zpci_set_irq_affinity and returns 0.

name: heartbeat_timer
prose: Timer callback for the SH heartbeat LED driver. It recovers hd (struct heartbeat_data) from the timer with timer_container_of, then calls heartbeat_toggle_bit(hd, bit, hd->flags & HEARTBEAT_INVERTED), where bit and up are function-static variables (initially 0 and 1) shared by all instances. heartbeat_toggle_bit does not toggle: it sets the LED register bits to the single bit (1 << hd->bit_pos[bit]) (or its complement when inverted), masked with hd->mask, preserving the bits outside hd->mask. name: set_thread_fault_code
prose: Static inline helper that updates the fault-code field of the current thread's flags. It computes ti->flags = (ti->flags & (~0 >> (32 - TI_FLAG_FAULT_CODE_SHIFT))) | (val << TI_FLAG_FAULT_CODE_SHIFT), with TI_FLAG_FAULT_CODE_SHIFT equal to 24. Here ~0 is the signed int -1, and on GCC right shift of a negative int is arithmetic, so the mask (~0 >> 8) is -1 (all ones) and the AND keeps every bit of ti->flags; the function therefore ORs (val << 24) into the flags and does not clear the previous upper byte first (the behaviour of the shift of a negative signed value is implementation-defined). Bits of val above bit 7 are shifted out of a 32-bit value. The function returns nothing, uses current_thread_info() and takes no lock.

name: denormal_muld
prose: Multiplies two double-precision bit patterns when hx is denormal (SH-2A FPU emulation helper). It masks magnitudes ix = |hx| and iy = |hy|. If iy is below 0x0010000000000000 or ix == 0 it returns only the XOR of the two sign bits ((hx ^ hy) & 0x8000000000000000), i.e. a signed zero. Otherwise it takes exp from the exponent field of iy, ix as the mantissa of hx and iy with the implicit bit set, forms the 128-bit product with mult64 into (mh, ml), and finds w, the index of its highest set bit. It sets exp += w - 1022 - 52 * 2; if exp > 0 it builds the result as (rshift64(mh, ml, w - 52) & 0x000fffffffffffff) | ((long long)exp << 52); else if exp + 51 >= 0 it uses rshift64(mh, ml, w - 51 - exp) & 0x000fffffffffffff; else it uses 0. It ORs in the sign (hx ^ hy) & 0x8000000000000000 and returns it. It does not check that the shift counts passed to rshift64 are in 1..127 (for example w == 52 passes n = 0, a shift by 64 inside rshift64), and its own comment says guard bits are not used (FIXME).

prose: Handler for the sparc64 performance-counter NMI (notrace __kprobes). If touched is 0 and last_irq_sum equals sum it increments alert_counter (so the counter is changed in this branch) and, when alert_counter reaches 30 * nmi_hz, calls die_nmi("BUG: NMI Watchdog detected LOCKUP", regs, panic_on_timeout); otherwise it stores sum in last_irq_sum and resets alert_counter to 0. It classifies the instruction as FPOP1 or FPOP2 by its opcode bits and sets type from a table of known operations (the ftt value expected, operand sizes and pack/unpack flags); for the conditional fmovq forms it evaluates the condition from %fsr or the condition codes: if false it clears the CEXC field of xfsr, sets tpc = tnpc, tnpc += 4 and returns 1, and if true it rewrites the instruction as a plain fmovq. Unrecognised opcodes leave type 0 and the function returns 0. If type is set: when illegal_insn_trap is false it requires the xfsr ftt field to equal the expected trap type, else it returns 0; then it clears the ftt field (&= ~0x1c000), decodes the source and destination FP registers (a quad register number with bit 1 set sets the invalid_fp_register trap type in xfsr and returns 0), unpacks the operands, performs the operation with the soft-float macros, and unless FP_INHIBIT_RESULTS stores the result in the destination register (or into the addressed fcc field of xfsr for compares). If _fex is nonzero it returns record_exception(regs, _fex); otherwise it clears the CEXC field of xfsr (FSR_CEXC_MASK), advances tpc = tnpc and tnpc += 4 and returns 1. When the destination register is written it also marks fpsaved (setting FPRS_FEF and zeroing the half of the register file that was not yet saved).
note: Reviewer 15 (says clears CEXC but code clears ftt 0x1c000) PARTLY right: the code clears the ftt field early (math_64.c:~375) and clears CEXC only in the success and fmov-false-nop paths (~352,~520); both are now stated. name: bpf_int_jit_compile
prose: Sparc64 BPF JIT entry point; returns the program to use (the JITed prog, or the original prog when JIT is not done or fails). It returns orig_prog at once if prog->jit_requested is false, and also if bpf_jit_blind_constants fails; if blinding returned a different program it is used (tmp_blinded). It uses prog->aux->jit_data, allocating it with kzalloc if NULL (failure: prog = orig_prog and return without the cleanup at out_off). If jit_data->ctx.offset is already set (an extra pass of a multi-function program) it reuses the saved ctx, image and header and jumps to the final pass. Otherwise it allocates ctx.offset (kmalloc_array; failure: orig_prog), then runs up to 39 passes of build_prologue/build_body/build_epilogue until the generated size stops changing (a build_body failure gives orig_prog); it allocates the image with bpf_jit_binary_alloc (failure: orig_prog). The final pass rebuilds the code into the image; a build_body failure or a size that differs from the previous pass frees the header and gives orig_prog. It flushes the icache, and, if the program is not a subprogram or this is the extra pass, makes the image read-only with bpf_jit_binary_lock_ro (failure: free header, orig_prog); otherwise it saves ctx, image and header in jit_data for the extra pass. It sets prog->bpf_func, jited and jited_len, and when finished (non-subprogram or extra pass) fills the jited line info and, at out_off, frees ctx.offset and jit_data and clears prog->aux->jit_data. At out, if constants were blinded it releases the unused one of the two programs with bpf_jit_prog_release_other. It returns prog.

name: prom_console_write_buf
prose: Writes len bytes of buf to the PROM console. It loops while len is nonzero: n = __prom_console_write_buf(buf, len); if n < 0 it retries with the same buf and len; otherwise it executes len -= n and then buf += len, that is, buf is advanced by the remaining length after the subtraction, not by n. It returns (void) only when len becomes exactly 0. A call that returns n == 0 leaves len unchanged but still moves buf forward by len; if n is greater than len, len becomes negative and the loop continues. So the pointer advance is not the number of bytes written.

name: prom_getintdefault
prose: Returns the integer property named property of PROM node node, or deflt. It calls prom_getint(node, property); if that returns -1 it returns deflt, otherwise it returns the value returned by prom_getint. prom_getint returns -1 when prom_getproperty(node, prop, &intprop, sizeof(int)) returns -1 and otherwise returns the local int intprop, whose value is whatever prom_getproperty stored (the code does not check that all four bytes were written, so a property shorter than four bytes can give an indeterminate value). A property whose genuine value is -1 also yields deflt.

prose: Returns the string to use as an xterm title. It gets the umid with get_umid(); if that string is empty it returns base unchanged. Otherwise it computes len for base + " ()" + umid + NUL and allocates title with kmalloc(len, GFP_KERNEL); if that fails it prints an error with printk and returns base. Otherwise it writes "base (umid)" into the new buffer with snprintf and returns that buffer. A returned title is newly allocated and is not freed here.

name: port_open
prose: Opens a port channel. It waits for a connection with port_wait(data->kernel_data), giving fd. If fd >= 0 and data->raw is set, it calls tcgetattr(fd, &data->tt) (retrying on EINTR) and, if that returns nonzero, returns the error at once; then it calls raw(fd) and returns its error if nonzero; both of these error returns happen before *dev_out is written and the fd is not closed here. In all other cases (including fd < 0) it sets *dev_out = data->dev and returns fd, which may be negative.

name: time_travel_ext_req
prose: Sends a time-travel request with opcode op and time to the external controller and waits for its ACK; it returns the msg.time value of the message. It increments the static sequence counter to get mseq, builds a struct um_timetravel_msg with op, time and seq, calls block_signals_hard(), and writes the message to time_travel_ext_fd with os_write_file (its result is not checked). If op is UM_TIMETRAVEL_WAIT and time_travel_shm is set it goes straight to unblocking (no ACK is read). Otherwise it loops calling time_travel_handle_message(&msg, ...) (mode TTMH_READ_START_ACK if op is UM_TIMETRAVEL_START, else TTMH_READ) until msg.op is UM_TIMETRAVEL_ACK; if the ACK's seq differs from mseq it calls panic. For UM_TIMETRAVEL_GET it then calls time_travel_set_time(msg.time). It calls unblock_signals_hard() and returns msg.time (the ACK's time, or the sent time in the shared-memory WAIT case).

name: segv
prose: Handles a UML segmentation fault; it always returns 0 on its normal paths (panic paths do not return). If !is_user and regs is non-NULL it saves regs in current->thread.segv_regs. Branches: (1) !is_user and init_mm.context.sync_tlb_range_to set: um_tlb_sync(&init_mm); -ENOMEM calls report_enomem; any error panics; otherwise it goes to out. (2) current->pagefault_disabled: if mc is NULL it calls show_regs and panics; if thread.segv_continue is NULL it panics; otherwise it sets the mcontext rip to segv_continue, clears segv_continue and goes to out. (3) current->mm == NULL: panic. (4) !is_user and address strictly between PAGE_SIZE and TASK_SIZE: panic (kernel access to user memory). Otherwise, if SEGV_IS_FIXABLE(&fi) it calls handle_page_fault(address, ip, is_write, is_user, &si_code), else err = -EFAULT and address = 0. If err is 0 it goes to out; for a kernel fault (!is_user) arch_fixup(ip, regs) true also goes to out; a remaining kernel fault panics. For a user fault it calls show_segv_info(regs), records the faultinfo, and sends SIGBUS (BUS_ADRERR) if err == -EACCES, else BUG_ON(err != -EFAULT) and SIGSEGV with si_code via force_sig_fault. At out it clears current->thread.segv_regs if regs is non-NULL and returns 0. Several panic paths dereference regs through container_of without a NULL check (a NULL regs is only safe on the paths that do not use it).
note: Reviewer 2 (pagefault-disabled case recovers via segv_continue, panics only when it is missing) RIGHT: trap.c:332-344. Reviewer 15 (precondition wrongly excludes NULL regs for a user fault) RIGHT: user faults handled without dereferencing regs except through show_segv_info/arch paths. name: __wrap_free
prose: UML wrapper that frees a pointer according to where it was allocated; returns void. It takes addr = (unsigned long)ptr. If addr is in [uml_physmem, high_physmem) it calls kfree(ptr) only if kmalloc_ok is set; else if addr is in [start_vm, end_vm) it calls vfree(ptr) only if kmalloc_ok is set; otherwise (any other address) it calls __real_free(ptr). When kmalloc_ok is clear and the pointer lies in one of the first two regions, nothing is freed (the source comment notes possible leaks).

name: __add_sigio_fd

A failure leaves the registration as epoll_ctl left it (for example -EEXIST means fd was already registered and stays registered). The function takes no lock itself.

name: map
prose: Queues a stub mmap for the child mm: map(mm_idp, virt, len, prot, phys_fd, offset), always returning 0. Otherwise it resolves phys_fd with get_stub_fd(mm_idp, phys_fd), allocates a new stub with syscall_stub_alloc and fills it with STUB_SYSCALL_MMAP, addr = virt, length = len, prot, fd = the resolved fd and offset = MMAP_OFFSET(offset), and returns 0.

name: cts_cbc_encrypt
prose: AES-NI CBC-CTS encrypt for a skcipher request (aesni-intel_glue.c:243-297). It sets up a sub-request subreq with the same tfm and callback flags. cbc_blocks = DIV_ROUND_UP(req->cryptlen, 16) - 2. If req->cryptlen <= 16: a length below 16 returns -EINVAL, and a length of exactly 16 sets cbc_blocks = 1. If cbc_blocks > 0 it CBC-encrypts the first cbc_blocks blocks with cbc_encrypt(&subreq) (returning its error if nonzero); if req->cryptlen == 16 it then returns 0 (a one-block message is processed by CBC only, not by the ciphertext-stealing step); otherwise it advances src and dst past those blocks with scatterwalk_ffwd. It then sets up subreq for the remaining bytes (req->cryptlen - cbc_blocks * 16) and calls skcipher_walk_virt (returning its error if nonzero), runs aesni_cts_cbc_enc on the walk's buffers inside kernel_fpu_begin()/kernel_fpu_end(), and returns skcipher_walk_done(&walk, 0).

name: DEFINE_FREDENTRY_RAW(int80_emulation)
prose: Generated FRED entry function for the 32-bit INT $0x80 vector (named fred_int80_emulation by the macro; the packet listed it as do_int80_emulation_fred); returns void. Given regs, it calls enter_from_user_mode(regs), then instrumentation_begin() and add_random_kstack_offset(). It sets regs->orig_ax = regs->ax & GENMASK(31, 0) (the low 32 bits of the syscall number) and regs->ax = -ENOSYS, calls nr = syscall_32_enter(regs), enables interrupts with local_irq_enable(), calls nr = syscall_enter_from_user_mode_work(regs, nr), then do_syscall_32_irqs_on(regs, nr), instrumentation_end() and syscall_exit_to_user_mode(regs). Unlike do_int80_emulation it does not check user_mode() or int80_is_external(). The effects of syscall_32_enter and the other helpers (for example any thread-flag changes) are not described here because they were not read.

name: emulate_vsyscall
prose: Called from the x86 page-fault path to emulate a vsyscall; returns true if it handled the fault (including by sending a signal) and false if it did nothing. It returns false, without modifying regs, when (error_code & (X86_PF_WRITE | X86_PF_USER)) != X86_PF_USER; when address != regs->ip (a data access, with a warning unless vsyscall_mode is EMULATE); and when vsyscall_mode == NONE (with a warning). With NX it WARNs once if X86_PF_INSTR is not set. Then vsyscall_nr = addr_to_vsyscall_nr(address); a negative value, an unreadable user stack slot at regs->sp (get_user of the return address), or a failed write_ok_or_segv check of the user buffers for the call (gettimeofday: di and si; time: di; getcpu: di and si) jumps to sigsegv, which calls force_sig(SIGSEGV) and returns true. Otherwise it sets regs->orig_ax = the real syscall number and regs->ax = -ENOSYS and calls secure_computing(); if seccomp changed the number or the ip it logs, calls force_exit_sig(SIGSYS) and returns true. It sets regs->orig_ax = -1; if secure_computing asked to skip the call it goes to do_ret (regs->ax remains -ENOSYS), otherwise it calls __x64_sys_gettimeofday, __x64_sys_time or __x64_sys_getcpu (for getcpu it temporarily sets regs->dx to 0 and restores it); a result of -EFAULT goes to sigsegv, any other result is stored in regs->ax. At do_ret it sets regs->ip to the saved return address (caller), adds 8 to regs->sp, and returns true.

name: intel_pmu_disable_event
prose: Disables a perf event according to event->hw.idx, takes no lock itself, and returns nothing. Idx in 0..INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED-1: clears bit idx in this CPU's intel_ctrl_guest_mask, intel_ctrl_host_mask and intel_cp_status, then calls x86_pmu_disable_event. Idx in INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED..INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED_BTS-1 or INTEL_PMC_IDX_METRIC_BASE..INTEL_PMC_IDX_METRIC_END: calls intel_pmu_disable_fixed, which for a TopDown idx returns without changing anything when other TopDown events are still set in active_mask (otherwise it switches to the SLOTS index), and otherwise clears the three masks for that index and clears that fixed counter's control bits in cpuc->fixed_ctrl_val; it does not itself write an MSR. Idx == INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED_BTS: calls intel_pmu_disable_bts and intel_pmu_drain_bts_buffer and returns at once, skipping the PEBS step. Idx == INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED_VLBR: clears the three masks for idx, then continues to the PEBS step below. Any other idx: clears the three masks for idx, prints a warning about the invalid index and returns at once, skipping the PEBS step. After every case except BTS and the invalid index, if event->attr.precise_ip is nonzero it calls the x86_pmu_pebs_disable static call for the event.
note: Reviewer round 1 (invalid idx clears masks before warning) right: core.c:2589-2592. Round 15 (FIXED_VLBR falls through to PEBS disable) right: core.c:2585-2587 break, then 2599-2600. Prose reworded to state it explicitly; also states intel_pmu_disable_fixed only updates fixed_ctrl_val (core.c:2561-2564), it does not write an MSR.

name: handle_pmi_common
prose: Handles the common part of a PMI on the current CPU. It increments the apic_perf_irqs IRQ stat and works on its own copy of status (passed by value). It returns 0 at once if status is zero after clearing GLOBAL_STATUS_COND_CHG, GLOBAL_STATUS_ASIF and GLOBAL_STATUS_LBRS_FROZEN. Otherwise it clears from status the bits of PEBS-enabled counters (cpuc->pebs_enabled & x86_pmu.pebs_capable) and then handles three special bits, each adding 1 to the handled count and being cleared from status when it was set: PEBS buffer overflow (calls x86_pmu_handle_guest_pebs and the drain_pebs static call, writes MSR_IA32_PEBS_ENABLE if cpuc->pebs_enabled changed during the drain, and clears the perf-metrics overflow bit when cpuc->events[INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED_SLOTS] is non-NULL and is a PEBS counter group); Intel PT ToPA PMI (calls intel_pt_interrupt unless perf_guest_handle_intel_pt_intr() returns nonzero); perf-metrics overflow (calls the intel_pmu_update_topdown_event static call with NULL, NULL). It then masks status with the hybrid intel_ctrl and ORs in cpuc->intel_cp_status. For each set bit below X86_PMC_IDX_MAX it adds 1 to handled first, then skips the bit if it is not set in cpuc->active_mask or cpuc->events[bit] is NULL; otherwise, if the event is a PEBS counter group it calls x86_pmu.drain_pebs, and then calls intel_pmu_save_and_restart and only when that returns nonzero it initializes the sample data, saves the LBR branch stack if the event has a branch stack, and calls perf_event_overflow. It returns the handled count, which can be 0 even when status was nonzero at entry, and does not acknowledge the global status register itself.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: x86_pmu.drain_pebs for PEBS counter group is after the active_mask/NULL-event checks (core.c:3293-3318); old prose put the drain first. Round 2 (skips overflow when save_and_restart fails) already handled (core.c:3322-3323). Original-round claim about clearing regular bits no longer applies, prose makes no such claim.

name: intel_pmu_hw_config
prose: Validates and configures a perf event for the Intel PMU and returns 0 or a negative errno; on an error return the event may already have been partly modified. It first returns any error from x86_pmu_hw_config and intel_pmu_bts_config. With attr.freq and attr.sample_freq set it initializes sample_period, last_period and period_left from intel_pmu_freq_start_period. With attr.precise_ip set it returns -EINVAL for the VLBR event config, sets PERF_X86_EVENT_AUTO_RELOAD (and, when the sample type and aux action allow, PERF_X86_EVENT_LARGE_PEBS and PERF_ATTACH_SCHED_CB) when neither freq nor wakeup_events without watermark is requested, and calls x86_pmu.pebs_aliases if present. It sets PERF_X86_EVENT_NEEDS_BRANCH_STACK for branch-stack sampling and, for branch-counter events, returns -EINVAL if the PMU lacks PMU_FL_BR_CNTR, the config has bits outside INTEL_ARCH_EVENT_MASK, a group member cannot take a branch-counter constraint, the counter count exceeds fls(x86_pmu.lbr_counters), or the leader is not a branch-stack event. When a branch stack is needed it sets up the LBR filter (returning its error), sets PERF_ATTACH_SCHED_CB, and unless BTS is in use takes the LBR exclusive reference (-EBUSY on conflict) and sets event->destroy. It returns -EINVAL for aux_output without precise_ip, otherwise sets PERF_X86_EVENT_PEBS_VIA_PT, may flag the group leader with PERF_X86_EVENT_PEBS_CNTR, and for an ACR group returns -EINVAL for metric events, freq mode, config2 with precise_ip above 2, sample_period above max_period, non-x86 leaders, non-x86 events between ACR events, or too many cause/counter bits, and otherwise sets the ACR counter constraints and PERF_X86_EVENT_ACR on the leader. For PERF_TYPE_HARDWARE and PERF_TYPE_HW_CACHE it returns 0 here. For TopDown slots/metric events it returns -EINVAL for disallowed config1, config2 or filter flags, and for metric events that sample or whose leader is not a non-sampling slots event, and otherwise marks the group PERF_X86_EVENT_TOPDOWN. For a load-latency event that needs the memory-loads auxiliary event it returns -ENODATA if the event is its own leader or no auxiliary event precedes it in the group. Finally, if the config lacks ARCH_PERFMON_EVENTSEL_ANY it returns 0; otherwise it returns -EINVAL when x86_pmu.version < 3, returns the error of perf_allow_cpu() if nonzero, and else sets ARCH_PERFMON_EVENTSEL_ANY in hw.config and returns 0.

Old prose claimed errors leave the event unmodified, which is false: flags, hw.config/period, attach_state, destroy and the exclusive-LBR count are set before later error returns (core.c:4294-4400).

name: precise_store_data
prose: Pure helper that turns a PEBS store data-source status word into a perf memory data-source encoding. It starts from PERF_MEM_S values OP=STORE, SNOOP=NA, LVL=L1 and TLB=L2 (0x40080104 together), then ORs in TLB=MISS (0x10000000) if bit 4 of status is set or TLB=HIT (0x8000000) otherwise, LVL=HIT (0x40) if bit 0 is set or LVL=MISS (0x80) otherwise, and LOCK=LOCKED (0x2000000) if bit 5 is set. Any 64-bit status is accepted, other status bits are ignored, and it reads or writes no state besides its argument.
note: All four reviewer claims wrong: constants checked against include/uapi/linux/perf_event.h:1339-1430 and ds.c:231-267. OP_STORE 4<<0, SNOOP_NA 1<<19=0x80000, LVL_L1 8<<5=0x100, TLB_L2 0x10<<26=0x40000000 -> base 0x40080104; TLB_MISS 4<<26=0x10000000, TLB_HIT 2<<26=0x8000000; LVL_HIT 2<<5=0x40, LVL_MISS 4<<5=0x80; LOCK_LOCKED 2<<24=0x2000000. Bits per union intel_x86_pebs_dse (st_l1d_hit bit0, st_stlb_miss bit4, st_locked bit5), ds.c:47-51.

name: imc_uncore_pci_init
prose: Calls imc_uncore_find_dev(), which tries snb_pci2phy_map_init(p->pci_id) for each entry of desktop_imc_pci_ids in order until one returns 0 and then returns that entry's PCI driver, or returns NULL if none succeeds (those calls can have effects of their own). If the driver is NULL it returns -ENODEV and does not write uncore_pci_uncores or uncore_pci_driver. Otherwise it sets uncore_pci_uncores to snb_pci_uncores, sets uncore_pci_driver to the found driver and returns 0.

name: branch_type
prose: Wrapper that returns get_branch_type(from, to, abort, false, NULL), so no fusion handling is done and no offset is written. get_branch_type computes the target privilege bit to_plm (X86_BR_KERNEL if to is a kernel address, else X86_BR_USER). It returns X86_BR_NONE if from or to is 0. Otherwise, if abort is nonzero, it returns X86_BR_ABORT | to_plm without examining any instruction. Otherwise, for a user from address it returns X86_BR_NONE if current->mm is NULL or copy_from_user_nmi copies zero bytes of the instruction; for a kernel from address it returns X86_BR_NONE unless from is a kernel text address outside the gate area. It then decodes the branch type of the instruction at from (decode result X86_BR_ABORT if the opcode or ModRM bytes cannot be decoded, X86_BR_NONE for non-branch or unknown opcodes). If from is a user address and to is a kernel address and the decoded type is neither X86_BR_SYSCALL nor X86_BR_INT, the type becomes X86_BR_IRQ, including when it was NONE or ABORT. If the final type is not X86_BR_NONE it is ORed with to_plm and returned, otherwise X86_BR_NONE is returned. It reads user memory through copy_from_user_nmi but allocates nothing and takes no locks.
note: Reviewers round 1/15 right on ordering: abort is tested at utils.c:113 before the address validity checks at 116-151, so abort returns ABORT|to_plm even for user/kernel addresses; old prose put the NONE checks first. Round 2 (decode failure can become IRQ) right: utils.c:194-196. branch_type is a wrapper (utils.c:208-211) calling get_branch_type(from,to,abort,false,NULL).

name: zhaoxin_pmu_init
prose: Boot-time initialization of the Zhaoxin PMU; returns 0 or -ENODEV. It prints a message, reads CPUID leaf 10, and returns -ENODEV without changing x86_pmu if eax.mask_length is below ARCH_PERFMON_EVENTS_COUNT - 1 or version_id is not 2. Otherwise it copies zhaoxin_pmu into x86_pmu, fills version, cntr_mask64, cntval_bits, cntval_mask, events_maskl, events_mask_len and fixed_cntr_mask64 from CPUID, and registers zhaoxin_arch_events_quirk. It then switches on boot_cpu_data.x86. Family 6: if model is 0x0f with stepping at least 0x0e, or model is 0x19, it sets max_period to cntval_mask >> 1, enabled_ack to 1, uses zxc_event_constraints and zeroes the INSTRUCTIONS, CACHE_REFERENCES, CACHE_MISSES and BUS_CYCLES entries of zx_pmon_event_map; any other family 6 CPU returns -ENODEV. Family 7: sets the stalled-cycles entries of zx_pmon_event_map, and for model 0x1b or 0x3b copies the ZXD or ZXE hw_cache_event_ids, uses zxd_event_constraints and sets the branch entries; any other model returns -ENODEV. Any other family returns -ENODEV. In the -ENODEV returns after the CPUID checks, x86_pmu has already been overwritten and the quirk registered. On success it sets intel_ctrl to cntr_mask64 | (fixed_cntr_mask64 << INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED) and, if event_constraints is set, ORs cntr_mask64 into each constraint's idxmsk64 and adds x86_pmu_num_counters(NULL) to its weight, then returns 0.
note: Slice cut the head: function is defined at zhaoxin/core.c:505-618. Prior prose checked against code and kept, with the family/model enumeration and failure side effects re-verified (core.c:520-617). Reviewer round 15 only criticised the contract; contract dropped (writes globals).

name: local_db_save
prose: Saves and disables hardware breakpoints, returning the value to pass to local_db_restore. If the CPU has X86_FEATURE_HYPERVISOR and the per-CPU cpu_dr7 has no DR_GLOBAL_ENABLE_MASK bit set (hw_breakpoint_active() is false), it returns 0 without reading or writing DR7. Otherwise it reads DR7, clears the DR7_FIXED_1 bit in the value read, writes DR7_FIXED_1 to DR7 only if the cleared value is nonzero, executes a compiler barrier and returns the cleared value. In both paths the returned value has the DR7_FIXED_1 bit clear. It reads cpu_dr7 but takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Reviewer round 15 right that it reads per-CPU cpu_dr7 via hw_breakpoint_active (debugreg.h:121-124,132); old prose said no memory involved. Prose now says it reads that variable. Early return 0 without reading DR7 re-verified at 132-133; DR7 write only if dr7 nonzero after masking (138-140).

name: BUILDIO(bwl, type)
prose: Generated by the BUILDIO macro for each width (inb_p for u8, inw_p for u16, inl_p for u32): static inline function taking a u16 port. It reads the port with the matching inb/inw/inl, then calls slow_down_io(), then returns the value read.

name: BUILDIO(bwl, type)
prose: Generated by the BUILDIO macro for each width (outb_p, outw_p, outl_p): static inline function taking the value (u8, u16 or u32) and a u16 port. It writes the value to the port with the matching outb/outw/outl and then calls slow_down_io(). It returns nothing.

name: BUILDIO(bwl, type)
prose: Generated by the BUILDIO macro for each width (outsb, outsw, outsl): static inline function outs##bwl(u16 port, const void *addr, unsigned long count). If cc_platform_has(CC_ATTR_GUEST_UNROLL_STRING_IO) is true it loops count times, writing the next element of that width from addr to the port with outb/outw/outl and advancing the pointer. Otherwise it executes a single 'rep outs' instruction with count repetitions (asm with memory clobber, advancing addr and counting count down). In both cases it reads count elements from addr, and nothing is done when count is 0. It returns nothing.
note: Macro-generated outsb/outsw/outsl (io.h:275-289). Old prose only described the guest-unroll path.

name: BUILDIO(bwl, type)
prose: Generated by the BUILDIO macro for each width (insb, insw, insl): static inline function ins##bwl(u16 port, void *addr, unsigned long count). If cc_platform_has(CC_ATTR_GUEST_UNROLL_STRING_IO) is true it loops count times, reading from the port with inb/inw/inl and storing each element at the advancing addr. Otherwise it executes a single 'rep ins' instruction with count repetitions (asm with memory clobber). In both cases it stores count elements at addr, and nothing is done when count is 0. It returns nothing.
note: Macro-generated insb/insw/insl (io.h:291-305). Old prose only described the guest-unroll path.

name: smap_save
prose: Static inline function that runs an inline-asm alternative selected by X86_FEATURE_SMAP and returns the unsigned long flags. If the CPU has X86_FEATURE_SMAP, the patched code executes pushf, pop into flags, then clac: flags receives the EFLAGS value from before the clac, and clac clears the AC flag, so SMAP checks apply to supervisor accesses to user pages. If the feature is absent the alternative is empty, so the asm writes nothing and the returned local variable flags, which is never initialized in C, has an unspecified value. The asm declares memory and condition-code clobbers. It takes no locks.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: CLAC clears EFLAGS.AC, which makes SMAP enforcement apply to supervisor accesses to user pages; old prose said it disabled the protection (smap.h:38-49). Also removed the 'never fails' claim. Uninitialised flags when SMAP feature absent is per code: asm writes nothing then (smap.h:40-48).
