name: sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export
prose: Precondition: argp points to a kernel copy of a sev_issue_cmd whose data field is a user pointer to a sev_user_data_pdh_cert_export that must be readable and also writable (the function writes it back); writable says whether the file was opened for writing; the caller holds the SEV command lock needed by __sev_do_cmd_locked. Behaviour: it returns -EFAULT if copy_from_user of the input struct fails. If any of the four user addresses or lengths in the input is zero it treats the call as a length query and skips the allocations; otherwise it returns -EFAULT if either requested length exceeds SEV_FW_BLOB_MAX_SIZE, returns -ENOMEM if the first kzalloc fails, and returns -ENOMEM after freeing the first blob if the second fails. If the platform is not in SEV_STATE_INIT it returns -EPERM when writable is false, or tries sev_move_to_init_state and returns its error (the blobs freed) on failure. It then calls __sev_do_cmd_locked(SEV_CMD_PDH_CERT_EXPORT) and always copies the firmware-reported lengths back into the user input struct; if that copy_to_user fails the result is -EFAULT (overriding the command result). Otherwise, if the command returned an error it returns that error, and if the command returned 0 but argp->error is nonzero it warns once and returns 0, in both cases without copying the blob contents. Otherwise it copies the PDH blob and then the cert chain blob to the user addresses, returning -EFAULT if a copy fails. On every path after the INIT-state check it shuts the firmware down with __sev_firmware_shutdown if sev_move_to_init_state requested it, and frees both blobs; the early -EFAULT returns happen before anything was allocated.
note: checked sev-dev.c:2250-2351 (slice cut head). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (copy_to_user(argp->data,&input) at line 2321); round 2 claim consistent with code (returns the __sev_do_cmd_locked error); original claim RIGHT (0 with argp->error set).

name: snp_map_cmd_buf_desc
prose: Precondition: desc points to a cmd_buf_desc with paddr_ptr, len and guest_owned set; if len is nonzero *desc->paddr_ptr is the physical address of the command buffer. Behaviour: if desc->len is 0 it returns 0 and changes nothing. If the descriptor is not guest owned it allocates a bounce buffer with alloc_pages of order get_order(len) (2^order pages, not get_order(len) pages), returning -ENOMEM with nothing changed if that fails; otherwise it saves the original *paddr_ptr in desc->paddr_orig and overwrites *paddr_ptr with the bounce buffer's physical address (no data is copied by this function); for a guest-owned descriptor neither is done. It then calls rmp_mark_pages_firmware(*paddr_ptr, PAGE_ALIGN(len) >> PAGE_SHIFT, true) and returns 0 on success. If that call fails it prints a warning and returns -EFAULT without freeing the bounce buffer and without restoring *paddr_ptr or paddr_orig.
note: checked sev-dev.c:684-714. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (order semantics and no rollback on failure); round 2 RIGHT (paddr_orig only set for non-guest-owned). The old claim that the pages are 'not firmware-owned' after failure was removed: the state left by a failed rmp_mark_pages_firmware is not visible here.

name: sfs_dev_init
prose: Precondition: psp is a valid psp_device with a device psp->dev. Behaviour: it allocates the sfs_device with devm_kzalloc (returning -ENOMEM if that fails) and a 2MB command buffer with snp_alloc_hv_fixed_pages; if that fails it goes to cleanup_dev, returning the initial value -ENOMEM. It marks the buffer uncacheable with set_memory_uc; on failure it frees the HV-fixed pages (without calling set_memory_wb) and cleans up, returning that error. It then sets psp->sfs_data and the dev/psp back-pointers and calls sfs_misc_init; if that fails it restores write-back caching with set_memory_wb, frees the HV-fixed pages and cleans up, returning that error. On success it logs a notice and returns 0 leaving psp->sfs_data set. The cleanup_dev label sets psp->sfs_data to NULL and frees the devm allocation with devm_kfree on all failure paths.
note: slice cut head; real function is sfs_dev_init (sfs.c:251-311), sfs_init does not exist. Old prose said the value of ret on page-allocation failure was 'not set by this path': it is the initial -ENOMEM.

name: sp_pci_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is the PCI device being probed and id->driver_data should point to an sp_dev_vdata. Behaviour: it allocates the sp_device (sp_alloc_struct) and a devm sp_pci, returning -ENOMEM through the e_err label if either fails; it returns -ENODEV (error printed) if id->driver_data is NULL; it calls pcim_enable_device, pci_select_bars and pcim_iomap_regions and returns their errors; it returns -ENOMEM if pcim_iomap_table returns NULL or the BAR chosen by sp->dev_vdata->bar is not mapped; and it calls sp_get_irqs, returning its error via e_err (without sp_free_irqs). After that it sets bus mastering and the PSP master-device callbacks, sets the DMA mask to 48 bits and, if that fails, to 32 bits, going to free_irqs with that error if the 32-bit mask also fails. It stores sp as the device's drvdata and calls sp_init; if that fails it goes to free_irqs with its error. On success it returns 0. free_irqs calls sp_free_irqs and then e_err prints a notice and returns the error; the drvdata is therefore set at the time of an sp_init failure but not for the earlier failures, and the PCI device enable and BAR mappings are released by devres.
note: slice cut head; function is sp-pci.c:231-316. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: sp_get_irqs failure jumps to e_err (line 284-286), so sp_free_irqs is only called for the DMA-mask failure and the sp_init failure.

name: cc_aead_alloc
prose: Precondition: drvdata is the CryptoCell driver data with hw_rev and std_bodies set. Behaviour: this is the whole function cc_aead_alloc; the slice shows its algorithm loop and unwind. It allocates the AEAD handle with devm_kmalloc (-ENOMEM if that fails), initialises its list, stores it in drvdata->aead_handle and allocates MAX_HMAC_DIGEST_SIZE bytes of SRAM workspace with cc_sram_alloc (-ENOMEM via fail1 if it returns NULL_SRAM_ADDR). For each entry of aead_algs it skips (continue) entries whose min_hw_rev exceeds drvdata->hw_rev or whose std_body is not in drvdata->std_bodies, otherwise it creates the algorithm with cc_create_aead_alg (jumping to fail1 with the error from PTR_ERR on failure), registers it with crypto_register_aead (jumping to fail1 with that error on failure, the failed algorithm not being added to the list) and adds it to the handle's list. It returns 0 after the loop. The fail1 label calls cc_aead_free, which unregisters and removes the algorithms already on the list, and then returns the error. The function does not copy tfm or context fields and does not allocate key buffers; those are done elsewhere (cc_aead_init).
note: slice cut head; real function is cc_aead_alloc (cc_aead.c:2611-2668), no cc_aead_init in this slice (cc_aead_init is at line 125 and is a different function). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the code allocates SRAM and registers algorithms; the old prose described a different function.

name: safexcel_send_req
prose: Precondition: base, sreq, src, dst, cryptlen, assoclen, digestsize, iv, commands and results describe a prepared request for ring ring, and ctx->key/ctx->key_len hold the key. Behaviour: the function is safexcel_send_req (the slice begins mid-body). It counts the source entries needed for cryptlen + assoclen, for AEAD adjusts the destination length by the digest size (minus for decrypt, plus otherwise) and copies the ipad/opad state into the context record, and for CBC decrypt first saves the last IV block of the source into areq->iv (these writes happen before any mapping and stay on failure). It returns -EINVAL if the in-place buffer is too small (nr_src <= 0 while a length is nonzero) or if, for src != dst, the source or destination list is too small, and returns -EIO if dma_map_sg of the source fails; if the destination length check or the destination dma_map_sg fails after the source was mapped, it jumps to the unmap label, which unmaps src and, when nr_dst > 0, dst. It then copies the key into the context record, adds command descriptors (a dummy one if the input length is zero, otherwise one per source segment up to the request length), writes the context control and token, and adds result descriptors for the destination (skipping AAD, or a dummy one for the AEAD decrypt with only AAD), returning the PTR_ERR of any failed descriptor allocation after rolling back the result and command ring write pointers added so far and unmapping src (and dst when src != dst). On success it queues the request with safexcel_rdr_req_set, stores the descriptor counts in *commands and *results, and returns 0, leaving the DMA mappings to be released at completion. *commands and *results are not modified on failure.
note: slice cut head; real name is safexcel_send_req (safexcel_cipher.c:673-916). Checked every return. Old prose omitted the source-buffer -EINVAL, the pre-mapping side effects, and that the destination unmap at the unmap label also runs after the destination's own mapping failure.

name: iaa_crypto_debugfs_init
prose: Precondition: none; an __init function. Behaviour: it returns -ENODEV without creating anything if debugfs_initialized() is false. Otherwise it creates the "iaa_crypto" debugfs directory, storing it in iaa_crypto_debugfs_root, then creates the global_stats, wq_stats and stats_reset files (mode 0644) under it, ignoring the return values of the create calls, and returns 0.
note: iaa_crypto_stats.c:258-273. Contract left empty because the return is an errno and it writes global state.

name: kmb_ocs_hcu_do_one_request
prose: Precondition: areq is the ahash request queued on the crypto engine, with its request and transform contexts set up. Behaviour: it finds the HCU device with kmb_ocs_hcu_find_dev and goes to the error label with -ENOENT if there is none. If REQ_FLAGS_HMAC_HW is set it maps the data (kmb_ocs_dma_prepare), runs ocs_hcu_hmac, cleans up the DMA list in any case, and goes to done on success or error on failure, skipping the final buffer wipe. If REQ_FINAL is clear it returns -EINVAL immediately, without wiping the buffer or finalizing the request, when there is no input data; otherwise it maps the data, calls ocs_hcu_hash_update, cleans up the DMA list, then resets buf_cnt and copies the leftover scatterlist data into the request buffer with flush_sg_to_ocs_buffer and goes to done, or to error if any step fails. For a final request it uses ocs_hcu_hash_finup (with DMA mapping and cleanup) when there is data, otherwise ocs_hcu_hash_final, and, for REQ_FLAGS_HMAC_SW, builds the key-xor-opad block plus the digest in the request buffer and hashes it with ocs_hcu_digest; any failing step goes to the error label. After a final request it wipes the request buffer (kmb_ocs_hcu_secure_cleanup) and falls into done. The done label calls crypto_finalize_hash_request with status 0 and returns 0; the error label only wipes the buffer with kmb_ocs_hcu_secure_cleanup and returns the error, so the request is not finalized with an error status.
note: checked keembay-ocs-hcu-core.c:420-568. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG: the error path (565-567) does not call crypto_finalize_hash_request; round 2 RIGHT (final finup/final path and non-update flows); original RIGHT (-EINVAL returned directly). The old prose said the buffer is zeroed on every success; update and HW-HMAC successes skip the wipe (they go to done).

name: adf_set_hb_counters_fail
prose: Precondition: accel_dev->heartbeat->dma.virt_addr points to a table of hb_cnt_pair entries holding at least 2 * max_aes * hb_ctrs entries (max_aes from hw_device->get_num_aes, hb_ctrs from hw_device->num_hb_ctrs), and ae * hb_ctrs + thr is below max_aes * hb_ctrs. Behaviour: it reads the u16 resp_heartbeat_cnt of the pair at index thr_id = ae * hb_ctrs + thr in the first block, increments that pair's req_heartbeat_cnt by one, and then stores the value it read into resp_heartbeat_cnt of the pair at the same index in the second block (offset by max_aes * hb_ctrs entries). It changes no other entry and returns nothing. The comment in the code says it injects live.req != live.rsp, but the code does not guarantee that for arbitrary starting counter values.
note: adf_heartbeat_inject.c:23-40. Reviewer rounds 1, 2 and 15 RIGHT: the second block is written, and live.req != live.rsp is not guaranteed (the old closing claim was dropped).

name: qat_rsa_enc
prose: Precondition: req is an akcipher request on a qat_rsa_ctx. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL if ctx->n or ctx->e is NULL; returns -EOVERFLOW after setting req->dst_len to ctx->key_sz if req->dst_len < ctx->key_sz; returns -EINVAL if req->src_len > ctx->key_sz or if no PKE function id exists for the key size. It fills the request message, then (error value -ENOMEM) maps the source: directly if it is a single scatterlist entry of exactly key_sz bytes, otherwise through a kzalloc'd copy src_align (returning -ENOMEM if that fails); a dma_map_single error goes to the unwind code with -ENOMEM. It does the same for the destination (dst_align) and then maps the input and output parameter blocks; any mapping or allocation failure unwinds the mappings made so far and frees src_align and dst_align with kfree_sensitive and returns -ENOMEM. It then returns the value of qat_alg_send_asym_message; only if that value is -ENOSPC does it unmap everything and free the buffers before returning it; for 0 or any other value the mappings and buffers stay for the completion callback.
note: slice cut head; function is qat_asym_algs.c:698-830. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the DMA-mapping failure paths return -ENOMEM after cleanup (lines 765-766, 780-781, 788-795).

name: otx2_sg_info_create
prose: Precondition: pdev and req are valid; req->in and req->out describe in_cnt and out_cnt gather/scatter entries. Behaviour: it returns NULL (after logging) if in_cnt or out_cnt exceeds OTX2_CPT_MAX_SG_IN_CNT or OTX2_CPT_MAX_SG_OUT_CNT, and NULL if the kzalloc of the info buffer fails. It computes the gather and scatter list lengths, sets info->dlen, in_buffer and out_buffer, writes the 8-byte SG list header, and sets up the gather and scatter components with setup_sgio_components; if either fails it calls otx2_cpt_info_destroy and returns NULL. It sets dma_len and maps in_buffer with dma_map_single (DMA_BIDIRECTIONAL); a mapping error also calls otx2_cpt_info_destroy and returns NULL. On success it sets completion_addr and comp_baddr past the SG lists and returns the info, which holds the DMA mapping to be released with otx2_cpt_info_destroy.
note: slice cut head; real name is otx2_sg_info_create (otx2_cpt_reqmgr.h:449-561); no otx2_cpt_info_create. Old prose omitted the too-many-components and kzalloc NULL returns.

name: otx2_cpt_discover_eng_capabilities
prose: Precondition: cptpf is the CPT physical function with its engine groups and LF state set up. Behaviour: it returns 0 immediately, changing nothing, if cptpf->is_eng_caps_discovered is already true. Otherwise it creates the capability-discovery engine groups (create_eng_caps_discovery_grps) and initialises the LFs with otx2_cptlf_init; either failure jumps to delete_grps with that error (after LF init failure the LFs are not shut down). It then kzallocs a buffer (-ENOMEM, via lf_cleanup, if that fails), maps it with dma_map_single (-EFAULT if the mapping fails), builds a LOAD_FVC command, and for each engine type from 1 to OTX2_CPT_MAX_ENG_TYPES-1 sends it, polls for completion up to a timeout and stores the 64-bit big-endian result in cptpf->eng_caps[etype]; if the poll times out it logs a warning, sets is_eng_caps_discovered to false and returns -ENODEV (capabilities of earlier types having already been stored). If all types complete it sets is_eng_caps_discovered to true and returns 0. On both the success path and the post-mapping failure paths it unmaps and frees the buffer, shuts down the LFs and deletes the engine groups before returning, so that cleanup is not specific to failure.
note: slice cut head; real function is otx2_cpt_discover_eng_capabilities (otx2_cptpf_ucode.c:1489-1596). Old prose said cleanup on failure only; the labels are also reached on success (lines 1580-1596).

name: NX842_COUNTER_INC(comp_complete)
prose: Generated function nx842_inc_comp_complete(dev), a static inline expanded from NX842_COUNTER_INC(comp_complete). Precondition: dev may be NULL; if it is non-NULL, dev->counters must be a valid pointer. Behaviour: if dev is non-NULL it atomically increments dev->counters->comp_complete with atomic64_inc, and otherwise it does nothing; it returns nothing.
note: nx-common-pseries.c:139-145 macro definition and instantiation.

name: NX842DEV_COUNTER_ATTR_RO(comp_complete)
prose: Generated function nx842_comp_complete_show(dev, attr, buf), expanded from NX842DEV_COUNTER_ATTR_RO(comp_complete) through nx842_counter_read. Precondition: buf is a sysfs page of PAGE_SIZE bytes. Behaviour: it takes rcu_read_lock, reads the global devdata pointer with rcu_dereference, and if it is non-NULL writes the value of atomic64_read of the comp_complete counter as "%lld\n" into buf with snprintf limited to PAGE_SIZE, returning the snprintf result; if devdata is NULL it returns 0 and writes nothing to buf. It releases the RCU read lock before returning and keeps no reference; rcu_read_lock may be nested, so the caller may already hold the RCU read lock.
note: nx-common-pseries.c:878-901. Removed the old claim that the caller must not hold the RCU read lock (not required by rcu_read_lock).

name: ahash_setkey
prose: Precondition: tfm is a talitos ahash transform and the transform context's key buffer can hold a key of up to the block size or the digest size. Behaviour: this is the whole function ahash_setkey; the slice shows its tail. If keylen is no more than the block size it copies the key into ctx->key; otherwise it computes the digest of the key with keyhash and returns -EINVAL if that fails (ctx unchanged), or copies the digest into ctx->key and uses the digest size as the key size. It then unmaps the previous key mapping with dma_unmap_single if ctx->keylen was nonzero, sets ctx->keylen to the key size, maps ctx->key with dma_map_single into ctx->dma_key (the mapping result is not checked) and returns 0.
note: slice cut head; function is ahash_setkey (talitos.c:2297-2328). Fixed under the real name instead of dropping.

name: DEF_TALITOS2_INTERRUPT(4ch, TALITOS2_ISR_4CHDONE, TALITOS2_ISR_4CHERR, 0)
prose: Generated function talitos2_interrupt_4ch(irq, data), expanded from DEF_TALITOS2_INTERRUPT(4ch, TALITOS2_ISR_4CHDONE, TALITOS2_ISR_4CHERR, 0). Precondition: data is the struct device whose drvdata is the talitos_private, and the caller does not hold priv->reg_lock. Behaviour: it takes priv->reg_lock with interrupts saved, reads ISR and ISR_LO, acknowledges by writing ICR = isr & (4CHDONE | 4CHERR) and ICR_LO = isr_lo. If isr & 4CHERR or isr_lo is nonzero it releases the lock and calls talitos_error(dev, isr & 4CHERR, isr_lo); otherwise, if isr & 4CHDONE is nonzero, it clears the 4CHDONE bits in IMR and schedules priv->done_task[0], and then releases the lock. It returns IRQ_HANDLED if (isr & (4CHDONE | 4CHERR)) or isr_lo is nonzero, else IRQ_NONE.
note: talitos.c:787-820; matches the macro body (lines 788-817).

name: DEF_TALITOS2_INTERRUPT(ch0_2, TALITOS2_ISR_CH_0_2_DONE, TALITOS2_ISR_CH_0_2_ERR, 0)
prose: Generated function talitos2_interrupt_ch0_2(irq, data), expanded from DEF_TALITOS2_INTERRUPT with the CH_0_2 done and error masks and tasklet index 0. Precondition: data is the struct device whose drvdata is the talitos_private, and the caller does not hold priv->reg_lock. Behaviour: it takes priv->reg_lock with interrupts saved, reads ISR and ISR_LO, acknowledges by writing ICR = isr & (CH_0_2_DONE | CH_0_2_ERR) and ICR_LO = isr_lo. If isr & CH_0_2_ERR or isr_lo is nonzero it releases the lock and calls talitos_error(dev, isr & CH_0_2_ERR, isr_lo); otherwise, if isr & CH_0_2_DONE is nonzero, it clears those bits in IMR and schedules priv->done_task[0], and then releases the lock. It returns IRQ_HANDLED if (isr & (CH_0_2_DONE | CH_0_2_ERR)) or isr_lo is nonzero, else IRQ_NONE.
note: talitos.c:821-822 instantiation of the macro at 787-817.

name: DEF_TALITOS2_INTERRUPT(ch1_3, TALITOS2_ISR_CH_1_3_DONE, TALITOS2_ISR_CH_1_3_ERR, 1)
prose: Generated function talitos2_interrupt_ch1_3(irq, data), expanded from DEF_TALITOS2_INTERRUPT with the CH_1_3 done and error masks and tasklet index 1. Precondition: data is the struct device whose drvdata is the talitos_private, and the caller does not hold priv->reg_lock. Behaviour: it takes priv->reg_lock with interrupts saved, reads ISR and ISR_LO, acknowledges by writing ICR = isr & (CH_1_3_DONE | CH_1_3_ERR) and ICR_LO = isr_lo. If isr & CH_1_3_ERR or isr_lo is nonzero it releases the lock and calls talitos_error(dev, isr & CH_1_3_ERR, isr_lo); otherwise, if isr & CH_1_3_DONE is nonzero, it clears those bits in IMR and schedules priv->done_task[1], and then releases the lock. It returns IRQ_HANDLED if (isr & (CH_1_3_DONE | CH_1_3_ERR)) or isr_lo is nonzero, else IRQ_NONE.
note: talitos.c:823-824 instantiation of the macro at 787-817 with tasklet index 1.

name: virtcrypto_algo_is_supported
prose: Precondition: vcrypto is a virtio_crypto device with its service and algorithm masks set. Behaviour: it computes service_mask = 1u << service (no check that service is below 32, so a larger value is an undefined shift) and, if algo is greater than 31, subtracts 32 from algo and remembers that the high mask applies. It returns false if the service bit is clear in vcrypto->crypto_services. It then picks an algorithm mask by service: for CIPHER cipher_algo_l or cipher_algo_h, for MAC mac_algo_l or mac_algo_h, for HASH hash_algo, for AEAD aead_algo, for AKCIPHER akcipher_algo (HASH, AEAD and AKCIPHER use their single mask regardless of the high/low choice), and for any other service the mask stays 0. It returns false if bit (1u << algo) (with algo already reduced) is clear in that mask (a shift count of 32 or more is again undefined), and true otherwise. It takes no locks.
note: slice cut head; real name is virtcrypto_algo_is_supported (virtio_crypto_mgr.c:243-293). The old claim that it returns false for service > 31 is not in the code (no such check).

name: CXL_ECS_GET_ATTR(threshold)
prose: Generated function cxl_ecs_get_threshold(dev, drv_data, fru_id, val), expanded from CXL_ECS_GET_ATTR(threshold). Precondition: drv_data is an initialised cxl_ecs_context and fru_id indexes one of its media FRUs (the index is not range-checked). Behaviour: it calls cxl_mem_ecs_get_attrbs, which allocates a buffer and reads the current ECS attributes; if that fails it returns its error (-ENOMEM or -EIO) with *val unmodified. Otherwise it stores in *val the value cxl_get_ecs_threshold computes as ecs_supp_threshold[config & 0x7] and returns 0. The table has entries only for indices 3, 4 and 5 (256, 1024, 4096), so indices 0, 1 and 2 give 0, and indices 6 and 7 read past the end of the 6-entry table.
note: checked edac.c:512-535, 541-574, 634-665. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: indices 6 and 7 are out of bounds, not 0; indices 0-2 give 0.

name: cxl_hdm_decode_init
prose: Precondition: cxlds, cxlhdm and info are valid, cxlhdm->regs.hdm_decoder is NULL or a mapped HDM decoder register block, cxlhdm->port is a registered CXL port, and info holds the DVSEC ranges. Behaviour: it reads the HDM global control register if the HDM block exists. If HDM decoding is already enabled, or the HDM block is absent and info->mem_enabled is set, it returns the result of devm_cxl_enable_mem(&port->dev, cxlds): that function sets the DVSEC memory-enable bit, returns 0 without registering a cleanup action if the bit was already set, and otherwise registers a devm action to clear it, returning the action registration's result or a config-space access error. If the HDM block is absent otherwise, it returns -ENODEV. If the block exists but is globally disabled and info->mem_enabled is clear, it calls devm_cxl_enable_hdm (setting the enable bit and registering a devm action to clear it; its error is returned) and then returns devm_cxl_enable_mem's result. If the block exists and info->mem_enabled is set, it walks from the port to the CXL root and returns -ENODEV (after an error message) if no root is found; then, for each DVSEC range, it looks for a child of the root that covers it with device_find_child and releases the found child with put_device, counting allowed ranges; it returns -ENXIO if none is allowed, and 0 otherwise.
note: checked pci.c:446-527, devm_cxl_enable_mem (289-299), cxl_set_mem_enable (261-282). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (no devm action when the memory-enable bit is already set); round 2 RIGHT (absent HDM block with DVSEC memory enabled goes to devm_cxl_enable_mem, not -ENODEV).

name: ACCESS_ATTR_RO(0, read_bandwidth)
prose: Generated function read_bandwidth_access0_show(dev, attr, buf), expanded from ACCESS_ATTR_RO(0, read_bandwidth). Precondition: dev is a CXL region device. Behaviour: it returns -ENOENT if cxlr->coord[0].read_bandwidth is 0; otherwise it writes that value as an unsigned decimal followed by a newline into buf with sysfs_emit and returns the number of bytes written. name: cxl_port_setup_targets
prose: Precondition: port holds a region reference for cxlr whose decoder is a switch decoder, cxled is an endpoint decoder whose memdev is an endpoint of port (cxl_rr_load and cxl_ep_load are assumed to return non-NULL). Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL if cxl_rr->nr_targets is not a power of 2. If cxl_rr->nr_targets_set is nonzero it computes the peer distance up the port chain and checks whether ep->dport is already in cxlsd->target[0 .. nr_targets_set-1]: if so it returns the error of check_last_peer if nonzero, otherwise it leaves nr_targets_set unchanged and returns 0; if not, it skips the decoder setup and goes to the add-target step. If nr_targets_set is zero it computes the parent granularity and ways (from the region and root decoder when the parent is the root, otherwise from the parent port's decoder), the port's eiw and the new granularity, returning the error of granularity_to_eig, ways_to_eiw or eig_to_granularity if one fails, returns -ENXIO if iw exceeds 8 or cxlsd->nr_targets, and then: for an auto-assembled region (CXL_REGION_F_AUTO) it returns -ENXIO if the decoder's ways, granularity (when iw > 1), HPA range or enable flag do not match; otherwise it returns the error of check_interleave_cap if the setting is unsupported, and sets cxld->interleave_ways, interleave_granularity and hpa_range. At the add-target step it returns -ENXIO if nr_targets_set equals nr_targets; for an auto region it returns -ENXIO if cxlsd->target[nr_targets_set] is not ep->dport; otherwise it stores ep->dport and its port_id in cxlsd->target and cxld.target_map at index nr_targets_set. It then increments nr_targets_set (by 1 on the add-target path, by 0 on the already-present path) and returns 0. The decoder fields are written before the add-target check, but on that path nr_targets_set is 0 and nr_targets is at least 1, so the targets-full return cannot be taken after the fields were written; all other error returns happen before any write to the decoder fields or nr_targets_set.
note: slice cut head; function is cxl_port_setup_targets (region.c:1327-1533). Reviewer round 15 only half right: the fields are written at 1494-1498 before the full check at 1504, but that check is unreachable on that path (is_power_of_2 rejects nr_targets == 0, and nr_targets_set == 0 there). Rounds 1 and 2 RIGHT: already-present peer does not increment, and an unseen dport with nr_targets_set > 0 skips decoder field updates.

name: region_offset_to_dpa_result
prose: Precondition: cxlr is a committed CXL region with valid params, the caller holds both the region and dpa rwsems (lockdep-asserted), offset is an offset into the region's resource and result is writable. Behaviour: it derives eig and eiw from the region's interleave granularity and ways with granularity_to_eig and ways_to_eiw (return values ignored); if the root decoder has a spa_to_hpa callback it converts p->res->start + offset with it and takes hpa_offset relative to p->res->start, otherwise hpa_offset is offset. It computes the interleave position: for eiw < 8 the eiw bits starting at bit eig + 8 of hpa_offset, otherwise (hpa_offset >> (eig + 8)) modulo the number of ways. If the position is not below p->nr_targets it logs and returns -ENXIO. It then computes the DPA offset: bits [eig+7:0] of hpa_offset pass through; for eiw < 8 the remaining bits with bits [eig+eiw+7:0] cleared are shifted right by eiw (this also clears those bits in the local hpa_offset); for eiw >= 8 it is ((hpa_offset >> (eig + eiw)) / 3) << (eig + 8). Finally it searches p->targets for the endpoint decoder whose pos equals the position; if found it stores that decoder's memdev in result->cxlmd and cxl_dpa_resource_start(cxled) plus the DPA offset in result->dpa and returns 0; otherwise it logs an error and returns -ENXIO with result untouched.
note: slice cut head; real function is region_offset_to_dpa_result (region.c:3021-3107); no cxl_calc_dpa_offset_and_lookup exists. Old prose took hpa_offset and pos as parameters, which this function does not; the position is computed inside and an out-of-range position returns -ENXIO.

name: trans_stat_store
prose: Precondition: dev is a devfreq device, buf a NUL-terminated string, count its length. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL if df->profile is NULL, and returns count without changing any state if df->max_state is 0 (this check comes before the parsing). Otherwise it parses buf with kstrtoint base 10 and returns -EINVAL if parsing fails or the value is not 0. It then takes df->lock, zeroes stats.time_in_state (max_state entries) and stats.trans_table (max_state * max_state entries), sets stats.total_trans to 0 and stats.last_update to get_jiffies_64(), releases the lock and returns count.
note: slice cut head; function is devfreq.c:1767-1795. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG for this tree: with max_state == 0 the function returns count at line 1777-1778 before total_trans and last_update are touched; old prose put the parse check ahead of the max_state check.

name: exynos_bus_ops_edev(enable_edev)
prose: Generated function exynos_bus_enable_edev(bus), expanded from exynos_bus_ops_edev(enable_edev). Precondition: bus is an initialised exynos_bus whose edev array has edev_count entries, each NULL or a devfreq-event device. Behaviour: it loops over the entries in index order, skips NULL ones, and calls devfreq_event_enable_edev on each other entry; if a call returns a negative value it returns that value immediately; the failing device has already been passed to the call, earlier devices stay as the calls left them, and later entries are not touched. It returns 0 if every call succeeded, including when edev_count is 0.
note: exynos-bus.c:44-59. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the failing device is the one whose call returned the error, so it was not left untouched.

name: at_xdmac_tx_status
prose: Precondition: chan is an at_xdmac channel; txstate may be NULL. Behaviour: it calls dma_cookie_status; if that returns DMA_COMPLETE, or txstate is NULL, it returns that status immediately (no lock and no runtime PM). Otherwise it calls pm_runtime_resume_and_get and returns DMA_ERROR without a residue if that fails. It takes atchan->lock and examines the first descriptor on atchan->xfers_list (not the one selected by the cookie, and the list is assumed non-empty). If that descriptor's transfer is not active it stores the full transfer size as the residue and unlocks. Otherwise, for peripheral-to-memory synchronised transfers it flushes the FIFO (busy-waiting for the flush status bit), then re-reads the next-descriptor, current microblock and INITD registers until they are consistent, up to AT_XDMAC_RESIDUE_MAX_RETRIES; if they never are, it sets the status to DMA_ERROR and unlocks without storing a residue. Otherwise it flushes again, subtracts the sizes of the microblocks already transferred, adds the current microblock's remaining size and stores the result with dma_set_residue. In every path after the runtime PM reference was taken, the lock is released with interrupts restored and the reference is dropped (mark_last_busy and put_autosuspend), and the function returns the status from dma_cookie_status (DMA_IN_PROGRESS) or DMA_ERROR.
note: slice cut head; the real function is at_xdmac_tx_status (at_xdmac.c:1540-1660); no at_xdmac_get_residue exists. Old prose said the cookie selects the descriptor and that DMA_SUCCESS is returned; neither matches the code (first list entry, status from dma_cookie_status).

name: at_xdmac_tasklet
prose: Precondition: the tasklet was scheduled for the channel, atchan->irq_status holds the pending channel status and the caller does not hold atchan->lock. Behaviour: if the channel is cyclic it returns the result of at_xdmac_handle_cyclic, which, under the lock, returns if xfers_list is empty and otherwise takes the head descriptor and, outside the lock, calls its callback only if its flags include DMA_PREP_INTERRUPT. For a non-cyclic channel it takes the lock; if neither AT_XDMAC_CIS_LIS nor any of RBEIS, WBEIS, ROIS is set in irq_status it unlocks and returns. If an error bit is set it calls at_xdmac_handle_error, which does nothing further if pm_runtime_resume_and_get fails (the channel is then not disabled by it), and otherwise logs the errors, disables the channel and waits until the status shows it disabled, and drops its runtime PM reference. It then takes the head descriptor of xfers_list; if it is not active it logs an error, unlocks and returns. Otherwise it completes the descriptor's cookie, removes it from the list, unlocks, invokes the callback only if DMA_PREP_INTERRUPT is set, runs dma_run_dependencies, retakes the lock, splices the descriptor's descs_list onto free_descs_list, calls at_xdmac_advance_work, unlocks and drops the runtime PM reference taken by at_xdmac_start_xfer.
note: checked at_xdmac.c:1702-1790. Matches the old prose on all listed points; added the handle_error pm failure case (reviewer round 2 RIGHT) and the list-empty cyclic case (original reviewer RIGHT).

name: jz4780_dma_tx_status
prose: Precondition: the caller does not hold jzchan->vchan.lock; if the cookie is not on the issued list, jzchan->desc must be non-NULL because it is dereferenced without a check. Behaviour: it takes vchan.lock with interrupts saved and calls dma_cookie_status, which sets the txstate fields (residue 0) when txstate is non-NULL and returns DMA_COMPLETE or DMA_IN_PROGRESS. If the status is DMA_COMPLETE or txstate is NULL it unlocks and returns that status. Otherwise it looks the cookie up on the issued list: if found, the residue is computed for that descriptor from its start; else if the cookie equals the active descriptor's cookie the residue is computed from the current hardware descriptor; else it is 0; the residue is stored with dma_set_residue. If the descriptor found on the issued list is also the active descriptor and the active descriptor's status has JZ_DMA_DCS_AR or JZ_DMA_DCS_HLT set the status becomes DMA_ERROR. The lock is released on every path and the status is returned.
note: checked dma-jz4780.c:641-674 and dma_cookie_status (dmaengine.h:68-83). Reviewer round 15 WRONG: dma_cookie_status returns only DMA_COMPLETE or DMA_IN_PROGRESS via dma_async_is_complete, so the NULL-txstate return is DMA_IN_PROGRESS; the first reviewer claim (no residue when txstate is NULL) is RIGHT.

name: axi_chan_is_hw_enable
prose: Precondition: chan is an initialised AXI DMA channel with valid chip, dw and hdata pointers. Behaviour: it reads DMAC_CHEN as a 64-bit value if hdata->nr_channels >= DMAC_CHAN_16 (16) and as a 32-bit value otherwise. For a channel id below 16 it returns whether bit id of the value is set. For id >= 16 it returns whether bit id + 16 (the channel's bit within the upper 32-bit word, DMAC_CHAN_BLOCK_SHIFT = 32 after BIT(id) >> 16) of the value is set. It has no other side effects.
note: slice cut head; function is axi_chan_is_hw_enable (dw-axi-dmac-platform.c:250-263). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: (BIT(id) >> 16) << 32 is bit id + 16.

name: idxd_drv_enable_wq
prose: Precondition: the caller holds wq->wq_lock (lockdep-asserted). Behaviour: it returns -ENXIO and sets idxd->cmd_status to IDXD_SCMD_DEV_NOT_ENABLED if the device is not IDXD_DEV_ENABLED; -EBUSY with IDXD_SCMD_WQ_ENABLED if the WQ is not disabled; -ENXIO with IDXD_SCMD_WQ_NO_GRP if the WQ has no group; -ENXIO with IDXD_SCMD_WQ_NO_NAME if its name is empty; -ENXIO with IDXD_SCMD_WQ_NO_SVM if it is shared but sharing is unsupported; and -ENXIO with IDXD_SCMD_WQ_NO_THRESH if it is shared with threshold 0. On a configurable device with PASID enabled it may set the WQ's PASID for kernel or shared WQs. It then calls idxd_device_config and idxd_wq_enable and, if either returns a negative value, returns it directly with cmd_status unchanged and without any disable call. It maps the portal with idxd_wq_map_portal (on a negative result sets IDXD_SCMD_WQ_PORTAL_ERR and calls idxd_wq_disable(wq, false), logging if that fails), sets client_count to 0, requests the irq with idxd_wq_request_irq (which does nothing and returns 0 unless the WQ type is kernel; on a negative result sets IDXD_SCMD_WQ_IRQ_ERR, unmaps the portal and disables the WQ, without calling idxd_wq_free_irq), allocates resources with idxd_wq_alloc_resources (on failure sets IDXD_SCMD_WQ_RES_ALLOC_ERR, frees the irq, unmaps the portal and disables) and initialises the percpu ref with idxd_wq_init_percpu_ref (on failure sets IDXD_SCMD_PERCPU_ERR, frees the resources, frees the irq, unmaps the portal and disables). It returns 0 when all steps succeed; the interrupt-related state is set only for kernel-type WQs.
note: checked device.c:1368-1495 and idxd_wq_request_irq (1326-1366). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (non-kernel WQs return 0 from idxd_wq_request_irq without requesting an irq); round 2 and the original claim RIGHT (no free_irq on request failure; cmd_status not set for config/enable failures).

name: perfmon_pmu_init
prose: Precondition: idxd is a valid idxd_device. Behaviour: it returns -ENODEV, allocating nothing, if idxd->perfmon_offset is 0, and -ENOMEM if the idxd_pmu allocation fails. It stores the allocation in idxd->idxd_pmu, names the PMU with sprintf as "dsa<id>" or "iax<id>" by device type (an unknown type goes to the free path with the initial -ENODEV), resets the perfmon registers, reads the capability register, and frees the idxd_pmu and clears idxd->idxd_pmu on the free path if the counter count, counter width, overflow interrupt/counter freeze, event category count or per-counter capability checks reject the hardware. It then records the capabilities, calls idxd_pmu_init and perf_pmu_register(..., -1), freeing the idxd_pmu and clearing idxd->idxd_pmu if registration fails, and returns the registration result (0 on success). The return value after the capability-check rejections is not -ENODEV: rc holds the result of the earlier sprintf (the length of the PMU name, a positive number), so those rejections return a positive value rather than a negative errno.
note: slice cut head; real function is perfmon_pmu_init (idxd/perfmon.c:474-562). Old prose said -ENODEV for unsupported capabilities, but rc is overwritten by sprintf's positive return value (lines 497-505) before the capability checks, so the `goto free` paths at 513-531 return that positive value.

name: sdma_config_channel
prose: Precondition: chan is a DMA channel embedded in a valid sdma_channel with its engine, register mapping and script_addrs set. Behaviour: it calls sdma_disable_channel, clears event_mask[0], event_mask[1], shp_addr and per_addr, and then calls sdma_config_ownership (ignoring its return value) with flags (event_override, mcu_override, dsp_override) of (false, true, true) for IMX_DMATYPE_DSP, (false, true, false) for IMX_DMATYPE_MEMORY and (true, true, false) for every other peripheral type; the function writes the three ownership override registers. It then calls sdma_get_pc and returns its nonzero result immediately, without the rest of the setup. For peripheral types other than MEMORY and DSP: if event_id1 is set it calls sdma_set_watermarklevel_for_p2p for ASRC and ASRC_SP and does nothing more for other types; if event_id1 is not set it calls sdma_set_watermarklevel_for_sais for MULTI_SAI and sets the event_id0 bit in event_mask; it then sets shp_addr to per_address and per_addr to per_address2. For MEMORY and DSP it sets watermark_level to 0. It returns 0.
note: slice cut head; function is imx-sdma.c:1315-1366. Reviewer round 15 not applicable here: the ownership flags per type are in lines 1327-1337 (DSP, MEMORY, default); the claim about CCM/IPU/HDMI concerns sdma_get_pc, which was not re-read line by line. Old prose misdescribed the ownership calls (the flag names are event/mcu/dsp override, not directions).

name: ioat_dca_init
prose: Precondition: pdev is the ioat PCI device and iobase its mapped register base. Behaviour: it returns NULL if system_has_dca_enabled(pdev) is false, if the DCA offset register read is 0, or if ioat_dca_count_dca_slots finds no slots. It allocates a DCA provider sized for the slots with alloc_dca_provider (NULL on failure), fills in iobase, dca_base and max_requesters, and sets the CSI prefetch bit and PCIe memory-write bit in the DCA control registers by read-modify-write if they are clear. It reads the 64-bit APICID tag map, stores its eight bytes masked with DCA_TAG_MAP_MASK in the private data, and if dca3_tag_map_invalid reports the BIOS default map it taints the kernel (TAINT_FIRMWARE_WORKAROUND), warns once, frees the provider and returns NULL. Otherwise it calls register_dca_provider(dca, &pdev->dev); if that fails it frees the provider and returns NULL, and on success it returns the provider.
note: slice cut head; real name is ioat_dca_init (ioat/dca.c:249-333); no ioat3_dca_init exists in this tree. Old prose matches the code except it omitted the control-register writes.

name: src_cnt_flags
prose: Precondition: src_cnt and flags are plain integer arguments (the sum is computed in unsigned arithmetic and returned as int). Behaviour: a pure function. It returns src_cnt + 1 if both DMA_PREP_CONTINUE and DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_P are set in flags (dmaf_p_disabled_continue), otherwise src_cnt + 3 if DMA_PREP_CONTINUE is set, otherwise src_cnt. It has no side effects.
note: prep.c:563-571; dmaf_continue and dmaf_p_disabled_continue at include/linux/dmaengine.h:1290-1300 test the flag bits by name. Contract left empty because the flag values are named constants not visible in the formula.

name: ioat_prep_pq
prose: Precondition: dst has at least two entries (written when the P or Q disable flag is set), src has src_cnt entries and scf src_cnt coefficient bytes. Behaviour: it returns NULL without touching dst if the channel has IOAT_CHAN_DOWN set. Otherwise it sets dst[0] = dst[1] if DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_P is set and dst[1] = dst[0] if DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_Q is set. If DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_P is set and src_cnt is 1 it BUG_ONs when DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_Q is also set, and builds a two-entry source list using src[0] twice with coefficients scf[0] and 0; in this and the normal case it returns the result of __ioat_prep_pq16_lock when src_cnt_flags(src_cnt, flags) is greater than 8 and of __ioat_prep_pq_lock otherwise. Those helpers return NULL when the ring has no space (the lock is released then), and the 16-source helper also returns NULL when no SED entry can be allocated, in which case it returns with the prep_lock still held; on success they return a descriptor with prep_lock left held to keep submission in order.
note: checked prep.c:573-616, 338-460, 462-561 and ioat_check_space_lock (dma.c:463-488). The old prose omitted that the SED-failure NULL return keeps prep_lock held (lines 505-511).

name: ioat_prep_pq_val
prose: Precondition: pq has at least two entries, src has src_cnt entries, scf has src_cnt coefficient bytes, pqres is writable. Behaviour: it returns NULL without touching pq or *pqres if the channel has IOAT_CHAN_DOWN set. Otherwise it sets pq[0] = pq[1] if DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_P is set and pq[1] = pq[0] if DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_Q is set, sets *pqres to 0, and returns the result of __ioat_prep_pq16_lock if src_cnt_flags(src_cnt, flags) > 8, else of __ioat_prep_pq_lock, passing pqres so that a validate operation is built. Those helpers return NULL if the ring has no space (prep_lock released) or, for the 16-source helper, if no SED entry can be allocated (prep_lock still held); on success they return a descriptor with prep_lock left held. The completion path sets bits in *pqres only on a validate failure.
note: checked prep.c:618-644 and the two helpers; same SED-failure lock behaviour as ioat_prep_pq.

name: ioat_prep_pqxor
prose: Precondition: src has src_cnt entries. Behaviour: it returns NULL if the channel has IOAT_CHAN_DOWN set or if src_cnt > MAX_SCF. Otherwise it zeroes the first src_cnt bytes of a stack coefficient table, sets pq[0] = pq[1] = dst, ORs DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_Q into flags, and returns the result of __ioat_prep_pq16_lock if src_cnt_flags(src_cnt, flags) > 8, else of __ioat_prep_pq_lock (no validate result pointer). Those helpers return NULL if the ring has no space (prep_lock released) or, for the 16-source helper, if no SED entry can be allocated (prep_lock still held); on success they return a descriptor with prep_lock left held.
note: checked prep.c:646-670; the coefficient table is memset only up to src_cnt, the rest of scf[MAX_SCF] is uninitialised.

name: start_pending_queue
prose: Precondition: chan is an mmp_pdma_chan whose device is an mmp_pdma_device. Behaviour: if chan->idle is false it returns with no changes. If chain_pending is empty it calls mmp_pdma_free_phy(chan) and returns; that helper does nothing when chan->phy is NULL, and otherwise writes 0 to the channel's DRCMR register of that phy and clears phy->vchan and chan->phy under phy_lock; chan->idle is left unchanged. If chan->phy is NULL it calls lookup_phy(chan), which takes phy_lock and picks the first phy (by priority group) with no vchan, setting its vchan to chan, and returns it or NULL; on NULL start_pending_queue returns without moving anything. Otherwise it moves all of chain_pending to the tail of chain_running, programs the first moved descriptor's physical address with pdev->ops->write_next_addr(chan->phy, ...), calls enable_chan(chan->phy) and sets chan->idle to false. enable_chan returns without doing anything if phy->vchan is NULL; otherwise it writes DRCMR_MAPVLD | phy->idx to the DRCMR register, sets (if byte_align) or clears (otherwise) the DALGN bit for the phy, and ORs the ops' run_bits into the DCSR register.
note: checked mmp_pdma.c:453-494, 396-428, 430-447, 294-317. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (free_phy returns early when phy is NULL, line 436-437); round 2 RIGHT (DALGN bit cleared when byte_align is false); original RIGHT (return when lookup_phy finds nothing).

name: poly_store
prose: Precondition: buf holds count bytes (a NUL-terminated string from sysfs); the MQ DCR mapping ppc440spe_mq_dcr_host is valid. Behaviour: when CONFIG_440SP is defined the function returns -EINVAL immediately (the rest is unreachable in that configuration). Otherwise it returns -EINVAL if count is 0 or greater than 6; parses buf as a base-16 unsigned long with kstrtoul and returns the parse error if it fails; returns -EINVAL if the value has any bit set outside 0x1FF; and otherwise reads DCRN_MQ0_CFBHL, replaces the 8 bits at MQ0_CFBHL_POLY with the low 8 bits of the value (the 0x100 bit is dropped), writes the register back and returns count.
note: slice cut head; function is poly_store (ppc4xx/adma.c:4367-4395). Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG: lines 4372-4375 return -EINVAL under CONFIG_440SP; the old prose was right on that point.

name: st_fdma_prep_slave_sg
prose: Precondition: chan is an ST FDMA channel, sgl a DMA-mapped scatterlist with sg_len entries, direction DMA_MEM_TO_DEV or DMA_DEV_TO_MEM. Behaviour: it returns NULL if st_fdma_prep_common rejects the arguments (chan NULL, sg_len 0 or a non-slave direction, the last case after logging), or if sgl is NULL. It allocates a descriptor with sg_len nodes with st_fdma_alloc_desc, returning NULL after logging 'no memory for desc' if that fails. It marks the descriptor non-cyclic and, for each scatterlist entry, fills a hardware node: next points to the following node (the last wraps to the first), control carries the DREQ line, fill_hw_node sets the common fields, saddr (for DMA_MEM_TO_DEV) or daddr (otherwise) gets the entry's DMA address, and nbytes and generic.length get its DMA length. It sets the end-of-node interrupt bit on the last node and returns the result of vchan_tx_prep(&fchan->vchan, &fdesc->vdesc, flags).
note: slice cut head; function is st_fdma_prep_slave_sg (st_fdma.c:507-558). Old prose matches the code; the 'caller must not free' wording was dropped as not shown in the function.

name: d40_alloc_mask_set
prose: Precondition: phy is a physical channel resource with an initialised lock, first_user is writable; for logical allocation (is_log true) log_event_line is a valid bit index. Behaviour: under phy->lock (irqsave) it sets *first_user to true when (allocated_src | allocated_dst) equals D40_ALLOC_FREE. If is_log is false it requires both allocated_src and allocated_dst to be D40_ALLOC_FREE: then it sets both to D40_ALLOC_PHY and returns true; otherwise it changes nothing and returns false. If is_log is true it works on allocated_src when is_src is true and allocated_dst otherwise: it returns false if that mask is D40_ALLOC_PHY; converts D40_ALLOC_FREE to D40_ALLOC_LOG_FREE (0, a conversion that stays even if the call then fails); and, if the BIT(log_event_line) bit is clear, sets it and returns true, else returns false. The other mask is not touched in the logical case. The lock is released with interrupts restored on every path.
note: checked ste_dma40.c:1767-1819. Reviewer rounds 1 and 15 WRONG: the physical path requires both masks FREE and sets both to D40_ALLOC_PHY (lines 1779-1783).

name: stm32_dma_set_xfer_param
prose: Precondition: chan is an initialised channel with a valid dma_sconfig and threshold, buswidth is writable, direction is DMA_MEM_TO_DEV or DMA_DEV_TO_MEM, and buf_len and buf_addr describe the buffer. Behaviour: for DMA_MEM_TO_DEV it derives the destination (device) bus width and burst from dma_sconfig, sets chan->mem_width to the maximum memory width for the buffer, derives the memory bus width and a memory burst (1 if buf_addr is not aligned to buf_len, else STM32_DMA_MAX_BURST) and builds dma_scr; it updates the FIFO threshold field of chan->chan_reg.dma_sfcr (set from the threshold unless it is STM32_DMA_FIFO_THRESHOLD_NONE), sets dma_spar to the destination address and *buswidth to the destination width. DMA_DEV_TO_MEM is analogous with the source side as the device, and additionally stores the burst values in chan->mem_burst (twice) and sets chan->mem_width. A failing stm32_dma_get_width or stm32_dma_get_burst returns its negative error at that point, with chan->mem_width (and in DEV_TO_MEM chan->mem_burst) possibly already updated, chan->chan_reg.dma_sfcr, dma_spar and dma_scr not yet modified and *buswidth unwritten; any other direction logs and returns -EINVAL. After the switch it calls stm32_dma_set_fifo_config(chan, src_best_burst, dst_best_burst), clears the direction, size and burst fields of chan->chan_reg.dma_scr, ORs in the new dma_scr and returns 0.
note: checked stm32-dma.c:930-1075. Reviewer round 15 WRONG: stm32_dma_set_fifo_config is called at line 1066; rounds 1-2 RIGHT: mem_burst is only set in DEV_TO_MEM while mem_width is set in both. The clause 'apart from nothing' was removed: the dma_sfcr FTH update only happens after the width/burst lookups succeed.

name: stm32_dma3_chan_irq
prose: Precondition: devid is the stm32_dma3_chan, and the caller does not hold chan->vchan.lock; chan->swdesc is valid whenever a transfer-complete interrupt with TCIE enabled is reported. Behaviour: it takes chan->vchan.lock (spin_lock, not irqsave) and reads MISR; if the channel's MIS bit is clear it unlocks and returns IRQ_NONE with no other change. Otherwise it reads CSR and the enabled-interrupt bits of CCR; if TCF and TCIE are set it calls vchan_cyclic_callback for a cyclic descriptor or stm32_dma3_chan_complete otherwise; if USEF and USEIE are set it logs, sets chan->dma_status to DMA_ERROR, calls stm32_dma3_check_user_setting and stm32_dma3_chan_reset; if ULEF and ULEIE are set, or DTEF and DTEIE are set, it logs, sets DMA_ERROR and calls stm32_dma3_chan_reset. It then masks csr with (ccr | CCR_HTIE) and, if the result is nonzero, writes it to CFCR to clear those flags; it unlocks and returns IRQ_HANDLED.
note: slice cut head; real name is stm32_dma3_chan_irq (stm32-dma3.c:1006-1064); no stm32_dma3_chan_irq_handler. Checked each branch.

name: get_host_pd0
prose: Precondition: length is a u32. Behaviour: a pure function that returns (DESC_TYPE_HOST << DESC_TYPE) | length computed in u32, where DESC_TYPE_HOST is 0x10 and DESC_TYPE is 27, so the type contribution is 0x10 << 27 = 0x80000000 (bit 31). Any bits of length at bit 27 and above are OR-ed in unmasked (bit 31 is already set by the type). It has no side effects.
note: cppi41.c:17-18 (DESC_TYPE 27, DESC_TYPE_HOST 0x10) and 516-524. All three reviewer values were WRONG: the host type is 0x10 shifted by 27, giving 0x80000000, not 1<<26 or 2<<26.

name: edma_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is the platform device for an EDMA3 controller with either an OF node or platform data. Behaviour: with an OF node it matches the binding, calls edma_setup_info_from_dt and returns its error (via PTR_ERR) if it fails; it returns -ENODEV if there is no info at all, the error from dma_set_mask_and_coherent(32 bits), -ENOMEM if the edma_cc allocation fails, -ENODEV if no memory resource exists (looked up as "edma3_cc" then index 0), and the error of devm_ioremap_resource; none of those paths has set the platform drvdata yet. It then sets the drvdata to ecc, enables runtime PM and calls pm_runtime_get_sync, on failure calling pm_runtime_disable and returning the error without a put. Later failures (edma_setup_from_hw, allocation of the slave/slot/mask arrays -> -ENOMEM, irq-name allocation -> -ENOMEM, devm_request_irq) go to err_disable_pm, which calls pm_runtime_put_sync and pm_runtime_disable and returns the error; failures after the dummy slot was allocated (a failed edma_alloc_slot returns its error to err_disable_pm; the tc_list allocation -> -ENOMEM, and the registration of the slave or memcpy dma_device) go to err_reg1, which frees the dummy slot and falls into err_disable_pm; if the memcpy registration fails the slave device is unregistered first. In the non-legacy path errors from of_parse_phandle_with_fixed_args stop the loop but are not returned. The OF DMA controller registration result is ignored. On success it returns 0 with the controller registered, runtime PM enabled and a runtime PM usage reference held; the drvdata remains set to ecc after any failure that came after platform_set_drvdata.
note: slice cut head; function is edma_probe (edma.c:2286-2554). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (drvdata set only at line 2345, after the early returns).

name: udma_check_tx_completion
prose: Precondition: work is the tx_drain.work of a udma_chan, called from a workqueue where sleeping is allowed, with uc->vc.lock not held. Behaviour: it loops: it takes uc->vc.lock (irqsave); if uc->desc is non-NULL it saves the previous tx_drain residue and timestamp and sets desc_done from udma_is_desc_really_done (which refreshes the tx_drain residue and timestamp for a PDMA TX channel); desc_done keeps its old value (true on the first pass) when uc->desc is NULL. If desc_done is false it computes the time and residue differences since the previous poll; if the residue changed it unlocks, sleeps for a delay derived from the drain rate with usleep_range and loops again; if it did not change it schedules tx_drain.work again after HZ (one second) and leaves the loop. If desc_done is true and uc->desc is non-NULL it decrements the byte counters by d->residue, calls udma_start and vchan_cookie_complete and leaves the loop; if uc->desc is NULL it leaves the loop. The lock is released with the saved flags on every exit from the loop. If uc->desc becomes NULL during a sleep, desc_done stays false and the next pass reuses the stale residue and time values, so the outcome (another sleep or a one-second reschedule) depends on the stale difference rather than being necessarily a reschedule.
note: checked k3-udma.c:1086-1153. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (residue_diff/time_diff are stale when desc is NULL after a sleep, so it may sleep and loop again); round 2 and original RIGHT.

name: f1x_lookup_addr_in_dct
prose: Precondition: nid is a node id for edac_mc_find and in_addr and dct select the system address and DCT to search. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL if edac_mc_find(nid) finds no memory controller. Otherwise, for each chip-select row of the DCT that is enabled (csrow_enabled), it fetches the base and mask with get_cs_base_and_mask and compares (in_addr & ~mask) with (base & ~mask); on the first match it stops and returns that row if the family is 0x15 with model 0x30 or later, or else the value of f10_process_possible_spare, which returns the row, or the first row whose base has bit 0x2 set when the online-spare swap is done and the matched row is the bad DRAM chip select. If no enabled row matches it returns -EINVAL. It takes no locks of its own.
note: checked amd64_edac.c:2214-2256 and f10_process_possible_spare (2189-2204). Old prose fine; added the family-0x15 shortcut and the -EINVAL for no match. Contract left empty because the function reads device state.

name: i82975x_init
prose: Precondition: called once at module load. Behaviour: it calls opstate_init, then pci_register_driver(&i82975x_driver) and, if that returns a negative value, goes to fail0 which calls pci_dev_put(mci_pdev) and returns that value (during registration the probe may already have set mci_pdev through i82975x_init_one, which takes a reference with pci_dev_get when mci_pdev is NULL). If registration succeeded and mci_pdev is still NULL it finds the Intel 82975_0 device with pci_get_device (storing the referenced device in mci_pdev), going to fail1 with -ENODEV if none exists, and otherwise calls i82975x_init_one on it, going to fail1 with -ENODEV (replacing the original error) if that returns a negative value. fail1 unregisters the driver and falls into fail0, which calls pci_dev_put(mci_pdev), leaving the mci_pdev pointer itself unchanged. It returns 0 if mci_pdev was already set after registration or the init_one succeeded.
note: checked i82975x_edac.c:644-684 and the pci_dev_get at line 601-602. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (the probe path through pci_register_driver can set mci_pdev, so pci_get_device may be skipped); round 2 RIGHT (init_one takes no extra reference on the pci_get_device path).

name: EDAC_SCRUB_ATTR_SHOW(addr, read_addr, u64, "0x%llx\n")
prose: Generated function addr_show(ras_feat_dev, attr, buf), expanded from EDAC_SCRUB_ATTR_SHOW(addr, read_addr, u64, "0x%llx\n"). Precondition: the attribute is a scrub attribute whose instance indexes a valid ctx->scrub[inst] with non-NULL scrub_ops and a non-NULL read_addr callback, and buf is the sysfs page buffer. Behaviour: it calls ops->read_addr(parent device, private, &data); if that returns nonzero it returns that value, otherwise it returns the result of sysfs_emit(buf, "0x%llx\n", data), normally the number of bytes written, or a negative error from sysfs_emit if buf is not page aligned.
note: scrub.c:38-55. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: sysfs_emit can return -EINVAL for an unaligned buffer (not shown in the function).

name: skx_init
prose: Precondition: called once at module load; it inspects global state itself. Behaviour: it returns -EBUSY if ghes_get_devices() is nonzero or another EDAC owner than this module exists, and -ENODEV if running under a hypervisor or if the CPU is not in skx_cpuids. It then stores the res_config, reads the top-of-memory registers with skx_get_hi_lo and returns its error directly (nothing to undo yet). It then calls skx_get_all_bus_mappings: a negative result goes to the fail label; a zero result returns -ENODEV without calling skx_remove; a positive result is the socket count. For each entry of skx_all_munits it calls get_all_munits (negative goes to fail; a count differing from per_socket * sockets sets -ENODEV and goes to fail), then for each socket reads the source id with skx_get_src_id (negative goes to fail) and registers each of its memory controllers with skx_register_mci (negative goes to fail). Success continues with skx_set_decode, the optional ADXL decode setup when nvdimm_count is nonzero, opstate_init, skx_setup_debug("skx_test") and mce_register_decode_chain, and returns 0. The fail label calls skx_remove and returns rc, so cleanup also happens when skx_get_all_bus_mappings itself returns a negative value.
note: checked skx_base.c:561-695. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the fail label is reached from the first negative skx_get_all_bus_mappings result (line 590-591); the old prose said only after controllers were found.

name: iso_resource_work
prose: Precondition: work is the delayed work of an iso_resource r with a client reference held by this work item. Behaviour: under client->lock it reads the bus generation and r->todo, and, when todo is ISO_RES_ALLOC and the last bus reset was less than one second ago, reschedules itself after 333 ms and sets skip; otherwise skip is set for ISO_RES_REALLOC when r->generation already equals the current generation. It sets free for ISO_RES_DEALLOC, ISO_RES_ALLOC_ONCE and ISO_RES_DEALLOC_ONCE, and stores the generation in r->generation (also in the skip case). If skip it jumps to out. Otherwise it calls fw_iso_resource_manage; if the channel result is -EAGAIN for an ALLOC or REALLOC request it jumps to out (no event, no free). It computes success (channel >= 0 or bandwidth > 0). Under the lock, if r->todo is still ISO_RES_ALLOC it becomes ISO_RES_REALLOC, and if r->todo is ISO_RES_REALLOC, success is false, the client is not shutting down and xa_erase removes the resource, it drops one extra client reference and sets free. For todo == ISO_RES_ALLOC and channel >= 0 it stores 1 << channel in r->channels. For ISO_RES_REALLOC with success it jumps to out without queueing an event. Otherwise it takes the e_alloc event (todo ISO_RES_ALLOC or ISO_RES_ALLOC_ONCE) or the e_dealloc event (all other todos, including a failed REALLOC), fills in the handle, channel and bandwidth and queues it with queue_event (the queued event buffer is owned by the client queue afterwards). If free is set it cancels the delayed work and kfree's r->e_alloc and r->e_dealloc (only the buffer not used for the queued event is still non-NULL) and r. The out label always drops one client reference.
note: checked core-cdev.c:1317-1409. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the queued event is not freed here (its pointer was set to NULL before kfree); rounds 1 and 2 RIGHT (skip/EAGAIN return silently, REALLOC success returns silently); the old prose also said the ALLOC skip returns 'within one second of the last reset' which matches line 1330-1333.

name: ffa_memory_attributes_get
prose: Precondition: none; func_id is a 32-bit function id. Behaviour: a pure function returning u16. It returns 0 if func_id equals FFA_FN_NATIVE(MEM_LEND) or FFA_MEM_LEND, and otherwise returns FFA_MEM_NORMAL | FFA_MEM_WRITE_BACK | FFA_MEM_INNER_SHAREABLE, which is BIT(5) | (3 << 2) | 3 = 0x2F. It reads only func_id and has no side effects.
note: slice cut head; function is ffa_memory_attributes_get (arm_ffa/driver.c:665-675). Constants checked in include/linux/arm_ffa.h: FFA_MEM_LEND is FFA_SMC_32(0x72), not 0x84000001, and the attribute value is 0x2F, not 0x7, so the old prose was wrong on both.

name: scmi_clock_state_get
prose: Precondition: ph is a protocol handle whose private data holds the clock_info; enabled should point to a writable bool. Behaviour: it performs no clock-domain lookup and no NULL check of its own; it returns the result of ci->clock_config_get(ph, clk_id, NULL_OEM_TYPE, NULL, enabled, NULL, atomic), the clock config getter installed for the protocol version. For the version installed as scmi_clock_config_get it returns -EINVAL if enabled is NULL and otherwise performs a CLOCK_ATTRIBUTES transfer, setting *enabled on success; the version scmi_clock_config_get_v2 accepts a NULL enabled and only writes it on success. The result is 0 on success or a negative error from the transfer setup or transfer.
note: checked clock.c:866-873, 836-864 (scmi_clock_config_get), and the v2 getter above it. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the NULL check is in the callee, not in this function, and the v2 callee accepts NULL; round 2 RIGHT (no clk_id lookup).

name: scmi_powercap_validate
prose: Precondition: none. Behaviour: a pure function. It returns -EPROTO if min_val or max_val is 0; -EPROTO if configurable is true and min_val equals max_val, or if configurable is false and min_val differs from max_val; -EPROTO if min_val differs from max_val and step_val is 0; and 0 otherwise. No other value is returned and nothing is modified.
note: powercap.c:177-192. Contract left empty because the return is an errno name.

name: sdei_to_linux_errno
prose: Precondition: none; sdei_err is an unsigned long firmware status. Behaviour: a pure switch with no side effects: SDEI_NOT_SUPPORTED (-1) gives -EOPNOTSUPP, SDEI_INVALID_PARAMETERS (-2) gives -EINVAL, SDEI_DENIED (-3) gives -EPERM, SDEI_PENDING (-5) gives -EINPROGRESS, SDEI_OUT_OF_RESOURCE (-10) gives -ENOMEM, and every other value, including SDEI_SUCCESS, gives 0.
note: arm_sdei.c:118-134, constants in include/uapi/linux/arm_sdei.h:41-45. Contract left empty because the prose lists errno names.

name: NVRAM_READ_VAL(u8)
prose: Generated function nvram_read_u8(prefix, postfix, name, val, allset, fallback), expanded from NVRAM_READ_VAL(u8). Precondition: name is a NUL-terminated string, prefix and postfix are NUL-terminated or NULL, val is writable. Behaviour: it looks the variable up with get_nvram_var (which, when fallback is set and the first lookup returns -ENOENT with a prefix, retries without the prefix) and returns without changes if the lookup returns a negative value. It trims the value with strim and parses it with kstrtou8 (base 0); if parsing fails it logs a warning that names the variable, the value and the error and returns without changing *val. If allset is nonzero and the parsed value equals allset it returns without changing *val. Otherwise it stores the value in *val. It returns nothing.
note: bcm47xx_sprom.c:65-89. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the parse-failure path logs a warning (pr_warn), so the function can have another effect.

name: cper_print_proc_arm
prose: Precondition: proc points to a CPER ARM processor error section whose section_length is trusted only as checked below, length is the size of the CPER record buffer, pfx is a NUL-terminated prefix. Behaviour: it prints the MIDR, then computes len = section_length - (sizeof(*proc) + err_info_num * sizeof(error info)); if len is negative or section_length exceeds length it prints diagnostics ("too small" or "too big") and returns without printing anything else. Otherwise it prints MPIDR, affinity level and running/PSCI state according to proc->validation_bits, then for each of the err_info_num error-info structures prints the error count, the flags selected by its validation bits, the error type (noting reserved bits), error_info (also decoded with cper_print_arm_err_info), virtual fault address and physical fault address as flagged. It then walks the context-info structures: for each it prints the index, computes the 16-byte-aligned size (reading ctx_info->size before checking it against len), and returns after printing 'section length is too small' and 'firmware-generated error record is incorrect' if the size exceeds the remaining len, or after printing 'Invalid context type' if the type is above the table maximum; otherwise it prints the register context type, hex-dumps its data, subtracts the size from len and advances. If len is still positive afterwards it hex-dumps the remaining bytes as vendor-specific error info. It returns nothing and allocates nothing.
note: slice cut head; real name is cper_print_proc_arm (cper-arm.c:248-345). Old prose omitted the up-front MIDR print and the early return on a bad section_length (lines 249-262).

name: efi_earlycon_write
prose: Precondition: the font and screen_info (lfb_width, lfb_height, lfb_linelength) are set up, the cursor globals efi_x, efi_y, cur_line_y, max_line_y are initialised, and str holds num bytes. Behaviour: it returns nothing. It repeatedly takes a chunk of text up to the next newline, limited to what fits on the current line, and draws it scanline by scanline: for each of the font->height scanlines it maps the framebuffer line with efi_earlycon_map and returns from the whole function immediately if the map returns NULL (leaving the rest of str undrawn, earlier scanlines of the chunk possibly drawn, and efi_x and efi_y not yet advanced for the chunk); it unmaps each line after drawing it. After a chunk it advances num, str and efi_x; if the next character is a newline it consumes it and moves to the start of the next text line (efi_x = 0, efi_y += font->height), and it does the same wrap if the next glyph would pass the right edge. If the next line would exceed lfb_height it records the cursor x in efi_x_array[cur_line_y], advances cur_line_y modulo max_line_y, lowers efi_y by one text row, calls efi_earlycon_scroll_up and clears the last text row's scanlines with efi_earlycon_clear_scanline; a map failure inside scroll_up or clear_scanline only ends that helper, not efi_earlycon_write. Every successful mapping is unmapped before moving on.
note: slice cut head; function is efi_earlycon_write (earlycon.c:145-216). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (helpers return on their own map failure, lines 107-114); round 2 RIGHT on newline vs space and the unchanged cursor on map failure.

name: efi_init
prose: Precondition: called once during early boot on an architecture using the FDT UEFI parameters. Behaviour: it calls efi_get_fdt_params(&data), which returns the EFI system table address (a u64, 0 meaning no UEFI information), and returns immediately if that is 0. It calls efi_memmap_init_early and panics if it returns a negative value; warns if the memory descriptor version is not 1. If uefi_init(efi_system_table) returns a negative value it calls efi_memmap_unmap and returns without further setup. Otherwise it calls reserve_regions, early_init_dt_check_for_usable_mem_range, efi_find_mirror, efi_esrt_init and efi_mokvar_table_init, reserves the memory-map pages with memblock_reserve, and, if CONFIG_X86, CONFIG_SYSFB or CONFIG_EFI_EARLYCON is enabled, calls init_screen_info. It returns nothing and leaves the memory map mapped on the success path.
note: slice cut head; function is efi_init (efi-init.c:233-278). Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG: efi_get_fdt_params returns the u64 table address and 0 means failure (line 239-241), not a negative value.

name: efi_random_get_seed
prose: Precondition: EFI boot services and variable services are callable. Behaviour: it locates the EFI RNG protocol (on failure the RNG seed size is 0 and the failing status is remembered) and reads the size of the "RandomSeed" variable; if neither the RNG nor a variable is available it returns that locate_protocol status immediately, before any allocation and before looking at a bootloader table. Otherwise it looks for an existing LINUX_EFI_RANDOM_SEED_TABLE_GUID table, using it only if its size is at most 512 (a smaller-or-zero or larger table is ignored), and allocates a pool buffer for the combined size, going to err_warn (returning the allocate_pool status, without freeing) if that fails. It fills it with EFI_RANDOM_SEED_SIZE bytes from GetRng (raw algorithm, falling back to any algorithm on EFI_UNSUPPORTED), and then with the "RandomSeed" variable, which counts only if both reading and deleting it succeed (otherwise that region is zeroed). If no bytes were obtained it frees (after zeroing) the buffer and returns the last status. Otherwise it appends the used previous table bytes, sets the size and installs the buffer with install_configuration_table; on failure it zeroes and frees the buffer and returns that status, leaving the old table in place. On success it zeroes and frees the previous table only if its bytes were used (size at most 512 and nonzero), and returns EFI_SUCCESS. Failures of GetRng or of the variable steps are ignored when other bytes were obtained.
note: checked libstub/random.c:65-179 (slice cut head). Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG: with neither RNG nor variable the function returns at line 82-83 before get_efi_config_table is called; round 1 RIGHT (set_efi_var failure does not by itself fail the function when bytes exist).

name: riscv_enable_runtime_services
prose: Precondition: runs once as an early initcall after the EFI boot state and memory map are initialised. Behaviour: it returns 0 (after a message) if EFI_BOOT is not enabled. Otherwise it unmaps the early memory map and remaps it with efi_memmap_init_late(efi.memmap.phys_map, desc_size * nr_map); if that fails it prints an error and returns 0. If efi_soft_reserve_enabled() it walks the memory descriptors and, for each with EFI_MEMORY_SP, kzallocs a 'Soft Reserved' IORESOURCE_MEM resource (IORES_DESC_SOFT_RESERVED) and inserts it into iomem_resource; if kzalloc fails it WARNs and stops the walk, keeping the already-inserted resources. It then returns 0 if efi_runtime_disabled() or if EFI_RUNTIME_SERVICES is already set in efi.flags. Otherwise it calls efi_virtmap_init; if that returns false it logs an error and returns -ENOMEM (the soft-reserve work stays done); if it returns true it calls efi_native_runtime_setup, sets EFI_RUNTIME_SERVICES in efi.flags and returns 0.
note: checked riscv-runtime.c:66-130. Reviewer rounds 2 and 15 RIGHT: a kzalloc failure only stops the soft-reserve loop, it does not fix the final return value, which is still -ENOMEM if efi_virtmap_init fails.

name: gsmi_exec
prose: Precondition: gsmi_dev.param_buf, smi_cmd and handshake_type are set up; func and sub are the command bytes. The function itself takes no lock and shares gsmi_dev's buffer, so concurrent callers must serialise externally. Behaviour: it builds cmd = (sub << 8) | func and triggers the SMI with inline assembly using the configured handshake (set carry and wait for the handler to clear it for GSMI_HANDSHAKE_CF, spin spincount iterations after the outb for GSMI_HANDSHAKE_SPIN, or only the outb for GSMI_HANDSHAKE_NONE), reading the status from AX. It then maps the status: GSMI_SUCCESS to 0; GSMI_VAR_NOT_FOUND to 1; invalid parameter to -EINVAL; buffer too small to -ENOMEM; GSMI_UNSUPPORTED and GSMI_UNSUPPORTED2 to -ENOSYS (logged unless sub is the handshake-type command); not ready to -EBUSY; GSMI_DEVICE_ERROR to -EFAULT; GSMI_NOT_FOUND to -ENOENT; GSMI_LOG_FULL to -ENOSPC; the three handshake codes GSMI_HANDSHAKE_SPIN, GSMI_HANDSHAKE_CF and GSMI_HANDSHAKE_NONE (0x7d, 0x7e, 0x7f) are returned unchanged as the result; any other status logs an unknown-error message and gives -ENXIO.
note: gsmi.c:190-304. Old prose was wrong on the handshake status values (they are 0x7d-0x7f, not 10-12); reviewer round 1 only partially RIGHT: the function does not take the lock, which matches the old wording, but callers are not verified here.

name: imx_sc_to_linux_errno
prose: Precondition: none; errno may be any int. Behaviour: a pure lookup with no side effects: if 0 <= errno < IMX_SC_ERR_LAST (12) it returns imx_sc_linux_errmap[errno], namely 0, -EINVAL, -EINVAL, -EINVAL, -EACCES, -EACCES, -ERANGE, -EEXIST, -EPERM, -EPIPE, -EBUSY, -EIO for errno 0 to 11; for any other value it returns -EIO.

name: psci_to_linux_errno

name: hotplug_tests
prose: Precondition: nb_available_cpus, tos_resident_cpu and the CPU topology are initialised. Behaviour: it allocates a cpumask (returning -ENOMEM at once if that fails), builds the CPU groups with alloc_init_cpu_groups (on a negative result it frees the cpumask and returns -ENOMEM, not the helper's error value) and allocates one page buffer (on failure it frees the groups and the cpumask and returns -ENOMEM). Otherwise it calls down_and_up_cpus on cpu_online_mask, then on each CPU group (printing the group's CPU list), adding the returned numbers of unexpected errors, frees the page buffer, the groups and the cpumask, and returns the accumulated error count (0 when nothing unexpected happened). The first call's count is assigned to err and each group's count is added to it.
note: psci_checker.c:186-229. Contract left empty because of the errno return and the global state it reads.

name: TRACE_EVENT(scm_smc_request,
prose: Generated function trace_scm_smc_request(a0, smc), a static inline expanded from TRACE_EVENT(scm_smc_request, ...). It returns nothing; when the scm_smc_request tracepoint is enabled it calls the registered probes with a0 and smc, and does nothing otherwise. smc must point to an arm_smccc_args. The probe's record fill (not this wrapper) stores smc_id = a0, svc_id = (args[0] >> 8) & 0xFF, cmd_id = args[0] & 0xFF, args_cnt = min(args[1] & 0xF, 6) and copies that many words from args[2] onward into a dynamic array.

It returns nothing; when the tracepoint is enabled it calls the registered probes with its arguments, and does nothing otherwise. smc_res must point to an arm_smccc_res. The probe's record fill stores ret, smc_id and smc_res->a0 to a3 (as res, res0, res1, res2).
