name: sysfb_unregister
prose: Precondition: the caller serialises access to the file-level pd (sysfb_disable and sysfb_init hold disable_lock). Behaviour: returns false without changing anything if pd is NULL or an error pointer. Otherwise it calls platform_device_unregister(pd), sets pd to NULL and returns true.
note: sysfb.c:44-53.

name: sysfb_disable
prose: Precondition: may sleep; dev may be NULL. Behaviour: it takes disable_lock and calls sysfb_parent_dev(&screen_info), which returns the PCI device that owns the screen_info framebuffer (with a device reference held), NULL if there is none, or an error pointer. If dev is NULL, or the parent is NULL, or dev equals the parent, it calls sysfb_unregister and sets disabled to true; an error pointer is neither NULL nor equal to a device, so with a non-NULL dev it changes nothing. It releases disable_lock and returns nothing. It never drops the reference that sysfb_parent_dev took on a valid parent, so that reference is left held.
note: checked sysfb.c:67-79 and sysfb_parent_dev (124-140). Old prose matches; the error-pointer case is now stated.

name: sysfb_handles_screen_info
prose: Precondition: none. Behaviour: returns true when screen_info_video_type(&screen_info) is nonzero and false otherwise; it only reads the global screen_info and takes no lock or reference.
note: sysfb.c:93-98.

name: sysfb_init
prose: Precondition: runs as an __init initcall and may sleep. Behaviour: it applies screen_info fixups, takes disable_lock and, if sysfb is already disabled, returns 0 without registering anything. Otherwise it applies the EFI quirks and looks up the parent with sysfb_parent_dev; if that returns an error pointer it returns the error with nothing registered and no parent reference held. Then, if sysfb_parse_mode reports a simple-framebuffer compatible mode, it tries sysfb_create_simplefb into pd and, if that succeeds, goes to put_device. Otherwise it picks a legacy name by video type (ega-, vga-, vesa-, efi-framebuffer, else platform-framebuffer), allocates the platform device (-ENOMEM on failure), sets its parent to the looked-up device, sets the efifb fwnode, adds the screen_info as platform data and calls platform_device_add; if the data or add call fails it calls platform_device_put (leaving the pd pointer set to that device) and returns the error. In every path after the lookup it calls put_device(parent) (a no-op for NULL), releases disable_lock and returns the result (0 on success).
note: checked sysfb.c:142-221. Reviewer round 1 RIGHT (simplefb failure falls back to the legacy device). Added the pd pointer being left as is after platform_device_put on the error paths (lines 214-215).

name: tegra_ivc_total_queue_size
prose: Precondition: queue_size is an unsigned int; the sum with the header size must not wrap if the result is to be meaningful. Behaviour: it returns 0 after logging an error that includes the function name, queue_size and the required alignment if queue_size is not a multiple of TEGRA_IVC_ALIGN (64); otherwise it returns queue_size + sizeof(struct tegra_ivc_header), which is 128 (two 64-byte unions: tx and rx). It has no other effects.
contract: /*@ requires queue_size <= 4294967167; ensures ((queue_size % 64 != 0) ==> result == 0) && ((queue_size % 64 == 0) ==> result == queue_size + 128); */
note: checked ivc.c:53-70 (struct size 2 x TEGRA_IVC_ALIGN = 128) and 562-571. Old prose and contract said the header is 64 bytes, which was wrong; the contract only describes the return value, the error log is the only other effect.

name: tf_prepare_idle
prose: Precondition: none; mode is an unsigned long. Behaviour: for TF_PM_MODE_LP0, LP1, LP1_NO_MC_CLK, LP2 and LP2_NOFLUSH_L2 it calls tf_generic_smc(TF_CPU_PM, <the matching TF_CPU_PM_S* code>, cpu_boot_addr); for TF_PM_MODE_NONE it issues no SMC. For each of those six modes it then sets the global tf_idle_mode to mode and returns 0. For any other mode it issues no SMC, leaves tf_idle_mode unchanged and returns -EINVAL.
note: trusted_foundations.c:65-100. Contract left empty because it writes a global and returns an errno.

name: altera_cvp_write
prose: Precondition: mgr->priv is the altera_cvp_conf with a nonzero priv->block_size, buf holds count readable bytes and is accessed as 32-bit words (so it should be 4-byte aligned), and the CVP write init succeeded. Behaviour: it sends count bytes in blocks of min(block_size, remaining) using altera_cvp_send_block, incrementing conf->sent_packets once per block. Before each block, if priv->wait_credit exists it calls it with the bytes sent so far and returns its nonzero status at once (the data sent so far stays sent, fewer than count bytes). When altera_cvp_chkcfg is set and the bytes sent so far are a multiple of 4 KiB after a block, it calls altera_cvp_chk_error and returns the status if it is negative (nonnegative values are ignored). After all blocks it returns 0 if altera_cvp_chkcfg is clear, or the result of altera_cvp_chk_error(mgr, count) if it is set.
note: altera-cvp.c:432-483. Reviewer rounds 1, 2 and 15 RIGHT (early wait_credit return, short final block, u32 access of buf).

name: feature_id
prose: Precondition: none; value is a 64-bit DFH register value. Behaviour: it extracts DFH_ID (bits 11:0) and DFH_TYPE (bits 63:60) and returns FEATURE_ID_FIU_HEADER (0xfe) when the type is DFH_TYPE_FIU (4), the 12-bit ID when the type is DFH_TYPE_PRIVATE (3), and FEATURE_ID_AFU (0xff) when the type is DFH_TYPE_AFU (1). For any other type it executes WARN_ON(1) and returns 0.
note: dfl.c:966-980 and dfl.h:72-82. Old prose had the wrong constants (FIU is type 4 and ID 0xfe, AFU is 0xff); all three reviewer notes about the constants were RIGHT.

name: i2cr_get_command
prose: Precondition: address fits in 31 bits (it is shifted left by one in 32-bit arithmetic); parity is a bool. Behaviour: it shifts address left by one, then calls i2cr_check_parity32 on the shifted value with parity as the starting value, which toggles that bool once for every set bit of the shifted value; if the result is true it sets bit 0 of the shifted value. It returns that value. The returned word's population count has the same parity as the starting parity value.
note: fsi-master-i2cr.c:39-72. Contract states only the shift (true); the parity bit is described in the prose.

name: fsi_occ_submit
prose: Precondition: request holds at least req_len bytes (req_len at least 2), response holds at least *resp_len bytes, resp_len is non-NULL. Behaviour: it first sets *resp_len to 0; then returns -ENODEV without locking if dev has no OCC driver data and -EINVAL without locking if the caller's response size was below 7. It checksums the request, takes occ->occ_lock interruptibly (returning that error on failure), sets occ->client_buffer to response, client_buffer_size to the caller's size and client_response_size to 0, and returns -ENOENT via done if occ->buffer is NULL. It allocates a sequence number, writes the request to SRAM (occ_putsram), triggers the attention (occ_trigger_attn) and polls the response header with occ_getsram until the response is ready (-ETIMEDOUT after OCC_TIMEOUT_MS), failing with the error of any SRAM access; it returns -EMSGSIZE if the response data length + 7 exceeds the caller's size, re-reads the whole response when the data length is above 1, and verifies the checksum with occ_verify_checksum (its error is returned). On success it stores data length + 7 in client_response_size. At done it sets *resp_len to occ->client_response_size (0 unless the response was verified) and releases occ->occ_lock, returning the result.
note: checked fsi-occ.c:465-599. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (*resp_len comes from occ->client_response_size, set at line 592/505, and is zeroed up front); round 2 RIGHT (NULL occ->buffer returns -ENOENT).

name: cs5535_gpio_set_irq
prose: Precondition: group and irq are unsigned ints. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL without touching hardware if group > 7 or irq > 15. Otherwise it reads MSR_PIC_ZSEL_HIGH with rdmsr, replaces the 4-bit field of the low word at bit position group * 4 with irq (the upper word is written back unchanged) and writes the MSR with wrmsr, returning 0.
note: gpio-cs5535.c:148-162. Contract left empty because it accesses an MSR and returns an errno.

name: sprd_pmic_eic_toggle_trigger
prose: Precondition: chip is the PMIC EIC gpio_chip and offset a line number. Behaviour: it returns nothing. It reads the irq's trigger type and, if neither the rising nor the falling edge bit (IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH mask) is set, returns without touching any register. Otherwise it reads the EIC data bit with sprd_pmic_eic_get (0, 1 or a negative regmap error), then loops: if the value is nonzero (including a negative error) it writes IEV to 0, else to 1; it re-reads the data bit and, if the new value differs from the previous one, logs a warning, adopts the new value and repeats the write. When two consecutive reads agree it sets the IE bit and then the TRIG bit of the line to 1. The return values of the register updates are ignored; the loop is unbounded while the input keeps changing.
note: gpio-pmic-eic-sprd.c:233-260. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG: the IE and TRIG updates are at lines 257-259; round 2 RIGHT (get can return a negative error); the old prose said the early return happens when IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH is not included, but the test is whether either edge bit is set.

name: gpiod_direction_output_nonotify
prose: Precondition: desc is a valid GPIO descriptor. Behaviour: it normalises value (inverting it if GPIOD_FLAG_ACTIVE_LOW is set, else !!value). It returns -EIO if the line is used as an enabled IRQ. If GPIOD_FLAG_OPEN_DRAIN is set it tries gpio_set_config(PIN_CONFIG_DRIVE_OPEN_DRAIN); if that succeeds it goes to set_output_value; otherwise, if the value is high, it emulates open drain by calling gpiod_direction_input_nonotify and, on success, setting GPIOD_FLAG_IS_OUT and returning 0 (returning the input call's error if it fails); if the value is low it falls through to set_output_value. Open source is symmetric (emulated by switching to input when the value is low). With neither flag it calls gpio_set_config(PIN_CONFIG_DRIVE_PUSH_PULL) and ignores its result. At set_output_value it calls gpio_set_bias, returning its error, and then returns the result of gpiod_direction_output_raw_commit, which returns -ENODEV if the chip guard cannot be obtained, -EIO if the chip has neither set() nor direction_output() or if it has no direction_output() and reports a non-output direction, the negative error of get_direction/direction_output/set (a positive callback result becomes -EBADE), and otherwise 0 with GPIOD_FLAG_IS_OUT set. gpio_set_config errors are never returned.
note: checked gpiolib.c:3008-3066, 2901-2953, 2793-2808, 2885-2899, 2722-2751. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG: the emulation path does call gpiod_direction_input_nonotify and return its error (3054-3057); rounds 1 and 2 RIGHT (config errors are not propagated; no -EOPNOTSUPP is reachable through the guards).

name: amdgpu_acpi_enumerate_xcc
prose: Precondition: none; it initialises the globals itself. Behaviour: it initialises amdgpu_acpi_dev_list and numa_info_xa, then for each id below AMD_XCC_MAX_HID looks up the ACPI device with HID "AMD<AMD_XCC_HID_START + id>"; at the first id with no device it stops (the loop ends, returning 0). For a found device it kzallocs an amdgpu_acpi_xcc_info; if that fails it logs, drops the ACPI device reference and returns -ENOMEM (nothing to free). Otherwise it stores the ACPI handle, drops the device reference, and calls amdgpu_acpi_get_xcc_info; on failure it frees the xcc_info and goes on to the next id. It then gets the existing device info for the returned sbdf, or creates one with amdgpu_acpi_dev_init if none exists; if amdgpu_acpi_dev_init returns -ENOMEM it frees the xcc_info and returns -ENOMEM; if no dev_info results (another failure) it frees the xcc_info and continues. Otherwise it appends the xcc_info to dev_info->xcc_list. It returns 0 after the loop. Earlier attachments are kept when an -ENOMEM return happens.
note: checked amdgpu_acpi.c:1093-1154. Matches the old prose; reviewer round 2 claim (nothing to free on kzalloc failure) is consistent with line 1119-1123. Contract left empty because the prose names -ENOMEM and the function writes globals.

name: trap_mask_map_hw_to_sw
prose: Precondition: none; mask is a 32-bit SPI_GDBG_PER_VMID_CNTL register value. Behaviour: a pure function. It returns the EXCP_EN field of mask (bits 12:4, shifted down to bits 8:0), with KFD_DBG_TRAP_MASK_TRAP_ON_WAVE_START (1 << 30) added when TRAP_ON_START (bit 14) is set and KFD_DBG_TRAP_MASK_TRAP_ON_WAVE_END (1 << 31) added when TRAP_ON_END (bit 15) is set. It reads no other state.
note: amdgpu_amdkfd_gfx_v12.c:261-272; field positions in gc_12_0_0_sh_mask.h:27240-27250 (EXCP_EN mask 0x1FF0, TRAP_ON_START 0x4000, TRAP_ON_END 0x8000) and include/uapi/linux/kfd_ioctl.h:925-926. All three old claims (mask & 0x3FF, bits 8/9) were wrong.

name: amdgpu_amdkfd_gpuvm_alloc_memory_of_gpu
prose: Precondition: adev and drm_priv are valid, mem is writable, offset may be NULL, flags select VRAM, GTT, or (otherwise) a CPU-domain allocation. Behaviour: with VRAM set it allocates in VRAM (or GTT when adev->apu_prefer_gtt is set); with GTT in GTT; otherwise the domain is CPU/GTT and flags must request USERPTR (returns -EINVAL if offset is NULL or *offset is 0) or DOORBELL/MMIO_REMAP (returns -EINVAL if size > UINT_MAX, -ENOMEM if the sg table cannot be created, using *offset as the address) or it returns -EINVAL. It kzallocs *mem (-ENOMEM via the err label if that fails), halves size for an AQL queue and returns -EINVAL (after the unwind) if the page-aligned size is 0. It reserves the memory limit (error returned after unwinding), creates the GEM object (error returned after unreserving the limit), allows the vma node for drm_priv, creates the GEM handle (those two failures unwind without an explicit unreserve, since dropping the GEM object frees the BO), fills in the kgd_mem (BO, va, domain, process_info) and adds it to the process BO list. For USERPTR it calls init_user_pages; for DOORBELL/MMIO_REMAP it pins the BO to GTT; otherwise, if the process has an unsignalled eviction fence, it validates the BO against it. Failures of those three steps remove the mem from the list, delete the GEM handle, revoke the vma node and then drop the GEM object reference (which frees the kgd_mem) or kfree *mem, free the sync object and the sg table; the error is returned and *mem is left dangling. On success it stores amdgpu_bo_mmap_offset(bo) in *offset if offset is non-NULL and returns 0.
note: checked amdgpu_amdkfd_gpuvm.c:1691-1889 (slice cut the head). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: drm_vma_node_allow and drm_gem_handle_create failures go to err_reserve_limit (line 1872) without unreserving the limit.

name: amdgpu_bo_list_ioctl
prose: Precondition: filp->driver_priv is the amdgpu_fpriv and data is a writable drm_amdgpu_bo_list. Behaviour: for every operation it first calls amdgpu_bo_create_list_entry_array on args->in (copying bo_number entries of bo_info_size bytes from bo_info_ptr), returning its error (-EINVAL for too many entries, -ENOMEM, -EFAULT or the memdup error) with *args untouched. CREATE builds a list with amdgpu_bo_list_create and allocates a handle with idr_alloc under bo_list_lock; a negative idr_alloc result puts the new list and returns it. DESTROY calls amdgpu_bo_list_destroy(fpriv, handle) and sets the output handle to 0 (success is returned whether or not that handle existed). UPDATE builds a list and swaps it in with idr_replace; an error pointer from idr_replace puts the new list and returns PTR_ERR(old), otherwise the old list is put. Any other operation returns -EINVAL. On every failure the info array is freed with kvfree, a just-created list is put and *args is not modified. On success it zeroes *args, stores the handle in args->out.list_handle, frees info and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; function is amdgpu_bo_list.c:223-295. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: DESTROY does not report a missing handle (the destroy helper returns void). The old prose also named the wrong input field (bo_info_ptr, not bo_list_ptr).

name: amdgpu_connector_dvi_detect
prose: Precondition: connector is an amdgpu DVI/HDMI-family connector, force requests forced detection, and the caller holds no runtime PM reference. Behaviour: unless running in the kms poll worker it takes a runtime PM reference with pm_runtime_get_sync; if that fails it calls pm_runtime_put_autosuspend and returns connector_status_disconnected immediately (no mark_last_busy, no scratch register update). If detected_hpd_without_ddc was set it clears it and forces detection. If not forced and amdgpu_connector_check_hpd_status_unchanged says so, it returns connector->status (through exit). If a ddc_bus exists it probes DDC; if the probe fails, force is false and HPD is sensed, it sets detected_hpd_without_ddc, schedules the hotplug work for one second later and returns the initial connector_status_disconnected through exit (without updating the scratch registers). If the probe succeeded it frees and re-reads the EDID: no EDID gives connector_status_connected with broken_edid set; a digital EDID gives connected and sets use_digital; an analog EDID on a shared DDC line gives disconnected (after freeing the EDID); amdgpu_connector_shared_ddc may then adjust the status. If connected and digital, or for DVI-D and HDMI-A connectors, it goes to out; if not forced it goes to out, returning connector->status when the last detection was by load (otherwise the current ret); if forced and dac_load_detect is set it asks the first DAC/TVDAC encoder with a detect hook: with a valid EDID result and status not connected it uses the encoder's detect result and updates use_digital and detected_by_load; with a broken EDID it only updates use_digital and keeps ret. At out it calls amdgpu_connector_update_scratch_regs(connector, ret). Unless in the poll worker it then marks the device last busy and puts the autosuspend reference, and returns ret.
note: slice cut the head; function is amdgpu_connectors.c:1011-1155. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (pm_runtime_get_sync failure path returns before mark_last_busy and the scratch update, lines 1024-1027).

name: amdgpu_device_reinit_after_reset
prose: Precondition: reset_context is valid. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL if reset_context->reset_device_list is NULL. Otherwise it computes full_reset and init_level (AMDGPU_INIT_LEVEL_DEFAULT for AMD_RESET_METHOD_ON_INIT, AMDGPU_INIT_LEVEL_RESET_RECOVERY otherwise), sets r to 0 and, for each device in the list, sets its init level. If full_reset is set it clears the DPC status and RAS error state and calls amdgpu_device_asic_init; if that fails it only logs and r keeps the error. If it succeeds it runs ip resume phase 1 (failure jumps to out), checks VRAM loss, creates a coredump unless AMDGPU_SKIP_COREDUMP is set, increments the VRAM-lost counter if lost, then calls amdgpu_device_fw_loading (on failure it returns that error immediately, without setting asic_reset_res), restores the XCP partition mode, runs resume phase 2, enables the TTM buffer functions if the ring is ready, runs phase 3, fills the reset magic if VRAM was lost, registers the GPU instance, adds an XGMI device for a standalone multi-node GPU, runs late init, resumes the DRM client, resumes RAS (a device in RMA state gives r = -EINVAL), and updates the XGMI topology if a hive exists (its result becomes r). Any of those failures jumps to out with r set; at out, if r is 0 it sets the init level to DEFAULT, runs the IRQ reset-resume helper and the IB ring tests (a failing test sets r to -EAGAIN and returns -EAGAIN immediately); if r is nonzero it stores r in tmp_adev->asic_reset_res and continues with the next device. With full_reset clear the phases are skipped and every device goes through the r == 0 branch. The final return value is r from the last processed device (0 if it succeeded), so errors of earlier devices are overwritten, apart from the immediate -EAGAIN return.
note: checked amdgpu_device.c:5999-6136. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (VRAM-lost check, coredump and counter come before fw_loading, lines 6039-6051); round 2 RIGHT (loop continues and the later device overwrites r; non-full reset also runs the IRQ helper and ring tests).

name: amdgpu_discovery_set_ip_blocks
prose: Precondition: adev is a valid amdgpu_device. Behaviour: for the legacy ASICs (Vega10/12/20, Raven, Arcturus, Aldebaran and Cyan Skillfish without the SKILLFISH2 flag) it calls amdgpu_discovery_init (failure is ignored), the ASIC's reg_base_init and fills in ip_versions and counts; for Cyan Skillfish2 it runs amdgpu_discovery_reg_base_init and returns -EINVAL if that fails, then the harvest/gfx/mall/vcn info helpers; for any other ASIC it runs amdgpu_discovery_reg_base_init and returns its error (after drm_err) if it fails, then the same info helpers. It then initialises the SoC config and sysfs, sets adev->family from the GC IP version (returning -EINVAL for an unknown version, and setting AMD_APU_IS_VANGOGH in apu_flags for 10.3.1), sets AMD_IS_APU for the APU GC versions and for SMUIO 13.0.3/13.0.11 when get_pkg_type reports AMDGPU_PKG_TYPE_APU, and assigns the nbio, hdp, df, smuio and lsdma function tables by IP version (left unchanged for unrecognised versions). It then registers IP blocks in this order, returning the error of the first failing helper: common, GMC; for SR-IOV VFs PSP then IH; otherwise IH and, when the firmware load type is PSP, PSP; SMU when the load type is PSP; display; GC; SDMA; SMU again when the load type is DIRECT (not SR-IOV VF) or RLC_BACKDOOR_AUTO with amdgpu_dpm == 1; MM; MES; VPE; UMSCH_MM; ISP. Blocks registered before a failing helper stay registered. It returns 0 if all succeed.
note: slice cut head; function is amdgpu_discovery.c:2559-3175 (checked 2559-3175). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the DIRECT/RLC_BACKDOOR_AUTO SMU registration happens after SDMA (lines 3143-3153), and SMU for PSP load happens before display (3129-3137).

name: amdgpu_ring_init
prose: Precondition: adev, ring and ring->funcs are valid; max_dw, hw_prio and sched_score as used by the caller. Behaviour: it chooses sched_hw_submission (the module value, at least 256 for a KIQ ring, 8 for a MES ring, 256 for the first SDMA page ring). If ring->adev is NULL it returns -EINVAL if adev->num_rings is already AMDGPU_MAX_RINGS; otherwise it sets ring->adev, num_hw_submission and sched_score, assigns the next ring index, stores the ring in adev->rings, increments num_rings and calls amdgpu_fence_driver_init_ring (returning its error, after the ring was already registered). It then gets five writeback slots (rptr, wptr, fence, trail_fence, cond_exe) with amdgpu_device_wb_get, returning the first error and leaving the slots obtained so far allocated; it fills in the matching GPU/CPU addresses and sets the cond_exe value to 1. For a non-CPER ring it calls amdgpu_fence_driver_start_ring (error returned), computes the maximum IB dwords, raises max_dw with a WARN if it is too small and sets ring_size to roundup_pow_of_two(max_dw * 4 * sched_hw_submission); for a CPER ring it sets ring_size from max_dw * 4, count_dw and zeroes wptr and the rptr value, without starting the fence ring. It sets buf_mask, ptr_mask and cached_rptr = 0, allocates ring_backup if NULL (-ENOMEM on failure) and, if ring_obj is NULL, creates the ring buffer object in GTT with amdgpu_bo_create_kernel (on failure it frees ring_backup with kvfree, does not set the pointer to NULL, and returns the error) and clears it. It stores max_dw and hw_prio, takes a stub fence for vmid_wait and, unless ring->no_scheduler is set or the ring type is not below AMDGPU_HW_IP_NUM, appends &ring->sched to the gpu_sched list for its type and priority and increments num_scheds. It returns 0.
note: slice cut head; function is amdgpu_ring.c:232-392. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: ring_backup is freed without being reset (line 374) and amdgpu_ring_fini (401-425) frees ring_backup again and never frees trail_fence_offs.

name: amdgpu_sdma_reset_engine
prose: Precondition: instance_id selects a valid SDMA instance of adev, and the caller does not hold that instance's engine_reset_mutex. Behaviour: it returns -EOPNOTSUPP without locking if adev is an SR-IOV VF. Otherwise it takes sdma_instance->engine_reset_mutex; if caller_handles_kernel_queues is false it stops the scheduler work queues of the instance's GFX ring and (when adev->sdma.has_page_queue) its page ring. If the instance has a stop_kernel_queue hook it calls it for the gfx ring and for the page ring when present. It calls amdgpu_sdma_soft_reset, which returns -EOPNOTSUPP if the instance has no soft_reset_kernel_queue hook; on failure it logs an error and skips restarting the queues, otherwise it calls the start_kernel_queue hook (if present) for the same rings. If caller_handles_kernel_queues is false and the reset succeeded it force-completes the rings' fences and restarts their scheduler work queues (on failure they stay stopped). It releases the mutex and returns the reset result (0 or a negative errno).
note: slice cut head; the real function is amdgpu_sdma_reset_engine(adev, instance_id, caller_handles_kernel_queues) at amdgpu_sdma.c:553-613, not amdgpu_sdma_reset_instance; the rings are derived inside from the instance.

name: amdgpu_vcn_resume
prose: Precondition: i is a VCN instance index; for a non-harvested instance vcpu_bo is expected to be set, and when saved_bo is NULL the instance's fw must be non-NULL (its header is read even for a PSP load). Behaviour: it returns 0 without doing anything if the instance is harvested (bit i of harvest_config) and -EINVAL if vcpu_bo is NULL. If saved_bo is non-NULL it copies it into the VCPU buffer with memcpy_toio only if drm_dev_enter succeeds (paired with drm_dev_exit), then always kvfrees saved_bo and sets it to NULL. If saved_bo is NULL and the firmware load type is not PSP, it copies the ucode into the start of the buffer only when drm_dev_enter succeeds, then in all cases advances past the ucode size and zeroes only the remaining bytes with memset_io (the ucode region is left untouched when drm_dev_enter fails); if the load type is PSP it zeroes the whole buffer with memset_io. It returns 0.
note: slice cut head; function is amdgpu_vcn.c:366-407. Reviewer rounds 2 and 15 RIGHT: when drm_dev_enter fails for a non-PSP load only the bytes after the ucode are zeroed (lines 400-403); the memset_io is not guarded by drm_dev_enter.

name: amdgpu_vram_mgr_new
prose: Precondition: man, tbo, place and res are valid and the caller does not hold mgr->lock. Behaviour: it returns -ENOMEM if the amdgpu_vram_mgr_resource cannot be allocated; it initialises the TTM resource and, if ttm_resource_manager_usage(man) exceeds the usable VRAM size (mc_vram_size, minus AMDGPU_VM_RESERVED_VRAM for non-kernel BOs), it finalises the resource, frees it and returns -ENOSPC. It sets the buddy allocation flags from the placement and BO flags (top-down, contiguous, cleared, range) and, for a contiguous GFX12 DCC BO with a DCC alignment, enlarges the request. Under mgr->lock it allocates blocks with gpu_buddy_alloc_blocks in a loop; when a contiguous request fails with -ENOSPC and the place does not itself demand TTM_PL_FLAG_CONTIGUOUS (pages_per_block is ~0ul only for contiguous BOs) it clears the contiguous flag, lowers pages_per_block and retries; any other buddy error frees the allocated blocks, releases the lock, finalises the resource, frees it and returns that error. On success it records the current pid and comm, appends the resource to mgr->allocated_vres_list, optionally trims the DCC block, releases the lock, computes base.start and the visible usage from the blocks, sets TTM_PL_FLAG_CONTIGUOUS in the placement if the blocks are contiguous, sets the bus caching (cached for XGMI connected to the CPU, otherwise write-combined), adds the visible usage to mgr->vis_usage, stores the resource in *res and returns 0.
note: slice cut head; function is amdgpu_vram_mgr.c:442-625 (this tree uses gpu_buddy). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the retry also requires pages_per_block == ~0ul (line 547-548).

name: gfx_v10_0_rlc_resume
prose: Precondition: adev is an initialised amdgpu_device with the firmware load type and PSP autoload support determined. Behaviour: if the load type is AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_PSP and psp.autoload_supported is set, it waits for the RLC autoload to complete (returning its error), initialises the clear-state buffer, sets the SPM vmid to 0xf and, unless the device is an SR-IOV VF, enables the RLC SRM, then returns 0. Otherwise, for an SR-IOV VF it only initialises the clear-state buffer and returns 0. For a non-VF it stops the RLC, writes 0 to the RLC CGCG/CGLS control register (clock gating off) and to RLC_PG_CNTL (power gating off), then loads the RLC microcode with gfx_v10_0_rlc_load_microcode if the load type is AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_DIRECT (returning its error) or enables backdoor autoload if it is AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_RLC_BACKDOOR_AUTO (returning its error); other load types do neither. It then initialises the clear-state buffer, sets the SPM vmid to 0xf, starts the RLC, and, for AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_RLC_BACKDOOR_AUTO, waits for autoload completion (returning its error). It returns 0 otherwise.
note: slice cut head; function is gfx_v10_0.c:5567-5624. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG for this tree: the code writes mmRLC_CGCG_CGLS_CTRL and mmRLC_PG_CNTL (5593-5596); round 2 RIGHT (microcode load only for AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_DIRECT).

name: gfx_v12_0_rlc_resume
prose: Precondition: adev is an initialised amdgpu_device whose firmware load type and SR-IOV role are known and whose gfx.rlc.funcs stop/start callbacks are set. Behaviour: if the load type is AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_PSP it initialises the clear-state buffer and, unless the device is an SR-IOV VF, enables the RLC SRM, then returns 0 without stopping or starting the RLC. For any other load type, an SR-IOV VF only initialises the clear-state buffer and returns 0; otherwise it stops the RLC, writes 0 to the RLC_CGCG_CGLS_CTRL (clock gating) and RLC_PG_CNTL (power gating) registers, loads the RLC microcode with gfx_v12_0_rlc_load_microcode only if the load type is AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_DIRECT, returning its error immediately on failure (that function returns -EINVAL when adev->gfx.rlc_fw is NULL or its header major version is not 2, in which case the RLC stays stopped with CG/PG disabled, the clear-state buffer not initialised and the RLC not started), then initialises the clear-state buffer, starts the RLC and returns 0.
note: slice cut head; function is gfx_v12_0.c:2070-2106 and gfx_v12_0_rlc_load_microcode (2042-2068). Reviewer rounds 2 and 15 RIGHT: a NULL rlc_fw is handled with -EINVAL, so a valid blob is not a precondition.

name: vcn_v3_0_stop
prose: Precondition: vinst points to a valid amdgpu_vcn_inst of an initialised amdgpu_device. Behaviour: it returns 0 at once, touching nothing, if the instance's bit is set in adev->vcn.harvest_config. If AMD_PG_SUPPORT_VCN_DPG is set in pg_flags it calls vcn_v3_0_stop_dpg_mode (which waits on status registers but ignores the wait results and returns 0) and goes to done with r = 0, skipping the VCPU reset and the clock/power-gating steps. Otherwise it waits for UVD_STATUS idle, for the LMI write/read-clean bits and, after stalling the UMC arbitration, for the UMC read/write-clean raw bits, going to done with the error of the first wait that fails. If all waits succeed it blocks VCPU register access, resets the VCPU, disables the VCPU clock, applies the LMI and LMI_UMC soft resets, clears UVD_STATUS, enables clock gating and static power gating, and falls into done. At done, if adev->pm.dpm_enabled it calls amdgpu_dpm_enable_vcn(adev, false, i) and then returns r (0 or the failed wait's error).
note: checked vcn_v3_0.c:1594-1711. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (a harvested instance returns before the dpm disable, lines 1639-1640); round 2 RIGHT (the DPG path always returns 0); the original claim (DPG path returns without VCPU reset) RIGHT.

name: vega10_ih_irq_init
prose: Precondition: adev is an initialised amdgpu_device whose IH rings adev->irq.ih, ih1 and ih2 have ring_size, doorbell and register offsets configured. Behaviour: it calls vega10_ih_toggle_interrupts(adev, false) and returns its error if nonzero; calls nbio.funcs->ih_control; on CHIP_RENOIR reads mmIH_CHICKEN, sets MC_SPACE_GPA_ENABLE if irq.ih.use_bus_addr is set and writes it back. For each of ih, ih1, ih2 whose ring_size is nonzero it calls vega10_ih_enable_ring and returns the first error immediately. Unless the device is an SR-IOV VF it calls nbio.funcs->ih_doorbell_range with irq.ih's use_doorbell and doorbell_index. It then calls pci_set_master, calls vega10_ih_toggle_interrupts(adev, true) and returns its error if nonzero, sets irq.ih_soft.enabled to true when irq.ih_soft.ring_size is nonzero, and returns 0. On an early error return the remaining steps are not performed.
note: slice cut head; function is vega10_ih.c:261-307 (the packet name vega10_ih_irq_enable does not exist). Old prose matches the code; the rings iterated are only ih, ih1 and ih2 (ih_soft is handled separately).

name: destroy_queue_cpsch
prose: Precondition: q belongs to qpd on dqm; the caller must hold q->process->mutex (wait_on_destroy_queue releases and re-takes it) and must not hold the dqm lock. Behaviour: for an SDMA or SDMA_XGMI queue it first reads the queue counter from user memory and only logs a failure (the counter then counts as 0). It takes the dqm lock and calls wait_on_destroy_queue, which returns -EBUSY (leaving q->properties.is_being_destroyed set) if the queue is already being destroyed, otherwise sets the flag and, if debug trap is enabled and the queue is suspended, waits interruptibly for it to resume (resetting the flag and returning the wait's error on interruption); it does nothing and returns 0 if the process device is missing or qpd is in debug mode. A nonzero return releases the dqm lock and is returned. If qpd->is_debug it resets is_being_destroyed to false and returns -EBUSY. Otherwise it deallocates the doorbell, for SDMA queues deallocates the sdma queue and adds the read counter to the process device's sdma_past_activity_counter, and, if the queue is active, decrements the queue count, clears is_active and runs execute_queues_cpsch (setting qpd->reset_wavefronts on -ETIME) or, with MES, remove_queue_mes; the result becomes the return value. It then unlinks the queue from qpd's list, decrements qpd->queue_count and dqm->total_queue_count, releases the dqm lock, raises the EC_DEVICE_QUEUE_DELETE debug event and frees the MQD, returning 0 for an inactive queue or the unmap/remove result (which can be a negative error even though the queue was removed and freed). is_being_destroyed stays true on those paths.
note: checked kfd_device_queue_manager.c:2561-2654 and wait_on_destroy_queue (2527-2559). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (mutex precondition); original reviewer RIGHT (error returned after the queue was removed).

name: kfd_signal_hw_exception_event
prose: Precondition: pasid is a PASID; the function may be called from workqueue context. Behaviour: it looks up the KFD process with kfd_lookup_process_by_pasid, which takes a reference on it; if there is none it returns. Otherwise it calls lookup_events_by_type_and_signal(p, KFD_EVENT_TYPE_HW_EXCEPTION, NULL) to signal the process's hardware-exception events and drops the process reference with kfd_unref_process. It returns nothing.
note: slice cut head; function is kfd_events.c:1195-1209 and matches the old prose. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG for this function: it does look up by pasid and call lookup_events_by_type_and_signal (lines 1202-1207); that description fits a different function in this file.

name: init_event_waiter
prose: Precondition: p, waiter and event_data are valid and the caller holds p->event_mutex. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL, without touching waiter, if lookup_event_by_id finds no event for event_data->event_id. Otherwise, under ev->lock, it sets waiter->event, sets waiter->activated to ev->signaled, clears ev->signaled if it was set and the event is not auto-reset, and, if the event is KFD_EVENT_TYPE_SIGNAL and event_data->signal_event_data.last_event_age is nonzero, sets waiter->event_age_enabled to true (even when the ages are equal) and sets waiter->activated to true if ev->event_age differs from last_event_age. If waiter->activated is false it adds the waiter to ev->wq. It releases ev->lock and returns 0.
note: kfd_events.c:841-868. Matches the old prose; reviewer round 2's note (age-enabled even when equal) is consistent with it.

name: kfd_wait_on_events
prose: Precondition: p is a kfd_process, data points to num_events user kfd_event_data entries, user_timeout_ms and wait_result are writable; the caller does not hold p->event_mutex. Behaviour: it converts the timeout, allocates the waiter array (-ENOMEM on failure, going to the exit that sets *wait_result to KFD_IOC_WAIT_RESULT_FAIL), takes p->event_mutex and for each event copies its data from user memory (-EFAULT on failure) and calls init_event_waiter (its -EINVAL for a bad id is returned); any such failure unlocks via out_unlock. It tests the wait condition once; if it is COMPLETE it copies the signalled event data back to user memory and returns that result (-EFAULT possible); if the test returns FAIL it WARNs and goes to out_unlock. Otherwise it drops the mutex and loops: a fatal signal gives -EINTR; any other pending signal gives -ERESTARTSYS and, unless the timeout was IMMEDIATE or INFINITE, updates *user_timeout_ms with the remaining time; otherwise it sleeps until the condition changes or the timeout expires. After the loop it retakes the mutex and, if there was no error and the result is COMPLETE, copies the signalled event data to user memory (an -EFAULT is returned). out_unlock frees the waiters (re-arming auto-reset events that were consumed only when the return value is -ERESTARTSYS) and releases the mutex. At the final exit it sets *wait_result to KFD_IOC_WAIT_RESULT_FAIL if ret is nonzero, and converts a FAIL result with ret 0 into -EIO. Success returns 0 with *wait_result COMPLETE or TIMEOUT.
note: kfd_events.c:981-1095. Matches the old prose; the free_waiters argument semantics (undo of auto-reset only for -ERESTARTSYS) were taken from the call at line 1086 without reading free_waiters.

name: dm_crtc_get_cursor_mode
prose: Precondition: state is the atomic state, dm_crtc_state the CRTC's amdgpu state, cursor_mode a writable pointer; zpos values are normalised. Behaviour: if the DCE hardware IP version is 4.0.1 (DCN401) it sets *cursor_mode to DM_CURSOR_NATIVE_MODE and returns 0. Otherwise it initialises *cursor_mode to dm_crtc_state->cursor_mode and scans the old/new plane states of planes on this CRTC; it records whether the cursor plane is in the state and stops with consider_mode_change set when a plane was enabled, disabled, changed format, or changed scale (it dereferences both old and new fb formats). If no plane changed and zpos did not change it returns 0 with *cursor_mode unchanged; if the cursor plane is not in the state and is not in the CRTC's plane mask it also returns 0. It gets the cursor plane state with drm_atomic_get_plane_state and returns its error pointer value if that fails (with *cursor_mode unchanged); if the cursor has no framebuffer it returns 0 unchanged. Then, for the other planes of this CRTC in descending z-order, it sets *cursor_mode to DM_CURSOR_OVERLAY_MODE and returns 0 as soon as a plane has a video format or has both its horizontal and vertical scale different from the cursor's, and stops scanning at the first plane that covers the whole CRTC. Finally it sets *cursor_mode to DM_CURSOR_NATIVE_MODE if a plane covered the entire CRTC and DM_CURSOR_OVERLAY_MODE otherwise, and returns 0.
note: slice cut head; real name is dm_crtc_get_cursor_mode(adev, state, dm_crtc_state, cursor_mode) (amdgpu_dm.c:12319-12441), not amdgpu_dm_crtc_compute_cursor_mode with a crtc_state parameter; the old prose checks out against the code except for its parameter list.

name: dm_crtc_high_irq_handler
prose: Precondition: adev and acrtc are valid; on DCN it is called from dm_vupdate_high_irq at VUPDATE_NO_LOCK and on DCE from dm_crtc_high_irq at VLINE0. Behaviour: if acrtc->wb_conn exists it clears wb_pending under the connector's job_lock when set and, if a writeback job was queued, waits one frame period with mdelay, signals the writeback completion with status 0 and force-disables writeback on the stream. It runs amdgpu_dm_crtc_handle_vblank only if the ASIC is DCN or VRR is inactive, and always runs the CRC irq handler. If adev->family is older than AMDGPU_FAMILY_AI it returns there. Otherwise, with the DRM event lock held (irqsave): when the CRTC has a stream whose vrr_params.supported is set it calls mod_freesync_handle_v_update and, if freesync is in VRR_STATE_ACTIVE_VARIABLE or neither PSR nor Replay is enabled, queues schedule_dc_vmin_vmax (which retains the stream and queues a worker that applies the adjust under dc_lock, releases the stream and frees its allocations; it silently does nothing if its allocations fail). On DCN, a flip with pflip_status AMDGPU_FLIP_SUBMITTED and a pending event is completed (event sent, vblank reference dropped, status set to AMDGPU_FLIP_NONE) when dc_get_flip_pending_on_otg reports no pending flip, otherwise it stays armed; on DCN, a SUBMITTED flip without a pending event and with no active planes is reset to AMDGPU_FLIP_NONE without sending an event or dropping a vblank reference. It then releases the event lock.
note: checked amdgpu_dm.c:590-712 and schedule_dc_vmin_vmax (550-576). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (the stream is retained by schedule_dc_vmin_vmax and released by the worker); round 2 RIGHT (the no-active-planes branch has no event); original RIGHT (the DCE path is driven by VLINE0).

name: amdgpu_dm_update_plane_color_mgmt
prose: Precondition: crtc is the dm_crtc_state, plane_state the DRM plane state and dc_plane_state the DC plane state being updated. Behaviour: it first calls amdgpu_dm_verify_lut3d_size and returns its error if nonzero. It takes the color capabilities from dc_plane_state->ctx->dc when available, sets the plane's input transfer function to bypass/linear, and calls __set_dm_plane_degamma: -ENOMEM is returned at once; if the CRTC has degamma (cm_has_degamma or cm_is_degamma_srgb) and that call did not return -EINVAL it returns -EINVAL (plane and CRTC degamma cannot both be used); if the CRTC has degamma it returns the error of map_crtc_degamma_to_dc_plane if that fails; any other nonzero result of __set_dm_plane_degamma is otherwise ignored. It then sets the gamut remap matrix from the plane CTM with enable_remap true when dm_plane_state->ctm is set, or sets enable_remap false, clears input_csc_color_matrix.enable_adjustment in both cases, and returns the result of amdgpu_dm_plane_set_color_properties.
note: slice cut head; real name amdgpu_dm_update_plane_color_mgmt (amdgpu_dm_color.c:1256-1340), no dm_plane_color_setup. Old prose omitted the amdgpu_dm_verify_lut3d_size early return.

name: amdgpu_dm_crtc_set_crc_source
prose: Precondition: crtc and src_name are valid. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL if src_name does not parse to a known source (no lock taken), then takes the CRTC mutex with drm_modeset_lock and returns its error if that fails (lock not held). It takes a reference on the first pending CRTC commit, if any, and waits for its hw_done interruptibly with a 10 second timeout: a negative result or -ETIMEDOUT (timeout) goes to cleanup. For a DPRX source, or for source NONE when the current source is DPRX, it finds the first non-writeback connector bound to the CRTC and returns -EINVAL (via cleanup) if there is none, no aux, or the connector is not DisplayPort/eDP. If the CRC source goes from invalid to valid it calls drm_crtc_vblank_get (a nonzero result goes to cleanup and becomes the return value, overwriting any earlier value). It then calls amdgpu_dm_crtc_configure_crc_source (-EINVAL via cleanup on failure, the vblank reference taken earlier not dropped). When enabling a DPRX source it starts DP CRC (-EINVAL via cleanup on failure); when disabling it drops the vblank reference and stops DP CRC for a DPRX source (-EINVAL via cleanup if that fails, after the vblank reference was dropped). On success it stores the new source in acrtc->dm_irq_params.crc_src under the event lock, clears crc_skip_count and falls into cleanup. cleanup drops the commit reference if one was taken, unlocks the CRTC mutex and returns ret: 0 normally, but a positive remaining-jiffies value when a commit wait succeeded and no vblank_get overwrote it. crc_src is unchanged on every failure path.
note: checked amdgpu_dm_crc.c:562-738. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (the return after a successful wait is the positive jiffies value unless drm_crtc_vblank_get ran and reset ret to 0); round 2 RIGHT (early parse and lock-failure returns do not unlock); original RIGHT (vblank reference not dropped after a failed configure/start).

name: amdgpu_dm_plane_get_plane_formats
prose: Precondition: plane is an initialised drm_plane, formats has room for max_formats entries plus up to six more, plane_cap may be NULL. Behaviour: for a primary plane, or a non-cursor plane whose plane_cap type is DC_PLANE_TYPE_DCN_UNIVERSAL, it copies the rgb_formats table entries one by one, stopping once num_formats reaches max_formats, and then, without any bound check, appends DRM_FORMAT_NV12 if plane_cap->pixel_format_support.nv12, DRM_FORMAT_P010 if .p010, and four fp16 formats if .fp16, so the count can exceed max_formats by up to six. Otherwise an overlay plane copies overlay_formats and a cursor plane copies cursor_formats, each bounded by max_formats, and any other plane type writes nothing. It returns the number of formats written, takes no locks and keeps no references.
note: slice cut head; real name amdgpu_dm_plane_get_plane_formats(plane, plane_cap, formats, max_formats) (amdgpu_dm_plane.c:761-818). Old prose otherwise matches.

name: amdgpu_dm_psr_wait_disable
prose: Precondition: stream points to a valid dc_stream_state (stream->link is read). Behaviour: it returns false if stream->link is NULL. Otherwise it polls dc_link_get_psr_state up to 1001 times (retry_count 0 to 1000), stopping at the first poll that leaves psr_state equal to PSR_STATE0 and delaying 500 microseconds between polls that do not. It returns false if the loop ended with retry_count == 1000, that is PSR_STATE0 first seen on the poll with retry_count 1000, and true otherwise, which includes PSR_STATE0 seen on any earlier poll and also the case where it was never seen (the loop then ends with retry_count 1001). psr_state starts as PSR_STATE0.
note: slice cut head; function is amdgpu_dm_psr_wait_disable(stream) (amdgpu_dm_psr.c:257-277), taking a stream rather than a link. Old prose's logic is right; the 'never seen -> true' behaviour follows from the exit value 1001.

name: dc_clk_mgr_create
prose: Precondition: ctx->asic_id.chip_family selects the chip family; pp_smu and dccg are passed to the family constructors that use them. Behaviour: it switches on the chip family; for each handled family it kzallocs the family-specific clk_mgr object (BREAK_TO_DEBUGGER and return NULL if that fails), calls the constructor selected by family, revision or dce_version (DCE, DCN2 through DCN4 families) and returns a pointer to the embedded struct clk_mgr base. For FAMILY_VI and FAMILY_RV the object is returned even when no revision check matches, in which case no constructor ran and the object stays zeroed; for FAMILY_VGH only the Van Gogh revision is handled and others fall to the end. For AMDGPU_FAMILY_GC_12_0_0 the object is allocated by dcn401_clk_mgr_construct (NULL gives BREAK_TO_DEBUGGER and NULL). For an unhandled family, or a family handled only for some revisions that does not match, it hits ASSERT(0) (unknown family) or falls out of the switch and returns NULL. The caller owns the returned object and releases it with dc_destroy_clk_mgr.
note: slice cut head; real name dc_clk_mgr_create (clk_mgr.c:147-384). Old prose said that every non-matching revision returns NULL; FAMILY_VI and FAMILY_RV return the zeroed object (lines 207, 249) and only the default and FAMILY_VGH non-Van Gogh case reach NULL/ASSERT.

name: rn_update_clocks
prose: Precondition: clk_mgr_base is a valid clk_mgr, context holds the requested clocks in context->bw_ctx.bw.dcn.clk. Behaviour: it returns immediately if dc->work_arounds.skip_clock_update is set. If safe_to_lower is true and 48 MHz power-down is not disabled it sets the DCN power state to LOW_POWER (through the vbios SMU) only if the state is not already LOW_POWER and rn_get_active_display_cnt_wa is 0, and otherwise leaves it; if safe_to_lower is false or 48 MHz power-down is disabled it sets MISSION_MODE if the state is not already that. It programs dcfclk and the deep-sleep dcfclk through the SMU when should_set_clock allows. It then writes into the context's requested values: a nonzero requested dppclk below 100000 kHz is raised to 100000, and if either the requested dppclk or dispclk is 0 both are replaced by the current clocks. If should_set_clock allows it records the new dppclk (noting whether it was lowered) and dispclk, setting the dispclk through the SMU. When dppclk was lowered it updates the per-DPP DTOs with the requested dppclk, sets the dppclk through the SMU and updates the DTOs again with the actual dppclk; otherwise it sets the dppclk through the SMU if either dppclk or dispclk was updated and then updates the DTOs with the actual dppclk. If dispclk was updated and a dmcu exists and is initialised it sets the PSR wait loop count to dispclk / 1000 / 7. It returns nothing.
note: slice cut head; function is rn_clk_mgr.c:131-251. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (dppclk is also programmed when dispclk changes, lines 233-235); round 2 RIGHT (no state change when safe_to_lower with 48 MHz power-down enabled and displays still active); original RIGHT (early return on skip_clock_update).

name: dcn401_clk_mgr_construct
prose: Precondition: ctx and dccg are valid. Behaviour: this is the function dcn401_clk_mgr_construct; it kzallocs the dcn401_clk_mgr itself and returns NULL if that fails. It fills in the base clk_mgr (ctx, dcn401_funcs, register/shift/mask tables, dccg), dfs_bypass_disp_clk 0, dprefclk_ss_percentage 0, dprefclk_ss_divider 1000, ss_on_dprefclk false, dfs_ref_freq_khz 100000, dprefclk_khz 720000 and dentist_vco_freq_khz from the VCO register (4500000 when the register gives 0). It dumps the boot clock snapshot, sets clks.ref_dtbclk_khz to the snapshot dtbclk if debug.disable_dtb_ref_clk_switch is set and they differ, replaces dprefclk_khz with the snapshot dprefclk when that is nonzero, reads the spread-spectrum info, sets dfs_bypass_enabled and smu_present false, kzallocs bw_params (BREAK_TO_DEBUGGER, free the object and return NULL on failure) and allocates the watermark range table as GART memory with dm_helpers_allocate_gpu_mem (BREAK_TO_DEBUGGER, free bw_params and the object and return NULL on failure). It returns &clk_mgr401->base.
note: slice cut head; function is dcn401_clk_mgr.c:1547-1621. Old prose wrongly said the memory was already allocated by the caller (it is allocated at line 1552) and omitted the NULL return for that allocation.

name: update_planes_and_stream_state
prose: Precondition: dc, stream and the output pointers are valid, srf_updates has surface_count entries with non-NULL surfaces, stream_update may be NULL. Behaviour: it returns false (ASSERT only if surface_count is nonzero) without writing outputs if dc_stream_get_status(stream) is NULL. It computes the update type, forces immediate-flip planes to flip, and for a FULL update backs up the current plane and stream state into dc->scratch.current_state. It applies the stream update, and returns false (stream state already modified) if any surface update has a surface with a zero src or dst rect width or height and no scaling_info, or a scaling_info that has any zero src or dst dimension. It copies each surface update into its plane. For an update type of FULL it creates a copy of dc->current_state (returning false if that fails), removes phantom streams and planes, removes and re-adds all planes of the stream, and jumps to a failure label that releases the new context and returns false if either step fails. For MED updates with position changes it rebuilds scaling parameters. For a FULL update it validates bandwidth and returns false (releasing the new context) unless it returns DC_OK. It then updates seamless-boot flags, sets *new_context (the new copy for FULL, dc->current_state otherwise) and *new_update_type, and for a FULL update backs up the post-update state into dc->scratch.new_state, returning true.
note: slice cut head; function is dc.c:3451-3585. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (pre-update backup is done only when update_type is FULL, line 3481-3482); round 2 RIGHT (any zero dimension in scaling_info fails).

name: vpg3_construct
prose: Precondition: vpg3 points to storage for a dcn30_vpg owned by the caller; ctx, inst and the register, shift and mask tables are valid. Behaviour: it allocates nothing and returns nothing; it sets vpg3->base.ctx to ctx, base.inst to inst, base.funcs to &dcn30_vpg_funcs, and the regs, vpg_shift and vpg_mask pointers to the given tables.
note: slice cut head; real function is vpg3_construct (dcn30_vpg.c:249-264), a void constructor; the old prose described a non-existent allocating function.

name: CalculateVMAndRowBytes
prose: Precondition: mode_lib->vba.GPUVMMaxPageTableLevels is initialised, BytePerPixel, VMMPageSize and Pitch are nonzero where they are divisors, and the output pointers are valid. Behaviour: a pure computation that returns PDEAndMetaPTEBytesFrame, the sum of MetaPTEBytesFrame, MPDEBytesFrame, DPDE0BytesFrame and ExtraDPDEBytesFrame. When DCCEnable it computes *meta_row_height and *MetaRowByte from the scan direction and SwathWidth and, with GPUVMEnable, MetaPTEBytesFrame and MPDEBytesFrame; when DCC is off they are 0 and *MetaRowByte is 0. It picks the macro tile size and height from SurfaceTiling and stores *MacroTileWidth. DPDE0BytesFrame and ExtraDPDEBytesFrame are nonzero only when GPUVMEnable and GPUVMMaxPageTableLevels > 1. If GPUVMEnable it computes the PTE request geometry from the tiling, then *dpte_row_height and *PixelPTEBytesPerRow for the linear, horizontal-scan or vertical-scan case, and sets *PTEBufferSizeNotExceeded to whether *PixelPTEBytesPerRow * (1 - FractionOfPTEReturnDrop) <= 64 * PTEBufferSizeInRequestsLuma; if GPUVMEnable is false it sets *PixelPTEBytesPerRow to 0, *PTEBufferSizeNotExceeded to true and leaves *dpte_row_height unchanged.
note: slice cut head; the real function is CalculateVMAndRowBytes in display_mode_vba_20.c:856-1080 (no dml20_pte_row_calc exists). Read in full.

name: CalculateWatermarksAndDRAMSpeedChangeSupport
prose: Precondition: the per-plane arrays have NumberOfActivePlanes valid entries and the output pointers are valid; *UrgentWatermark is written before it is read. Behaviour: it returns nothing. It sets *UrgentWatermark = UrgentLatency + ExtraLatency, *DRAMClockChangeWatermark = DRAMClockChangeLatency + *UrgentWatermark, and the writeback watermarks from WritebackLatency (adding a chunk-size term when more than one writeback is active). It computes, for each plane, the effective line-buffer hiding, the DET buffering times, the active DRAM-clock-change latency margin (reduced for multiple planes, combined with chroma and writeback margins) and stores them in mode_lib->vba (TotalActiveDPP, TotalDCCActiveDPP, TotalActiveWriteback, TotalNumberOfActiveOTG, ActiveDRAMClockChangeLatencyMargin, MinActiveDRAMClockChangeMargin and the intermediate line-buffer fields). It sets *MinActiveDRAMClockChangeLatencySupported = MinActiveDRAMClockChangeMargin + DRAMClockChangeLatency; *DRAMClockChangeSupport to dm_dram_clock_change_vactive if the minimum margin is positive, else dm_dram_clock_change_vblank if PrefetchMode is 0 and (SynchronizedVBlank, exactly one OTG, or a positive second-smallest margin), else dm_dram_clock_change_unsupported. It finds the stutter-critical plane (smallest full DET buffering time) and sets *StutterExitWatermark = SRExitTime + ExtraLatency + 10 / DCFCLKDeepSleep and *StutterEnterPlusExitWatermark to the maximum of SREnterPlusExitTime + ExtraLatency + 10 / DCFCLKDeepSleep and that plane's time to finish the swath transfer.
note: slice cut head; real function is CalculateWatermarksAndDRAMSpeedChangeSupport (display_mode_vba_30.c:5067-5282). Checked outputs at lines 5153-5176, 5237-5282; divisions by plane quantities are unguarded.

name: CalculatePrefetchSchedule
prose: Precondition: mode_lib->vba is initialised and the pipe, byte counts and output pointers are valid; myPipe->HTotal, PixelClock and the clocks used as divisors are nonzero. Behaviour: the return value is an error flag (true means failure, false means the schedule validated). It computes the host-VM factor, calls CalculateDynamicMetadataParameters, and writes v->Tdmdl[k], v->Tdmdl_vm[k] and *NotEnoughTimeForDynamicMetadata (true when VStartup * LineTime is less than Tsetup + Tdmdl + Tdmbf + Tdmec + Tdmsks and dynamic metadata is enabled, false otherwise); then it returns true immediately if myPipe->DPPCLK or myPipe->DISPCLK is 0, before writing v->DSTXAfterScaler[k], DSTYAfterScaler[k], Tno_bw[k] or any of the prefetch outputs. Otherwise it computes DSTXAfterScaler/DSTYAfterScaler and Tno_bw, zeroes the prefetch outputs (all except *RequiredPrefetchPixDataBWChroma, which is written only later) and, if dst_y_prefetch_equ > 1, chooses between the one-to-one (oto) and equation (equ) schedules to set *DestinationLinesForPrefetch, *PrefetchBandwidth, *DestinationLinesToRequestVMInVBlank, *DestinationLinesToRequestRowInVBlank, *VRatioPrefetchY/C and *RequiredPrefetchPixDataBWLuma/Chroma, setting MyError when the lines for prefetch pixel data are not positive or the swath constraints fail; if dst_y_prefetch_equ <= 1 it sets MyError. It always computes v->prefetch_vmrow_bw[k] and sets MyError if a needed request-lines value is not positive. If MyError it zeroes all the prefetch outputs. It returns MyError, which is false when everything validated.
note: slice cut head; function is display_mode_vba_30.c:782-1239 (the first hit at line 80 is only the forward declaration). Read in full.

name: dcn302_fpu_update_bw_bounding_box
prose: Precondition: floating-point use is enabled (dc_assert_fp_enabled), dc and bw_params are valid with a populated clock table. Behaviour: it returns nothing. Unconditionally it copies num_chans and dram_channel_width_bytes from the BIOS vram info into dcn3_02_soc when they are nonzero and sets dispclk_dppclk_vco_speed_mhz in both dcn3_02_soc and dc->dml.soc from the clock manager's VCO frequency. Only if bw_params->clk_table.entries[0].memclk_mhz is nonzero does it go on: it finds the maximum dcfclk, dispclk, dppclk and phyclk over MAX_NUM_DPM_LVL entries (using dcn3_02_soc.clock_limits[0] when a maximum is 0), merges the DCFCLK STA targets with the per-uclk optimal dcfclk values into a table of at most DC__VOLTAGE_STATES entries, and if the merged count exceeds MAX_NUM_DPM_LVL it calls ASSERT(0) and returns without changing dcn3_02_soc.num_states, clock_limits or the DML instances (the chans, width and VCO writes above remain). Otherwise it sets dcn3_02_soc.num_states and fills clock_limits[0..num_states-1] from the merged table, the maximum clocks and bw_params (dtbclk and socclk fall back to the previous state's value when zero), and reinitialises DML for dc->dml and, if dc->current_state is non-NULL, for dc->current_state->bw_ctx.dml.
note: slice cut head; function is dcn302_fpu.c:195-346 (named dcn302_fpu_update_bw_bounding_box). Old prose omitted the unconditional writes and the no-update case when memclk_mhz is 0.

name: CalculatePrefetchSchedule
prose: Precondition: the pipe description myPipe, the byte and line counts and all output pointers are valid; myPipe->HTotal, PixelClock and the clocks used as divisors are nonzero. Behaviour: the return value is an error flag (true means failure, false means the schedule validated). Using the host-VM inefficiency factor it calls CalculateVupdateAndDynamicMetadataParameters, which fills *TSetup, the Tdmbf/Tdmec/Tdmsks times and the VUpdate/VReady pixel offsets, then writes *Tdmdl, *Tdmdl_vm and *NotEnoughTimeForDynamicMetadata (true when VStartup * LineTime is less than *TSetup + *Tdmdl + Tdmbf + Tdmec + Tdmsks and dynamic metadata is enabled, false otherwise). It returns true immediately if myPipe->DPPCLK or myPipe->DISPCLK is 0, before writing *DSTXAfterScaler, *DSTYAfterScaler, *Tno_bw, *prefetch_vmrow_bw or the prefetch results. Otherwise it computes *DSTXAfterScaler and *DSTYAfterScaler and *Tno_bw, the one-to-one (oto) prefetch figures and, if dst_y_prefetch_equ > 1, four candidate prefetch bandwidths of which the first valid case selects the equation (equ) schedule, then sets *DestinationLinesForPrefetch and *PrefetchBandwidth from the oto or equ schedule (whichever needs fewer lines), *DestinationLinesToRequestVMInVBlank and *DestinationLinesToRequestRowInVBlank, and *VRatioPrefetchY/C and *RequiredPrefetchPixDataBWLuma/Chroma when the lines left for prefetch pixel data are positive and prefetch_bw_equ > 0; if dst_y_prefetch_equ <= 1, or the swath constraints cannot be met, it sets MyError. name: TruncToValidBPP
prose: Precondition: PixelClock is nonzero; HTotal, HActive, DSCSlices, AudioRate and AudioLayout are not used. Behaviour: a pure function returning a bits-per-pixel value as a double, or BPP_INVALID. From Format it selects the non-DSC tiers and DSC limits: for dm_420 the non-DSC values 12, 15, 18 with MinDSCBPP 6 and MaxDSCBPP 1.5 * DSCInputBitPerComponent - 1/16; for dm_444 24, 30, 36 with 8 and 3 * bpc - 1/16; otherwise 16, 20, 24 with MinDSCBPP 7 and MaxDSCBPP 2 * bpc - 1/16 for dm_n422 or 8 and 3 * bpc - 1/16 for the other formats. MaxLinkBPP is LinkBitRate / 10 * 8 * Lanes / PixelClock, multiplied by (1 - 2.4/100) when DSCEnable and Output is dm_dp, then capped at 16 for dm_odm_combine_mode_4to1 or at 32 for dm_odm_combine_mode_2to1 if it is larger. If DesiredBPP is 0: with DSC it returns BPP_INVALID if MaxLinkBPP < MinDSCBPP, MaxDSCBPP if MaxLinkBPP >= MaxDSCBPP, else floor(16 * MaxLinkBPP) / 16; without DSC it returns the third tier if MaxLinkBPP >= it, else the second tier if MaxLinkBPP >= it, else 16.0 if MaxLinkBPP >= the first tier, otherwise BPP_INVALID. If DesiredBPP is nonzero it returns DesiredBPP when (no DSC and DesiredBPP equals the third or second tier or is at most the first tier) or (DSC and MinDSCBPP <= DesiredBPP <= MaxDSCBPP), and BPP_INVALID otherwise.

name: CalculateStutterEfficiency
prose: Precondition: the per-plane arrays have NumberOfActivePlanes entries and all output pointers are valid; TotalDataReadBandwidth, TotalCompressedReadBandwidth, ReturnBW, DCFCLK, PixelClock[k], SwathWidthY[k], BytePerPixelDETY[k], VRatio[k] and the resulting *StutterPeriod must be nonzero or the divisions are undefined; with no active planes *StutterPeriod is not assigned by this function. Behaviour: it returns nothing. It sums the compressed, zero-size and row read bandwidths (applying a DCC maximum effective compression of 2 or 4 per plane), derives the average DCC compression rate and zero-size fraction and the EffectiveCompressedBufferSize. For each plane it computes LinesInDETY and the DET buffering time, and sets *StutterPeriod to the smallest such time (the first plane always sets it), recording that plane's frame and active times, swath data and MinTTUVBlank as the critical plane. It computes StutterBurstTime (raised to at least the time to finish the critical swath), counts active writebacks, and, if none, sets *StutterEfficiencyNotIncludingVBlank and *Z8StutterEfficiencyNotIncludingVBlank to max(0, 1 - (SRExitTime or SRExitZ8Time + StutterBurstTime) / *StutterPeriod) * 100 and both burst counts to ceil(VActiveTimeCriticalPlane / *StutterPeriod) when the corresponding efficiency is above 0 (otherwise 0); with a writeback active all four are 0. It then counts OTGs (planes with BlendingAndTiming[k] == k) and sets *StutterEfficiency (and the Z8 value) to 0 when the not-including-VBlank efficiency is not above 0, to the formula 1 - (bursts * SRExitTime + StutterBurstTime * VActiveTime / StutterPeriod) / FrameTime (times 100) when (SynchronizedVBlank or one OTG) and LastStutterPeriod + MinTTUVBlankCriticalPlane exceeds the stutter enter-plus-exit watermark, and otherwise to the not-including-VBlank value; the Z8 case uses *NumberOfStutterBurstsPerFrame (not the Z8 count) in its last-period and efficiency formulas.

It computes *prefetch_vmrow_bw, setting MyError if a needed request-lines value is not positive; if MyError it zeroes *PrefetchBandwidth, the two request-lines outputs, *DestinationLinesForPrefetch, the VRatio outputs and the required pixel-data bandwidths, and it returns MyError.

name: dml32_CalculateStutterEfficiency
prose: Precondition: the per-surface arrays have NumberOfActiveSurfaces entries and all output pointers are valid; TotalDataReadBandwidth, the compressed-bandwidth totals, ReturnBW, DCFCLK and *StutterPeriod must be nonzero where they are divisors, and with no non-phantom surface *StutterPeriod is not assigned. Behaviour: it returns nothing. Surfaces using MALL phantom pipes are skipped everywhere. It computes the compression-based EffectiveCompressedBufferSize like the dcn314 version, then for each non-phantom surface the DET buffering time and sets *StutterPeriod to the smallest of them (the first one found always sets it), recording that critical surface's frame/active times, swath data, DET size and MinTTUVBlank, and whether it is single-plane and single-pipe. StutterBurstTime is the larger of the computed burst time and the time to finish the critical swath. With no active writeback it sets the stutter and Z8 efficiencies not including vblank to max(0, 1 - (SRExitTime or SRExitZ8Time + StutterBurstTime) / *StutterPeriod) * 100 and the burst counts to ceil(VActiveTimeCriticalSurface / *StutterPeriod) when positive, otherwise all four are 0. It counts OTGs and checks that all of them have the same timing, and sets *StutterEfficiency and *Z8StutterEfficiency as in the dcn314 version except that the vblank-inclusive formula also requires SameTiming. Finally it sets *DCHUBBUB_ARB_CSTATE_MAX_CAP_MODE to false only when unbounded requests are disabled, there is exactly one surface that is single-plane and single-pipe, the last swath chunk size is in 1..4096 and the missing part of the last DET swath is in 1..the last chunk size, and to true otherwise.

name: dml32_rq_dlg_get_dlg_reg

name: dcn35_populate_dml_pipes_from_context_fpu
prose: Precondition: dc, context and pipes are valid, pipes has room for dc->res_pool->pipe_count entries, and FPU access is enabled (it calls dc_assert_fp_enabled); validate_mode is the DC validation mode passed on to dcn31. Behaviour: it calls dcn31_populate_dml_pipes_from_context and then, for each pipe in context->res_ctx with a stream, sets pipes[pipe_cnt].pipe.dest.vtotal to adjust.v_total_min only when adjust.v_total_max equals v_total_min and v_total_min exceeds timing->v_total; sets dest.vblank_nom to timing->v_total - dest.vactive, then applies min(num_lines), max(v_sync_width + v_back_porch + 2) and finally min(1023), so the final value is at most 1023 and exceeds num_lines whenever the lower bound is larger than num_lines (and when the lower bound exceeds 1023 the result is 1023, below that bound); sets src.immediate_flip to true, src.unbounded_req_mode to false, zeroes the DCC fraction via dcn31_zero_pipe_dcc_fraction, sets dest.vfront_porch, src.dcc_rate to 3, dout.dsc_input_bpc (0, or 8/10/12 when dout.dsc_enable is set, with ASSERT(0) on another depth) and src.gpuvm_min_page_size_kbytes to 256; records an upscaling plane; and increments pipe_cnt. It then sets det_buffer_size_kbytes to 384 and dc->config.enable_4to1MPC to false; if exactly one pipe was populated (using the last pipe seen), it has a plane and z9_mpc is not disabled, it enables 4to1MPC for a dual-plane format with source at most 1920x1080 or, for a non-dual-plane format with source width at most 5120, sets det_buffer_size_kbytes to 192 and pipes[0].src.unbounded_req_mode to true; otherwise it uses crb_alloc_policy * 64 for det_buffer_size_kbytes when stream_count reaches crb_alloc_policy_min_disp_count and the policy exceeds DET_SIZE_DEFAULT, or 192 when there are at least 3 streams and an upscaled plane. Finally it scans the pipes and, for the first eDP stream with seamless_boot_odm_combine, apply_seamless_boot_optimization and apply_boot_odm_mode equal to dm_odm_combine_policy_2to1, sets vba.ODMCombinePolicy to dm_odm_combine_policy_2to1 and stops scanning. It returns pipe_cnt, the number of pipes with a stream.

name: CalculatePrefetchSchedule
prose: Precondition: scratch and p are valid; p holds the pipe description, byte counts, flags and output pointers and scratch holds the locals structure. Behaviour: the return value is an error flag (true means failure). It starts with s->MyError false, computes the host-VM trip levels and the dynamic-metadata and VUpdate parameters (writing the Tdmdl, Tdmdl_vm and NotEnoughTimeForDynamicMetadata outputs), and returns true immediately if p->myPipe->Dppclk or Dispclk is 0, before writing the DST after-scaler outputs and prefetch results. It computes *p->prefetch_vmrow_bw and sets MyError if a needed request-lines value is not positive. On error it zeroes the request-lines outputs, *DestinationLinesForPrefetch, the VRatio outputs and the two required prefetch bandwidths (this variant does not zero *PrefetchBandwidth), and it returns s->MyError.

name: CalculateWatermarksMALLUseAndDRAMSpeedChangeSupport
prose: Static void function that takes the scratch area and a parameter struct p, returns nothing, and has no early return and no goto; it runs straight through to the end. It writes the watermark fields of p->Watermark (Urgent, USRRetraining, DRAMClockChange, FCLKChange, StutterExit, StutterEnterPlusExit, Z8StutterExit, Z8StutterEnterPlusExit) from the latencies in p->mmSOCParameters, and the writeback watermarks: WritebackLatency, plus p->WritebackChunkSize*1024/32/SOCCLK when more than one surface has WritebackEnable set, plus USRRetrainingLatency when USRRetrainingRequiredFinal is set. For each active surface k it computes latency-hiding margins from line-buffer lines and DET buffering, subtracts the watermarks (the writeback margins are cross-wired: the DRAM margin is min-ed with the writeback FCLK margin and the FCLK margin with the writeback DRAM margin), and writes p->MaxActiveDRAMClockChangeLatencySupported[k] (0 for a phantom-pipe surface), p->ActiveDRAMClockChangeLatencyMargin[k] and p->SubViewportLinesNeededInMALL[k] (the larger of the luma and chroma line counts only when BytePerPixelDETC[k] > 0). It sets *p->USRRetrainingSupport to true and then to false if any non-phantom surface has a negative USR retraining margin. It writes *p->MaxActiveFCLKChangeLatencySupported only when at least one non-phantom surface exists (the minimum of FCLK margin plus FCLKChangeLatency over them); otherwise that location is left as it was. It writes *p->FCLKChangeSupport (vactive, vblank or unsupported) and *p->DRAMClockChangeSupport (vactive, vblank, vblank_drr, with the _w_mall_full_frame or _w_mall_sub_vp variants when any surface uses full-frame or sub-viewport MALL, or unsupported) from the margins, PrefetchMode, DRR flags and the synchronization relation between surfaces. Many intermediate values are stored in the scratch locals struct. Divisions by DCFClkDeepSleep, SOCCLK, PixelClock, HTotal, VRatio, SwathWidth and LBBitPerPixel are not guarded, so the caller must supply nonzero values.
note: slice cut the head (real head at display_mode_core.c:2822, named CalculateWatermarksMALLUseAndDRAMSpeedChangeSupport, not CalculateWatermarksAndDRAMSpeedChangeSupport); prior rejection 'name not in slice' was right; prior prose also described fields differently and said nothing of the cross-wired writeback margins (lines 2953-2954). name: CalculateOutputLink
prose: Static void function with no return statements and no goto. It first sets *RequiresDSC and *RequiresFEC to false, *OutBpp to 0, *OutputType to dml_output_type_unknown and *OutputRate to dml_output_rate_unknown, and does nothing more when IsMainSurfaceUsingTheIndicatedTiming is false or when Output is not HDMI, DP, DP2.0 or eDP (*RequiredSlots untouched in those cases). For HDMI it sets *OutputType to dml_output_type_hdmi and *OutBpp to the result of TruncToValidBPP(min(600,PHYCLKPerState)*10, 3 lanes, ...) with a local dummy in place of RequiredSlots; *RequiresDSC and *RequiresFEC stay false and *OutputRate stays unknown. For DP, DP2.0 and eDP it sets *RequiresDSC true when DSCEnable is dml_dsc_enable (and *RequiresFEC true for DP and DP2.0 in that case), otherwise *RequiresDSC false and *RequiresFEC true only for DP2.0. It then tries link-rate tiers in order (UHBR10, UHBR13p5, UHBR20 for DP2.0; HBR, HBR2, HBR3 for DP and eDP), each tier only if OutputLinkDPRate is dml_dp_rate_na or that rate, the PHY clock is large enough, and (for tiers after the first) *OutBpp is still 0. In a tier it calls TruncToValidBPP with the downspread-adjusted rate, passing RequiredSlots as an output, and when that gives 0, DSCEnable is dml_dsc_enable_if_necessary, ForcedOutputLinkBPP is 0 and (for the lower tiers) the PHY clock is below the next tier's threshold, it sets *RequiresDSC true (and *RequiresFEC true for DP, not for eDP, in the HBR tiers) and calls TruncToValidBPP again. When a tier is entered it sets *OutputType (dml_output_type_dp2p0, dml_output_type_dp or dml_output_type_edp) and *OutputRate for that tier, so they keep the value of the last tier entered and stay unknown if no tier condition held (then *OutBpp is 0 as well).

name: dml_core_mode_programming
prose: Non-static void function (display_mode_core.c:8291-9912) taking the mode library state and a clock configuration; it has no return statement inside the body and no goto, so it runs straight through. It first derives the active plane and pipe counts and the pipe/plane mapping from mode_lib->ms.cache_display_cfg and stores them in mode_lib->ms and mode_lib->mp, and sets locals->Dcfclk to mode_lib->ms.DCFCLK unless clk_cfg->dcfclk_option is dml_use_override_freq, in which case it takes clk_cfg->dcfclk_mhz. It then fills the programming results in mode_lib->mp (display, DPP and DSC clocks with required or override frequencies per clk_cfg option, read bandwidths, swath/DET configuration, DCFCLK deep sleep, DSC delays, MALL surface sizes, and further prefetch, watermark and stutter values by calling the helper functions) and uses the shared scratch area for temporary parameter structs. The returned information is in mode_lib->mp; there is no return value. The slice given covers only the part from the dispclk calculation through the DSCCLK calculation. Many divisions in the body (HTotal, PixelClock and similar) are not guarded.

name: CalculateStutterEfficiency
prose: Static void function (dml2_core_dcn4_calcs.c:10072-10359) that takes the internal scratch and a params struct p, returns nothing and has no return or goto. It zeroes its locals struct with memset, then over the non-phantom surfaces accumulates total compressed, zero-size-request and row read bandwidths (with a per-surface maximum compression of 2 or 4 chosen from block size and DCC uncompressed block limits for DCC surfaces), derives AverageDCCCompressionRate and AverageDCCZeroSizeFraction from p->TotalDataReadBandwidth and the compressed total (divisions are not guarded), and computes an effective compressed buffer size by one of three formulas depending on whether the zero-size fraction is 1, above 0, or 0. It sets *p->StutterPeriod to the minimum DET buffering time over non-phantom surfaces (0 if there is none) and records that critical surface's frame time, active time and sizes. It writes *p->StutterEfficiencyNotIncludingVBlank, *p->Z8StutterEfficiencyNotIncludingVBlank and the two burst counts as 0 when any non-phantom stream has an active writeback and otherwise from the SR exit times, the burst time and the stutter period; it then writes *p->StutterEfficiency and *p->Z8StutterEfficiency (equal to the not-including-vblank value unless timings are synchronized or there is one OTG with the same timing, and 0 with a burst count of 0 when that value is 0), and *p->DCHUBBUB_ARB_CSTATE_MAX_CAP_MODE. All outputs go through pointers in p.

name: CalculatePrefetchSchedule
prose: Static function (dml2_core_dcn4_calcs.c:5102-5940) taking the internal scratch and a params struct p and returning a bool. It sets s->NoTimeToPrefetch to false at entry, computes trip and dynamic-metadata timing values (writing s->TWait_p, s->LineTime, *p->Tvm_trips, *p->Tr0_trips, the flip variants, *p->Tdmdl_vm, *p->Tdmdl, *p->NotEnoughTimeForDynamicMetadata and the VUpdate/VReady offsets through CalculateVUpdateAndDynamicMetadataParameters) and the DPP and DISPCLK cycle counts. There are two returns. At line 5246 it returns true immediately if p->myPipe->Dppclk or p->myPipe->Dispclk is 0.0, before writing *p->DSTXAfterScaler, *p->DSTYAfterScaler and the later prefetch outputs. Otherwise it continues through the prefetch bandwidth and line-count computations and, at line 5939, returns s->NoTimeToPrefetch, which is true when the computation found there was not enough time to prefetch (in which case the prefetch outputs dst_y_per_vm_vblank, dst_y_per_row_vblank, dst_y_prefetch, VRatioPrefetchY/C, the required prefetch pixel-data bandwidths and prefetch_vmrow_bw are reset to 0) and false otherwise. The function does not always return true.
