name: math_log2_approx
prose: Returns 0 when a is 0 or 1; for a greater than 1 it returns the number of times a can be shifted right by one before it reaches 1 or less, which is floor(log2(a)) and at most 31. The parameter is a by-value copy that the loop shifts, so the caller's variable is unchanged; no memory, locks or globals are touched. The loop terminates for every unsigned int input.
note: Prose already correct (lib_float_math.c:132-140, single return at 139). Reviewer objections were all about the formal contract (uses modified parameter a, unbound result, signed 1<<31 overflow), which are right for the old contract text; contract left empty because the post-state of a (it is shifted down to 0/1) makes any contract that mentions a ambiguous. R:right

name: dpp401_dscl_set_scaler_manual_scale
prose: Void function (dcn401_dpp_dscl.c:1052-1186) that programs the DSCL scaler and line buffer in manual scaling mode from scl_data. It compares the cached dpp->scl_data with *scl_data using memcmp and returns at once with no register writes when they are byte-equal. If scl_data->dscl_prog_data.isharp_en is set and the cached sharpness_level differs, it programs the isharp delta filter, copies the new sharpness level and the isharp_delta table into the cache, and returns if the cache now equals *scl_data; otherwise it sets program_isharp_1dlut to true. It then replaces the cache with *scl_data. When config.use_spl is set and debug.disable_spl is clear it takes dscl_mode, recout, MPC size and tap counts from scl_data->dscl_prog_data. When debug.enable_mem_low_power.bits.dscl is set and the mode is not DCN401_DSCL_MODE_DSCL_BYPASS it powers on the DSCL. It writes DSCL_AUTOCAL (off), DSCL_CONTROL boundary mode 0, recout, MPC_SIZE and SCL_MODE. For DSCL bypass it powers the DSCL off if the low-power debug flag is set and returns. Otherwise it picks an LB memory config and sets the line buffer; for DCN401_DSCL_MODE_SCALING_444_BYPASS it disables EASF if config.prefer_easf is set, programs isharp and returns. In the remaining modes it writes the black offsets if the SCL_BLACK_OFFSET register exists, sets manual ratio and init values, the tap control, programs isharp, sets the SCL filter, and programs EASF if config.prefer_easf is set. It returns nothing and reports no error. After the cache is replaced, every return leaves dpp->scl_data equal to *scl_data.

name: dcn401_update_bandwidth
prose: Returns bool. It calls dc->res_pool->funcs->validate_bandwidth(dc, context, DC_VALIDATE_MODE_AND_PROGRAMMING) and returns false right away if the result is not DC_OK, before calling prepare_bandwidth (validate_bandwidth itself may change the context). Otherwise it calls dc->hwss.prepare_bandwidth(dc, context) and loops over all pipes in context->res_ctx.pipe_ctx up to the pool pipe_count. Pipes whose plane_state is NULL are skipped. For a pipe with a plane_state and no top_pipe it programs the timing generator global sync (vready offset for the group, vstartup, vupdate offset and width, pstate keepout) and VTG params, calls hws->funcs.blank_pixel_data(dc, pipe_ctx, blank) when prev_odm_pipe is NULL (blank is true when is_pipe_tree_visible is false, so this can blank or unblank), and calls setup_vupdate_interrupt if that hook exists. For every pipe with a plane_state (top pipe or not) it then calls hubp_setup2 with the pipe's hubp_regs, global_sync and stream timing if that hook exists. It returns true at the end. The pipe's stream_res.tg, stream and plane_res.hubp pointers are dereferenced without checks.

Reviewer claim (precondition omits stream validity for non-top pipes using hubp_setup2) is right: line 2451 reads pipe_ctx->stream->timing for any pipe with plane_state. Earlier reviewer claim (skips NULL plane_state pipes) was already covered by the old prose. R:right

name: construct_phy
prose: Static bool (link_factory.c:454-758) that fills in a struct dc_link for a physical connector from the BIOS object table. It sets irq sources to DC_IRQ_SOURCE_INVALID, copies dc, ctx and link_index, clears the preferred training and link settings, gets the connector id from the BIOS and sets ep_type to DISPLAY_ENDPOINT_PHY. Returns false (via create_fail) when the object type is not OBJECT_TYPE_CONNECTOR, when the connector id is an eDP and smart mux is configured while dc_edp_id_count is already non-zero, or for an unsupported connector id. It optionally calls the resource pool link_init hook, gets and opens the HPD gpio (interrupt mode, unlocks the pin) when one exists, sets connector_signal and the HPD/HPD-RX/read-request irq sources by connector type, creates the ddc service, sets ddc_hw_inst, creates the link encoder via the pool's link_enc_create, records eng_id in res_pool->link_encoders[] and increments dig_link_enc_count, sets link_enc_hw_inst, and for eDP/LVDS creates a panel controller if the pool has panel_cntl_create (incrementing dc_edp_id_count whether or not creation succeeds). It then loops up to 4 times calling get_device_tag; a failing call jumps to device_tag_fail, while a loop that finds no matching tag simply ends and keeps the last tag read. It optionally copies channel mapping, chip caps and forced drive settings from bios->integrated_info, calls get_atom_dc_golden_table if present, calls program_hpd_filter, sets PSR version to unsupported and returns true. Failure labels cascade: device_tag_fail destroys the link encoder (but not its entry in res_pool->link_encoders and not the incremented count) and falls through; link_enc_create_fail destroys panel_cntl if non-NULL; panel_cntl_create_fail destroys the ddc service; ddc_create_fail and create_fail (reached directly) do not destroy the ddc service, so a ddc service created but lacking ddc_pin is not destroyed there; all failure paths destroy the hpd gpio irq and clear hpd_gpio when it exists, and return false. The panel_cntl_create_fail path does not destroy the link encoder.

name: dp_handle_hpd_rx_irq
prose: Returns bool and handles a DP short-pulse (HPD RX) interrupt on a link. At entry it sets *out_link_loss and *has_left_work to false when those pointers are non-NULL, reads the IRQ data with dp_read_hpd_rx_irq_data and copies it to *out_hpd_irq_dpcd_data (if non-NULL) even when the read failed. Return paths in order: false if the DPCD read did not return DC_OK; false after an AUTOMATED_TEST request (it clears the AUTOMATED_TEST bit in the device service IRQ vector by a DPCD write, then either defers the work by setting *has_left_work when defer_handling is set and has_left_work is non-NULL, or runs the automated test handler directly); false if dp_should_allow_hpd_rx_irq says no (no established lane count and not a branch device); true if handle_hpd_irq_psr_sink reports a PSR error was handled; true if UP_REQ_MSG_RDY is set (deferred via *has_left_work when requested); false if DOWN_REP_MSG_RDY is set. Otherwise, for non-eDP signals, if link loss is parsed from the IRQ data it defers via *has_left_work or calls dp_handle_link_loss, sets the result to false and sets *out_link_loss true; if DP tunneling is supported and the tunneling IRQ bit is set it calls dp_handle_tunneling_irq; and for an SST branch link whose reported sink count differs from link->dpcd_sink_count it sets the result to true (this can override a false set by link loss). The final return is that result, true only when a sink-count change was seen on an SST branch.

name: perform_link_training_with_retries
prose: Returns bool and runs DP link training with retries and optional fallback to lower link settings. It copies link_setting into the current and maximum settings, sets up the stream encoder for 8b/10b, and loops while j < attempts and fail_count < attempts*10 (so it returns false without any attempt when attempts is 0 or less). Each iteration enables the link PHY with the current settings, optionally sleeps for the sink's dppowerup_delay, sets the panel mode and ASSR, then: if link->aux_access_disabled, it runs AUX-less training and returns true at once without checking a status. Otherwise it trains (through dpia_perform_link_training for a USB4 DPIA endpoint when consolidated_dpia_dp_lt is not set, else dp_perform_link_training) and returns true if the status is LINK_TRAINING_SUCCESS and is_link_bw_low is false; before that return, a USB4 DPIA endpoint with an MST stream has link->verified_link_cap updated and dm_helpers_dp_mst_update_branch_bandwidth called. A failed attempt increments fail_count. For a DISPLAY_ENDPOINT_PHY endpoint the loop is left with a break, before dp_disable_link_phy is called, when this was the last attempt or the status is LINK_TRAINING_ABORT, so the PHY stays enabled on that path and the function returns false. Otherwise the PHY is disabled; for LINK_TRAINING_ABORT it then breaks (returning false, PHY already disabled) if link_detect_connection_type reports dc_connection_none. If the attempt is not retried at lower bandwidth (do_fallback false, abort, success with low bandwidth, or minimum RBR x 1 already) it increments j, resets the settings to link_setting and lengthens the delay; otherwise it picks a fallback with decide_fallback_link_setting and recomputes is_link_bw_low and is_link_bw_min. It sleeps between attempts. After the loop it returns false.
note: Checked against link_dp_training.c:1618-1815. Reviewer claims: (a) PHY stays on at final failed PHY-endpoint attempt (break at 1729 before 1755), right; (b) sink-unplug abort disables PHY before break (1755 then 1763) and success also needs !is_link_bw_low, right; (c) omitted false return on sink-unplug break before limits, right. All three round-1/2/15 claims were valid against the older prose. R:right

name: dp_perform_fixed_vs_pe_training_sequence
prose: Returns enum link_training_result and trains an 8b/10b DP link through a fixed-VS/PE vendor retimer. If lt_settings->lttpr_mode is LTTPR_MODE_NON_TRANSPARENT it returns at once the status from perform_fixed_vs_pe_nontransparent_training_sequence (which raises cr_pattern_time to at least 16000, applies the vendor link-rate toggle workaround, writes link settings, and runs clock recovery and channel equalization per repeater from the repeater count down and then for DPRX, stopping at the first non-success). Otherwise it sets pre_disable_intercept_delay_ms from debug.fixed_vs_aux_delay_config_wa (1x for 2 repeaters, 2x for more than 2, 0 otherwise), sends vendor reset, vs, pe and intercept-enable writes to the retimer, writes DP_DOWNSPREAD_CTRL and DP_LANE_COUNT_SET (enhanced framing; POST_LT_ADJ_REQ_GRANTED taken from the sink capability when pattern_for_eq is below pattern sequence 4), and, when the LTTPR OUI is all zero, writes a toggled link rate to DP_LINK_BW_SET if link->vendor_specific_lttpr_link_rate_wa equals the rate or is 0 and updates that field to the rate. It then writes the real rate to DP_LINK_BW_SET, sends the dpmf vendor writes (plus five more for four lanes), and runs a clock recovery loop (bounded by LINK_TRAINING_MAX_RETRY_COUNT and LINK_TRAINING_MAX_CR_RETRY, with up to 10 intercept-disable attempts on the first pass) and sets status from dp_get_cr_failure. If that status is success it runs the channel equalization loop with the vendor eq writes, where the status becomes LINK_TRAINING_EQ_FAIL_CR if clock recovery is lost, LINK_TRAINING_SUCCESS when ch_eq, symbol lock and interlane alignment are all done, and stays LINK_TRAINING_EQ_FAIL_EQ when the retry count is exhausted. It returns that status.

name: core_link_read_dpcd
prose: Returns enum dc_status and reads size bytes of DPCD starting at address into data. It first calls dpcd_extend_address_range, which, if the requested range starts or ends inside the mandatory block from DP_LT_TUNABLE_PHY_REPEATER_FIELD_DATA_STRUCTURE_REV to DP_PHY_REPEATER_128B132B_RATES, widens it to cover that block and then allocates a temporary zeroed buffer with kcalloc (only an ASSERT checks for failure, so a NULL result is not handled); otherwise the buffer is data itself. It then reads partition by partition through internal_link_read_dpcd, splitting on the mandatory DPCD partition table (dpcd_get_next_partition_size searches the table and would run past it for addresses beyond the table). internal_link_read_dpcd returns DC_OK without reading when link->aux_access_disabled is set, and DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED when dm_helpers_dp_read_dpcd fails; the loop stops at the first non-DC_OK status. When the range was extended, dpcd_reduce_address_range copies reduced_size bytes from the caller's data into the temporary buffer (the wrong direction) and frees the buffer, so the bytes read are not copied back to data and data is unchanged in that case. The return value is DC_OK if every partition read returned DC_OK (including all reads skipped because aux access is disabled, in which case data is not filled), DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED if a partition read failed, and DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED without any read when the loop is not entered, which is the case for size 0 (even when aux_access_disabled is set). It keeps no references.
note: Checked against link_dpcd.c:44-57, 111-126, 138-195, 197-228. Reviewer claims: (1) copy-back goes the wrong way: right (line 193 memcpy(&extended_data[offset], reduced_data, ...)); (2) aux_access_disabled returns DC_OK without reading: right (50-56); (3) aux disabled with size 0 returns DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED: right (loop at 217 never runs). R:right

name: core_link_write_dpcd
prose: Returns enum dc_status and writes size bytes from data to DPCD at address, partition by partition. The loop runs while size is non-zero: it takes the next partition size from the mandatory DPCD partition table (dpcd_get_next_partition_size, which would run past the table for addresses beyond it), calls internal_link_write_dpcd, and stops at the first status other than DC_OK. internal_link_write_dpcd returns DC_OK without writing when link->aux_access_disabled is set and DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED when dm_helpers_dp_write_dpcd fails. The result is DC_OK when every partition returned DC_OK (so with aux access disabled it returns DC_OK having written nothing), DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED when a partition write failed (partitions already written stay written), and DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED without any write when size is 0, even when aux_access_disabled is set. It keeps no references or locks.
note: Checked against link_dpcd.c:59-72, 230-250. All three reviewer claims right (size 0 returns DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED at 238/240; aux disabled returns DC_OK without writing; both combined for size 0). R:right

name: edp_set_backlight_level
prose: Returns bool. It reads backlight_pwm_u16_16 and frame_ramp from backlight_level_params and logs them with DC_LOG_BACKLIGHT (a log call that executes on every path). If link->connector_signal is not an embedded signal (dc_is_embedded_signal) it does nothing else and returns true. For an embedded signal it looks up the pipe for the link with get_pipe_from_link, stores backlight_pwm_u16_16 in link->panel_cntl->stored_backlight_registers.USER_LEVEL when link->panel_cntl is non-NULL (this store happens before the pipe check, so it also happens on the false return), and returns false if no pipe is found. Otherwise it sets frame_ramp to 0 when the pipe's plane_state is NULL, writes the resulting frame_ramp back into backlight_level_params->frame_ramp, calls dc->hwss.set_backlight_level(pipe_ctx, backlight_level_params) and returns true.

Reviewer claims: USER_LEVEL write conditional on panel_cntl (right, 563), still written on the no-pipe false return (right, 563-573), and 'no side effects' for non-embedded is wrong because DC_LOG_BACKLIGHT always logs (right, 556-558). name: edp_set_psr_allow_active
prose: Returns bool and applies PSR settings to an eDP link. In order: returns false if the pool's psr (dmub_psr) is NULL and force_static is true; returns false if dc_get_edp_link_panel_inst fails; returns false if allow_active is non-NULL, *allow_active is true and link->type is dc_connection_none. If power_opts is non-NULL and differs from link->psr_settings.psr_power_opt it stores the new value and, when psr is non-NULL, psr_feature_enabled is set and the psr_set_power_opt hook exists, calls it. If psr is non-NULL, psr_feature_enabled is set, force_static is true and the psr_force_static hook exists it calls that hook. If allow_active is non-NULL and *allow_active differs from link->psr_settings.psr_allow_active it stores the new value, calls dc_z10_restore(dc) when the new value is false, then calls psr_enable when psr is non-NULL and psr_feature_enabled is set, else dmcu set_psr_enable when a dmcu exists, is initialized and psr_feature_enabled is set, else returns false (after the stored value and any z10 restore, power-option change and force-static call have already happened). Otherwise it returns true. psr_enable is called without checking that the hook pointer is non-NULL.
note: Checked against link_edp_panel_control.c:585-632. Reviewer claims: false path when no psr and no dmcu after allow_active changed (right, 629), that path has already stored psr_allow_active and may call dc_z10_restore (right, 618-621), and force_static also requires psr_feature_enabled (right, 612-613). R:right

name: dcn10_mpc_construct
prose: Void constructor (dcn10_mpc.c:498-520) that initialises a struct dcn10_mpc. It stores ctx in mpc10->base.ctx, sets mpc10->base.funcs to &dcn10_mpc_funcs, stores the register, shift and mask table pointers in mpc10->mpc_regs, mpc_shift and mpc_mask, sets mpc10->mpcc_in_use_mask to 0 and mpc10->num_mpcc to num_mpcc, and then for i from 0 to MAX_MPCC-1 calls mpc1_init_mpcc(&mpc10->base.mpcc_array[i], i). The loop count is MAX_MPCC regardless of num_mpcc. It returns nothing, has no failure path, and does not copy the tables (it keeps the pointers).

name: dcn30_split_stream_for_mpc_or_odm
prose: Static bool (dcn30_resource.c:1520-1580) that sets up sec_pipe as a second pipe split from pri_pipe, either as an ODM neighbour (odm true) or as a bottom pipe (odm false). It saves sec_pipe->pipe_idx, copies *pri_pipe over *sec_pipe, restores pipe_idx, and points sec_pipe's plane resources (mi, hubp, ipp, xfm, dpp, mpcc_inst) at the pool entries for that index and clears stream_res.dsc. In the ODM case it relinks next_odm_pipe/prev_odm_pipe and the top/bottom pointers through any ODM neighbours of pri_pipe's top and bottom pipes, makes sec_pipe pri_pipe's next_odm_pipe, takes the opp from the pool when sec_pipe has no top_pipe and from top_pipe otherwise, and if the stream's timing.flags.DSC is 1 calls dcn20_acquire_dsc; if no DSC was acquired it returns false (after the pipes were already relinked). In the non-ODM case it makes sec_pipe the bottom pipe of pri_pipe, linking in pri_pipe's previous bottom pipe if any. Otherwise it returns true. False is returned only for the failed DSC acquisition.

name: dcn316_resource_construct
prose: Static bool (dcn316_resource.c:1728-2026) that builds the DCN 3.16 resource pool. It points the BIOS registers, pool res_cap (res_cap_dcn31) and pool funcs at static tables, derives pipe_count and mpcc_count from res_cap->num_timing_generator, fills in dc->caps fields (including color-pipeline capabilities), queries the VBIOS for LTTPR support when the get_lttpr_caps hook exists (vbios_lttpr_aware is set true regardless), copies debug_defaults_drv for the production environment, and initialises the vm_helper if present. It then creates the clock sources, DP DTO clock source, DCCG, IRQ service, HUBBUB, hubps/dpps, opps, timing generators, PSR, ABMs, MPC, DSCs, DWB, MMHUBBUB, aux engines and hw i2cs, and calls resource_construct. prose: Returns enum mod_hdcp_status and runs one step of the HDCP 2.x DisplayPort transition state machine with a switch on current_state(hdcp), filling the output callback and watchdog fields and setting the next state. name: amdgpu_od_set_init
prose: Static int (amdgpu_pm.c:4528-4660) that creates the gpu_od sysfs directory tree for overdrive controls. It allocates top_set with kzalloc and returns -ENOMEM immediately (no cleanup needed) if that fails; otherwise it adds top_set to adev->pm.od_kobj_list, creates its kobject named gpu_od under the device kobject (failure goes to err_out), and then, for each named container in amdgpu_od_set.containers: a self-contained container whose feature is not supported is skipped with nothing created; a supported self-contained container gets an od_attribute (linked into top_set->attribute, not into the od_kobj_list) and a sysfs file under gpu_od; any other container gets a sub_set added to adev->pm.od_kobj_list with a kobject named after the container under gpu_od, plus an od_attribute (linked into sub_set->attribute) and sysfs file for each supported sub_feature. Failures of kzalloc (-ENOMEM), kobject_init_and_add or sysfs_create_file jump to err_out, which calls amdgpu_od_set_fini(adev) and returns the error. Finally, if adev->pm.od_kobj_list holds only gpu_od (list_is_singular), it also goes to err_out, so amdgpu_od_set_fini removes everything and the function returns the current ret value, which is 0 at that point. Otherwise it returns 0. If kobject_init_and_add fails for top_set or a sub_set, that entry is already on the list but its attribute list head is not yet initialised, so amdgpu_od_set_fini, which walks the attribute list of every list entry, reads a zeroed list head there.

name: smu10_read_sensor
prose: Returns int. It decides has_gfx_busy: true for a Picasso APU with smu_version at least 0x41e3b or a Raven APU with smu_version at least 0x1e5500, false otherwise. Then by sensor index: AMDGPU_PP_SENSOR_GFX_SCLK and AMDGPU_PP_SENSOR_GFX_MCLK send PPSMC_MSG_GetGfxclkFrequency or PPSMC_MSG_GetFclkFrequency via smum_send_msg_to_smc; if that returns nonzero the function returns that value with *value and *size untouched, otherwise it stores the reported value times 100 in *(uint32_t *)value and sets *size to 4. AMDGPU_PP_SENSOR_GPU_TEMP stores smu10_thermal_get_temperature(hwmgr) in *(uint32_t *)value, leaves *size unchanged and returns 0. AMDGPU_PP_SENSOR_VCN_POWER_STATE stores 0 when vcn_power_gated is set and 1 otherwise, sets *size to 4 and returns 0. AMDGPU_PP_SENSOR_GPU_LOAD returns -EOPNOTSUPP when has_gfx_busy is false (so it is supported only on those firmware versions); otherwise it sends PPSMC_MSG_GetGfxBusy, stores min(activity_percent, 100) in *(uint32_t *)value and returns 0 on success, or returns -EIO if the message fails (it does not set *size). Any other idx returns -EOPNOTSUPP.

name: smu7_apply_state_adjust_rules
prose: Returns int. It returns -EINVAL immediately if cast_phw_smu7_power_state of request_ps->hardware is NULL; otherwise it returns 0 after adjusting the requested power state in place. It sets data->battery_state (true when the ui_label is PP_StateUILabel_Battery) and clears data->mclk_ignore_signal. Only when the AC flag adev->pm.ac_power is false does it clamp every performance level's memory and engine clock down to the DC maximums (max_clock_voltage_on_dc). It takes minimum clocks from the display configuration; when the StablePState platform cap is enabled it instead uses AC limits, sets the minimum engine clock to the highest vdd_dep_on_sclk entry not above 75 percent of the AC max sclk (or entry 0 if none), and sets the minimum memory clock to the full AC max mclk (not 75 percent). It then decides whether to disable mclk switching (frame-lock cap, or several unsynchronised displays, or a vblank that is too short); with no displays it sets mclk_ignore_signal on POLARIS10 through VEGAM chips and otherwise disables the no-switching condition. Level 0 gets the first level's clocks raised to the minimums (capped at the limit), and when switching is disabled on a chip outside POLARIS10..VEGAM the memory clock is taken from the last performance level (index performance_level_count - 1), not the second. Level 1's engine clock is raised to at least level 0's. With switching disabled it uses level 1's memory clock as a floor and, for POLARIS10..VEGAM with display-based disabling, searches the mclk latency table for the lowest frequency within the tolerable latency (setting mclk_ignore_signal if none qualifies), or uses level 1's memory clock for frame lock; with switching enabled it only raises level 1's memory clock to at least level 0's. With StablePState enabled every performance level is overwritten with the stable-pstate engine and memory clocks and with pcie_gen and pcie_lane both set to data->pcie_gen_performance.max.

name: analogix_dp_transfer
prose: Returns ssize_t and performs one DP AUX transaction through the Analogix DP controller registers. It returns -E2BIG (after a WARN_ON) if msg->size is above 16 and -EINVAL, before any further register access beyond the initial buffer clear, if the request (with DP_AUX_I2C_MOT masked off) is not one of I2C write, I2C read, native write or native read. It programs the command, length and 20-bit address registers and, when bit 0 of msg->request is clear (the write requests), writes msg->buffer bytes into the data registers. It sets AUX_EN (plus ADDR_ONLY for size 0) and polls for AUX_EN to clear (500 ms) and for RPLY_RECEIV (20 ms); on either timeout, or when an AUX error is flagged with a status other than timeout, it reinitialises the AUX channel with analogix_dp_init_aux and returns -EREMOTEIO. An AUX_ERR with AUX_STATUS_TIMEOUT_ERROR returns -ETIMEDOUT directly (without the reinitialisation). On success it copies msg->size bytes from the data registers into msg->buffer when bit 0 of msg->request is set (that is the I2C read and the native read), sets msg->reply to the native or I2C defer value if the RX command register shows a defer, otherwise to the I2C ACK or native ACK according to the request type, and returns msg->size.

name: sp_tx_edid_read
prose: Static int (anx7625.c:1122-1235) that reads the EDID through the AUX channel into pedid_blocks_buf. It writes the AUX address registers and returns -EIO if any of those register writes returns a negative value; returns the negative value of sp_tx_get_edid_block if that fails; then loops count from 0 while blocks_num >= count. For count 0 and 1 it reads eight chunks of MAX_DPCD_BUFFER_SIZE bytes with edid_read and copies each successful chunk into the buffer, stopping that inner loop at a failure (edid_read failure does not make the function fail, and the remaining chunks are not read for that count); for count 2 and 3 it reads eight chunks each with segments_edid_read and returns that function's negative value (an errno from the register, AUX or retry logic, not necessarily -EIO) as soon as one fails; other counts do nothing. After the loop it returns -EINVAL if drm_edid_is_valid fails on the buffer, returns the negative value of sp_tx_rst_aux if the final AUX reset fails (not necessarily -EIO), and otherwise returns blocks_num + 1, even if some edid_read chunk failed earlier but the buffer still passed the validity check. The buffer is written at offsets up to 32 chunks of MAX_DPCD_BUFFER_SIZE bytes, so it must be at least that large, and drm_edid_is_valid reads according to the block count in the data.

name: samsung_dsim_transfer
prose: Static int (samsung_dsim.c:1530-1564) that submits one DSI transfer and waits for it. It sets xfer->tx_done and rx_done to 0, xfer->result to -ETIMEDOUT and initialises the completion. Under dsi->transfer_lock (irqsave) it records whether the transfer list was empty and appends xfer; if the list was empty it calls samsung_dsim_transfer_start. It then waits for xfer->completed for DSI_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS (the return value of the wait is ignored). If xfer->result is still -ETIMEDOUT afterwards it calls samsung_dsim_remove_transfer to take the transfer off the list (starting the next queued one when the head was removed), logs the packet, and returns -ETIMEDOUT; otherwise it returns xfer->result, which also covers a hardware timeout reported by the interrupt handler. The caller keeps ownership of xfer.

name: tc_probe
prose: Static int I2C probe function (tc358767.c:2456-2604) with many early error returns, each after devm-managed allocations that are released by the driver core. In order it picks the bridge funcs from tc_probe_get_mode, allocates tc with devm_drm_bridge_alloc (returns PTR_ERR on failure), calls tc_probe_bridge_endpoint (returns its nonzero error, covering panel or bridge lookup, panel bridge add and DPI probe failures), gets and enables the 'ref' clock (error returned through dev_err_probe), handles the optional shutdown and reset GPIOs (errors returned), initialises the regmap (error returned), reads the optional toshiba,hpd-pin property (hpd_pin becomes -ENODEV if absent; a value outside 0 to 1 returns -EINVAL), and when client->irq > 0 writes INTCTL_G and requests the threaded irq (failure returned, success sets have_irq). It reads TC_IDREG into tc->rev and returns the read error, or -EINVAL when the ID is neither 0x6601 nor 0x6603; sets assr for 0x6601; performs a software reset sequence if there is no reset GPIO; programs HPD counters and, if have_irq, enables the HPD interrupts when hpd_pin is valid; for non-DPI (eDP/DP) output calls tc_aux_link_setup and returns its error if nonzero. It then sets bridge.of_node, calls drm_bridge_add, stores tc as i2c clientdata, and for DSI input calls tc_mipi_dsi_host_attach; if that fails it calls drm_bridge_remove and returns the error via dev_err_probe, but the clientdata set before is not cleared. Otherwise it returns 0. Failures after drm_bridge_add other than the DSI attach cannot occur.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at tc358767.c:2456). Reviewer claims: DSI attach failure leaves clientdata set (right, 2593 vs 2598-2599), omits -EINVAL for hpd-pin and tc_aux_link_setup error (right, 2519 and 2585-2587), omits tc_probe_bridge_endpoint failures (right, 2473-2475). R:right

name: process_single_tx_qlock
prose: Static int (drm_dp_mst_topology.c:2792-2853) that sends one chunk of a sideband message; the caller is expected to hold mgr->qlock (the _qlock suffix). It returns 0 at once, sending nothing, when txmsg->state is already DRM_DP_SIDEBAND_TX_SENT. Otherwise it zeroes a local header, changes txmsg->state from QUEUED to START_SEND, and calls set_hdr_from_dst_qlock, which fills the header (broadcast with lct 1 and lcr 6 for connection-status-notify, resource-status-notify and clear-payload-id-table requests, otherwise lct/lcr and rad from txmsg->dst) and in the code shown always returns 0 (the early return of a negative value after it is therefore unreachable). It computes the bytes left, limits the chunk to 48 minus 1 CRC byte minus the header size, sets SOMT when nothing has been sent yet and EOMT when the whole remainder fits, encodes the header, copies the chunk, adds the CRC and calls drm_dp_send_sideband_msg on the down or up channel according to up. If that returns nonzero it optionally dumps the message and returns that value; txmsg->cur_offset is not advanced but txmsg->state has already moved from QUEUED to START_SEND. On success it advances cur_offset and returns 1 with state set to DRM_DP_SIDEBAND_TX_SENT if the message is complete, otherwise 0.
note: Checked against drm_dp_mst_topology.c:2763-2788 and 2792-2853. Reviewer claims: precondition names qlock not lock (right: the _qlock suffix and callers), returns 1 on completion and negative on send failure (right, 2850 and 2844), state may already have changed to START_SEND on failure (right, 2806-2807 happens before the send). R:right

name: drm_dp_mst_process_up_req
prose: Static inline bool (drm_dp_mst_topology.c:4055-4098). It looks up the MST branch the request came from: for a broadcast header it uses the GUID of a DP_CONNECTION_STATUS_NOTIFY or DP_RESOURCE_STATUS_NOTIFY body (any other broadcast request type leaves no GUID and so no branch) via drm_dp_get_mst_branch_device_by_guid, and for a non-broadcast header it uses drm_dp_get_mst_branch_device with lct and rad. If no branch is found it returns false at once (no reference was taken). Otherwise, for DP_CONNECTION_STATUS_NOTIFY, if primary_mstb_probing_is_done is false it does nothing (CSN skipped), else it calls drm_dp_mst_handle_conn_stat, remembers whether that asks for more work, and sets the return value true. Resource-status notifications and other request types are not handled (the TODO). It then drops the branch reference with drm_dp_mst_topology_put_mstb, queues mgr->work on system_long_wq if the handler asked for work, and returns the hotplug flag, which is true only for a connection-status notification handled after probing finished; false for every other case, including a skipped CSN and unknown branch.
note: Checked against drm_dp_mst_topology.c:4055-4098. Reviewer claim (true for any resolved request, skipped CSN returns true too) is wrong: hotplug is initialised false (4062) and set true only in the else branch at 4089, which is reached only when probing is done. R:wrong

name: drm_atomic_helper_setup_commit
prose: Returns int. For every CRTC in the state it allocates a drm_crtc_commit (-ENOMEM on failure), initialises it, stores it in new_crtc_state->commit and calls stall_checks, whose error is returned (-EBUSY when nonblock is true and the CRTC's latest commit has not finished flip_done, or a negative errno from the interruptible wait for an older commit). If both the old and new CRTC states are inactive, or state->legacy_cursor_update is set, it completes the commit's flip_done and moves on. Otherwise, if new_crtc_state->event is NULL it allocates an event (-ENOMEM on failure) and stores it, then sets the event's completion to the commit's flip_done, takes references on the commit twice (one for the event, one for state->crtcs[i].commit) and sets abort_completion. For each connector, it returns -EBUSY when nonblock is true and the old connector state has a commit whose flip_done is not complete, then takes a commit from crtc_or_fake_commit (-ENOMEM when that returns NULL) and stores a referenced copy in new_conn_state->commit. Planes are handled the same way. At the end it returns the result of mode_config.helper_private->atomic_commit_setup(state) if that hook exists, otherwise 0. On any earlier error return, commits and references already stored in the state stay there for the caller's cleanup, and the hook is not called.
note: Checked against drm_atomic_helper.c:2508-2619 and stall_checks 2372-2420. Reviewer claims: (round 2) omits -EBUSY from a CRTC commit (right, stall_checks 2388-2394); (round 15) 'no event allocation occurs' is wrong (2553-2556 allocates an event), 'a hook error return means the hook was called' is right (2615-2616). R:mixed

name: drm_atomic_helper_check_modeset
prose: Returns int. For each CRTC in the state it WARNs if the CRTC mutex is not held; sets mode_changed when the mode differs; sets mode_changed and connectors_changed when enable differs; sets active_changed when active differs; returns -EINVAL if new_crtc_state->enable disagrees with whether the connector_mask is non-empty; and sets no_vblank true or false according to drm_dev_has_vblank. It then calls handle_conflicting_encoders (returning its error), and for each connector calls update_connector_routing (returning its error), marks the old CRTC's connectors_changed when the link status or max_requested_bpc changed, and calls the connector helper's atomic_check hook if present (returning its error). For each CRTC whose new state needs a modeset (drm_atomic_crtc_needs_modeset, i.e. mode, active or connectors changed) it calls drm_atomic_add_affected_connectors, drm_atomic_add_affected_planes and drm_atomic_check_valid_clones, returning the first error. It then calls atomic_check on connectors not yet checked, calls drm_atomic_add_encoder_bridges for the old and new best encoder of every connector in the state, and returns the result of mode_valid(state) if nonzero, else the result of mode_fixup(state). The state may be partially updated on an error return.
note: Checked against drm_atomic_helper.c:647-827. Reviewer claims: (a) precondition wrongly requires all connectors present, since the function adds affected connectors (right, 769-775); (b) 'adds connectors and planes only when CRTC enabled and connector_mask empty' is wrong: the condition is drm_atomic_crtc_needs_modeset at 760; and 'does not set active_changed/no_vblank' is wrong (692 and 703-706). R:mixed

name: drm_client_firmware_config
prose: Static bool (drm_client_modeset.c:619-803) that tries to reuse the firmware (BIOS) display configuration for a DRM client. It returns false at the start, before locking or modifying anything, when the driver does not use atomic modesetting, when min(connector_count, BITS_PER_LONG) is not positive (with a warning), or when the kcalloc of save_enabled fails. Otherwise it takes all modeset locks (retrying with backoff), saves a copy of enabled[], and counts connected tiled connectors. It then scans the first count connectors, repeating while it makes progress and some are not configured: a connector that is not enabled is marked configured; one forced off is set disabled but not marked configured; one without a best encoder (or whose state has no CRTC) goes to bail if its force is above DRM_FORCE_OFF, else it is disabled and marked configured; an enabled one counts as enabled, goes to bail if the same CRTC already appears in crtcs[], and otherwise gets its mode replaced by the cmdline, preferred, first, current-CRTC or (for incomplete tile groups) non-tiled mode, its CRTC stored in crtcs[i], and is marked configured with fallback cleared. Afterwards it calls drm_client_get_tile_offsets for each tiled connector, which fills the offsets array. If fewer connectors are enabled than detected and fewer than the CRTC count, or if no connector was configured, fallback stays or is set true. Both the fallback and bail paths restore enabled[] from the saved copy and make the result false (the modes and crtcs entries already changed are not restored). It then drops the locks, frees save_enabled and returns true only when neither bail nor fallback happened.
note: Checked against drm_client_modeset.c:619-803. Reviewer claims (from round 1): offsets are never filled (wrong, 769-776 call drm_client_get_tile_offsets), early false returns for non-atomic, count <= 0 and allocation failure (right, 638-646). R:mixed

name: drm_draw_color_from_xrgb8888
prose: Returns u32 by a switch on format with no side effects other than a possible one-time warning. For DRM_FORMAT_RGB888 and DRM_FORMAT_XRGB8888 it returns color unchanged. For DRM_FORMAT_RGB565, RGBA5551, XRGB1555, ARGB1555, ARGB8888, XBGR8888, ABGR8888, XRGB2101010, ARGB2101010 and ABGR2101010 it returns the result of the matching drm_pixel_xrgb8888_to_<format> conversion of color. For every other format it executes WARN_ONCE and returns 0. Any u32 values are accepted.
note: Checked against drm_draw.c:27-57. Reviewer claims about the RGBA5551 fourcc being wrong in the old prose (0x31414752 is not DRM_FORMAT_RGBA5551, which is 'R','A','1','5' = 0x35314152) are right; the prose now uses only symbolic format names. Contract left empty. R:right

name: add_3d_struct_modes
prose: Static int (drm_edid.c:4762-4794) that adds up to three 3D variants of the mode at VIC index vic_index. For each of bit 0, bit 6 and bit 8 of structure that is set, it calls drm_display_mode_from_vic_index; when that returns a mode it ORs in DRM_MODE_FLAG_3D_FRAME_PACKING (bit 0), DRM_MODE_FLAG_3D_TOP_AND_BOTTOM (bit 6) or DRM_MODE_FLAG_3D_SIDE_BY_SIDE_HALF (bit 8), passes it to drm_mode_probed_add (so the connector's probed list owns it) and counts it. The mode lookup returns NULL (adding nothing for that bit) when the connector has no VIC list, when vic_index is not below vics_len, when the VIC entry is 0, or when the mode allocation fails; a negative vic_index is not rejected by the check (it only tests vic_index >= vics_len) and would index before the array. It returns the number of modes added, from 0 to 3; the result is 0 when none of the three bits is set or all lookups failed, and a failure for one bit does not stop the other bits from adding modes.
note: Checked against drm_edid.c:4583-4593 and 4762-4794. Reviewer claims: partial success possible so result can be nonzero after an allocation failure (right, no early return), negative vic_index is not bounds-checked (right, 4589), formal-contract claim not applicable (contract left empty). R:right

name: drm_fb_helper_check_var
prose: Returns int and validates an fb_var_screeninfo request against the fbdev emulation framebuffer (drm_fb_helper.c:1205-1293). It returns -EINVAL immediately if in_dbg_master() is true. After that it sets var->pixclock to 0 when it was nonzero, so that change happens on every later path including the error returns. It returns -EINVAL if the framebuffer format is not DRM_FORMAT_C1, C2 or C4 and its plane-0 block width or block height is above 1; if var->bits_per_pixel exceeds the format's bpp or any of xres, yres, xres_virtual, yres_virtual exceeds the framebuffer width or height. It then calls __fill_var(var, info, fb), which rewrites the geometry and virtual sizes, and returns -EINVAL if yoffset or xoffset is greater than the virtual minus visible size, if var->grayscale > 0, or if var->nonstd is nonzero. Only after those checks, if all colour offset, length and msb_right fields are zero, it fills the pixel format fields with drm_fb_helper_fill_pixel_fmt. It then returns -EINVAL if the pixel format fields differ from info->var (drm_fb_pixel_format_equal), otherwise 0. Pixel-format filling therefore does not occur on the offset, grayscale or nonstd error returns.
note: Checked against drm_fb_helper.c:1205-1293. Reviewer claims: C1/C2/C4 exempt from the block-size -EINVAL (right, 1222-1233), omits -EINVAL for pixel format mismatch after normalisation (right, 1287-1289), pixel format filled only after the offset/grayscale/nonstd checks (right, 1258-1281). R:right

name: cdv_intel_lvds_init
prose: Void function (cdv_intel_lvds.c:477-667) that sets up the LVDS output on a Cedarview GPU. It returns having done nothing when dev_priv->lvds_enabled_in_vbt is false or lvds_is_present_in_vbt says no panel. It then allocates the encoder, connector and private data (returning, with partial frees through the error labels, when an allocation fails), creates the DDC i2c bus (GPIOC), initialises the LVDS connector and simple encoder, attaches the scaling-mode and backlight properties, and creates the backlight i2c bus on GPIOB with target address 0x2C, storing it in gma_encoder->i2c_bus and dev_priv->lvds_i2c_bus. Under dev->mode_config.mutex it reads EDID modes through psb_intel_ddc_get_modes and, if a preferred probed mode exists, stores a duplicate in mode_dev->panel_fixed_mode and jumps to out (even if the duplicate is NULL); otherwise it tries the VBT mode (duplicate marked preferred, jump to out if it succeeded), then, if the LVDS port is enabled and a CRTC exists for its pipe, the mode from the CRTC (marked preferred, jump to out if it succeeded). If panel_fixed_mode is still NULL it unlocks and unwinds everything (destroying the backlight bus, encoder, connector, DDC bus and freeing the private structures), so no LVDS output is registered. The PWM setup (BLC_PWM_CTL2 pipe select and PWM_ENABLE) is reached only when none of the three sources jumped to out yet panel_fixed_mode is non-NULL (for example already set before the call); when the mode comes from EDID, VBT or the CRTC the code jumps to out and does not program the PWM. It unlocks the mutex at out and returns void.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at cdv_intel_lvds.c:477). Reviewer claim (PWM not programmed when the mode is found via EDID or VBT; goto out before the PWM block) is right: gotos at 595, 606 and 624, PWM at 636-646. R:right

name: gma_find_best_pll
prose: Returns bool (gma_display.c:750-811). It picks clock.p2: if the crtc has an LVDS output and the LVDS port is enabled it takes limit->p2.p2_fast when the LVDS clock-B power bits show power-up and p2_slow otherwise; for other cases it takes p2_slow when target is below limit->p2.dot_limit and p2_fast otherwise. It zeroes *best_clock, then loops m1, m2 (bounded by m1 or any value when m1 is 0), n and p1 over the limit ranges, computes each candidate with clock_funcs->clock(refclk, &clock), skips candidates rejected by clock_funcs->pll_is_valid, and for accepted candidates whose abs(clock.dot - target) is strictly smaller than the best error so far (initially target) copies the candidate to *best_clock. It returns true if at least one accepted candidate improved on the initial error of target (so some candidate had error below target), and false otherwise, in which case *best_clock stays zeroed. It takes no locks.
note: slice cut the head: the function is gma_find_best_pll (gma_display.c:750), not cdv_intel_find_best_PLL (that name does not exist in this file). Old prose matched the code. R:n/a

name: hibmc_de_init
prose: Returns int (hibmc_drm_de.c:492-528). It initialises the primary plane with drm_universal_plane_init (logging and returning the error if that fails), adds the plane helper funcs, initialises the CRTC with drm_crtc_init_with_planes (error returned), sets the gamma size to 256 with drm_mode_crtc_set_gamma_size (error returned), adds the CRTC helper funcs and returns 0. On an error return it does not undo earlier steps (the plane or CRTC stays initialised); later steps are skipped.

name: ivch_mode_set
prose: Static void (dvo_ivch.c:399-440) that programs the IVCH panel-fit registers. It calls ivch_reset, which writes VR10 = 0 and then each backup register from priv->reg_backup, takes the last saved backup value as vr10 and sets vr01 to VR01_DITHER_ENABLE when its VR10_INTERFACE_DEPTH_MASK bits equal VR10_INTERFACE_2X18 or VR10_INTERFACE_1X18 (otherwise 0). vr40 starts as VR40_STALL_ENABLE | VR40_VERTICAL_INTERP_ENABLE | VR40_HORIZONTAL_INTERP_ENABLE. If mode->hdisplay or vdisplay differs from adjusted_mode->crtc_hdisplay or crtc_vdisplay, it also sets VR01_PANEL_FIT_ENABLE and VR40_CLOCK_GATING_ENABLE and writes the horizontal ratio to VR42 and the vertical ratio to VR41, each computed as ((mode size - 1) << 16) / (crtc size - 1) >> 2; a crtc_hdisplay or crtc_vdisplay of 1 makes that division by zero, so the caller must not pass one. VR41 and VR42 are written only in the size-mismatch case. In the other case it clears VR01_PANEL_FIT_ENABLE and VR40_CLOCK_GATING_ENABLE (they were not set). Finally it clears VR40_AUTO_RATIO_ENABLE and writes VR01 and VR40 on every call. It returns nothing.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at dvo_ivch.c:399). Reviewer claims: VR41/VR42 written only on size mismatch (right, 430-431), division by crtc size minus 1 when the value is 1 (right, 426-429), VR01 may also include VR01_PANEL_FIT_ENABLE (right, 424). R:right

name: g4x_hdmi_init
prose: Returns bool (g4x_hdmi.c:669-779). It returns false without allocating anything when assert_port_valid or assert_hdmi_port_valid fail. Otherwise it looks up the VBT child device data (a missing entry only logs), allocates a digital port (false if that fails) and a connector (on failure frees dig_port and returns false), initialises the encoder with drm_encoder_init as a TMDS encoder named by port (on failure frees connector and dig_port and returns false), fills in the encoder hooks according to PCH, Cherryview and Valleyview platform checks, sets type, power domain, port, pipe_mask, cloneable and hpd_pin, stores hdmi_reg in dig_port->hdmi.hdmi_reg, calls intel_infoframe_init, and calls intel_hdmi_init_connector; if that returns false it calls drm_encoder_cleanup, frees the connector and dig_port and returns false. Otherwise it returns true, leaving dig_port and the connector owned by the driver's encoder and connector lists.
note: slice cut the head: function is g4x_hdmi_init (head at g4x_hdmi.c:669; slice started at 762). The old prose treated the arguments as caller-allocated objects, which is not the case: the function allocates dig_port and the connector itself (690-696) and frees them on failure. R:n/a

name: ilk_wm_fbc
prose: Static u32 function (i9xx_wm.c:2420-2434). If cpp is 0 it executes WARN_ON and returns 0; otherwise, if horiz_pixels is 0 it executes WARN_ON and returns 0. Otherwise it returns DIV_ROUND_UP(pri_val * 64, horiz_pixels * cpp) + 2, computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic, so pri_val * 64, horiz_pixels * cpp and the DIV_ROUND_UP addend all wrap modulo 2^32 for large inputs; for inputs where nothing wraps the result is the ceiling of pri_val * 64 / (horiz_pixels * cpp) plus 2. It has no other effect beyond the warnings and takes no locks.
note: Checked against i9xx_wm.c:2420-2434. Reviewer claims: the contract omits the zero-argument WARN return path and the WARN side effect (right); an overflow input (pri_val=7, horiz_pixels=4294967285, cpp=1) falsifies the old contract (right, horiz_pixels*cpp wraps only for cpp>1 but the +d-1 addend in DIV_ROUND_UP wraps). Contract left empty because of the WARN side effect and u32 wrap-around. R:right

name: _i9xx_lut_10_ldw
prose: Static u32 function (intel_color.c:834-837) that returns drm_color_lut_extract(a, 10) & 0xff, i.e. the low 8 bits of the 10-bit value obtained from a 16-bit LUT sample. drm_color_lut_extract with 10 bits of precision returns DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(a * 1023, 65535), which is (a * 1023 + 32767) / 65535 in unsigned arithmetic; for any u16 a the product fits in 32 bits. It has no other effects.
note: Checked against intel_color.c:834-837 and drm_color_mgmt.h:43-51. Reviewer claim (formal contract used /65536 and +32768 rather than rounding by 65535, e.g. a=65503 gives 254 not 255) is right; the replacement contract uses DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST's (x + 32767) / 65535. R:right

name: skl_commit_modeset_enables
prose: Static void (intel_display.c:6950-7106) that commits CRTC updates in a DDB-safe order. It computes entries[] and the pipe masks itself: for each CRTC whose new state is hw.active it records the old DDB entry and adds the pipe to update_pipes when no modeset is needed, otherwise adds it to modeset_pipes. It calls intel_pre_update_crtc (forward order) for the update pipes, calls intel_dbuf_mbus_pre_ddb_update, then loops until update_pipes is empty: in reverse pipe order it skips a pipe whose new DDB allocation overlaps another pipe's entry (retrying later; the loop has no other exit), otherwise records the entry, clears the pipe's bit, calls intel_update_crtc, and waits for the next vblank when that pipe's DDB changed and update_pipes or modeset_pipes still has bits. It then calls intel_dbuf_mbus_post_ddb_update, enables modeset pipes with intel_enable_crtc (first those that are neither joiner secondaries nor MST slaves or port-sync masters, then the remaining non-secondary ones, clearing each enabled pipe's joined pipe mask from modeset_pipes), calls intel_pre_update_crtc in forward order for the pipes that were modeset, and then calls intel_update_crtc in reverse order for them, with drm_WARN_ON on any DDB overlap. Finally it warns if modeset_pipes or update_pipes is not empty. It returns void.
note: Checked against intel_display.c:6950-7106. Reviewer claims: precondition wrongly requires the caller to precompute masks (right, 6959-6972); intel_pre_update_crtc for the modeset pipes runs forward, only intel_update_crtc is reverse (right, 7075-7101). R:right

name: intel_dp_detect
prose: Static int connector detect callback (intel_dp.c:5924-6063) whose return value is a connector_status_* value, or -EDEADLK. It warns if connection_mutex is not held. It returns connector_status_disconnected at once when the display device is not enabled, and returns the connector's existing status (connector->base.status) at once when intel_display_driver_check_access fails; neither of these paths touches PPS VDD. Otherwise it flushes pending connector commits, turns PPS VDD on, and determines a status: edp_detect for eDP, intel_dp_detect_dpcd when the digital port is connected, else disconnected; a non-disconnected status is turned into disconnected if intel_dp_mst_verify_dpcd_state fails. When the status is disconnected it resets the test and DSC/panel-replay sink state, calls intel_dp_mst_disconnect and intel_dp_tunnel_disconnect and jumps to out_unset_edid. Otherwise it initialises the source OUI and runs intel_dp_tunnel_detect: -EDEADLK is stored as the status and the function jumps straight to out_vdd_off (no EDID unsetting, no probe or subconnector update); a result of 1 bumps the epoch counter. It then reads PSR (non-eDP), DSC and SDP caps, resets the link params if requested, calls intel_dp_mst_configure, and if the port is in MST mode sets the status to disconnected and goes to out_unset_edid, with the MST and tunnel state left untouched and the EDID not unset because is_mst is true. In SST mode it checks the link state (non-eDP), clears the AUX NACK and defer counters, calls intel_dp_set_edid and sets the status to connected for eDP or when a detect EDID exists; if no EDID was read the status stays at the value determined earlier (it is not recomputed from the EDID read), then it checks the device service IRQ. At out_unset_edid it unsets the EDID when the status is not connected and not MST, turns the DPCD probe flag off and updates the subconnector property for non-eDP. At out_vdd_off it turns PPS VDD off and returns the status.

name: intel_dp_aux_xfer
prose: Static int (intel_dp_aux.c:236-453) that performs one AUX transaction. It takes the digital port lock; for a non-eDP port that is not connected it returns -ENXIO after releasing only that lock. Otherwise it takes an AUX power-domain reference, takes the PPS lock for eDP or on VLV/CHV, turns VDD on (remembering whether this call did it), and sets the CPU latency QoS request to 0. It waits up to three times for the channel not to be busy; if still busy it returns -EBUSY after cleanup. It returns -E2BIG after cleanup (checked after the busy wait) when send_bytes or recv_size exceeds 20. It then tries each AUX clock divider, up to five attempts each, writing the send data and control, waiting for completion, clearing done/error status, retrying on timeout (continue) or receive error (after a sleep), and going to done on success; if no attempt completed it returns -EBUSY. At done it returns -EIO on a receive error, -ETIMEDOUT on a timeout, and -EBUSY when the reported message size is 0 or above 20. Otherwise it clamps the reply size to recv_size, reads the reply words into recv and returns that byte count, which is 0 when recv_size is 0. After the busy check, every return path restores the QoS request, turns VDD off only if this call turned it on, releases the PPS lock if taken, releases the power reference asynchronously, and unlocks the digital port.

name: intel_dp_init_lttpr_phys
prose: Static int (intel_dp_link_training.c:147-195). It returns 0 if intel_dp_read_lttpr_common_caps fails, and 0 if drm_dp_lttpr_count of the common caps is 0 (no LTTPR). If the link is active it never changes the mode: for a negative count (an invalid caps value) or when transparent mode is already enabled it resets the repeater count byte and returns 0, otherwise it returns the positive count. If the link is inactive it calls drm_dp_lttpr_init(aux, count); when that returns nonzero (which includes every negative count, since it returns -ENODEV for them, as well as AUX write failures) it sets the transparent mode and resets the repeater count byte and returns 0; when it succeeds the count is positive, it sets non-transparent mode and returns the count. The function therefore returns 0 or a positive repeater count and never a negative value.

Reviewer claims: out_reset_lttpr_count also resets the count byte on active links for transparent mode or negative count (right, 170-172, 191-194); a negative return is impossible when inactive because drm_dp_lttpr_init rejects negative counts (right, drm_dp_helper.c:2995-2996). name: bxt_ddi_pll_enable
prose: Static void (intel_dpll_mgr.c:2040-2146), returns nothing and reports no failure. It derives the port from pll->info->id (1:1 mapping) and the PHY and channel with bxt_port_to_phy_channel. It sets PORT_PLL_REF_SEL (non-SSC reference); on Geminilake it sets PORT_PLL_POWER_ENABLE and waits up to 200 us for PORT_PLL_POWER_STATE, logging drm_err if that wait fails. It clears the 10-bit clock enable, and read-modify-writes the P1/P2 fields (EBB0), M2 integer (PLL0), N (PLL1), M2 fraction (PLL2) and its enable (PLL3), the coefficient fields (PLL6), target count (PLL8), lock threshold (PLL9) and DCO amplitude fields (PLL10) from hw_state, then triggers recalibration through EBB4 and writes hw_state->ebb4. It then sets PORT_PLL_ENABLE, posts the read, and waits up to 200 us for PORT_PLL_LOCK, logging drm_err if it does not lock. Only after that, on Geminilake it ORs DCC_DELAY_RANGE_2 into the TX DW5 group register, and finally it writes the lane stagger fields into the PCS DW12 group register. A timeout is only logged; execution continues.

name: intel_fb_is_rc_ccs_cc_modifier

name: do_gmbus_xfer
prose: Static int (intel_gmbus.c:659-788) that performs an I2C transfer over GMBUS. It first disables GMBUS clock gating (display workaround) on Geminilake, Broxton, SPT or CNP platforms. It writes GMBUS0 and loops over the messages (an index read/write pair counts as two): each message is sent with gmbus_index_xfer, gmbus_xfer_read or gmbus_xfer_write, followed by a hardware-ready wait if that returned 0. A -ETIMEDOUT from a transfer or wait goes to the timeout path: GMBUS0 is cleared and the function returns -EAGAIN (to let the i2c core fall back to bit banging), not -ETIMEDOUT. Any other nonzero result goes to clear_err: it waits for idle, sets the result to -ENXIO, or -ETIMEDOUT if the idle wait failed, toggles the software clear-interrupt bit, clears GMBUS1 and GMBUS0 and, if the result is -ENXIO, the failing message is the first one and this is the first try, retries from the start once; otherwise it returns that result. When all messages succeed it writes a STOP cycle, waits for idle and returns -ETIMEDOUT if that wait fails, or the number of messages transferred (i, equal to num) otherwise; GMBUS0 is cleared on this path too. All paths re-enable clock gating before returning.

Reviewer claims: -ETIMEDOUT if the idle wait after STOP fails, so the bus is not always left idle (right, 709-714); round 15 claim that wait timeouts during a transfer return -ETIMEDOUT rather than -EAGAIN is wrong (693-694 goto timeout, 778 sets -EAGAIN). name: hdcp2_disable_encryption

It warns (drm_WARN_ON) if LINK_ENCRYPTION_STATUS is not set in HDCP2_STATUS but does not stop, clears CTL_LINK_ENCRYPTION_REQ in HDCP2_CTL, and waits up to HDCP_ENCRYPT_STATUS_CHANGE_TIMEOUT_MS for LINK_ENCRYPTION_STATUS to clear (a -ETIMEDOUT result is only logged). If hdcp->shim->toggle_signalling is non-NULL it calls it with enable false and overwrites ret with its result: on failure it logs and returns that error, and on success ret becomes 0, so a wait timeout is hidden and the function returns 0. If toggle_signalling is NULL it returns the wait result (0 or -ETIMEDOUT or another wait error).

name: intel_hdcp2_check_link
prose: Static int (intel_hdcp.c:2152-2236). It takes hdcp->mutex and then dig_port->hdcp.mutex itself and releases both at out before returning. It returns -EINVAL if hdcp->value is not DRM_MODE_CONTENT_PROTECTION_ENABLED or hdcp2_encrypted is false. If the hardware no longer reports HDCP2 encryption in use it logs, returns -ENXIO after _intel_hdcp2_disable and setting the value to DESIRED. It then calls shim->check_2_2_link: for HDCP_LINK_PROTECTED it sets the value to ENABLED unless the current value is UNDESIRED, and returns the status value it got (HDCP_LINK_PROTECTED); for HDCP_TOPOLOGY_CHANGE, if the current value is UNDESIRED it returns at once with that status unchanged, otherwise it re-authenticates the repeater topology and on success sets ENABLED and returns 0; on a failed topology authentication, or for any other status, it calls _intel_hdcp2_disable, sets the value to DESIRED and returns the disable result (0 on success, the error otherwise).

name: intel_hdcp_gsc_initiate_locality_check

name: intel_pps_vdd_on_unlocked
prose: Returns bool (intel_pps.c:745-801). It records need_to_disable as the inverse of intel_dp->pps.want_panel_vdd at entry. It returns need_to_disable, so for an eDP the return value is true exactly when want_panel_vdd was false on entry (the caller then owes a matching VDD off), whether or not VDD was already on in hardware.

name: skl_compute_plane_wm
prose: Static void (skl_watermark.c:1798-1934) that computes one watermark level into *result. It returns after writing only result->min_ddb_alloc = U16_MAX (the level is rejected, other fields untouched) when latency is 0, or when use_minimal_wm0_only holds and level > 0, or when the computed lines value is greater than skl_wm_max_lines(display); the line-count rejection happens after lines has been set to 0 for levels without line watermarks and does not depend on level. Otherwise it computes method1 and method2, selects a result (Y-tiled: max of method2 and the Y-tile minimum; non-Y-tiled: method2 for very small plane sizes, else method2 when latency >= linetime (min of both on display version 9), else method1), rounds it up to blocks (plus one below display version 30; raised to at least one line's blocks when skl_wm_has_lines), and computes lines; on display version 9 it applies WA 1125/1126 adjustments using result_prev->blocks, and on version 11 and above computes min_ddb_alloc from lines or blocks. Then it writes result->blocks, result->lines (0 when the level has no lines), result->min_ddb_alloc = max(min_ddb_alloc, blocks) + 1, result->enable = true and result->auto_min_alloc_wm_enable, and, only for display version below 12 with a nonzero sagv block time, result->can_sagv = latency >= sagv.block_time_us; otherwise can_sagv is left unchanged.

name: i915_gem_execbuffer2_ioctl
prose: Returns int (i915_gem_execbuffer.c:3553-3642). It returns -EINVAL if check_buffer_count(args->buffer_count) fails, the error from i915_gem_check_execbuffer if that is nonzero, -ENOMEM if the kvmalloc_array of count + 2 elements fails, and -EFAULT (after freeing the array) if copy_from_user of the exec object list fails. Whatever err is, if args->flags has __EXEC_HAS_RELOC it tries to copy the updated offsets back: it opens a user write window on the user exec list (skipping the copy if that fails) and, for each entry with the UPDATE bit set, canonicalises the offset and writes it to the user list with unsafe_put_user, leaving the loop at the first fault; copy-back failures are ignored. It then clears __I915_EXEC_UNKNOWN_FLAGS in args->flags, frees exec2_list with kvfree and returns err, the result of i915_gem_do_execbuffer.

name: igt_mock_exhaust_device_supported_pages
prose: Static int selftest (huge_pages.c:422-495). It saves RUNTIME_INFO(i915)->page_sizes and restores it at out_device on every return after the loop starts. For each non-empty subset of the page_sizes table it builds the combination (always including SZ_4K), sets the runtime page sizes to it, and for single = 0 and 1 creates a fake huge-page object (the error from fake_huge_pages_object is returned, via out_device), returns -EINVAL if obj->base.size differs from the combination (object put first), returns the error of i915_vma_instance or i915_vma_pin (object put first), then calls igt_check_page_sizes and, without testing its result first, compares vma->page_sizes.sg with the combination and sets err to -EINVAL on a mismatch (this overwrites an error returned by igt_check_page_sizes). It unpins and puts the object and goes to out_device if err is nonzero. After all subsets it returns err, which is 0 if every check passed. The function therefore stops at the first failing iteration, but within one iteration the sg check runs even after igt_check_page_sizes failed, so the returned error is the igt_check_page_sizes error unless the sg check also fails.

name: igt_ctx_exec
prose: Static int selftest (i915_gem_context.c:659-782). It returns 0 immediately if the device has no logical contexts. For every uabi engine that can store a dword and has a nonzero context_size it creates a mock file (an error from mock_file is returned at once with nothing to release), starts a live test (igt_live_test_begin; an error goes to out_file) and, until the timeout, repeatedly creates a kernel context, creates a test object when needed (create_test_object), fills one dword with gpu_fill, throttles with throttle(), then releases the context. Errors from kernel_context, create_test_object, gpu_fill or throttle jump to out_file. After the loop it reads the dwords back with cpu_check on each object (an error breaks out of that loop). At out_file it releases the throttled requests, replaces err with -EIO if igt_live_test_end fails (even if err was 0), drops the file, and returns err from the function if it is nonzero. The other engines are not tried after an error. If every engine passes (or is skipped) it drains freed objects and finally returns 0; the initial err value of -ENODEV is never returned, because the last statement is return 0.

Reviewer claims: omits cpu_check and igt_live_test_end error returns (right, 762-764 and 771-772); the claim that -ENODEV is returned when no engine qualifies (round 1 and 15) is wrong, since err starts as -ENODEV but only a nonzero err set inside the engine loop is returned and the function ends with return 0 (781). name: gen8_ppgtt_create
prose: Returns struct i915_ppgtt * or an ERR_PTR (gen8_ppgtt.c:1002-1085). It allocates the ppgtt with kzalloc and returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) if that fails. Otherwise it calls ppgtt_init, sets vm.top to 3 for a 4-level vm and 2 otherwise, sets pd_shift, sets has_read_only to false for graphics versions 11 and 12 and true otherwise, selects alloc_pt_dma (LMEM or system variant by HAS_LMEM), alloc_scratch_dma, pte_encode (gen12 or gen8 variant), bind_async_flags, insert_entries, insert_page, allocate_va_range, clear_range, foreach and cleanup. It then initialises the scratch page (gen8_init_scratch), allocates the top-level page directory (gen8_alloc_top_pd), preallocates the top-level PDPs when the vm is not 4-level, notifies the vGPU layer when a vGPU is active, and calls gen8_init_rsvd. A failure of any of those steps (scratch, top pd, preallocation or gen8_init_rsvd) goes to err_put, which releases the vm with i915_vm_put and returns ERR_PTR of that step's error. On success it returns the ppgtt, and the caller holds the one vm reference that it must release with i915_vm_put.

name: signal_irq_work
prose: Static void irq_work callback (intel_breadcrumbs.c:170-273) for a struct intel_breadcrumbs b; it returns nothing. It takes a timestamp and drains b->signaled_requests into a local list with llist_del_all if that list is non-empty. If that local list is empty, the irq is armed and b->signalers is empty, it disarms the interrupt. Then, under RCU and with b->signaler_active incremented, it walks every context in b->signalers and, for each context, its signals list: it stops at the first request that is not complete or whose I915_FENCE_FLAG_SIGNAL bit was not set (the bit is cleared with test_and_clear_bit). For each request taken, under ce->signal_lock it removes it from ce->signals and calls remove_signaling_context; if that releases the context from b->signalers it calls add_retire when the request is the timeline's last, and drops a context reference. It then signals the dma-fence: if __dma_fence_signal reports it was newly signaled the request is added to the local list, otherwise a request reference is dropped. After decrementing signaler_active and leaving RCU, each request on the local list gets its engine's retire_inflight_request_prio hook called if set, then under rq->lock its fence callbacks are moved to a local list, the fence timestamp is set and the callbacks are notified, and the request reference is dropped. Finally it arms the irq if it is not armed and signalers exist, and disarms it if it is armed and b->active is zero. New entries can be added to b->signaled_requests concurrently, so the list is not guaranteed to be empty at return.
note: Checked against intel_breadcrumbs.c:170-273. Reviewer claims: disarm needs no pending signals and no signalers (right, 206), entries drained from the llist are not removed from the context lists here (right, the context lists are handled by the rcu walk), and signaled_requests is not guaranteed empty afterwards (right, concurrent llist_add). R:right

name: heartbeat
prose: Static void work function (intel_engine_heartbeat.c:136-240). It flushes the engine's submission, takes engine->heartbeat.systole with xchg, drops that request if it already completed and puts it back otherwise. It then calls intel_engine_pm_get_if_awake and returns at once, leaving any pending systole, when the engine is not awake. With the wakeref held: if the GT is wedged it goes to out; if the scheduler engine is disabled it calls reset_engine with the systole and goes to out; if a systole request is still pending then, unless the current time is after the request's emitted_jiffies plus the heartbeat interval (so also when exactly equal), it goes to out; otherwise, if the request's submit fence has not signalled it does nothing, else if the engine can schedule and the request's priority is below I915_PRIORITY_BARRIER it raises its priority one step (normal, then heartbeat, then barrier), else it resets the engine; then it updates the request's emitted_jiffies and goes to out. With no pending systole it compares engine->serial with wakeref_serial and goes to out if equal; tries mutex_trylock on the kernel timeline (on failure, if the engine was already marked blocked for this serial it calls intel_gt_handle_error, then goes to out); otherwise it creates and commits a new heartbeat request (if creation fails it just unlocks). At out, if hangcheck is disabled or next_heartbeat says no more beats are needed, it drops any systole request; in all paths that took the wakeref it calls intel_engine_pm_put.
note: Checked against intel_engine_heartbeat.c:136-240. Reviewer claims: a stuck systole is not always escalated or reset (right: the not-yet-submitted case does neither, 175-185); the wedged path still drops the systole at out when hangcheck is disabled or next_heartbeat is false (right, 159-160 and 234-238); the delay test also exits when elapsed equals the interval (right, !time_after at 171). R:right

name: intel_gt_resume
prose: Returns int (intel_gt_pm.c:240-311). It first returns the error of intel_gt_has_unrecoverable_error(gt) if nonzero, before anything else. It then calls gt_sanitize(gt, true), takes a GT PM wakeref and FORCEWAKE_ALL forcewake, and sanitises rc6. If the GT is wedged it sets err to -EIO and goes to out_fw. It calls intel_gt_init_hw (on failure it logs and goes to err_wedged), finishes the uc reset, enables rps and llc, and for each engine takes an engine pm reference, increments engine->serial, calls intel_engine_resume and drops the reference; a failure of intel_engine_resume logs and goes to err_wedged. On success it enables rc6, resumes uc, drops the user forcewake and falls into out_fw. err_wedged calls intel_gt_set_wedged and goes to out_fw. At out_fw it releases the forcewake, the GT wakeref, marks the GT bind context ready and returns err, which is 0 on success, -EIO for the wedged case, or the error from intel_gt_init_hw or intel_engine_resume.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at intel_gt_pm.c:240). Reviewer claim (round 15: no early unrecoverable-error check exists and the wakeref is taken first) is wrong: the check is at 247-249, before gt_sanitize and intel_gt_pm_get. R:wrong

name: intel_ring_begin
prose: Returns u32 * (intel_ring.c:230-309): a pointer into the ring buffer where num_dwords u32 values can be written, or ERR_PTR(error). It requires (GEM_BUG_ON checks) an even num_dwords and bytes plus rq->reserved_space not above ring->effective_size. If the request plus reserved space does not fit before the end of the usable ring it either plans to wrap (when the request itself does not fit, need_wrap is the remaining tail size) or only counts the reserved space from the start. If the needed bytes exceed ring->space it calls wait_for_space and returns ERR_PTR of its nonzero result (ring->emit is not advanced, though ring->space may change while waiting). When wrapping, it fills the tail with MI_NOOP (zeros), subtracts the tail size from ring->space and sets ring->emit to 0. It then takes the pointer at ring->emit (poisoning the area when CONFIG_DRM_I915_DEBUG_GEM is enabled), advances ring->emit by num_dwords * 4 and decreases ring->space by the same amount, and returns the pointer.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at intel_ring.c:230). Reviewer claim (wrapping also subtracts need_wrap from ring->space, so total space decrease is more than the bytes) is right (296). R:right

name: xehp_sseu_info_init
prose: Static void (intel_sseu.c:208-250). It sets num_geometry_regs and num_compute_regs to 1 and calls intel_sseu_set_info(sseu, 1, 32 * max(1, 1), 8 or 16) where the EUs per subslice is 8 when HAS_ONE_EU_PER_FUSE_BIT is true and 16 otherwise; sets has_xehp_dss to 1; loads geometry_subslice_mask from GEN12_GT_GEOMETRY_DSS_ENABLE and compute_subslice_mask from GEN12_GT_COMPUTE_DSS_ENABLE only (xehp_load_dss_mask reads numregs registers, here 1, so the extra XEHPC_GT_COMPUTE_DSS_ENABLE_EXT argument is passed but not read). It reads XEHP_EU_ENABLE and takes the XEHP_EU_ENA_MASK field as eu_en_fuse; eu_en equals eu_en_fuse when HAS_ONE_EU_PER_FUSE_BIT is true, otherwise each set fuse bit eu below max_eus_per_subslice/2 sets bits 2*eu and 2*eu+1. It then calls xehp_compute_sseu_info, which ORs bit 0 into slice_mask, sets subslice_mask to the OR of the compute and geometry masks, applies eu_en to each enabled subslice, and sets eu_per_subslice (the popcount of eu_en) and eu_total. It returns nothing.
note: Checked against intel_sseu.c:167-185, 187-206 and 208-250. Reviewer claim (XEHPC_GT_COMPUTE_DSS_ENABLE_EXT is passed but not read because num_compute_regs is 1) is right (201-202, 218). R:right

name: intel_wopcm_init
prose: Void function (intel_wopcm.c:233-322) that computes the GuC WOPCM region and stores it in wopcm->guc.base and wopcm->guc.size. It returns without changing anything when the GuC firmware upload size is 0, when i915_inject_probe_failure injects a failure, and, for registers that are not locked, when the device has a media GT (it logs an error and returns). If the WOPCM registers are already locked it takes base and size from them (using MAX_WOPCM_SIZE as the verification size when the registers are not writable by i915, which happens with GuC deprivilege) and skips the computation. Otherwise it computes guc_wopcm_base from the HuC firmware size plus the reserved size, aligned and capped at wopcm_size minus the context reserved size, and guc_wopcm_size as the remainder masked with GUC_WOPCM_SIZE_MASK. It then runs __check_layout and only if that passes stores base and size in wopcm->guc (the GEM_BUG_ON checks assert, but the code does not guarantee, that both are nonzero). When the layout check fails it leaves wopcm->guc untouched. GEM_BUG_ON checks also require wopcm->guc.base and size to be zero on entry and the firmware and context sizes to be smaller than the WOPCM size. It takes no locks.

The old prose attached the media-GT early return to the already-locked case, which is wrong (it applies to unlocked registers, 289-292), and it omitted the early return when guc_fw_size is zero (244-245). R:n/a

name: intel_engine_emit_ctx_wa
prose: Returns int (intel_workarounds.c:990-1063). It returns 0 at once if the engine's context workaround list is empty. Otherwise it first calls engine->emit_flush(rq, EMIT_BARRIER) and returns its error if nonzero. It reserves ring space with intel_ring_begin (wal->count * 2 + 6 dwords for a render engine on IP versions 12.70 to 12.74 or DG2, wal->count * 2 + 2 otherwise) and returns PTR_ERR(cs) if that fails. It then takes the MCR lock, the uncore lock and forcewake for the needed domains, and for each workaround entry computes the value (the set value for masked or full-mask entries, otherwise the current register value read with MCR or plain access, with clr bits removed and set bits added) and emits the MI_LOAD_REGISTER_IMM entries; on the DG2 and 12.70-12.74 render engines it also emits the extra 3DSTATE_MESH_CONTROL sequence. It then releases forcewake, the uncore lock and the MCR lock, advances the ring and calls emit_flush(rq, EMIT_BARRIER) again, returning that call's error if nonzero, otherwise 0.
