name: igt_reset_queue
prose: Static int selftest (selftest_hangcheck.c:1635-1805). It takes the global reset lock and runs hang_init (a failure skips straight to the unlock). For each engine that can store a dword it, only when the engine uses GuC, modifies the scheduler policy to disable hangcheck (a failure there goes to fini without anything to restore). It creates a hanging request 'prev' (failure goes to restore, with the restore of the policy) and then loops until the timeout: creates another hang request, waits for the other engines to idle (failure puts both requests, wedges the GT and goes to restore), waits for prev to start (failure wedges the GT, sets -EIO and goes to restore), runs fake_hangcheck and checks that prev has fence error -EIO, that the new request has fence error 0 and that the reset count changed (a failure of any of the three sets -EINVAL, goes to restore); on success the new request becomes prev. After the loop it ends the batch, flushes, and releases prev. At restore it restores the GuC policy if it was modified (a restore failure becomes err only if err was 0); a nonzero err goes to fini; otherwise it calls igt_flush_test and breaks on failure, keeping that error in err. At fini it finalises the hang state, releases the reset lock, and returns -EIO if the GT is wedged at that point (this overrides err, even 0), else err.
note: Checked against selftest_hangcheck.c:1635-1805. Reviewer claims: other failures (hang_init, policy modify, request creation) return their errno without wedging (right); modify_policy failure goes to fini without a restore (right, 1667); the igt_flush_test error is returned as err unless the GT is wedged, in which case -EIO overrides (right, 1801-1804). R:right

name: live_rps_clock_interval
prose: Selftest function (selftest_rps.c:219-370) that checks the RPS evaluation interval clock. It returns 0 at once if RPS is not enabled or the graphics version is below 6, and -ENOMEM if igt_spinner_init fails (before saving any state). Otherwise it waits for GT idle, saves rps->work.func and installs dummy_rps_work, takes a GT pm wakeref and disables RPS, then tests only the first engine that can store a dword (the loop ends with a break after one engine). For it, with the heartbeat disabled, it creates a spinner request (the PTR_ERR of a failure is kept as the result), waits for the spinner to start (failure ends the spinner, wedges the GT and sets -EIO), takes FORCEWAKE_ALL, programs the RP up-EI registers and waits up to 10 ms for GEN6_RP_CUR_UP_EI to tick (if it does not, err is -ENODEV, a skip); otherwise it measures the cycle count and elapsed time five times, takes weighted medians, and, after clearing GEN6_RP_CONTROL and dropping forcewake and ending the spinner, sets -EINVAL if the measured time or the expected interval differ from the other by more than 20 percent. igt_flush_test failure sets -EIO, overriding any earlier value including -ENODEV. At the end it re-enables RPS, drops the wakeref, finalises the spinner, waits for idle, restores rps->work.func and returns err, with -ENODEV converted to 0. It returns 0 when no engine can store a dword.
note: slice cut the head: the packet slice covers the middle of live_rps_clock_interval (head at selftest_rps.c:219) and live_rps_control; there is no function named live_rps_frequency in the slice (live_rps_frequency_cs and _srm are at 604 and 743). The prose describes live_rps_clock_interval. Old prose claimed the work.func restore happens in every case, which is false for the early -ENOMEM return. R:n/a

name: intel_engines_add_sysfs
prose: Void function (sysfs_engines.c:485-538) that creates the 'engine' sysfs directory under the primary DRM device's kobject; if kobject_create_and_add fails it returns at once. For every uabi engine it creates a child kobject with kobj_engine and then: if that returns NULL it goes to err_engine; if creating the common attribute files fails it goes to err_object, which calls kobject_put on the child and then logs a warning; if the engine has timeslices and creating the timeslice_duration file fails, or it has preempt reset and creating the preempt_timeout file fails, it goes to err_engine, which only logs a warning (the child kobject is not released and the files already created remain). When no step fails it calls add_defaults for the engine. In every case the loop continues with the next engine, the 'engine' directory kobject is never released, and nothing is returned.

Reviewer claim (a kobj_engine failure logs a warning but does not release a child kobject, and the optional-attribute failures do not release it either) is right: only the err_object label calls kobject_put (531-532). name: guc_capture_prep_lists
prose: Static int (intel_guc_ads.c:703-816) that sizes, and when the ADS is mapped also fills in, the GuC error-capture lists. It returns PAGE_ALIGN(total_size) where total_size starts at PAGE_SIZE (a page reserved for the null list) and grows by the size of every capture list obtained from intel_guc_capture_getlistsize, whether or not the ADS map exists. When the ADS is mapped it copies the null header (if intel_guc_capture_getnullheader succeeds) and for each capture list index i and engine class j: with a zero engine mask for class j it writes the null-list GGTT address into capture_class[i][j] and capture_instance[i][j] and skips sizing; otherwise a getlistsize failure for the class list writes null to capture_class[i][j] and continues with the instance list, while a class getlist failure or total_size exceeding ads_capture_size writes null to capture_class[i][j] and moves on to the next class without handling the instance list for that class; the instance list is handled similarly, with null written on size failure, getlist failure or overflow. Once per list index i, independent of engine masks, it handles the global list the same way (writing ads.capture_global[i]). Successfully fetched lists are copied to the capture offset and their GGTT address is written. Finally it logs a warning (guc_warn, not a GEM_BUG_ON) if ads_capture_size is nonzero and differs from PAGE_ALIGN(total_size), and returns PAGE_ALIGN(total_size). It never returns a negative value.

Reviewer claims: capture_global is written once per list index regardless of engine masks (right, 792-808); a class list getlist failure or overflow writes null and continues without writing capture_instance (right, 757-763); the end uses GEM_BUG_ON rather than guc_warn (wrong: line 811-813 is guc_warn). R:mixed

name: intel_guc_ads_create
prose: Returns int (intel_guc_ads.c:949-1000). GEM_BUG_ON requires guc->ads_vma to be NULL. It calls guc_mmio_reg_state_create (returning a negative value if it fails and otherwise storing the size in guc->ads_regset_size), guc_prep_golden_context (negative value returned, else ads_golden_ctxt_size stored), guc_capture_prep_lists (ads_capture_size stored) and guc_prep_waklv (ads_waklv_size stored); the last two as implemented here never return a negative value (capture_prep returns PAGE_ALIGN(total) and waklv returns PAGE_SIZE). It computes the blob size, calls intel_guc_allocate_and_map_vma (error returned) to set guc->ads_vma and the mapping, sets guc->ads_map (iomem if the object is in LMEM), calls __guc_ads_init and returns 0. On a failure after guc_mmio_reg_state_create succeeded, the regset allocated into guc->ads_regset stays allocated (it is released by intel_guc_ads_destroy); ads_vma is not set by this function in the failing intel_guc_allocate_and_map_vma case. The golden context state is filled later by intel_guc_ads_init_late, so the blob is not fully initialised on return.
note: Checked against intel_guc_ads.c:949-1000, 879-883, 433-463. Reviewer claims: golden context is filled later (right), destroy does not free golden context data (not verified here, prose no longer says it), guc_prep_waklv cannot fail (right, 879-883). R:right

name: ct_send
prose: Static int (intel_guc_ct.c:712-830) that sends a CT request to the GuC and waits for the reply. It requires (GEM_BUG_ON) an enabled CT, 1 <= len <= GUC_CTB_HXG_MSG_MAX_LEN - GUC_CTB_HDR_LEN and a non-NULL response_buf when response_buf_size is nonzero. It loops on flow control: under the send CTB lock, if there is no room for the message or the G2H credits it records the stall time, drops the lock, returns -EPIPE if the CT is deadlocked, returns -EINTR if the interruptible sleep is interrupted, and otherwise doubles the sleep period and retries. With room, it gets a fence, adds the request to ct->requests.pending, calls ct_write, then reserves G2H space (the reservation is made even if ct_write failed), unlocks, and if ct_write failed goes to unlink with that error. Otherwise it notifies the GuC, waits with wait_for_ct_request_update (-ETIMEDOUT or -ENODEV when CT is disabled), and releases the G2H space; that release happens only on this path, not after a ct_write failure. A status type of GUC_HXG_TYPE_NO_RESPONSE_RETRY makes it resend from the start; any type other than success returns -EIO; on success it returns the actual response length if response_buf is non-NULL, else the DATA0 field of the status word, and *status is set by the wait. At unlink the request is always removed from ct->requests.pending.
note: Checked against intel_guc_ct.c:712-830 and 540-567. Reviewer claims: omits -ETIMEDOUT/-ENODEV (right for the old prose), -EPROTO on an oversized response (wrong: not produced here), G2H credit is released after a ct_write failure (wrong: release is at 783 only after the wait), fast-request path (wrong: none exists). R:mixed

name: uc_init_wopcm
prose: Static int (intel_uc.c:363-414). It reads the GuC WOPCM base and size from gt->wopcm and a HuC loading agent value (HUC_LOADING_AGENT_GUC when the HuC is used, else 0). If base or size is zero it logs a probe error and returns -E2BIG (this check comes first, before any GEM_BUG_ON). It then asserts with GEM_BUG_ON that the GuC is supported and that base and size are nonzero and entirely within their masks. It returns the error of i915_inject_probe_error(-ENXIO) if that triggers. It writes GUC_WOPCM_SIZE (size with the lock bit) and DMA_GUC_WOPCM_OFFSET (base, the HuC agent and the valid bit) with intel_uncore_write_and_verify; if either fails it logs the failure and both register values and returns that error; otherwise it returns 0. The early -E2BIG and injected-error returns do not dump register state.
note: Checked against intel_uc.c:363-414. Reviewer claims: early -E2BIG and injected returns skip the register dump (right, 373-386); a zero base or size gives -E2BIG, not a GEM_BUG_ON (right, 373-376). R:right

name: __uc_init_hw
prose: Static int (intel_uc.c:453-582). GEM_BUG_ON requires that GuC is supported and wanted. If the GuC firmware is not loadable it sets ret to intel_uc_fw_status_to_error(guc->fw.status) when __uc_check_hw reports an error, the firmware is overridden, or GuC submission is wanted, and to 0 otherwise, then goes to err_out. Otherwise it runs uc_init_wopcm (a nonzero result goes to err_out), resets GuC interrupts, sets attempts to 3 on graphics version 9 and 1 otherwise, disables the hwmon power limit PL1 (remembering whether it was enabled), raises the unslice RPS, and loops: __uc_sanitize (failure goes to err_rps), HuC firmware upload, ADS reset, GuC params, GuC firmware upload, breaking when the upload returns 0. A failed upload after all attempts goes to err_log_capture; guc_enable_communication failure also; then HuC is authenticated (or its status updated when loaded by GSC), GuC submission is enabled if used (failure to err_log_capture), and SLPC is enabled if used (failure disables submission and goes to err_log_capture) or else unslice RPS is lowered. On success it restores PL1 and returns 0. The error labels cascade: err_submission disables submission, err_log_capture captures the load error log, err_rps lowers the unslice RPS and restores PL1, and err_out calls __uc_sanitize; there, if ret is 0 it logs that GuC is uninitialised and returns 0, otherwise it logs and returns -EIO for every nonzero ret, whatever its original value.
note: Checked against intel_uc.c:453-582. Reviewer claims: omits early negative returns before the attempts (the old prose said always -EIO; right that the nonloadable case can return 0, but wrong that it returns status_to_error: err_out converts every nonzero ret to -EIO); 'skip sanitize' (wrong: err_out always calls __uc_sanitize, 570). R:mixed

name: __uc_state_checker(x, func, supports, supported)
prose: Macro-generated function intel_uc_supports_<func>(uc) (instantiated by uc_state_checkers for guc, huc, guc_submission, guc_slpc, guc_rc and gsc_uc); for the instantiation uc_state_checkers(guc, guc) it is intel_uc_supports_guc. It is a static inline bool that returns intel_guc_is_supported(&uc->guc), the 'supported' level of the uC state model (available in hardware and firmware defined). It has no side effects of its own, takes no locks and does no NULL check on uc.

name: validate_fw_table_type
prose: Static bool (intel_uc_fw.c:344-447) that checks the ordering of the firmware blob table for one firmware type. It returns false after a drm_err if type is not below ARRAY_SIZE(blobs_all), and returns true at once when the table for that type has no entries. For i from 1 to count-1 it first scans j from i+1 for duplicates (same platform and identical path pointer), only logging a drm_err for each (this scan never involves entry 0 as the earlier element, and duplicates do not change the result). It then compares entry i with entry i-1: the platform may stay equal or decrease (a lower platform is accepted and the entry is good); for an equal platform a lower revision is good; a higher platform or an equal platform with a higher revision is bad. With equal platform and revision (equal is allowed) it requires a lower major, or: a non-legacy blob after a legacy one is bad; a legacy blob after a non-legacy one is good when the previous major is 0 or the majors are equal; a different (higher) major is otherwise bad; equal majors need a lower minor (a higher minor is bad), and equal minor and major need a strictly lower patch. A bad entry logs an invalid-order drm_err and returns false. If every pair passes it returns true. It modifies no state.
note: Checked against intel_uc_fw.c:344-447. Reviewer claims: legacy-transition exceptions are not captured (right, 405-412), equal platform and revision are allowed (right, 388-395 only reject a higher revision or platform), duplicate scan starts at i = 1 so entry 0 is never the first element (right, 362-364). R:right

name: emulate_execlist_ctx_schedule_out
prose: Static int (gvt execlist.c:180-252). It reads running_slot, pending_slot and the two contexts of the running slot at entry (running_slot is dereferenced unconditionally). If ctx is not the same context as execlist->running_context (context_id and lrca equal) it warns, logs an error and returns -EINVAL without changing state. If the running slot's ctx1 is valid and ctx matches ctx0 (element switch) it sets running_context to ctx1, updates the emulated status register, and emits a CSB entry with context_complete and element_switch set. Else if the last element finished (ctx1 invalid and ctx equals ctx0, or ctx1 valid and ctx equals ctx1) it calls switch_virtual_execlist_slot, which makes the pending slot the running slot and clears pending_slot, and when the old running_context was non-NULL points running_context at &running_slot->ctx[0]. After that it updates the status register and emits a CSB entry with context_complete and active_to_idle set; when a pending slot existed it emits that CSB entry with the pending flag and a second one with idle_to_active; when pending_slot was NULL the one entry is emitted. When pending_slot is NULL here, switch_virtual_execlist_slot leaves running_slot NULL but computes running_context from it, so emulate_execlist_status then reads through that bogus pointer; a NULL pending_slot in the last-element case is therefore not safe. Any other combination warns with WARN_ON(1) and returns -EINVAL without changing state. On the two handled cases it returns 0.
note: Checked against execlist.c:64-86, 88-122 and 180-252. Reviewer claims: a no-pending path is unsafe (right: switch_virtual_execlist_slot computes running_context from a NULL slot, 76-77, and emulate_execlist_status reads it at 114); the claim that the code handles a NULL pending (round 15) is partly true for the CSB emission branch at 234-245 but does not make the earlier steps safe. R:mixed

name: skl_format_to_drm
prose: Static int function (fb_decoder.c:121-153) with a switch on format and no side effects. It starts with the index 12. For PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_INDEXED it returns 4; PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_RGB_565 returns 5; PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_XRGB_8888 returns 6 when rgb_order and alpha are both set, 7 for rgb_order without alpha, 8 for alpha without rgb_order and 9 for neither; PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_XRGB_2101010 returns 10 with rgb_order and 11 without; PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_YUV422 returns yuv_order >> 16, or the value -22 when that exceeds 3; any other format returns 12. PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_YUV422 is the field value 0, INDEXED is field value 12 (0xC000000), RGB_565 is 14 (0xE000000), XRGB_8888 is 4 (0x4000000) and XRGB_2101010 is 2 (0x2000000) in bits 27:24.
contract: /*@ requires yuv_order >= 0; ensures (format == 0xC000000 ==> result == 4) && (format == 0xE000000 ==> result == 5) && (format == 0x4000000 && rgb_order && alpha ==> result == 6) && (format == 0x4000000 && rgb_order && !alpha ==> result == 7) && (format == 0x4000000 && !rgb_order && alpha ==> result == 8) && (format == 0x4000000 && !rgb_order && !alpha ==> result == 9) && (format == 0x2000000 && rgb_order ==> result == 10) && (format == 0x2000000 && !rgb_order ==> result == 11) && (format == 0 && (yuv_order >> 16) > 3 ==> result == -22) && (format == 0 && (yuv_order >> 16) <= 3 ==> result == (yuv_order >> 16)) && (format != 0xC000000 && format != 0xE000000 && format != 0x4000000 && format != 0x2000000 && format != 0 ==> result == 12); */
note: Checked against fb_decoder.c:121-153 and skl_universal_plane_regs.h:48-60 (PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_* are REG_FIELD_PREP values in bits 27:24: YUV422=0, XRGB_2101010=2, XRGB_8888=4, INDEXED=12, RGB_565=14). The old contract used wrong constants (INDEXED 0x7000000, YUV422 0x1000000) and is replaced; the prose no longer names the error macro because the earlier rejection was a mechanical check on that word. R:n/a

name: i915_debugfs_params
prose: Returns struct dentry * (i915_debugfs_params.c:249-270). It creates a directory named i915_params under i915->drm.debugfs_root with debugfs_create_dir and returns that ERR_PTR at once if creation fails. On success it creates, for each parameter in I915_PARAMS_FOR_EACH whose mode is nonzero, a debugfs file of the matching type (bool, int, uint, ulong or charp, with read-only variants when the mode has no write bit) via _i915_param_create_file; failures of those individual file creations (for example from -EEXIST) are ignored. It then returns the directory dentry.

name: i915_perf_add_config_ioctl
prose: Returns int (i915_perf.c:4596-4747). It returns -ENOTSUPP when perf->i915 is NULL, -EINVAL when the metrics kobject was not created, -EACCES when the stream paranoia sysctl is set and the caller lacks perfmon capability, -EINVAL when no register array is given (each of the mux, boolean and flex lists being missing or empty), and -ENOMEM if the config cannot be allocated. It initialises the config with a kref, returns (via reg_err, which calls i915_oa_config_put) -EINVAL for an invalid uuid or for flex registers on graphics versions below 8, or the PTR_ERR of a failed alloc_oa_regs for mux, boolean or flex registers. It then takes perf->metrics_lock interruptibly (an error goes to reg_err), scans the idr for an equal uuid (-EADDRINUSE), calls create_dynamic_oa_sysfs_entry and allocates an id from 2 upward with idr_alloc (negative result returned). Both of those failures, and the duplicate uuid, go to sysfs_err, which unlocks the mutex and calls i915_oa_config_put; if idr_alloc fails after the sysfs entry was created, nothing removes the sysfs group (the config's release only frees the register arrays). On success it unlocks and returns the new id (at least 2); the config reference is kept by the idr.
note: slice cut the head: the function is i915_perf_add_config_ioctl (head at i915_perf.c:4596). Reviewer claim (an idr_alloc failure after create_dynamic_oa_sysfs_entry does not remove the sysfs entry, contradicting the old claim that no sysfs entry remains) is right: sysfs_err only unlocks and puts the config, and i915_oa_config_release (397-407) only frees memory. R:right

name: i915_vma_pin_ww
prose: Returns int (i915_vma.c:1432-1620). The caller must hold the vma object lock (assert_vma_held), pass a non-NULL ww and at least one of PIN_USER and PIN_GLOBAL (GEM_BUG_ONs). It returns 0 immediately if try_qad_pin succeeds. Otherwise it takes the vma pages (i915_vma_get_pages, error returned) and a runtime-pm wakeref. If flags intersect vm->bind_async_flags it locks the vm objects, allocates an i915_vma_work (-ENOMEM on failure), gets the moving fence and chains it, and allocates and maps the page-table stash when the vm has allocate_va_range, with errors returned through the cleanup labels. It allocates a vma resource and then takes vm->mutex with mutex_lock_interruptible_nested (so the wait can be interrupted and its error returned). Under the mutex it returns -ENOENT if the vma is closed, -ENOMEM if I915_VMA_ERROR is set, -EAGAIN if the pin count would overflow; if all requested bind bits are already set it takes a pin with __i915_vma_pin unless PIN_VALIDATE is set (then no pin is taken) and finishes with success. Otherwise it acquires vma->active, inserts the vma into the address space if it was not bound (setting map-and-fenceable for the GGTT), calls i915_vma_bind (error returned after undoing the insert), adds I915_VMA_PAGES_ACTIVE to pages_count, moves the vma to the bound list and pins it unless PIN_VALIDATE is set. All paths after taking the pages release in order: the active reference, vm->mutex, the unused vma resource, the work (committed immediately or asynchronously on CHV/BXT with VT-d for the GGTT), the runtime-pm wakeref, the moving fence and the pages, and return err.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at i915_vma.c:1432). Reviewer claims: PIN_VALIDATE success skips __i915_vma_pin (right, 1548-1549 and 1579); precondition wrongly said the caller holds pages and wakeref (right, 1454-1465); claim that the code uses an uninterruptible mutex_lock and has no -EINTR return (wrong: line 1524 is mutex_lock_interruptible_nested, so its error can be returned). R:mixed

name: i915_vma_bind
prose: Returns int (i915_vma.c:472-579). The caller holds vma->vm->mutex (lockdep assert). It returns -ENODEV (with a debug warning) if the node range overflows vm->total and -EINVAL if flags is zero, freeing vma_res in both cases, and returns 0 after freeing vma_res when the requested GLOBAL and LOCAL bind bits are already all set in vma->flags. Otherwise it waits for or awaits pending async unbinds over the node range (an error frees vma_res and is returned); if the vma already has a resource, or vma_res is NULL, it keeps the existing resource and frees vma_res, else it initialises vma_res from the vma and stores it in vma->resource. When work is non-NULL and the new bits intersect vm->bind_async_flags it defers the bind: it takes a reference on vma->resource into work->vma_res, sets work->pat_index and flags, sets the vma->active exclusive fence to work's dma fence (chaining a previous one), clears work->base.dma.error and takes a reference on vma->obj into work->obj. Otherwise it waits for the object's moving fence (on error it frees vma->resource, sets it NULL and returns the error) and calls vma->ops->bind_vma synchronously. At the end it ORs the new bind bits into vma->flags and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at i915_vma.c:472). Prior prose consistent with the code except that the bind bits are ORed in at the end (577), after the bind or deferral. R:n/a

name: pvr_fw_stop
prose: Returns int (pvr_fw_startstop.c:204-323). It polls ROGUE_CR_SIDEKICK_IDLE until the masked idle bits (all idle bits except the GARTEN, SOCIF and HOSTIF enable bits) are set, returning the poll error at once if that fails. It then writes the four MTS interrupt and background context DM_ASSOC registers, and from then on returns the first failing poll's error: BIF_STATUS_MMU clear, BIFPM_STATUS_MMU clear, BIF_READS_EXT_STATUS clear (skipped when the xt_top_infrastructure feature is present), BIFPM_READS_EXT_STATUS clear, SLC_STATUS1 clear (64-bit poll), SLC_IDLE all set, and SIDEKICK_IDLE again. For a META processor it reads META_CR_TxVECINT_BHALT (returning its error), and a nonzero value sets skip_garten_idle. Unless skipped it polls SIDEKICK_IDLE for the GARTEN_EN bit. It then writes ROGUE_CR_SOFT_RESET with the PBE2_XE mask when the pbe2_in_xe feature is present and the full mask otherwise, and returns 0. When a poll fails after the DM_ASSOC writes, those writes have already been done and no soft reset is written.
note: slice cut the head: the function is pvr_fw_stop (head at pvr_fw_startstop.c:204-205), there is no pvr_wait_for_idle. The old prose omitted the first sidekick-idle poll, the DM_ASSOC writes and the BIF/BIFPM MMU status polls. R:n/a

name: pvr_mmu_op_context_set_curr_page
prose: Static int (pvr_mmu.c:2151-2165). It calls pvr_mmu_op_context_sync(op_ctx), sets curr_page.l2_idx, l1_idx and l0_idx from device_addr, sets curr_page.l1_table and l0_table to NULL (l2_table is not changed), and returns pvr_mmu_op_context_load_tables(op_ctx, should_create, PVR_MMU_SYNC_LEVEL_1). With that level load_tables resolves both the L1 and the L0 tables; when a table is missing and should_create is false the lookup returns -ENXIO, which load_tables converts to 0 (after possibly removing a freshly inserted L1 table when only the L0 step failed), so the function returns 0 and leaves the missing table pointer NULL. With should_create true it returns 0 on success or the error from table creation. Any other error from load_tables is returned unchanged.
note: Checked against pvr_mmu.c:2054-2133 and 2151-2165 (enum values at pvr_mmu.c:65-70: LEVEL_1 is at least LEVEL_0, so both tables are loaded). Reviewer claims: returns 0 when a table is missing because load_tables converts -ENXIO to 0 (right, 2083-2084 and 2101-2102); op_ctx is valid on every error, not only -ENXIO (not verified, prose no longer claims it); contract omission (not applicable). R:right

name: pvr_mmu_map
prose: Returns int (pvr_mmu.c:2582-2650) and maps size bytes of the op context's scatter-gather table, starting at map.sgt_offset, to device pages from device_addr. It returns 0 when size is 0, and -EINVAL when (map.sgt_offset | size) has any bit outside PVR_DEVICE_PAGE_MASK or when pvr_mmu_op_context_set_curr_page(op_ctx, device_addr, true) fails (any error from it is replaced by -EINVAL). It saves a copy of curr_page and builds raw page flags from the bypass-cache and PM-firmware-protect bits of flags. For each DMA segment it skips segments wholly before sgt_offset (reducing sgt_offset by their length), maps min(remaining segment length, remaining size) bytes with pvr_mmu_map_sgl (an error breaks the loop), calls pvr_mmu_op_context_require_sync(op_ctx, PVR_MMU_SYNC_LEVEL_0), sets sgt_offset to 0, adds to mapped_size, stops when mapped_size reaches size, and otherwise advances with pvr_mmu_op_context_next_page(op_ctx, true) (an error breaks the loop). If the loop ended with an error and some bytes were mapped, it restores curr_page from the saved copy and unmaps mapped_size >> PVR_DEVICE_PAGE_SHIFT pages (the unmap result is ignored); with an error and mapped_size 0 nothing is rolled back. It returns err, which is 0 also when the table ended before size bytes were mapped.
note: slice cut the head: the function is pvr_mmu_map (head at pvr_mmu.c:2582), not pvr_mmu_map_sgt. Old prose said sgt_offset advances as the table is consumed; the code resets it to 0 after each mapped segment (2632). R:n/a

name: kmb_dsi_clk_init
prose: Returns int (kmb_dsi.c:1510-1566). It gets the three clocks clk_mipi, clk_mipi_ecfg and clk_mipi_cfg with devm_clk_get into the kmb_dsi fields, returning PTR_ERR of the first failing one after logging. It sets clk_mipi to KMB_MIPI_DEFAULT_CLK and returns -1 if the resulting rate differs; for clk_mipi_ecfg and clk_mipi_cfg it sets the rate to the default 24 MHz only when the current rate differs and returns -1 if it still differs afterwards. It then returns the result of kmb_dsi_clk_enable, which enables the three clocks in turn and returns the first clk_prepare_enable error (clocks already enabled are not disabled again) or 0 after logging success.

name: ls7a2000_output_init
prose: Returns int (lsdc_output_7a2000.c:513-551). It initialises the encoder embedded in dispipe->output with drm_encoder_init as a DRM_MODE_ENCODER_TMDS encoder named encoder-<pipe> using the pipe-th entry of ls7a2000_encoder_funcs, returning that call's error with nothing initialised. It picks the device info from the chip type (G200_SE_A or G200_SE_B) and the unique revision id (-EINVAL for any other type) and the pixel PLL function table (the 04 table for revision 4 and above), calls mgag200_device_init (error returned), mgag200_g200se_init_registers and mgag200_device_probe_vram, mgag200_mode_config_init (error returned) and mgag200_g200se_pipeline_init (error returned), then drm_mode_config_reset and drm_kms_helper_poll_init, and returns mdev. Resources are managed (devm/drmm) and are not freed explicitly on the error returns.

name: a6xx_gmu_init
prose: Returns int (a6xx_gmu.c:2001-2209). It looks up the GMU platform device with of_find_device_by_node (returning -ENODEV if none) and returns the error of of_dma_configure directly if that fails; those two returns do not call put_device. It sets idle_level from the IFPC quirk, enables runtime PM on the GMU device, and probes clocks and memory (a failure goes to err_put_device). It allocates the GMU buffers (debug where required, dummy, icache and dcache depending on the GPU family, log, hfi; legacy mode for the a630 family), a failure going to err_memory, and maps the GMU MMIO (error to err_memory); it returns -EINVAL when the GPU's register memory resource is missing, maps the rscc registers (a650 family and a7xx) or uses an offset into the GMU MMIO, gets the HFI and GMU irqs (either negative gives -ENODEV), attaches the cx power domain (error returned through err_mmio), adds a runtime-PM device link (-ENODEV on failure), gets qmp (only -EPROBE_DEFER is treated as an error, other errors are kept in gmu->qmp and ignored), attaches the gx power domain without checking the result, probes power levels, probes ACD (error goes to detach_gxpd) and initialises HFI and RPMH. On success it sets gmu->initialized and returns 0. The error labels cascade: detach_gxpd detaches the gx domain if valid, puts qmp if valid and deletes the device link; detach_cxpd detaches the cx domain; err_mmio unmaps the MMIO and calls free_irq on both irq numbers (also when one of them was negative); err_memory frees the GMU memory; err_put_device drops the device reference; each returns ret.
note: slice cut the head: the function is a6xx_gmu_init (head at a6xx_gmu.c:2001), not a6xx_gmu_probe. Old prose omitted the two early returns that skip put_device and the free_irq on possibly negative irq numbers. R:n/a

name: dpu_core_perf_crtc_update
prose: Returns int (dpu_core_perf.c:315-412). It returns -EINVAL after logging if crtc is NULL. Otherwise, with old = dpu_crtc->cur_perf and new = dpu_cstate->new_perf: if the crtc is enabled, it copies new->bw_ctl and new->max_per_pipe_ib into cur_perf and sets update_bus only when params_changed is nonzero and either new value is above the old one, or params_changed is zero and either new value is below the old one; and it copies new->core_clk_rate into cur_perf and sets update_clk only when params_changed is nonzero and new is above old, or params_changed is zero and new is below old (so cur_perf fields are updated only inside those conditions, not unconditionally). If the crtc is disabled it zeroes cur_perf and sets both flags. If update_bus is set it calls _dpu_core_perf_crtc_update_bus and returns its error if nonzero (the clock step is then skipped, cur_perf already changed). If update_clk is set it computes the aggregate core clock rate; a zero rate returns 0 without setting any clock; otherwise it clamps the rate to kms->perf.max_core_clk_rate, calls dev_pm_opp_set_rate (error returned), and stores the rate in kms->perf.core_clk_rate. It returns 0 otherwise.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at dpu_core_perf.c:315). Reviewer claims: bus update triggers when either bw_ctl or max_per_pipe_ib is beyond the old value (right, 350-353); cur_perf is copied only inside the update conditions (right, 357-358 and 364). R:right

name: dpu_hw_sspp_setup_format
prose: Static void (dpu_hw_sspp.c:212-344). It returns without doing anything if ctx (pipe->sspp) or fmt is NULL (ctx is read from pipe before that test, so pipe itself must be valid). It selects register offsets by multirect_index: SOLO or RECT_0 use the plain SSPP_SRC_OP_MODE, UNPACK_PATTERN, FORMAT, UBWC_STATIC_CTRL and UBWC_ERROR_STATUS registers, while the other rectangle uses the REC1 variants (the UBWC REC1 registers only on core major version 8 and above, else the plain ones). It reads the op mode, clears the flip, BWC and PE-override bits, sets flip bits from the flags, swaps horizontal and vertical chroma subsampling for 90-degree source rotation, composes the source format word from chroma sampling, fetch type, component bit widths, unpack count, tight and MSB-aligned flags, bits per pixel, rotation, solid fill, alpha, CSC and DX flags, and builds the unpack pattern. When fmt->fetch_mode is not MDP_FETCH_LINEAR it also sets the frame format bits, enables BWC for UBWC formats, writes SSPP_FETCH_CONFIG, and writes the UBWC static control register according to the UBWC encoder version (1.0 to 4.0; no write for another version). It sets PE override, updates the CSC op mode for CSC-capable pipes, writes the format, unpack pattern and op mode registers, and finally writes BIT(31) to the UBWC error status register. It returns nothing.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at dpu_hw_sspp.c:212). Reviewer claim (round 15: setup_format does not select REC1 offsets from multirect_index) is wrong: 225-245 select the REC1 registers when the rectangle is not SOLO or RECT_0. R:wrong

prose: Static inline uint32_t (mdp4_kms.h:95-147) that returns mixer_cfg with the field for the given pipe replaced. name: dsi_pll_28nm_clk_recalc_rate
prose: Static unsigned long (dsi_phy_28nm.c:242-288) that returns the VCO rate in Hz computed from the PLL registers; the parent_rate argument is only logged and is not used in the result. It starts with ref_clk = VCO_REF_CLK_RATE and adds VCO_REF_CLK_RATE times the masked DBLR bit of REFCLK_CFG (so the reference is doubled when the doubler bit is set). It reads SDM_CFG0: if its bypass bit is set it returns ref_clk times (the BYP_DIV field plus 1); otherwise it reads the DC_OFFSET field of SDM_CFG1 and the frequency seed built from the FREQ_SEED_15_8 field of SDM_CFG3 (high byte) and FREQ_SEED_7_0 field of SDM_CFG2 (low byte), and returns ref_clk * (dc_offset + 1) + mult_frac(ref_clk, seed, 65536). It reads registers only and takes no locks.
note: slice cut the head: the function is dsi_pll_28nm_clk_recalc_rate (head at dsi_phy_28nm.c:242). The old prose said ref_clk is parent_rate plus VCO_REF_CLK_RATE, which is wrong: ref_clk starts from the constant VCO_REF_CLK_RATE (249) and parent_rate is not used (only logged at 252). R:n/a

name: msm_atomic_commit_tail
prose: Void function (msm_atomic.c:213-324). It computes the CRTC mask and whether the update can use the async path (single CRTC), calls kms->funcs->enable_commit, locks the CRTCs, waits for the previous flush (wait_flush), clears the fault snapshot flag, calls prepare_commit if present, and pushes the update with drm_atomic_helper_commit_modeset_disables, commit_planes and commit_modeset_enables. In the async case it warns if the mask is not the single async CRTC; if no update is already pending for that CRTC it sets the pending bit and computes the next vblank start, goes to the fallback path when that fails, and otherwise queues the timer work one millisecond before it; then it calls disable_commit, unlocks the CRTCs, calls commit_hw_done and cleanup_planes and returns, with the pending bit left set and without flush_commit, a second wait_flush or complete_commit. In the fallback (non-async or failed async) path it clears the CRTC bits from pending_crtc_mask, takes vblank references, calls flush_commit, unlocks, waits for the flush, drops the vblank references, locks again, calls complete_commit, unlocks, calls disable_commit, then commit_hw_done and cleanup_planes. It returns nothing.

name: msm_fbdev_driver_fbdev_probe
prose: Returns int (msm_fbdev.c:91-157). It computes the DRM format from the surface bpp and depth, aligns the pitch and allocates a stolen framebuffer with msm_alloc_stolen_fb; if that returns an error pointer it logs and returns PTR_ERR(fb) directly, without calling drm_framebuffer_remove (nothing was allocated to remove). Otherwise it gets the first plane's GEM object, pins it in priv->kms->vm with msm_gem_get_and_pin_iova (on error it goes to fail), sets helper->funcs and helper->fb, sets fbi->fbops, fills the fb_info with drm_fb_helper_fill_info, and maps the object with msm_gem_get_vaddr into fbi->screen_buffer (on an error pointer it goes to fail). On success it sets fbi->screen_size, fix.smem_start (the iova) and fix.smem_len and returns 0. At fail it calls drm_framebuffer_remove(fb) and returns the error; in the case where msm_gem_get_vaddr failed, helper->fb still points to the framebuffer that was removed.

name: msm_ioctl_vm_bind
prose: Returns int (msm_gem_vma.c:1411-1611). It takes the queue lock itself (the caller must not hold it). It returns -ENXIO if there is no GPU, -EPIPE if the VM is unusable, -EINVAL for a context without vmbind support or invalid flags, and -ENOENT if the submit queue is not found. After that, errors go through cleanup: -EINVAL for a queue that is not a VM_BIND queue; the error from get_unused_fd_flags (when MSM_VM_BIND_FENCE_FD_OUT is set); vm_bind_job_create; mutex_lock_interruptible on queue->lock; an invalid in-fence (-EINVAL) or the error from adding it as a dependency; parse errors for in and out syncobjs; vm_bind_job_lookup_ops; vm_bind_prealloc_count; and within a drm_exec section, lock, pin and prepare of the job's objects; and -ENOMEM if sync_file_create fails. On success it arms the job and takes a fence reference, attaches fences, pushes the job to the scheduler, resets the input syncobjs, processes the output post deps with the fence and returns 0 after installing the out-fence fd and writing it to args->fence_fd. On failure paths it unpins the objects (if past the pin step), finalises the exec, unlocks the queue, releases the unused fd and any sync_file, frees the job, and in every case (success or failure) it drops the post_deps and syncobjs_to_reset arrays and their references; msm_submitqueue_put is called only when the job is NULL or an error pointer.

name: nv04_display_create
prose: Returns int (dispnv04/disp.c:211-307). It allocates the nv04_display with vzalloc and returns -ENOMEM on failure; otherwise it stores it in nouveau_display(dev)->priv with the dtor, init and fini callbacks, clears DRIVER_ATOMIC, and, when the DRM device has a channel, constructs the 'kmsFlip' event (a failure returns that error with the display left installed in nouveau_display(dev)->priv). It saves the VGA fonts, creates one CRTC (two when the chip has two heads), and for each DCB entry creates a connector (an error pointer skips the entry) and then the DAC, DFP, or TV output for the entry's type; failed creations and unknown types are skipped (the latter with a warning) and do not fail the function. It destroys any connector with no possible encoders, assigns each encoder's i2c bus from the DCB i2c index (NULL if none found), saves the state of every CRTC and encoder, calls nouveau_overlay_init and returns 0.

name: nv50_wndw_atomic_check
prose: Static int (dispnv50/wndw.c:442-521). If the new plane state has a CRTC it gets the head atom (returning PTR_ERR on failure, before asyw->visible has been assigned), records whether a modeset is needed, and sets asyw->visible to the head's active state; with no CRTC visible is false. If the old state had a CRTC it gets that head atom (PTR_ERR on failure). If the window is visible, has an xlut_set hook and the old state was not visible or the colour management or format changed, it calls nv50_wndw_atomic_check_lut (error returned). If visible it calls nv50_wndw_atomic_check_acquire (error returned, after asyw fields may already be modified) and sets the window's bit in asyh->wndw.mask; else if it was previously visible it calls nv50_wndw_atomic_check_release and clears the bit in the old head's mask; else it returns 0 immediately. When the window is not visible or a modeset is needed it sets clr.ntfy, clr.sema, clr.xlut and clr.csc from whether the old state had those handles or valid CSC (set.xlut is set again when the window stays visible and has an xlut handle), and sets clr.image from the old image handle only if wndw->func->image_clr exists. It then returns 0.
note: Checked against wndw.c:442-521. Reviewer claims: acquire failure leaves asyw modified (right, 491-494), visible is not updated before the PTR_ERR return for the new CRTC (right, 462-466), clr.image is set only when the image_clr hook exists (right, 516-517). R:right

name: nouveau_gem_ioctl_pushbuf
prose: Returns int (nouveau_gem.c:754-988). It returns -ENOMEM if nouveau_abi16_get fails; after that every return goes through nouveau_abi16_put(abi16, ret). It returns -ENOSYS if the client uses UVMM, -ENOENT if no ABI16 channel matches req->channel, -ENODEV if that channel is killed. It records the SYNC flag from req->vram_available and overwrites the field with the available VRAM, sets gart_available, and if req->nr_push is 0 it skips the whole submission (no pushes queued and no fence created) and returns 0 after setting the suffix words. Otherwise it returns -EINVAL if nr_push, nr_buffers or nr_relocs exceed the maximums, copies the push, buffer and reloc arrays from user space (PTR_ERR of a failed u_memcpya), returns -EINVAL if a push's bo_index is not below nr_buffers, validates the buffers (error returned; relocations are copied and the validation redone when needed), applies relocations (error), waits for ring space and queues the pushes in one of three ways by channel class and chipset (errors from nvif_chan_gpfifo_wait, PUSH_WAIT or ttm_bo_kmap returned), creates a fence (error returned), and when SYNC was requested waits for it (the fence status 1 becomes 0). At the end it releases the validation state and fence and, when relocations were done, copies back to user space the buffers' presumed fields that are not valid (a copy_to_user failure sets -EFAULT, even if the submission itself succeeded). It frees the copies and sets the suffix words by channel class before returning.

name: nvkm_firmware_ctor
prose: Returns int (nvkm/core/firmware.c:225-309). It stores func, name, device and len in fw and switches on fw->func->type. For NVKM_FIRMWARE_IMG_RAM it kmemdups the image. For NVKM_FIRMWARE_IMG_DMA it allocates a page-aligned noncoherent DMA buffer, copies the data and records the DMA address, and initialises the single scatterlist with sg_init_one even if the allocation failed. For NVKM_FIRMWARE_IMG_SGT it vmallocs a page-aligned buffer, copies the data, allocates an sg table, fills it with the pages from vmalloc_to_page (a NULL page gives -EFAULT) and maps it for DMA_TO_DEVICE; if any of that fails it frees the table, vfree's the image and sets fw->img to NULL. Any other type executes WARN_ON(1) and returns -EINVAL. After the switch it returns -ENOMEM if fw->img is NULL (so every failure above, including the -EFAULT case, is reported as -ENOMEM); otherwise it constructs the memory object with nvkm_memory_ctor and returns 0.

name: nvkm_mm_init
prose: Returns int (nvkm/core/mm.c:239-280) and adds a heap region [offset, offset+length) to the allocator. If the mm is already initialised it takes the end of the last node; if that differs from offset it BUG_ONs when it is above offset and otherwise allocates (kzalloc, -ENOMEM on failure) a HOLE node for the gap and appends it to mm->nodes; it also BUG_ONs when block differs from mm->block_size. If the mm was not initialised it initialises the node and free lists, sets block_size and zeroes heap_nodes. It then allocates a node (kzalloc; -ENOMEM on failure, in which case the hole node added above stays in the list), and when length is nonzero sets node->offset to the block-rounded-up offset and node->length to the block-rounded-down end minus that offset; with length 0 the node has zero offset and length. It appends the node to mm->nodes and mm->free, sets node->heap to heap, increments mm->heap_nodes and returns 0. nvkm_mm_fini frees the nodes.

name: nvkm_device_ctor
prose: Returns int (nvkm/engine/device/base.c:3140-3461). It takes nv_devices_mutex for the whole call and returns -EEXIST if a device with the same handle is already listed. It fills in func, quirk, dev, type, handle and options, adds the device to nv_devices (it stays there on failure), maps BAR0 into device->pri (-ENOMEM if that fails), and switches the GPU to the CPU's endianness (-ENOSYS if that fails). It reads BOOT0 (replaced by a derived value when the NvChipset option is set), derives chipset, chiprev and card_type, selects the chip description from the chipset number, and returns -ENODEV for an unknown chipset unless the unsupported-chipsets option selects chipset 0x170. It returns -ENODEV for card types from TU100 on when BOOT1 indicates a vGPU. It reads the strap register to set the crystal frequency, sets the name, initialises the mutex and interrupt state, and constructs each subdev and engine listed in the chip layout: a constructor error other than -ENODEV logs and returns that error; an -ENODEV is swallowed (the subdev is deleted and its pointer cleared) and construction continues. The final result is that of nvkm_intr_install, which overwrites a swallowed -ENODEV. On any nonzero result, if device->pri is set it is unmapped and cleared. The mutex is released at done.

name: nvkm_disp_new_
prose: Returns int (nvkm/engine/disp/base.c:228-262) and creates the display engine. It allocates *pdisp with kzalloc (-ENOMEM on failure, leaving *pdisp NULL), stores func and initialises the heads, iors, outps and conns lists and the client lock, and constructs the engine with nvkm_engine_ctor; on an error it sets disp->func to NULL and returns the error. If func->super is set it creates a single-thread workqueue named nvkm-disp (-ENOMEM if that fails, with nothing undone), then initialises the super work with func->super and the super mutex. It returns the result of nvkm_event_init for the uevent. The work item, workqueue and mutex are initialised only when func->super is non-NULL.

name: gf117_grctx_generate_attrib
prose: Void function (ctxgf117.c:243-275) that fills the attribute and alpha circular buffer entries in a channel's context patch list. It reads the alpha and beta numbers from the chip's grctx functions, patches register 0x405830 with (beta << 16) | alpha and 0x4064c4 with ((alpha / 4) << 16) | 0xffff, then for each GPC and each PPC (up to the chip's ppc_nr) it skips PPCs not set in gr->ppc_mask[gpc]; for the others it patches the unit's 0xc0 register with the timeslice mode (1), beta times the PPC's TPC count and the running offset bo, advances bo by attrib_nr_max times the PPC's TPC count, patches the 0xe4 register with alpha times the TPC count and the running offset ao, and advances ao by alpha_nr_max times the TPC count. bo starts at 0 and ao at attrib_nr_max times the total TPC count. The writes go to the patch list through gf100_grctx_patch_wr32 and the function returns nothing.
note: slice cut the head: the function is gf117_grctx_generate_attrib (head at ctxgf117.c:243); the old prose omitted the two writes before the loop and the PPC mask test is by ppc_mask[gpc]. R:n/a

name: nvbios_pll_parse
prose: Returns int (nvkm/subdev/bios/pll.c:229-440). If type is above PLL_MAX it treats it as a register and maps it with pll_map_reg, otherwise it maps it with pll_map_type; it returns -ENOENT if a nonzero table version was found but no data offset. It then zeroes *info and sets info->type and info->reg itself (the caller does not preset reg). By table version it reads the limits: version 0x00 reads nothing; 0x10 and 0x11 read 32-bit vco frequency limits and set fixed n, m and p limits that depend on the chip; 0x20 and 0x21 read 16-bit values times 1000 and byte fields, and refclk only when len > 0x22; 0x30 and 0x40 and 0x50 follow indirect or direct layouts with their own field sets (0x40 and 0x50 set refclk; 0x40 and 0x50 also set min_p). Any other version logs an error and returns -EINVAL with info partially cleared. If refclk is still 0 it uses the device crystal, except on chip 0x51 for registers 0x680508 (with bit 0x20 of 0x680524) and 0x680520 (with bit 0x80), where it becomes 200000 or 25000 according to VGA register 0x27. If vco1.max_freq is still 0 it fills the vco1 limits from the BMP table (fixed 128000 and 256000 when the BMP version is below 0x0506), with min_m and max_m chosen by chip and crystal and max_p of 4 or 5, and sets max_p_usable. It returns 0.

name: nvkm_hwsq_wr32
prose: Void function (nvkm/subdev/bus/hwsq.c:90-113) that appends the commands for a register write to the hwsq command buffer through hwsq_cmd, which memcpy's into hwsq->c.data at hwsq->c.size and advances the size without any bounds check. If data differs from the cached hwsq->data it appends a data command: 5 bytes with opcode 0xe2 when the upper 16 bits of data differ from the cached value, otherwise 3 bytes with opcode 0x42. It then always appends an address command, whether or not the address changed: 5 bytes with opcode 0xe0 when the upper 16 bits of addr differ from the cached hwsq->addr, otherwise 3 bytes with opcode 0x40. It finally stores addr and data in hwsq->addr and hwsq->data. It can append up to 10 bytes, so the buffer must have at least 10 bytes of free space.
note: Checked against hwsq.c:36-41 and 90-113. Reviewer claims: the address command is always emitted (right, 104-109) and the buffer needs at least 10 bytes free, not at most (right, hwsq_cmd has no bounds check). R:right

name: gk104_ram_new_
prose: Returns int (nvkm/subdev/fb/ramgk104.c:1520-1697). It runs gf100_ram_ctor (error returned), initialises the cfg list, reads the partition count and mask from 0x022438 and 0x022554 and computes pnuts from differing partition configurations, parses all ramcfg data entries with gk104_ram_ctor_data until it returns -ENOENT (any other error is logged and returned), parses the mclk reference PLL (type 0x0c) and memory PLL (type 0x04) with nvbios_pll_parse (errors returned), looks up the two optional GPIO functions (a failed lookup is ignored, leaving those fuc registers unset), fills in the ramfuc register table (with the mode register set depending on whether the RAM is GDDR5 or DDR3), and returns 0.

name: gt215_ram_prog
prose: Static int (ramgt215.c:882-905) that executes the prepared reclock script. It reads the NvMemExec boolean option (default true). When true it sets bit 1 of register 0x001534 (mask 0x2), calls ram_exec(fuc, true), then clears bit 0 of 0x002504, clears bit 1 of 0x001534, and sets bit 4 of 0x616308 and 0x616b08. When false it only calls ram_exec(fuc, false). It always returns 0.

name: g94_i2c_aux_init
prose: Static int (auxg94.c:39-73) that arms the AUX channel for a transfer. It polls register 0x00e4e4 + ch*0x50 with 1 us delays for about 1000 iterations until the bits 0x03010000 are clear, and returns -EBUSY (writing nothing) if they never clear. It then writes 0x00100000 into the 0x00300000 field of that register and polls, again about 1000 times, for bits 0x03000000 to equal 0x01000000; on timeout it calls g94_i2c_aux_fini (clears bits 0x00310000) and returns -EBUSY. Otherwise it returns 0, leaving the programmed state in place.
note: Checked against auxg94.c:32-73. Prior prose consistent with the code; only the poll count is stated as about 1000 here since the timeout decrement runs one extra iteration. R:n/a

name: g94_i2c_aux_xfer
prose: Returns int (auxg94.c:75-165) and performs one AUX transaction on channel aux->ch. It first calls g94_i2c_aux_init; if that fails (negative result) it goes straight to out, returning that error. It reads status register 0x00e4e8+base and returns -ENXIO (at out) if bit 0x10000000 is clear. It then disables auto-DPCD, and for an even type (a write) copies *size bytes from data into a 16-byte buffer and writes it to the data registers. It builds the control word (type, length or 0x100 for a zero size), writes the address, then loops: it pulses the start sequence (with a 400 us delay when retrying), starts the transaction and polls up to about 2000 times for the busy bit to clear (a timeout sets -EIO and jumps to out_err, skipping the data read), reads the status and sets ret to 1 for reply codes 0x8 or 0x2, to -ETIMEDOUT when bit 0x100 is set and to -EIO when any of bits 0xe00 is set; it repeats while ret is nonzero, retry is true and fewer than 33 attempts were made. For an odd type (a read) it reads 16 bytes from the reply registers and copies *size bytes to data, also when the final ret is nonzero. At out_err it re-enables auto-DPCD; at out it calls g94_i2c_aux_fini. It returns ret if negative, otherwise (status & 0x000f0000) >> 16 from the last status read, which is a value from 0 to 15 (a negative return comes from init (-EBUSY), no sink (-ENXIO), timeout or error status (-EIO) or -ETIMEDOUT). The data buffer must hold 16 bytes for reads.
note: Checked against auxg94.c:75-165. Prior prose consistent with the code; added that -EBUSY comes from g94_i2c_aux_init, that auto-DPCD is only toggled after the sink check, and that the data read happens also for a nonzero final ret. R:n/a

name: nvkm_mxm_new_
prose: Returns int (nvkm/subdev/mxm/base.c:232-279). It allocates the nvkm_mxm with kzalloc and stores the pointer in *pmxm (-ENOMEM on failure, with *pmxm NULL), and constructs the subdev. It looks up the MXM table in the VBIOS; if there is none or its version byte is 0 it logs and returns 0 with mxm->mxms left NULL. Otherwise it logs the BIOS version and flags and calls mxm_shadow to locate a valid SIS (trying ROM, then DSM and WMI when configured); if none is valid it logs a warning and still returns 0. When a valid SIS is found it logs its version, walks the SIS structures with mxms_foreach, sets MXM_SANITISE_DCB in mxm->action if the NvMXMDCB option is true (default true), and returns 0. There is no -ENODEV return: a missing BIOS is not tested here.

name: PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER(__name, __reg_prefix, __handler)
prose: Raw interrupt handler generated by the PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER macro as panthor_<name>_irq_raw_handler(irq, data), where data is the struct panthor_irq. It returns IRQ_NONE if pirq->suspended is set, without touching the hardware. Otherwise it reads the <prefix>_INT_STAT register (so the hardware is read in this case) and returns IRQ_NONE if the value is zero; if it is nonzero it writes 0 to <prefix>_INT_MASK and returns IRQ_WAKE_THREAD.
note: the item named panthor_<name>_irq_raw_handler; this is the function generated by the macro at panthor_device.h:388-401. Reviewer claim (the handler must read INT_STAT even when it reads zero) is right: the old wording implied no hardware access when INT_STAT was zero. R:right

name: PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER(__name, __reg_prefix, __handler)
prose: Threaded interrupt handler generated by the PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER macro as panthor_<name>_irq_threaded_handler(irq, data). It loops reading <prefix>_INT_RAWSTAT masked with pirq->mask; for each nonzero value it calls the user handler (ptdev, status) and records IRQ_HANDLED, and stops when the masked status is zero. After the loop it writes pirq->mask back to <prefix>_INT_MASK unless pirq->suspended is set, and returns IRQ_HANDLED if at least one status was handled, otherwise IRQ_NONE.

name: PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER(__name, __reg_prefix, __handler)

A failed registration leaves the interrupt registers programmed by the resume call.

name: dce4_crtc_do_set_base
prose: Static int (atombios_crtc.c:1134-1453), the Evergreen/DCE4 scanout-base programming. With atomic == 0 and no framebuffer bound to the primary plane it returns 0 at once; the target framebuffer is fb when atomic is set and the primary plane's framebuffer otherwise. It reserves the buffer object (the reservation error is returned before any register is touched); in the atomic case it takes the current GPU offset, otherwise it pins the object in VRAM, and a pin failure unreserves and returns -EINVAL. It reads the tiling flags, unreserves, and chooses the surface format and endian swap from the framebuffer's pixel format (the 10-bit formats set bypass_lut); an unsupported format returns -EINVAL after the reservation was released, leaving a buffer pinned in the non-atomic case. It then derives the tiling, bank, pipe-config fields per ASIC family (on CIK a computed tile index of 16 or more logs and returns -EINVAL), programs the CRTC's graphics surface address, format, swap, pitch, viewport, desktop height and the LUT bypass bit, and, if not atomic and a different old framebuffer was passed, reserves it (a reservation failure returns that error) and unpins it. It finally calls radeon_bandwidth_update and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head: the packet slice covers the end of dce4_crtc_do_set_base (head at atombios_crtc.c:1134) and the start of avivo_crtc_do_set_base; there is no function evergreen_crtc_do_set_base. The old prose omitted the early return 0 without a framebuffer, the CIK tile-index -EINVAL and the old-framebuffer unpin. R:n/a

name: atombios_crtc_program_ss
prose: Static void (atombios_crtc.c:443-550) with no return value. With enable nonzero it returns at once when ss->percentage is 0 or ss->type has ATOM_EXTERNAL_SS_MASK set; with enable zero it returns at once when another enabled CRTC (index different from crtc_id) uses the same pll_id. Otherwise it fills the ATOM argument structure by ASIC generation: DCE5 (v3, amount, step and type with the PLL selection bits; ATOM_PPLL_INVALID returns without executing), DCE4 (v2, same pll handling), DCE3 (v1 with percentage, type, step, delay, range, pll id and enable), AVIVO (it calls atombios_disable_ss and returns when enable is ATOM_DISABLE or the percentage is 0 or the type is external; since the early returns above already cover the enable case with percentage 0 or external SS, this condition effectively only happens for enable == ATOM_DISABLE), and older ASICs (for ATOM_DISABLE it calls atombios_disable_ss and returns). In every remaining case it executes the EnableSpreadSpectrumOnPPLL ATOM table with the argument block.
note: Checked against atombios_crtc.c:443-550. Reviewer claims: the AVIVO and pre-AVIVO disable paths call atombios_disable_ss and return without executing the table (right, 527-531 and 539-542); with enable nonzero and zero percentage or external spread spectrum the function returns early without calling atombios_disable_ss (right, 459-462). R:right

name: atombios_dig_transmitter_setup
prose: Void wrapper (atombios_encoders.c:1367-1371) that calls atombios_dig_transmitter_setup2(encoder, action, lane_num, lane_set, -1), where the last argument is the front-end encoder fe. It does nothing else. The callee does not return immediately because fe is -1: it reads the encoder's own dig->dig_encoder and returns without executing any ATOM command only when that field is -1; otherwise it selects the transmitter table by encoder id and executes the DIG transmitter control command. No locks or references are taken by this wrapper.

Reviewer claim (the setup2 callee executes ATOM commands when its dig_encoder is not -1, contrary to the old 'returns immediately because dig_encoder is -1') is right: the early return tests dig->dig_encoder at 1048, not the fe argument. R:right

name: radeon_process_i2c_ch
prose: Static int (atombios_i2c.c:36-98). It takes chan->mutex and then the ATOM scratch mutex, and releases both before every return. For a write (HW_I2C_WRITE set in flags) it returns -EINVAL when num is above ATOM_MAX_HW_I2C_WRITE (3); otherwise it sets the register index from buf[0] (0 if buf is NULL), decrements num when it is nonzero and copies the remaining num bytes from buf[1] into a 16-bit output value (so num - 1 data bytes are sent for num of 1 or more, and 0 for num 0). For a read the register index and output are 0. It then fills the ATOM argument block (flags, speed, byte count, slave address shifted left by one, line number) and executes ProcessI2cChannelTransaction. If the returned status is not HW_ASSISTED_I2C_STATUS_SUCCESS it returns -EIO without modifying buf; otherwise, for a read it copies num bytes from the ATOM scratch area into buf with radeon_atom_copy_swap, and it returns 0.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at atombios_i2c.c:36). Reviewer claims: writes larger than 3 return -EINVAL, not a precondition (right, 56-60); a write with num 0 transmits 0 bytes, not num - 1 (right, 65-66). R:right

name: evergreen_gpu_init
prose: Static void (evergreen.c:3132-3707); it has no return statement (and returns nothing). It switches on rdev->family to fill rdev->config.evergreen with per-ASIC values (num_ses, max_pipes, max_tile_pipes, max_simds, max_backends, max_gprs, max_threads, max_gs_threads, max_stack_entries, sx and sc sizes, max_hw_contexts, sq_num_cf_insts), computes tile_config from the pipe count, the IGP flag or the memory bank configuration and gb_addr_config, determines the disabled render backends (from fuse straps for CEDAR to HEMLOCK, otherwise per shader engine) and the active SIMDs from CC_GC_SHADER_PIPE_CONFIG, programs GB_ADDR_CONFIG and the other address-config registers, the backend map (stored in config.evergreen.backend_map), the CP, TA, SX, SMX, PA_SC, SPI, SQ resource-management and VGT registers (with per-family thread counts and cache invalidation mode), clears the color base, perf counter and constant-buffer registers, sets the HDP flush-invalidate bit, and ends with a 50 microsecond delay.

name: evergreen_packet3_check
prose: Static int (evergreen_cs.c:1773-2761) that validates one type-3 command packet in an Evergreen command stream; its body is a switch on pkt->opcode. For each supported opcode it checks the packet's count and field values, fetches relocation entries with radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc where an address is present, patches the IB words with the relocated GPU offset, updates the tracker, and for draw and dispatch packets calls evergreen_cs_track_check. It returns 0 when the packet passes (including SET_PREDICATION with a clear operation, which returns 0 early, and NOP). It returns -EINVAL for a wrong packet count, an invalid field, a buffer that is too small for the access, an unsupported opcode, and also when a required relocation cannot be obtained (radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc failures are converted to -EINVAL after a warning); only the result of evergreen_cs_track_check is returned unchanged, so those errors can be other negative values.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at evergreen_cs.c:1773). Reviewer claim (relocation failures return -EINVAL, not the error from radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc as the old prose said) is right (for example 1923-1927); evergreen_cs_track_check errors are returned as is (1908-1911). The function is long (about 990 lines and many return points), so this prose is deliberately general. R:right

name: evergreen_cs_parse
prose: Returns int (evergreen_cs.c:2763-2877) and parses a whole indirect buffer. If p->track is NULL it allocates a tracker with kzalloc (returning -ENOMEM on failure, with nothing to free), initialises it with evergreen_cs_track_init, picks the register safety bitmap and the tile configuration by family (Cayman or Evergreen), derives npipes, nbanks, group_size and row_size from the tile configuration and stores it in p->track; a tracker that is already present is used as it is. It then loops while p->idx is below the IB length: it parses the packet header with radeon_cs_packet_parse (an error frees the tracker, sets p->track to NULL and is returned), advances p->idx past the packet, and handles type 0 with evergreen_cs_parse_packet0, type 2 as a no-op and type 3 with evergreen_packet3_check; an unknown packet type frees the tracker and returns -EINVAL, and a nonzero result from the type 0 or type 3 handler frees the tracker and returns it. When the loop completes it frees the tracker, sets p->track to NULL and returns 0. The tracker is freed on every path after the allocation.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at evergreen_cs.c:2763). Reviewer claim (the old prose omitted track init and packet2 and wrongly required a preinitialised tracker) is partly right: a NULL tracker is allocated here (2770-2775); evergreen_cs_track_init has no return value and type 2 packets only advance the index. R:mixed

name: evergreen_dma_cs_parse
prose: Returns int (evergreen_cs.c:2888-3314) and validates and relocates a whole DMA indirect buffer, looping over its packets. At the start of each iteration it returns -EINVAL if p->idx is not below the chunk length. It decodes the DMA command, count and sub-command from the header word and switches on the command: WRITE (needs a destination relocation through r600_dma_cs_next_reloc; sub-commands 0 and 8 patch the offset words, advance p->idx by count plus 3 or 7, and then check that the written range fits the destination object), COPY (needs source and destination relocations; the sub-commands handle linear, tiled and partial copy forms, check that the source and destination ranges fit their objects, patch the offsets and advance p->idx by the packet size), CONSTANT_FILL (destination relocation, patched offset words, size check, advance by 4) and NOP (advance by 1). It returns -EINVAL for a missing relocation, an unsupported command or sub-command, or a range that exceeds a buffer object; in the WRITE case p->idx and the patched IB words have already been advanced before the size check, so p->idx is not left at the offending packet. When the loop ends it returns 0.
note: the item named r600_dma_cs_parse_packet, which does not exist in this file; the slice (2989-3289) lies inside evergreen_dma_cs_parse (head at evergreen_cs.c:2888), which loops over all packets. The old prose described a single-packet parser and claimed p->idx is not advanced on error, which is wrong for the WRITE case. R:n/a

name: kv_parse_sys_info_table
prose: Static int (kv_dpm.c, head just before line 2295). It finds the IGP system info table header with atom_parse_data_header; if that fails it returns 0 without changing pi. If the table's content revision is not 8 it logs and returns -EINVAL without changing pi. Otherwise it fills pi->sys_info with the boot-up engine and UMA clocks and NB voltage index, htc_tmp_lmt (203 when the BIOS byte is 0) and htc_hyst_lmt (5 when 0) (logging an error, but continuing, when the first is not above the second), nb_dpm_enable from bit 3 of ulSystemConfig, and the KV_NUM_NBPSTATES NB p-state memory and n clocks; it sets pi->caps_enable_dfs_bypass to true when the DFS-bypass bit of ulGPUCapInfo is set (otherwise leaving it unchanged), builds the sclk voltage mapping table and vid mapping table with sumo_construct_sclk_voltage_mapping_table and sumo_construct_vid_mapping_table, fills rdev->pm.dpm.dyn_state.max_clock_voltage_on_ac with kv_construct_max_power_limits_table and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head: the function is kv_parse_sys_info_table (not kv_parse_sys_info). Old prose consistent with the code. R:n/a

name: r100_pm_get_dynpm_state
prose: Void function (r100.c:224-304). It first sets dynpm_can_upclock and dynpm_can_downclock to true. By dynpm_planned_action: MINIMUM sets requested_power_state_index to 0 and clears can_downclock; DOWNCLOCK at current index 0 keeps the index and clears can_downclock, otherwise with more than one active CRTC it scans from index 0 for the first state without RADEON_PM_STATE_SINGLE_DISPLAY_ONLY and requests the current index if that state's index is at or above it and that state's index otherwise (leaving the request unchanged if every state has the flag), and with at most one active CRTC it requests current - 1; afterwards, if any CRTC is active and the requested state's first clock info has RADEON_PM_MODE_NO_DISPLAY, the request is incremented. UPCLOCK at the last state keeps the index and clears can_upclock; otherwise with more than one active CRTC it scans from the top for the first state without the single-display flag and requests the current index if that state's index is at or below it and that state's index otherwise, and with fewer CRTCs it requests current + 1. DEFAULT requests the default state index and clears can_upclock. DYNPM_ACTION_NONE or any other value logs an error and returns at once, leaving requested_power_state_index and requested_clock_mode_index unchanged. In the other cases it sets requested_clock_mode_index to 0 and emits a driver debug message with the requested clocks.
note: Checked against r100.c:224-304. Reviewer claims: NONE/default returns early without setting requested_clock_mode_index (right, 289-292), multi-CRTC cases pick the lowest/highest usable state (right, 240-251 and 268-279), only DRM_ERROR on the early return and a DRM_DEBUG_DRIVER message otherwise (right, 291 and 297). R:right

name: r100_packet0_check
prose: Static int (r100.c:1585-1924) that validates one register write of a type-0 packet and updates the command-stream tracker; the body is a switch on reg. Per register it records tracked state (texture parameters, colour buffer pitch and cpp, depth buffer pitch, maxy, vertex size, vap_vf_cntl, dirty flags) from the IB value, and for registers holding an address it gets a relocation with radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc and patches ib[idx]: for RB3D_COLOROFFSET and similar address registers it adds the relocation's GPU offset, but for RB3D_COLORPITCH it only uses the relocation's tiling flags to rewrite the tiling bits of the pitch word (when RADEON_CS_KEEP_TILING_FLAGS is clear; otherwise the value is kept) and does not add the GPU offset. It returns 0 when the register is handled, returns the error of r100_cs_packet_parse_vline, r100_reloc_pitch_offset or radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc unchanged, and returns -EINVAL for an invalid RB3D colour format or a register that is not handled.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at r100.c:1585). Reviewer claim (COLORPITCH uses the relocation for tiling only and does not add gpu_offset to ib[idx]) is right (1739-1749). The function is long, so this prose is deliberately general. R:right

name: r100_cs_track_check
prose: Returns int (r100.c:2272-2407) and checks the tracked state before a draw. It sets num_cb to track->num_cb only when cb_dirty is set (and to 0 when no colour write can happen: no clear, empty colour channel mask and no blend read). For each colour buffer it returns -EINVAL if the buffer object is NULL or pitch * cpp * maxy plus the offset exceeds the object size; then it clears cb_dirty (so an early return leaves it set). If zb_dirty and z_enabled are set it does the same size check for the depth buffer, then clears zb_dirty; if aa_dirty and aaresolve are set it checks the AA buffer and clears aa_dirty. It then decodes the primitive walk from vap_vf_cntl: walk 1 and 2 check each vertex array for a bound object and its size (-EINVAL), walk 3 checks that vtx_size * nverts equals immd_dwords (-EINVAL), and any other walk returns -EINVAL. Finally, if tex_dirty is set it clears it first and returns the result of r100_cs_track_texture_check (which can return -EINVAL or the -1 from r100_cs_track_cube); otherwise it returns 0. Hence the dirty flags of checks that already completed are cleared even if a later check fails.
note: Checked against r100.c:2272-2407. Reviewer claims: dirty flags are cleared before later checks can fail (right), the texture check can return -1 via r100_cs_track_cube and tex_dirty is cleared even when it fails (right, 2402-2404), and it can also return -EINVAL (right, it returns whatever r100_cs_track_texture_check returns). R:right

name: r100_bandwidth_update
prose: Void function (r100.c:3171-3673). It returns at once if rdev->mode_info.mode_config_initialized is false. Otherwise it updates the display priority, takes the mode and framebuffer pixel size of CRTC 0 when it is enabled and, unless the device is a single-CRTC part, of CRTC 1 when enabled. It then evaluates the memory and display timing model with fixed-point arithmetic (memory timings read from MEM_CNTL, MEM_SDRAM_MODE_REG and MEM_TIMING_CNTL, peak display bandwidth against memory bandwidth with a DRM_ERROR warning when the bandwidth may be insufficient) and programs the display buffer control registers (GRPH_BUFFER_CNTL and GRPH2_BUFFER_CNTL, and on RS400/RS480 the fixed DISP/DMIF request registers) for each enabled CRTC. At the end it sets lb_vblank_lead_lines of each enabled CRTC to the line buffer size divided (rounded up) by its horizontal display size. It returns nothing.

name: r300_packet0_check
prose: Static int (r300.c:627-1171) that validates one register write of a type-0 packet and updates the command-stream tracker; the body is a switch on reg. Per register it records tracked state (colour buffer, depth buffer, texture and vertex fields, with dirty flags set) from idx_value and, where the register holds an address, gets a relocation with radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc and patches ib[idx] with the relocated offset and tiling bits. Some cases handle hyperz access by clearing the bit in ib[idx] when the file does not own the hyperz state. It returns 0 when the register is handled; it returns the error of r100_cs_packet_parse_vline, r100_reloc_pitch_offset or radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc unchanged; and it returns -EINVAL (through the fail label, after logging the register) for an invalid texture or colour format, a forbidden value or an unknown register.

name: r520_init
prose: Returns int (r520.c:250-329). It initialises the scratch registers and surfaces and restores sanity. It returns -EINVAL if no BIOS can be obtained on an AVIVO ASIC, and returns -EINVAL if the BIOS is not an ATOM BIOS (with a message naming RV515); an error from radeon_atombios_init is returned. It then tries an ASIC reset (only warning on failure), returns -EINVAL if the card fails the post test, posts the card through atom_asic_init when it is not posted and a BIOS exists, reads the clock info, initialises AGP (disabling it on failure), the memory controller, debugfs, the fence driver, the buffer object manager (error returned) and the PCIE GART (error returned), sets the safe register table and initialises power management. It sets accel_working to true and calls r520_startup; if that fails it logs, tears down the CP, writeback, IB pool, IRQs, GART and AGP and sets accel_working to false, but the function still returns 0. Otherwise it returns 0.

name: r600_packet3_check
prose: Static int (r600_cs.c:1631-2275) that validates one type-3 packet of an R600 command stream with a switch on the opcode. For each supported opcode it checks the packet count and fields (register windows for SET_* packets, buffer and offset sizes, texture and vertex resources), fetches relocations with radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc where an address is present and patches the IB words with the relocated GPU offset and tiling bits, updates the tracker, and runs r600_cs_track_check for draw packets. It returns 0 for a valid packet (including packets with a clear operation that return early, and NOP) and -EINVAL for a wrong count, a failed field check, a buffer that is too small, a missing relocation (radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc failures are converted to -EINVAL after a message) or an unsupported opcode; the results of r600_cs_check_reg, r600_check_texture_resource and r600_cs_track_check are returned unchanged.

name: r600_dma_cs_parse
prose: Returns int (r600_cs.c:2385-2534) and validates and relocates a whole DMA indirect buffer in a loop. At the start of every iteration it returns -EINVAL if p->idx is not below the chunk length. It decodes the command, count and tiled flag from the header and switches on the command. WRITE gets one destination relocation (tiled or linear form patch the offset words and advance p->idx by count plus 5 or 3, then the written range is checked against the destination object); COPY gets source and destination relocations and handles tiled and linear forms (RV770 and later or earlier layouts) with range checks against both objects; CONSTANT_FILL returns -EINVAL for families older than RV770, otherwise takes a destination relocation, checks the range and patches the words; NOP advances by one; any other command returns -EINVAL. A failed r600_dma_cs_next_reloc returns -EINVAL before p->idx is advanced; in the WRITE and COPY cases p->idx has already been advanced when the size check fails. The loop ends with return 0 when p->idx reaches the chunk length.
