name: radeon_get_atom_connector_info_from_object_table
prose: Returns bool (radeon_atombios.c:517-831). It parses the Object_Header data header and returns false if that fails or the content revision is below 2. Otherwise it walks the display path table; for each path whose device tag is supported by the header and is not the CV device, it works out the connector type and object id (for an IGP PCIE connector from the IntegratedSystemInfo table's slot config when its revision is at least 2, otherwise from the connector object id; paths whose IGP lookup fails are skipped) and skips paths whose connector type is unknown. For each graphics object in the path it registers encoders with radeon_add_atom_encoder (with their capability record) and gathers router information (I2C, DDC and clock/data mux records); for non-TV, non-CV paths it finds the connector object and reads its I2C (DDC) and HPD records. It applies board quirks with radeon_atom_apply_quirks (a path rejected by the quirks is skipped) and registers each connector with radeon_add_atom_connector. After the loop it calls radeon_link_encoder_connector and returns true. It takes no locks and the caller releases nothing.
note: slice cut the head: the function is radeon_get_atom_connector_info_from_object_table's real name radeon_get_atom_connector_info_from_object_table (head at radeon_atombios.c:517; the packet name radeon_atombios_get_connector_info_from_object_table does not exist). Old prose omitted that encoders are registered here too and that paths can be skipped. R:n/a

name: radeon_gpu_reset
prose: Returns int (radeon_device.c:1755-1857). It takes rdev->exclusive_lock for writing; if rdev->needs_reset is false it releases it with up_write and returns 0. Otherwise it bumps gpu_reset_counter, saves the BIOS scratch registers, suspends the device, stops HPD, backs up each ring's pending commands, and calls radeon_asic_reset; on success it resumes the device. It restores the BIOS scratch registers, then for each ring either restores the saved commands (reset succeeded and data saved) or force-completes the ring's fences and frees the backup. It then redoes power management: radeon_pm_late_init when DPM is the method and enabled (its result replaces r, so a failed ASIC reset can be overwritten by a 0 result; a failed late init disables DPM) or radeon_pm_resume otherwise. For ATOM BIOS it reinitialises the encoders, the display engine PLL and the backlight, re-initialises HPD, sets in_reset and clears needs_reset, downgrades the lock to read mode, forces the display mode back, recomputes clocks for DPM, and, if r is 0 after those steps, runs radeon_ib_ring_tests (a failure with saved commands becomes -EAGAIN) or logs the failed reset. It sets needs_reset when r is -EAGAIN, clears in_reset, releases the read lock and returns r.

name: radeon_fence_default_wait
prose: Static signed long (radeon_fence.c:1003-1043). It first calls dma_fence_add_callback; if that returns nonzero (for example the fence is already signalled) it returns t unchanged, without changing the task state. Otherwise, while t > 0 it sets the task state to interruptible or uninterruptible according to intr, breaks if the fence is signalled (t then keeps the value it had) or if rdev->needs_reset is set (t becomes -EDEADLK), else sleeps with schedule_timeout(t), and sets t to -ERESTARTSYS if the sleep ended with time left, intr is set and a signal is pending. After the loop it sets the task state to TASK_RUNNING, removes the callback and returns t: the remaining timeout, 0 on expiry, -EDEADLK or -ERESTARTSYS, or the original t if it was not positive.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at radeon_fence.c:1003). Reviewer claim (round 15: on a failed dma_fence_add_callback it can return -ERESTARTSYS) is wrong: that path returns t at line 1013 before any signal test. R:wrong

name: radeon_info_ioctl
prose: Returns int (radeon_kms.c:231-616) and implements the radeon info query ioctl with a switch on info->request, copying a value of the request's size to the user buffer at info->value. It returns -EFAULT when copy_from_user or copy_to_user fails, and -EINVAL for an unknown or unsupported request, an out-of-range input (WANT_HYPERZ and WANT_CMASK values of 2 or more, an unknown CRTC id or ring id, a disallowed register) or a request the device family does not support. For WANT_HYPERZ and WANT_CMASK the file's ownership flag is updated and the resulting ownership is reported. It returns 0 after the final copy_to_user succeeds. A failing copy_to_user can leave the user buffer partially written, so the buffer is not guaranteed unwritten on error.

name: uvd_v1_0_ib_test
prose: Returns int (uvd_v1_0.c:500-542). It raises the UVD clocks (10000/10000 for families older than RV740, 53300/40000 otherwise) and returns the error at once if that fails, without releasing anything. It then gets the UVD create message and the destroy message (with a fence); a failure of either goes to error. It waits for the fence for RADEON_USEC_IB_TEST_TIMEOUT microseconds: a negative result is returned, zero (timeout) becomes -ETIMEDOUT, and a positive result is a success, logged as such with result 0. At the error label, reached on every path after the clocks were raised including success, it releases the fence reference and sets the UVD clocks back to 0, then returns the result.

name: awg_generate_instr
prose: Static int (sti_awg_utils.c:28-118) that appends AWG RAM instruction words to fwparams. It loops while arg_tmp (initially arg) is positive; each iteration returns -EINVAL if fwparams->instruction_offset is already AWG_MAX_INST (words written by earlier iterations stay in ram_code and instruction_offset stays advanced) and then handles the opcode: SKIP decrements arg and arg_tmp and turns into SET when arg reaches 0, or clears mux and data enable and masks the argument; REPEAT and REPLAY clear mux and data enable and mask the argument; JUMP sets bit 6 of the argument and masks it; STOP sets arg to 0; SET, RPTSET, RPLSET and HOLD mask the argument to 8 bits; any other opcode returns -EINVAL. It subtracts the consumed arg from arg_tmp, combines arg, mux and data enable, stores the opcode and argument in 14 bits at ram_code[instruction_offset] and increments instruction_offset. Because arg is positive inside the loop, the SKIP arg < 0 return and the REPEAT/REPLAY arg == 0 return are never reached, so each iteration writes exactly one word. With arg <= 0 on entry nothing is written and it returns 0; otherwise it returns 0 when the loop ends.
note: Checked against sti_awg_utils.c:28-118. Reviewer claims: -EINVAL on the AWG_MAX_INST check can leave earlier words written (right, 48-51); the SKIP/REPEAT/REPLAY early returns are unreachable inside a loop that needs arg_tmp > 0 (right, 57-63, 79-82); round 15 claim (one word per iteration is false because those branches return 0 without writing) is wrong for the same reason. R:mixed

name: sti_crtc_vblank_cb
prose: Returns int (sti_crtc.c:242-279). It is a VTG vblank notifier callback: data is the drm_crtc, its index selects the pipe, and nb is the vtg_vblank_nb[pipe] member of the compositor from which the mixer is found. It returns -EINVAL (after logging) if event is neither VTG_TOP_FIELD_EVENT nor VTG_BOTTOM_FIELD_EVENT. prose: Static void (vmwgfx_surface.c:1845-1890). prose: Returns int (xe_exec.c:110-379) and submits a batch (or just syncs) on an exec queue. For the DMA-fence engine-group mode it gets the engine group mode (error returned). It takes the VM lock for writing (and repins userptrs) when a userptr repin is needed, otherwise for reading (interruptible); when the call has no batch buffers it takes the VM lock object, signals the syncs with a fence from the input syncs and finishes (returning 0 through the unlock path without creating a job). Otherwise it waits for pm_block, locks the VM objects and validates (non-LR VMs), returns -ECANCELED when the VM is closed or banned, returns -EWOULDBLOCK (with skip_retry set) when an LR queue's ring is full, validates PXP-protected VMs, creates the job, adds dependencies from the VM objects and syncs, takes the notifier lock and checks whether a userptr repin is needed, then arms the job, adds fences, signals syncs, pushes the job and reactivates rebinds. If the last step set err to -EAGAIN (and skip_retry is false) it retries from the VM lock. On success err is 0. All paths release the VM lock, the validation context, the job reference on failure, the engine group reference, the syncs and the queue reference.

name: vf_query_runtime_info
prose: Static int (xe_gt_sriov_vf.c:832-909). It returns -ENOPKG at once (before touching the runtime table) if the negotiated PF interface version is below 1.0. Otherwise it sends VF2PF_QUERY_RUNTIME requests through the GuC relay, starting at 0 and asking for up to 16 registers per response. A negative result of the send, a response shorter than the minimum length, a payload of odd size, or a count field different from the number of entries goes to failed with -EPROTO (or the send error). On the first response (start 0) it calls vf_prepare_runtime_info for num + remaining entries (a failure goes to failed); on later responses it returns -EPROTO via failed if start + num exceeds the recorded size. It copies the reported offset and value pairs into gt->sriov.vf.runtime.regs and repeats with start advanced while remaining is nonzero. When remaining is 0 it returns 0 without checking that the table was completely filled. At failed it calls vf_prepare_runtime_info(gt, 0), which resets the runtime table, and returns the error.

name: __guc_ct_send_locked
prose: Static int (xe_guc_ct.c:870-941); the caller holds ct->lock. It returns -EPIPE if the H2G buffer is marked broken, -ENODEV if the CT state is disabled, -ECANCELED if it is stopped (all through the out label, before any other lock is taken). With a g2h_fence it uses the maximum G2H length and one expected G2H, and if the fence needs a sequence number it assigns one and stores the fence in ct->fence_lookup with xa_store (a failure returns its xa_err result with seqno already assigned but the fence not registered); without a fence it takes the next ordinary sequence number. It takes ct->fast_lock (spin_lock_irq) only when g2h_len is nonzero, and releases it on every path after that. It then loops: has_room (nonzero result, which is -EPIPE for a broken buffer or -EBUSY for lack of H2G or G2H space, goes to out_unlock), then h2g_write: -EAGAIN (a ring wrap) retries from has_room (with fast_lock held only if g2h_len is nonzero), another nonzero result goes to out_unlock. On success it reserves g2h_len dwords of G2H space and num_g2h replies, notifies the GuC and returns 0.

Reviewer claims: fast_lock is only taken when g2h_len is nonzero (right, 920-921 and 937-938); h2g_write can also return -EPIPE for a corrupted buffer and the lock is released then (right); the -EAGAIN retry may run without fast_lock when g2h_len is zero (right). name: guc_exec_queue_timedout_job
prose: Static enum drm_gpu_sched_stat (xe_guc_submit.c:1226-1438), the DRM scheduler timeout handler of a GuC exec queue. It returns DRM_GPU_SCHED_STAT_NO_HANG at once, before stopping submission, if the job's fence is already signalled. Otherwise it stops scheduler submission, decides whether to skip the timeout check (reset, killed, banned, wedged or destroyed queue), optionally captures a snapshot under forcewake (releasing it before continuing), and determines whether the device is wedged. For a registered queue while not wedged it may wait up to 5 s for pending enable and disable, disable scheduling and wait again; if a wait fails or the GuC reading is stopped it takes the trigger_reset path: devcoredump, sets an extra queue reference (taken for the asynchronous GT reset), bans the queue, starts an async GT reset, queues an immediate TDR and goes to rearm. If the job is not actually timed out (not wedged, timeout check not skipped, no reset, still registered) it clears the check flag and goes to sched_enable, which re-enables scheduling and then to rearm. For a kernel or VM queue (not wedged) it tries to invalidate the job: if that fails it clears the check flag, starts an async GT reset (without banning the queue or taking an extra reference) and goes to rearm. Otherwise it bans the queue; for a registered, not destroyed queue (not wedged) it takes an extra reference and deregisters it. It then stops the fence irq, re-adds the job to the pending list, restarts submission, triggers queue cleanup, sets the error of the pending jobs (the first gets err, the rest -ECANCELED), restarts the fence irq and returns DRM_GPU_SCHED_STAT_RESET. At rearm it restarts submission and returns DRM_GPU_SCHED_STAT_NO_HANG.

name: xe_pcode_request
prose: Returns int (xe_pcode.c:181-216). It asserts timeout_base_ms is at most 3, takes tile->pcode.lock and calls pcode_try_request with timeout_base_ms * 1000 microseconds without disabling preemption; if that returns 0 it unlocks and returns. The function returns the last status if nonzero, else the pcode_try_request result. With skip_pcode set the mailbox status is 0, so it returns 0 only if request already satisfies the reply mask, else -ETIMEDOUT. The request value is passed by value and is not modified; no reply is returned.

name: xe_vm_create
prose: Returns struct xe_vm * or an ERR_PTR (xe_vm.c:1453-1668). It then runs xe_svm_init (an error goes to err_no_resv), allocates the VM reservation object (-ENOMEM goes to err_svm_fini), initialises the GPU VM and, in a validation guard that retries on contention or out-of-memory, locks the VM, sets the 64K flag on DGFX with NEED64K, creates a page table root for each tile (for a migration VM only the tile selected by the flags, not every tile), creates scratch page tables when needed, and fills the roots with empty entries; an error inside the guard breaks out and goes to err_close. For a non-migration VM it creates a bind exec queue for each tile that has a root (an error goes to err_close), sets a composite fence context when more than one tile is used, and, when xef is given and the device has ASIDs, allocates an ASID (an error goes to err_close). prose: Returns int (amd_sfh_client.c:218-360). It installs suspend and resume handlers in mp2_ops, queries the sensor count, and returns -ENODEV at once (with no cleanup) when it is zero. name: amd_sfh_float_to_int
prose: Returns int (amd_sfh_desc.c:135-174), a conversion of an IEEE-754 single-precision bit pattern to an integer that rounds a fraction of one half or more away from zero. The sign comes from bit 31 and the exponent is taken from bits 23 to 30 (the sign is excluded) minus 127. It returns 0 for a zero exponent field with a zero mantissa. For a negative unbiased exponent it returns 0 when its magnitude is 32 or more, otherwise it computes (((2^23 + mantissa) * 100) >> 23) >> magnitude and returns the sign (plus or minus 1) if that is at least 50 and 0 otherwise. For a non-negative exponent it returns 0 if the distance 23 - exp is 32 or more in magnitude; otherwise it builds the integer part as BIT(exp) plus the mantissa shifted right (or left when exp exceeds 23) by that distance, computes the discarded fraction, and returns sign times the integer part, plus one when the discarded fraction is one half or more. Exponents of 31 and above (biased 158 and above, up to those reaching the 32-bit shift limit) can overflow the int result; the function has no side effects.

name: uclogic_params_ugee_v2_init
prose: Static int (hid-uclogic-params.c:1401-1534) that fills *params for a UGEE v2 tablet interface. It returns -EINVAL if params or hdev is NULL, before anything is read or modified. It reads the driver data and the interface number into local variables, and builds the result in a local struct p. Interface 0 gets a mouse frame from uclogic_params_ugee_v2_init_frame_mouse (its error, if nonzero, is returned); interface 0 and any other interface other than 2 are handled without the pen path (an interface other than 0 and 2 gives an invalid parameter set). For interface 2 it probes the interface with uclogic_probe_interface; if the probe fails it makes p invalid and takes the output path. It then reads a 12-byte string descriptor; if the read does not return exactly 12 it logs with hid_err, makes p invalid and takes the output path. It parses the descriptor with uclogic_params_parse_ugee_v2_desc (a nonzero result is returned), frees the string descriptor, applies the pen report descriptor template (NULL gives -ENOMEM), fills the pen descriptor, id 2 and the first subreport, forces the mouse frame type when UCLOGIC_MOUSE_FRAME_QUIRK is set in the driver quirks, and initialises the frame with the dial initialiser (dial and mouse types) or the buttons initialiser (buttons and any other type); a nonzero result is returned. If the device has a battery it initialises it (an error is logged and returned), then initialises the event hooks (an error is logged and returned). On the output path it copies p into *params, clears the local copy and returns 0, so the invalid-parameter cases above return 0 with *params set to the invalid set. On each error return *params is left unmodified, and the string descriptor and the local parameter set (including the pen report descriptor) are freed.

name: wacom_wac_pen_serial_enforce
prose: Static int (wacom_sys.c:105-172). It returns 0 at once, touching neither the queue nor the serial state, if wacom_wac->serial[0] is already nonzero or the features lack WACOM_QUIRK_TOOLSERIAL. Otherwise it scans every usage of every field of the report whose equivalent usage is HID_DG_INRANGE, HID_DG_TOOLSERIALNUMBER, WACOM_HID_WD_SERIALHI or WACOM_HID_WD_TOOLTYPE, extracting the value from raw_data + 1 and inverting the value for HID_DG_INRANGE (so a zero in-range field counts as nonzero). A usage with a nonzero value sets a flush flag and additionally stores the value into wacom_wac->serial[0] (HID_DG_TOOLSERIALNUMBER, replacing it), ORs it shifted by 32 into serial[0] (WACOM_HID_WD_SERIALHI) or stores it into wacom_wac->id[0] (WACOM_HID_WD_TOOLTYPE); an in-range usage records nothing besides the flag. A usage whose value is 0 sets an insert flag. If flush is set it calls wacom_wac_queue_flush, which replays every queued entry through hid_report_raw_event (an entry whose buffer cannot be allocated is dropped silently, an entry of unexpected size is dropped with a warning, a replay error only logs a warning). Otherwise, if insert is set, it appends raw_data (report_size bytes) to pen_fifo, dropping the oldest entries to make room, and a too-large report is only logged. The return value is insert && !flush, so it returns 1 only when a usage set insert and none set flush, and 0 otherwise.

name: ssi_flush
prose: Static int (omap_ssi_port.c:510-573) that stops all traffic on an HSI port. It takes a runtime PM reference with pm_runtime_get_sync and the port lock with spin_lock_bh, selects the idle pinctrl state, and waits 1 us for racing frames. For each GDD logical channel whose pending message belongs to this port it clears the channel control register, drops one autosuspend runtime PM reference when the message is a read, and clears the channel's message pointer. It then writes zero to the SST buffer and TX state registers and to the SSR RX state, buffer and break registers, reads the SSR error register and writes it back as the error acknowledgement, clears the port's MPU interrupt enable and sets the status bits to 0xffffff00, and clears the GDD MPU interrupt enable and acknowledges all GDD status bits (0xff). For each channel it drops one autosuspend reference if the tx queue is non-empty, then flushes the tx and rx queues with ssi_flush_queue (NULL client, so every message is completed with an error status), and finally flushes the break queue. It selects the default pinctrl state, releases the lock, drops the reference it took at the start and returns 0 (its only return). The function must not be entered with omap_port->lock held, since it takes that lock.

name: hte_ts_dis_en_common
prose: Static int (hte.c:237-305) that enables (en true) or disables (en false) the timestamping of one line. It returns -EINVAL, before taking any lock, if desc is NULL, if desc->hte_data is NULL or if its gdev is NULL. It then takes ei->req_mlock; if the timestamp is not marked HTE_TS_REGISTERED it releases the mutex and returns -EUSERS (not -EINVAL). Otherwise it takes ei->slock with interrupts saved. If the state already matches (enable requested and HTE_TS_DISABLE not set, or disable requested and HTE_TS_DISABLE set) it releases both locks and returns 0 without calling the chip. Otherwise it drops slock, calls the chip's enable or disable op; a nonzero result is logged with dev_warn, req_mlock is released and the result is returned with the flag unchanged. On success it retakes slock, clears HTE_TS_DISABLE (enable) or sets it (disable), releases both locks and returns 0. On each return after the registration test slock (where taken) and req_mlock are released before returning; on the early -EINVAL paths no lock was taken.

name: vmbus_onoffer_rescind
prose: Static void (channel_mgmt.c:1143-1278) that handles a rescind-offer message. It first traces the message and sleeps 1 ms at a time until vmbus_connection.offer_in_progress is zero. Under channel_mutex it looks up the channel for rescind->child_relid; if one is found and its rescind_ref is already set it unlocks and returns; if found and not set it sets rescind_ref and unlocks; if none is found it unlocks, returns, and rescind_ref is not set (the offer failed earlier). For a found channel it records whether it is an hvsock channel or a sub-channel, resets the channel callback, calls vmbus_rescind_cleanup, and sleeps 1 ms at a time until probe_done is set. If the channel has a device_obj and a chn_rescind_callback, it calls the callback, calls check_ready_for_suspend_event when the channel was an hvsock or sub-channel, and returns. If it has a device_obj without that callback, it takes a reference on the device and, if that succeeds, unregisters the vmbus device (outside channel_mutex) and drops the reference. If it has no device_obj but has a primary channel, it takes channel_mutex and calls hv_process_channel_removal when the channel state is CHANNEL_OPEN_STATE, or otherwise completes rescind_event, then releases the mutex. After either of these two branches (and when neither applies) it calls check_ready_for_suspend_event when the channel was an hvsock or sub-channel, without touching the channel again (it may already have been freed).

name: hv_common_cpu_init
prose: Int (hv_common.c:472-546), the CPU online callback for cpu. It picks GFP_ATOMIC when interrupts are disabled, otherwise GFP_KERNEL. If this CPU's hyperv_pcpu_input_arg is still NULL (it is already set when the CPU was online before), it kmallocs one page, or two when hv_output_page_exists(), and returns -ENOMEM if that fails. When there is an output page it stores the second page in hyperv_pcpu_output_arg at that point; in an SNP or TDX guest without a paravisor it then decrypts the memory with set_memory_decrypted, returning its error (the memory is not freed, the output pointer already stored stays set, and the input pointer is not set) or, on success, zeroing it. It publishes the memory in hyperv_pcpu_input_arg only after that. It then reads the VP index MSR, stores it in hv_vp_index[cpu] and raises hv_max_vp_index when it is larger. In a parent partition it kcallocs HV_SYNIC_SINT_COUNT bytes for this CPU's hv_synic_eventring_tail, and when that fails it returns -ENOMEM without undoing the earlier steps (the VP index and input page stay set). Otherwise it returns 0.

name: heartbeat_onchannelcallback
prose: Static void (hv_util.c:510-577), the receive callback of the heartbeat channel (the item name heartbeat_work_func does not exist in this file). It loops reading with vmbus_recvpacket into util_heartbeat.recv_buffer (HV_HYP_PAGE_SIZE bytes). If the read fails it logs a rate-limited error and returns. If the received length is 0 it leaves the loop silently, without logging. If the length is smaller than ICMSG_HDR it logs and leaves the loop. For a negotiate message it calls vmbus_prep_negotiate_resp and logs the negotiated version only when that returns true. For a heartbeat message with a length below ICMSG_HDR plus 8 it logs and leaves the loop without replying; otherwise it increments seq_num. Any other message type sets the status to HV_E_FAIL and logs the type. For negotiate, heartbeat and unknown messages it then sets icflags to TRANSACTION | RESPONSE and sends the buffer back with the same length and request id by vmbus_sendpacket as an in-band packet, ignoring its result, and loops to read the next packet. It returns when a read fails and when the loop is left; nothing is returned.

name: hv_do_map_gpa_hcall
prose: Static int (mshv_root_hv_call.c:184-265) that maps page_struct_count pages (or 2 MB pages) into a guest partition with batched hypercalls. It returns -EINVAL if page_struct_count is 0, if both pages and mmio_spa are nonzero, if HV_MAP_GPA_LARGE_PAGE is set together with a nonzero mmio_spa, or if the large-page flag is set and the count is not a multiple of 512 pages. With the large-page flag the page count is divided by 512 and gfn and indexes are scaled by 2 MB. In each batch it saves and disables local interrupts, fills the page frame list of the per-CPU input page (zero entries when HV_MAP_GPA_NO_ACCESS is set, page_to_pfn of pages[index] when pages is non-NULL, otherwise mmio_spa plus the index), and issues the repeat hypercall HVCALL_MAP_GPA_PAGES with interrupts restored just after it. The batch-fill -EINVAL branch for an out-of-range index would break with interrupts still disabled, but with the 2 MB alignment check it cannot be reached. When the hypercall returns HV_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY it deposits HV_MAP_GPA_DEPOSIT_PAGES pages with hv_call_deposit_pages and returns that error if the deposit fails (retrying otherwise); any other hypercall failure returns the errno translated from the status. The loop advances by the number of reps completed. On an error after at least one rep was completed it unmaps the done pages with hv_call_unmap_gpa_pages (with the large-page flag when set), and returns the error; it returns 0 when every page is mapped.

name: hv_call_delete_vp
prose: Int (mshv_root_hv_call.c:405-417) that asks the hypervisor to delete virtual processor vp_index of partition partition_id. It performs no validation of its arguments itself: it packs the two values into a hv_input_delete_vp, issues the fast hypercall HVCALL_DELETE_VP with it, and returns hv_result_to_errno(status) of the hypercall status. That is 0 when the status is success, the Linux error mapped to the hypervisor status for a known failure status, -EOPNOTSUPP when the status is U64_MAX (hypercalls not possible), and -EIO for an unknown status (hv_common.c:812-825). It takes no locks and no references and does not change any other state of its own.

name: vmbus_bus_init
prose: Static int (vmbus_drv.c:1412-1524) that brings up the VMBus bus. It returns the error of hv_init (after a log message) with nothing else done. It then registers hv_bus (its error is returned, nothing to undo). On a PREEMPT_RT kernel, when vmbus_irq_initialized is false, it registers the per-CPU IRQ kthreads (an error goes to the bus unregister and is returned) and sets vmbus_irq_initialized. If vmbus_irq is -1 it installs vmbus_isr with hv_setup_vmbus_handler; otherwise it allocates vmbus_evt with alloc_percpu (the result is not checked) and requests the per-CPU IRQ, and if that fails it logs, frees vmbus_evt and unwinds to the kthread and bus steps. It then calls hv_synic_alloc, and allocates a per-CPU work_struct (-ENOMEM on failure); each failure there unwinds the synic and interrupt setup. Under cpus_read_lock it schedules vmbus_percpu_work on every online CPU, waits for each, registers the CPU-hotplug online state hyperv/vmbus:online with cpuhp_setup_state_nocalls_cpuslocked, releases the lock and frees the work array; a negative result unwinds as above, otherwise it is stored in hyperv_cpuhp_online. It calls vmbus_connect; if that fails the hotplug state is removed first and the same unwinding follows. On success it registers hyperv_panic_vmbus_unload_block on the panic notifier chain, requests the offers with vmbus_request_offers and returns 0. The unwinding runs, in this order, hv_synic_free, removal of the vmbus handler or freeing of the per-CPU IRQ and vmbus_evt, unregistering the per-CPU kthreads on PREEMPT_RT when they were registered (and clearing vmbus_irq_initialized), and bus_unregister, and returns the failing step's error.

name: vmbus_acpi_add
prose: Static int (vmbus_drv.c:2546-2598, the CONFIG_ACPI version; without CONFIG_ACPI the stub at 2600-2603 ignores its argument and returns 0). It takes the ACPI companion of pdev->dev (there is no NULL check on it) and stores the device in vmbus_root_device. It sets the companion of that device to itself, and when CONFIG_ACPI_CCA_REQUIRED is enabled and no DMA attribute is found it marks the device as coherent (logging that no _CCA was found). It walks the device's _CRS resources with vmbus_walk_resources; if that walk fails it takes the cleanup path, which calls vmbus_mmio_remove and returns -ENODEV. Otherwise it walks up the ancestor devices (stopping at the ACPI root) and walks each one's _CRS; a failing ancestor walk is skipped, and when a successful walk leaves hyperv_mmio set it calls vmbus_reserve_fb and stops the loop. It then returns 0, also when no MMIO range was recorded.

name: abituguru_detect_bank1_sensor_type
prose: Static int (abituguru.c:471-607) that detects whether bank 1 sensor sensor_addr is a voltage sensor, a temperature sensor or not connected; it sleeps (schedule_timeout of 20 ms and 50 ms), so the caller must be able to sleep. If the module parameter bank1_types[sensor_addr] holds a value from ABIT_UGURU_IN_SENSOR to ABIT_UGURU_NC it returns that value without touching the hardware. If reading the sensor fails it returns -ENODEV. If the reading is below 10 or above 250 it logs a warning and returns ABIT_UGURU_NC. Otherwise it writes test settings (a volt alarm with an extreme limit, the low alarm test when the reading is at most 240 and the high alarm test otherwise), waits 20 ms, reads the alarm bank, and if the sensor's alarm bit is set reads the sensor settings back and returns ABIT_UGURU_IN_SENSOR when the expected volt alarm flag is set. If not, it writes a temperature high-alarm test, waits 50 ms and, when the alarm bit is set and the temperature high flag is set in the settings read back, returns ABIT_UGURU_TEMP_SENSOR; otherwise ABIT_UGURU_NC. A failing read or write during the tests leaves the result -ENODEV. Each path after the first test write goes through the restore step, which writes data->bank1_settings[sensor_addr] back, retrying up to 3 times; if all three writes fail it logs an error and returns -ENODEV in place of the result. The early returns before the first test write have nothing to restore.

name: cvt_auto_temp
prose: Static int (adt7462.c:1365-1374) that converts a temperature-zone input to an index. It returns 6 when input is 15 and 5 when input is 9. For any other input it returns -22 (the invalid-argument error) when input is below 1 or is not a power of two, and otherwise the base-2 logarithm of input (0 to 30). It allocates nothing and takes no locks.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (input == 15 ==> result == 6) && (input == 9 ==> result == 5) && ((input != 15 && input != 9 && (input < 1 || (input & (input - 1)) != 0)) ==> result == -22) && ((input != 15 && input != 9 && input >= 1 && (input & (input - 1)) == 0) ==> (0 <= result && result <= 30 && (1 << result) == input)); */

The earlier rejections were a mechanical check on the prose naming the macro for the invalid-argument error and an unbound ilog2 in the old contract; neither concerns the behaviour. The prose no longer uses the macro name and the contract states the power-of-two case without ilog2. R:n/a

name: IN_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:262-265) that converts a voltage register value to millivolts. It returns (reg * nominal + (3 << (res - 3))) / (3 << (res - 2)), that is reg scaled by nominal over 3 * 2^res with rounding to nearest (the added term is half the divisor). res is the register resolution in bits (8 or 16 for the callers), so the shifts are well defined only for res of at least 3 and the products must fit in an int. It has a single return, takes no locks and changes no state.
contract: /*@ requires 3 <= res <= 16 && 0 <= reg <= 65535 && 0 <= nominal <= 20000; ensures result == (reg * nominal + (3 << (res - 3))) / (3 << (res - 2)); */
note: Checked against dme1737.c:262-265. The earlier contract failed random testing with res=86, an out-of-range shift; the precondition now bounds res, reg and nominal so that nothing overflows. R:n/a

name: IN_TO_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:267-271) that converts millivolts to the 8-bit limit register value. It first clamps val to the range 0 to 255 * nominal / 192 and then returns DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(val * 192, nominal), that is the clamped value times 192 divided by nominal with rounding to nearest. For positive nominal the result is in the range 0 to 255. nominal is not checked, so a zero nominal would divide by zero. It has a single return and changes no state.
contract: /*@ requires 1 <= nominal <= 100000; ensures \let m = 255 * nominal / 192; \let v = (val < 0 ? 0 : (val > m ? m : val)); 0 <= result <= 255 && result == (v * 192 + nominal / 2) / nominal; */
note: Checked against dme1737.c:267-271. The earlier contract used clamp_val, which Frama-C does not know; the clamp is written out. R:n/a

name: TEMP_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:279-282) that converts a temperature register value to millidegrees Celsius. It returns (reg * 1000) >> (res - 8), where res is the register resolution in bits (16 for input registers, 8 for limit registers). The shift count must be non-negative and below the width of int, and reg * 1000 must fit in an int; a negative reg is shifted arithmetically on the usual targets. It has a single return and changes no state.
note: Checked against dme1737.c:279-282. The earlier contract failed random testing with res=38, an out-of-range shift; the precondition now bounds res and reg. R:n/a

name: TEMP_TO_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:284-288) that converts millidegrees Celsius to an 8-bit limit register value in two's complement. It clamps val to -128000..127000 and returns DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(val, 1000), that is the clamped value divided by 1000 rounded to nearest with halves away from zero. The result is in the range -128 to 127. It has a single return and changes no state.
note: Checked against dme1737.c:284-288. The earlier contract had no requires clause and used clamp_val; the clamp is now written out. R:n/a

name: TEMP_RANGE_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:295-298) that returns the temperature range in millidegrees for a register value. It returns the entry of the TEMP_RANGE table selected by the high nibble of reg, that is TEMP_RANGE[(reg >> 4) & 0x0f] (2000 to 80000). It has a single return and changes no state.
note: Checked against dme1737.c:295-298. The earlier rejection was only the missing requires clause. R:n/a

name: TEMP_RANGE_TO_REG
prose: Static int (dme1737.c:300-309) that converts a temperature range in millidegrees to the register value, keeping the low nibble of reg. It looks for the largest index i from 15 down to 1 for which val is above the rounded midpoint (TEMP_RANGE[i] + TEMP_RANGE[i - 1] + 1) / 2, and uses i = 0 when no index qualifies. It returns (reg & 0x0f) | (i << 4), so the low nibble of reg is preserved and the high nibble holds i. It has a single return and changes no state.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures 0 <= result <= 255 && (result & 0x0f) == (reg & 0x0f) && \let i = result >> 4; (i == 0 || val > (TEMP_RANGE[i] + TEMP_RANGE[i - 1] + 1) / 2) && (\forall integer k; i < k <= 15 ==> val <= (TEMP_RANGE[k] + TEMP_RANGE[k - 1] + 1) / 2); */
note: Checked against dme1737.c:300-309. The earlier rejection was only the missing requires clause; the contract now also states how the high nibble is chosen. R:n/a

name: TEMP_HYST_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:318-321) that extracts a temperature hysteresis from a register byte in millidegrees. For ix equal to 1 it takes the low nibble of reg, for any other ix the high nibble (reg >> 4), and returns that 4-bit value times 1000. It has a single return and changes no state.
note: Checked against dme1737.c:318-321. The earlier rejection was only the missing requires clause. R:n/a

name: TEMP_HYST_TO_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:323-329) that converts a hysteresis to its 4-bit register field. It clamps hyst to the range temp - 15000 to temp, converts the difference temp - hyst to units of 1000 with rounding to nearest (a value in the range 0 to 15), and merges it into reg: for ix equal to 1 it keeps the high nibble of reg and puts the value in the low nibble, otherwise it keeps the low nibble and puts the value in the high nibble. It has a single return and changes no state.
contract: /*@ requires -1000000 <= temp <= 1000000; ensures \let c = (hyst < temp - 15000 ? temp - 15000 : (hyst > temp ? temp : hyst)); \let h = (temp - c + 500) / 1000; result == ((ix == 1) ? ((reg & 0xf0) | h) : ((reg & 0x0f) | (h << 4))); */

name: FAN_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:332-338) that converts a fan tachometer register to RPM. When tpc is nonzero it returns tpc * reg. When tpc is 0 it returns 0 for a reg of 0 or 0xffff and otherwise 90000 * 60 / reg (5400000 / reg). It has a single return per branch and changes no state.
contract: /*@ requires 0 <= reg <= 65535 && 0 <= tpc <= 60; ensures (tpc != 0 ==> result == tpc * reg) && (tpc == 0 ==> result == ((reg == 0 || reg == 65535) ? 0 : 5400000 / reg)); */
note: Checked against dme1737.c:332-338. The old prose is right. The earlier rejection was only the missing requires clause. R:n/a

name: FAN_TO_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:340-348) that converts RPM to a fan tachometer register. When tpc is nonzero it returns val / tpc clamped to 0..0xffff. When tpc is 0 it returns 0xffff for val at or below 0, and otherwise 90000 * 60 / val (5400000 / val) clamped to 0..0xfffe. A nonzero tpc is expected to be positive; the callers pass 0 or a divisor from FAN_TPC_FROM_REG. It has a single return per branch and changes no state.
note: Checked against dme1737.c:340-348. The earlier rejection was only the missing requires clause. R:n/a

name: FAN_TPC_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:355-358) that converts a register to the tach pulse count multiplier. It returns 0 when bit 5 of reg (0x20) is set (legacy, non-tpc mode) and otherwise 60 >> (reg & 0x03), which is 60, 30, 15 or 7. It has a single return and changes no state.
note: Checked against dme1737.c:355-358. The earlier rejection was only the missing requires clause. R:n/a

name: FAN_TYPE_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:365-370) that converts a register to the number of pulses per revolution. It takes edge = (reg >> 1) & 0x03 and returns 1 << (edge - 1) when edge is above 0 (1, 2 or 4) and 0 when edge is 0. It has a single return and changes no state.
contract: /*@ requires 0 <= reg <= 255; ensures \let edge = (reg >> 1) & 0x03; (edge == 0 ==> result == 0) && (edge > 0 ==> result == (1 << (edge - 1))); */
note: Checked against dme1737.c:365-370. The earlier rejection was only the missing requires clause. R:n/a

name: FAN_TYPE_TO_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:372-376) that stores a fan pulse-per-revolution type in a register. It takes edge as 3 when val is 4 and as val otherwise (converted to int), and returns (reg & 0xf9) | (edge << 1), so every bit of reg except bits 1 and 2 is kept and bits 1 and 2 hold edge. For val from 0 to 4 edge fits in two bits. It has a single return and changes no state.
note: Checked against dme1737.c:372-376. The earlier rejection was only the missing requires clause; the contract now also states the stored type. R:n/a

name: FAN_MAX_FROM_REG
prose: Static int (dme1737.c:383-392) that converts the fan max register to RPM. It searches FAN_MAX from index 10 down to 1 for the first entry equal to reg, leaving the index at 0 when none matches (including when reg equals FAN_MAX[0]), and returns 1000 + i * 500, a value from 1000 to 6000. It has a single return and changes no state.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures 1000 <= result <= 6000 && (result - 1000) % 500 == 0 && \let i = (result - 1000) / 500; (i == 0 || FAN_MAX[i] == reg) && (\forall integer k; i < k <= 10 ==> FAN_MAX[k] != reg); */
note: Checked against dme1737.c:383-392. The old prose said 10 when nothing matches; the code gives index 0 (result 1000), since the loop ends with i equal to 0. R:n/a

name: FAN_MAX_TO_REG
prose: Static int (dme1737.c:395-403) that converts an RPM maximum to the fan max register value. It looks from index 10 down to 1 for the first i for which val is above 1000 + (i - 1) * 500, using i = 0 when none qualifies, and returns FAN_MAX[i], which is one of the table values 0x54 down to 0x0e (0x54 for i = 0). It has a single return and changes no state.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures \exists integer i; 0 <= i <= 10 && result == FAN_MAX[i] && (i == 0 || val > 1000 + (i - 1) * 500) && (\forall integer k; i < k <= 10 ==> val <= 1000 + (k - 1) * 500); */
note: Checked against dme1737.c:395-403. The earlier contract had no requires and used a free variable; it is now a bounded existential. R:n/a

name: PWM_EN_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:419-423) that converts the top three bits of a PWM register to an enable mode. It returns the entry of the table {2, 2, 2, 0, -1, 2, 2, 1} selected by (reg >> 5) & 0x07: 0 for full on (index 3), -1 for disabled (index 4), 1 for manual mode (index 7) and 2 for the automatic modes. It has a single return and changes no state.

name: PWM_EN_TO_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:426-430) that stores a PWM enable mode in a register. It encodes manual mode (val equal to 1) as 7 and any other val as 3, and returns (reg & 0x1f) | (en << 5), so the low five bits of reg are kept and the top three bits hold the encoding. It has a single return and changes no state.

name: PWM_ACZ_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:446-450) that converts the top three bits of a PWM register to the auto-channel zone bitmask. It returns the entry of the table {1, 2, 4, 0, 0, 6, 7, 0} selected by (reg >> 5) & 0x07, a value from 0 to 7. It has a single return and changes no state.

name: PWM_ACZ_TO_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:453-457) that stores an auto-channel zone in a register. It takes acz as 2 when val is 4 and as val - 1 otherwise (converted to int), and returns (reg & 0x1f) | ((acz & 0x07) << 5), so the low five bits of reg are kept and the top three bits hold acz. It has a single return and changes no state.

name: PWM_FREQ_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:464-467) that converts a PWM register to a frequency in Hz. It returns the entry of the PWM_FREQ table selected by the low nibble of reg, that is PWM_FREQ[reg & 0x0f] (11 to 30000, and 0 for the four unused codes 12 to 15). It has a single return and changes no state.

name: PWM_FREQ_TO_REG
prose: Static int (dme1737.c:469-488) that converts a PWM frequency in Hz to the register value, keeping the high nibble of reg. For val above 27500 it uses index 10, for val above 22500 (and at most 27500) index 11, and otherwise it looks from index 9 down to 1 for the first i for which val is above the rounded midpoint (PWM_FREQ[i] + PWM_FREQ[i - 1] + 1) / 2, using 0 when none qualifies. It returns (reg & 0xf0) | i, so the result has the high nibble of reg and the index in the low nibble (0 to 11).

name: PWM_RR_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:496-500) that converts a PWM ramp-rate field to a rate. It takes rr as reg >> 4 when ix is 1 and as reg otherwise, and returns PWM_RR[rr & 0x07] (206 down to 5) when bit 3 of rr (0x08) is set and 0 when it is clear. It has a single return and changes no state.

name: superio_enter
prose: Precondition: base is the I/O port address of the Super-I/O index/data pair. Postcondition: if request_muxed_region(base, 2, DRVNAME) fails, it prints an error with pr_err and returns -EBUSY without writing to any port; otherwise it writes SIO_UNLOCK_KEY (0x87) twice to port base with outb and returns 0, leaving the 2-port region reserved; the caller is expected to release it later (superio_exit writes SIO_LOCK_KEY and calls release_region).
note: reviewer reasons were only mechanical contract complaints (contract names/omits EBUSY); contract dropped because the function touches I/O ports. f71882fg.c:2080-2093, superio_exit at 2101-2105.

name: rpm_from_cnt
prose: Precondition: when cnt is not 0xff, p and clk_div are nonzero (otherwise the integer division is by zero) and (cnt ? cnt : 1) * p * clk_div, computed in signed int, does not overflow. Postcondition: it returns 0 when cnt == 0xff; otherwise it returns (clk_freq * 30 * gear_mult) / ((cnt ? cnt : 1) * p * clk_div) as an unsigned int, where the numerator is computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic (modulo 2^32 if it exceeds 4294967295). It reads no global state, takes no lock and allocates nothing.
contract: /*@ requires cnt == 255 || (p != 0 && clk_div != 0 && (cnt == 0 ? 1 : cnt) * p * clk_div <= 2147483647 && clk_freq * 30 * gear_mult <= 4294967295); ensures (cnt == 255 ==> result == 0) && (cnt != 255 ==> result == (clk_freq * 30 * gear_mult) / ((cnt == 0 ? 1 : cnt) * p * clk_div)); */
note: reviewer claim (gear_mult != 0 needed to avoid overflow of clk_freq*30) is wrong: g762.c:171-173 the numerator is u32 unsigned arithmetic, which wraps by definition, and with gear_mult == 0 the product is 0 either way; the real hazards are the signed denominator product and a zero denominator, now stated.

name: cnt_from_rpm
prose: Precondition: when rpm is nonzero, p and clk_div are both nonzero, so f2 = p * clk_div is nonzero (otherwise 255 * f2 or ULONG_MAX / f2 divides by zero). Postcondition: it returns 0xff when rpm is 0. Otherwise it computes f1 = clk_freq * 30 * gear_mult in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic (wrapping modulo 2^32), f2 = p * clk_div, replaces rpm by clamp_val(rpm, f1 / (255 * f2), ULONG_MAX / f2), and returns DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(f1, rpm * f2) converted to unsigned char, i.e. reduced modulo 256 if the quotient exceeds 255. It takes no lock and allocates nothing.
note: g762.c:180-193. Old prose had the clamp and round-half-up right; contract dropped (clamp_val unbound in ACSL, rejected in every round). Width of unsigned long is architecture dependent.

name: ina209_to_reg
prose: Precondition: val is not LONG_MIN (it is negated for the INA209_CRITICAL_DAC_NEG case) and, for the power registers, DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(val, 20000) fits in int, since the result is returned as int. Postcondition: depending on reg it returns: for INA209_SHUNT_VOLTAGE_POS_WARN and _NEG_WARN (0x0c, 0x0d) clamp(val, -320, 320) * 100; for INA209_BUS_VOLTAGE_OVER_WARN, _UNDER_WARN, _OVER_LIMIT and _UNDER_LIMIT (0x0f, 0x10, 0x12, 0x13) (DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(clamp(val, 0, 32000), 4) << 3) | (old & 0x7); for INA209_CRITICAL_DAC_NEG (0x15) (clamp(-val, 0, 255) << 8) | (old & 0xff); for INA209_CRITICAL_DAC_POS (0x14) (clamp(val, 0, 255) << 8) | (old & 0xff); for INA209_POWER_WARN and INA209_POWER_OVER_LIMIT (0x0e, 0x11) DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(val, 20000); for any other reg value -EACCES. It has no side effects.
note: ina209.c:154-195. Prose was already right; register numbers checked against the #defines at ina209.c:45-54. Contract dropped: long ternary form was rejected (unbalanced brackets, unbound DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST) and the -EACCES clause cannot be stated simply.

name: it87_find
prose: Precondition: sioaddr is the Super-I/O index port, address and sio_data point to writable storage, and chip_cnt indexes force_id when force_id_cnt != 1. Postcondition: it first calls superio_enter(sioaddr, true) (reserving the region without entering configuration mode) and returns that call's nonzero error immediately if it fails. After that it returns -ENODEV, with the chip left unrecognized or skipped, when DEVID reads 0xffff both before and after entering configuration mode, when the (possibly forced) chip id is 0xffff or not in the supported list, when the device activation bit is clear, or when the base address read is 0; in those cases it does not fill in *address. It returns 0 only after the base address is nonzero, having set *address, sio_data->sioaddr, revision, type and the skip_in, skip_pwm, skip_fan, skip_temp, skip_vid, internal, beep_pin, vid_value, need_in7_reroute, ec_special_config and smbus_bitmap fields from per-chip GPIO/pin registers (and may have written the PINX2 register to re-route VCCH5V to in7). Every path after the successful superio_enter reaches the exit label, which calls superio_exit(sioaddr, !enabled).
note: slice cut the head; packet name it87_sio_probe does not exist in it87.c, the function is it87_find (it87.c:2673-3194, head at 2673). Old prose claimed only that fields 'reflect' GPIO config and omitted the -ENODEV/err returns and exit cleanup.

name: LM93_IN_REL_TO_REG
prose: Precondition: vid * 1000 does not overflow int. Postcondition: uv_offset (a long) is initialised to vid * 1000 - val * 10000 evaluated in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic because val is unsigned, so on an LP64 target it is always a nonnegative value below 2^32 and on a 32-bit-long target it is that value reinterpreted as signed. If upper is nonzero, uv_offset is clamped to [12500, 200000] and the function returns (u8)((uv_offset / 12500 - 1) << 4). If upper is zero, uv_offset is clamped to [-400000, -25000] and the function returns (u8)(uv_offset / -25000 - 1): on a target where long is 64 bits the nonnegative uv_offset always clamps to -25000 so the result is 0, but where long is 32 bits a wrapped negative uv_offset can give a nonzero result in 0..15. It has no side effects.
note: reviewer was right: old prose claimed the lower branch always returns 0, which holds only for 64-bit long (lm93.c:392-404). Contract left empty: clamp_val and the arch-dependent long.

name: superio_enter
prose: Precondition: ioreg is the base I/O port of the Super-I/O index/data pair. Postcondition: if request_muxed_region(ioreg, 2, DRVNAME) fails it returns -EBUSY (-16) without writing to any port; otherwise it writes 0x87 twice to port ioreg with outb and returns 0, leaving the 2-port region reserved for the caller to release later.

name: nct6775_asuswmi_write
prose: Precondition: none beyond the u8 argument types. Postcondition: it calls nct6775_asuswmi_evaluate_method(ASUSWMI_METHODID_WHWM, bank, reg, val, NULL) and returns its result unchanged: with CONFIG_ACPI it is 0 when acpi_evaluate_integer on the WMBD method succeeds and -EIO when it fails; without CONFIG_ACPI it is -EOPNOTSUPP. It takes no lock and allocates nothing; the result retval pointer is NULL so no value is stored.

name: bpa_rs600_read_vin
prose: Precondition: client is a valid i2c_client for the BPA-RS600. Postcondition: it reads the word PMBUS_READ_VIN with pmbus_read_word_data(client, 0, 0xff, ...) and returns a negative value from that call unchanged. Otherwise, if bit 10 of the word is clear it returns the word unchanged; if bit 10 is set it returns ((word >> 11) + 1) << 11 | ((word & 0x7ff) >> 1), which can be as large as 0x103ff when the exponent field is 31 (0x10000 | 0x3ff) and therefore does not always fit in 16 bits. It has no other side effects.

name: max34451_set_supported_funcs
prose: Precondition: client is the i2c_client of a MAX34451-family device and data points to its max34440_data with info already initialised. Postcondition: it reads PMBUS_MFR_REVISION with i2c_smbus_read_word_data and returns the negative errno if that fails. If the revision is at least MAX34451ETNA6_MFR_REV it sets data->info.format, m, b and R for PSC_VOLTAGE_IN and PSC_CURRENT_IN (direct, m=1, b=0, R=3 and 2) and sets data->iout_oc_fault_limit and data->iout_oc_warn_limit. Then for each page 0..15 it writes PMBUS_PAGE (sleeping MAX34440_PAGE_CHANGE_DELAY after the write, before checking its result), returns the negative errno if the write failed, reads MAX34451_MFR_CHANNEL_CONFIG and returns the negative errno if that read failed, and sets data->info.func[page] by the selection field: 0x10 or 0x20 voltage out plus status, 0x21 voltage out, 0x22 current out plus status, 0x23 current out, adding the input flags when the revision was at least MAX34451ETNA6_MFR_REV; any other selection leaves func[page] unchanged. It returns 0 after all 16 pages. On an error return the earlier pages may already be updated, and PMBUS_PAGE is not restored. It takes no lock.

prose: Precondition: none; module init function. prose: Precondition: dev's driver data is a valid vt1211_data, attr is a sensor_device_attribute_2 whose index (ix) selects pwm_ctl and whose nr (ap) indexes pwm_auto_temp, and buf is a NUL-terminated string. Postcondition: it calls csdev_access_relaxed_write_pair(&drvdata->csdev->access, val, CATU_SLADDRLO, CATU_SLADDRHI), which writes the low 32 bits of val to the register at offset 0x020 and the high 32 bits to the register at offset 0x024; it returns nothing and takes no lock.
note: macro-generated: CATU_REG_PAIR at coresight-catu.h:84-94.

name: etm_event_stop
prose: Precondition: called on the CPU that owns the per-CPU etm_ctxt, with event and mode valid. Postcondition: if mode has PERF_EF_PAUSE it only returns etm_event_pause(path, event, ctxt) (a void call), changing nothing else here. Otherwise: if handle->event is set and perf_get_aux(handle) != ctxt->event_data it WARNs and returns before changing anything; else it reads ctxt->event_data and sets ctxt->event_data to NULL, and then returns without further work if event->hw.state is already PERF_HES_STOPPED or (after a WARN) if the saved event_data is NULL. If handle->event is set, PERF_EF_UPDATE is requested and this CPU is not in event_data->mask, it sets event->hw.state to PERF_HES_STOPPED, calls perf_aux_output_end(handle, 0) and returns. If the path has no source or no sink it returns, leaving the state and path untouched. Otherwise it disables the source, sets event->hw.state to PERF_HES_STOPPED and, when handle->event is set and PERF_EF_UPDATE is requested, returns early (path not disabled) after a WARN_ON_ONCE if handle->event != event or if the sink has no update_buffer op; otherwise it calls update_buffer with event_data->snk_config and ends the AUX handle with the returned size when handle->event is still set (WARN_ON(size) when it is not). Unless one of those earlier returns was taken, it finally calls coresight_disable_path(path).
note: reviewers were right that the old prose misdescribed the PAUSE return and path disabling; but the round-15 claim 'WARNs on == vs !=' is a misreading of the old precondition wording, code WARNs on != (coresight-etm-perf.c:~707, WARN_ON(perf_get_aux(handle) != ctxt->event_data)). Verified every return at lines 664-751.

name: reset_store
prose: Precondition: dev is an ETMv4 device whose parent holds a valid etmv4_drvdata, and buf is a NUL-terminated string. Postcondition: if kstrtoul(buf, 16, &val) fails it returns -EINVAL without changing anything. Otherwise, with drvdata->spinlock held (raw_spin_lock), it sets config->mode to 0 if val is nonzero, and in all cases (including val == 0) clears the load/store and data-trace mode and cfg bits, zeroes the event, timestamp, stall controls, ViewInst include/start-stop controls, the sequencer, external-input, counter, resource (from index 2), single-shot, address-comparator, context-ID and VMID configuration and their index fields, sets config->syncfreq to 0x8 only when drvdata->syncpr is false, and sets config->vinst_ctrl to FIELD_PREP(TRCVICTLR_EVENT_MASK, 0x01), additionally setting ETM_MODE_VIEWINST_STARTSTOP in config->mode and TRCVICTLR_SSSTATUS in vinst_ctrl when drvdata->nr_addr_cmp > 0. It then releases the spinlock, calls etm4_release_trace_id(drvdata) and cscfg_csdev_reset_feats(to_coresight_device(dev)) and returns size.
note: reviewer (round 15) claim 'reset_store clears vinst_ctrl' is wrong: coresight-etm4x-sysfs.c line ~185 sets vinst_ctrl = FIELD_PREP(TRCVICTLR_EVENT_MASK, 0x01) unconditionally and ORs in SSSTATUS only if nr_addr_cmp > 0; old prose wrongly tied the event mask to the comparator condition, and omitted that val == 0 still resets everything except mode. Verified all returns (kstrtoul failure and final).

name: tmc_panic_sync_etf
prose: Precondition: csdev is a valid coresight device whose parent's drvdata is an initialised tmc_drvdata. Postcondition: both of its return statements return 0. If tmc_has_reserved_buffer(drvdata) or tmc_has_crash_mdata_buffer(drvdata) is false it returns 0 immediately without touching hardware or metadata. Otherwise it marks the crash metadata invalid with tmc_crashdata_set_invalid, calls CS_UNLOCK(drvdata->base) (the CoreSight unlock-access macro; no mutex or spinlock is taken), reads TMC_CTL and, if TMC_CTL_CAPT_EN is clear, or reads TMC_MODE and it is not TMC_MODE_CIRCULAR_BUFFER, jumps to the out label. When capture is enabled in circular-buffer mode it does a manual flush and stop (tmc_flush_and_stop) unless TMC_FFSR_FT_STOPPED is already set, in which case it waits for TMC ready, copies TMC_STS, TMC_MODE, TMC_FFCR and TMC_FFSR into the metadata, sets drvdata->buf to the reserved buffer and dumps the internal SRAM into it with tmc_etb_dump_hw, fills in the ram size, rrp, dba, rwp, trace physical address and version fields, issues dmb(sy), sets mdata->valid to true, computes crc32_tdata then crc32_mdata, and calls tmc_disable_hw. The out label then calls CS_UNLOCK(drvdata->base) a second time (not CS_LOCK) and returns 0.
note: reviewers (round 2 and 15) were right: old prose called CS_UNLOCK 'taking the device lock' and said it was 'released again' before returning, but out: calls CS_UNLOCK again and CS_LOCK is never called (coresight-tmc-etf.c:604-677).
